51You people of Jerusalem have sinned twice as much as the people of Samaria. In fact, your evil ways have made both Sodom and Samaria look innocent. 52So their punishment will seem light compared to yours. You will be disgraced and put to shame because of your disgusting sins.
Jerusalem Will Be Ashamed
The Lord said to Jerusalem:
53Someday I will bless Sodom and Samaria and their nearby villages. I will also bless you, Jerusalem. 54Then you will be ashamed of how you've acted, and Sodom and Samaria will be relieved that they weren't as sinful as you. 55When that day comes, you and Sodom and Samaria will once again be well-off, and all nearby villages will be restored.
56Jerusalem, you were so arrogant that you sneered at Sodom. 57But now everyone has learned how wicked you really are. The countries of Syria and Philistia, as well as your other neighbors, hate you and make insulting remarks. 58You must pay for all the vulgar and disgusting things you have done. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Makes a Promise to Jerusalem
The Lord said:
59Jerusalem, you deserve to be punished, because you broke your promises and ignored our agreement. 60But I remember the agreement I made with you when you were young, and so I will make you a promise that will last forever. 61When you think about how you acted, you will be ashamed, especially when I return your sisters to you as daughters, even though this was not part of our agreement. 62I will keep this solemn promise, and you will know that I am the Lord. 63I will forgive you, but you will think about your sins and be too ashamed to say a word. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
(Kwe̱ Yitšo 23.)
1Ni Iehowa wiemo̱ sā ba miṅõ ake̱:
2Gbomobi, hã Ierusalem aná ale enihĩnii le̱,
3ni okē̱: Bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ Ierusalem ne̱: Odšē̱he ke̱ heni afo̱o ye̱ dši Kanaanbii le̱ ašikpoṅ le̱ no̱: otše̱ le̱ Amornyo ni, ni onye le̱ Hityō ni.
4Asaṅ ofo̱mo̱ mli le̱, gbĩ ní afo̱o le̱, afoo olaṅmo̱, ake̱-nu hũ dšuu ohe ni ohe adše, awoo bo ṅō hũ kwrā, ni ake̱ mama eblaa ohe kwrā.
5Mokomoko enaao mo̱bo̱, ní eefe ene̱mei eko ehão, ní emũsũṅ aatšōle̱ ye̱ ohe, ši moṅ aše̱o afo ṅãno̱ ye̱ nyãṅemo̱ ni anyãṅe osusuma gbĩ ní afo̱o le̱ hewo̱.
6Ke̱ke̱ ni mihatšṍ omase̱i ke̱-ho, ni minao, ní ōkoklo ši ye̱ olá le̱ mli, ni mike̱o ye̱ olá le̱ mli ake̱: Oyi aná wala! hẽ mike̱o ye̱ olá le̱ mli ake̱: Oyi aná wala!
7Mihã oyi fá babaō tamo̱ ṅāno̱ kwẽnii, ni oſere ni oda kple, ni ohe fe fe̱o teke no̱; ofufo̱i badăra ni oyitšo̱i ba; kẽle̱ onyie yayai ke̱ ohe pasā.
8Ni mibatšṍ omase̱i ke̱-ho, ni minao, ni na, oše̱ suomo̱; ni miṅõ *mitade le̱ milē̱ ono̱, ni miṅõ-ha oyayaiaṅ; ni mikã kitã mitšõo, ni mike̱o †kpãṅ, Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱, ni otšṍ minõ! *Rut. 3,9. †2 Mose 19,5.
9Ke̱ke̱ ni mike̱ nu dšu ohe, ni mi-fo̱ ohe lai le̱ kwrā, ni mikpao mũ;
10ni misā miwoö atade ní aye mli ṅābii, ni miwoö nuṅgbẽ́ wolo tokotai, ni mike̱ klala kpakpa fĩ ohe, ni mike̱ seda ha ohe;
11ni misā miwulao ke̱ wulamo̱nii, ni mike̱ ninešigai wo onidšiaši, ni mike̱ kõsõṅkõsõ wo okue̱,
12ni mike̱ ga wo ogugõṅ, ni mike̱ toiiaṅnii hũ wo otoiiaṅ, ni mike̱ akekre fe̱fe̱o fĩ oyitšo.
13Ni oke̱ šika ke̱ dſie̱te̱i wula ohe, ni otadei dši klala ke̱ seda ke̱ mama ní aye mli ṅābii. Šikišaṅ ke̱ wò ke̱ mū so̱ṅṅ oyeo̱, ni ohe fe fe̱o naakpa dientše̱, ni onine še̱ maṅtše̱yeli no̱.
14Ni ogbe̱i hehe ke̱-te dšeṅmãdši le̱ ateṅ ye̱ ohefe̱o le̱ hewo̱, edšake̱ miwulamo̱nii ní miṅõ woö le̱ hã eye emū. Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱. Yāfó 2.15.
15Ši oṅõ ohĩe ofõ ohefe̱o le̱ no̱, ní ogbe̱i ní ehehe le̱ hewo̱ le̱ *obo̱ adſamaṅ, ni ofo̱fe odſamaṅbō̱i le̱ oſie mofẽmo ní hoo̱ le̱ no̱: eno ni! *2 Mose 34,16.
16Ni oko̱ otadei le̱ eko ni oke̱-fe heii groṅṅi ní ake̱ asāsā ewula ohã ohe, ni obo̱ adſamaṅ ye̱ no̱: noni esaa ake̱ ake̱-baä dšeṅ lo afeo̱ le̱!
17Osā oṅõ odſinei fe̱fe̱dši le̱ ní dši mišika ke̱ midſie̱te̱i ní mihão le̱ eko, ni oṅõ-fe hĩĩ-amãgãi ohã ohe, ni oke̱ame̱ bo̱ adſamaṅ.
18Ni oṅõ otadei ní aye mli ṅābii le̱ oha ame̱he, ni oṅõ mimũ ke̱ mitšofã-ke̱-ṅma le̱ omãmo̱ ame̱hĩe.
19Ni miniyenii ni mihão, ní dši šikišaṅ ke̱ mũ ke̱ wò ni mike̱-lè̱o̱o le̱,, oṅõ-mãmo̱ ame̱hĩe ní edše ṅma. Ni eba nakai! Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱.
20Asaṅ oṅõ *obihĩĩ ke̱ obiyei ní ofo̱ ohãmi le̱ ošã afo̱lei ohãame̱ ní ame̱ye Aso odſamaṅbō̱i le fáá hãão, *2 Maṅ. 16,3. Ier. 7,31.
21hewo̱ ni osā ogbe mibii le̱, ni oṅõ-ame̱ ohã ní ame̱tšṍ la mli ame̱hãame̱ le̱?
22Ni onihĩnii le̱ ke̱ odſamaṅbō̱i le̱ fè mli le̱ okaii oblayeiaṅ gbĩĩ le̱, *beni onyie yayai ke̱ ohe pasā, ní okokloo̱ olá mli le̱. *K. 6. 7.
23Ni onifõdšianii le̱ fẽ se̱ le̱ eba mli, (kpóo, kpóo häo! Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱,)
24ake̱ ofe koi ohã ohe, ni ofe he groṅṅ ohã ohe ye̱ blohũ-fè-blohũ mli.
25Ṅmaṅmaša-fẽ-ṅmaṅmaša no̱ omãmo̱ ohei groṅṅi le̱ ye̱, ni ohã ohefe̱o le̱ tšṍ noni ahĩo̱, ni ogble onãdšiaṅ ohã mofẽmo ní hoo̱ le̱, ni ohã odſamaṅbō̱i le̱ fá.
26Asaṅ oke̱ Mizraimbii ní oke̱-dše ſieka, ní ame̱helo fá le̱, hũ bo̱ adſamaṅ; ni ohã odſamaṅbō̱i le̱ fá ni oke̱-wo mimli la.
27Nohewo̱ le̱, na, mikpã minine mli ye̱ ono̱, ni mitše odā-ṅmā̃ le̱ no̱, ni mi-ṅõo mihã ohenye̱lo̱i, ní dši Filistibii le̱ abiyei le̱, ní hĩe gboo onyenyeṅtſibō̱ gbe̱ le̱ he le̱, ní ame̱feo bo̱ni ame̱sumoo̱.
28Osā oke̱ Ašurbii le̱ bũ bo̱ adſamaṅ, edšake̱ oto̱o̱; ni oke̱ame̱ bo̱ adſamaṅ, ši kẽle̱ eše̱e̱ onā.
29Ni osā ohã odſamaṅbō̱ le̱ fá ye̱ Kanaan šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ āhũ ke̱-yaſie Kaldea, ši kẽle̱ no bũ še̱e̱ onā.
30Kwe̱, bo̱ni otšui eto̱ biti! Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱, ake̱-ni ofeo̱ ene̱mei fẽ, ni dši yō adſamaṅ ní hĩe gboo nõ nifemo̱-nii le̱;
31ni ofeo̱ okoi ye̱ ṅmaṅmaša-fẽ-ṅmaṅmaša no̱, ni ofeo̱ ohei groṅṅi le̱ ye̱ blohũ-fẽ-blohũ mli; ni ofee tamo̱ adſamaṅ tete, ake̱-ní okpōo̱ nyõmo̱wo le̱; K. 24. 25.
32ṅã ní fiteo̱ gblã, ní eṅõo̱ meikrokomei ye̱ ewù nãdšiaṅ!
33Adſamaṅi fẽ le̱, nii akeo̱ame̱, ši bo le̱ oṅõo̱ onikēnii le̱ okeo̱ osuolo̱i fẽ, ni ohãa-ame̱ nyõṅnii, koni ame̱dše̱ hefẽhe ame̱ba oṅõ ye̱ odſamaṅbō̱i le̱ ahewo̱.
34Ni bo le̱, sŏro bo ni sŏro yei fẽ ye̱ odſamaṅbō̱i le̱ amli, ake̱-ní mokomoko enyiee ose̱ ke̱-bo̱o̱ adſamaṅ, ni asaṅ bo owoo̱ nyõmo̱, ši moko woo bo nyõmo̱, hewo̱ le̱ sŏro bo kwrā.
35Nohewo̱ le̱, adſamaṅ, bo Iehowa wiemo̱ toi!
36Bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Ake̱-ní ofo̱seo̱ otãṅtãṅnii le̱ oſieo̱ ši, ni odšieo̱ oyayaiaṅ ye̱ odſamaṅbō̱i le̱ amli ye̱ osuolo̱i le̱ ahĩe ke̱ onihĩnii awo̱dši le̱ ahĩe, asaṅ ye̱ obii le̱ ní oṅõ-hãame̱ le̱ alá hewo̱,
37nohewo le̱, na, mabua osuolo̱i le̱ fẽ ní oke̱ame̱ eſe̱ le̱ ke̱ mei fẽ ní osumoo̱ le̱ ke̱ mei fẽ ní onye̱o̱ le̱ hũ nā ke̱-kpe; ni mabua ame̱na mawo ohe ke̱-akpe, ni madšie oyayaiaṅ matšõame̱, ko-ni ame̱na oyayaiaṅ fẽ. Ier. 13,22. 26.
38Ni makodšoṍ tamo̱ akodšoo̱ yei gblãṅkũo̱lo̱i ke̱ lášiſielo̱i, ni mike̱ mlila ke̱ awuṅãyeli lá aaba ono̱!
39Ni masā maṅõo mawo ame̱deṅ, ni ame̱akũmo̱ okoii le̱, ní ame̱atšire̱ ohei groṅṅi le̱ ame̱atſia ši, ni ame̱akplo̱ ohe atadei hũ, ni ame̱aṅõ odſinei fe̱fe̱dši le̱, ni ame̱ašĩo yayai ke̱ ohe pasā.
40Ni asaṅ ame̱abo̱ gwa ame̱awo ohe, ni ame̱atſiao te̱i, ni ame̱ke̱ ame̱klantei aaflo̱ omli.
41Ni ame̱ke̱ la aašã ošĩai le̱, ni ame̱-akodšoö ye̱ yei babaō ahĩe; ni mahã ofo adſamaṅbō̱, ni owoṅ nyõmo̱ doṅṅ.
42Ni mahã *mimli ní ewoö la le̱ nā adšo̱, ni miwuṅãyeli le̱ aadše ono̱, ni mafe diṅṅ ni mimli fũṅ doṅṅ. *5,13.
43Ake̱-ni okaii oblayeiaṅ gbĩĩ le̱, ši moṅ oke̱ ene̱mei fẽ womi mlifũ hewo̱ le̱, na, mi hũ mahã ogbe̱ le̱ abua oyiteṅ, Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱, koni okabo̱ nyenyeṅtſi oši onihĩnii le̱ fẽ no̱.
44Na, mofẽmo ní bubuo̱ abe̱i le̱ aaba ne̱ke̱ abe̱ ne̱ ašio ake̱: “Bo̱ni nye le̱ yo̱ le̱, nakai ebiyō le̱ yo̱!”
45Onye ní enyãṅe ewù ke̱ ebii le̱ biyō dšio, ni enyemimeiyei ní enyãṅe ame̱wùmei ke̱ ame̱bii le̱ anyemiyõ dšio. *Nyenye le̱ Hityō ni, ni nyetše̱ le̱ Amornyo ni. *K. 3.
46Ni *onyemiyō nukpa dši Samaria ni ke̱ ebiyei le̱ hĩo̱ obe̱kugbe̱ le̱; ni onyemiyō gbekẽ ní hĩo̱ oninedšŭrõgbe̱ dši Sodom ke̱ ebiyei le̱. *23,4.
47Ši onyiee ame̱gbè̱i le̱ ano̱, ni ofee ame̱nihĩnii le̱; kẽle̱ eyee be ko, ni ofite fèame̱ ye̱ ogbè̱i fẽ mli.
48Gbĩĩabo̱ ní mihĩe kã ne̱, Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱: onyemiyō Sodom ke̱ ebiyei le̱ efee tamo̱ bo̱ni bo ke̱ obiyei le̱ fe le̱!
49Na, onyemiyō Sodom nišaianii ne̱: Hewō, niyenii fále̱ ke̱ hedšo̱le̱ šihile̱ yo̱ le̱ ke̱ ebiyei le̱ ahe, ši ewadšee ohĩaſo ke̱ moni efĩle̱ nidšiaṅ;
50ši moṅ ame̱wo ame̱he ni ame̱fe nihĩnii ye̱ mihĩe, ni beni mina le̱, mĩlōame̱ miſie. 1 Mose 18,20.
51Samaria hũ efee ohe ešai le̱ amli fã tete; ši ohã onihĩnii le̱ fá fèame̱, ni oke onihĩnii le̱ fẽ ní ofe le̱ ebu onyemimeiyei le̱ abem.
52Bo hũ tĕremo̱ bodientše̱ ohĩegbĕle le̱, ake̱-ní odamo̱ mli ohã onyemimeiyei le̱; ohe ešai ní dši nihĩnii ní ofe fèame̱ le̱ hewo̱ le̱ ame̱dša fèo. Bĕle̱ bo hũ ohĩe agbo, ni otĕre ohĩegbĕle le̱, ake̱-ní obu onyemimeiyei le̱ abem le̱!
53Ni makpale *ame̱nomṅō̃ le̱ ke̱-aba ekoṅ, Sodom ke̱ ebiyei le̱ anomṅō̃ le̱ ke̱ Samaria ke̱ ebiyei le̱ anomṅō̃ le̱, ni makpale onomi le anomṅō̃ le̱ ye̱ ame̱teṅ, *11,17.
54beni afe ní otĕre ohĩegbĕle le̱, ni ohĩe agbo ye̱ nii fẽ ní ofe le̱ hewo̱, ake̱-ní oše̱dše ame̱mī le̱.
55Ni onyemimeiyei ní dši Sodom ke̱ ebiyei le̱ aakũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-aba ame̱sá šihĩle̱ le̱ṅ, ni Samaria hũ ke̱ ebiyei le̱ aakũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-aba ame̱sá šihĩle̱ le̱ṅ, ni bo hũ oke̱ obiyei le̱ aakũ nyese̱ ke̱-aba nyesá šihĩle̱ le̱ṅ.
56Nto ohewō gbĩĩ le̱ amli le̱ onyemiyō Sodom le̱ tšṍ odāṅ lala,
57beni anáko adšie onõfõṅfemo̱ le̱ kpo, tamo̱ be mli ní Aram biyei le̱ ke̱ mei fẽ ní ebo̱lele̱ ke̱-kpe le̱ ke̱ Filistibii le̱ abiyei ní he tšẽo̱o le̱ bo̱o ahora ke̱-kpe le̱?
58Onyenyeṅtſibō̱ ke̱ onihĩnii le̱, bo otĕre, Iehowa kē̱.
59Edšake̱ bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Mafeo tamo̱ bo̱ni ofe le̱, ní ogbe kitã ní akã le̱ he guo, ni okũ kpãṅmo̱ le̱ mli le̱.
60Kẽle̱ mi le̱ *makai mikpãṅmo̱ le̱ ní mĩke̱o kpãṅ ye̱ †oblayeiaṅ gbĩĩ le̱ amli le̱, ni mate **nāno̱ kpãṅmo̱ ši mamã ši mahão! *3 Mose 26,45. †Hos 2,17. **37,26. Ier. 31,31-34.
61No le̱ *ookai ogbè̱i le̱, ni ohĩe aagbo, beni ooṅõ onyemimeiyei onukpai le̱ ofata onyemimeiyei gbekẽbii le̱ fẽ he, ni maṅōame̱ mahão ake̱ bĩyei le̱, ši dšee bodientše̱ okpãṅmo̱ nā. *20,43.
62Ni mahã mike̱o teṅ kpãṅmo̱ le̱ amã ši, ni ooná ole ake̱ midši Iehowa le̱,
63beni afe ní *okai ni ohĩe agbo, ni okatſa odāṅ doṅṅ ye̱ ohĩegbĕle le̱ hewo̱, beni mike̱ nii ní ofe le̱ fẽ efao le̱, Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱. *36,31-32.

english_text:
A Story about Two Eagles and a Vine
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel the following story, 3so they will understand what I am saying to them:
A large eagle with strong wings and beautiful feathers once flew to Lebanon. It broke the top branch off a cedar tree, 4then carried it to a nation of merchants and left it in one of their cities. 5The eagle also took a seed from Israel and planted it in a fertile field with plenty of water, like a willow tree beside a stream. 6The seed sprouted and grew into a grapevine that spread over the ground. It had lots of leaves and strong, deep roots, and its branches grew upward toward the eagle.
7There was another eagle with strong wings and thick feathers. The roots and branches of the grapevine soon turned toward this eagle, hoping it would bring water for the soil. 8But the vine was already growing in fertile soil, where there was plenty of water to produce healthy leaves and large grapes.
9Now tell me, Ezekiel, do you think this grapevine will live? Or will the first eagle pull it up by its roots and pluck off the grapes and let its new leaves die? The eagle could easily kill it without the help of a large and powerful army. 10The grapevine is strong and healthy, but as soon as the scorching desert wind blows, it will quickly wither.
The Lord Explains the Story
11The Lord said:
12 Ezekiel, ask the rebellious people of Israel if they know what this story means.
Tell them that the king of Babylonia came to Jerusalem, then he captured the king of Judah and his officials, and took them back to Babylon as prisoners. 13He chose someone from the family of Judah's king and signed a treaty with him, then made him swear to be loyal. He also led away other important citizens, 14so that the rest of the people of Judah would obey only him and never gain control of their own country again.
15But this new king of Judah later rebelled against Babylonia and sent officials to Egypt to get horses and troops. Will this king be successful in breaking the treaty with Babylonia? Or will he be punished for what he's done?
16As surely as I am the living Lord God, I swear that the king of Judah will die in Babylon, because he broke the treaty with the king of Babylonia, who appointed him king. 17Even the king of Egypt and his powerful army will be useless to Judah when the Babylonians attack and build towers and dirt ramps to destroy the cities of Judah and its people. 18The king of Judah broke his own promises and ignored the treaty with Babylonia. And so he will be punished!
19He made a promise in my name and swore to honor the treaty. And now that he has broken that promise, my name is disgraced. He must pay for what he's done. 20I will spread out a net to trap him. Then I will drag him to Babylon and see that he is punished for his unfaithfulness to me. 21His best troops will be killed in battle, and the survivors will be scattered in every direction. I, the Lord, have spoken.
22Someday, I, the Lord,
will cut a tender twig
from the top of a cedar tree,
then plant it on the peak
of Israel's tallest mountain,
23where it will grow
strong branches
and produce large fruit.
All kinds of birds will find
shelter under the tree,
and they will rest in the shade
of its branches.
24Every tree in the forest
will know that I, the Lord,
can bring down tall trees
and help short ones grow.
I dry up green trees
and make dry ones green.
I, the Lord, have spoken,
and I will keep my word.
translation_text:
1Ni Iehowa wiemo̱ ba miṅõ ake̱:
2Gbomobi, to ablõṅ, ni obu abe̱ otšõ Israel we le̱,
3ni okē̱: Bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Okropoṅ kpeteṅkple ko ke̱ efĩdši agboi ke̱ etše̱dši kakadãdši, ní ehe eyi to̱ ke̱ tše̱dši bibii ní mli yo̱ sãmãisãmãi, ba Lebanon ni ebakpo̱ tšenedru le̱ yiteṅ.
4Ekũ enidši fo̱bii le̱ ayiteṅ fo̱flo̱ō le̱, ni eṅõ-kõ enā ke̱-te *dšrayeli šikpoṅ ko no̱, eke̱-te eyate̱o ye̱ guo̱yelo̱i amaṅ ko mli. *16,29.
5Ni esã eṅõ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ nidũmo̱-nii le̱ eko, ni eke̱-te eyadũ ye̱ nidũmo̱-he ko; eṅõ-mã nu pī nā, ete̱ole̱ tamo̱ fānā-tšo ko.
6Ni ekwẽ ni etšõ *weintšo likpitī ní lē̱ ši, ni enidši le̱ dŏ̱ro̱ ke̱-ba eṅõgbe̱, ni ešišifãi le̱ ye̱ ešiši; ke̱ke̱ ni etšṍ weintšo, ni egblá nidsi, ni etšẽrẽ bāi. *19,10.
7Ši okropoṅ kpeteṅkple kroko hũ ye̱ ke̱ efĩdši kplei ke̱ etše̱dši pī; ni na, ne̱ke̱ weintšo ne̱ dŏ̱ro̱ ešišifãi le̱ ke̱-ba eṅõgbe̱, ni egblá enidšĩ le̱ ke̱-ba eṅõgbe̱, koni ehãle̱ nu ke̱-dše̱ eṅmõ le̱ṅ akofii le̱ amli.
8Šikpoṅ kpakpa no̱ ke̱ nu pī nā ate̱ole̱ ye̱, koni egblá nidši, ní ewo yibii, ní kũle̱ etšṍ weintšo fe̱fe̱o.
9Kē̱mo̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Aso eebi ehãle̱? Ani efãmo̱ṅ ešišifãi le̱, ni eflo eyibii le̱ eſie, koni eṅălã? Eyibāi fo̱bii le̱ fë aaṅălã, ni dšee ninešiwale̱ lo mei babaō aafãmo̱ ešišifãi le̱.
10Ni na, ní ate̱ole̱ ne̱, aso eehĩ ehãle̱? Ani ké̱ bokã kō̱yo̱ le̱ sa ehe le̱, dšee ṅălãmo̱ eeṅălã? eeṅălã ye̱ akofii ní ekwẽ ye̱ no̱ le̱ ano̱!
11Ni Iehowa wiemo̱ sā ba miṅõ ake̱:
12Kē̱mo̱ weku toigbolo̱i le̱ ake̱: Ani nyenua ene̱mei ašiší? Kē̱mo̱ ake̱: Na, *Babel maṅtše̱ le̱ ba Ierusalem, ni ebaṅõ emli maṅtše̱ le̱ ke̱ emli lume̱i le̱, ni ekpla-ame̱ eſie ese̱ ke̱-te Babel. *2 Maṅ. 21,10. 15.
13Ni *eṅõ maṅtše̱ sešibii le̱ eko, ni eke̱le̱ kpãṅ, ni ehã ekãle̱ kitã; ni eṅõ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ agboi le̱ ke̱-te, *2 Maṅ. 24,17.
14koni efe maṅtše̱yeli ní eba ši, ní ekawó ehe no̱, koni eto ekpãṅmo̱ le̱, ní edamo̱ ši.
15Ši kẽle̱ etše ehĩe atũa, ni etšũ ebo̱foi ke̱-te Mizraim, koni ahãle̱ okpo̱ṅo̱i ke̱ ta ní fá. Aso eehĩ ehãle̱? Aso moni feo ene̱mei ne̱, eedše mli? Aso eekũ kpãṅmo̱ le̱ṅ, ni eedše mli?
16Gbĩĩabo̱ ní mihĩe kã ne̱, Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱, le̱le̱ṅ, heni maṅtše̱ ní wole̱ maṅtše̱, ní egbe ekitã le̱ he guo, ní ekũ ekpãṅmo̱ le̱ mli le̱, yo̱ le̱, dše̱i noṅṅ eegbo ye̱, ye̱ eṅõ ye̱ Babel teṅ!
17Ni kē̱ ame̱tſa kpokui ni ame̱mãmo̱ mõdši, ní ake̱-kpãtã mei pī ahĩe le̱, Farao ke̱ eta kple le̱ ke̱ asafo babaō le̱ nyẽṅ he eko afe ahãle̱.
18Edšake̱ egbe kitã le̱ he guo̱ ke̱ kpãṅmo̱ le̱ mli ní ekũ le̱; ni na, eṅõ enine ehã, ni kẽle̱ efe ene̱mei fẽ; edšeṅ mli!
19Nohewo̱ le̱ bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Gbĩĩabo̱ ní mihĩe kã ne̱, mikitã le̱ ní egbe he guo̱ ke̱ mikpãṅmo̱ le̱ ní ekũ mli le̱, eyiteṅ kẽ maṅõ-bua;
20ni maṅõ *miyã le̱ malē̱ eno̱, ni eedũ mitšõne le̱, ni mike̱le̱ aate Babel tō̃, ni mike̱le̱ aayakodšo ye̱ dše̱i ye̱ mino̱ ní etõ le̱ hewo̱. *12,13.
21Ni etai le̱ fẽ mli foidšelo̱i le̱ fẽ le̱, ame̱anyõnyõi ye̱ klante nā, ni mei ní eſe̱ le̱ hũ, aagbe̱ame̱ aſã kō̱yo̱-fẽ-kō̱yo̱ mli, ní nyeaná nyele ake̱ mi, Iehowa, miwie le̱!
22Be̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Mi hũ makpo̱ tšenedru ní kwo̱ le̱ yiteṅ, ni mayate̱o; makũ *enidši fo̱bii le̱ ayiteṅ fo̱flo̱ō, ni mayate̱o ye̱ goṅ ní kwo̱ groṅṅ ko no̱; *Ies. 11,1; 53,2.
23Israel *goṅ ní kwo̱ le̱ no̱ mate̱o ye̱, ni eegbla nidši, ni eewo yibii, ni eetšṍ tšenedru fe̱fe̱o, ni †lofõdši sro̱toi fẽ aabahĩ ešiši; ame̱ahī efīdši ašiši hō̃ṅ le̱ mli. *20,40. †Dan. 4,12. Mat 13,32.
24Ni ṅãno̱ tšei le̱ fẽ aaná ale ake̱ mi, Iehowa, mihã *tšo ní kwo̱ le̱ eba ši, miwó tšo te̱ṅē̱ le̱ no̱ ke̱-te ṅwei, mi-hã tšo ṅmõṅ le̱ egbĩ, ni mihã tšo gbĩṅ le efeo. Mi, Iehowa, miwie ni mife. *21,31.

english_text:
Those Who Sin Will Die
1The Lord said:
2 Ezekiel, I hear the people of Israel using the old saying,
“Sour grapes eaten by parents
leave a sour taste in the mouths
of their children.”
3Now tell them that I am the Lord God, and as surely as I live, that saying will no longer be used in Israel. 4The lives of all people belong to me—parents as well as children. However, only those who sin will be put to death.
5Suppose there is a truly good man who always does what is fair and right. 6He refuses to eat meat sacrificed to foreign gods at local shrines or to worship Israel's idols. He doesn't have sex with someone else's wife or with a woman having her monthly period. 7He never cheats or robs anyone and always returns anything taken as security for a loan; he gives food and clothes to the poor 8and doesn't charge interest when lending money. He refuses to do anything evil; he is fair to everyone 9 and faithfully obeys my laws and teachings. This man is good, and I promise he will live.
10But suppose this good man has an evil son who is violent and commits sins 11his father never did. He eats meat at local shrines, has sex with someone else's wife, 12cheats the poor, and robs people. He keeps what is given to him as security for a loan. He worships idols, does disgusting things, 13and charges high interest when lending money. An evil man like that will certainly not live. He is the one who has done these horrible sins, so it's his own fault that he will be put to death.
14But suppose this evil man has a son who sees his father do these things and refuses to act like him. 15He doesn't eat meat at local shrines or worship Israel's idols, and he doesn't have sex with someone else's wife. 16He never cheats or robs anyone and doesn't even demand security for a loan. He gives food and clothes to the poor 17and refuses to do anything evil or to charge interest. And he obeys all my laws and teachings. Such a man will live. His own father sinned, but this good man will not be put to death for the sins of his father. 18It is his father who will die for cheating and robbing and doing evil.
19You may wonder why a son isn't punished for the sins of his father. It is because the son does what is right and obeys my laws. 20 Only those who sin will be put to death. Children won't suffer for the sins of their parents, and parents won't suffer for the sins of their children. Good people will be rewarded for what they do, and evil people will be punished for what they do.
21Suppose wicked people stop sinning and start obeying my laws and doing right. They won't be put to death. 22All their sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they did right. 23I, the Lord God, don't like to see wicked people die. I had much rather see them turn back from their sins and live.
24But when good people start sinning and doing disgusting things, will they live? No! All their good deeds will be forgotten, and they will be put to death because of their sins.
25You people of Israel accuse me of being unfair! But listen—I'm not unfair; you are! 26If good people start doing evil, they must be put to death, because they have sinned. 27And if wicked people start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment. 28They will think about what they've done and stop sinning, and so they won't be put to death. 29But you still say that I am unfair. You are the ones who have done wrong and are unfair!
30I will judge each of you for what you've done. So stop sinning, or else you will certainly be punished. 31Give up your evil ways and start thinking pure thoughts. And be faithful to me! Do you really want to be put to death for your sins? 32 I, the Lord God, don't want to see that happen to anyone. So stop sinning and live!
translation_text:
1Ni Iehowa wiemo̱ ba miṅõ ake̱:
2Té nyesuauo̱ tēṅ ní nyebuo̱ abe̱ ne̱ ye̱ Israel šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ake̱: *“Tše̱mei le̱ yeo̱ weinyibii ṅmlikitii, ni bii le̱ moṅ anyãnyõdši ſãa” le̱? *Ier. 31,29.
3Gbĩĩabo̱ ní mihĩe kã ne̱, Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱, nyebuṅ ne̱ke̱ abe̱ ne̱ ye̱ Israel doṅṅ!
4Na, susumai le̱ fẽ le̱, minii ni; bo̱ni tše̱ susuma dši minõ le̱, nakai noṅṅ bi susuma hũ dši minõ; susuma ní feo̱ eša le̱, le̱ noṅṅ eegbo!
5Moko dši dšalo̱, ni eyeo̱ dšale̱ sane ni efeo noni dša,
6ni eyee nii ye̱ gõdši le̱ ano̱, ni eholeo ehĩṅme̱ii ano̱ ekwe̱e̱ Israel we le̱ wo̱dši le̱, ni *ebulee enanyo ṅã, ni ebe̱ṅ-ke̱e̱ yō ni ete tšũi ase̱, *3 Mose 18,19. 20.
7ni *ewaa moko yi, ni †ekpaleo̱ nyõmo̱tše̱ awabatōnii ehãale̱, ehaa moko noko, eṅõo̱ ebolo ehãa moni hõmo̱ yeo̱-le̱, ni asaṅ heyayaiatše̱ le̱, ebuo̱le̱ mama, *Lal. 15,3. †5 Mose 24,10-13.
8*efaa nii ehee hekpa ní fè nine, ni ehee hebō̱, ni edšieo̱ enine ye̱ nõša-femo̱ he, ekodšoo̱ ano̱kwa kodšomo̱ ye̱ mo ke̱ mo teṅ, *2 Mose 22,25.
9enyieo̱ ye̱ mikpo̱i le̱ anā, ni eyeo̱ mimlai le̱ ano̱, ni eyeo̱ ano̱kwa le̱; le̱ le̱ dšalo̱ dšile̱, eyi aaná wala kẽ, Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱.
10Ši ke̱dši efo̱ bi yiwalo̱ ko ni ſieo̱ lá ši, ni efeo ne̱ke̱ nibii ne̱ ateṅ eko,
11ni efee nii [ní sa femo̱ ne̱] ateṅ eko eko, ši moṅ eyeo̱ nii ye̱ gõdši le̱ ano̱, ni ebuleo̱ enanyo ṅã,
12ewaã ohĩafo ke̱ moni efĩle̱ yi, ehaä nii, ekpalee awabatōnii ehãã, eholeo ehĩṅme̱ii ano̱ ekwe̱o̱ wo̱dši, esā efeo̱ nihĩnii,
13efaä nii eheo̱ hekpa ni fè nine, ni eheo̱ hebō̱ le̱: aso eyi aaná wala? Eyi náṅ wala! Ní efeo̱ ne̱ke̱ nihĩnii ne̱ fẽ hewo̱ le̱, gbo eegbo; elá le̱ aabua eyiteṅ!
14Ši na, ke̱dši efo̱ bi ko, ni le̱ le̱ ena etše̱ he ešai le̱ ní efe le̱ fẽ, ni eše gbeyei, ni efee nakai noko,
15eyee nii ye̱ gõdši le̱ ano̱, ni eholee ehĩṅme̱ii ano̱ ekwe̱e̱ Israel we le̱ wo̱dši le̱, ebulee enanyo ṅã hũ,
16ni ewaa mokomoko yi, ehee awabatōnii, ehaa nii, ši moṅ eṅõo̱ ebolo ehãa moni hõmo̱ yeo̱le̱, ni asaṅ heyayaiatše̱ le̱, ebuo̱le̱ mama,
17edšieo̱ enine ye̱ nõšafemo̱ he, ehee hekpa ní fè nine lo hebō̱, eyeo mimlai le̱ ano̱, ni enyieo̱ ye̱ mikpoi le̱ anā le̱: le̱ le̱ egboṅ ye̱ etše̱ nišaianii le̱ ahewo̱, ši moṅ eyi aaná wala kẽ.
18Etše̱ le̱, ake̱-ní ewaä yi, ni ehaä enyemi, ni efeo̱ noni ehĩĩ ye̱ emaṅ le̱ teṅ hewo̱ le̱, na, eegbo ye̱ enišaianii le̱ ahewo̱!
19Kẽle̱ nyekē̱o̱ ake̱: Mẽhewo̱ bi tĕree etše̱ nišaianii le̱? Ké̱ bi le̱ yeo̱ dšale̱ sane ni efeo̱ noni dša, ni eyeo mikpoi le̱ fẽ no̱ ni efeo̱ le̱, eyi aaná wala kẽ.
20*Susuma ní feo̱ eša le̱, le̱ noṅṅ eegbo. †Bi tĕreṅ etše̱ nišaianii, ni tše̱ hũ tĕreṅ ebi nišaianii; dšalo̱ le̱ dšale̱ le̱ ahĩ eno̱, ni mofõṅ nõfõṅ le̱ hũ aahĩ eno! *2 Mose 20,5. †4 Mose 26,11.
21Ni ke̱dši mofõṅ le̱ kpale ke̱-dše̱ ehe ešai ní efe le̱ fẽ mli, ni eye mikpo̱i le̱ fẽ no̱, ni eye dšale̱ sane, ni efe noni dša le̱, eyi aaná wala kẽ, egboṅ!
22Eno̱tõmo̱i ní etõ le̱ *akaiṅ eko eko ahãṅle̱ doṅṅ; eyi aaná wala ye̱ edšale̱nii ní efe le̱ hewo̱. *Ies. 43,25; 44,22.
23Aso mináa *mīše̱ ye̱ efõṅfelo̱ gbĕle hewo̱? Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱; ni dšee ake̱ ekpale ke̱-dše̱ egbe̱ le̱ no̱ ní eyi aná wala moṅ? *K. 32. Y. 33,11.
24Ši ké̱ dšalo̱ kpale ke̱-dše̱ edšale̱ le̱ mli ni efe nišaianii, ni efe nihĩnii fẽ ní mofõṅ feo̱ le̱: aso eyi aaná wala? Edšale̱nii fẽ ní efe le̱ akaiṅ eko eko; etõmo̱ ní etõ le̱ ke̱ ehe ešai ní efe le̱, eegbo ye̱ nomei ahewo̱! 3,20.
25Ni kẽle̱ nyekē̱o̱ ake̱: *Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ gbe̱ le̱ yee egbo̱! Nyeboa toi ko, nye Israel we: Ani migbe̱ le̱ yee egbo̱? ani dšee nye moṅ nyegbè̱i le̱ yee egbo? *33,17-20.
26Ké̱ dšalo̱ kpale ke̱-dše̱ edšale̱ le̱ mli ni eyafe nišaianii ní egbo ye̱ mli le̱: bĕle̱ egbo ye̱ enišaianii ní efe le̱ mli.
27Asaṅ ké̱ efõṅfelo̱ kpale ke̱-dše̱ enõfõṅ ní efe le̱ mli ni eye dšale̱ sane ni efe noni dša le̱: le̱ le̱ ehere esusuma yiwala.
28Edšake̱ eko̱ eyiṅ, ni ekpale ke̱-dše̱ etõmo̱i ní etõ le̱ fẽ mli: eyi aaná wala kẽ, egboṅ.
29Kẽle̱ Israel we le̱ kē̱o̱ ake̱: Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ gbe̱ le̱ yee egbo̱! Ani migbè̱i le̱ yee egbo̱, Israel we? ani dšee nye nyegbè̱i le̱ yee egbo̱?
30Nohewo̱ le̱ makodšonye, Israel we, mofẽmo ye̱ egbe̱i anā! Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱. *Nyekpalea ni nyetšṍmo̱a nyehe ke̱-dše̱a nyeno̱tõmo̱i le̱ fẽ mli, koni nišai-anii akafenye pãmpi! *33,11. Ies. 55,7.
31Nyeše̱re̱a nyeno̱tõmo̱i le̱ fẽ ní nyeke̱-tõ le̱ nyeſiea ke̱-dše̱a nyehe, ni nyefea *tšui hẽ ke̱ mumo̱ hē nyehãa nyehe! ši mẽba nyeagboi, Israel we? *36,26.
32Edšake̱ *mináá moni gboo̱ le̱ gbĕle he mīše̱, Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱. Nohewo̱ le̱ nyekpalea, ní nyeyi aná wala! *K. 23.

english_text:
A Funeral Song for Israel's Leaders
The Lord said:
1Ezekiel, sing a funeral song for two of Israel's leaders:
2Your mother was a brave lioness
who raised her cubs
among lions.
3She taught one of them to hunt,
and he learned to eat people.
4When the nations heard of him,
they trapped him in a pit,
then they used hooks
to drag him to Egypt.
5His mother waited
for him to return.
But soon she lost all hope
and raised another cub,
who also became fierce.
6He hunted with other lions
and learned to eat people.
7He destroyed fortresses
and ruined towns;
his mighty roar
terrified everyone.
8Nations plotted to kill him,
and people came from all over
to spread out a net
and catch him in a trap.
9They put him in a cage
and took him to Babylonia.
The lion was locked away,
so that his mighty roar
would never again be heard
on Israel's hills.
10Your mother was a vine like you,
growing near a stream.
There was plenty of water,
so she was filled with branches
and with lots of fruit.
11Her strong branches
became symbols of authority,
and she was taller
than all other trees—
everyone could see how strong
and healthy she was.
12But in anger, I pulled her up
by the roots
and threw her to the ground,
where the scorching desert wind
dried out her fruit.
Her strong branches wilted
and burned up.
13Then she was planted
in a hot, dry desert,
14where her stem caught fire,
and flames burned
her branches and fruit.
Not one strong branch is left;
she is stripped bare.
This funeral song must be sung with sorrow.
translation_text:
1Ni bo le̱, wó yāfó lala no̱ ohã Israel lume̱i le̱,
2ni okē̱ ake̱: Meni dši onye? Dšatayō ni; ebu dšatahĩĩ ateṅ, elè̱ ebii le̱ ye̱ dšatai oblahĩĩ ateṅ.
3Ni etšo̱se ebii le̱ ateṅ ekome; etšṍ dšata oblanyo ní ekase lōmõmo̱, eyeo̱ gbomei tete.
4Ni dšeṅmãdši le̱ banu ehe; adũle̱ ye̱ ame̱bu le̱ mli, ni ame̱ke̱ kpodši gblale̱ ke̱-te Mizraim šikpoṅ le no. 2 Maṅ. 23,30-34.
5Ni beni enye le̱ na ake̱ emẽ āhũ ni ehĩeno̱kãmo̱ elādše le̱, esā eṅõ ebii le̱ ateṅ ekroko efe dšata oblanyo.
6Ni beni eke̱ dšatai le̱ nyie āhũ le̱, etšṍ dšata oblanyo, ni ekase lōmõmo̱, eyeo̱ gbomei tete. 2 Maṅ. 24,8. 9.
7Ni efe ame̱teṅ yei pī okũlafoi, ni efe ame̱mãdši le̱ amaṅfõi, ni šikpoṅ le̱ ke̱ eno̱ nii le̱ ahe dšō ame̱he ye̱ ehū̃mo̱ le gbē̱mo̱ nā.
8Ke̱ke̱ ni dšeṅmãdši ní dše̱ šikpõdši le̱ ano̱ le̱ bagba wole̱ ke̱-kpe, ni ame̱ke̱ ame̱yā le̱ lē̱ eno̱, ni adũle̱ ye̱ ame̱bu le̱ṅ.
9Ni ame̱ke̱ kpodši gblale̱ ame̱wo koloi adeka mli, ni *ame̱ke̱le̱ yahã Babel maṅtše̱ le̱; ni ake̱le̱ to mõdši le̱ amli, beni afe ní akanu egbē ye̱ Israel gõdši le̱ ano̱ doṅṅ. *2 Maṅ. 24,15.
10Onye tamo̱ weintšo ye̱ olá le̱ṅ, ní ate̱ole̱ ye̱ nu he; ewo yibii ní egbla ni-dši ye̱ nu babaō le̱ hewo̱. 17,6.
11Ni ená tšei ní wa ní hĩ hã no̱yelo̱i amaṅtše̱tšei, ni awó ekwo̱le̱ le̱ no̱ ye̱ nidši kusukusui le̱ ateṅ, ni anale̱ ye̱ ekwo̱le̱ ke̱ enidši ní fá le̱ hewo̱.
12Ši afãle̱ ye̱ mlila nā aše̱le̱ afõ šikpoṅ, ni bokă kō̱yo̱ le̱ gbĩ eyibii le̱; akũmo̱ etšei ní wa le̱ ni *ame̱gbīgblĩ la sãame̱. *15,4.
13Ni agbe̱ne̱ le̱ ayate̱ole̱ ye̱ ṅãno̱, ye̱ šikpoṅ gbĩṅ ní nu be̱ no̱ le̱ no̱.
14Ni la dše̱ enidši le̱ amli tšei le̱ ateṅ, ni ešã eyibii le̱, ni tšo ní wa ní hĩ hã no̱yelo̱ maṅtše̱tšo be̱ no̱ doṅṅ. Yāfó lala dši ene̱, ni eetšṍ yāfó lala hũ.

english_text:
Israel Keeps On Rebelling
1Seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, some of Israel's leaders came to me on the tenth day of the fifth month. They sat down and asked for a message from the Lord. 2Just then, the Lord God said:
3Ezekiel, son of man, these leaders have come to find out what I want them to do. As surely as I live, I will not give them an answer of any kind.
4Are you willing to warn them, Ezekiel? Then remind them of the disgusting sins of their ancestors.
5 Tell them that long ago I, the Lord God, chose Israel to be my own. I appeared to their ancestors in Egypt and made a solemn promise that I would be their God and the God of their descendants. 6I swore that I would rescue them from Egypt and lead them to a land I had already chosen. This land was rich with milk and honey and was the most splendid land of all. 7I told them to get rid of their disgusting idols and not to sin by worshiping the gods of Egypt. I reminded them that I was the Lord their God, 8but they still rebelled against me. They refused to listen and kept on worshiping their idols and foreign gods.
In my anger, I decided to punish the Israelites in Egypt. 9But that would have made me look like a liar, because I had already promised in front of everyone that I would lead them out of Egypt. 10So I brought them out and led them into the desert. 11 I gave them my laws and teachings, so they would know how to live right. 12 And I commanded them to respect the Sabbath as a way of showing that they were holy and belonged to me. 13But the Israelites rebelled against me in the desert. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath like any other day.
Then in my anger, I decided to destroy the Israelites in the desert once and for all. 14But that would have disgraced me, because many other nations had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt. 15 Instead, I told them in the desert that I would not lead them into the beautiful, fertile land I had promised. 16I said this because they had not only ignored my laws and teachings, but had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped idols.
17Yet, I felt sorry for them and could not let them die in the desert. 18So I warned the children not to act like their parents or follow their evil ways or worship their idols. 19I reminded them that I was the Lord their God and that they should obey my laws and teachings. 20I told them to respect my Sabbath to show that they were my people and that I was the Lord their God. 21But the children also rebelled against me. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath as any other day.
I became angry and decided to punish them in the desert. 22But I did not. That would have disgraced me in front of the nations that had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt. 23 So I solemnly swore that I would scatter the people of Israel across the nations, 24because they had disobeyed my laws and ignored my teachings; they had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped the idols their ancestors had made. 25I gave them laws that bring punishment instead of life, 26and I let them offer me unacceptable sacrifices, including their first-born sons. I did this to horrify them and to let them know that I, the Lord, was punishing them.
27Ezekiel, tell the people of Israel that their ancestors also rejected and insulted me 28by offering sacrifices, incense, and wine to gods on every hill and under every large tree. I was very angry, because they did these things in the land I had given them! 29I asked them where they went to worship those gods, and they answered, “At the local shrines.” And those places of worship are still called shrines.
30Then ask the Israelites why they are following the example of their wicked ancestors 31by worshiping idols and by sacrificing their own children as offerings. They commit these sins and still think they can ask me for a message. As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will give them no answer. 32They may think they can be like other nations and get away with worshiping idols made of wood and stone. But that will never happen!
The Lord Promises To Restore Israel
The Lord said to the people of Israel:
33As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will rule over you with my powerful arm. You will feel my fierce anger 34and my power, when I gather you from the places where you are scattered 35and lead you into a desert surrounded by nations. I will meet you there face to face. Then I will pass judgment on you 36and punish you, just as I punished your ancestors in the desert near Egypt. 37I will force each of you to obey the regulations of our solemn agreement. 38I will separate the sinful rebels from the rest of you, and even though I will bring them from the nations where they live in exile, they won't be allowed to return to Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
39Go ahead and worship your idols for now, you Israelites, because soon I will no longer let you dishonor me by offering gifts to them. You will have no choice but to obey me! 40When that day comes, everyone in Israel will worship me on Mount Zion, my holy mountain in Jerusalem. I will once again call you my own, and I will accept your sacred offerings and sacrifices. 41When I bring you home from the places where you are now scattered, I will be pleased with you, just as I am pleased with the smell of the smoke from your sacrifices. Every nation on earth will see that I am holy, 42and you will know that I, the Lord, am the one who brought you back to Israel, the land I promised your ancestors. 43Then you will remember your wicked sins, and you will hate yourselves for doing such horrible things. They have made you unacceptable to me, 44so you deserve to be punished. But I will treat you in a way that will bring honor to my name, and you will know that I am the Lord God.
Fire from the South
45The Lord said, 46“Ezekiel, son of man, turn toward the south and warn the forests 47that I, the Lord God, will start a fire that will burn up every tree, whether green or dry. Nothing will be able to put out the blaze of that fire as it spreads to the north and burns everything in its path. 48Everyone will know that I started it, and that it cannot be stopped.”
49But I complained, “Lord God, I don't want to do that! People already say I confuse them with my messages.”
translation_text:
1Ni eba mli ake̱ afi ni dši kpawo le̱ no̱ nyõṅ ní dši enumo̱ le̱ no̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ nyoṅma le̱ no̱ le̱ Israel *onukpai le̱ ateṅ meikomei ba ame̱babi Iehowa nii, ni ame̱trá mihĩe. *14,1.
2Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehowa wiemo̱ ba miṅõ ake̱;
3Gbomobi, oke̱ Israel onukpai le̱ awie ni okē̱ame̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Ani mi nibimo̱ nyeba ne̱? Gbĩĩabo̱ ní mihĩe kã ne̱, mihãṅ abimi nii ahãnye. 14,8.
4Ani ookodšoame̱? ani ookodšo, gbomobi? Hã ame̱le ame̱tše̱mei le̱ anihĩnii le̱,
5ni okē̱ame̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Gbĩ ní mihala Israel, ni miwó minine no̱ mitšõ Iakob we le̱ seši le̱, ni mihã ame̱lemi ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni *miwó minine no̱ mitšõame̱ ake̱: Midši Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱! *2 Mose 6,7. 8.
6Obi le̱ miwó minine no̱ mitšõame̱, ni madšieame̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ke̱-ya šikpoṅ ní mitao mihãame̱ le̱ no̱, noni fufo̱ ke̱ wò boo̱ ye̱ no̱, ní dši šikpõdši le̱ ateṅ noni yo̱ fe̱o fè fẽ le̱.
7Ni mikē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyeteṅ *mofẽmo aše̱re̱ ehĩṅme̱ii anihĩnii le̱ aſie, ni nyeke̱ Mizraim wo̱dši le̱ akabulea nyehe! Midši Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱! *Ios. 24,14. 23.
8Ši ame̱tše mihĩe atũa, ni e̱me̱kplẽẽ-mi toibõ; ame̱teṅ mokomoko še̱re̱e̱ ehĩṅme̱ii anihĩnii le̱ eſiee̱, ni Mizraim wo̱dši le̱ hũ ame̱šĩĩ. Ke̱ke̱ ni mikē̱: Mafo̱se mimlila le̱ maſie ame̱no̱, ni maṅmẽ mimlifũ le̱ gbe̱ ke̱-ba ame̱no̱ ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ teṅ.
9Ši *kẽle̱ mitšu nii ye̱ migbe̱i le̱ hewo̱, koni akabulele̱ ye̱ dšeṅmãdši ní ame̱yo̱ ame̱teṅ le̱ ahĩe, mei ahĩe ní mi-hã ame̱lemi ye̱, beni midšieame̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no le̱. *36,21. 22. 2 Mose 32,12.
10Ni midšieame̱ ke̱-dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni mike̱ame̱ ba ṅã le̱ no̱;
11ni mike̱ mikpo̱i le̱ hãame̱, ni mi-hã ame̱le mimlai le̱, ni *ké̱ gbomo ye no̱ ní eyi aaná wala ye̱ mli le̱. *3 Mose 18,5.
12Asaṅ miṅõ mihedšō̱mo̱gbĩĩ le̱ mihã-ame̱, ní etšṍ *okadi ye̱ mike̱ame̱ teṅ, ní ame̱ná ame̱le ake̱ midši Iehowa ní feo̱-ame̱ kroṅkroṅ le̱. *2 Mose 31,13. 17.
13Ši Israel we le̱ tše mihĩe atũa ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱; ame̱nyiee ye̱ mikpo̱i le̱ anã, ni amegbe mimlai le̱ ahe guo̱, nii ní ké̱ gbomo ye no̱ ni eyi aaná wala ye̱ mli le̱, ni ame̱bule mihedšō̱mo̱gbĩĩ le̱ pī. Ke̱ke̱ ni mikē̱: Mafo̱se mimlila maſie ame̱-no̱ ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱, ní maplenēame̱.
14Ši kẽle̱ mitšu nii ye̱ migbe̱i le̱ hewo̱, koni akabulele̱ ye̱ dšeṅmãdši, mei ahĩe ní midšieame̱ ye̱ le̱, ahĩe. K. 9.
15Asaṅ *miwó minine no̱ mitšõame̱ ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱, ako̱ mike̱ame̱ eyaa šikpoṅ ní miṅõ-hãame̱ ní fufo̱ ke̱ wò hoo̱ ye̱ no̱ ní dši šikpõdši le̱ ateṅ noni yo̱ fe̱o fè fẽ le̱ no̱; *4 Mose 14,12.
16edšake̱ ame̱gbe mimlai le̱ ahe guo̱, ni ame̱nyiee ye̱ mikpo̱i le̱ anā, ni ame̱bule mihedšō̱mo̱gbĩĩ le̱; edšake̱ ame̱tšui nyie ame̱wo̱dši lo̱ ase̱.
17Kẽle̱ mihĩṅme̱ii naame̱ mo̱bo̱ ní mikpãtãã ame̱hĩe ni mitãã ame̱yi ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱.
18Ši mikē̱ ame̱bii le̱ ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ ake̱: Nyekanyiea ye̱ nyetše̱mei le̱ akpo̱i le̱ anā, ni nyekayea ame̱mlai le̱ ano̱, ni nyeke̱ ame̱wo̱dši le̱ akabulea nyehe!
19Midši Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱; nyenyiea ye̱ mikpo̱i le̱ moṅ anā, ni nyeyea mimlai le̱ ano̱ ni nyefea!
20Ni nyeyea mihedšō̱mo̱gbĩĩ le̱ kroṅkroṅ, ní ame̱tšṍmo̱ okadi ye̱ mike̱nye teṅ, koni nyená nyele ake̱ midsi Iehowa, nye-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱. K. 12.
21Ši bii le̱ hũ tše mihĩe atũa: ame̱nyiee ye̱ mikpo̱i le̱ anā, ni asaṅ ame̱yee mimlai le̱ ano̱ ni ame̱fe, nii ní ké̱ gbomo ye no̱ ní eyi aaná wala ye̱ mli le̱; ame̱bule mihedšō̱mo̱gbĩĩ le̱ hũ. Ke̱ke̱ ni mikē̱: Mafo̱se mimlila le̱ maſie ame̱no̱, ni maṅmẽ mimlifũ le̱ gbe̱ ke̱-ba ame̱no̱ ye̱ ṅã le̱ no̱.
22Kẽle̱ misu minine miwo mli, ni mitšu nii ye̱ migbe̱i le̱ hewo̱, koni akabulele̱ ye̱ dšeṅmãdši, mei ehĩe ni midšieame̱ ye̱ le̱, ahĩe. K. 9.
23Asaṅ miwó minine no̱ mitšõame̱ ye̱ ṅã le̱ ne̱, ake̱ matšire̱ ame̱yise̱ ke̱-ate dšeṅmãdši le̱ amli, ni magbe̱ame̱ maſã šikpõdši le̱ ano̱;
24edšake̱ ame̱yee mimlai le̱ ano̱, ši ame̱gbe mikpo̱i le̱ ahe guo̱, ni ame̱bule mihedšō̱mo̱gbĩĩ le̱, ni ame̱hĩe nyie ame̱tše̱mei awo̱dši le̱ ase̱.
25Nohewo̱ le̱ mi hũ mĩhãame̱ akpo̱i ní ehĩĩ ke̱ mlai ní ame̱yi náṅ wala ye̱ mli,
26ni mibuleame̱ ye̱ ame̱dientše̱ ame̱nikēnii le̱ amli, ake̱-ní *ame̱hãa nii fẽ ní gbleo̱ mũsũ nā le̱ tšṍo̱ la mli le̱, ko-ni mafeame̱ ſe̱m, ní ame̱ná ame̱le ake̱ midši Iehowa le̱. *K. 31. 2 Kron. 33,6.
27Nohewo̱ lo̱, gbomobi, oke̱ Israel we le̱ awie, ni okē̱ame̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Ene̱ mli hũ nyetše̱mei le̱ bo̱ musu šimi ye̱, ake̱-ní ame̱tõ mino̱ le̱.
28Edšake̱ beni mike̱ame̱ ba šikpoṅ ní miwó minine no̱ ake̱ maṅõ-hãame̱ le̱ no̱ le̱, goṅkpo̱-fẽ-goṅkpo̱ ní kwo̱ lo tšo kusũ-fẽ-tšo kusū ní ame̱ana le̱, ame̱yašãa ame̱gbē-afo̱lei le̱ ye̱ dše̱i, ni ame̱ke̱ ame̱mlilawō nikēnii le̱ yakeo̱ ye̱ dše̱i; dše̱i noṅṅ ame̱hãa ame̱tšofãi le̱ dšeo̱ ṅma ye̱, ni ame̱yeo̱ ame̱ṅkpai ye̱ dše̱i.
29Ni mikē̱ame̱ ake̱: He groṅṅ le̱ ní nyeyaä le̱, té ešišiṅ? Ši atšé̱o̱ dše̱i ake̱ he groṅṅ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱.
30Nohewo̱ le̱ kē̱mo̱ Israel we le̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ no̱: Aso nyeabule nyehe bo̱ni nyetše̱mei le̱ fe le̱, ni nyeabo adſamaṅ ke̱-nyie ame̱nihĩnii le̱ ase̱?
31Ní nyeke̱ nyenikēnii le̱ yahãa, ní nyehãa *nyebii tšṍo̱ la mli ne̱, nyemībule nyehe ye̱ nyewo̱dši le̱ fẽ hewo̱ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱, ni mahã ebimi nii ahãnye, Israel we? Gbĩĩabo̱ ní mihĩe kã ne̱, Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱, mihãṅ abimi nii ahãnye! *K. 26. 2 Maṅ. 16,3; 17,17.
32Noni baä nyedſẽṅmo̱ mli le̱, baṅ mli kwrā, ní nyekē̱o̱ ake̱: “Wo̱o̱tamo̱ dšeṅmãdši le̱, tamo̱ šikpõdši le̱ ano̱ wekui le̱, ní wo̱súmo̱ tšo ke̱ te̱” le̱.
33Gbĩĩabo̱ ní mihĩe kã ne̱, Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱, ninešiwale̱ ke̱ nine ní akpa mli ke̱ mlila ní afo̱se aſie ši mike̱-aye nyeno̱ maṅtše̱.
34Ni madšienye ke̱-adše̱ mãdšimãdši le̱ ateṅ, ni mabua nyenā ke̱-adše̱ šíkpõdši ní agbenye aſã no̱ le̱ ano̱, ke̱ ninešiwale̱ ke̱ nine ní akpa mli ke̱ mlila ní afo̱se aſie ši,
35ni mike̱nye aaba mãdšimãdši le̱ *aṅã le̱ no̱, ni mike̱nye aabakodšo ye̱ dše̱i hĩe ke̱ hĩe. *Hos. 2,16.
36Bo̱ni mike̱ nyetše̱mei le̱ kodšo ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ le̱, nakai mike̱nye aakodšo. Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱. 3 Mose 14,22. 23,
37Ni mahã nyetšṍ tšo le̱ šiši, ni mike̱nye aawo kpãṅmo̱ le̱ kpã le̱ mli.
38Ni madšie atũatšelo̱i le̱ ke̱ mei ní etõ mino̱ lo̱ ke̱-adše̱ nyeteṅ; madšieame̱ ke̱-adše̱ ame̱gbo̱tō šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ moṅ, ši ame̱baṅ Israel šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ni nyeaná nyele ake midši Iehowa le̱.
39Ši nye, Israel we, bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Nyeyaä ní nyeteṅ mofẽmo ayasúmo̱ ewo̱dši le̱; ši ké̱ fe se̱ le̱, nyeabomi toi kẽ, ni nyeke̱ nyenikē-nii ke̱ nyewo̱dši le̱ buleṅ migbe̱i kroṅkroṅ le̱ doṅṅ.
40Ši migoṅ kroṅkroṅ le̱ *ní dši Israel goṅ ní kwo̱ le̱ no̱ le̱, Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱, dše̱i Israel we le̱ fẽ, ame̱fẽ-kwa ní ame̱-yo̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱, ame̱abasúmo̱mi ye̱: maná ame̱he tšui ye̱ dše̱i, ni dše̱i noṅṅ mabi nyeno̱wómo̱-nikēnii ke̱ nyenikēnii le̱ amli kleṅkleṅnii le̱ ke̱ nyenii kroṅkroṅi le̱ fẽ ši ye̱. *17,23.
41Maná nyehe tšui tamo̱ noko ní dšeo̱ ṅma dšogbāṅ, beni midšienye ke̱-dše̱ mãdšimãdši le̱ amli, ni mibua nye-nā ke̱-dše̱ šikpõdši ní agbe̱nye aſā no̱ le̱ ano̱ le̱, ni mihã afemi kroṅkroṅ ye̱ nyemli ye̱ dšeṅmãdšimãdši le̱ ahĩe le̱.
42Ni nyeaná nyele ake̱ midši Iehowa le̱, beni mike̱nye eba Israel šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, šikpoṅ le̱ ní miwó minine no̱ ye̱ hewo̱ ake̱ maṅõ-hã nyetše̱mei le̱ no̱ le̱.
43Ni nyeakai nyegbè̱i ke̱ nyenifemo̱-nii fẽ ní nyeke̱-bule nyehe le̱ ye̱ dše̱i, ni nyedientše̱ nyehe aafenye nyãṅemo̱ ye̱ nyenifõdšianii fẽ ní nyefe le̱ hewo̱. 36,31. 32.
44Ni nyeaná nyele ake̱ midši Iehowa le̱, beni mike̱nye eye ye̱ migbe̱i le̱ hewo̱, dšee nyegbè̱i fõdši le̱ anā, lo nyeniſemo̱nii ní efite le̱ anā, nye, Israel we! Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱.

english_text:
The Lord Will Punish Jerusalem
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the places in Jerusalem where people worship. Warn everyone in Israel 3that I am about to punish them. I will pull out my sword and have it ready to kill everyone, whether good or evil. 4From south to north, people will die, 5knowing that my sword will never be put away.
6Ezekiel, groan in sorrow and despair so that everyone can hear you. 7When they ask why you are groaning, tell them you have terrifying news that will make them faint and tremble in fear and lose all courage. These things will happen soon. I, the Lord God, make this promise!
A Sword Is Ready To Attack Israel
8The Lord said:
9-10Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Jerusalem:
I have sharpened my sword
to slaughter you;
it is shiny and will flash
like lightning!
Don't celebrate—
punishment is coming,
because everyone has ignored
my warnings.
11My sword has been polished;
it's sharp and ready to kill.
12Groan in sorrow, Ezekiel;
the sword is drawn against
my people and their leaders.
They will die!
So give up all hope.
13I am testing my people,
and they can do nothing
to stop me.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
14Ezekiel, warn my people,
then celebrate my victory
by clapping your hands.
My vicious sword will attack
again and again,
killing my people
with every stroke.
15They will lose all courage
and stumble with fear.
My slaughtering sword
is waiting at every gate,
flashing and ready to kill.
16It will slash right and left,
wherever the blade is pointed.
17Then I will stop being angry,
and I will clap my hands
in victory.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The King of Babylonia and His Sword
18The Lord said:
19Ezekiel, son of man, mark two roads for the king of Babylonia to follow when he comes with his sword. The roads will begin at the same place, but be sure to put up a signpost where the two roads separate and go in different directions. 20Clearly mark where the two roads lead. One goes to Rabbah, the capital of Ammon, and the other goes to Jerusalem, the fortified capital of Judah. 21When the Babylonian king stands at that signpost, he will decide which way to go by shaking his arrows, by asking his idols, and by carefully looking at the liver of a sacrificed animal. 22His right hand will pull out the arrow marked “Jerusalem.” Then he will immediately give the signal to shout the battle cry, to build dirt ramps up to the top of the city walls, to break down its walls and gates with large wooden poles, and to kill the people. 23Everyone in Jerusalem had promised to be loyal to Babylonia, and so none of them will believe that this could happen to them. But Babylonia's king will remind them of their sinful ways and warn them of their coming captivity.
24Ezekiel, tell the people of Jerusalem and their ruler that I, the Lord God, am saying:
Everything you do is wicked and shows how sinful you are. You are guilty and will be taken away as prisoners.
25And now, you evil and wicked ruler of Israel, your day of final punishment is almost here. 26I, the Lord God, command you to take off your royal turban and your crown, because everything will be different. Those who had no power will be put in charge, and those who now rule will become nobodies. 27I will leave Jerusalem in complete ruins like no one has ever seen until my chosen one comes to punish this city.
Judgment against Ammon
28 The Lord God said:
Ezekiel, son of man, the Ammonites have insulted Israel, so condemn them and tell them I am saying:
A sword is drawn,
ready to slaughter;
it is polished and prepared
to kill as fast as lightning.
29You wicked Ammonites see false visions and believe untrue messages. But your day of punishment is coming soon, and my sword will slaughter you!
30Your days to punish others are over, so put your swords away. You will be punished in the land of your birth. 31My furious anger will scorch you like fire, and I will hand you over to cruel men who are experts in killing. 32You will be burned and will die in your own land. Then you will be forgotten forever. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
1[Y. 20,45.] Ni Iehowa wiemo̱ ba miṅõ ake̱:
2[46.] Gbomobi, tšṍ ohĩe ohã wuoyigbe̱, ni ošie̱ otšṍ wuoyigbe̱, ni ogba oši ṅã le̱ no̱ kō ní yo̱ wuoyigbe̱ le̱,
3[47.] ni okē̱ wuoyigbe̱ kō le̱ ake̱: Bo Iehowa wiemo̱ toi! Bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Na, mibaše̱re la ye̱ omli, ni eešã omli tšo ṅmõṅ-fẽ-tšo ṅmõṅ ke̱ tšo gbĩṅ-fẽ-tšo gbĩṅ. Lalilei ní tšoo̱ plamplam le̱ agbeṅ, ni eešã hĩeaṅ fẽ ke̱-dše̱ wuoyigbe̱ āhũ ke̱-yaši kōyigbe̱ tō̃.
4[48.] Ni helo fẽ aana ake̱ mi, Iehowa, miše̱re; anyẽṅ agbe.
5[49.] Ke̱ke̱ ni mikē̱: Ao, Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa! ame̱kē̱o̱ ye̱ mihe ake̱: Ani dšee abe̱i so̱ṅṅ ebuo̱?
6[1.] Ke̱ke̱ ni Iehowa wiemo̱ ba miṅõ ake̱:
7[2.] Gbomobi, tšṍ ohĩe ohã Ierusalem, ni ošie̱ otšõ hei kroṅkroṅi le̱, ni ogba oši Israel šikpoṅ le̱,
8[3.] ni okē̱ Israel šikpoṅ le̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Na, mike̱o ená, ni magbla miklante le̱ ke̱-adše̱ ehebo le̱ṅ, ni maflo̱ dšalo̱ ko̱ mofõṅ ke̱-adšo̱ ono̱ maše̱re̱ maſie!
9[4] Ake̱-ní mibaflo̱ dšalo̱ ke̱ mofõṅ ke̱-adše̱ ono̱ maše̱re̱ mafie hewo̱ le̱, miklante le̱ aadše kpo ke̱-adše̱ ehebo le̱ṅ awo helo fiā ke̱-dše̱ wuoyigbe̱ āhũ ke̱-yaši kōyigbe̱ tō̃.
10[5.] Ni helo fẽ aaná ale ake̱ mi, Iehowa, migbla miklante le̱ ke̱-dše̱ ehebo le̱ṅ; ekũṅ ese̱ eyaṅ mli doṅṅ.
11[6.] Nohewo̱ lo̱ bo, gbomobi, dõmo̱ ntšo̱i ye̱ ohe̱ ní ekũ le̱ hewo̱, ni odõmo̱ ntšo̱i wā yo̱ ame̱hĩe!
12[7.] Ni aaba mli ake̱, ké̱ ame̱bio ake̱: Mẽhewo̱ po odõmoo̱ ntšo̱i? le̱, okē̱ ake̱: Adafitſā le̱ hewo̱ṅ; edšake̱ ēba, ni tšui-fẽ-tšui aafã, ni nidšiaṅ fẽ aadše wui, ni mnmo̱-fẽ-mumo̱ afe vī̃, ni nakutšei fẽ-tſẽm aasĕre tamo̱ nu. Na, ēba, ni ebaba mli! Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱.
13[8.] Ni Iehowa wiemo̱ sā ba miṅõ ake̱:
14[9.] Gbomobi, gba ní okē̱: Bo̱ni Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Kē̱mo̱ ake̱: *Klante, klante, adšo̱ nā, ni aša he kãṅkãṅ! *32,20.
15[10.] Adšo̱ nā, beni afe ní ake̱-gbe gbē ní mli wa; aša he kãṅkãṅ, beni afe ní ekpe̱ tamo̱ srawa. Aso wo̱mli afliwo̱? Mibinū le̱ tšo le̱ gbeo̱ tšo-fẽ-tšo he guo̱.
16[11.] Ni aṅõ-hã ní aša he, koni awo hĩemo̱; adšo̱ klante ne̱ nā, ni asaṅ aša he, koni ake̱-wo mogbelo̱ le̱ deṅ.
17[12.] Blo̱mo̱ ní owo lele, gbomobi; edšake̱ ene̱ baha mimaṅ le̱ no̱, ene̱ baba Israel lume̱i le̱ fẽ no̱! Aṅõame̱ ke̱ mimaṅ le̱ ahã klante; nohewo̱ le̱ tſiamo̱ oſuo̱ he mãi!
18[13] Edšake̱ aka akwe̱; ni ké̱ tšo ní gbeo̱ he guo̱ le̱ tete nyẽẽ noko atšu le̱, meni ebafe? Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱. Ies. 1,5.
19[14.] Nohewo̱ le̱, bo gbomobi, gba ni otſa odẽ: ní akũ klante le̱ ní dši mogbẽ klante le̱ abo̱ he toi etẽ; mogbē klante kpeteṅkple ní ebo̱leame̱ ke̱-kpe le̱ ni.
20[15.] Beni afe ní ame̱tšui afã ni mei ní enyōnyõi le̱ afá pī hewo̱ le̱ mitšõ klante le̱ nā mihã ame̱gbói le̱ fẽ. Ao, ahã ekpe̱ tamo̱ srawa, adšo̱ nā ahã mogbē!
21[16.] Tšṍ ohe ke̱-ya ninedšŭrõgbe̱, ni oya abe̱kugbe̱ le̱ hũ, hefẽhe ní ohĩe aatua!
22[17.] Ni mi hũ matſa midẽ, ni maṅmẽ mimlila le̱ gbe̱; mi, Iehowa, miwie!
23[18.] Ni Iehowa wiemo̱ ba miṅõ ake̱:
24[19.] Asaṅ bo, gbomobi, *to gbè̱i enyo̱ ohã ohe, ní Babel maṅtše̱ le̱ klante le̱ atšṍ no̱ ke̱-ba; enyo̱ le̱ fẽ adše̱ šikpoṅ kome no̱ ke̱-ba. Ni oto gbe̱tšõmo̱nii ye̱ maṅ le̱ ṅmaṅmaša. *4,1.
25[20.] To gbe̱ ko ní klante le̱ atšṍ no̱ ke̱-ya Raba ní dši Amonbii le̱ amaṅ le̱, ke̱ Iuda ke̱-bote Ierusalem ní atſa gbogbo awo he le̱.
26[21.] Edšake̱ Babel maṅtše̱ le̱ aaba-damo̱ gbe̱nta le̱ no̱, yo̱ gbè̱i enyo̱ le̱ ašiši-dšēhe le̱, koni ekla; ni eehoso gãimlibii le̱, ni eebi amãgãi le̱ anii, ni eekwe̱ mle̱bo mli.
27[22.] Klamo̱ le̱ tšṍ ninedšŭrõgbe̱ ke̱-te Ierusalem, koni aṅõ gbogbokū̃mo̱-nii ato dše̱i, ni agble dāṅ ke̱ blo̱mo̱, ni awó gbē no̱ ke̱ ošebō̱, ni aṅõ gbogbo-kū̃mo̱nii ato agbói le̱ ahe, ni atſa kpokui, ni amãmo̱ mõdši.
28[23.] Ši eetšṍ tamo̱ yaka klamo̱ ehãame̱ ye̱ ame̱hĩe, tše̱ ame̱kãmo̱kãmo̱ kitãi ame̱tšōame̱; ši eekai ame̱nõša le̱, koni amõmo̱ame̱.
29[24.] Nohewo̱ le̱ be̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Ake̱-ní nyehã akai nyenišaianii le̱, ni adšie nyenifõdšianii le̱ akpo, ni nyehe ešai le̱ edše kpo ye̱ nyenifemo̱nii fẽ mli, — ake̱-ní akainye he-wo̱ le̱, ake̱ nine amõmo̱nye.
30[25.] Ni bo mofõṅ ní sa gbĕle, Israel lumo̱ ní egbĩ eše̱ ye̱ nāgbē nõša be le̱ mli:
31[26.] Be̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Adšie *fai le̱, ni akpo̱ akekre le̱! Ene̱ ehĩṅ bo̱ni eyo̱ le̱ doṅṅ; †noni eba ši le̱, aawó no̱, ni noni awó no̱ le̱, aabale̱ ši! *2 Mose 28,4. †Ezek. 17,24. Luk. 18,14.
32[27.] Butumo̱, butumo̱, butumo̱ mabutule̱; ni ene̱ hũ ehĩṅ ši ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni *mo gbe̱nā ní dši le̱ aaba, ni maṅõ-hãle̱! *1 Mose 49,10.
33[28.] Ši bo, gbomobi, gba ní okē̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ye̱ *Amonbii le̱ ke̱ ame̱horabō̱ le̱ hewo̱ ne̱; ni okē̱: Klante, klante le̱ agbla ahã gbē, aša he kãṅkãṅ ní egbe mei, ní ekpe̱ tamo̱ srawa, *25,2-7.
34[29.] beni ame̱naä yakanii ame̱hãao, ni ame̱klaä amale klamo̱i ame̱hãao, koni aṅõo afõ meifōdši ní enyõnyõi le̱ akue̱i ano̱, mei ní ame̱gbĩ le̱ eše̱ momo ye̱ nāgbẽ nõša be le̱ mli le̱.
35[30.] Oke̱-kũ se̱ owo ehebo le̱ṅ! Heni abo̱o ye̱ le̱, šikpoṅ ní odše̱ no̱ le̱ no̱ makodšoö ye̱.
36[31.] Ni mafo̱se mimlila le̱ maſie ono̱, ni mafli mimlifũ la le̱ṅ mawoö, ni madšieo mawo hĩĩ dikalo̱i ní le fitemo̱ he ṅã le̱ adeṅ.
37[32.] Ootšṍ lai ohã la; olá le̱ aaſie šikpoṅ le̱ teṅ; akaiṅo doṅṅ; edšake̱ mi, Iehowa mikē̱!

english_text:
Jerusalem Is Condemned
1Some time later, the Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, are you ready to condemn Jerusalem? That city is filled with murderers, so remind the people of their sins 3and tell them I am saying:
Jerusalem, you have murdered many of your own people and have worshiped idols. You will soon be punished! 4Those crimes have made you guilty, and the idols have made you unacceptable to me. So your final punishment is near. Other nations will laugh at you and make insulting remarks, 5and people far and near will make fun of your misery.
6Your own leaders use their power to murder. 7 None of you honor your parents, and you cheat foreigners, orphans, and widows. 8 You show no respect for my sacred places and treat the Sabbath just like any other day. 9Some of your own people tell lies, so that others will be put to death. Some of you eat meat sacrificed to idols at local shrines, and others never stop doing vulgar things. 10 Men have sex with their father's wife or with women who are having their monthly period 11or with someone else's wife. Some men even sleep with their own daughter-in-law or half sister. 12 Others of you accept money to murder someone. Your own people charge high interest when making a loan to other Israelites, and they get rich by cheating. Worst of all, you have forgotten me, the Lord God.
13I will shake my fist in anger at your violent crimes. 14When I'm finished with you, your courage will disappear, and you will be so weak that you won't be able to lift your hands. I, the Lord, have spoken and will not change my mind. 15I will scatter you throughout every nation on earth and put a stop to your sinful ways. 16You will be humiliated in the eyes of other nations. Then you will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things.
Jerusalem Must Be Purified
17The Lord said:
18Ezekiel, son of man, I consider the people of Israel as worthless as the leftover metal in a furnace after silver has been purified. 19So I am going to bring them together in Jerusalem. 20-21I will be like a metalworker who collects that metal from the furnace and melts it down. I will collect the Israelites and blow on them with my fiery anger. They will melt inside the city of Jerusalem 22like silver in a furnace. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them in my anger.
Everyone in Jerusalem Is Guilty
23The Lord said:
24Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel that their country is full of sin, and that I, the Lord, am furious! 25Their leaders are like roaring lions, tearing apart their victims. They put people to death, then steal everything of value. Husbands are killed, and many women are left as widows.
26 The priests of Israel ignore my Law! Not only do they refuse to respect any of my sacred things, but they don't even teach the difference between what is sacred and what is ordinary or between what is clean and what is unclean. They treat my Sabbath like any other day, and so my own people no longer honor me.
27Israel's officials are like ferocious wolves, ripping their victims apart. They make a dishonest living by injuring and killing people.
28And then the prophets in Israel cover up these sins by giving false visions. I have never spoken to them, but they lie and say they have a message from me. 29The people themselves cheat and rob; they abuse the poor and take advantage of foreigners.
30I looked for someone to defend the city and to protect it from my anger, as well as to stop me from destroying it. But I found no one. 31So in my fierce anger, I will punish the Israelites for what they have done, and they will know that I am furious. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
1Ni Iehowa wiemo̱ ba miṅõ ake̱:
2Ni bo, gbomobi, ani ookodšo, ani ookodšo *lášiſiemo̱ maṅ le̱? Bĕle̱ hã ele enihĩnii le̱ fẽ, *24,6.
3ni okē̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Bo maṅ ní oſieo̱ lá ši ye̱ omli, koni obe aše̱, ni ofeo̱ wo̱dši ohãa ohe ní oke̱-bule ohe!
4Olá ní ofo̱se oſie ši le̱ hewo̱ le̱ otĕre sõ, ni owo̱dši ní ofe le̱ oke̱-bule ohe; ni ohã ogbĩĩ le̱ ebe̱ṅke̱, ni oše̱ ofii le̱ amli; nohewo̱ le̱ miṅõo mife ahorabō̱ mihã dšeṅmãdši le̱ ke̱ hefe̱oyeli mihã šikpõdši le̱ fẽ.
5Mei ní be̱ṅke̱o ke̱ mei ní ke̱o teṅ dšeke̱ le̱ aaye ohe fe̱o, bo moni abule ogbe̱i ní hōfemo̱ eyi omli obõ.
6Na, Israel lume̱i le̱, ame̱teṅ rnofẽmo ſieo̱ lá ši ye̱ omli bo̱ni eenyẽ.
7Abuu tše̱ ke̱ nye ye̱ omli, ayeo̱ gbo̱ amim ye̱ omli, ni awaä awusã ke̱ yō okũlafo yi ye̱ omli. 2 Mose 22,21. 22.
8Ogbeo̱ minii kroṅkroṅi le̱ ahe guo̱, ni obuleo̱ mihedšō̱mo̱gbĩĩ le̱.
9Hĩĩ ošekuyelo̱i ye̱ omli, beni afe ní aſie lá ši, ni ayeo̱ nii ye̱ gõdši le̱ ano̱ ye̱ omli; abo̱ö̱ nyenyeṅtſĩ ye̱ omli.
10Adšieo̱ tše̱ yayaiaṅ kpo ye̱ omli; moni ete tšũi ase̱ ní ehe tšee le̱, atuaäle̱ ye̱ omli. 3 Mose 18,7. 19.
11Mo ke̱ enanyo ṅã feo̱ nihĩnii; moko hũ buleo̱ ešayō ye̱ nyenyeṅtſibō̱ mli, ni mokroko hũ tuaä enyemiyō ní dši etše̱ bi ye omli. 3 Mose 18,9. 15. 20.
12Aheo̱ nyōṅnii ye̱ omli, beni afe ní aſie lá ši; *oheo̱ hekpa ní fè nine ke̱ hebō̱; oyeo̱ onanyo se̱ ke̱ amimyeli, ni mi le̱ ohĩe ekpa mino̱, Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱. *2 Mose 22,25.
13Na, mitſa midẽ ye̱ se̱ ní oyeo̱ ke̱ lá ní eſie ši ye̱ omli le̱ hewo̱.
14Aso gbĩ ní mike̱o aaye le̱ otšui aanyẽ mli amõ, alo onidši amli aawa? Mi, Iehowa, miwie, ni mafe hũ.
15Ni matši oyise̱ ke̱-ate dšeṅmãdši le̱ amli, ni magbeo maſã šikpõdši le̱ ano̱, ni mahã ohemũdši le̱ atã ye̱ ohe;
16ni aabuleo ye̱ dšeṅmãdši le̱ ahĩe, ni ooná ole ake̱ midši Iehowa le̱.
17Ni Iehowa wiemo̱ sā ba miṅõ ake̱:
18Gbomobi, Israel we le̱ etšṍ šĩkafei ehãmi; ame̱ fẽ le̱, akō̱ble ke̱ sãnyā̃ ke̱ dade ke̱ sumui ní yo̱ seremo̱ flõnõ mli dšiame̱; ame̱tšṍmo̱ dſie̱te̱ifei. Ies 1,22. Ier. 6,28.
19Nohewo̱ le̱ bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Ake̱-ní nyeblublu nyetšṍmo̱ šikafei hewo̱ le̱, na, mabua nyenā mawo Ierusalem.
20Take̱ bo̱ni abuaä dſie̱te̱i ke̱ akō̱ble ke̱ dade ke̱ sumui ke̱ sãnyā̃ nā awoo seremo̱ flõnõ mli, ni ahūo̱ la awoo̱ he ni esĕreo̱ le̱, nakai mabua nyenā ye̱ mimlifũ ke̱ mlila le̱ṅ, ni mike̱nye aawo mli ni masĕrenye.
21Ni mabua nyenã, ni mahū mimlifũ la le̱ mawo nyehe ní nyesĕre ye̱ mli!
22Bo̱ni asĕreo̱ dſie̱te̱i ye̱ flõnõ mli le̱, nakai noṅṅ kẽ aasĕrenye ye̱ mli, ni nye-aná nyele ake̱ mi, Iehowa, mifo̱se mimlila le̱ miſie nyeno̱ le̱.
23Ni Iehowa wiemo̱ sā ba miṅõ ake̱:
24Gbomobi, kē̱mo̱le̱ ake̱: Bo dši šikpoṅ ko ní nu ſãṅ no̱, ni nyoṅmo̱ ene̱ṅ no̱ ye̱ mlifũ be le̱ṅ.
25Egbalo̱i ní yo̱ no̱ le̱ ete apãm; ame̱tamo̱ dšata ní hū̃o̱ ni tšere̱o̱ emĩle̱lo; *ame̱yeo̱ susumai; †ame̱ṅõo̱ dſetri ke̱ nii ní dšra wa; ame̱hã eyei okũlafoi le̱ efá ye̱ eno̱. *34,3. 8. Lal. 14,4. †Mat. 23,14.
26*Eso̱foi le̱ tšṍo̱ mimla le̱ hĩe ame̱buo̱ ši, ni ame̱buleo̱ minii kroṅkroṅi le̱; ame̱fee sro̱to ye̱ †nõ kroṅkroṅ ke̱ noni abule teṅ, ame̱tšõõ mei sro̱to ní yo̱ noni he tšee ke̱ noni he tše teṅ, ni ame̱kũo̱ ame̱hĩe ame̱ſieo̱ mihedšō̱mo̱gbĩĩ le̱ ano̱, ni abuleo̱mi tete yo̱ ame̱teṅ. *Zef. 3,4. †Ezek. 44,23.
27Elumei ní yo̱ emli le̱ tamo̱ klãdši ní tšere̱o̱ mīle̱lo mli, koni ame̱ſie lá ši, ní ame̱kpãtã susumai ahĩe, beni afe ní ame̱wo se̱yeli!
28Ni emli *gbalo̱i le̱ ke̱ yaka kālō mãa he, ni ame̱naä yakanii, ni ame̱klaä amale, ame̱kē̱o̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱! tše̱ Iehowa ewieko tete. *13,6.
29Šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bii le̱ yeo̱ amim, ni ame̱haä nii, ni ame̱waä ohĩafo ke̱ moni efĩle̱ yi, ni ame̱yeo gbo̱ amim ní ehĩĩ. K. 7.
30Ni mitao ame̱teṅ moko ní aafo afãbaṅ lo ní *eedamo flo̱ le̱ nā ye̱ mihĩe ehã šikpoṅ le̱, koni mikafitele̱; ši minaa mokomoko. *13,5.
31Nohewo̱ le̱ mifo̱se mimlila le̱ miſie ame̱no̱, mike̱ mimlifũ la le̱ plenēame̱, mihã ame̱gbe̱ le̱ bua ame̱yiteṅ! Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱. 21,36.

english_text:
Two Sinful Sisters
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, listen to this story about two sisters. 3While they were young and living in Egypt, they became prostitutes. 4The older one was named Oholah, which stands for Samaria; the younger one was Oholibah, which stands for Jerusalem. They became my wives and gave birth to my children.
5Even though Oholah was my wife, she continued to be a prostitute and chased after Assyrian lovers. 6She offered herself to soldiers in purple uniforms: handsome, high-ranking officers and cavalry troops. 7She had sex with all the important Assyrian officials and even worshiped their disgusting idols. 8Once she started doing these things in Egypt, she never stopped. Men slept with her, and she was always ready for sex.
9So I gave Oholah to the Assyrian lovers she wanted so badly. 10They ripped off her clothes, then captured her children and killed her. Women everywhere talked about what had happened to Oholah.
11Oholibah saw all this, but she was more sinful and wanted sex more than her sister Oholah ever did. 12Oholibah also chased after good-looking Assyrian officers, uniformed soldiers, and cavalry troops. 13Just like her sister, she did vulgar things.
14But Oholibah behaved worse than her sister. Oholibah saw images of Babylonian men carved into walls and painted red. 15They had belts around their waists and large turbans on their heads, and they reminded her of Babylonian cavalry officers. 16As soon as she looked at them, she wanted to have sex with them. And so, she sent messengers to bring them to her. 17Men from Babylonia came and had sex with her so many times that she got disgusted with them. 18She let everyone see her naked body and didn't care if they knew she was a prostitute. That's why I turned my back on her, just as I had done with her older sister.
19Oholibah didn't stop there, but became even more immoral and acted as she had back in Egypt. 20She eagerly wanted to go to bed with Egyptian men, who were famous for their sexual powers. 21And she longed for the days when she was a young prostitute, when men enjoyed caressing her body.
The Lord Will Punish Oholibah
22The Lord God said:
Oholibah, though you no longer want to be around your lovers, they will surround you like enemies, when I turn them against you. 23I will gather all the handsome young officials and the high-ranking cavalry officers from Babylonia and Assyria, as well as from the Chaldean tribes of Pekod, Shoa, and Koa. 24Their large armies will come from the north with chariots and wagons carrying weapons. They will wear shields and helmets and will surround you, and I will let them judge and sentence you according to their own laws. 25I am angry with you, so I will let them be very cruel. They will cut off your nose and ears; they will kill your children and burn alive anyone in your family who survives. 26Your clothes and jewelry will be torn off. 27I will stop your wickedness and the prostitution you started back in Egypt. You will never want to think about those days again.
28I, the Lord God, am ready to hand you over to those hateful enemies that you find so disgusting. 29They will cruelly take away everything you have worked for and strip you naked. Then everyone will see you for the prostitute you really are. Your own vulgar sins 30have led to this. You were the one determined to have sex with men from other nations and to worship their idols. 31You have turned out no better than your older sister, and now you must drink from the cup filled with my anger.
32I, the Lord God, gave your sister a large, deep cup filled with my anger. And when you drink from that cup, you will be mocked and insulted. 33You will end up drunk and devastated, because that cup is filled with horror and ruin. 34But you must drink every drop! Then smash the cup and chew on its broken pieces. Use them to cut your breasts in sorrow. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
35You have completely rejected me, and so I promise that you will be punished for the disgusting things you did as a prostitute.
The Two Sisters Are Condemned
36The Lord said:
Ezekiel, son of man, it's time for you to tell Oholah and Oholibah that they are guilty. Remind them of their evil ways! 37They have been unfaithful by worshiping idols, and they have committed murder by sacrificing my own children as offerings to idols. 38-39They came into my temple that same day, and that made it unfit as a place to worship me. They have even stopped respecting the Sabbath.
40They sent messengers to attract men from far away. When those men arrived, the two sisters bathed themselves and put on eye shadow and jewelry. 41They sat on a fancy couch, and in front of them was a table for the olive oil and incense that had belonged to me. 42Their room was always filled with a noisy crowd of drunkards brought in from the desert. These men gave the women bracelets and beautiful crowns, 43and I noticed that the men were eager to have sex with these women, though they were exhausted from being prostitutes. 44In fact, the men had sex over and over with Oholah and Oholibah, the two sinful sisters. 45But honest judges will someday accuse those two of murder and of being unfaithful, because they are certainly guilty.
46So I, the Lord God, now say to these sisters:
I will call together an angry mob that will abuse and rob you. 47They will stone you to death and cut you to pieces; they will kill your children and burn down your houses. 48I will get rid of sinful prostitution in this country, so that women everywhere will be warned not to act as you have. 49You will be punished for becoming prostitutes and for worshiping idols. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_text:
(Kwe̱ Y. 13.)
1Ni Iehowa wiemo̱ ba miṅõ ekoṅ ake̱:
2Gbomobi, yei enyo̱ ko ní dši yō kome bii ni yo̱,
3ni ame̱bo̱ adſamaṅ ye̱ Mizraim, ame̱blayeiaṅ bēbe ame̱dše ame̱bo̱ adſamaṅ. Dše̱i atăra ame̱fufo̱i ahe ye̱, ni dše̱i noṅṅ amĩamĩa ame̱blayeiaṅ kpokuai ye̱.
4Ni ame̱gbe̱ii ne̱: Onukpa le̱, atšé̱o̱le̱ Ohola, ni enyemiyō le̱, atšé̱o̱le̱ Oholiba. Ni ame̱tšṍmo̱ minii, ni ame̱fo̱fō̱ bihĩĩ ke̱ biyei. Ni ame̱gbe̱ii ne̱: Samaria dši Ohola, ni Ierusalem dši Oholiba.
5Ni Ohola dše mise̱ yabo̱ adſamaṅ, ni ehĩe tšu esuolo̱i le̱ ano̱, ye̱ Ašurbii ni be̱ṅke̱o̱le̱ le̱ ano̱,
6mei ní woo̱ mama afaseo atadei, amraloi ke̱ lume̱i, oblahĩĩ ní he yo̱ ako̱no̱ so̱ṅṅ, okpo̱ṅo̱iatše̱mei ní tráa okpo̱ṅo̱i ano̱ ni.
7Ni Ašur hĩĩ ní ahala le̱ fẽ le̱, eke̱-ame̱ bo̱ adſamaṅ, ni mei fẽ ní ehĩe tšu ame̱no̱ le̱ eke̱ ame̱wo̱dši le̱ fẽ bule ehe.
8Asaṅ edſamaṅbō̱ ní eke̱-dše̱ Mizraim le̱ efõko; edšake̱ ame̱ke̱le̱ wo̱ ye̱ eblayeiaṅ, ni ame̱mĩamĩa eblayeiaṅ kpokuai le̱, ni ame̱fo̱se ame̱dſamaṅbō̱ le̱ ame̱ſie eno̱.
9Nohewo̱ le̱ mitule̱ miwo esuolo̱i le̱ ní dši Ašur hĩĩ le̱ ní ehĩe tšu ame̱no̱ le̱ adeṅ.
10Mene̱mei dšie eyayaiaṅ kpo; ame̱lō ebihĩĩ ke̱ ebiyei le̱ ke̱-te, ni le̱dientše̱ le̱, ame̱ke̱ klante gbele̱. Ni etšṍ yei le̱ afe̱oyeli wiemo̱; ši ame̱kodšole̱. K. 29.
11Ni enyemiyō Oholiba na ene̱, ši kẽle̱ efe efõṅ ye̱ ehĩetšũ le̱ mli *fèle̱, ni edſamaṅbō̱ le̱ fá fè enyemiyō le̱ adſamaṅbō̱ le̱. *16,51.
12Ehĩe tšu Ašur hĩĩ le̱, ní dši amraloi ke̱ lume̱i so̱ṅṅ ní be̱ṅke̱o̱le̱, ní woo̱ atadei fe̱fe̱dši, okpo̱ṅo̱iatše̱mei ní tráa okpo̱ṅo̱i ano̱, nī dši oblahĩĩ nī he yo̱ ako̱no̱ so̱ṅṅ le̱ ano̱.
13Ke̱ke̱ ni mina ake̱ ebule ehe, ni ame̱yi enyo̱ le̱ fẽ amenyie gbe̱ kome no̱.
14Ni ehã edſamaṅbō̱ le̱ fá; edšake̱ beni ena hĩĩ ní atẽṅ ye̱ gbogbo he, ní dši Kaldeabii amfonirii ní atẽṅ ní ake̱ atīfo̱ tšuru etẽṅ,
15ní ame̱ke̱ he̱fĩnii efĩmo̱ ame̱he̱i, ní ame̱ke̱ yitšofĩnii kakadãdši efĩmo̱ ame̱yitšei, ní ké̱ okwe̱ame̱ le̱, asafoiatše̱mei so̱ṅṅ ni, tamo̱ Babelbii ní afo̱ame̱ ye̱ Kaldea šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱:
16amrõ pe̱ ní enaame̱ le̱, ehĩe tšu ame̱no̱, ni etšũ bo̱foi ke̱-te ame̱ṅõ, ye̱ Kaldea tō̃.
17Ke̱ke̱ ni Babel hĩĩ le̱ ba eṅõ, ni ame̱ke̱le̱ bawo̱ ye̱ suomo̱ nā, ni ame̱ke̱ ame̱dſamaṅbō̱ le̱ bulele̱; ni beni eke̱ame̱ ebule ehe le̱, no dãni etšine dšeame̱.
18Ni heni edšie edſamaṅbō̱ le̱ kpo ni edšie eyayaiaṅ kpo le̱, ke̱ke̱ ni mitšine dšele̱, take̱ bo̱ni mitšine dše enyemiyō le̱.
19Ši kẽle̱ ehã edſamaṅbō̱ le̱ fá, ni ekai eblayeiaṅ gbĩĩ le̱, beni ebo̱ adſamaṅ ye̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱.
20Ni ehĩe tšu ame̱hemei le̱ ano̱, mei ní ame̱helō tamo̱ tedšii ahelō, ni ame̱henu tamo̱ okpo̱ṅo̱i ahenu le̱.
21Ni okai oblayeiaṅ nyenyeṅtſibō̱ le̱, beni Mizraimbii mĩamĩa ofufo̱i ni ame̱tăratăra oblayeiaṅ kpokuai le̱ ahe le̱.
22Nohewo̱ le̱, Oholiba, bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Na, mibatē osuolo̱i ní otšine edšeame̱ le̱ aši mawoö, ni mahã ame̱dše̱ hefẽhe ameba ono̱:
23Babel hĩĩ le̱ ke̱ Kaldeabii le̱ fẽ, tatše̱mei ke̱ abladei ke̱ odehei, ke̱ Ašur hĩĩ le̱ fẽ fata ame̱he, oblahĩĩ ní he yo̱ ako̱no̱, amraloi ke̱ lume̱i so̱ṅṅ, asafoiatše̱mei ke̱ mei ní yo̱ gbei, ame̱fẽ ame̱trá okpo̱ṅo̱i ano̱.
24Ni ame̱aha ono̱ ke̱ tawūnii ke̱ taſīlii ke̱ nigblamo̱-ſīlii ke̱ mãdšimãdši asafo, ame̱agbá ame̱wo ohe ke̱ tše̱ṅi wudši ke̱ tše̱ṅi bibii ke̱ dadefai; ni mike̱ kodšomo̱ aawo ame̱deṅ, ni ame̱akodšoö ye̱ ame̱dientše̱ ame̱kodšomo̱ le̱ nā. Luk. 19,43.
25Ni matē miwuṅãyeli le̱ ši mawoö, ni ame̱ke̱o aaye ye̱ mlila nā; ame̱aflo̱ ogugõ ke̱ otoii, ni omei ní eſe̱ le̱ aanyõnyõi ye̱ klante nā. Ame̱alō obihĩĩ ke̱ obiyei le̱ ke̱-ate, ni omei ní eſe̱ le̱, la aakpãtã ame̱hĩe.
26Ni ame̱akplo̱ otadei ye̱ ohe, ni ame̱adšie odſinei fe̱fe̱dši le̱.
27Ni mahã onyenyeṅtſibō̱ le̱ ke̱ odſamaṅbō̱ hũ ní oke̱-dše̱ Mizraim šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ bēbe le̱ se̱ afo ye̱ ohe, ni oholeṅ ohĩṅme̱ii ano̱ okwe̱ṅame̱, ni okaiṅ Mizraim doṅṅ!
28Edšake̱ bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Na, mibatuo mawo mei ní onye̱o̱ le̱ ke̱ mei ní otšine edšeame̱ le̱ adeṅ.
29Ni ame̱ke̱o aaye ye̱ nyē̱ nā, ni ame̱alō nii ní ogbo deṅme ye̱ he le̱ fẽ, ni ame̱ašĩo yayai ke̱ ohe pasā, ni aadšie odſamaṅbō̱ yayaiaṅ ke̱ onyenyeṅtſibō̱ ke̱ odſamaṅbō̱i le̱ fẽ kpo.
30Aafeo ene̱mei, edšake̱ oyabo̱ adſamaṅ ke̱-nyie dšeṅmãdši le̱ ase̱, ni oke̱ ame̱wo̱dši le̱ ebule ohe.
31Onyemiyō le̱ gbe̱ le̱ no̱ onyie, hewo̱ le̱ mike̱ *ekpulu le aawo odeṅ. *K. 33.
32Bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Oonu onyemiyō le̱ kpulu ní mli kwo̱ ni emli lē̱ ni emli nii fá le̱; aaṅmõo ni aaye ohe fe̱o.
33*Ooyi obõ ke̱ dā̃tō̱ ke̱ aw̌ere̱hō, hedšõmo̱ ke̱ hedšramo̱ kpulu dši onyemiyō Samaria kpulu le̱. *Ies. 51.17. Ier. 25,15. 18.
34Ni oonu ni ooſo̱ mli, ni ookpe ekói le̱ tete, ni oke̱-aše̱te ofufo̱i ahe; edšake̱ mi, miwie, Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱.
35Nohewo̱ le̱ bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Ake̱-ní ohĩe kpa mino̱, ni oše̱mi ofo okotose̱ hewo̱ le̱, bo hũ, tĕremo̱ onyenyeṅtſibō̱ ke̱ odſamaṅbō̱i le̱!
36Ni Iehowa sā kē̱mi ake̱: Gbomobi, ani ookodšo Ohola ke̱ Oholiba? bĕle̱ dšadšemo̱ ame̱nihĩnii le̱ otšõame̱!
37Edšake̱ ame̱fite gblã, ni lá ye̱ ame̱dẽ; ni ame̱ke̱ ame̱wo̱dši le̱ efite gblã, ni ame̱hã *ame̱bii ní ame̱fo̱ ame̱hãmi le̱ etšṍmo̱ la mli ehãame̱ ame̱ye! *Ier. 7,31.
38Asaṅ nõ hũ ní ame̱femi ne̱: Ame̱wo mihekroṅkroṅ le̱ he mũdši nakai gbĩ le̱ noṅṅ, ni ame̱bule mihedšō̱mo̱gbĩĩ le̱.
39Edšake̱ beni ame̱gbe ame̱bii le̱ ame̱hã ame̱wo̱dši le̱, ame̱ba mihekroṅkroṅ le̱ nakai gbĩ le̱ noṅṅ ni ame̱babulele̱; ni na, nakai noṅṅ amefe ye̱ mišĩa le̱ teṅ!
40Asaṅ tete po le̱ ame̱tšũ ayaṅõ hĩĩ ní dše̱ šoṅṅ ba, ame̱tšũ bo̱fo ke̱-te ame̱ṅõ, ni na, ame̱ba; ni odšu ohe ohãame̱, ni oke̱ adibri diki ohĩṅme̱ii, ni oke̱ wulamo̱nibii wula ohe;
41ni otá sā fe̱fe̱o no̱, ni okplõ ní aṅmẽ mã hĩe, ni oke̱ mitšofã-ke̱-ṅma ke̱ mimũ le̱ emãmo̱ no̱;
42ni anu nyã́mo̱ gbẽ kpeteṅkple ye̱ dše̱i, ni ayaṅõ dā̃to̱lo̱i ke̱-dše̱ ṅã le̱ no̱ ebafata mei babaō le̱ he; ni ame̱ke̱ ninešĩgai wo yei le̱ anidši, ni ame̱ke̱ akekrei fe̱fe̱dši fĩmo̱ ame̱yitsei.
43Ke̱ke̱ ni mikē̱ ake̱: Aso moni egbo̱ ne̱ aafite gblã lolo? kpāko moṅ ake̱le̱ babo̱ adſamaṅ.
44Ni ayaä eṅõ tamo̱ ayaä yō adſamaṅ ko ṅõ; nakai ame̱yaä Ohola ke̱ Oholiba ní dši yei nyenyeṅtſii le̱ aṅõ.
45Ši hĩĩ ní dši *dšalo̱i le̱, ame̱ke̱ yei gblãfitelo̱i akodšomo̱ ke̱ yei lášiſielo̱i akodšomo̱ aakodšoame̱; edšake̱ gblãfitelo̱i dšiame̱, ni lá ye̱ ame̱dẽ. *3 Mose 20,10.
46Edšake̱ bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Mahã asafo yū afã ke̱-ba ame̱no̱, ni maṅõame̱ mahã ní atſiaame̱ ši ni ahaame̱.
47Ni asafo le̱ aatſiaame̱ te̱i, ni ame̱ke̱ ame̱klantei le̱ aabãmo̱ame̱; ame̱bihĩĩ ke̱ ame̱biyei le̱, ame̱agbeame̱, ni ame̱šĩai le̱ hũ ame̱ke̱ la aašã.
48Ni mahã nyenyeṅtſibō̱ se̱ afo ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ní aṅõ-bo̱ yei fẽ-kwa ko̱ko̱, koni ame̱kafe nyenyenyeṅtſiianii ne̱ eko.
49Ni maṅõ nyenyenyeṅtſibō̱ le̱ mafõ nyeno̱, ni nyeatĕre ešai ní nyeke̱ nyewo̱dši le̱ fe le̱, ni nyeaná nyele ake̱ midši Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa le̱.

english_text:
A Cooking Pot
1Nine years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the tenth day of the tenth month. He said:
2 Ezekiel, son of man, write down today's date, because the king of Babylonia has just begun attacking the city of Jerusalem. 3Then tell my rebellious people:
“Pour water in a cooking pot
and set it over a fire.
* 4Throw in the legs and shoulders
of your finest sheep
and put in the juicy bones.
5Pile wood underneath the pot,
and let the meat and bones
boil until they are done.”
6These words mean that Jerusalem is doomed! The city is filled with murderers and is like an old, rusty pot. The meat is taken out piece by piece, and no one cares what happens to it. 7The people of Jerusalem murdered innocent people in the city and didn't even try to cover up the blood that flowed out on the hard ground. 8But I have seen that blood, and it cries out for me to take revenge.
9I, the Lord God, will punish that city of violence! I will make a huge pile of firewood, 10so bring more wood and light it. Cook the meat and boil away the broth to let the bones scorch. 11Then set the empty pot over the hot coals until it is red-hot. That will clean the pot and burn off the rust. 12I've tried everything else. Now the rust must be burned away.
13Jerusalem is so full of sin and evil that I can't get it clean, even though I have tried. It will stay filthy until I let loose my fierce anger against it. 14That time will certainly come! And when it does, I won't show the people of Jerusalem any pity or change my mind. They must be punished for the evil they have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
Ezekiel's Wife Dies
15The Lord said, 16“Ezekiel, son of man, I will suddenly take the life of the person you love most. But I don't want you to complain or cry. 17Mourn in silence and don't show that you are grieving. Don't remove your turban or take off your sandals; don't cover your face to show your sorrow, or eat the food that mourners eat.”
18One morning, I was talking with the people as usual, and by sunset my wife was dead. The next day I did what the Lord had told me, 19and when people saw me, they asked, “Why aren't you mourning for your wife?”
20I answered:
The Lord God says 21he is ready to destroy the temple in which you take such pride and which makes you feel so safe. Your children who now live in Jerusalem will be killed. 22Then you will do the same things I have done. You will leave your face uncovered and refuse to eat the food that mourners usually eat. 23You won't take off your turbans and your sandals. You won't cry or mourn, but all day long you will go around groaning because of your sins.
24I am a warning sign—everything I have done, you will also do. And then you will know the Lord God has made these things happen.
25The Lord said, “Ezekiel, I will soon destroy the temple that makes everyone feel proud and safe, and I will take away their children as well. 26On that same day, someone will escape from the city and come to tell you what has happened. 27Then you will be able to speak again, and the two of you will talk. You will be a warning sign to the people, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_text:
1Ni Iehowa wiemo̱ ba miṅõ ye̱ *afi ní dši ne̱hũ le̱ no̱ nyõṅ ní dši nyoṅma le no gbĩ ní dši gbĩ nyoṅma le̱ no̱ ake̱ *2 Maṅ. 25,1. Ier. 52,4.
2Gbomobi, ṅmã ne̱ke̱ gbĩ ne̱ ní dši ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ gbe̱i! Babel maṅtše̱ le̱ ewo Ierusalem he ká ṅme̱ne̱ gbĩ ne̱ noṅṅ.
3Ni oba weku toigbolo̱i le̱ abe̱, ni okē̱ame̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Ṅõ kukwe̱i le̱ omã no̱, ṅõ-mã no̱, ni osā ofo̱se nu owo mli;
4ṅõ lō ní asā le̱ fẽ owo mli, hei ní hĩ le̱ fẽ, ſuo̱ ke̱ nine, ke̱ wui ní hĩ fè fẽ le̱ oke̱-wo mli.
5Ṅõ tōi ní hĩ fè fẽ le̱ eko, ni oto lai owo šiši; hã etſa dšogbāṅ, ni ewui le̱ tete abe ye̱ mli.
6Nohewo̱ le̱ bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: *Kpóo hã lášiſiemo̱ maṅ le̱! kukwe̱i ní mli edo̱ ṅkanale ní emli ṅkanale le̱ edšee le̱! Kŏ̱lo̱mo̱ emli nii le̱ ekomekome, akafõ no̱ ošiki! *K. 9.
7Edšake̱ elá le̱ ye̱ eteṅ; te̱sā kpatā no̱ eke̱-ſie, dšee šikpoṅ eke̱-ſie ní ake̱ sũ aaha no̱.
8Beni afe ní ehã mlila ate ši, ni ebato̱ owele hewo̱ ni mihã eke̱ elá le̱ fĩe te̱sā kpatā no̱ ní akaha no̱ le̱.
9Nohewo̱ le̱ bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Kpóo hã *lášiſiemo̱ maṅ le̱! Mi hũ mahã ešiši laike le̱ ada! *Nah. 3,1.
10Hã lai le̱ afá, hã la le̱ atšo! Ha lō le̱ abe dšogbāṅ, hã wonu le̱ afĩ, ni wui le̱ tete aṅălã!
11Ni ohã emã eṅãi la le̱ no̱ eflo, beni afe ní edo̱, ní ehe akō̱ble le̱ atšu he̱ṅṅ, ni emli mũdši le̱ asĕre, ní emli ṅkanale le̱ atã kwrā!
12Agbo he deṅme bo̱ni aagbo, ši kẽle̱ emli ṅkanale babaō le̱ edšee; la le̱ po nyẽẽ emli ṅkanale le̱ adšie!
13Omũdšinii le̱ nyenyeṅtſibō̱ ye̱ mli; ake̱-ní mitšū ohe ni ohe tšee hewo̱ le̱, ohe tšeṅ ke̱-dše̱ṅ omũdšinii le̱ amli doṅṅ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní maṅmẽ *mimlila gbe̱ ke̱-aba ono̱. *5,13.
14Mi, Iehowa, miwie; eeba mli, ni mafe hũ: mifõṅ, ni minaṅ mo̱bo̱ ni miſaṅ mihe hũ. Bo̱ni ogbè̱i le̱ yo̱ ke̱ bo̱ni onifemo̱nii le̱ yo̱ le̱, nakai ame̱akodšoö, Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱.
15Ni Iehowa wiemo̱ ba miṅõ ake̱:
16Gbomobi, na, mike̱ gbĕle-hela baṅõ *ohĩṅme̱ii atšuihenõ le̱ ke̱-dše̱ ohe; ši kāwo yăra ni kāfó hũ ni kāhã ohĩeyāfónui mīdše. *K. 18.
17Dõmo̱ ntšo̱i diō, kāfe gbohĩĩ ahe yăra ko; oke̱ oyitšofĩnii le̱ afĩ oyitšo, ni oke̱ tokotai le̱ awo onãdši, ni kāha onābu no̱, nĩ kāye yăra no̱ niyenii hũ!
18Ke̱ke̱ ni mike̱ maṅ le̱ wie lebi, ni gbe̱ke̱ le̱ miṅã le̱ gbo; ni lebi le̱ mife bo̱ni awomi kitã le̱.
19Ke̱ke̱ ni maṅ le̱ bimi ake̱: Ani otšōṅwo̱ noni dši nii ní ofeo̱ ne̱ ašiši hãwo̱?
20Ni mikē̱ame̱ ake̱: Iehowa wiemo̱ ba miṅõ ake̱:
21Kē̱me̱ Israel we le̱ ake̱: Bo̱ni Nuṅtšo̱ Iehowa kē̱ ne̱: Na, mibabule mihekroṅkroṅ le̱, ni dši nyehewale̱ hewo le̱ ke̱ nyehĩṅme̱ii atšuihenõ le̱ ke̱ nyesusumai ahedō̱nii le̱, ni nyebihĩĩ ke̱ nyebiyei le̱ ní nyešĩ le̱ aanyõnyõi ye̱ klante nā.
22Ni nyeafe tamo̱ bo̱ni mife ne̱: nyehaṅ nyenābui ano̱, ni nyeyeṅ yăra no̱ niyenii hũ,
23ni nyeyitšofĩnii le̱ aafĩmo̱ nyeyitšei, ni nyetokotai le̱ aahĩ nyenãdši; nyewoṅ yăra ni asaṅ nyefóṅ, ši nyeatără lō ye̱ nyenišaianii le̱ ahewo̱, ni nyeakẽmo̱ nyetšõtšō̃ nyehe.
24Ni Ezekiel aatšṍ *okadi ahãnye; bo̱ni efe le̱, nakai pe̱ nyeafe, ké̱ eba mli le̱; ni nyeaná nyele ake̱ midši Iehowa le̱. *K. 27. Y. 12,11.
25Ni bo, gbomobi, le̱le̱ṅ ake̱ gbĩ ní mašõ ame̱hewale̱ le̱, ame̱numnyam le̱ he nyã́mo̱ le̱, ame̱hĩṅme̱ii atšuihenõ le̱ ke̱ ame̱susumai ataomo̱nii le̱, ame̱bihĩĩ ke̱ ame̱biyei le̱, ke̱-adše̱ ame̱deṅ le̱,
26nakai gbĩ le̱ noṅṅ *moko ní edše mli aaba oṅõ, ní ebawó otoi no̱. *33,21.
27Nakai gbĩ le̱ noṅṅ oke̱ moni edše mli le̱ fẽ nābu aagble, ni oowie ni oto̱ṅ mṹ doṅṅ; ni ootšṍ okadi ohãame̱, koni ame̱ná ame̱le ake̱ midši Iehowa le̱.

english_text:
Judgment on Ammon
1 The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Ammon 3and tell them:
You celebrated when my temple was destroyed, when Israel was defeated, and when my people were taken away as prisoners. 4Now I am going to let you be conquered by tribes from the eastern desert. They will set up their camps in your land and eat your fruit and drink your milk. 5Your capital city of Rabbah will be nothing but pastureland for camels, and the rest of the country will be pastures for sheep. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
6You hated Israel so much that you clapped and shouted and celebrated. 7And so I will hand you over to enemies who will rob you. I will completely destroy you. There won't be enough of your people left to be a nation ever again, and you will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
Judgment on Moab
8 The Lord God said, “The people of Moab thought Judah was no different from any other nation. 9So I will let Moab's fortress towns along its border be attacked, including Beth-Jeshimoth, Baal-Meon, and Kiriathaim. 10The same eastern desert tribes that invade Ammon will invade Moab, and just as Ammon will be forgotten forever, 11Moab will be punished. Then the people there will know that I am the Lord.”
Judgment on Edom
12 The Lord God then said, “The people of Edom are guilty of taking revenge on Judah. 13So I will punish Edom by killing all its people and livestock.
