41Nye le̱, nyetše̱ nitšumo̱i nyetšuo̱ le̱. Ke̱ke̱ le̱ ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Wo̱ le̱, afó̱ó̱wo̱ ye̱ adſamaṅbō̱ mli; tše̱ kome wo̱yo̱, le̱ dši Nyoṅmo̱.
42Ke̱ke̱ le̱ Iesu kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyoṅmo̱ dši nyetše̱ kũle̱, nyeasumo̱mi; edšake̱ mi le̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ṅõ midše̱ miba; ni asaṅ mitoo midientše̱ miyi mibaa, ši moṅ le̱ etšũmi.
43Ši mẽhewo̱ nyenaa miwiemo̱ nā le̱? Edše̱ miwiemo̱ toi ni nyeboo le̱.
44Nye le̱ *nyetše̱ ní nyedše̱ emli dši abonsam, ni nyetše̱ le̱ tšinebānii nyesumoo̱ ake̱ nyefe. Le̱ le̱ †gbomogbelo̱ dšile̱ ke̱-dše̱ tetēte, ni **edamo̱o̱ ano̱kwale le̱ mli, edšake̱ ano̱kwale be̱ emli. Ké̱ ēmale le̱, le̱dientše̱ enii ahe ewieo̱, edšake̱ amalelo̱ ke̱ malemo̱tše̱ dšile̱. *1 Ioh. 5,8-10. †1 Mose 3,4. **2 Pet. 2,4.
45Ši mi le̱, ake̱-ní miwieo̱ ano̱kwale hewo̱ le̱, nyeheemi nyeyee.
46*Nyeteṅ namo kãami ye̱ eša ko hewo̱? Ši ke̱dši miwie ano̱kwale le̱, mẽhewo̱ ni nyeheemi nyeyee le̱? *2 Kor. 5,21. 1 Pet. 2,22
47Moni *dše̱ Nyoṅmo̱ mli le̱, enuo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ wiemo̱i; nohewo̱ ni nye le̱ nyenuu le, edšake nyedšee̱ Nyoṅmo̱ mli. *18,37.
48Agbe̱ne̱ Iudafoi le̱ here no̱ ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ani dšee egbe̱nā wo̱kē̱o̱ ake̱ Samarianyo dšio, ni *daimonio hũ ye̱ omli? *7,20.
49Iesu here no̱ ake: Daimonio be̱ mimli, ši miwo mitše̱, ni nye le̱ nyemīgbe mihe guo̱ moṅ.
50Mitaoo midientše̱ minumnyam; ši moko ye̱ ni taoo̱ ni ekodšoo̱. 5,41.
51Le̱le̱ṅ, le̱le̱ṅ, mīkē̱nye ake̱: Ke̱dši moko ye miwiemo̱ le̱ no̱ le̱, enaṅ gbẽle ke̱-ate nāno̱. 6,40. 47.
52Ke̱ke̱ le̱ Iudafoi le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Kpāko wo̱ná wo̱le ake̱ daimonio ye̱ omli. Abraham gbo, ni gbaloi le̱ hũ gboi, ni bo le̱ okē̱o̱ ake̱: Ke̱dši moko ye miwiemo̱ le̱ no̱ le̱, esaṅ enā gbĕle kwrā ke̱-ate nāno̱.
53Ani ofè wo̱tše̱ Abraham ní gbo le̱? ni gbalo̱i le̱ hũ gboi. Té otšé̱o̱ ohe tēṅ ne̱?
54Iesu here no̱ ake̱: Ke̱dši miwo midientše̱ mihĩe nyam le̱, minumnyam le̱ dšee noko; mitše̱ dši moni woo̱ mihĩe nyam, moni nyekē̱o̱ ake̱ nye-Nyoṅmo̱ dšile̱ le̱,
55ni *nyeyokole̱, ši mi le̱ milele̱; ni ke̱dši mikē̱ ake̱ mileele̱ le̱, matšṍ amalelo̱ tamo̱nye; ši milele̱, ni miyeo̱ ewiemo̱ no̱. *7,28.
56Nyetše̱ Abraham mli flile̱ ake̱ eena migbĩ le̱, ni ena ni emī še̱.
57Ke̱ke̱ le̱ Iudafoi le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Onáko oye afii nyoṅmai-ennmo̱, ni ona Abraham lo?
58Iesu kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Le̱le̱ṅ, le̱le̱ṅ, mīkē̱nye ake̱: Miye̱ dãni Abraham yo̱.
59Ke̱ke̱ ni *ame̱kŏ̱lo̱ tei ní ame̱batſiale̱; ši Iesu tē ehe, ni edše so̱lemo̱we le̱ ete. *10,31.

english_text:
Jesus Heals a Man Born Blind
1As Jesus walked along, he saw a man who had been blind since birth. 2Jesus' disciples asked, “Teacher, why was this man born blind? Was it because he or his parents sinned?”
3“No, it wasn't!” Jesus answered. “But because of his blindness, you will see God work a miracle for him. 4As long as it is day, we must do what the one who sent me wants me to do. When night comes, no one can work. 5 While I am in the world, I am the light for the world.”
6After Jesus said this, he spit on the ground. He made some mud and smeared it on the man's eyes. 7Then he said, “Go wash off the mud in Siloam Pool.” The man went and washed in Siloam, which means “One Who Is Sent.” When he had washed off the mud, he could see.
8The man's neighbors and the people who had seen him begging wondered if he really could be the same man. 9Some of them said he was the same beggar, while others said he only looked like him. But he told them, “I am that man.”
10“Then how can you see?” they asked.
11He answered, “Someone named Jesus made some mud and smeared it on my eyes. He told me to go and wash it off in Siloam Pool. When I did, I could see.”
12“Where is he now?” they asked.
“I don't know,” he answered.
The Pharisees Try To Find Out What Happened
13-14The day when Jesus made the mud and healed the man was a Sabbath. So the people took the man to the Pharisees. 15They asked him how he was able to see, and he answered, “Jesus made some mud and smeared it on my eyes. Then after I washed it off, I could see.”
16Some of the Pharisees said, “This man Jesus doesn't come from God. If he did, he would not break the law of the Sabbath.”
Others asked, “How could someone who is a sinner work such a miracle?”
Since the Pharisees could not agree among themselves, 17they asked the man, “What do you say about this one who healed your eyes?”
“He is a prophet!” the man told them.
18But the Jewish leaders would not believe that the man had once been blind. They sent for his parents 19and asked them, “Is this the son that you said was born blind? How can he now see?”
20The man's parents answered, “We are certain that he is our son, and we know that he was born blind. 21But we don't know how he got his sight or who gave it to him. Ask him! He is old enough to speak for himself.”
22-23The man's parents said this because they were afraid of their leaders. The leaders had already agreed that no one was to have anything to do with anyone who said Jesus was the Messiah.
24The leaders called the man back and said, “Swear by God to tell the truth! We know that Jesus is a sinner.”
25The man replied, “I don't know if he is a sinner or not. All I know is that I used to be blind, but now I can see!”
26“What did he do to you?” they asked. “How did he heal your eyes?”
27The man answered, “I have already told you once, and you refused to listen. Why do you want me to tell you again? Do you also want to become his disciples?”
28The leaders insulted the man and said, “You are his follower! We are followers of Moses. 29We are sure God spoke to Moses, but we don't even know where Jesus comes from.”
30“How strange!” the man replied. “He healed my eyes, and yet you don't know where he comes from. 31We know that God listens only to people who love and obey him. God doesn't listen to sinners. 32And this is the first time in history anyone has ever given sight to someone born blind. 33Jesus could not do anything unless he came from God.”
34The leaders told the man, “You have been a sinner since the day you were born! Do you think you can teach us anything?” Then they said, “You can never come back into any of our synagogues!”
35When Jesus heard what had happened, he went and found the man. Then Jesus asked, “Do you have faith in the Son of Man?”
36He replied, “Sir, if you will tell me who he is, I will put my faith in him.”
37“You have already seen him,” Jesus answered, “and right now he is talking with you.”
38The man said, “Lord, I put my faith in you!” Then he worshiped Jesus.
39Jesus told him, “I came to judge the people of this world. I am here to give sight to the blind and to make blind everyone who can see.”
40When the Pharisees heard Jesus say this, they asked, “Are we blind?”
41Jesus answered, “If you were blind, you would not be guilty. But now that you claim to see, you will keep on being guilty.”
translation_text:
1Ni beni ehoo̱ le̱, ena nū ko ní eſila ke̱-dše̱ efo̱mo̱ mli.
2Ni ekaselo̱i le̱ bile̱ ake̱: Babi, namo fe esa, mone̱ lo efo̱lo̱i, hewo̱ ni afó̱le̱ ſilafo ne̱? Luk. 13,2.
3Iesu here no̱ ekē̱: Dšee mone̱ lo eſo̱lo̱i ni fe eša, ši moṅ beni afe ní *Nyoṅmo̱ nitšumo̱ĩ le̱ aná adše kpo ye̱ emli. *11,4.
4Wo̱ le̱, ni dše etše̱re ne̱, dša wo̱tšu moni tšũwo̱ le̱ nitšumo̱i le̱; dše bana, beni moko nyẽṅ nii atšu. 5,17.
5Gbĩĩ abo̱ ní miyo̱ dše le̱ mli ne̱, dše le̱ṅ la dšimi. 8,12.
6Beni ekē̱ ene̱ le̱, etšẽ ladšõ efo ši, ni eke̱ ladšõ le̱ kpo̱to̱ sũ, ni eṅõ sũ le̱ ekpá ſilafo le̱ hĩṅme̱ii ano̱, Mar. 8,23.
7ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Yadšu ye̱ Siloam (ešiši dši: moni atšũle̱) kpākpo le̱ mli. Ke̱ke̱ ni ete eyadšu, ni eba ní ēna nii.
8Ke̱ke̱ le̱ ekūṅbii ke̱ mei ní nale̱ sá ake sisẽlo̱ dšile̱ le̱ kē̱: Ani dšee moni kũle̱ etaa ši ni esisẽo̱ le̱ ne̱?
9Meikomei kē̱: Le̱ ni; meikomei hũ kē̱: Etamo̱le̱; le̱dientše̱ ekē̱: Mi ni.
10Nohewo̱ le̱ ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Té fe tēṅ ní ohĩṅme̱ii le̱ gbleṅ?
11Ehere no̱ ekē̱: Nū ko ní atšé̱o̱le̱ Iesu le̱ kpo̱to̱ sũ, ni eke̱-kpá mihĩṅme̱ii le̱, ni ekē̱mi ake̱: Ya Siloam kpākpo le̱ mli ní oyadšu. Ni beni mite miyadšu le̱, mina nii.
12Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Nẽgbe̱ eyo̱? Ekē̱ ake̱: Milee.
13Ni ame̱ke̱ moni sá ní éſila le̱ te Farisifoi le̱ aṅõ.
14Ši gbĩ ni Iesu kpo̱to̱ sũ ní egble ehĩṅme̱ii le̱ hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ ni. 5,9.
15Ke̱ke̱ ni Farisifoi le̱ hũ sā bile̱ bo̱ni fe ní ena nii le̱. Ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Sũ ní akpo̱to̱ eke̱-kpá mihĩṅme̱ii, ni miyadšu, ni minaä nii ne̱.
16Nohewo̱ le̱ Farisifoi le̱ ateṅ meikomei kē̱: Nū ne̱ dše̱e̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ṅõ, edšake̱ eyee hedšō̱mo̱gbĩ le̱. Meikomei hũ kē̱: Té *gbomo ko ní dši ešafelo̱ aafe tēṅ ní enyẽ efe okadii ní tamo̱ enemeiṅ? Ni †mligblamo̱ ha ameteṅ. *K. 31.33. †7,43.
17Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱kē̱ ſilafo le̱ ekoṅ ake̱: Bo hũ, té okē̱o̱ ye̱ ehe tēṅ, ake̱-ní egble ohĩṅme̱ii le̱? Ni ekē̱: Gbalo̱ dšile̱.
18Ši Iudafoi le̱ hee yee ake̱ ſilafo dšile̱ sá dãni enaä nii ne̱, ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ni ame̱yatšé̱ moni ena nii le̱ fo̱lo̱i,
19ni ame̱biame̱ ake̱: Ani nyebi le̱ ni nyekē̱e̱ ake̱ afó̱le̱ ſilafo le̱ ne̱? Té fe tēṅ ni agbe̱ne̱ enaä niiṅ?
20Efo̱lo̱i le̱ hereame̱ no̱ ame̱kē̱: Wo̱le ake̱ wo̱bi le̱ ne̱, ni we̱le ake̱ afó̱le ſilafo;
21ši bo̱ni fe ní enaä nii agbe̱ne̱ ne̱, wolee, asaṅ moni gble ehĩṅme̱ii le̱ hũ wo̱lee; éda, nyebiale̱, le̱dientše̱ eewie ehã ehe.
22Efo̱lo̱i le̱ kē̱ ene̱, edšake̱ *ame̱mīše Iudafoi le̱ agbeyei; ši Iudafoi le̱ ékpãṅ éto ake̱, ke̱dši moko gba mli kē̱ ake̱, le̱ dši Kristo le̱, †abaſiele̱ ke̱-dše̱ kpēhe le̱. *7,13. †12,42.
23Nohewo̱ ni efo̱lo̱i le̱ kē̱ ake̱: Eda, nyebia le̱dientše̱ le̱.
24Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱tšé̱ nū ní sá ni edši ſilafo le̱, noni dši ši enyo̱, ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ṅõ anumnyam *ohã Nyoṅmo̱; ši wo̱ le̱ wo̱le ake̱ gbomo ne̱ ešafelo dšile̱. *Ios. 7,19.
25Ke̱ke̱ ni ehere no̱ ekē̱: Ešafelo̱ dšile̱ dšĩṅ, milee; nokome mile, ake̱ kũle̱ ſilafo dšimi, ši agbe̱ne̱ mina nii.
26Ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ekoṅ ake̱: Meni efeo? Té efe tēṅ ní egble ohĩṅme̱ii le̱?
27Ehereame̱ no̱ ake̱: Mikē̱nye momo, ni nyenuu; mẽhewo̱ nyetaoo̱ toi nyebo ekoṅ? Ani nye hũ nyemīsumo̱ ake̱ nyeatšṍmo̱ ekaselo̱i?
28Ame̱dšé̱le̱ ame̱kē̱: Bo odši ekaselo̱, ši wo̱ le̱, Mose kaselo̱i dši wo̱.
29Wo̱le ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱ Mose wie; ši mone̱ le̱, wo̱lee heni edše̱.
30Nū le̱ here no̱ ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Ei, ene̱ dši noni yo̱ nākpe̱, ake̱ nyelee heni edše̱, ni kẽle̱ égble mihĩṅme̱ii le̱!
31Wo̱le ake̱ *Nyoṅmo̱ boo ešafelo̱i atoi; ši moṅ ke̱dši mo dšáa Nyoṅmo̱ ni efeo̱ esuomo̱nānii le̱, le̱ toi eboo̱. *Ies. 1,15. Abe̱i 15,29.
32Ke̱-dše̱ ní abo̱ ade ne̱ anuko ake̱ moko égble moni afó̱le̱ ſilafo hĩṅme̱ii dã.
33Ke̱dši mone̱ dše̱e̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ṅõ kũle̱, enyẽṅ noko efe. K. 16.
34Ame̱here no̱ ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Bo le̱, *afó̱o ye̱ eša mli kwrā, ni bo moṅ otšõo̱we̱ nii ne̱? Ni ame̱ſiele̱. *K. 2.
35Iesu nu ake̱ ame̱ſiele̱; ni beni enale̱ le̱, ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Ōhe Nyoṅmo̱ bi le̱ no̱ ōye lo?
36Ehere no̱ ekē̱: Namo dšile̱, Nuṅtšo̱, koni mahe eno̱ maye?
37Ši Iesu kē̱le̱ ake̱: Onale̱ momo, ni asaṅ moni ke̱o wieo̱ le̱, le̱ noṅṅ ni. 4,26.
38Ni ekē̱: Mīhe mīye, Nuṅtšo̱; ni edšale̱.
39Ni Iesu kē̱: Kodšomo̱ hewo̱ miba dše ne̱ṅ, koni mei ní enaa nii le̱ ána, ni mei ní naä le̱ atšṍmo ſilafoi. Mat 13,11-15.
40Ni Farisifoi le̱ ateṅ meikomei ní yo̱ dše̱i le̱ nu ene̱, ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ani wo̱ hũ wo̱ſila?
41Iesu kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Edši nyéſila moṅ kũle̱, nyehe be̱ eša; ši agbe̱ne̱ nyekē̱o̱ ake̱: Wo̱mīna nii; nohewo̱ le̱ nyehe eša le̱ éka nyehe. Abe̱i 26,12.

english_text:
A Story about Sheep
1Jesus said:
I tell you for certain only thieves and robbers climb over the fence instead of going in through the gate to the sheep pen. 2-3But the gatekeeper opens the gate for the shepherd, and he goes in through it. The sheep know their shepherd's voice. He calls each of them by name and leads them out.
4When he has led out all of his sheep, he walks in front of them, and they follow, because they know his voice. 5The sheep will not follow strangers. They don't recognize a stranger's voice, and they run away.
6Jesus told the people this story. But they did not understand what he was talking about.
Jesus Is the Good Shepherd
7Jesus said:
I tell you for certain that I am the gate for the sheep. 8Everyone who came before me was a thief or a robber, and the sheep did not listen to any of them. 9I am the gate. All who come in through me will be saved. Through me they will come and go and find pasture.
10A thief comes only to rob, kill, and destroy. I came so everyone would have life, and have it fully. 11 I am the good shepherd, and the good shepherd gives up his life for his sheep. 12Hired workers are not like the shepherd. They don't own the sheep, and when they see a wolf coming, they run off and leave the sheep. Then the wolf attacks and scatters the flock. 13Hired workers run away because they don't care about the sheep.
14 I am the good shepherd. I know my sheep, and they know me. 15 Just as the Father knows me, I know the Father, and I give up my life for my sheep. 16I have other sheep that are not in this sheep pen. I must also bring them together, when they hear my voice. Then there will be one flock of sheep and one shepherd.
17The Father loves me, because I give up my life, so I may receive it back again. 18No one takes my life from me. I give it up willingly! I have the power to give it up and the power to receive it back again, just as my Father commanded me to do.
19The people took sides because of what Jesus had told them. 20Many of them said, “He has a demon in him! He is crazy! Why listen to him?”
21But others said, “How could anyone with a demon in him say these things? No one like this could give sight to a blind person!”
Jesus Is Rejected
22 That winter, Jesus was in Jerusalem for the Temple Festival. 23One day he was walking in the part of the temple known as Solomon's Porch, 24and the people gathered all around him. They said, “How long are you going to keep us guessing? If you are the Messiah, tell us plainly!”
25Jesus answered:
I have told you, and you refused to believe me. The things I do by my Father's authority show who I am. 26But since you are not my sheep, you don't believe me. 27My sheep know my voice, and I know them. They follow me, 28and I give them eternal life, so that they will never be lost. No one can snatch them out of my hand. 29 My Father gave them to me, and he is greater than all others. No one can snatch them from his hands, 30and I am one with the Father.
31Once again the people picked up stones in order to kill Jesus. 32But he said, “I have shown you many good things my Father sent me to do. Which one are you going to stone me for?”
33They answered, “We are not stoning you because of any good thing you did. We are stoning you because you did a terrible thing. You are just a man, and here you are claiming to be God!”
34 Jesus replied:
In your Scriptures doesn't God say, “You are gods”? 35You can't argue with the Scriptures, and God spoke to those people and called them gods. 36So why do you accuse me of a terrible sin for saying that I am the Son of God? After all, it is the Father who prepared me for this work. He is also the one who sent me into the world. 37If I don't do as my Father does, you should not believe me. 38But if I do what my Father does, you should believe because of that, even if you don't have faith in me. Then you will know for certain that the Father is one with me, and I am one with the Father.
39Again they wanted to arrest Jesus. But he escaped 40 and crossed the Jordan to the place where John had earlier been baptizing. While Jesus was there, 41many people came to him. They were saying, “John didn't work any miracles, but everything he said about Jesus is true.” 42A lot of those people also put their faith in Jesus.
translation_text:
1Le̱le̱ṅ, le̱le̱ṅ, mīkē̱nye ake̱: Moni tšṍṍ šĩnā le̱ ní eke̱-bote gwanteṅi atšũ le̱ mli, ši moṅ etšṍo̱ he kroko ekwo̱ö̱ le̱, dšule̱ ke̱ odšotſalo̱ dšile̱.
2Ši moni tšṍo̱ šĩnā le̱ ke̱-boteo̱ mli le̱, tōi le̱ akwe̱lo̱ dšile̱.
3Le̱, šĩnākwe̱lo̱ le̱ gbleo̱ hãa, ni tōi le̱ nuo̱ egbē, ni eke̱ le̱dientše̱ etōi le̱ agbe̱i tšé̱o̱ame̱, ni eke̱ame̱ dšee̱ kpo.
4Ni ké̱ edšie etoi le̱ fẽ le̱, enyieo̱ ame̱hĩe, ni tōi le̱ nyieo̱ ese, edšake̱ ame̱le egbē.
5Ši mokpoṅ le̱, ame̱nyieṅ ese̱, ši moṅ ame̱adšo foi ye̱ eṅõ, edšake̱ ame̱lee meikpõdši agbē.
6Iesu buame̱ abe̱ ne̱; ši ame̱ le̱ ame̱naa noni eke̱ame̱ wieo̱ le̱ šiši.
7Nohewo̱ le̱ Iesu sā kē̱ame̱ ekoṅ ake̱: Le̱le̱ṅ, le̱le̱ṅ, mīkē̱nye ake̱: Midši tōi le̱ ašĩnā le̱.
8Mei fẽ ní tšṍ mihĩe ba le̱, dšulo̱i ke̱ odšotſalo̱i dšiame̱: ši tōi le̱ booame̱ toi hũ. Ier. 23,1. 2.
9Midši šĩnā le̱. Mi le̱, ke̱dši moko tšṍ mina ete mli le̱, aahere eyiwala, ni eete mli ni eedše kpo, ni eená lē̱nii.
10Dšulo̱ baa yaka, ši dšū ke̱ gbē ke̱ hĩekpãtãmo̱ hewo̱ ebaä; mi le̱ miba beni afe ní ame̱ná wala ni ame̱ná ni ateke no̱. Lal. 23,1.
11Midši *tōkwe̱lo̱ kpakpa le̱. Tōkwe̱lo̱ kpakpa le̱ †ṅõo̱ esusuma eṅmẽo̱ ši ye̱ etoi le̱ anãdšiaṅ. *Ies. 40,11. Ezek. 34,11-23; 37,24. †Ioh. 15,13.
12Ši moni dši apāfonyo ni edšee tōi le̱ akwe̱lo̱, moni tōi le̱ dšee enõ le̱, naä ake̱ klaṅ mība, ni ešĩo̱ tōi le̱ edšoo̱ foi, ni klaṅ le̱ bamõmoo̱ame̱ ni egbe̱o̱ tōi le̱ amli eſãa.
13Ši apāfonyo le̱ edšoo̱ foi, edšake̱ apāfonyo dšile̱, ni tōi le̱ ahe edo̱o̱le̱.
14Midši tōkwe̱lo̱ kpakpa le̱, ni *mile mei ní dši mimei, ni mimei le̱ hũ lemi, *2 Tim 2,19.
15take̱ bo̱ni *tše̱ le̱ lemi, ni mi hũ mile tše̱ le̱; ni miṅõo̱ miwala miṅmẽo̱ ši ye̱ tōi le̱ anãdšiaṅ le̱. *Mat. 11,27.
16Ni miye̱ *tōi krokomei ní dše̱e̱ tōi atšũ ne̱ mli; ni nomei hũ, dša miṅõame̱ ke̱-ba, ni ame̱banu migbē, ní tōi le̱ ſe ku kome ke̱ kwe̱lo̱ kome. *11,52.
17Nohewo̱ ni tše̱ le̱ sumoo̱mi le̱, edšake̱ miṅõo̱ miwala miṅmẽo̱ ši, koni maṅõle̱ ekoṅ.
18Moko šõõ ye̱ mideṅ, ši moṅ midientše̱ miṅõ-ṅmẽo̱ ši; miye̱ hewale̱ ake̱ mĩke̱-ṅmẽo̱ ši, ni miye̱ *hewale̱ ake̱ miṅõo̱ ekoṅ; bo̱ni mitše̱ kē̱mi ne̱. *5,26.
19Wiemoi ne̱ ahewo̱ le̱ mligblamo̱ sā ba Iudafoi le̱ ateṅ ekoṅ. 7,43; 9,16.
20Ni ame̱teṅ mei pī kē̱: Daimonio ye̱ emli ni eye se̱ke̱; mẽhewo̱ nyeboo̱le̱ toi? 7,20.
21Meikomei hũ kē̱: Moni daimonio yo̱ emli wiemo̱i ne̱? ani daimonio aanyẽ ſilafo hĩṅmeii agble?
22Ši aye šo̱lemo̱tšũnāgblemo̱-kaimo̱-gbīdšŭrõ ye̱ Ierusalem, ni fẽibe ni.
23Ni Iesu mīšĕra ši ye̱ so̱lemo̱we le̱ ye̱ *Salomo ablanā le̱ no̱. *Bo̱f. 3,11.
24Ke̱ke̱ ni Iudafoi le̱ babo̱le ehe, ni ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Mẽ beyino noṅṅ oohã wo̱yiṅ afewo̱ ko̱šiko̱ši ke̱-yaši? Ké̱ bo dši Kristo le̱, kē̱mo̱wo̱ faṅṅ.
25Iesu hereame̱ no̱ ake̱: Mikē̱nye, ni nyehee nyeyee. *Nitšumo̱i ní mitšuo̱ ye̱ mitše̱ gbe̱i ano̱ le̱, nomei mīye mihe odase; *5,36.
26ši nye moṅ nyehee nyeyee, edšake̱ nyedšee mitōi le̱ eko, take̱ bo̱ni mĩkē̱nye le̱. 8,45.
27Mitōi le̱ nuo̱ migbē, ni mile-ame̱, ni ame̱nyieo̱ mise̱, K. 3.4; 8,47.
28*ni mi noṅṅ mihāäame̱ nāno̱ wala, ni ame̱hĩe kpãtãṅ ke̱-ate nāno̱, ni asaṅ moko šõṅame̱ ye̱ mideṅ.
29Mitše̱ ní ṅõame̱ ehãmi le̱ fè mei fẽ, ni moko nyẽṅ ašõame̱ ye̱ mitše̱ deṅ.
30Mi ke̱ tše̱ le̱ fẽ le̱, ekomeṅ.
31Ke̱ke̱ ni Iudafoi le̱ *kŏ̱lo̱ te̱i ekoṅ ake̱ ame̱batſĩale̱. *8,59.
32Iesu hereame̱ no̱ ako̱: Nitšumo̱i kpakpai pī mitšõnye ke̱-dše̱ mitše̱ ṅõ; té nakai nitšumo̱i le̱ ateṅ nõ hewo̱ ni nyebatſiami te̱i ne̱?
33Iudafoi le̱ herele̱ no̱ ni āme̱kē̱: Dšee nitšumo̱ kpakpa ko hewo̱ wo̱batſiao te̱i le̱, ši moṅ musubō̱ hewo̱ṅ, edšako̱ bo ní gbomo dšio le̱ otšé̱o̱ ohe ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ dšio. 5,18. Mat. 26,65.
34Iesu hereame̱ no̱ ake̱: Ani *aṅmãko ye̱ nyemla le̱ mlĩ ake̱: “Mĩkē̱, nyoṅmo̱i dšinye?” *Lal. 32,6.
35Ke̱dši mei aṅõ ní Nyoṅmo̱ wiemo̱ le̱ ba le̱ tete le̱ etšé̱ame̱ nyoṅmo̱i, ni anyēṅ ṅmãle̱ le̱ mli akũ le̱, —
36nyemīkē̱ ye̱ moni tše̱ le̱ efele̱ kroṅkroṅ ní etšũle̱ ke̱-ba dše le̱ mli le̱ hewo̱ ake̱: Obo̱ musu, ake̱-ní mĩkē̱ ake̱: Nyoṅmo̱ bi dšimi le̱? 5,17-20.
37Ké̱ mitšuu mitše̱ nitšumo̱i le̱, no le̱ nyekaheami nyeyea;
38ši ke̱dši mitšuo̱, ni kẽle̱ nyeheemi nyeyee le̱, nyehea nitšumo̱i le̱ nyeyea mo̱, koni nyele ni nyehe nyeye ake̱ tše̱ le̱ ye̱ mimli, ni mi hũ miye̱ tše̱ le̱ mli.
39Nohewo̱ le̱ ame̱mĩtao ekoṅ ake̱ ame̱mõle̱, ni edše ame̱deṅ. 8,59. Luk. 4,30.
40Ni eyiṅ ete Iordan se̱ ekoṅ, heni *Iohane baptisi ye̱ tšutšu le̱, ni eyahĩ dše̱i. *1,28.
41Ni mei pī ba eṅō ni ame̱kē̱: Iohane efee okadi ko moṅ, ši nii fiā ní Iohane wie ye̱ nū ne̱ he le̱, ano̱kwaṅ.
42Ni mei pī he ene̱ ye ye̱ dše̱i.

english_text:
The Death of Lazarus
1-2 A man by the name of Lazarus was sick in the village of Bethany. He had two sisters, Mary and Martha. This was the same Mary who later poured perfume on the Lord's head and wiped his feet with her hair. 3The sisters sent a message to the Lord and told him that his good friend Lazarus was sick.
4When Jesus heard this, he said, “His sickness won't end in death. It will bring glory to God and his Son.”
5Jesus loved Martha and her sister and brother. 6But he stayed where he was for two more days. 7Then he said to his disciples, “Now we will go back to Judea.”
8“Teacher,” they said, “the people there want to stone you to death! Why do you want to go back?”
9Jesus answered, “Aren't there twelve hours in each day? If you walk during the day, you will have light from the sun, and you won't stumble. 10But if you walk during the night, you will stumble, because you don't have any light.” 11Then he told them, “Our friend Lazarus is asleep, and I am going there to wake him up.”
12They replied, “Lord, if he is asleep, he will get better.” 13Jesus really meant that Lazarus was dead, but they thought he was talking only about sleep.
14Then Jesus told them plainly, “Lazarus is dead! 15I am glad I wasn't there, because now you will have a chance to put your faith in me. Let's go to him.”
16Thomas, whose nickname was “Twin,” said to the other disciples, “Come on. Let's go, so we can die with him.”
Jesus Brings Lazarus to Life
17When Jesus got to Bethany, he found that Lazarus had already been in the tomb four days. 18Bethany was less than three kilometers from Jerusalem, 19and many people had come from the city to comfort Martha and Mary because their brother had died.
20When Martha heard that Jesus had arrived, she went out to meet him, but Mary stayed in the house. 21Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died. 22Yet even now I know that God will do anything you ask.”
23Jesus told her, “Your brother will live again!”
24 Martha answered, “I know he will be raised to life on the last day, when all the dead are raised.”
25Jesus then said, “I am the one who raises the dead to life! Everyone who has faith in me will live, even if they die. 26And everyone who lives because of faith in me will never really die. Do you believe this?”
27“Yes, Lord!” she replied. “I believe you are the Christ, the Son of God. You are the one we hoped would come into the world.”
28After Martha said this, she went and privately said to her sister Mary, “The Teacher is here, and he wants to see you.” 29As soon as Mary heard this, she got up and went out to Jesus. 30He was still outside the village where Martha had gone to meet him. 31Many people had come to comfort Mary, and when they saw her quickly leave the house, they thought she was going out to the tomb to cry. So they followed her.
32Mary went to where Jesus was. Then as soon as she saw him, she knelt at his feet and said, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.”
33When Jesus saw that Mary and the people with her were crying, he was terribly upset 34and asked, “Where have you put his body?”
They replied, “Lord, come and you will see.”
35Jesus started crying, 36and the people said, “See how much he loved Lazarus.”
37Some of them said, “He gives sight to the blind. Why couldn't he have kept Lazarus from dying?”
38Jesus was still terribly upset. So he went to the tomb, which was a cave with a stone rolled against the entrance. 39Then he told the people to roll the stone away. But Martha said, “Lord, you know that Lazarus has been dead four days, and there will be a bad smell.”
40Jesus replied, “Didn't I tell you that if you had faith, you would see the glory of God?”
41After the stone had been rolled aside, Jesus looked up toward heaven and prayed, “Father, I thank you for answering my prayer. 42I know that you always answer my prayers. But I said this, so the people here would believe you sent me.”
43When Jesus had finished praying, he shouted, “Lazarus, come out!” 44The man who had been dead came out. His hands and feet were wrapped with strips of burial cloth, and a cloth covered his face.
Jesus then told the people, “Untie him and let him go.”
The Plot To Kill Jesus
(Matthew 26.1-5; Mark 14.1,2; Luke 22.1,2)
45Many of the people who had come to visit Mary saw the things Jesus did, and they put their faith in him. 46Others went to the Pharisees and told what Jesus had done. 47Then the chief priests and the Pharisees called the council together and said, “What should we do? This man is working a lot of miracles. 48If we don't stop him now, everyone will put their faith in him. Then the Romans will come and destroy our temple and our nation.”
49One of the council members was Caiaphas, who was also high priest that year. He spoke up and said, “You people don't have any sense at all! 50Don't you know it is better for one person to die for the people than for the whole nation to be destroyed?” 51Caiaphas did not say this on his own. As high priest that year, he was prophesying that Jesus would die for the nation. 52Yet Jesus would not die just for the Jewish nation. He would die to bring together all of God's scattered people. 53From that day on, the council started making plans to put Jesus to death.
54Because of this plot against him, Jesus stopped going around in public. He went to the town of Ephraim, which was near the desert, and he stayed there with his disciples.
55It was almost time for Passover. Many of the Jewish people who lived out in the country had come to Jerusalem to get themselves ready for the festival. 56They looked around for Jesus. Then when they were in the temple, they asked each other, “You don't think he will come here for Passover, do you?”
57The chief priests and the Pharisees told the people to let them know if any of them saw Jesus. This is how they hoped to arrest him.
translation_text:
1Ši nū ko ní atšé̱o̱le̱ Lazaro, ni dše̱ Betania, *Maria ke̱ enyemi Marta mei akrowa le̱, he mīye. *Luk. 10,38. 39.
2(Ši Maria le̱ ní ṅõ mũ-ke̱-ṅma ekpá Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ ni eke̱ eyitšo̱i tšumo̱ enãdši ahe le̱ noṅṅ enyemi Lazaro he yeo ne̱.) 12,3.
3Nohewo̱ le̱ enyemimeiyei le̱ tšũ aba eṅõ abakē̱ ake̱: Nuṅtšo̱, na, moni osumoo̱le̱ he mīye.
4Ši beni Iesu nu ene̱ le̱, ekē̱: Ne̱ke̱ hela ne̱ dšee gbĕle hela ni, ši moṅ *Nyoṅmo̱ anumnyam le̱ hewo̱ ni, heni afe ni awo Nyoṅmo̱ bi le̱ hĩe nyam. *9,3.
5Ši Iesu sumoo̱ Marta ke̱ enyemiyō le̱ ke̱ Lazaro fẽ.
6Ši beni ena ake̱ ehe mīye le̱, no se̱ le̱ ehĩ ši ye̱ heni eyo̱ le̱ noṅṅ gbĩĩ enyo̱.
7Ni no se̱ le̱ ekē̱ ekaselo̱i le̱ ake̱: Nyehăa wo̱yaä Iudea ekoṅ.
8Kaselo̱i le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Rabi, *eyeko gbĩko ni Iudafoi le̱ tao bo te̱i atſia le̱, ni ōya dše̱i ekoṅ lo? *8,59; 10,31.
9Iesu here no̱ ake̱: Ani dšee ṅmle̱tſāi nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱ yo̱ dšenamo̱ mli? Ke̱dši mo nyie ſane le̱, ete̱e̱, edšake̱ enaä dše ne̱ mli la le̱. 9,4. 5.
10Ši ke̱dši mo nyie nyōṅ le̱, no ete̱o̱, edšake̱ la be̱ emli. 12,35.
11Ewie nii ne̱, ni no se̱ le̱ ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Wo̱šientše̱ Lazaro *ewo̱; ši mīya ni mayatšĩele̱ ye̱ wo̱ le̱ mli. *Mat. 9,24.
12Ke̱ke̱ ni ekaselo̱i le̱ kē̱: Nuṅtšo̱, ké̱ wo̱ ewo̱ le̱, no le̱ ehe bawale̱ mo̱.
13Ši egbĕle he Iesu wie le̱; ši ame̱ le̱ ame̱susu ake̱ wo̱ kpakpa hewo̱ ewie.
14Agbe̱ne̱ Iesu kē̱ame̱ ſaṅṅ ake̱: Lazaro égbo;
15ni nyehewo̱ le̱ eṅõ minā ake̱ mibe̱ dše̱i le̱, beni afe ní nyehe nyeye; ši nyehãa wo̱yaä eṅõ.
16Ke̱ke̱ le̱ Toma, moni atšé̱o̱le̱ Didimo le̱, kē̱ enanemei kaselo̱i le̱ ake̱: Nyehãa wo̱ hũ wo̱yaä, ní wo̱ke̱le̱ ayagbo.
17Agbe̱ne̱, beni Iesu še̱ dše̱i le̱, ebana ake̱ eye gbĩĩ edſe̱ momo ye̱ bu leṅ.
18Ši Betania ke̱ Ierusalem teṅ dšeke̱mo̱ aafe stadioi nyoṅma ke̱ enumo̱.
19Ni Iudafoi le̱ ateṅ mei pī éba Marta ke̱ Maria mei aṅõ, koni ame̱bayeame̱ ṅko̱mo̱ ye̱ ame̱nyeminū le̱ gbĕle le̱ hewo̱.
20Ke̱ke̱ le̱, beni Marta nu ake̱ Iesu mība le̱, ete ni eyakpele̱; ši Maria le̱, le̱ le̱ etá šĩa le̱.
21Agbe̱ne̱ Marta bakē̱ Iesu ake̱: Nuṅtšo̱, edši oye̱ bie̱ kũle̱, minyemi le̱ náá agbo.
22Ši agbe̱ne̱ hũ tete po mile ake̱, nofẽno ní oobi Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, Nyoṅmo̱ aahão.
23Iesu kē̱le̱ ake̱: Onyeminū le̱ bate ši.
24Marta kē̱le̱ ake̱: Mile ake̱ *ebate ši ye̱ ghohĩĩašitē le̱ mli ye nāgbēgbĩ le̱ no̱. *5,29; 6,40. Luk. 14.14.
25Iesu kē̱le̱ ake̱: Mi le̱ midši šitē le̱ ke̱ wala le̱; moni heo̱ mino̱ eyeo̱ le̱, ke̱dši egbo tete le̱, ehĩe aakã;
26ni mofẽmo ní hĩe kã ní eheo̱ mino̱ eyeo̱ le̱, egboṅ gbĩkogbĩko ke̱-ate nāno̱. Oheo̱ ene̱ oyeo̱ lo? 8,51.
27Ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Hē̃, Nuṅtšo̱; mīhe mīye ake̱ bo dši Kristo, Nyoṅmo̱ bi le̱ ní baä dše le̱ mli le̱. 6,69.
28Ni beni ekē̱ ne̱ke̱ le̱, eyiṅ ete, ni eyatšé̱ enyemi Maria le̱ nĩgĩ, ekē̱: Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ éba, ni ētšé̱o.
29Le̱ le̱, beni enu le̱, ete ši oyá ni eba eṅõ.
30Ši Iesu náko áše̱ akrowa le̱, ši eye hégbe̱ *ní Marta ke̱le̱ kpe ye le̱ lolo. *K. 20.
31Ke̱ke̱ le̱, beni Iudafoi le̱ ni ke̱le̱ yo̱ šīa le̱ ni ame̱yeo̱le̱ ṅko̱mo̱ le̱ na ake̱ Maria eša ehe ke̱-dše kpo le̱, ame̱tiule̱, amesusu ake̱, bene̱ ēya fū̃he le̱ eyafó ye̱ dše̱i.
32Agbe̱ne̱, beni Maria ba heni Iesu yo̱ le̱ ni enale̱ le̱, eho egbē enãdši anā, ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Nuṅtšo̱, edši oye̱ bie̱ kũle̱, minyemi le̱ náá agbo.
33Agbe̱ne̱, beni Iesu nale̱ ake̱ ēfó, ke̱ Iudafoi le̱ hũ ní ke̱le̱ ba le̱, ake̱ ame̱ hũ ame̱mīfó le̱, ehũṅ ye̱ emumo̱ mli ni *ekpokpo; *13,21.
34ni ekē̱: Nẽgbe̱ nyetole̱ ye̱? Ame̱kē̱le̱ ake̱: Nuṅtšo̱, ba ní obakwe̱.
35Ni Iesu fó. Luk. 19,41.
36Ke̱ke̱ le̱ Iudafoi le̱ kē̱: Kwe̱, bo̱ni edo̱ö̱ ehe!
37Ši ame̱teṅ meikomei kē̱: Nū ne̱ ní gble ſilafo le̱ hĩṅme̱ii le̱, aso enyẽṅ efe ní kũle̱ nū ne̱ akagbo?
38Ke̱ke̱ ni Iesu sā hũṅ ye̱ emli ekoṅ, ni ete fū̃he le̱; ši te̱-kplo ni, ni *te̱ bu nā. *Mat. 27,60.
39Iesu kē̱: Nyedšiea te̱ le̱. Marta, moni egbo le̱ nyemiyō le̱, kē̱le̱ ake̱: Nuṅtšo̱, be ne̱ mli le̱ eša, edšake̱ éye gbĩĩ edſe̱.
40Iesu kē̱le̱ ake̱: Ani mikē̱ē̱o ake̱: Ke̱dši ohe oye le̱, oona *Nyoṅmo̱ anumnyam le̱? *K. 4. 23. 25. 26.
41Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱dšie te̱ le̱ ye̱ heni gbonyo le̱ kã le̱. Ni Iesu hole ehĩṅme̱ii ano̱ ke̱-te ṅwei ni ekē̱: Atā, mīdao ši ake̱ obomi toi le̱.
42Ši mi le̱, mile ake̱ dā oboo̱mi toi; ši *asafo le̱ ní damo̱ ši le̱ hewo̱ mikē̱o̱, koni amehe ame̱ye ake̱ bo otšũmi. *12,30.
43Ni beni éwie ne̱ke̱ le̱, ebo ke̱ gbē wā ake̱: Lazaro ē, dše kpo!
44Ni gbonyo le̱ dše kpo, fū̃-mamai le̱ fĩmo̱ enãdši ke̱ enidši, ni duku fĩ ehĩe. Iesu kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nyefẽneale̱, ní nyehãa eyaä.
45Nohewo̱ le̱ Iudafoi le̱ ní ba Maria ṅõ le̱ ateṅ mei pī he eno̱ ye, beni ame̱na nii ni Iesu fe le̱.
46Ši ame̱teṅ meikomei yiṅ te Farisifoi le̱ aṅõ, ni ame̱yagbaame̱ nii ní Iesu fe le̱.
47Nohewo̱ le̱ oso̱fonukpai le̱ ke̱ Farisifoi le̱ tšé̱ kpē, ni ame̱kē̱: Té wo̱feo̱ tēṅ? ši nūu ne̱ mīfe okadii sro̱toi pī.
48Ke̱dši wo̱ṅmẽle̱ gbe ne̱ke̱ le̱, mei fẽ aahe eno̱ aye; ni Romabii le̱ aaba ni ame̱abašõ wo̱maṅ ke̱ wo̱sikpoṅ le̱ fẽ.
49Ši ame̱teṅ mokome, Kaiafa ní yeo̱ oso̱fonukpa ye̱ nakai afi le̱ mli le̱, kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Nye le̱ nyelee noko kwrā,
50ni nyesa nyedſẽṅṅ hũ ake̱ ehĩ hãwo̱ ake̱ mokome agbo ye̱ maṅ le̱ nãdšĩaṅ, fè noni maṅbii le̱ fẽ hĩe aakpãtã le̱. 18,14.
51Ši ene̱ le̱, dšee le̱dientše̱ eto eyi ewie; ši moṅ, edšake̱ oso̱fonukpa dšile̱ ye̱ nakai afi le̱ no̱ hewo̱ le̱, *gba egba ake Iesu bagbo ye̱ maṅ le̱ nãdšĩaṅ; *2 Mose 28,30. 4 Mose 27,21.
52ni dšee ye̱ maṅ le̱ ke̱ke̱ nãdsiaṅ hewo̱ṅ, ši beni afe ní ebua Nyoṅmo̱ bii ni egbe̱ eſã le hũ nā *efe ekome. *10,16.
53Ni ke̱-dše̱ nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱ le̱ ame̱kpe̱ ame̱yiṅ ake̱ ame̱bagbele̱.
54Nohewo̱ le̱ Iesu edšee faṅṅ enyiee ye̱ Iudafoi le̱ ateṅ doṅṅ, ši edše dše̱i ete šikpoṅ ko ni kã ṅã le̱ nā le̱ no̱, ye̱ maṅ ko ní atšé̱o̱ Efraim le mli, ni eke̱ ekaselo̱i le̱ yahĩ dše̱i.
55Agbene Iudafoi le̱ a-Hehō le̱ éše̱ étã. Ni mei babaō dše̱ šikpoṅ le̱ fẽ no̱ ame̱te Ierusalem, dãni Hehō le̱ aše̱, *koni ame̱yatšū ame̱he. *2 Kron. 30,17.
56Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱bõi Iesu taomo̱, ni beni ame̱damo̱damo̱ ši ye̱ so̱lemo̱we le̱, ame̱kē̱kē̱ ame̱he ake̱: Té nyesusuo̱ tēṅ, ani ebaṅ gbĩdšŭrõ le̱?
57Ši oso̱fonukpai le̱ ke̱ Farisifoi le̱ éwo kitã ake̱, ké̱ moko le heni eyo̱ le̱, étſa he adafi, koni ayamõle̱.

english_text:
At Bethany
(Matthew 26.6-13; Mark 14.3-9)
1Six days before Passover Jesus went back to Bethany, where he had raised Lazarus from death. 2A meal had been prepared for Jesus. Martha was doing the serving, and Lazarus himself was there.
3 Mary took a very expensive bottle of perfume and poured it on Jesus' feet. She wiped them with her hair, and the sweet smell of the perfume filled the house.
4A disciple named Judas Iscariot was there. He was the one who was going to betray Jesus, and he asked, 5“Why wasn't this perfume sold for 300 silver coins and the money given to the poor?” 6Judas did not really care about the poor. He asked this because he carried the moneybag and sometimes would steal from it.
7Jesus replied, “Leave her alone! She has kept this perfume for the day of my burial. 8 You will always have the poor with you, but you won't always have me.”
A Plot To Kill Lazarus
9A lot of people came when they heard that Jesus was there. They also wanted to see Lazarus, because Jesus had raised him from death. 10So the chief priests made plans to kill Lazarus. 11He was the reason that many of the people were turning from them and putting their faith in Jesus.
Jesus Enters Jerusalem
(Matthew 21.1-11; Mark 11.1-11; Luke 19.28-40)
12The next day a large crowd was in Jerusalem for Passover. When they heard that Jesus was coming for the festival, 13 they took palm branches and went out to greet him. They shouted,
“Hooray!
God bless the one who comes
in the name of the Lord!
God bless the King
of Israel!”
14Jesus found a donkey and rode on it, just as the Scriptures say,
15 “People of Jerusalem,
don't be afraid!
Your King is now coming,
and he is riding
on a donkey.”
16At first, Jesus' disciples did not understand. But after he had been given his glory, they remembered all this. Everything had happened exactly as the Scriptures said it would.
17-18A crowd had come to meet Jesus because they had seen him call Lazarus out of the tomb. They kept talking about him and this miracle. 19But the Pharisees said to each other, “There is nothing we can do! Everyone in the world is following Jesus.”
Some Greeks Want To Meet Jesus
20Some Greeks had gone to Jerusalem to worship during Passover. 21Philip from Bethsaida in Galilee was there too. So they went to him and said, “Sir, we would like to meet Jesus.” 22Philip told Andrew. Then the two of them went to Jesus and told him.
The Son of Man Must Be Lifted Up
23Jesus said:
The time has come for the Son of Man to be given his glory. 24I tell you for certain that a grain of wheat that falls on the ground will never be more than one grain unless it dies. But if it dies, it will produce lots of wheat. 25 If you love your life, you will lose it. If you give it up in this world, you will be given eternal life. 26If you serve me, you must go with me. My servants will be with me wherever I am. If you serve me, my Father will honor you.
27Now I am deeply troubled, and I don't know what to say. But I must not ask my Father to keep me from this time of suffering. In fact, I came into the world to suffer. 28So Father, bring glory to yourself.
A voice from heaven then said, “I have already brought glory to myself, and I will do it again!” 29When the crowd heard the voice, some of them thought it was thunder. Others thought an angel had spoken to Jesus.
30Then Jesus told the crowd, “That voice spoke to help you, not me. 31This world's people are now being judged, and the ruler of this world is already being thrown out! 32If I am lifted up above the earth, I will make everyone want to come to me.” 33Jesus was talking about the way he would be put to death.
34 The crowd said to Jesus, “The Scriptures teach that the Messiah will live forever. How can you say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?”
35Jesus answered, “The light will be with you for only a little longer. Walk in the light while you can. Then you won't be caught walking blindly in the dark. 36Have faith in the light while it is with you, and you will be children of the light.”
The People Refuse To Have Faith in Jesus
After Jesus had said these things, he left and went into hiding. 37He had worked a lot of miracles among the people, but they were still not willing to have faith in him. 38 This happened so that what the prophet Isaiah had said would come true,
“Lord, who has believed
our message?
And who has seen
your mighty strength?”
39The people could not have faith in Jesus, because Isaiah had also said,
40 “The Lord has blinded
the eyes of the people,
and he has made
the people stubborn.
He did this so that they
could not see
or understand,
and so that they
would not turn to the Lord
and be healed.”
41Isaiah said this, because he saw the glory of Jesus and spoke about him. 42Even then, many of the leaders put their faith in Jesus, but they did not tell anyone about it. The Pharisees had already given orders for the people not to have anything to do with anyone who had faith in Jesus. 43And besides, the leaders liked praise from others more than they liked praise from God.
Jesus Came To Save the World
44In a loud voice Jesus said:
Everyone who has faith in me also has faith in the one who sent me. 45And everyone who has seen me has seen the one who sent me. 46I am the light that has come into the world. No one who has faith in me will stay in the dark.
47I am not the one who will judge those who refuse to obey my teachings. I came to save the people of this world, not to be their judge. 48But everyone who rejects me and my teachings will be judged on the last day by what I have said. 49I don't speak on my own. I say only what the Father who sent me has told me to say. 50I know that his commands will bring eternal life. This is why I tell you exactly what the Father has told me.

(12,1-8. Mat. 26,6-13. Mar. 14,3-9.)
1Agbe̱ne̱, beni eſe̱ gbĩĩ ekpa ni ayeo̱ Hehō le̱, Iesu ha Betania, heni Lazaro, moni gbo ni etēle̱ ši ke̱-dše̱ gbohĩĩ ateṅ le̱, yo̱ le̱. 11,1. 43.
2Ke̱ke̱ ni ame̱ṅmēle̱ okplõ ye̱ dše̱i, ni Marta súmo̱, ši Lazaro dši mei ní ke̱le̱ trá okplõ le̱ he le̱ ateṅ mokome.
3Agbe̱ne̱ Maria ṅõ nardo-mũ kro̱ṅṅ ní dšra wa naakpa ni ṅmẽo̱ nsẽnite̱ kome, nĩ eke̱-bakpá Iesu nãdšĩ ahe, ni eke̱ eyitšo̱ì le̱ tšumo̱ enãdši le̱ ahe; nĩ mũ le̱ ṅma yi šĩa le̱ to̱. Luk. 7,38.
4Ke̱ke̱ ni Iuda Iskariot, Simon bi le̱, ekaselo̱i le̱ ateṅ mokome, ni batšõ ese̱gbe̱ le̱, kē̱:
5Mẽhewo̱ ahõõ mũ ne̱ ahee denarioi ohai-etẽ, ní aṅõ-hã ohĩafoi?
6Ši ene̱ ni ekē̱ ne̱, dšee ohĩafoi le̱ ahe ni do̱ö̱le̱ hewo̱ṅ, ši moṅ dšulo̱ dšile̱, ni le̱ etoo̱ fotro le̱ ni ehĩeo̱ *noni aṅõwoo̱ mli le̱. *Luk. 8,3.
7Nohewo̱ le̱ Iesu kē̱: Kāgba enā; efe ene̱ eto mifũ gbĩ le̱.
8Edšake̱ *ohĩafoi le̱, nyeke̱ame̱ ye̱ dā; ši mi le, dšee dā nyekemi yo̱. *5 Mose 15,11.
9Agbe̱ne̱ Iudafoi le̱ ateṅ mei pī ná le ake̱ eye̱ dše̱i, ni ame̱ba, dšee Iesu ke̱ke̱ hewo̱ṅ, ši moṅ koni ame̱na Lazaro moni etele̱ ši ke̱-dše̱ gbohĩĩ ateṅ le̱ hũ.
10Ni oso̱fonukpai le̱ kpe ame̱yiṅ ake̱, ame̱agbe Lazaro hũ;
11ehewo̱ dše̱ ni Iudafoi le̱ ateṅ mei pī te ni ame̱yahe Iesu no̱ ame̱ye le̱.
(12-19. Mat. 21,1-11. Mar. 11,1-10. Luk. 19,29-40.)
12Dšetše̱reno̱ le̱ mei babaō ni éba gbĩdšŭrõ le̱, beni amenu ake̱ Iesu mība Ierusalem le̱,
13ame̱kŏ̱lo̱ ble̱oi, ni ame̱dše kpo ame̱yakpele̱, ni ame̱blo̱ ake̱: *Hosiana! Adšō̱ moni baä ye̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ gbe̱i ano̱ le̱, Israel maṅtše̱ le̱! *Lal. 118,25. 26.
14Ši Iesu ená tedšibi ko ni eho etá no̱, take̱ bo̱ni *aṅmã le̱ ake̱: *Zak. 9,9.
15“Kāše gbeyei, Zion biyō; na, omaṅtše̱ le̱ tá tedšibi no̱ ke̱-mība.”
16Ši ekaselo̱i le̱ enaa nii ne̱ ašiši mrã mli, ši beni awo Iesu hĩe nyam le̱, no dãni ame̱kai ake̱ aṅmã nii ne̱ ye ehewo̱, ni no afe ahãle̱ le̱.
17Agbe̱ne̱ asafo ni ke̱le̱ yo̱ be mli ni etšé̱ Lazaro ke̱-dše̱ gbonyobu le̱ mli ni etēle̱ ši ke̱-dše̱ gbohĩĩ ateṅ le̱ ye he odase.
18Ene̱hewo̱ hũ ni asafo le̱ yakpele̱ le̱, edšake̱ amenu ake̱ efe okadi ne̱.
19Nohewo̱ le̱ Farisifoi le̱ kē̱ ye̱ ame̱teṅ ake̱: Té nyena ake̱ nyenyẽẽ fē̱i nyefe; na, *dše le̱ efã ke̱-nyie ese le̱. 11,48.
20Ši Helabii komei ye̱ mei ni ba koni ame̱badšá Nyoṅmo̱ ye̱ gbĩdšŭrõ le̱ no̱ le̱ ateṅ;
21mene̱mei ba Filipo *ni dše̱ Betsaida ye̱ Galilea le̱ ṅõ, ni ame̱babile̱ ake̱: Nuṅtšo̱, wo̱mītao ake̱ wo̱na Iesu. *1,44.
22Filipo ba ni ebakē̱ Andrea, ni asaṅ Andrea ke̱ Filipo bakē̱ Iesu.
23Ni Iesu hereame̱ no̱ ekē̱: Ṅmletſā ní ake̱-bawo gbomobi le̱ hĩe nyam le̱ eše̱.
24Le̱le̱ṅ, le̱le̱ṅ, mīkē̱nye ake̱: Ké̱ *ṅmā̃kuli enyõõ šikpoṅ ní egbo le̱, no le̱ bo̱ni eyo̱ le̱ noṅṅ eyo̱; ši ke̱dši egbo le̱, ewoo̱ yibii pī. *Rom 14,9.
25Moni do̱ö̱ ewala he le̱, elādšeo̱le̱, ši moni nye̱o̱ ewala ye̱ dše ne̱ mli le̱, eetole̱ ke̱-ate nāno̱ wala mli. Mat. 10,39. Luk. 17,38.
26Ke̱dši moko mīsúmo̱mi le̱, hã ní enyie mise̱, ni heni *miyo̱ le̱, dše̱i misúolo̱ le̱ hũ aahĩ; ke̱dši moko mīsúmo̱mi le̱, mitše̱ le̱ aawole̱. *14,3; 17,24.
27Agbene *misusuma mihao, ni meni makē̱? Atā, heremo̱mi ye̱ ṅmle̱tſā ne̱ mli? Tše̱bele̱ ene̱ hewo̱ noṅṅ miba ye̱ ṅmle̱tſā ne̱ mli. *Mat. 26,38.
28Atā, wo ogbe̱i le̱ hĩe nyam! Ke̱ke̱ ni gbē ko dše̱ ṅwei kē̱: Mi ná miwo ehĩe nyam, ni masā mawo ehĩe nyam ekoṅ.
29Ke̱ke̱ ni mei ní damo̱ dše̱i ní nu le̱ kē̱ ake̱: Nyoṅmo̱ éši; meikomei hũ kē̱: Ṅweibo̱fo ko ke̱le̱ éwie.
30Iesu here no̱ ni ekē̱: Dšee mihewo̱ gbē ne̱ ba, ši *nye moṅ nyehewoṅ. *11,42.
31Agbe̱ne̱ dše ne̱ṅ kodšomo̱ le̱ eše: kpāko abafã dše ne̱ṅ lumo̱ le̱ aše̱ afõ; 14,30; 16,11. Luk. 10,18.
32ni mi le̱, ke̱dši *awó mino̱ ke̱-dše̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱ le̱, magbla mei fẽ ke̱-aba miṅõ. *8,28.
33Ši ene̱ le̱ ekē̱ eke̱-tšõ nõ gbĕle ní ebagbo le̱.
34Asafo le̱ herele̱ no̱ ake̱: Wo̱ le̱ wonu ye̱ mla le̱ mli ake̱ Kristo le̱ *hĩo̱ ši ke̱-yaä nāno̱; ni té tēṅ ní bo le̱ okē̱o̱ ake̱: Dša awó gbomobi le̱ no̱ṅ? Namo dši ne̱ke̱ gbomobi ne̱? *Lal. 110,4. Dan. 7,14.
35Ke̱ke̱ le̱ Iesu kē̱ame̱ ake̱: Be kukuō ke̱ke̱ eſe̱ ehã *la le̱ ye̱ nyeteṅ. Gbĩĩ abo̱ ní nyeyo̱ la le̱ ne̱, nyenyiea, koni duṅ akabaninanye; ši †moni nyieo̱ duṅ mli le̱, elee heni eyaä. *8,12; †11,10.
36Gbĩĩ abo̱ ní nyeyo̱ la le̱ ne̱, nyehea la le̱ no̱ nyeyea, koni *nyetšṍmo̱ la-bii. Iesu wie nii ne̱, ni eyiṅ ete ni eyatē ehe ye̱ ame̱hĩe. Ef. 5,9.
37Tše̱bele̱ éfe okadii wudši ye̱ ame̱hĩe, ši kẽle̱ ame̱hee eno̱ ame̱yee;
38koni gbalo̱ Iesaia wiemo̱ ni ewie le̱ ana aba mli ake̱: *“Nuṅtšo̱, namo ehe wo̱sane le̱ eye, ni namo adšie Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ nine le̱ kpo atsõ?” *Ies. 53,1. Rom. 10,16.
39Ene̱hewo̱ ni ame̱nyẽẽ ame̱he ame̱ye le̱, edšake̱ Iesaia sã kē̱ ekoṅ ake̱: Ies. 6,9. 10. Mat. 13,14. 15.
40“Eſila ame̱hĩṅme̱ii, ni ekplim ame̱tšuii; koni ame̱kana ke̱ ame̱hĩṅme̱ii, ni ame̱na nā ke̱ ame̱tšuĩi, ní ame̱kũ ame̱se̱, ni mĩtšáame̱.”
41Nii ne̱ Iesaia kē̱, edšake̱ ena *enumnyam le̱, ni ewie ehe. *Ies. 6,1.
42Tše̱bele̱ onukpai le̱ tete ateṅ mei pī he eno̱ ye, ši kẽle̱ Farisifoi le̱ ahewo̱ le̱ ame̱dšadšee faṅṅ, koni *akaſieame̱ ke̱-dše̱ kpēhe le̱; *9,22.
43edšake̱ ame̱mīsumo̱ gbomei ahĩenyam fè Nyoṅmo̱ nõ. 5,44.
44Ši Iesu bo ekē̱ ake̱: Moni heo̱ mino̱ eyeo̱ le̱, dšee mi mino̱ eheo̱ eyeo̱ le̱, ši moṅ moni tšũmi le̱;
45ni *moni naämi le̱ naä moni tšũmi le̱. *14,9.
46Mi le̱ miba dše le̱ mli ake̱ la, koni mofẽmo ní heo̱ mino̱ yeo̱ le̱ akahī duṅ le̱ mli. K. 35.
47Ni ke̱dši moko nu miwiemo̱i le̱ ni eyee no̱ le̱, mi le̱, mikodšoole̱; edšake̱ mibaa koni mibakodšo dše le̱, ši moṅ miba koni mibahere dše le̱ yiwala. 8,17. Luk. 9,56.
48Moni kwaämi ni emõõ miwiemo̱i le̱ amli le̱, eye̱ moko ní kodšoo̱le̱; wiemo̱ ní míwie le̱, no noṅṅ aakodšole̱ ye̱ nāgbēgbĩ le̱ no̱.
49Edšake̱ mi le̱ mitoo midientše̱ miyi miwiee; ši tše̱ ní tšũmi le̱, le̱ moṅ ewomi kitã, noni mikē̱ ke̱ noni míwie.
50Ni mile ake̱ ekitã le̱ nāno̱ wala ni; nohewo̱ le nofẽno ní miwieo̱ le̱, bo̱ni tše̱ le̱ ékē̱mi le̱, nakai miwieo̱.

english_text:
Jesus Washes the Feet of His Disciples
1It was before Passover, and Jesus knew that the time had come for him to leave this world and to return to the Father. He had always loved his followers in this world, and he loved them to the very end.
2Even before the evening meal started, the devil had made Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, decide to betray Jesus.
3Jesus knew he had come from God and would go back to God. He also knew that the Father had given him complete power. 4So during the meal Jesus got up, removed his outer garment, and wrapped a towel around his waist. 5He put some water into a large bowl. Then he began washing his disciples' feet and drying them with the towel he was wearing.
6But when he came to Simon Peter, this disciple asked, “Lord, are you going to wash my feet?”
7Jesus answered, “You don't really know what I am doing, but later you will understand.”
8“You will never wash my feet!” Peter replied.
“If I don't wash you,” Jesus told him, “you don't really belong to me.”
9Peter said, “Lord, don't wash just my feet. Wash my hands and my head.”
10Jesus answered, “People who have bathed and are clean all over need to wash just their feet. And you, my disciples, are clean, except for one of you.” 11Jesus knew who would betray him. That is why he said, “except for one of you.”
12 After Jesus had washed his disciples' feet and had put his outer garment back on, he sat down again. Then he said:
Do you understand what I have done? 13You call me your teacher and Lord, and you should, because that is who I am. 14And if your Lord and teacher has washed your feet, you should do the same for each other. 15I have set the example, and you should do for each other exactly what I have done for you. 16 I tell you for certain that servants are not greater than their master, and messengers are not greater than the one who sent them. 17You know these things, and God will bless you, if you do them.
18 I am not talking about all of you. I know the ones I have chosen. But what the Scriptures say must come true. And they say, “The man who ate with me has turned against me!” 19I am telling you this before it all happens. Then when it does happen, you will believe who I am. 20 I tell you for certain that anyone who welcomes my messengers also welcomes me, and anyone who welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me.
Jesus Tells What Will Happen to Him
(Matthew 26.20-25; Mark 14.17-21; Luke 22.21-23)
21After Jesus had said these things, he was deeply troubled and told his disciples, “I tell you for certain that one of you will betray me.” 22They were confused about what he meant. And they just stared at each other.
23Jesus' favorite disciple was sitting next to him at the meal, 24and Simon motioned for this disciple to find out which one Jesus meant. 25So the disciple leaned toward Jesus and asked, “Lord, which one of us are you talking about?”
26Jesus answered, “I will dip this piece of bread in the sauce and give it to the one I was talking about.”
Then Jesus dipped the bread and gave it to Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot. 27Right then Satan took control of Judas.
Jesus said, “Judas, go quickly and do what you have to do.” 28No one at the meal understood what Jesus meant. 29But because Judas was in charge of the money, some of them thought that Jesus had told him to buy something they needed for the festival. Others thought that Jesus had told him to give some money to the poor. 30Judas took the piece of bread and went out.
It was already night.
The New Command
31After Judas had gone, Jesus said:
Now the Son of Man will be given glory, and he will bring glory to God. 32Then, after God is given glory because of him, God will bring glory to him, and God will do it very soon.
33 My children, I will be with you for only a little while longer. Then you will look for me, but you won't find me. I tell you just as I told the people, “You cannot go where I am going.” 34 But I am giving you a new command. You must love each other, just as I have loved you. 35If you love each other, everyone will know that you are my disciples.
Peter's Promise
(Matthew 26.31-35; Mark 14.27-31; Luke 22.31-34)
36Simon Peter asked, “Lord, where are you going?”
Jesus answered, “You can't go with me now, but later on you will.”
37Peter asked, “Lord, why can't I go with you now? I would die for you!”
38“Would you really die for me?” Jesus asked. “I tell you for certain before a rooster crows, you will say three times that you don't even know me.”
translation_text:
1Ši dãni Hehō gbĩdšŭrõ le̱ aaše̱ le̱, ake̱-ní Iesu le ake̱ eṅmle̱tſā ní eke̱-badše dše ne̱ mli ke̱-ya tše̱ le̱ ṅõ le̱ eše̱ hewo̱ le̱, bo̱ni esumoo̱ emei ni yo̱ dše le̱ṅ le̱, nakai esumo̱ame̱ ke̱-wula ši.
2Ni beni ame̱yeo̱ nii le̱, — bĕle̱ *abonsam éṅõ-wo Iuda Iskariot, Simon bi le̱, tšui mli momo, ake̱ etšõ ese̱gbe̱, — *Luk. 22,3.
3ni Iesu le ake̱ *tše̱ le̱ étu nii fẽ éwo edeṅ, ni ake̱ †Nyoṅmo̱ ṅõ edše̱ ni esa ēya Nyoṅmo̱ ṅõ le̱: *3,35; †16,28.
4ete ši ye̱ niyenii le̱ aši, ni edšie etadei le̱ eſie ši, ni eko̱ papaṅ ni eṅõ-ṅmõ ehe.
5No se̱ le̱ efo̱se nu ewo kulo mli, ni ebõi ekaselo̱i le̱ anãdši ahe fo̱mo̱, ni eke̱ papaṅ ní ṅmõ ehe̱ le̱ tšumoo̱.
6Beni eše̱ Simon Petro no̱ lo̱, no kē̱le̱ ake̱: Nuṅtšo̱, bo ofo̱ö̱mi minādši ahe ne̱?
7Iesu here no̱ ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Noni mifeo̱ ne̱, amrõamrõ ne̱ olee, ši ké̱ fe se̱ le̱ obale.
8Petro kē̱le̱ ake̱: Kāfo̱ minādši ahe ko̱kō̱ko̱. Iesu herele̱ uo̱ ake̱: Ke̱dši mifo̱o̱ ohe le̱, obe̱ gbe̱fãṅnõ ko ye̱ miṅõ.
9Simon Petro kē̱le̱ ake̱: Nuṅtšo̱, dšee minãdši ahe ke̱ke̱, ši moṅ minidši ke̱ miyitšo hũ.
10Iesu kē̱le̱ ake̱: Moni adšu ehe le̱, ehĩaale̱ hefo̱flo̱mo̱, dša enãdši ahe ke̱ke̱, ši ehe edše ke̱-mõ ši; ni nye le̱ nyehe *edše moṅ, ši dšee nyefẽ ni. *15,3.
11Edšake̱ ele moni batšõ ese̱gbe̱ le̱; nohewo̱ ni ekē̱ ako̱: Dšee nyefẽ nyehe edše le̱. 6,64. 70. 71.
12Agbe̱ne̱, beni efo̱ ame̱nãdši ahe ni ekō̱lo̱ etadei le̱ ni eho etá ši ekoṅ le̱, ekē̱: Nyele noni mifenye ne̱ lo?
13Nye le̱ nyetšé̱o̱mi tšõlo̱ ke̱ Nuṅtšo̱; ni nyetõõ nā, edšake̱ nakai dšimi. Mat. 23,8. 10.
14Agbe̱ne̱, ke̱dši mi, tšõlo̱ ke̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱, mifo nyenãdši ahe le̱, esa ake̱ nye hũ nyefo̱fo̱ö̱ nyenanemei anãdši ahe. Luk. 22.27.
15Ši okadi mito mihãnye, koni bo̱ni mifenye ne̱, nye hũ nyefe nakai. Fil. 2,5. Kol. 3,18.
16Le̱le̱ṅ, le̱le̱ṅ, mīkē̱nye ake̱: Nyṍṅ efèè enuṅtšo̱, ni asaṅ bo̱fo efèè moni tšũle̱ le̱. Mat. 10,24.
17Ke̱dši nyele nii ne̱ ní nyeye no̱ le̱, adšō̱nye. Mat. 7,24.
18Dšee nyefẽ nyehe miwieo̱; mi le̱ mile mei ni mihala; ši moṅ beni afe ni *noni aṅmã le̱ aba mli ake̱: “Moni ke̱mi yeo̱ abolo le̱, áwó enanetšitši no ẽšími.” *Lal. 41,10.
19Agbe̱ne̱ mīkē̱nye mato dãni aba mli, koni ké̱ eba mli le̱ nyehé nyeye ake̱ mi ni.
20Le̱le̱ṅ, le̱le̱ṅ, mīkē̱nye ake̱: Moni hereo̱ moni mitšũo̱ le̱, mi noṅṅ ehereo̱ le̱; šĩ moni hereo̱mi le̱, ehereo̱ moni tšũmi le̱ hũ. Mat. 10,40.
(21-30. Mat. 26,21-25. Mar. 14,18-21. Luk. 22,21-25.)
21Beni ekē̱ nii ne̱ le̱, *ehao ye̱ mumo̱ mli, ni eye odase ekē̱: Le̱le̱ṅ, le̱le̱ṅ, mīkē̱nye ake̱: Nyeteṅ mokome batšõ mise̱gbe̱. *12,27.
22Ke̱ke̱ le̱ kaselo̱i le̱ kwe̱kwē̱ ame̱hĩeiaṅ, ni ame̱naa mokōme he ní ewieo̱ le̱.
23Ši kaselo̱i le̱ ateṅ *mokome ní Iesu sumoo̱ le̱ kpasa Iesu tšitši. *19,26; 20,2; 21,20.
24Nohewo̱ le̱ Simon Petro be̱le̱ hĩṅme̱i ake̱ ébile̱ mo he ní ewieo̱ le̱.
25Ši le̱ le̱ eho egbē Iesu tšitši no̱ ni ebile̱ ake̱: Nuntše̱, namo ni?
26Iesu here no̱ ake̱: Le̱ dši moni mike̱ atrõma le̱ batšo̱ mli mahãle̱ le̱. Ni eke̱ atrõma le̱ tšo̱ mli ni eṅõ-hã Iuda Iskariot, Simon bi le̱.
27Ni atrõma le̱ se̱ pe̱ ni *satan bote emli. Agbe̱ne̱ Iesu kē̱le̱ ake̱: Noni ofeo̱ le̱, femo̱ mrãmrã! *K. 2.
28Ši mei ní trá okplõ le̱ be le̱ ateṅ mokomoko lee nõhewo̱ ní ekē̱le̱ nakai le̱.
29Edšake̱ ame̱teṅ meikomei susu, ake̱-ní Iuda *too̱ fotro le̱, nohewo̱ ní Iesu kē̱le̱ ake̱: Yahe nii ní he hĩaãwo̱ oto gbìdšŭrõ le̱, alo ake̱ eṅõ noko ehã ohĩafoi. *12,6.
30Ke̱ke̱ le̱, beni ehé atrõma le̱ noṅṅ le̱, edše kpo. Ši dše éna.
31Ši beni edše kpo le̱, Iesu kē̱: Agbe̱ne̱ áwo gbomobi le̱ hĩe nyam, ni áwo Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe nyam ye̱ emli.
32Ke̱dši áwo Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe nyam ye̱ emli le̱, *Nyoṅmo̱ hũ aawo ehĩe nyam ye̱ le̱dientše̱ emli, ni eewo ehĩe nyam oyá. *12,23; 17,1-5.
33Bii bibii, be fiō ke̱ke̱ eſe̱ ni mike̱nye bahĩ ši; nyeataomi, ni bo̱ni mĩkē̱ *Iudafoi le̱ ake̱: Heni miyaä le̱, nye le̱ nyenyẽṅ dše̱i nyeba le̱, nakai mikē̱onye hũ agbe̱ne ne. *8,21.
34Kitã hē miṅõ-hãanye, ake̱ nyesumo̱ nyehe; take̱ bo̱ni misumo̱nye le̱, nakai nye hũ nye-sumo̱a nyehe. 15,12. 13. 17.
35Ke̱dši nyesumoo̱ nyehe le̱, no mei fẽ ke̱-ale ake̱ mikaselo̱i dšinye.
(36-38. Mat 26,33-35. Mar. 14,29-31. Luk. 22,31-34.)
36Simon Petro kē̱le̱ ake̱: Nuṅtšo̱, nẽgbe̱ oyaã? Iesu herele̱ no̱ ekē̱: Heni *miyaã le̱, onyẽṅ mise̱ onyie amrõ ne̱, ši oonyie mise̱ †wó̱se̱ ko. *7,34; †21,18. 19.
37Petro kē̱le̱ ake̱: Nuntše̱, mẽhewo̱ minyẽṅ ose̱ manyie amrõ ne̱? Miwala tete maṅõ-ṅmẽ ši ye̱ ohewo̱.
38Iesu herele̱ no̱ ake̱: Ooṅõ owala oṅmẽ ši ye̱ mihewo? Le̱le̱ṅ, le̱le̱ṅ, mīkē̱o ake̱: Wuo̱ náṅ agbe̱ ni ookpá ye̱ mise̱ šii etẽ.

english_text:
Jesus Is the Way to the Father
1Jesus said to his disciples, “Don't be worried! Have faith in God and have faith in me. 2There are many rooms in my Father's house. I wouldn't tell you this, unless it was true. I am going there to prepare a place for each of you. 3After I have done this, I will come back and take you with me. Then we will be together. 4You know the way to where I am going.”
5Thomas said, “Lord, we don't even know where you are going! How can we know the way?”
6 “I am the way, the truth, and the life!” Jesus answered. “Without me, no one can go to the Father. 7If you had really known me, you would have known the Father. But from now on, you do know him, and you have seen him.”
8Philip said, “Lord, show us the Father. That is all we need.”
9Jesus replied:
Philip, I have been with you for a long time. Don't you know who I am? If you have seen me, you have seen the Father. How can you ask me to show you the Father? 10Don't you believe that I am one with the Father and that the Father is one with me? What I say isn't said on my own. The Father who lives in me does these things.
11Have faith in me when I say that the Father is one with me and that I am one with the Father. Or else have faith in me simply because of the things I do. 12I tell you for certain that if you have faith in me, you will do the same things I am doing. You will do even greater things, now that I am going back to the Father. 13Ask me, and I will do whatever you ask. This way the Son will bring honor to the Father. 14I will do whatever you ask me to do.
The Holy Spirit Is Promised
15 Jesus said to his disciples:
If you love me, you will do as I command. 16Then I will ask the Father to send you the Holy Spirit who will help you and always be with you. 17The Spirit will show you what is true. The people of this world cannot accept the Spirit, because they don't see or know him. But you know the Spirit, who is with you and will keep on living in you.
18I won't leave you like orphans. I will come back to you. 19In a little while the people of this world won't be able to see me, but you will see me. And because I live, you will live. 20Then you will know I am one with the Father. You will know you are one with me, and I am one with you. 21 If you love me, you will do what I have said, and my Father will love you. I will also love you and show you what I am like.
22The other Judas, not Judas Iscariot, then spoke up and asked, “Lord, what do you mean by saying that you will show us what you are like, but you will not show the people of this world?”
23Jesus replied:
If anyone loves me, they will obey me. Then my Father will love them, and we will come to them and live in them. 24But anyone who doesn't love me, won't obey me. What they have heard me say doesn't really come from me, but from the Father who sent me.
25I have told you these things while I am still with you. 26But the Holy Spirit will come and help you, because the Father will send the Spirit to take my place. The Spirit will teach you everything and will remind you of what I said while I was with you.
27I give you peace, the kind of peace only I can give. It isn't like the peace this world can give. So don't be worried or afraid.
28You have already heard me say I am going and I will also come back to you. If you really love me, you should be glad I am going back to the Father, because he is greater than I am.
29I am telling you this before I leave, so when it does happen, you will have faith in me. 30I cannot speak with you much longer, because the ruler of this world is coming. But he has no power over me. 31I obey my Father, so everyone in the world might know that I love him.
It is time for us to go now.
translation_text:
1Nyekayea nyetšuii; nyehea Nyoṅmo̱ no̱ nyeyea, ni mi hũ nyehea mino̱ nyeyea.
2Šihĩle̱hei pī ye̱ mitše̱ we le̱; dšee nakai kũle̱, mikē̱nye momo; edšake̱ mīya ni miyasā gbe̱he matonye.
3Ni ke̱dši mite ni miyasā gbe̱he mitonye le̱, mibaba ekoṅ ni *mibabaṅõnye ke̱-ya heni midientše̱ miyo̱ le̱, koni heni miyo̱ le̱ nye hũ nyehĩ dše̱i. *12,26; 17,24.
4Ni heni miyaä le̱, nyele, ni gbe̱ le̱ hũ, nyele.
5Toma kē̱le̱ ake̱: Nuṅtšo̱, wo̱lee heni oyaä, ni té aafe tēṅ ni wo̱o̱nyẽ gbe̱ le̱ wo̱le hũ?
6Iesu kē̱le̱ ake̱: Mi noṅṅ dši *gbe̱ le̱ ke̱ †ano̱kwale le̱ ke̱ **wala le̱; ††moko baa tše̱ le̱ ṅõ, ake̱ dša etšṍ mino̱. *Heb. 10,20. †Mat. 11,27. **Ioh. 11,25. ††Rom. 5,1. 2.
7Edši nyelemi kũle̱, nyele mitše̱ hũ; ni ke̱-dše̱ ṅme̱ne̱ ke̱-ya ne̱ nyelele̱, edšake̱ nyénale̱.
8Filipo kē̱le̱ ake̱: Nuṅtšo̱, tšõmo̱wo̱ tše̱ le̱, ni no fá hãwo̱.
9Iesu kē̱le̱ ake̱: Dšeeṅmõ ni mike̱nye yo̱ ne̱, olekomi lolo, Filipo? Moni enami le̱, ena tše̱ le̱, ni té tēṅ ní okē̱o̱ ake̱: Tšõme̱wo̱ tše̱ le̱? 12,45. Heb. 1,8.
10Ani ohee oyee ake̱ miye̱ tše̱ le̱ mli ni tše̱ le̱ hũ ye̱ mimli? Wiemo̱i ni mike̱nye wiee̱ le̱, dšee *midientše̱ miyi mitoo̱ miwieo̱; ši tše̱ le̱ ní hĩo̱ mimli le̱, le̱ etšuo̱ nitšumo̱i le̱. *12,49.
11Nyeheami nyeyea ake̱ miye̱ tše̱ le̱ mli ni tše̱ le̱ hũ ye̱ mimli; ši ké̱ dšee nakai le̱, nyeheami nyeyea ye̱ nakai nitšumo̱i le̱ noṅṅ hewo̱. K. 20; 10,25. 38.
12Le̱le̱ṅ, le̱le̱ṅ, mīkē̱nye ake̱: Moni heo̱ mino̱ yeo̱ le̱, nitšumo̱i ni mitšuo̱ le̱, le̱ hũ eetšu, ni eetšu nii ní fè nomei tete, edšake̱ miya tše̱ le̱ ṅõ, Mar. 16,19. 20.
13ni nofẽno ní nyeakpa he fai ye̱ migbei ano̱ le̱, no mafe, koni tše̱ le̱ hĩe aba nyam ye̱ bi le̱ mli. 15,7. Mar. 11,24.
14Ke̱dši nyekpa noko he fai *ye̱ migbei ano̱ le̱, mafe. *16,23. 24.
15Ke̱dši nyemīsumo̱mi le̱, nyeaye mikitãi le̱ ano̱. 15,10. 1 Ioh. 5,3.
16Ni mi le̱ mabi tše̱ le̱, ni eehãnye *hefatalo̱ kroko, koni eke̱nye ahĩ ši ke̱-ya nāno̱; *K. 26; 15,26; 16,7.
17*ano̱kwale Mumo̱ le̱ ni †dše le̱ nyẽẽle̱ aṅõ le̱, edšake̱ énaale̱ ni asaṅ eleele̱; ši nye le̱ nyelele̱, edšake̱ eke̱nye yo̱, ni eehĩ nyemli. *16,15. †7,39.
18Mišīṅnye awusãi, miba nyeṅõ.
19Eſe̱ fiõ ke̱ke̱ ni dše le̱ enaṅmi doṅṅ; ši nye le̱ nyemīnami; edšake̱ mihĩe kã, ni nye hũ nyehĩe aakã. 16,16.
20Nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱ le̱ nyedientše̱ nyeale ake̱ miye̱ mitše̱ mli ni nye hũ nyeye̱ mimli ni mi hũ miye̱ nyemli. 17,21-23.
21Moni mikitãi le̱ yo̱ edeṅ ni eyeo̱ no̱ le̱, le̱ dši moni sumoo̱mi; ni moni sumoo̱mi le̱, mitše̱ aasumo̱le̱, ni mi hũ masumo̱le̱, ni *madšie mihe ši matšõle̱. *2 Kor. 3,18.
22Iuda, dšee Iskariot le̱, kē̱le̱ ake̱: Nuṅtšo̱, meni éba hewo̱ ni wo̱ ke̱ke̱ obadšie ohe ši otšõ, ni odšieṅ otšõṅ dše le̱?
23Iesu here no̱ ni ekē̱le̱ ake̱: Ke̱dši moko mīsumo̱mi le̱, eeye miwiemo̱ le̱ no̱, ni mitše̱ aasumo̱le̱, ni wo̱o̱ba eṅõ, ni wo̱ke̱ eṅõ aafe wo̱šihĩle̱he. K. 21; 13,34. Abe̱i 3,17. Ef. 3,17.
24Moni sumo̱o̱mi le̱ eyee miwiemo̱i le̱ ano̱; *ni wiemo̱ ní nyenuo̱ le̱ dšee minõṅ, ši moṅ tše̱ ní tšũmi le nõṅ. *7,16.
25Be mli ní mike̱nye yo̱ ne̱, mikē̱nye nii ne̱.
26Ši hefatalo̱ le̱, ni dši Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ le̱, moni tše̱ le̱ batšũ ye̱ migbe̱i ano̱ le̱, le̱ eetšõnye nii fẽ, ni eekainye nii fẽ ní mikē̱nye le̱. K. 16.
27*Hedšo̱le̱ mišīo̱ mahãnye, hedšo̱le̱ ní dši minõ le̱ miṅõhãanye, dšee bo̱ni dše le̱ hãa le̱, mihãanye ne̱. Nyetšui akayea, ni asaṅ ekafãa. *16,38. Fil. 4,7.
28Nyénu ake̱ *mikē̱nye ake̱: Mīya ni mība nyeṅõ. Nyemīsumo̱mi kũle̱, nyeaná mīše̱ †ake̱ mīya tše̱ le̱ ṅõ, edšake̱ mitše̱ da fèmi. *K. 3,18. †K. 6.
29Ni agbe̱ne̱ mikē̱nye dãni eba mli, koni ké̱ eba mli le̱, ní nyehe nyeye.
30Mike̱nye ewieṅ nibii pī doṅṅ, edšake̱ *dše le̱ṅ lumo̱ le̱ mība, ni ebe noko ye̱ mimli; *12,31. Ef. 2,2.
31ši beni afe ní dše le̱ aná ale ake̱ mīsumo̱ tše̱ le̱ ni *bo̱ni tše̱ le̱ womi kitã le̱ nakai mifeo̱ hewo̱ le̱: Nyetea ši, nyehãa wo̱dšea bie̱. *10,18.

english_text:
Jesus Is the True Vine
1Jesus said to his disciples:
I am the true vine, and my Father is the gardener. 2He cuts away every branch of mine that doesn't produce fruit. But he trims clean every branch that does produce fruit, so that it will produce even more fruit. 3You are already clean because of what I have said to you.
4Stay joined to me, and I will stay joined to you. Just as a branch cannot produce fruit unless it stays joined to the vine, you cannot produce fruit unless you stay joined to me. 5I am the vine, and you are the branches. If you stay joined to me, and I stay joined to you, then you will produce lots of fruit. But you cannot do anything without me. 6If you don't stay joined to me, you will be thrown away. You will be like dry branches that are gathered up and burned in a fire.
7Stay joined to me and let my teachings become part of you. Then you can pray for whatever you want, and your prayer will be answered. 8When you become fruitful disciples of mine, my Father will be honored. 9I have loved you, just as my Father has loved me. So remain faithful to my love for you. 10If you obey me, I will keep loving you, just as my Father keeps loving me, because I have obeyed him.
11I have told you this to make you as completely happy as I am. 12 Now I tell you to love each other, as I have loved you. 13The greatest way to show love for friends is to die for them. 14And you are my friends, if you obey me. 15Servants don't know what their master is doing, and so I don't speak to you as my servants. I speak to you as my friends, and I have told you everything my Father has told me.
16You did not choose me. I chose you and sent you out to produce fruit, the kind of fruit that will last. Then my Father will give you whatever you ask for in my name. 17So I command you to love each other.
The World's Hatred
18If the people of this world hate you, just remember that they hated me first. 19If you belonged to the world, its people would love you. But you don't belong to the world. I have chosen you to leave the world behind, and this is why its people hate you. 20 Remember how I told you that servants are not greater than their master. So if people mistreat me, they will mistreat you. If they do what I say, they will do what you say.
21People will do to you exactly what they did to me. They will do it because you belong to me, and they don't know the one who sent me. 22If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not be guilty of sin. But now they have no excuse for their sin.
23Everyone who hates me also hates my Father. 24I have done things no one else has ever done. If they had not seen me do these things, they would not be guilty. But they did see me do these things, and they still hate me and my Father too. 25 This is why the Scriptures are true when they say, “People hated me for no reason.”
26I will send you the Spirit who comes from the Father and shows what is true. The Spirit will help you and will tell you about me. 27Then you will also tell others about me, because you have been with me from the beginning.
translation_text:
1Midsi ano̱kwa weintšo le̱, ni mitše̱ dši okwafonyo le̱.
2Mihe nine-fẽ-nine ní woo yibii le̱, efloö̱, ni nofẽno ní woo̱ yibii le̱, ekplo̱ö̱ he, beni afe ní ewo yibii fè tšutšu le̱.
3Agbe̱ne̱ nyehe édše momo ye̱ wiemo̱ ní mike̱nye éwie le̱ hewo̱;
4nyehĩa mimli, ni mi hũ mahĩ nyemli. Take̱ bo̱ni tšonine nyẽṅ adše̱ le̱dientše̱ emli awo yibii ake̱ dša emã weintšo le̱ he le̱, nakai nye hũ nyenyẽṅ ake̱ dša nyehĩ mimli.
5Midši weintšo le̱, nyedši nidši le̱. Moni hĩo̱ mimli ni mi hũ mihĩo̱ emli le̱, le̱ noṅṅ ewoo̱ yibii pī; edšake̱ *ké̱ dšee miṅ le̱ nyenyẽṅ noko nyefe. *2 Kor. 3,5.
6Ke̱dši moko ehĩĩ mimli le̱, atše̱o̱le̱ afõo̱ tamo tšonine, ni egbĩo̱, ni abuaä nā awoo̱ la mli, ni ašãa.
7Ke̱dši nyehĩ mimli ni miwiemo̱i le̱ hĩ nyemli le̱, nyeakpa nofẽno ní nyetaoo̱ he fai, ni aafe aahãnye. Mar. 11,24.
8Ene̱ ake̱-woo̱ mitše̱ hĩe nyam, ké̱ nyewo yibii pī, ní nyetšṍmo̱ mikaselo̱i le̱.
9Bo̱ni tše̱ le̱ sumo̱mi le̱, nakai mi hũ misumo̱nye; nyehĩa ši ye̱ misuomo̱ le̱ mli.
10Ke̱dši nyeye mikitãi le̱ ano̱ le̱, nyeahĩ misuomo̱ le̱ mlĩ; take̱ bo̱ni mi hũ miye mitše̱ kitãi le̱ ano̱ ni mihĩo̱ esuomo̱ le̱ mli le̱. 14,15.
11Mike̱nye wie ene̱mei, koni mimīše̱ le̱ ahĩ nyemli, ni nyemīše̱ le̱ ayi. 17,13.
12Ene̱ dši mikitã, ake̱ nyesumo̱ nyehe tamo̱ bo̱ni misumo̱nye le̱. 13,34.
13Moko be̱ *suomo̱ ní da fè one̱, ake̱ mo aaṅõ ewala eṅmẽ ši ehã ešientše̱meĩ. *10,11. 1 Ioh. 3,16.
14Ke̱dši nyefe nii ní miwoo̱nye he kitã le̱, no le̱ mišĩentše̱mei dšĩnye. 8,31.
15Mĩtšé̱é̱nye nyṍdši doṅṅ, edšake̱ nyṍṅ lee noni enuṅtšo̱ feo̱; ši moṅ šĩentše̱mei mítšé̱nye, edšake̱ nii fẽ ní minu ye̱ mitše̱ nā le̱, mitšĩ tã mikē̱nye.
16Dšee nye nyehalami, ši mi moṅ mihalanye, ni mitonye koni nye hũ nyeya ni nyeyawo yibii, ni nyeyibii le̱ ahĩ ši, koni nofẽno he fai ní nyeakpa tše̱ le̱ ye̱ migbei ano̱ le̱, eṅõ-hãnye.
17Ene̱ mikē̱o̱nye, ake̱ nyesumo̱ nyehe.
18Ke̱dši dše le̱ mīnye̱nye le̱, nyenáa nyelea ake̱ mi tšutšu enye̱. 7,7.
19Edši dše le̱ṅ nyedše̱ kũle̱, dše le̱ aasumo̱ le̱dientše̱ emei, ši ake̱-ní nye-dše̱e̱ dše le̱ṅ, ši mi moṅ mihalanye ke̱-dše̱ dše le̱ṅ le̱, nohewo̱ dše le̱ nye̱o̱nyele̱. 1 Ioh. 5,4. Ioh. 17,14.
20Nyehĩe ahĩa wiemo̱ ní mi noṅṅ mikē̱nye lo̱ no̱, ake̱: *Nyṍṅ efèè enuṅtšo̱. Ké̱ ame̱wami yi le̱, ame̱awa nye hũ yi; ké̱ ame̱ye miwiemo̱ no̱ le̱, ame̱aye nye hũ nyenõ no̱. *13,16.
21Ši ame̱aṅõ ene̱mei fẽ ame̱fenye ye̱ migbe̱i le̱ hewo̱; edšake̱ *ame̱lee moni tšũmi le̱. *16,3.
22Mibaa mike̱ame̱ ebawiee dšikule̱, ame̱he be̱ eša ko; ši ene̱ le̱ ame̱be̱ ame̱he eša le̱ he lakpatō ko.
23Moni nye̱o̱mi le̱ ẽnye̱ mitše̱ hũ. 5,28.
24Edši mitšuu nitšumo̱i ní mokomoko tšuko eko dã ye̱ ame̱teṅ kũle̱, ame̱he be̱ aša ko; ši ene̱ le̱ amé̱na, ni kẽle̱ ame̱mīnye̱mi ke̱ mitše̱ fẽ. 14,11.
25Ši beni afe ni wiemo̱ le̱ ní aṅmã ye̱ ame̱mla le̱ mli ake̱: “Ame̱nye̱mi yakatſā” le̱ aná aba mli. Lal. 69,5.
26Ši *hefatalo̱ le̱, ní †mibatšũle̱ nyeṅō ke̱-adše̱ tše̱ le̱ ṅõ le̱, moni dši ano̱kwale Mumo̱ le̱ ní dše̱o̱ tšo̱ le̱ ṅõ baä le̱, le̱, ké̱ eba le̱, eeye mihe odase; *14,26. †Luk. 24,49.
27ni nye hũ nyeaye odase, edšake̱ nyeke̱mi yo̱ ke̱-dše̱ šišidšē. Bo̱f. 1,8; 5,32.

english_text:
1I am telling you these things, so that you will not turn away. 2You will be chased out of the synagogues. And the time will come when people will kill you and think they are doing God a favor. 3They will do these things because they don't know either the Father or me. 4I am saying this to you now, so that when the time comes, you will remember what I have said.
The Work of the Holy Spirit
I was with you at the first, and so I didn't tell you these things. 5But now I am going back to the Father who sent me, and none of you asks me where I am going. 6You are very sad from hearing all of this. 7But I tell you I am going to do what is best for you. This is why I am going away. The Holy Spirit cannot come to help you until I leave. But after I am gone, I will send the Spirit to you.
8The Spirit will come and show the people of this world the truth about sin and God's justice and the judgment. 9The Spirit will show them that they are wrong about sin, because they didn't have faith in me. 10They are wrong about God's justice, because I am going to the Father, and you won't see me again. 11And they are wrong about the judgment, because God has already judged the ruler of this world.
12I have much more to say to you, but right now it would be more than you could understand. 13 The Spirit shows what is true and will come and guide you into the full truth. The Spirit doesn't speak on his own. He will tell you only what he has heard from me, and he will let you know what is going to happen. 14The Spirit will bring glory to me by taking my message and telling it to you. 15Everything the Father has is mine. This is why I have said that the Spirit takes my message and tells it to you.
Sorrow Will Turn into Joy
16Jesus told his disciples, “For a little while you won't see me, but after a while you will see me.”
17They said to each other, “What does Jesus mean by saying that for a little while we won't see him, but after a while we will see him? What does he mean by saying he is going to the Father? 18What is this ‘little while’ that he is talking about? We don't know what he means.”
19Jesus knew they had some questions, so he said:
You are wondering what I meant when I said that for a little while you won't see me, but after a while you will see me. 20I tell you for certain that you will cry and be sad, but the world will be happy. You will be sad, but later you will be happy.
21When a woman is about to give birth, she is in great pain. But after it is all over, she forgets the pain and is happy, because she has brought a child into the world. 22You are now very sad. But later I will see you, and you will be so happy that no one will be able to change the way you feel. 23When that time comes, you won't have to ask me about anything. I tell you for certain the Father will give you whatever you ask for in my name. 24You have not asked for anything in this way before, but now you must ask in my name. Then it will be given to you, so you will be completely happy.
25I have used examples to explain to you what I have been talking about. But the time will come when I will speak to you plainly about the Father and will no longer use examples like these. 26You will ask the Father in my name, and I won't have to ask him for you. 27God the Father loves you because you love me, and you believe I have come from him. 28I came from the Father into the world, but I am leaving the world and returning to the Father.
29The disciples said, “Now you are speaking plainly to us! You are not using examples. 30At last we know that you understand everything, and we don't have any more questions. Now we believe you truly have come from God.”
31Jesus replied:
Do you really believe me? 32The time will come and is already here when all of you will be scattered. Each of you will go back home and leave me by myself. But the Father will be with me, and I won't be alone. 33I have told you this, so that you might have peace in your hearts because of me. While you are in the world, you will have to suffer. But cheer up! I have defeated the world.
translation_text:
1Mikē̱nye nii ne̱, beni afe ní nyenãdši akatõtõ. 14,29.
2Ame̱aſienye ke̱-adše̱ kpēhei le̱. Ni be baba tete, ní mofẽmo ní gbeo̱nye le̱ aasusu ake̱ eke̱-mīdšá Nyoṅmo̱. Mat. 24,9.
3Ni ame̱afe ene̱mei, edšake̱ ame̱lee tše̱ le̱ lo mi hũ. 15,21.
4Ši mikē̱nye nii ne̱, koni, ké̱ be le̱ še̱ le̱, ni nyekai ake̱ mitšĩ tã mikē̱nye. Ši ke̱-dše̱ šišidšē le̱ mikē̱ē̱nye nii ne̱, edšake mike̱nye ye̱.
5Ši agbe̱ne̱ le̱, *mīya moni tšũmi le̱ ṅõ, ni nyeteṅ moko biimi ake̱: Nẽgbe̱ oyaã? *7,33.
6Ši ní mitšĩ nii ne̱ atã mikē̱nye hewo̱ le̱, ṅko̱mo̱yeli éyi nyetšuiaṅ.
7Ši kẽle̱ mīkē̱nye ano̱kwale: ehĩ hãnye ake̱ mate; edšake̱, ke̱dši miyaa le̱, hefatalo̱ le̱ baṅ nyeṅõ; ši ke̱dši mite le̱, mabā eba nyeṅõ. 14,16. 26.
8Ni le̱ le̱, ke̱dši eba le̱, eekã dše le̱ ye̱ eša hewo̱ ke̱ dšale̱ hewo̱ ke̱ kodšomo̱ hewo̱: 1 Kor. 14,24.
9eša hewo̱, edšake̱ ame̱hee mino̱ ame̱yee; 3,18.
10dšale̱ hewo̱, edšake̱ miya mitše̱ ṅõ, ni nyenaṅmi doṅṅ; Bo̱f. 5,31. Rom. 4,25.
11kodšomo̱ hewo̱, edšake̱ akodšo dše ne̱ṅ lumo̱ le̱. 12,31; 14,30.
12Miye̱ nii pī lolo ní makenye; ši nyenyẽṅ mli nyemõ amrõ ne̱; 1 Kor. 3,1.
13ši ké̱ le̱, ano̱kwale Mumo̱ le̱, ená eba le̱, eetšõnye ano̱kwale le̱ fẽ mli gbe̱; edšake̱ etoṅ le̱dientše̱ eyi ewieṅ; ši moṅ nofẽno ní eenu le̱, no eewie, ni nii ni baä le̱, eetšĩ tã etšõnye. 14,23. 1 Ioh. 2,27.
14Le̱ ebawo mihĩe nyam, edšake̱ eeṅõ minõ le̱ eko ní eetšĩ tã etšõnye.
15Nii fiā *ni dši tše̱ le̱ nõ le̱, minõṅ; nohewo̱ ni mikē̱ ake̱: Ebaṅõ minõ le̱ eko, ní etšĩ tã etšõnye le̱, *17,10.
16Eſe̱ fiō, ni nyenaṅmi, ni asaṅ eſe̱ fiō, ninyebanami; edšake̱ miya tše̱ le̱ ṅõ. 14,19.
17Ke̱ke̱ ni ekaselo̱i le̱ ateṅ meikomei bibī ame̱he ake̱: Meni dši noni ekē̱o̱wo̱ ne̱: Eſe̱ fiō, ni nyénaṅmi, ni asaṅ eſe̱ fiō, ni nyebanami, ni asaṅ: mīya tše̱ le̱ ṅõ?
18Nohewo̱ lo̱ ame̱kē̱: Meni dši noni ekē̱o̱ ne̱: Eſe̱ fiō? Wo̱lee noni ekē̱o̱ ne̱.
19Agbe̱ne̱ Iesu na ake̱ ame̱mītao ake̱ ame̱bio̱le̱, ni ekē̱ame̱ ake̱: Ní mĩkē̱: Eſe̱ flō ní nyenaṅmi, ni asaṅ eſe̱ fiō ní nyebanami le̱, no nyebibīo̱ nyehe ne̱?
20Le̱le̱ṅ, le̱le̱ṅ, mīkē̱nye ake̱: Nye le̱ nyebafó ni nyeba wo yăra, ši dše le̱ banyã́; nye le̱ nyebaye ṅko̱mo̱, ši nye-ṅko̱mo̱yeli le̱ aatšṍ mīše̱.
21Ké̱ yō mīkõmo̱ le̱, ehaoo̱, edšake̱ eṅmle̱tſã le̱ eše̱; ši beni éfó̱ bi le̱ se̱ le̱, ekaii hedšramo̱ le̱ doṅṅ ye̱ mīše̱ ní enáa ake̱ éfó̱ gbomo ke̱-ba dše le̱ṅ le̱ hewo. Ies. 26,17.
22Nohewo̱ le̱ nye hũ, agbe̱ne̱ nyemīye ṅko̱mo̱ moṅ; ši mibananye ekoṅ, ni nyetšui aanyõ nyemli, ni nyemīše̱ le̱ moko šõṅ ye̱ nyedeṅ;
23ni *no gbĩ le̱ no̱ le̱ nyebiṅmi nokonoko. Le̱le̱ṅ, le̱le̱ṅ, mīkē̱nye ake̱: Nofẽno he †fai ní nyeakpa tše̱ le̱ ye̱ migbe̱i ano̱ le̱, eehãnye. *14,20; †14,13. 14.
24Ke̱-baši be ne̱ le̱ nyekpako noko he fai ye̱ migbe̱i ano̱; nyekpaä fai, ni nyeana, koni *nyemīšo̱ le̱ ayi. *15,11.
25Nii ne̱, abe̱buai amli mike̱nye wieo̱ ye̱ ne̱; ši be mība, ní mike̱nye ewieṅ ye̱ abe̱buai amli doṅṅ, ši moṅ faṅṅ madšadše tše̱ le̱ he sane matšõnye.
26Nakai gbĩ le̱ no̱ le̱ nyeakpa fai ye̱ migbe̱i ano̱, ši mikē̱ē̱nye ake̱ mi mabi tše̱ le̱ mahãnye;
27edšake̱ *tše̱ le̱ dientše̱ mīsumo̱nye, edšake̱ nye hũ nyemīsumo̱mi, ni nyehe nyeye ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ṅõ mĩdšo̱. *14,21.
28Tše̱ le̱ ṅõ midše̱ miba dše le̱ mli, asaṅ mīdše dše le̱ṅ maya tše̱ le̱ ṅõ.
29Ekaselo̱i le̱ kē̱le̱ ake̱: Na, agbe̱ne̱ owie faṅṅ ni owiee ye̱ *abe̱bua mli. *K. 25.
30Agbe̱ne̱ wo̱yo ake̱ ole nii fẽ ni ehĩaa ake̱ moko bio̱o sane ko; ene̱ wo̱ke̱heo̱ wo̱yeo̱, ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ṅõ odše̱.
31Iesu hereame̱ no̱ ake̱: Agbe̱ne̱ nyemīhe nyemīye?
32Na, ṅmle̱tſā le̱ mība ni eše̱ po, ní *nyebagbe̱ nyeſā ni mofẽmo aako̱ egbe̱, ni nyeašĩ mikome; ši dšee †mikome ni, edšake tše̱ le̱ ke̱mi ye. *Zak. 13,7. Mat 26,31. Mar. 14,27. †Ioh. 8,29.
33Mikē̱nye nii ne̱, koni *nyewonyetšui ye̱ mimli. Dše le̱ṅ le̱, hedšramo̱ nyenáa, ši kẽle̱ nyetšui anyõa nyemli: miye dše le̱ no̱ †kũnim. 14,27. Rom. 5,1. †1 Ioh. 5,4.

english_text:
Jesus Prays
1After Jesus had finished speaking to his disciples, he looked up toward heaven and prayed:
Father, the time has come for you to bring glory to your Son, in order that he may bring glory to you. 2And you gave him power over all people, so he would give eternal life to everyone you give him. 3 Eternal life is to know you, the only true God, and to know Jesus Christ, the one you sent. 4I have brought glory to you here on earth by doing everything you gave me to do. 5Now, Father, give me back the glory I had with you before the world was created.
6You have given me some followers from this world, and I have shown them what you are like. They were yours, but you gave them to me, and they have obeyed you. 7They know that you gave me everything I have. 8I told my followers what you told me, and they accepted it. They know I came from you, and they believe you are the one who sent me. 9I am praying for them, but not for those who belong to this world. My followers belong to you, and I am praying for them. 10All I have is yours, and all you have is mine, and they will bring glory to me.
11Holy Father, I am no longer in the world. I am coming to you, but my followers are still in the world. So keep them safe by the power of the name you have given me. Then they will be one with each other, just as you and I are one. 12 While I was with them, I kept them safe by the power you have given me. I guarded them, and not one of them was lost, except the one who had to be lost. This happened so that what the Scriptures say would come true.
13I am on my way to you. But I say these things while I am still in the world, so my followers will have the same complete joy that I do. 14I have told them your message. But the people of this world hate them, because they don't belong to this world, just as I don't.
15Father, I don't ask you to take my followers out of the world, but keep them safe from the evil one. 16They don't belong to this world, and neither do I. 17Your word is the truth. So let this truth make them completely yours. 18I am sending them into the world, just as you sent me. 19I have given myself completely for their sake, so they may belong completely to the truth.
20I am not praying just for these followers. I am also praying for everyone else who will have faith because of what my followers will say about me. 21I want all of them to be one with each other, just as I am one with you and you are one with me. I also want them to be one with us. Then the people of this world will believe that you sent me.
22I have honored my followers in the same way you honored me, in order that they may be one with each other, just as we are one. 23I am one with them, and you are one with me, so they may become completely one. Then this world's people will know that you sent me. They will know that you love my followers as much as you love me.
24Father, I want everyone you have given me to be with me, wherever I am. Then they will see the glory you have given me, because you loved me before the world was created. 25Good Father, the people of this world don't know you. But I know you, and my followers know that you sent me. 26I told them what you are like, and I will tell them even more. Then the love you have for me will become part of them, and I will be one with them.
translation_text:
1Nii ne̱ Iesu wie, ni ehole ehĩṅme̱ii ano̱ ke̱-te ṅwei, ni ekē̱: Atā, ṅmle̱tſā le̱ éše̱: wo obi le̱ hĩe nyam, koni obi le̱ hũ awo ohĩe nyam;
2take̱ bo̱ni ohãle̱ *hegbe̱ ye̱ helo fẽ no̱, koni mei fẽ ní oṅō-hãle̱ le̱, ehã-ame̱ nāno̱ wala le̱. *Mat. 11,27.
3Ši ene̱ dši nāno̱ wala le̱, ake̱ ame̱le ho, *ano̱kwa Nyoṅmo̱ kome le̱, ke̱ Iesu Kristo, moni otšũ le̱. *1 Ioh. 5,20.
4Mi le̱ miwo ohĩe nyam ye̱ šikpoṅ le̱ no̱, ake̱-ní nitšumo̱ le̱ ní oṅõ-hãmi tšumo̱ le̱, migbe nā le̱.
5Ni agbe̱ne̱, Atā, ṅõ anumnyam ní miyo̱ ye̱ oṅõ dãni dše le̱ yo̱ le̱ owo mihĩe nyam. K. 24; 1,1. Fil. 2,3.
6Midšie ogbe̱i le̱ aši mitšõ gbomei ni oṅõame̱ ke̱-dše̱ dše le̱ṅ *ohãmi le̱. Onii dšiame̱, ni oṅõame̱ ohãmi, ni ame̱ye owiemo̱ le̱ no̱. *K. 9.
7Agbe̱ne̱ ame̱le ake̱, nii flã ní oṅõ-hãmi le̱, oṅõ edše̱,
8edšake̱ wiemo̱i le̱ ní oṅõ-hãmi le̱, mĩṅō-hãame̱; ni amé̱hē, ni *ame̱ná ame̱le kre̱dē̱ ake̱ oṅõ midše̱, ni ame̱he ame̱ye ake̱ bo otšũmi. *16,30.
9Mi le̱, ame̱ mibio̱ mahã; dšee dše le̱ mibio̱ mahã, ši moṅ mei ni *oṅõ-hãmi le̱, edšake̱ onii dšiame̱; *6,37. 44.
10ni minii fẽ le̱ onōṅ, ni *onõ hũ le minõṅ, ni mihĩe éba nyam ye̱ ame̱mli. *16,15.
11Ni mibe̱ dše le̱ mli doṅṅ, ši mene̱mei ye̱ dše le̱ mli, ni mi le̱ miba oṅõ. Atā kroṅkroṅ, mei ní oṅõ-hãmi ne̱, toame̱ ye̱ ogbe̱i le̱ amli, beni afe ní ame̱fe ekome *tamo̱wo̱. *10,30.
12Beni mike̱ame̱ yo̱ dše le̱ mli le̱, mitoame̱ ye̱ ogbe̱i le̱ amli; mei ní oṅõ-hãmi le̱, mibu ame̱he, ni ame̱teṅ *mokomoko elãdšeko, dša lãdšemo̱ bi le̱, koni noni †aṅmã le̱ aba mli. *6,39. †Lal. 41,10; 109,8.
13Ši agbe̱ne̱ le̱, mība oṅõ, ni mīwie nii ne̱ ye̱ dše le̱ mlĩ, koni ame̱ná mimīše̱ le̱ ní eye mū ye̱ ame̱mli. 15,11.
14Miṅõ owiemo̱ le̱ mihãame̱, ni dše le̱ mīnye̱ame̱, edšake̱ ame̱dše̱e̱ dše le̱ mli, take̱ bo̱ni mi hũ midše̱e̱ dše le̱ mli le̱. 15,19.
15Mibii ake̱ odšieame̱ ke̱-dše̱ dše le̱ mli, ši moṅ ake̱ *obu ame̱he ye̱ efõṅ le̱ mli. *2 Tes. 3,3.
16Ame̱dše̱e̱ dše le̱ mli, take̱ bo̱ni mi hũ midše̱e̱ dše le̱ mli le̱.
17Femo̱ame̱ kroṅkroṅ ye̱ ono̱kwale le̱ mli; owiemo̱ le̱ ano̱kwaleṅ. 6,63.
18Take̱ bo̱ni otšũmi dše le̱ mli le̱, nakai noṅṅ mi hũ mitšũo̱ame̱ dše le mli. 20,21.
19Ni ame̱hewo̱ midientše̱ mifeo̱ mihe kroṅkroṅ le̱, koni ame̱ hũ afeame̱ kroṅkroṅ ye̱ ano̱kwale mli. Heb. 10,10.
20Ši dšee mene̱mei ahewo̱ ke̱ke̱ mibio̱ le̱, ši mei ní bahe mino̱ aye ye̱ ame̱wiemo̱ nā le̱ hũ ahewo̱ṅ;
21koni ame̱fẽ *amefe ekome, take̱ bo̱ni bo, Atā, oyo̱ mimli ni mi hũ miyo̱ omli le̱, koni ame̱ hũ ame̱fe ekome ye̱ wo̱mli, koni dše le̱ ahe aye ake bo otšũmi. *Gal. 3,28.
22Ni anumnyam ní oṅõ-hãmì le̱, miṅõ-hãame̱, koni *ame̱fe ekome, take̱ bo̱ni wo̱ hũ wo̱yo̱ ekome le̱; *Bo̱f. 4,32.
