7Ši nū le̱, esaa ake̱ ehaä eyitšo he, edšake̱ *Nyoṅmo̱ subāṅ ke̱ anumnyam dšile̱; ši yō le̱, nū anumnyam dšile̱. *1 Mose 1,27.
8Edšake̱ nū dše̱e̱ yō mli, ši yō moṅ dše̱ nū mli. 1 Mose 3,22. 23.
9Ni asaṅ abo̱o̱ nū ye̱ yō hewo̱; ši yō moṅ abo̱ ye̱ nū hewo̱, 1 Mose 2,13.
10Nohewo̱ le̱ esa ake̱ yō aná hewale̱ he okadi ko ye̱ eyiteṅ ye̱ ṅweibo̱foi le̱ ahewo̱.
11Tše̱bele̱ nū akaši yō, ni yō hũ akaši nū, ye̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ mli;
12edšake̱ take̱ bo̱ni yō dše̱ nū mli le̱, nakai noṅṅ kẽ nū hū tšṍ yō mli ke̱-ba; ši nii fẽ dše̱ Nyoṅmo̱ mli.
13Nyedientše̱ nyehalaä mli ye̱ nyeteṅ: ani eye̱ fe̱o ake̱ yō aaso̱le ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe ní ehaa eyi no̱?
14Ani fo̱mo̱su dientše̱ etšõõnye ake̱, ke̱dši nū ṅmē̃ eyi kusū le̱, eye̱ hĩegbẽle hãle̱,
15ši yō le̱, ke̱dši eṅmẽ eyi kusū le̱, edši anumnyam hãle̱? edšake̱ ake̱ yitšo̱i le̱ hãle̱ ake̱ hehanõ.
16Ši ke̱dši moko mīsumo̱ ake̱ eefe ehe helo̱ le̱, wo̱ le̱ wo̱fee nakai, ni Nyoṅmo̱ asafoi le̱ hũ efee nakai.
17Ši kítã ní miwoo̱nye ne̱, dšee nyeyi mike̱-dšieo̱ le̱, edšake̱ ké̱ nyekpe le̱, dšee ekpakpa dše̱o̱ mli, ši moṅ efõṅ dšeo̱ mli. K. 22.
18Ši kleṅkleṅ le̱ minuo̱ ake̱, ké̱ nyeyabua nyehe nā ye̱ asafo le̱ mli le̱, mligblamo̱i ye̱ nyeteṅ, ni miheo̱ miyeo̱ fã-ke̱-fã; 1,10-12; 3,2.
19edšake̱ *dša amaletšõmo̱i te ši ye̱ nyeteṅ, koni mei kpakpai le̱, †adšie ame̱he ši faṅṅ ye̱ nyeteṅ. *1 Ioh. 2,19. †5 Mose 13,4.
20Agbe̱ne̱, kē̱ nyenā bakpe ši le̱, edšee Nuṅtšo̱ niyenii le̱ yeli;
21edšake̱ ne̱ke̱ nyeniyeli ne̱ mli le̱, mofẽmo ṅõo̱ le̱dientše̱ eniyenii ni eyeo̱, ni beni hõmo̱ yeo̱ moko le̱, bĕle̱ moko eto̱ dā̃.
22Aso nyebe̱ šĩai ní nyeaye nii ni nyeanu ye̱ dše̱i? Alo Nyoṅmo̱ asafo le̱ he guo̱ nyegbee, ni *nyewoo̱ mei ní be̱ noko le̱ ahĩegbĕle? Té makē̱nye tēṅ? Ani midšie nyeyi? Ene̱ le̱, midšiee nyeyi ye̱ mli. *Iak. 2,5. 6.
23Edšake̱ midientše̱ miná ke̱-dse̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ deṅ, ni no noṅṅ miṅõ-hãnye, *ake̱ Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu le̱, nakai nyō le̱ṅ noṅṅ ni atšõ ese̱-gbe̱ le̱, eko abolo, *Mat 26,25-28. Mar. 14,22-24. Luk. 22,19. 20.
24ni eda ši, ni ekũmo̱ mli, ni ekē̱: Nyehea, nyeyea: ene̱ dši migbomotšo ní akũmo̱ ye̱ nyehewo̱; nyefea ene̱ ní nyeṅõ-kaimi.
25Nakai noṅṅ ewó kpulu le̱ hũ ye̱ niyenii le̱ ase̱, ni ekē̱: Ne̱ke̱ kpulu ne̱ dši kpãṅmo̱ hē le̱ ye̱ milá le̱ mli; nyefea ene̱, šii-abo̱ ní nyeanu le̱, ní nyeṅõ-kaimi.
26Ši šiiabo̱ ní nyeyeo̱ ne̱ke̱ abolo ne̱ ni nyenuo̱ ne̱ke̱ kpulu ne̱ hũ le̱, nyemī-dšadše Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ gbĕle le̱ nyemītšõ *ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní eeba. *Mat. 25,29.
27Nohewo̱ le̱, mofẽmo ní yeo̱ ne̱ke̱ abolo ne̱ ni enuo̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ kpulu le̱ bo̱ni esaa le̱, ētõ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ gbomotšo le̱ ke̱ elá le̱ no̱. Heb. 6,6.
28Ši gbomo *áka le̱dientše̱ ehe dãni eye abolo ne̱ eko ni enu kpulu ne̱ eko; *Mat. 26,22. 2 Kor. 13,5.
29edšake̱ moni yeo̱ ni enuo̱ bo̱ni esaa le̱, kodšomo̱ moṅ eyeo̱ ni enuo̱ ehãa ehe, edšake̱ ebuu Nuṅtšo̱ lo̱ gbomotšo le̱.
30Nohewo̱ hũ ni nyeteṅ mei pī he yeo̱ ni ame̱he waaame̱, ni mei babaō hũ *ewo ne̱. *15,20.
31Ši edši wo̱kaã wo̱dientše̱ wo̱he wo̱kwe̱o̱ kũle̱, akodšoowo̱.
32Ši ké̱ akodšoo̱wo̱ le̱, Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ tšo̱semo̱ ni, beni afe ní akabuwo̱ ke̱ dše le̱ fẽ fo̱. Heb. 12,5. 6.
33Nohewo̱ le̱, minyemimei, ké̱ nyenä bakpe ši nyebaye nii le̱, nyemēmēa nyehe;
34ši ké̱ hõmo̱ mīye moko le̱, hã ní eye nii ye̱ šĩa dã, beni afe ní nyekpē le̱ akatšé̱ kodšomo̱ mihãnye. Ši nii ní eſe̱ le̱, ké̱ miba le̱, matoame̱ gbe̱dšiano̱.

english_text:
Spiritual Gifts
1My friends, you asked me about spiritual gifts. 2I want you to remember that before you became followers of the Lord, you were led in all the wrong ways by idols that cannot even talk. 3Now I want you to know that if you are led by God's Spirit, you will say that Jesus is Lord, and you will never curse Jesus.
4 There are different kinds of spiritual gifts, but they all come from the same Spirit. 5There are different ways to serve the same Lord, 6and we can each do different things. Yet the same God works in all of us and helps us in everything we do.
7The Spirit has given each of us a special way of serving others. 8Some of us can speak with wisdom, while others can speak with knowledge, but these gifts come from the same Spirit. 9To others the Spirit has given great faith or the power to heal the sick 10or the power to work mighty miracles. Some of us are prophets, and some of us recognize when God's Spirit is present. Others can speak different kinds of languages, and still others can tell what these languages mean. 11But it is the Spirit who does all this and decides which gifts to give to each of us.
One Body with Many Parts
12 The body of Christ has many different parts, just as any other body does. 13Some of us are Jews, and others are Gentiles. Some of us are slaves, and others are free. But God's Spirit baptized each of us and made us part of the body of Christ. Now we each drink from that same Spirit.
14Our bodies don't have just one part. They have many parts. 15Suppose a foot says, “I'm not a hand, and so I'm not part of the body.” Wouldn't the foot still belong to the body? 16Or suppose an ear says, “I'm not an eye, and so I'm not part of the body.” Wouldn't the ear still belong to the body? 17If our bodies were only an eye, we couldn't hear a thing. And if they were only an ear, we couldn't smell a thing. 18But God has put all parts of our body together in the way that he decided is best.
19A body isn't really a body, unless there is more than one part. 20It takes many parts to make a single body. 21That's why the eyes cannot say they don't need the hands. That's also why the head cannot say it doesn't need the feet. 22In fact, we cannot get along without the parts of the body that seem to be the weakest. 23We take special care to dress up some parts of our bodies. We are modest about our personal parts, 24but we don't have to be modest about other parts.
God put our bodies together in such a way that even the parts that seem the least important are valuable. 25He did this to make all parts of the body work together smoothly, with each part caring about the others. 26If one part of our body hurts, we hurt all over. If one part of our body is honored, the whole body will be happy.
27Together you are the body of Christ. Each one of you is part of his body. 28 First, God chose some people to be apostles and prophets and teachers for the church. But he also chose some to work miracles or heal the sick or help others or be leaders or speak different kinds of languages. 29Not everyone is an apostle. Not everyone is a prophet. Not everyone is a teacher. Not everyone can work miracles. 30Not everyone can heal the sick. Not everyone can speak different kinds of languages. Not everyone can tell what these languages mean. 31I want you to desire the best gifts. So I will show you a much better way.
translation_text:
1Ši agbe̱ne̱, anyemimei, mīsumo̱ ake̱ mahã nyele noko ye̱ mumo̱ṅnii le̱ ahe.
2Nyele ake̱, beni nyedši wo̱ṅdšálo̱i le̱, *amãgãi mumuii le̱ aṅõ akplanye ke̱-te, bo̱fẽbo̱ ní akplanye ahã le̱. *Hab. 2,13. 19.
3Nohewo̱ le̱ mīhã nyele ake̱, moni wieo̱ ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ Mumo̱ mli le̱, ekē̱ē̱ ake̱ Iesu dši musumo; ni moko nyẽṅ ekē̱ ake̱ Iesu dši Nuṅtšo̱ hũ, ake̱ dša ye̱ Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ mli. Mar. 9,39. 1 Ioh. 4,2. 8.
4Ši dromo̱kēnii sro̱toi ye̱, ši Mumo̱ kome le̱ noṅṅ ni; Rom. 12,6. Ef. 4,4.
5ni súomo̱nitšumo̱i sro̱toi hũ ye̱, ši Nuṅtšo̱ kome le̱ noṅṅ ni; K. 28. Ef. 4,11.
6ni nitšumo̱i sro̱toi hũ ye̱, ši Nyoṅmo̱ kome le̱ noṅṅ dši moni tšuo̱ fẽ ye̱ mei fẽ mli.
7Ši mofẽmo le̱, ake̱ Mumo̱ le̱ kpodšiemo̱ le̱ hãale̱ koni ahī ahã mei. 14,26.
8Ši moko le̱, atšṍ Mumo̱ le̱ no̱ ahãle̱ nilē-wiemo̱; ni mokroko hũ ahãle̱ niiašiši-namo̱-wiemo̱ ye̱ nakai Mumo̱ le̱ noṅṅ nā;
9moko le̱, ahãle̱ hemo̱-ke̱-yeli ye̱ nakai Mumo̱ le̱ noṅṅ mli; ni mokroko hũ ahãle̱ tšámo̱ dromo̱kēnii ye̱ nakai Mumo̱ le̱ noṅṅ mli;
10moko le̱ hewale̱nii atšnmo̱; mokroko le̱ gbale̱; moko hũ mumo̱i ašikpamo̱; moko hũ *wiemo̱i sro̱toi awiemo̱; ni mokroko bũ wiemo̱i ašišitšõmo̱. *14,5. Bo̱f. 2,4.
11Ši ne̱ko̱ nibii no̱ fẽ, Mumo̱ kome le̱ noṅṅ tšuo̱, ni edšaä mli ehãa mofẽmo ekroekro, bo̱ni esumoo̱. 7,7. Rom. 12,3. Ef. 4,7.
12Ši take̱ bo̱ni gbomotšo le̱ ekome ni, ši ehĩe henii pī, ni gbomotšo le̱ he-nii pī le̱ fẽ dši gbomotšo kome le̱: nakai noṅṅ kẽ dši Kristo. K. 27; 10,17.
13Edšake̱ *Iudafoi dšiwo̱ dšio, Helabii dšiwo̱ dšio, nyṍdši dšio, hehĩelo̱i dšio, wo̱ fẽ le̱ Mumo̱ kome mli atšṍ abaptisiwo̱ awo gbomotšo kome mli; ni wo̱ fẽ, Mumo̱ kome ake̱-hãwo̱ ni wo̱nu. *Gai. 3,28.
14Edšake̱ gbomotšo le̱ hũ dšee henõ kome ni, ši pī ni. K. 20.
15Ke̱dši nane aakē̱ ake̱: Ake̱-ní mi-dšee nine hewo̱ le̱, midšee gbomotšo le̱ henii le̱ eko le̱; ani ene̱hewo̱ le̱ edšee gbomotšo le̱ henii le̱ eko?
16Ni ke̱dši toi hũ aakē̱ ake̱: Ake̱ noni midšee hĩṅme̱i hewo̱ le̱, midšee gbomotšo le̱ henii le̱ eko le̱; ani ene̱hewo̱ le̱ edšee gbomotšo le̱ henii le̱ eko?
17Ké̱ gbomotšo mū le̱ fẽ le̱ hīṅme̱i ni le̱, nẽgbe̱ ninumo̱ yo̱? Ké̱ ninumo̱ so̱ṅṅ ni le̱, nẽgbe̱ nifũ le̱ yo̱?
18Ši agbe̱ne̱ Nyoṅmo̱ to henii le̱, ame̱teṅ nofẽno ekro ye̱ gbomotšo le̱ he, bo̱ni esumoo̱.
19Ši ké̱ ame̱fẽ ame̱dši henõ kome le̱, nēgbe̱ gbomotšo le̱ yo̱?
20Ši agbe̱ne̱ le̱ henii pī ni moṅ, ši gbomotšo komeṅ. K. 14.
21Ši hĩṅme̱i nyẽṅ ekē̱ nine ake̱: Mibe̱ ohe nitšumo̱; ni asaṅ yitšo nyẽṅ ekē̱ nãdši ake̱: Mibe̱ nyehe nĩtšumo̱.
22Ši gbomotšo le̱ henii ní efeo̱wo̱ ake̱ ame̱he waa kwrā le̱, ame̱ moṅ ame̱he hĩaäwe̱ titri;
23ni nii ní efeo̱wo̱ ako̱ ame̱dši gbomotšo henii ní hĩe be̱ nyam kwrā le̱, nomei titri ahĩe nyam wo̱woo̱, ni wo̱henii ni be̱ fe̱o moṅ le̱, nomei yo̱ fe̱o titri;
24ši wo̱henii ni yo̱ fe̱o momo le̱ ehĩaa no. Ši Nyoṅmo̱ to gbomotšo le̱ gbe̱dšiano̱ etšăra, ni noni ſe̱o̱le̱ noko le̱, no titri eke̱ wō hã;
25koni mligblamo̱ akaba gbomotšo le̱ mli, ši moṅ henii le̱ abābā ame̱he yi pe̱pe̱pe̱.
26Ni ke̱dši henõ kome mīna nõ le̱, henii le̱ fẽ ke̱le̱ naä nõ; ni ke̱dši henõ kome hĩe ba nyam hũ, henii fẽ le̱ ke̱le̱ náa miše̱.
27Ši nye le̱, Kristo gbomotšo dšinye, ke̱ ehenii ye̱ mokomekome gbe̱fãṅ. Rom. 12,5. Ef. 5,30.
28Ni kleṅkleṅ le̱ Nyoṅmo̱ wo meikomei bo̱foi ye̱ asafo le̱ mli, noni dši enyo̱ le̱, gbalo̱i, noni dši etẽ le̱, tšōlo̱i, no se̱ le̱, hewale̱i, no se̱ le̱, helai-atšámo̱ dromo̱kēnii, yeli-ke̱-buamo̱, no̱yelii, wiemo̱i sro̱toi awiemo̱. Ef. 4,11. 12.
29Ani mei fẽ dši bo̱foi? ani mei fẽ dši gbalo̱i? ani mei fẽ dši tšõlo̱i? ani mei fẽ dši hewale̱-nitšulo̱i?
30ani mei fẽ yo̱ helai-atšámo̱ dromo̱kēnii? ani mei fẽ wieo̱ wiemo̱i sro̱toi? ani mei fẽ tšõo̱ wiemo̱i ašiši?
31Ši nyehīe ado̱a dromo̱kēnii ní hĩ titri le̱ ahe. Ni masā matšõnye gbe̱ ní hĩ fè fẽ. 14,1.

english_text:
Love
1What if I could speak
all languages of humans
and even of angels?
If I did not love others,
I would be nothing more
than a noisy gong
or a clanging cymbal.
2 What if I could prophesy
and understand all mysteries
and all knowledge?
And what if I had faith
that moved mountains?
I would be nothing,
unless I loved others.
3What if I gave away all
that I owned
and let myself
be burned alive?
I would gain nothing,
unless I loved others.
4Love is patient and kind,
never jealous, boastful,
proud, or 5rude.
Love isn't selfish
or quick tempered.
It doesn't keep a record
of wrongs that others do.
6Love rejoices in the truth,
but not in evil.
7Love is always supportive,
loyal, hopeful,
and trusting.
8Love never fails!
Everyone who prophesies
will stop,
and unknown languages
will no longer
be spoken.
All that we know
will be forgotten.
9We don't know everything,
and our prophecies
are not complete.
10But what is perfect
will someday appear,
and what isn't perfect
will then disappear.
11When we were children,
we thought and reasoned
as children do.
But when we grew up,
we quit our childish ways.
12Now all we can see of God
is like a cloudy picture
in a mirror.
Later we will see him
face to face.
We don't know everything,
but then we will,
just as God completely
understands us.
13For now there are faith,
hope, and love.
But of these three,
the greatest is love.
translation_text:
1Ke̱dši mike̱ gbomei ke̱ ṅweibo̱foi alile̱ii wieo̱, ši mibe̱ suomo̱ le̱, kũle̱ mitšṍ ayawa ní dšidšeo̱ lo ṅmle̱ ní gbē̱o̱.
2Ni ke̱dši miye̱ gbale̱, ni minaä tẽmo̱nii fẽ nā, ni mile nii fẽ, ni ke̱dši miye̱ hemo̱-ke̱-yeli fẽ hũ, bo̱ni manyẽ gõdši matšire̱, ši mibe̱ suomo̱ le̱, dšikũle̱ midšee noko. Mat. 7,22; 17,20.
3Ni ke̱dši miṅõ minii fẽ mikũma mei, ni ke̱dši miṅõ migbomotšo mihã ni ašãmi, ši mibe̱ suomo̱ le̱, dšikũle̱ mináá se̱ ko. Mat. 6,2.
4Suomo̱ too̱ etšui ši, emli hĩ: suomo̱ he tšẽẽ mo; suomo̱ eſãã, efee pupūpu,
5efee nii ni esaa, *eplee le̱dientše̱ enõ, emli woo la, eniṅṅ efõṅ he, Fil. 2,4. 21.
6enyã́ã́ nõša he, ši enyã́a ano̱kwale he; Rom. 12,9.
7*emĩo̱ ṅō̃ ye̱ nii fẽ mli, eheo̱ nii fẽ eyeo̱, ehĩe kãa nii fẽ no̱, etoo̱ etsui ši ye̱ nii fẽ mli. *Abe̱i 10,12. Rom. 15,1.
8Suomo̱ se̱ efoo gbĩkogbĩko. Ši ke̱-dši gbale̱i ni le̱, ame̱se̱ bafo; ke̱dši wiemo̱i ni le̱, abafõ; ke̱dši nilē ni le̱, ese̱ bafo.
9Edšake̱ wo̱nii ní wo̱le le̱, fã-ke̱-fã ni, ni wo̱gbale̱ hũ fã-ke̱-fã ni,
10Ši ké̱ noni eye emū le̱ ba le̱, no le̱ noni dši fã-ke̱-fã le̱ se̱ aafo.
11Beni midsi abifao le̱, miwieo̱ tamo̱ abifao, midſẽṅo̱ nii ahe tamo̱ abifao, misusuo̱ tamo̱ abifao; ši beni mitšṍ ṅũ nukpa le̱, miše̱re̱ abiſabiianii le̱ miſie se̱.
12Edšake̱ ṅme̱ne̱ṅme̱ne̱ le̱ aſiſe̱ mli wo̱tšṍo̱ wo̱naä nii tūtū, ši no mli le̱, hĩe ke̱ hĩe; ṅme̱ne̱ṅme̱ne̱ le̱ mile nii fã-ke̱-fã, ši no mli le̱, male nii ke̱-yiši tamo̱ bo̱ni alemi ke̱-yiši le̱. 2 Kor. 5,7.
13Ši agbe̱ne̱ *hemo̱-ke̱-yeli, hĩeno̱kãmo̱, suomo̱, ne̱ke̱ nii etẽ ne̱ hĩo̱ ši; ši †suomo̱ dši ame̱teṅ noni fè fẽ. *1 Tes. 13. †1 Ioh. 4,16.

english_text:
Speaking Unknown Languages and Prophesying
1Love should be your guide. Be eager to have the gifts that come from the Holy Spirit, especially the gift of prophecy. 2If you speak languages that others don't know, God will understand what you are saying, though no one else will know what you mean. You will be talking about mysteries that only the Spirit understands. 3But when you prophesy, you will be understood, and others will be helped. They will be encouraged and made to feel better.
4By speaking languages that others don't know, you help only yourself. But by prophesying you help everyone in the church. 5I am glad for you to speak unknown languages, although I prefer that you would prophesy. In fact, prophesying does much more good than speaking unknown languages, unless someone can help the church by explaining what you mean.
6My friends, what good would it do, if I came and spoke unknown languages to you and didn't explain what I meant? How would I help you, unless I told you what God had shown me or gave you some knowledge or prophecy or teaching? 7If all musical instruments sounded alike, how would you know the difference between a flute and a harp? 8If a bugle call isn't clear, how would you know to get ready for battle?
9This is how it is when you speak unknown languages. If no one can understand what you are talking about, you will only be talking to the wind. 10There are many different languages in this world, and all of them make sense. 11But if I don't understand the language that someone is using, we will be like foreigners to each other. 12If you really want spiritual gifts, choose the ones that will be most helpful to the church.
13When we speak languages that others don't know, we should pray for the power to explain what we mean. 14For example, if I use an unknown language in my prayers, my spirit prays but my mind is useless. 15Then what should I do? There are times when I should pray with my spirit, and times when I should pray with my mind. Sometimes I should sing with my spirit, and at other times I should sing with my mind.
16Suppose some strangers are in your worship service, when you are praising God with your spirit. If they don't understand you, how will they know to say, “Amen”? 17You may be worshiping God in a wonderful way, but no one else will be helped. 18I thank God that I speak unknown languages more than any of you. 19But words that make sense can help the church. This is why in church I would rather speak five words that make sense than to speak 10,000 words in a language that others don't know.
20My friends, stop thinking like children. Think like mature people and be as innocent as tiny babies. 21 In the Scriptures the Lord says,
“I will use strangers
who speak unknown languages
to talk to my people.
They will speak to them
in foreign languages,
but still my people
won't listen to me.”
22Languages others don't know may mean something to unbelievers, but not to the Lord's followers. Prophecy, on the other hand, is for followers, not for unbelievers. 23Suppose everyone in your worship service started speaking unknown languages, and some outsiders or some unbelievers come in. Won't they think you are crazy? 24But suppose all of you are prophesying when those unbelievers and outsiders come in. They will realize that they are sinners, and they will want to change their ways because of what you are saying. 25They will tell what is hidden in their hearts. Then they will kneel down and say to God, “We are certain that you are with these people.”
Worship Must Be Orderly
26My friends, when you meet to worship, you must do everything for the good of everyone there. That's how it should be when someone sings or teaches or tells what God has said or speaks an unknown language or explains what the language means. 27No more than two or three of you should speak unknown languages during the meeting. You must take turns, and someone should always be there to explain what you mean. 28If no one can explain, you must keep silent in church and speak only to yourself and to God.
29Two or three persons may prophesy, and everyone else must listen carefully. 30If someone sitting there receives a message from God, the speaker must stop and let the other person speak. 31Let only one person speak at a time, then all of you will learn something and be encouraged. 32A prophet should be willing to stop and let someone else speak. 33God wants everything to be done peacefully and in order.
When God's people meet in church, 34the women must not be allowed to speak. They must keep quiet and listen, as the Law of Moses teaches. 35If there is something they want to know, they can ask their husbands when they get home. It is disgraceful for women to speak in church.
36God's message did not start with you people, and you are not the only ones it has reached.
37If you think of yourself as a prophet or a spiritual person, you will know I am writing only what the Lord has commanded. 38So don't pay attention to anyone who ignores what I am writing. 39My friends, be eager to prophesy and don't stop anyone from speaking languages that others don't know. 40But do everything properly and in order.
translation_text:
1Nyedia suomo̱ se̱. Ši nyehĩe ado̱a ye̱ mumo̱ṅnii le̱ ahe, ši titri le̱, koni nyegba. 12,10. 31.
2Edšake̱ moni wieo̱ ke̱ lile̱i sro̱to ko le̱, dšee gbomei ewieo̱ etšõo̱, ši Nyoṅmo̱ moṅ; edšake̱ mokomoko nuu, ši mumo̱ mli ewieo̱ tēmo̱sãdši ye̱.
3Ši moni gbaä le̱, gbomei ewieo̱ etšõo̱ ni eṅõ-hã ame̱nane amõ šĩ, ni ebo̱ame̱ ko̱ko̱, ni eše̱dše ame̱mī.
4Moni wieo̱ ke̱ lile̱i sro̱to ko le̱, le̱dientše̱ enane ehãa mõo̱ ši; ši moni gbaä le̱, asafo le̱ nane ehãa mõo̱ ši.
5Ši mīsumo̱ ni *nyefẽ nyewie ke̱ lile̱ii sro̱toi; ši noni misumoo̱ titri dši ake̱ nyegbe; edšake̱ moni gbaä le̱ efè moni wieo̱ ke̱ lile̱ii sro̱toi, dša †etšõ šiši hũ, koni asafo le̱ nane amõ ši. *4 Mose 11,29. †1 Kor. 12,10.
6Ši agbe̱ne̱, anyemimei, ke̱dši miba nyeṅõ mibawie ke̱ lile̱ii sro̱toi ní dšee kpodšiemo̱ alo *nilē alo gbale̱ alo nitšõmo̱ ko ni le̱, mẽ se̱ mihãa nyenaa? *12,8.
7Take̱ bo̱ni nii ni be̱ wala le̱ gbē̱o̱ le̱, ble̱ dsio, saṅkũ dšio, ke̱dši egbē̱ē̱ ke̱ gbēi sro̱toisro̱toi le̱, té aafe tēṅ ní aale noni akpāa lo noni atſaä le̱ṅ?
8Edšake̱ ke̱dši te̱tre̱mantre̱ egbē̱ē̱ gbē̱mo̱ ní yo̱ faṅṅ le̱, namo aasā ehe ato ta?
9Nakai noṅṅ kẽ dši nye̱ hũ ye̱ lile̱i gbe̱fāṅ: ke̱dši nyewiee wiemo̱ ní šiši yo̱ faṅṅ le̱, té aafe tẽṅ ní aale noni akē̱o̱ le̱? Edšake̱ nyetamo̱ mei ní wieo̱ tšõo̱ kō̱yo̱.
10Gbēĩ sro̱toi pī ye̱ dše le̱ṅ moṅ, ši ekomeflo be̱ ní be̱ šiši.
11Ši agbe̱ne̱ ke̱dši minaa wiemo̱ le̱ šiši le̱, bĕle̱ mibatšṍ dšekõnyo ye̱ moni wieo̱ le̱ hĩe, ni moni wieo̱ le̱ hũ batšṍ dšekõnyo ye̱ mihĩe.
12Gbĩĩ abo̱ ní nyehĩe do̱ō̱ ye̱ mumo̱ṅnii ahe le̱, nakai noṅṅ nyetaoa koni nyeteke no̱ ni asafo le̱ nane amõ ši. K. 1-4.
13Nohewo̱ le̱ moni wieo̱ ke̱ lile̱i sro̱to ko le̱, hā ní eso̱le koni etšõ šiši, hũ. 12,10.
14Edšake̱ ke̱dši miso̱leo̱ ke̱ lile̱i sro̱to dšiṅṅ, mimumo̱ le̱ so̱leo̱ moṅ, ši midſẽṅmo̱ le̱ ewoo yibii.
15Agbe̱ne̱ meni? Mĩke̱ mumo̱ aaso̱le, ši mĩke̱ dſẽṅmo̱ hũ aaso̱le; mala *lala ke̱ momo, ši mala lala ke̱ dſẽṅmo hũ. *Ef. 5,19.
16Edšake̱ ké̱ oke̱ mumo̱ mīdšō̱ le̱, té aafe tẽṅ ni moni tá mei ni lee mli eko le̱ agbe̱he le̱ aakē̱ Amen aši ošidā le̱ no̱, ake̱-ní elee noni okē̱o̱ le̱?
17Edšake̱ bo le̱, oda ši dšogbāṅ moṅ, šĩ kẽle̱ mokroko le̱ nane mõõ ši.
18Mīda mi-Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ ši ake̱ mifè nyefẽ ye̱ lile̱ii sro̱toi amli;
19ši kẽle̱, asafo le̱ mli le̱, mīsumo̱ ake̱ mike̱ midſẽṅmo̱ awie wiemo̱i komekomei enumo̱, koni maṅõ-tšõ meikrokomei anii moṅ, fè noni mawie wiemo̱i komekomei akpei-nyoṅma ye̱ lile̱i sro̱to mli.
20Anyemimei, nyekafea nyehe *gbekẽbii ye̱ dſẽṅmo̱ gbe̱ſāṅ, ši efõṅ gbe̱ſāṅ le̱ nyefea nyehe abifabii; ši dſẽṅmo̱ gbe̱fāṅ le̱, nyefea nyehe mei ní †edăra. *Ef. 4,15. †Fil. 3,12. 15.
21*Aṅmã ye̱ mla le̱ mli ake̱: “Wiemo̱i sro̱toi amli ke̱ nãbui sro̱toi ano̱ matšṍ mike̱ ne̱ke̱ maṅ ne̱ awie, ši no hū tete ame̱boṅmi toi, Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ kē̱.” *5 Mose 28,49. Ies. 28,11. 12.
22Nohewo̱ le̱ lile̱ii sro̱toi le̱ edšee okadi hã heyelilo̱i, ši moṅ edši okadi hã mei ni hee yee; ni gbale̱ le̱, edšee mei ní hee yee le̱ anõ, ši moṅ heyelilo̱i anõ ni.
23Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ ke̱dši asafo mū le̱ fẽ nā bakpe ši ye̱ hekome, ni mei le̱ fẽ ke̱ lile̱ii sro̱toi mīwie, ni mei ní lee mli eko alo mei ní hee yee le̱ ateṅ meikomei hũ ba dše̱i le̱, ani ame̱kē̱ṅ ake̱ nyemīye se̱ke̱?
24Ši ke̱dši mei le̱ fẽ mīgba, ni moko ní hee yee alo elee mli eko ba dše̱i le̱, mei le̱ fẽ aakãle̱, mei le̱ fẽ aakodšole̱,
25aadšie etšuiṅ tēmo̱nii akpo faṅṅ, ni no aahã eke̱ ehĩe abu ši edšá Nyoṅmo̱, ni eedšadše ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ye̱ nyeteṅ le̱le̱ṅ. Ioh. 14,8.
26Bĕle̱ meniṅ mo̱, anyemimei? Ké̱ *nyenā bakpe ši, ni nyeteṅ moko ye̱ lala ko, moko hũ †ye̱ tšõmo̱ ko, moko ye̱ lile̱i sro̱to ko, moko ye̱ kpodšiemo̱ ko, moko ye̱ šišitšõmo̱ ko le̱: nyehãa afea fẽ **bo̱ni mei anane aamõ ši. *11,18. 20. †12,8-10. **Ef. 4,12.
27Ke̱dši aawie lile̱i sro̱to le̱, dāne̱, mei enyo̱ lo, ké̱ efá āhũ le̱, mei etẽ pe̱ áwĩe, mokomekome, ni mokome hũ átšõ šiši;
28ši ke̱dši šĩšitšõlo̱ ko be̱ le̱, hã ní efe diō ye̱ asafo le̱ mli, ši ewie ehã le̱dientše̱ ehe ke̱ Nyoṅmo̱.
29Ši gbaloi le̱, mei enyo̱ lo mei etẽ awie, ni mei ní eſe̱ le̱ *akodšo. *1 Tes. 5,21. Bo̱f. 17,11.
30Ši ke̱dši adšie noko kpo atšõ moko ni tá ši le̱, tšutšumo le̱ afe diō.
31Edšake̱ ké̱ afe mokomekome le̱, nyefẽ nyeanyẽ nyegba, koni mei fẽ akase nii ni awie atšõ mei fẽ.
32Ši gbalo̱i amumo̱i le̱ baã ame̱he ši ame̱hãa gbaloi le̱;
33edšake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, edšee sakasa-kafemo̱ Nyoṅmo̱, ši moṅ hedšo̱le̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ni; take̱ bo̱ni eyo̱ ye̱ hetšelo̱i asafoi le̱ fẽ mli le̱.
34Nyehãa *yei le̱ afea diō ye̱ asafoi le̱ amli, edšake̱ aṅmẽẽame̱ gbe̱ ní ame̱wie, ši moṅ †ame̱ba ame̱he ši, take̱ bo̱ni mla le̱ hũ kē̱o le̱. *1 Tim. 2,12. †1 Kor. 11.3. Ef. 5,22. Tit. 2,5. 1 Mose 3,16.
35Ši ké̱ ame̱mīsumo̱ ake̱ ame̱kase noko le̱, ame̱bi ame̱dientše̱ ame̱wùmei ye̱ šĩa. Edšake̱ eye̱ hīegbĕle hã yei ake̱ ame̱awie ye̱ asafo mli.
36Alo nyeṅõ Nyoṅmo̱ wiemo̱ le̱ dše̱? Alo nye ke̱ke̱ nyeṅõ eba?
37Ké̱ efeo̱ moko ake̱ gbalo̱ alo mumo̱ṅgbomo dšile̱ le̱, sa ake̱ ele ake̱ noni miṅmãnye ne̱, Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ kitãi ni; 1 Ioh. 4,6.
38ši ké̱ moko lee noko le̱, ekale.
39Nohewo̱ le̱, anyemimei, nyehĩe ado̱a ye̱ gbalo̱ hewo̱, ni lile̱ii sro̱toi ke̱ wiemo̱ le̱ hũ nyekatšĩa nā.
40Afe nii fẽ bo̱ni yo̱ fe̱o ke̱ gbe̱nā-gbe̱nā. Kol. 2,5.

english_text:
Christ Was Raised to Life
1My friends, I want you to remember the message I preached and that you believed and trusted. 2You will be saved by this message, if you hold firmly to it. But if you don't, your faith was all for nothing.
3 I told you the most important part of the message exactly as it was told to me. This part is:
Christ died for our sins,
as the Scriptures say.
4 He was buried,
and three days later
he was raised to life,
as the Scriptures say.
5 Christ appeared to Peter,
then to the twelve.
6After this, he appeared
to more than five hundred
other followers.
Most of them are still alive,
but some have died.
7He also appeared to James,
then to all of the apostles.
8 Finally, he appeared to me, even though I am like someone who was born at the wrong time.
9 I am the least important of all the apostles. In fact, I caused so much trouble for God's church that I don't even deserve to be called an apostle. 10But God treated me with undeserved grace! He made me what I am, and his grace wasn't wasted. I worked much harder than any of the other apostles, although it was really God's grace at work and not me. 11But it doesn't matter if I preached or if they preached. All of you believed the message just the same.
God's People Will Be Raised to Life
12If we preach that Christ was raised from death, how can some of you say the dead will not be raised to life? 13If they won't be raised to life, Christ himself wasn't raised to life. 14And if Christ wasn't raised to life, our message is worthless, and so is your faith. 15If the dead won't be raised to life, we have told lies about God by saying he raised Christ to life, when he really did not.
16So if the dead won't be raised to life, Christ wasn't raised to life. 17Unless Christ was raised to life, your faith is useless, and you are still living in your sins. 18And those people who died after putting their faith in him are completely lost. 19If our hope in Christ is good only for this life, we are worse off than anyone else.
20But Christ has been raised to life! And he makes us certain that others will also be raised to life. 21Just as we will die because of Adam, we will be raised to life because of Christ. 22Adam brought death to all of us, and Christ will bring life to all of us. 23But we must each wait our turn. Christ was the first to be raised to life, and his people will be raised to life when he returns. 24Then after Christ has destroyed all powers and forces, the end will come, and he will give the kingdom to God the Father.
25 Christ will rule until he puts all his enemies under his power, 26and the last enemy he destroys will be death. 27 When the Scriptures say he will put everything under his power, they don't include God. It was God who put everything under the power of Christ. 28After everything is under the power of God's Son, he will put himself under the power of God, who put everything under his Son's power. Then God will mean everything to everyone.
29 If the dead are not going to be raised to life, what will people do who are being baptized for them? Why are they being baptized for those dead people? 30And why do we always risk our lives 31and face death every day? The pride that I have in you because of Christ Jesus our Lord is what makes me say this. 32 What do you think I gained by fighting wild animals in Ephesus? If the dead are not raised to life,
“Let's eat and drink.
Tomorrow we die.”
33Don't fool yourselves. Bad friends will destroy you. 34Be sensible and stop sinning. You should be embarrassed that some people still don't know about God.
What Our Bodies Will Be Like
35Some of you have asked, “How will the dead be raised to life? What kind of bodies will they have?” 36Don't be foolish. A seed must die before it can sprout from the ground. 37Wheat seeds and all other seeds look different from the sprouts that come up. 38This is because God gives everything the kind of body he wants it to have. 39People, animals, birds, and fish are each made of flesh, but none of them are alike. 40Everything in the heavens has a body, and so does everything on earth. But each one is very different from all the others. 41The sun isn't like the moon, the moon isn't like the stars, and each star is different.
42That's how it will be when our bodies are raised to life. These bodies will die, but the bodies that are raised will live forever. 43These ugly and weak bodies will become beautiful and strong. 44As surely as there are physical bodies, there are spiritual bodies. And our physical bodies will be changed into spiritual bodies.
45 The first man was named Adam, and the Scriptures tell us that he was a living person. But Jesus, who may be called the last Adam, is a life-giving spirit. 46We see that the one with a spiritual body did not come first. He came after the one who had a physical body. 47The first man was made from the dust of the earth, but the second man came from heaven. 48Everyone on earth has a body like the body of the one who was made from the dust of the earth. And everyone in heaven has a body like the body of the one who came from heaven. 49Just as we are like the one who was made out of earth, we will be like the one who came from heaven.
50My friends, I want you to know that our bodies of flesh and blood will decay. This means they cannot share in God's kingdom, which lasts forever. 51 I will explain a mystery to you. Not every one of us will die, but we will all be changed. 52It will happen suddenly, quicker than the blink of an eye. At the sound of the last trumpet the dead will be raised. We will all be changed, so we will never die again. 53Our dead and decaying bodies will be changed into bodies that won't die or decay. 54 The bodies we now have are weak and can die. But they will be changed into bodies that are eternal. Then the Scriptures will come true,
“Death has lost the battle!
55 Where is its victory?
Where is its sting?”
56Sin is what gives death its sting, and the Law is the power behind sin. 57But thank God for letting our Lord Jesus Christ give us the victory!
58My dear friends, stand firm and don't be shaken. Always keep busy working for the Lord. You know that everything you do for him is worthwhile.
translation_text:
1Ši, anyemimei, mihã nyele ake̱ sanekpakpa le̱ ní mīdšadše mitšõnye, ni nyemõ mli hũ, ni nyehĩe mli hũ le̱,
2no noṅṅ ake̱-aahere nyeyiwala, ké̱ nyemõmo̱ mli bo̱ni midšadše mitšõnye le̱, ké̱ dšee nakai le̱ nyehe nyeye yakatſā.
3Edšake̱ kleṅkleṅ sãdši ní mike̱-hãnye le̱ ateṅ eko dši noni mi hũ ake̱-hãmi, ake̱ Kristo gbo ye̱ wo̱he ešai le̱ ahewo̱ ye̱ *ṅmãle̱i le̱ anā, *Ies. 53.8. 9.
4ni ake̱ afũle̱, ni ake̱ atēle̱ ši ekoṅ ye̱ gbĩ ní dši gbĩ etẽ le̱ no̱ ye̱ *ṅmãle̱i le̱ anā; *Lal. 16,10.
5ni ake̱ edšie ehe kpo etšõ *Kefa, no se̱ le̱ †mei nyoṅma ke̱ enyo̱ le̱. *Luk. 24,34. †Mar. 16,14.
6No se̱ le̱ edšie ehe kpo etšõ aafe nyemimei ohai-enumo̱ lo nõ šikome, mei ni ame̱teṅ mei pī yo̱ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱, ši meikomei hũ éwo̱.
7No se̱ le̱ edšie ebe kpo etšõ Iakobo, no se̱ le̱ *bo̱foi le̱ fẽ. *Luk. 24,50.
8Ši ame̱fẽ ame̱se̱ le̱ edšie ehe kpo etšõ *mi hũ ní mitamo̱ moko ní akpatu afo̱le̱ le̱. *9,1.
9Edšake̱ mi le̱ midši *bibiō fè fẽ ye̱ bo̱foi le̱ ateṅ, ni misaa tete ake̱ atšé̱o̱mi bo̱fo hũ, edšake̱ miwa Nyoṅmo asafo le yi. *Ef. 3,8.
10Ši Nyoṅmo̱ dromo̱ mike̱-dši noni midši ne̱, ni edromo̱ le̱ ni edromi le̱ efee yaka; ši moṅ noni teke ame̱fẽ ame̱nõ le̱ ne̱ ni mitšu; ši dšee mi tete, ši moṅ Nyoṅmo̱ dromo̱ ní ke̱mi yo̱ le. 2 Kor. 11,5. 25.
11Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱, miṅ ō, ame̱ṅ ō, nakai wo̱šie̱o̱, ni nakai nyehe nyeye hũ.
12Ši kē̱ ãšie̱ ye̱ Kristo be ake̱ atēle̱ ši ke̱-dše̱ gbohĩĩ ateṅ le̱, té tẽṅ ní nyeteṅ meikomei kē̱o̱ ake̱ gbohĩĩašitē ko be̱ le̱?
13Ši ké̱ gbohĩĩašitē ko be̱ le̱, bĕle̱ Kristo hũ atēēle̱ ši.
14Ši ké̱ atēē Kristo ši le̱, bĕle̱ we̱šie̱mo̱ le̱ efe yaka, ni nyehemo̱-ke̱-yeli le̱ hū efe yaka;
15ni asaṅ akpawo̱ ši ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ be amale-odaseyelo̱i dšiwo̱, edšake̱ wo̱ye Nyoṅmo̱ he odase ako̱ etē Kristo ši, moni, ke̱dši eye̱ mli ake̱ gbohĩĩ etee ši le̱, bĕle̱ etēkole̱ ši. Bo̱f. 1,22.
16Edšake̱ ké̱ atēē gbohĩĩ aši le̱, bĕle̱ Kristo hũ atēkole̱ ši. 6,14.
17Ni asaṅ ké̱ atēko Kristo ši le̱, no le̱ nyehemo̱-ke̱-yeli le̱ efe yaka, ni nye-kãmo̱ nyehe ešai le̱ amli lolo; K. 14.
18no le̱ mei ní ewo̱ ye̱ Kristo mli le̱ hũ elādše.
19Ké̱ wala ne̱ mli ke̱ke̱ wo̱hĩe kã Kristo no̱ yo̱ le̱, wo̱nii ye̱ mo̱bo̱ fè gbomei fẽ.
20Ši agbe̱ne̱ atē Kristo ši ke̱-dše̱ gbohĩĩ ateṅ, efe *kleṅkleṅmo ye̱ mei ní †ewo̱ le̱ ateṅ. *Kol. 1,18. †1 Kor. 11,30.
21Edšake̱ bo̱ni gbĕle tšṍ gbomo no̱ ke̱-ba le̱, nakai noṅṅ šitē hũ tšṍ gbomo no̱ ko̱-ba. 1 Mose 3,17-18. Rom. 5,12. 18.
22Edšake̱ take̱ bo̱ni Adam mli ni mei fẽ gboio̱ ye̱ le̱, nakai noṅṅ kẽ Kristo mli ni ame̱fẽ ame̱yi aaná wala ye̱.
23Ši mofẽmo ye̱ le̱dientše̱ egbe̱dšiano̱: *kleṅkleṅmo dši Kristo, †no se̱ le̱ mei ni dši Kristo nii le̱, ye̱ ebā le̱ mli; *K. 20. †1 Tes. 4,15. Kpods. 20,5.
24no se̱ dãni nāgbē le̱ baba, beni eeṅõ maṅtše̱yeli le̱ ehã Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱ tše̱ le̱, ni eefo no̱yeli fẽ ke̱ hegbe̱ fẽ ke̱ hewale̱ fẽ se̱ le̱. Dan. 2,44.
25Ši dša eye maṅtše̱ ke̱-yaši beyino̱ ní eeṅõ henye̱lo̱i le̱ fẽ eto enãdšiaši. Lal. 110,1. Mat. 22,44.
26Nāgbē henye̱lo̱ ní abafo ese̱ dši gbĕle. Kpods. 20,14; 21,5.
27Edšake̱ *eṅõ nibii fẽ-kwa eto enãdšiaši. Ši ké̱ ekē̱ ake̱ aṅõ nibii fẽ ato ešiši le̱, bĕle̱ eye̱ faṅṅ ake̱ moni ṅõ nibii fẽ to ešiši le̱ be̱ mli. *Lal. 8,7.
28Ši beni aṅõ nii fẽ ato bi le̱ šiši le̱, no le̱ le̱dientše̱ hũ eeṅõ ehe eto moni ṅõ nii fẽ to ešiši le̱ šiši, koni Nyoṅmo̱ afe nibii fẽ ayitšo.
29Edšake̱, mei ní hãa abaptisio̱ame̱ ye̱ gbohĩĩ anãdšiaṅ le̱, tē ame̱bafe tēṅ? Ké̱ gbohĩĩ eteṅ ši kwrā le̱, mẽba mo̱ ni ame̱hãa abaptisio̱ame̱ ye̱ gbohĩĩ anãdšiaṅ le̱?
30Mẽba wo̱ hũ wo̱naã amane ṅmle̱tſā-fẽ-ṅmle̱tſā le̱? Rom. 8,36.
31Mina nyeheſā̃ ní miyo̱ ye̱ wo̱-Nuṅtšo̱ Kristo Iesu mli le̱, ake̱ migboo̱ dãne̱. 2 Kor. 4,10. 11.
32Ké̱ gbomo gbe̱fãṅ ni mike̱ koloi awuyelo̱i wu ye̱, ye̱ Efeso le̱, kũle̱ mẽ se̱námo̱ miyo̱? Ké̱ gbohĩĩ etee ši le̱: *“Nyehãa wo̱yea nii ni wo̱nua dā̃i, edšake̱ wó̱ le̱, wo̱bagboi!” *Ies. 22,13.
33Nyekahša ašišinanye. Nanyobō̱ fõṅ fiteo̱ dšeṅba kpakpa.
34*Nyehãa nyehĩe atše̱re̱anye dšogbāṅ, ni nyekafea eša; edšake̱ nyeteṅ meikomei †lee nokonoko ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ hewo̱. **Mīkē̱ ene̱ mike̱-wonye hĩegbĕle. *Rom. 13,11. Ef. 5,14. †Bo̱f. 26,8. **1 Kor. 6,5.
35Ši ekole̱ moko aabi ake̱: Té gbohĩĩ aafe tẽṅ ate šiṅ? ni asaṅ mẽ gbomotšo ame̱ke̱-aba?
36Kwašia! Noni bo̱dientše̱ odũo̱ le̱, *dša egbo fẽdã ni eyi náa wala, *Ioh. 12,24.
37ni asaṅ noni odũo̱ le̱, dšee tšo ní babale̱ odũo̱ lé̱, ši moṅ dũmo̱wú kuli ko ke̱ke̱, ké̱ ṅmã ni dšio, nii ni eſe̱ le̱ eko ni dšio;
38ši Nyoṅmo̱ hãale̱ tšo bo̱ni esumoo̱, ni wú-fẽ-wú le̱, ehãale̱ le̱dientše̱ etšo. 1 Mose 1,11.
39Dšee helo ſẽ dši helo kome, ši moṅ esõro gbomei ahelo, ni esõro koloi ahelo, esõro nuṅloi anõ, ni esõro lofõdši anõ hũ.
40Ni ṅwei gbomotšei ye̱, ni šikpoṅ no̱ gbomotšei hũ ye̱; ši kẽle̱ esõro ṅwei nii anumnyam, ni esõro šikpoṅ no̱ nii le̱ hũ anõ.
41Esŏro hũlũ anumnyam, ni esõro nyoṅtšẽre hũ anumnyam, ni esŏro ṅulamii anumnyam; edšake̱ ṅulami kome fè ṅulami kroko anumnyam.
42Nakai noṅṅ dši gbohĩĩašitē le̱ hũ. Adũo̱le̱ ye̱ fitemo̱ mli, atēo̱le̱ ši ye̱ noni fitee mli;
43adũo̱le̱ ye̱ noni be̱ nyam mli, atēo̱le̱ ši ye̱ *anumnyam mli; adũo̱le̱ ye̱ gbedemo̱ mli, atēo̱le̱ ši ye̱ hewale̱ mli; *Fil. 3,20. 21.
44aduo̱ susuma gbomotšo, atēo̱ mumo̱ gbomotšo ši. Ké̱ Susuma gbomotšo ye̱ le̱, mumo̱ gbomotšo hũ ye̱.
45Nakai *aṅmā hũ ake̱: “Adam ni dši kleṅkleṅ gbomo le̱ tšṍ misusu ní hĩe kã,” nāgbē Adam le̱ tšṍ †mumo̱ ní hãa mo yi náa wala. *1 Mose 2,7. †2 Kor. 3,17.
46Ši dšee mumo̱nõ le̱ dši kleṅkleṅnõ, ši moṅ susumanõ le̱, no se̱ le̱ mumo̱nõ le̱.
47Kleṅkleṅ gbomo le̱ ní dše̱ šikpoṅ no̱ le̱, šikpoṅno̱nyo ni; gbomo ní dši enyo̱ le̱, dši Nuṅtšo̱ ní dše̱ ṅwei le̱.
48Bo̱ni šikpoṅno̱nyo le̱ yo̱ le̱, nakai šikpoṅno̱bii le̱ hũ yo̱; ni bo̱ni ṅweinyo le̱ yo̱ le̱, nakai ṅweibii le̱ hũ yo̱;
49ni tamo̱ bo̱ni wo̱hĩe šikpoṅno̱nyo le̱ *subãṅ le̱, nakai noṅṅ wo̱bahĩe ṅweinyo le̱ hũ subãṅ. 1 Mose 5,3.
50Anyemimei, noni mikē̱o̱ dši ake̱, helo ke̱ lá nine še̱ṅ Nyoṅmo̱ maṅtše̱yeli le̱ no̱, ni asaṅ fitemo̱ hũ nine še̱ṅ noni fitee le̱ no̱. 6,13.
51Na, tēmo̱sane miṅõ-kē̱o̱nye ne̱: *Dšee wo̱fẽ wo̱bawo̱ le̱, ši abatšake wo̱fẽ, *1 Tes. 4,15. 17.
52trukă, hĩṅme̱itſā mli, beni aakpã́ nāgbē *te̱tre̱mantre̱ le̱; edšake̱ abakpã́ te̱tre̱mantre̱, ni aatē gbohĩĩ aši ni ame̱fiteṅ doṅṅ, ni wo̱ le̱, abatšakewo̱. *Mat 24,31. 1 Tes. 4,16.
53Edšake̱ dša ne̱ke̱ fitemo̱nō ne̱ wo noni fitee le̱, ni ne̱ke̱ gbĕlenō ne̱ wo noni gboo le̱. 2 Kor. 5,4.
54Ši beni ne̱ke̱ fitemo̱nõ ne̱ ewo nom fitee le̱, ni ne̱ke̱ gbĕlenõ ne̱ ewo noni gboo le̱, no le̱ wiemo̱ ní aṅmã le̱ aaba mli ake̱:
55“Amĩ gbĕle ye̱ kũnim mli. Bo gbĕle, nēgbe̱ ogãi le̱ yo̱? bo gbohĩĩadše, nẽgbe̱ okũnim le̱ ye̱?” Ies. 25,8. Hos. 13,14.
56Ši gbĕle gãi dši eša; ni *eša hewale̱ dši mla le̱. *Rom. 7,13; 6,14.
57Ši šidā ahã Nyoṅmo̱, moni tšṍ wo̱-Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu Kristo no̱ ni ehã wo̱ye kũnim le̱.
58Nohewo̱ le̱, minyemimei ni misumoo̱, nyefĩa ši ní nyekagbugbãa, ni nyetekea no̱ ye̱ Nuntše̱ le̱ nitšumo̱ le̱ mli dāne̱, edšake̱ nyele *ake̱ nyemo̱deṅbō̱ le̱ efee yaka ye̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ mli. *2 Kron. 15,7.

english_text:
A Collection for God's People
1 When you collect money for God's people, I want you to do exactly what I told the churches in Galatia to do. 2That is, each Sunday each of you must put aside part of what you have earned. If you do this, you won't have to take up a collection when I come. 3Choose some followers to take the money to Jerusalem. I will send them on with the money and with letters which show that you approve of them. 4If you think I should go along, they can go with me.
Paul's Travel Plans
5 After I have gone through Macedonia, I hope to see you 6and visit with you for a while. I may even stay all winter, so that you can help me on my way to wherever I will be going next. 7If the Lord lets me, I would rather come later for a longer visit than to stop off now for only a short visit. 8 I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost, 9because there is a wonderful opportunity for me to do some work here. But there are also many people who are against me.
10 When Timothy arrives, give him a friendly welcome. He is doing the Lord's work, just as I am. 11Don't let anyone mistreat him. I am looking for him to return to me together with the other followers. So when he leaves, send him off with your blessings.
12I have tried hard to get our friend Apollos to visit you with the other followers. He doesn't want to come just now, but he will come when he can.
Personal Concerns and Greetings
13Keep alert. Be firm in your faith. Stay brave and strong. 14Show love in everything you do.
15 You know that Stephanas and his family were the first in Achaia to have faith in the Lord. They have done all they can for God's people. My friends, I ask you 16to obey leaders like them and to do the same for all others who work hard with you.
17I was glad to see Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus. Having them here was like having you. 18They made me feel much better, just as they made you feel better. You should appreciate people like them.
19 Greetings from the churches in Asia.
Aquila and Priscilla, together with the church that meets in their house, send greetings in the name of the Lord.
20All the Lord's followers send their greetings.
Give each other a warm greeting.
21I am signing this letter myself: PAUL.
22I pray that God will put a curse on everyone who doesn't love the Lord. And may the Lord come soon.
23I pray the Lord Jesus will be kind to you.
24I love everyone who belongs to Christ Jesus.
translation_text:
1Ši *onĩa ní atšũo̱ ayahã hetšelo̱i le̱ hewo̱ le̱, take̱ bo̱ni mito mihã Galatia asafoi le̱, nye hã nyefea nakai. *Bo̱f. 11,29. 2 Kor 8; 9. Gal. 2,10.
2Dā otši mli *kleṅkleṅ gbĩ le̱ no̱ le̱, ṅyeteṅ mofẽmo atĩa noko ato, ye̱ bo̱ni enáa le̱ nā, koni mikaba dãni atšũ onĩa le̱. *Bo̱f. 20,7.
3Ni ke̱dši miba le̱, matšũ mei ní nyebuo̱ ake̱ ame̱sa ke̱ wodši, ní ame̱hĩe nyenikēnii le̱ ke̱-ya Ierusalem.
4Ši ke̱dši esa ake̱ mi hũ mate le̱, mike̱ame̱ ate.
5Ši miyatšṍ Makedonia dãni maba nyeṅõ; edšake̱ Makedonia miyatšṍ. Bo̱f. 19,21.
6Ši ekole̱ mahĩ nyeṅõ fiō, ni ekole̱ maye fẽibe le̱ hũ ye̱ dše̱i, koni hefẽhe ní miyaä le̱, *nyeyadšiemi gbe̱. *Rom. 15,24.
7Edšake̱ agbe̱ne̱ misumo̱o̱ ake̱ minaänya ye̱ gbe̱teṅ ke̱ke̱, ši mihĩe kã no̱ ake̱, *ké̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ aaṅmẽmi gbe̱ le̱, †matše̱ fiō ye̱ nyeṅõ. *Bo̱f. 18,21. †Bo̱f. 20,2.
8Ši mĩbahĩ *Efeso ke̱-yaši Pentekoste-gbĩ le̱ no̱. *Bo̱f. 19,1. 10.
9Edšake̱ agble *šĩnā kpeteṅkple nā ahãmi, ni nitšumo̱ pī ye̱, ši mei ní kūo̱ nā hũ le̱ ayi fá. *2 Kor. 2,12. Kol. 4,3. Kpods. 3,9.
10Ši ke̱dši *Timoteo ba nyeṅõ le̱, nyekwe̱a ní eke̱ gbeyeišemo̱ akahĩ nyeteṅ; †edšake̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ nitšumo̱ noṅṅ etšuo̱ tamo̱ mi hũ. *4,17. †Fil. 2,20.
11Hewo̱ le̱ moko *akagbe ehe guo̱; †ši nyedšieale̱ gbe̱ ye̱ hedšo̱le̱ mli koni eba miṅõ; ši mihĩe kã no̱ ake̱ eke̱ nyemimei le̱ aaba. *1 Tim 4,12. †1 Kor. 16,6.
12Ši wo̱nyemi *Apolo le̱, mikpale fai āhũ ní eke̱ nyemimei le̱ aba nyeṅõ; ši ekplẽẽ kwrā ake̱ eeba amrõmrõ ne̱, ši ké̱ ená ehe dekã dšiṅṅ eeba. *1,12.
13Nyebua, nyedamo̱a ši šiṅṅ ye̱ hemo̱-ke̱-yeli le̱ mli, nyefea hĩĩ, ni *nyehe awaä! *Ef. 6,10.
14Nyefea nyenii fẽ ye̱ suomo̱ mli,
15Ši mīkpanye fai, anyemimei, nyele *Stefana šĩabii le̱, ake̱ ame̱dši Akaia †kleṅkleṅyibii, ni ame̱ko̱ meikroṅkroṅi le̱ asúomo̱ ame̱fõ ame̱no̱: *1,16. †Rom. 16,5.
16koni nye hū nyeba nyehe ši nyehã mene̱mei, ke̱ mofẽmo ní ke̱wo̱ tšuo̱ nii ni ebo̱ö̱ mo̱deṅ le̱. Fil. 2,20.
17Ši miná mīše̱ ye̱ Stefana ke̱ Fortunato ke̱ Akaiko bā le̱ hewo̱, edšake̱ ní nyebe̱ miṅõ ne̱, ame̱ ame̱baye nyenãdšiaṅ.
18Edšake̱ ame̱bahã mimumo̱ ke̱ nye hũ nyemumo̱ ewo ame̱tšui. Nohewo̱ le̱ ne̱ke̱ gbomei ne̱ *nyeleaame̱ dšogbāṅ. *1 Tes. 5,12
19Asia asafoi le̱ mībinye. *Akwila ke̱ Priskila ke̱ asafo ní yo̱ ame̱we le̱ mībinye dšogbāṅ ye̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ mli. *Bo̱f. 18,2. 18. 26. Rom. 16,3. 5.
20Nyemimei le̱ fẽ mībinye. *Nyeṅãṅãa nyehe ke̱ nāſo̱mo̱ kroṅkroṅ. *Rom. 16,16. 2 Kor. 13,12. 1 Pet. 5,14.
21Mi, Paulo dientše̱, minine nā bimo̱ ne̱. Kol. 4,18. 2 Tes. 3,17.
22Ké̱ moko sumo̱o̱ Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu Kristo sane le̱, *hã mo le̱ atšṍ musumo! Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ miba (Maran-ata)! *Gal. 1,8. 9.
23Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu Kristo dromo̱ le̱ kenye ahĩ ši!
24Misuomo̱ le̱ kenye fẽ ahĩ ši ye̱ Kristo Iesu mli! Amen.
(Kleṅkleṅ wolo ní aṅmã ke̱-yahã Korintobii le̱, ní aṅõ-mãdše ke̱-dše̱ Filipi ke̱-tšṍ Stefana ke̱ Fortunato ke̱ Akaiko ke̱ Timoteo no̱.)

english_text:
1 From Paul, chosen by God to be an apostle of Jesus Christ, and from Timothy, who is also a follower.
To God's church in Corinth and to all of God's people in Achaia.
2I pray that God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace!
Paul Gives Thanks
3Praise God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! The Father is a merciful God, who always gives us comfort. 4He comforts us when we are in trouble, so that we can share this same comfort with others in trouble. 5We share in the terrible sufferings of Christ, but also in the wonderful comfort he gives. 6We suffer in the hope that you will be comforted and saved. And because we are comforted, you will also be comforted, as you patiently endure suffering like ours. 7You never disappoint us. You suffered as much as we did, and we know that you will be comforted as we were.
8 My friends, I want you to know what a hard time we had in Asia. Our sufferings were so horrible and so unbearable that death seemed certain. 9In fact, we felt sure we were going to die. But this made us stop trusting in ourselves and start trusting God, who raises the dead to life. 10God saved us from the threat of death, and we are sure that he will do it again and again. 11Please help us by praying for us. Then many people will give thanks for the blessings we receive in answer to all these prayers.
Paul's Change of Plans
12We can be proud of our clear conscience. We have always lived honestly and sincerely, especially when we were with you. And we were guided by God's gift of undeserved grace instead of by the wisdom of this world. 13I am not writing anything you cannot read and understand. I hope you will understand it completely, 14just as you already partly understand us. Then when our Lord Jesus returns, you can be as proud of us as we are of you.
15I was so sure of your pride in us that I had planned to visit you first of all. In this way you would have the blessing of two visits from me— 16 once on my way to Macedonia and again on my return from there. Then you could send me on to Judea. 17Do you think I couldn't make up my mind about what to do? Or do I seem like someone who says “Yes” or “No” simply to please others? 18God can be trusted, and so can I, when I say our answer to you has always been “Yes” and never “No.” 19 This is because Jesus Christ the Son of God is always “Yes” and never “No.” And he is the one Silas, Timothy, and I told you about.
20Christ says “Yes” to all God's promises. This is why we have Christ to say “Amen” for us to the glory of God. 21And so God makes it possible for you and us to stand firmly together with Christ. God is also the one who chose us 22and put his Spirit in our hearts to show that we belong only to him.
23God is my witness that I stayed away from Corinth, just to keep from being hard on you. 24We are not bosses who tell you what to believe. We are working with you to make you glad, because your faith is strong.
translation_text:
1Paulo, ní dši Iesu Kristo bo̱fo *ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ suomo̱ nā le̱, ke̱ wo̱nyemi Timoteo le̱ ṅmã yahã Nyoṅmo̱ asafo ní yo̱ Korinto le̱ ke̱ hetšelo̱i fẽ ní yo̱ Akaia mū le̱ fẽ le̱: *1 Kor. 1,1.
2Dromo̱ ke̱ hedšo̱le̱ ní dše̱ wo̱tše̱ Nyoṅmo̱ le̱ ke̱ Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu Kristo deṅ le̱ ahãnye. Rom. 1,7.
3Adšō̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ke̱ wo̱-Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu Kristo tše̱ le̱, moni dši mũsũṅtšõle̱i atše̱ ke̱ *mīše̱dšemo̱ fẽ Nyoṅmo̱ le̱, *Rom. 15,5.
4moni še̱dšeo̱ womī ye̱ wo̱manehũlũi le̱ fẽ mli, koni wo̱ hũ wo̱nyẽ wo̱ke̱ mīše̱dšemo̱, ní Nyoṅmo̱ ṅõ-še̱dšeo̱ wo̱dientše̱ wo̱mī le̱, aše̱dše mei ni naä amanehũlũ-fẽ-amanehũlũ le̱ amī;
5edšake̱ boni Kristo amanehũlũi le̱ baä wo̱no̱ tekeo̱ no̱ le̱, nakai noṅṅ kẽ Kristo hewo̱ le̱ wo̱mīše̱dšemo̱ hū fáa tekeo̱ no̱. Lal. 34,20; 94,19.
6Ši ke̱dši amanehũlũ wo̱naä dšiṅṅ, *nyemīše̱dšemo̱ ke̱ walaheremo̱ hewo̱ ni; ni ke̱dši wo̱mī aše̱dšeo̱ hũ dšiṅṅ, nyemīše̱dšemo̱ ní hãa wo̱too̱ wo̱tšui ši kpō ke̱-naä nakai amanehũlũi le noṅṅ le̱ hewo̱ ni. *4.14. 11.
7Ni wo̱hĩe ní kã nyeno̱ le̱ gbugbãã, edšake̱ wo̱le ake̱, boni nyenaä amanehũlũi le̱ eko le̱, nakai noṅṅ kẽ nyenaa mīše̱dšemo̱ le̱ hũ eko.
8Edšake̱, anyemimei, wo̱sumo̱o̱ ake̱ wo̱ṅõ *wo̱manehũlũĩ ni wo̱na ye̱ Asia le̱ wo̱tēnye, ake̱ wo̱na nõ tšṍ, fè boni wo̱o̱nyẽ po, ni wo̱hĩe kãã wala no̱ tete; *Bo̱f. 19,23. 1 Kor. 15,32.
9ši moṅ wo̱dientše̱ wo̱na ye̱ wo̱mli faṅṅ ake̱ wo̱bagboi, koni wo̱kaṅõ wo̱hĩe wo̱fõ wo̱dientše̱ wo̱he no̱, ši moṅ wo̱ṅõ-fõ Nyoṅmo̱ ní tēo̱ gbohĩĩ aši le̱-no̱;
10mo hũ ni dšiewo̱ ke̱-dše̱ gbĕle ní tamo̱ ne̱ke̱ ne̱ mli, ni edšieo̱wo̱ lolo, ni wo̱hĩe kã eno̱ ake̱ esā eedšiewo̱ kwrā, 2 Tim. 4,18.
11ake̱ noni nye hũ nyefataä wo̱he ke̱-kpaä fai, koni mei pī ada ši ahãwo̱ ye̱ dromo̱kēnii ni aṅõ-hãwo̱ ye̱ mei pī ahewo̱ le̱ hewo̱.
12Ši wo̱ſā̃ le̱ ne̱: *wo̱henilē odase ní eyeo̱, ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ kro̱ṅṅfemo̱ ke̱ hetšemo̱ mli wo̱ba wo̱dšeṅ ye̱ dše ne̱ṅ, titri le̱ ye̱ nyeteṅ, ni dšee †heloṅ nilē nā, ši moṅ Nyoṅmo̱ dromo̱ nā. *2,17. Heb. 13,18. †1 Kor. 1,17.
13Edšake̱ wo̱nmãã nibii krokomei wo̱hããnye, fè nii ní nyekaneo̱ ni asaṅ nyele, ni mihĩe kã no̱ ake̱ nyeale ke̱-ate nāgbē hũ le̱,
14take̱ bo noṅṅ ni nyená nyelewo̱ hũ fã-ke̱-fã, ake̱ nyeſā̃nõ *dšiwo̱, tamo̱ boni †nye hũ nyedši wo̱nõ ye̱ Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu gbĩ le̱ no̱ le̱. *5,12. †Fil. 2,16.
15Ni ne̱ke̱ hĩe-ke̱-no̱fõ ne̱ hewo̱ mito miyiṅ ake̱ maba nyeṅõ tšutšu le̱, koni nyená dromo̱ ni dši enyo̱,
16ni mibatšṍ nyeṅõ ke̱-ya Makedonia, ni asaṅ makũ mise̱ ke̱-dše̱ Makedonia maba nyeṅõ ekoṅ, koni nyeyadšiemi gbe̱ ke̱-ya Iudea. 1 Kor. 16,5. 6.
17Bĕle̱ ní mito miyiṅ nakai le̱, yiṅ-fle̱fle̱ mike̱-fe? Alo miyiṅ ní mito le̱, helo nā mito ye̱? Dabi! ši mi-hē̃ le̱ hē̃ ni, ni mi-dabi le̱ dabi ni.
18Ši ano̱kwafo dši Nyoṅmo̱, ake̱ wo̱-wiemo̱ ní wo̱ke̱nye wie le̱ edšee hē̃ ke̱ dabi šikome.
19Edšake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ bi Iesu Kristo, moni mike̱ Silvano ke̱ Timoteo šie̱ ehe sane ye̱ nyeteṅ le̱, edšee hē̃ ke̱ dabi šikome, ši moṅ emli hē̃ yo̱.
20Ši Nyoṅmo̱ šiwōi abo̱ ní yo̱ ne̱, emli hē̃ le̱ yo̱ ni emli noṅṅ *amen le̱ yo̱, koni etšṍ wo̱no̱ awo Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe nyam. *Kpods 8,14.
21Ši Nyoṅmo̱ dši moni hãa wo̱ ke̱ nye-fẽ fĩo̱ ši ye̱ Kristo mli ni *efo̱wo̱ mũ, *1 Ioh. 2,27.
22le̱ noṅṅ ni eso̱o wo̱nā, ni eke̱ Mumo̱ le̱ yibāfonõ ehãwo̱ ye̱ wo̱tšuii amli hũ. 5,5. Rom. 8,16. Ef. 1,13. 14.
23Ši mi le̱, mītšé̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ní *ebaye misusuma odase, ake̱ nyeyibāmo̱ hewo̱ ni mináko maba Korinto le̱, *11,31. Rom. 1,9.
24Dšee ake̱ nyehemo̱-ke̱-yeli le̱ *nyṍṅ wo̱yeo̱, ši moṅ nyemīše̱ le̱ he nitšume̱ hefatalo̱i dšiwo̱, edšake̱ hemo̱-ke̱-yeli mli nyedamo̱ ši ye̱. *1 Pet. 5,3.

english_text:
1I have decided not to make my next visit with you so painful. 2If I make you feel bad, who would be left to cheer me up, except the people I had made to feel bad? 3The reason I want to be happy is to make you happy. I wrote as I did because I didn't want to visit you and be made to feel bad, when you should make me feel happy. 4At the time I wrote, I was suffering terribly. My eyes were full of tears, and my heart was broken. But I didn't want to make you feel bad. I only wanted to let you know how much I cared for you.
Forgiveness
5I don't want to be hard on you. But if one of you has made someone feel bad, I am not really the one who has been made to feel bad. Some of you are the ones. 6Most of you have already pointed out the wrong that person did, and this is punishment enough for what was done.
7When people sin, you should forgive and comfort them, so they won't give up in despair. 8You should make them sure of your love for them.
9I also wrote because I wanted to test you and find out if you would follow my instructions. 10I will forgive anyone you forgive. Yes, for your sake and with Christ as my witness, I have forgiven whatever needed to be forgiven. 11I have done this to keep Satan from getting the better of us. We all know what goes on in his mind.
12 When I went to Troas to preach the good news about Christ, I found that the Lord had already prepared the way. 13But I was worried when I didn't find my friend Titus there. So I left the other followers and went on to Macedonia.
14I am grateful that God always makes it possible for Christ to lead us to victory. God also helps us spread the knowledge about Christ everywhere, and this knowledge is like the smell of perfume. 15-16In fact, God thinks of us as a perfume that brings Christ to everyone. For people who are being saved, this perfume has a sweet smell and leads them to a better life. But for people who are lost, it has a bad smell and leads them to a horrible death.
No one really has what it takes to do this work. 17A lot of people try to get rich from preaching God's message. But we are God's sincere messengers, and by the power of Christ we speak our message with God as our witness.
translation_text:
1Ši mikpe̱ mli ye̱ midientše̱ miyiṅ, ake̱ mike̱ ṅko̱mo̱yeli baṅ nyeṅõ doṅṅ. 1 Kor 4,21. 2 Kor. 12,21.
2Edšake̱ ke̱ mi mihã nyeye ṅko̱mo̱ le̱, namo dši moni hãa mimī še̱o̱ mo̱, ake̱ dša mo noṅṅ ní mihã eye ṅko̱mo̱ le̱?
3Ni *miṅmãnye ene̱ noùṅ, koni, ke̱ miba le̱, mikabaye ṅko̱mo̱ ye̱ mei ni kũle̱ sa ake̱ mináa amehe mīše̱ le̱ ahewo̱, edšake̱ mihĩe kã nyefẽ nyeno̱, ake̱ mimīše̱ dši nyefē nyemīše̱. *1 Kor. 5.
4Ši mitšuĩṅ amanehũlũ ke̱ fĩmo̱ babaō mli miṅmãnye ye̱, ke̱-tšṍ yāfónui babaō hũ mli, dšee ní nyew̌ere̱ aho nyehe hewo̱ṅ, ši moṅ ni nyena no suomo̱ babaō ní misumoo̱nye.
5Ši ke̱ moko ehã aye ṅko̱mo̱ le̱, dšeemi ni ehã miye ṅko̱mo̱, ši (koni mina akawa tūtu le̱) ehã nyefē nyeye ṅko̱mo̱ fã-ke̱-fã. 1 Kor. 5,1.
6Nakai mo le̱ ehĩe ní mei pī ekã le̱ fá hãle̱,
7hewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ nyeṅõ-faäle̱, ni nye-še̱dše emī moṅ, koni ṅko̱mo̱yeli tūtu le̱ akabasu etsui.
8Nohewo̱ le̱ mīkpanye fai ní nyehã nyesuomo̱ le̱ mli awa ye̱ ene̱;
9edšake̱ ene̱hewo̱ hũ ní miṅmãnye wolo le̱, koni mike̱-le bo̱ni nyenā kpaä, ake̱ *nyeboo toi ye̱ nofẽno gbe̱fãṅ lo. *7,15.
10Ši moni nyeṅõo̱ noko nyefaäle̱ le̱, mi hũ miṅõ-faäle̱; edšake̱ mi hũ, ké̱ mike̱ noko fa le̱, noni miṅõ-fa le̱, miṅõ-fa ye̱ nyehewo̱ ye̱ *Kristo hĩe; *Luk. 10,16.
11koni *satan akayewo̱ amim, edšake̱ edſẽṅmo̱i le̱ aṅõ-tẽẽwe̱. *Luk. 22,31.
12Ši beni miba Troa ye̱ Kristo sanekpakpa le̱ hewo̱ ni *agble šĩnā ahãmi ye̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ mli le̱, *Bo̱f. 14,27. 1 Kor. 16,9.
13mináá hedšo̱le̱ ye̱ mimumo̱ mli, edšake̱ minaa minyemi Tito; hewo̱ le̱ miše̱ame̱ ni miyiṅ ke̱-ba Makedonia. Bo̱f. 20,1.
14Ši šidā ahã Nyoṅmo̱, moni hãa wo̱-yeo̱ kũnim dā ye̱ Kristo mli, ni ehãa ehe nilē ṅmadšē le̱ tšṍo̱ wo̱no̱ dšeo̱ kpo ye̱ hefẽhe le̱.
15Edšake̱ Kristo ṅmadšē kpakpa dšiwo̱ hã Nyoṅme̱ *ye̱ mei ni ahereo̱ ame̱yiwala le̱ ke̱ mei ní lādšeo̱ le̱ fẽ mli: *1 Kor. 1,18.
16*mene̱mei le̱, wo̱dši gbĕle ṅma ní dšeo̱ ke̱-yaã gbĕle mli hãame̱; ši meikrokomei le̱, wo̱dši wala ṅma ní dšeo̱ ke̱-yaä wala mli hãame̱. Ni †namo sa hã ene̱mei? *Luk. 2,34. †2 Kor. 3,5. 6.
17Edšake̱ wo̱fee tamo̱ mei pī ni futuo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ wiemo̱ le̱, ši moṅ wo̱wieo̱le̱ ṅmīṅmi bo̱ni edše̱ Nyoṅmo̱ mli le̱ ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe, ye̱ Kristo mli. 1,12.

english_text:
God's New Agreement
1Are we once again bragging about ourselves? Do we need letters to you or from you to tell others about us? Some people do need letters telling about them. 2But you are our letter, and you are in our hearts for everyone to read and understand. 3 You are like a letter written by Christ and delivered by us. But you are not written with pen and ink or on tablets made of stone. You are written in our hearts by the Spirit of the living God.
4We are sure about all this. Christ makes us sure in the very presence of God. 5We don't have the right to claim that we have done anything on our own. God gives us what it takes to do all we do. 6 He makes us worthy to be the servants of his new agreement that comes from the Holy Spirit and not from a written Law. After all, the Law brings death, but the Spirit brings life.
7 The Law of Moses brought only the promise of death, even though it was carved on stones and given in a wonderful way. Still the Law made Moses' face shine so brightly the people of Israel could not look at it, even though it was a fading glory. 8So won't the agreement the Spirit brings to us be even more wonderful? 9If something that brings the death sentence is glorious, won't something that makes us acceptable to God be even more glorious? 10In fact, the new agreement is so wonderful that the Law is no longer glorious at all. 11The Law was given with a glory that faded away. But the glory of the new agreement is much greater, because it will never fade away.
12This wonderful hope makes us feel like speaking freely. 13 We are not like Moses. His face was shining, but he covered it to keep the people of Israel from seeing the brightness fade away. 14The people were stubborn, and something still keeps them from seeing the truth when the Law is read. Only Christ can take away the covering that keeps them from seeing.
15When the Law of Moses is read, they have their minds covered over 16 with a covering that is removed only for those who turn to the Lord. 17The Lord and the Spirit are one and the same, and the Lord's Spirit sets us free. 18 So our faces are not covered. They show the bright glory of the Lord, as the Lord's Spirit makes us more and more like our glorious Lord.
translation_text:
1Aso wo̱sā wo̱bõi *wo̱he yidšiemo̱? Alo ehīawo̱, tamo̱ meikomei, ake̱ wo̱hĩeo̱ yidšiemo̱-wodši ke̱-bahãanye alo ne̱ke̱ wodši ne̱ ke̱-dše̱ nyedeṅ lo? *5,12.
2Nyedši wo̱wolo ní aṅmã awo wo̱-tšuii amli ní mei fẽ le ni ame̱kaneo̱; 1 Kor. 9,2.
3ni adšienye faṅṅ atšõ ake̱ nyedši Kristo wolo ní wo̱súmo̱ ye̱ he, ní dšee ble̱gi, ši moṅ Nyoṅmo̱ hĩekãlo̱ le̱ Mumo̱ le̱ ake̱-ṅmã, dšee ye̱ *te̱-tāoi ano̱, ši moṅ tšui ní dši helo-tāoi ano̱. *2 Mose 24,12.
4Ši Kristo hewo̱ wo̱yo̱ ne̱ke̱ hĩe-ke̱-nofõ ne̱ ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ gbe̱fãṅ:
5dšee ake̱ wo̱dientše̱ le̱ wo̱sa, ni wo̱dſẽṅ ake̱ noko dše̱ wo̱dientše̱ wo̱mli, ši wo̱sale̱ le̱ Nyoṅmo̱ mli edše̱; 2,16.
6le̱ noṅṅ ehã wo̱sa ní wo̱tšṍmo̱ *kpãṅmo̱ hẽ le̱ he súolo̱i, †dšee ṅmãle̱-okadi nõ, ši moṅ mumo̱ nõ; edšake̱ ṅmãle̱-okadi le̱ gbeo̱ mo; ši **mumo̱ le̱ hãa mo yi náa wala. *Ier. 31,31. 1 Kor. 11,25. †Rom. 7,5. **Ioh. 6,63.
7Ši ké̱ gbĕle súomo̱ ni aṅõ ṅmãle̱-okadii akadi ye̱ te̱i ano̱ le̱ hĩe ba nyam bo̱ni Israelbii le̱ *nyẽẽ Mose hĩe ame̱kwe̱ ye̱ ehĩe nyam ní se̱ foo̱ le̱ hewo̱ po le̱: *2 Mose 34.30.
8ani mumo̱ súomo̱ le̱ hĩe baṅ nyam āhũ fè no? Gal. 3,2. 5.
9Edšake̱, ke̱ *fo̱bū súomo̱ le̱ hĩe ba nyam le̱, ani †dšale̱ súomo̱ le̱ hĩe baṅ nyam ke̱-tekeṅ no? *5 Mose 27,26. †Rom. 1,17; 3,21.
10Edšake̱ anumnyam le̱ ní fá babaō tšṍ le̱ hewo̱ le̱, noni awo ehĩe nyam tete le̱, hĩe be̱ nyam ye̱ ene̱ gbe̱fãṅ.
11Edšake̱ ké̱ noni se̱ foo̱ le̱ tšṍ anumnyam mli le̱, bĕle̱ noni hĩo̱ ši le̱ moṅ anumnyam le̱ fá āhũ.
12Agbene ake-ní wo̱yo̱ ne̱ke̱ hĩeno̱-kãmo̱ ne̱ hewo̱ le̱ wo̱feo̱ ekã babaō,
13ni wo̱fee tamo̱ Mose ní ke̱ hĩehānõ ha ehĩe, koni Israelbii le̱ akakwe̱ noni se̱ foo̱ le̱ nāgbē le̱. 2 Mose 34,33. 35.
14Ši moṅ awadše ame̱dſẽṅmo̱i le̱. Edšake̱ ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱-gbĩ-ne̱ no̱ le̱ nakai hĩehānõ le̱ noṅṅ ha kpãṅmo̱ momo le̱ kanemo̱ le̱ no̱; adšieko ši ake̱ Kristo mli ese̱ foo̱ ye̱. Rom. 11,25.
15Ši ke̱-baši ṅme̱ne̱-gbĩ-ne̱ no̱ le̱, befẽbe ní akaneo̱ Mose wolo le̱, hĩehānõ ha ame̱tšui no̱;
16ši *ké̱ ame̱kũ ame̱se̱ ke̱-ba Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ ṅõ le̱, aadšie hĩehānõ le̱. *Rom. 11,23. 24.
17Ši Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ dši Mumo̱ le̱; ši heni Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ Mumo̱ le̱ yo̱ le̱, dše̱i heyeli yo̱.
18Ši wo̱fẽ ní wo̱ke̱ hĩe kpetekplē kwe̱o̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ anumnyam le̱ tamo̱ akwe̱o̱ aſiſe̱ mli le̱, wo̱mīltšake wo̱mītšṍmo̱ nakai subãṅ le̱ noṅṅ ke̱-mīdše̱ anumnyam mli ke̱-mīya anumnyam mli, take̱ bo̱ni edše̱o̱ Nuṅtšo̱ ní dši Mumo̱ le̱ ṅõ le̱.

english_text:
Treasure in Clay Jars
1God has been kind enough to trust us with this work. This is why we never give up. 2We don't do shameful things that must be kept secret. And we don't try to fool anyone or twist God's message around. God is our witness that we speak only the truth, so others will be sure we can be trusted. 3If there is anything hidden about our message, it is hidden only to someone who is lost.
4The god who rules this world has blinded the minds of unbelievers. They cannot see the light, which is the good news about our glorious Christ, who shows what God is like. 5We are not preaching about ourselves. Our message is that Jesus Christ is Lord. He also sent us to be your servants. 6 The Scriptures say, “God commanded light to shine in the dark.” Now God is shining in our hearts to let you know that his glory is seen in Jesus Christ.
7We are like clay jars in which this treasure is stored. The real power comes from God and not from us. 8We often suffer, but we are never crushed. Even when we don't know what to do, we never give up. 9In times of trouble, God is with us, and when we are knocked down, we get up again. 10-11We face death every day because of Jesus. Our bodies show what his death was like, so his life can also be seen in us. 12This means that death is working in us, but life is working in you.
13In the Scriptures it says, “I spoke because I had faith.” We have this same kind of faith. So we speak 14because we know that God raised the Lord Jesus to life. And just as God raised Jesus, he will also raise us to life. Then he will bring us into his presence together with you. 15All of this has been done for you, so more and more people will know how kind God is and will praise and honor him.
Faith in the Lord
16We never give up. Our bodies are gradually dying, but we ourselves are being made stronger each day. 17These little troubles are getting us ready for an eternal glory that will make all our troubles seem like nothing. 18Things that are seen don't last forever, but things that are not seen are eternal. This is why we keep our minds on the things that cannot be seen.
translation_text:
1Nohewo̱ le̱, ake̱ noni wo̱hĩe ne̱ke̱ *súomo̱ ne̱, take̱ bo̱ni †anawo̱ mo̱bo̱ le̱, wo̱tšui efãã, *3,6. †1 Kor. 7,25.
2ši wo̱gu hĩegbedšianii ní aṅõ-tē le̱, ni wo̱baa wo̱dšeṅ *ye̱ kũtũmpo̱o mli, ni asaṅ wo̱futuu Nyoṅmo̱ wiemo̱ le̱, ši moṅ wo̱ke̱ ano̱kwale le̱ kpodšiemo̱ le̱ dšieo̱ wo̱he wo̱tšõo̱ gbomei ahenilē fẽ ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe. *2,17. 1 Tes. 2,5.
3Ši ké̱ ha aha wo̱sanekpakpa le̱ no̱ tete le̱, mei ní lādšeo̱ le̱ amli ke̱ke̱ aha no̱ ye̱, 1 Kor. 1,18.
4mei amli ní dše ne̱ṅ nyoṅmo̱ le̱ eſila mei ní hee yee le̱ adſẽṅmo̱i le̱ ye̱, koni Kristo, ní dši *Nyoṅmo̱ subãṅ le̱, anumnyam sanekpakpa le̱ la ní tšoo̱ le̱ akakpé̱ mīhãame̱. *Heb. 1,3.
5Edšake̱ dšee wo̱dientše̱ wohe wo̱šie̱o̱, ši moṅ Kristo Iesu, ake̱ le̱ dši Nuṅtšo̱, ši wo̱ le̱, nyetšũdši dšiwo̱ ye̱ Iesu hewo; 1,24.
6edšake̱ *Nyoṅmo̱ ní kē̱ ake̱ la adše̱ duṅ mli akpé̱ le̱, le̱ noṅṅ †ekpé̱ ye̱ we̱tšuii amli hũ, koni Nyoṅmo̱ anumnyam he nilē le̱ akpé̱ ye̱ Iesu Kristo hĩe. *1 Mose 1,3. †2 Kor. 3,18.
7Ši wo̱hĩe ne̱ke̱ dſetri ne̱ ye̱ *sũnii amli — koni hewale̱ ni fá ke̱-teke no̱ afe Nyoṅmo̱ nõ ni dšee wo̱nõ—: *5,1.
8afĩfĩaäwo̱ ye̱ hefẽhe, ši kẽle̱ wo̱tšui esuu; wo̱feo̱ yeyēye, ši kẽle̱ wo̱nidšiaṅ edšeko wui; 1,8; 7,5.
9awaäwo̱ yi, ši kẽle̱ akwakowo̱; atſiaäwo̱ ši, ši kẽle̱ wo̱plenēko;
10dāne̱ *wo̱hĩe Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu gbĕle le̱ ye̱ wo̱gbomotšo le̱ mli ke̱-nyie, koni Iesu wala le̱ hũ adše kpo ye̱ wo̱gbomotšo le̱ mli. *1 Kor. 15,31.
11Edšake̱ wo̱ ni wo̱hĩe kãmo̱ ne̱, dāne̱ atuwo̱ awo *gbĕle deṅ ye̱ Iesu hewo̱, koni Iesu wala le̱ hũ adše kpo ye̱ wo̱helo ní bagbo le̱ mli. *Rom 8,36.
12Nohewo̱ le̱ agbe̱ne̱ gbĕle tsuo̱ nii ye̱ wo̱mli, ši nye le̱, wala tšuo̱ nii ye̱ nyemli.
13Ši ake̱ noni wo̱yo̱ nakai hemo̱-ke̱-yeli mumo̱ le̱ noṅṅ, take̱ bo̱ni *aṅmã ake̱: “Mihe miye hewo̱ ni miwie le̱,” hewo̱ le̱ wo̱ hũ wo̱heo̱ wo̱yeo̱, nohewo le̱ wo̱wieo̱ hũ; *Lal. 116,19.
14edšake̱ wo̱le ake̱ moni tē Nuṅtšo̱ Iesu ši le̱, eetēwo̱ ke̱ Iesu ši, ni eedšie-wo̱ ke̱ nyefẽ kpo etšõ. 1 Kor. 6,14.
15Edšake̱ nyehewo̱ afeo fẽ, koni dromo̱ ní fá babaō le̱ atšṍ mei pī ašidā no̱ ateke no̱ ahã Nyoṅmo̱ anumnyam. 1,3-6.
16Nohewo̱ ni wo̱tšui efãã le̱, ši moṅ ké̱ *wo̱kpono̱gbe̱-gbomo le̱ fiteo̱ kwrā tete le̱, kẽle̱ †wo̱mligbomo le̱ tšṍo̱ ehē gbĩ-fẽ-gbĩ. *K. 10. †Ef. 3,16.
17Edšake̱ wo̱-mrõmrõ-amanehũlũ, ní dšraa ne̱, mītšu nāno̱ anumnyam babaō ní teke no̱ ní dšra wa āhũ ehãwo̱. Rom. 8,17. 18.
18Wo̱ ní wo̱dšee mei ní kwo̱o̱ nii ni anaä le̱, ši moṅ *nii ni anaa le̱ wo̱kwe̱o̱; edšake̱ nii ní anaä le̱ hĩo̱ ši be fio̱ ke̱ke̱, ši nii ní anaa le̱ hĩo ši ke̱-yašio̱ nāno. *Heb. 11,1.

english_text:
1 Our bodies are like tents that we live in here on earth. But when these tents are destroyed, we know that God will give each of us a place to live. These homes will not be buildings someone has made, but they are in heaven and will last forever. 2While we are here on earth, we sigh because we want to live in that heavenly home. 3We want to put it on like clothes and not be naked.
4These tents we now live in are like a heavy burden, and we groan. But we don't do this just because we want to leave these bodies that will die. It is because we want to change them for bodies that will never die. 5God is the one who makes all this possible. He has given us his Spirit to make us certain he will do it. 6So always be cheerful!
As long as we are in these bodies, we are away from the Lord. 7But we live by faith, not by what we see. 8We should be cheerful, because we would rather leave these bodies and be at home with the Lord. 9But whether we are at home with the Lord or away from him, we still try our best to please him. 10 After all, Christ will judge each of us for the good or the bad that we do while living in these bodies.
Bringing People to God
11We know what it means to respect the Lord, and we encourage everyone to turn to him. God himself knows what we are like, and I hope you also know what kind of people we are. 12We are not trying once more to brag about ourselves. But we want you to be proud of us, when you are with those who are not sincere and brag about what others think of them.
13If we seem out of our minds, it is between God and us. But if we are in our right minds, it is for your good. 14We are ruled by Christ's love for us. We are certain that if one person died for everyone else, then all of us have died. 15And Christ did die for all of us. He died so we would no longer live for ourselves, but for the one who died and was raised to life for us.
16We are careful not to judge people by what they seem to be, though we once judged Christ in this way. 17Anyone who belongs to Christ is a new person. The past is forgotten, and everything is new. 18God has done it all! He sent Christ to make peace between himself and us, and he has given us the work of making peace between himself and others.
19What we mean is that God was in Christ, offering peace and forgiveness to the people of this world. And he has given us the work of sharing his message about peace. 20We were sent to speak for Christ, and God is begging you to listen to our message. We speak for Christ and sincerely ask you to make peace with God. 21Christ never sinned! But God treated him as a sinner, so Christ could make us acceptable to God.
translation_text:
1Edšake̱ wo̱le ake̱, ke̱ akũmo̱ *wo̱šikpoṅ ne̱ no̱ bū šĩa ne̱ dšiṅṅ, wo̱ye̱ tšũ ko ni dše̱ Nyoṅmo̱ ṅõ, šĩa ko ní dšee nidši ake̱-fe, ní hĩo̱ ši ke̱-yaä nāno, ye̱ ṅwei. *Hiob 4,19. 2 Pet. 1,13. 14.
2Edšake̱ wo̱dõmoo̱ ntšo̱i tete ye̱ ene̱ mli, ni wo̱ſeo̱ ake̱ aṅõ wo̱tšũ ní dše̱ ṅwei le̱ awowo̱, Rom. 8,23.
3ni ke̱ ake̱-wowo̱ ne̱ke̱ le̱, no le̱ anaṅwo̱ ake̱ mei ní nyie yayai.
4Edšake̱ wo̱ ní wo̱yo̱ bū le̱ṅ le̱ hū, ake̱-ní wohe dšrawo̱ hewo̱ le̱, wo̱dõmoo̱ ntšo̱i, edšake̱ wo̱sumo̱o̱ ake̱ adšie wo̱henii, ši moṅ wo̱sumoo̱ ake̱ *awowo̱ nii aſie no̱, koni wala le̱ amĩ noni gboo̱ le̱. *1 Kor. 15,53.
5Ši moni sāwo̱ hã ene̱ noṅṅ dši Nyoṅmo̱, mo hũ ní hãwo̱ Mumo̱ le̱ kleṅkleṅnõ le̱. 1,22. Rom. 8,16. 25. Ef. 1,18. 14.
6Nohewo̱ le̱ wo̱ye̱ tšui dā, ni wo̱le ake̱ gbĩĩ abo̱ ni wo̱yo̱ gbomotšo le̱ mli ne̱ wo̱dom *ke̱-dše̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ ṅõ, — *Heb. 11,13.
7edšake̱ hemo̱-ke̱-yeli nā wo̱-nyieo̱ ye̱, ši dšee ninamo̱ nā, — 1 Kor. 13,12.
8ši wo̱ye̱ tšui, ni esa wo̱hĩe moṅ ake̱ wo̱o̱dom ke̱-dše̱ gbomotšo ne̱ mli, ni wo̱yahĩ šĩa ye̱ Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ ṅõ. Fil. 1,23.
9Nohewo̱ le̱ oti ní wo̱ṅõ-mã wo̱hĩe dši ake, šĩa wo̱yo̱ dsio, *dommo̱ wo̱dom dšio, ní wo̱sa ehĩe. *Lal. 39,13.
10Edšake̱ dša wo̱fẽ wo̱pue ſaṅṅ *ye̱ Kristo kodšomo̱sẽi le̱ hĩe, koni mofẽmo aná nii ní efe ye̱ gbomotšo mli le̱, bo̱bo̱ ní efe le̱, ekpakpa dšio, efõṅ dšio. *Bo̱f. 17,31. Rom. 2,16; 14,10.
11Nohewo le̱, ake̱-ní wo̱le Nuṅtšo̱ le̱ he ni yo̱ gbeyei hewo̱ le̱, wo̱wieo̱ wo̱tšõo̱ gbomei, ši wo̱ye̱ faṅṅ ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe; ni mihĩe kã no̱ ake̱ wo̱ye̱ faṅṅ ye̱ nyehenilē mli hũ.
12Edšake̱ dšee *wo̱dientše̱ wo̱he yi wo̱dšieo̱ wo̱hãanye ekoṅ, ši moṅ wo̱ke̱mīhãnye gbe̱ ní nyeṅõ-fã nyefõ wo̱no̱, koni nyená eko nyekē̱ mei ni ſãa ye̱ hĩeaṅ ši dšee tšui mli le̱. *3,1.
13Edšake̱, ké̱ se̱ke̱ wo̱yeo̱ dšiṅṅ, Nyoṅmo̱ wo̱yeo̱ wo̱hãa; ní ké̱ wo̱hĩe kã ši hũ dšiṅṅ, ekã ši ehãnye.
14Edšake̱ Kristo suomo̱ le̱ nyẽo̱ wo̱no̱, ni wo̱kodšoo̱ ne̱ke̱, ake̱, ké̱ mokome gbo mei fẽ yigbĕle le̱, bĕle̱ mei le̱ fẽ egboi.
15Ni egbo *mei fẽ yigbĕle, †koni mei ni hĩe kãmo̱ le̱ ahĩe akakãmo̱ mīhã ame̱dientše̱ ame̱he doṅṅ, ši moṅ ame̱hĩe akãmo̱ ahã moni gbo ni atēle̱ ši ekoṅ ahãame̱ le̱. *1 Tim 2,9. †Rom. 14,7. 8.
16Nohewo̱ le̱, ke̱-dše̱o̱ ṅme̱ne̱ no̱ ke̱-yaä ne̱, wo̱lee mokomoko doṅṅ ye̱ helo mli; ni ké̱ helo mli wo̱le Kristo ye̱ tete le̱, kẽle̱ agbe̱ne̱ le̱ wo̱leele̱ nakai doṅṅ.
17Hewo̱ le̱, *ke̱ moko ye̱ Kristo mli le̱, †bō̱nõ hi dšile̱; blemanii le̱ ého; **na, nibii fẽ étšṍmo ehẽ. *Rom. 8,1. 10. †Gal. 6,15. **Kpods. 21,5.
18Ši nibii ne̱ fã dše̱ Nyoṅmo̱ deṅ, *moni tšṍ Iesu Kristo no̱ ekpãtã le̱dientše̱ eke̱wo̱ teṅ, ni eke̱ kpãtãmo̱-súomo̱ le̱ hãwo̱ le̱; *Rom. 5,10.
19no dši ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ tšṍ Kristo no̱ ekpãtã le̱dientše̱ eke̱ dše le̱ teṅ, ni ebuu ame̱no̱tõmo̱i le̱ ehããame̱, ni etu kpãtãmo̱-wiemo̱ le̱ ewo wo̱deṅ. Rom. 8,24. 25. Kol. 1,19. 20.
20Nohewe̱ le̱ wo̱dši *bo̱foi ye̱ Kristo, nãdšiaṅ, tamo̱ ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ etšṍ wo̱no̱ eke̱ mei mīwie: wo̱damoo̱ Kristo nãdšiaṅ wo̱kpaänye fai ake̱: nyehãa akpãtãa nye ke̱ Nyoṅmo̱ teṅ! *Ies. 13,7.
21Edšake̱ *moni lee eša le̱, wo̱hewo̱ le̱ ehã etšṍ †eša, koni wo̱ le̱ wo̱tšṍmo̱ **Nyoṅmo̱ dšale̱ ye̱ emli. *Heb. 4,15. †Gal. 3,13. **1 Kor. 1,30. Fil. 3,9.

english_text:
1We work together with God, and we beg you to make good use of God's gift of undeserved grace. 2 In the Scriptures God says,
“When the time came,
I listened to you,
and when you needed help,
I came to save you.”
That time has come. This is the day for you to be saved.
3We don't want anyone to find fault with our work, and so we try hard not to cause problems. 4But in everything and in every way we show we truly are God's servants. We have always been patient, though we have had a lot of trouble, suffering, and hard times. 5 We have been beaten, put in jail, and hurt in riots. We have worked hard and have gone without sleep or food. 6But we have kept ourselves pure and have been understanding, patient, and kind. The Holy Spirit has been with us, and our love has been real. 7We have spoken the truth, and God's power has worked in us. In all our struggles we have said and done only what is right.
8Whether we were honored or dishonored or praised or cursed, we always told the truth about ourselves. But some people said we did not. 9We are unknown to others, but well known to you. We seem to be dying, and yet we are still alive. We have been punished, but never killed, 10and we are always happy, even in times of suffering. Although we are poor, we have made many people rich. And though we own nothing, everything is ours.
11Friends in Corinth, we are telling the truth when we say there is room in our hearts for you. 12We are not holding back on our love for you, but you are holding back on your love for us. 13I speak to you as I would speak to my own children. Please make room in your hearts for us.
The Temple of the Living God
14Stay away from people who are not followers of the Lord! Can someone who is good get along with someone who is evil? Are light and darkness the same? 15Is Christ a friend of Satan? Can people who follow the Lord have anything in common with those who don't? 16 Do idols belong in the temple of God? We are the temple of the living God, as God himself says,
“I will live with these people
and walk among them.
I will be their God,
and they will be
my people.”
17 The Lord also says,
“Leave them and stay away!
Don't touch anything
that isn't clean.
Then I will welcome you
18 and be your Father.
You will be my sons
and my daughters,
as surely as I am God,
the All-Powerful.”
translation_text:
1Ši ake̱ noni *hefatalo̱i nitšulo̱i dšiwo̱ hewo̱ le̱, wo̱wieo̱ wo̱tšõo̱nye hũ, ní nyekahé Nyoṅmo̱ dromo̱ le̱ yakatſā; *1,24; 5,20.
2edšake̱ *ekē̱ ake̱: “Be ni sa mli miboö toi ye̱, ni walaheremo̱ gbĩ no̱ hũ miye mibuao ye̱.” Na, †be ní sa dšogbāṅ ne̱; na, walaheremo̱ gbĩ ne̱. *Ies. 49,8. †Luk. 4,19. 21.
3Ni asaṅ wo̱too mokomoko pāmpi ye̱ nokonoko mli, koni akagbe súomo̱ le̱ he guo̱;
4ši moṅ, nofẽno mli le̱ *wo̱ke̱ wo̱he tšõo̱ ake̱ Nyoṅmo̱ súolo̱i, ye̱ tšuišĩṅmē̃ babaō mli, ye̱ amanehũlũi amli, ye̱ fĩmo̱i amli, ye̱ haomo̱i amli, *4,2.
5ye̱ yii amli, ye̱ gbokle̱foi-atšũi amli, ye̱ hōfemo̱i amli, ye̱ deṅme-gbomo̱i amli, ye̱ kpešii amli, ye̱ buadayelii amli, 11,23-27.
6ye̱ *hetšemo̱ mli, ye̱ nilē mli, ye̱ dſẽṅmo̱ ní se̱ tše̱o̱ mli, ye̱ mlihĩle̱ mli, ye̱ Mumo̱ kroṅkroṅ mli, ye̱ suomo̱ ní pasaa mli, *1 Tim. 4,12.
7ye̱ ano̱kwale wiemo̱ mli, ye̱ *Nyoṅmo̱ hewale̱ mli, ke̱-tšṍ dšale̱ tawūnii ni dši ninedšŭrõ nõ ke̱ nineabe̱ku nõ le̱ amli, *1 Kor. 2,4.
8ke̱-tšṍ anumnyam ke̱ heguo̱gbē mli, ke̱-tšṍ hewiemo̱ fõṅ ke̱ hewiemo̱ kpakpa mli; tamo̱ šišiulo̱i, kẽle̱ ano̱kwafoi dšiwo̱;
9tamo̱ mei ní alee ke̱ mei ní ale kre̱dē̱; tamo̱ mei ní *gboio̱, ni na, wo̱hĩe kãmo̱; tamo̱ mei ní †agblaame̱ toi, ni kẽle agbekowo̱; *4,10. 11. †Lal. 118,18.
10tamo̱ ṅko̱mo̱yelilo̱i, ši wo̱mī še̱o̱ dā; tamo̱ ohĩafoi, ši wo̱tšakeo̱ mei pī wo̱feo̱ame̱ niiatše̱mei; tamo̱ mei ní be̱ noko, ni kẽle̱ wo̱ye̱ nii fiā. Fil. 4,12. 13.
11Wo̱nābu egble ehãnye, Korintobii, wo̱tšui mli hũ elē̱.
12Gbe̱ ye̱ wo̱mli hãnye, ši nyedientše̱ nyemli moṅ nyefīo̱ ye̱.
13Ni nye hã nyehãa nyemli alē̱a nakai noṅṅ, ní nyeke̱-towo̱ nãdšiaṅ (mike̱nye mīwie *tamo̱ bii). *1 Kor. 4,14.
14Nyeke̱ mei ni hee yee le̱ akagblaä kõṅtšo kome ní yee egbo̱! Edšake̱ *mẽ bō̱ dšale̱ ke̱ mlatõmo̱ yo̱? alo mẽ yeli la ke̱ duṅ yo̱? *Ef. 5,11.
15Ni mẽ gbēkpãmo̱ Kristo ke̱ Belial yo̱? alo mẽ nidšā moni heo̱ yeo ke̱ moni hee yee yo̱?
16Ni asaṅ mẽ ekomefemo̱ Nyoṅmo̱ so̱lemo̱we ke̱ amãgãi yo̱? Edšake̱ *Nyoṅmo̱ hĩekãlo̱ le̱ so̱lemo̱tšũ dšinye, take̱ bo̱ni Nyoṅmo̱ †kē̱ ake̱: “Mahĩ ame̱mli, ni manyie ye̱ ame̱teṅ, ni matšṍ ame̱-Nyoṅmo̱, ni ame̱ hũ ame̱atšṍ mimaṅ.” *1 Kor. 3,15. †3 Mose 26,12.
17*Nohewo̱ le̱ Iehowa kē̱, nyedšea ame̱teṅ, ni nyetšea nyehe, ni nyekataä mũdši noko he, ni maherenye atū, *Ies. 52,11. Kpods 18,4.
18ni matšṍ nyetše̱, ni nye hũ nyeatšṍmo̱ mibihĩĩ ke̱ mibiyei, bo̱ni Iehowa, Ofe le̱, kē̱ ne̱. Ier. 21,9; 32,38.

english_text:
1My friends, God has made us these promises. So we should stay away from everything that keeps our bodies and spirits from being clean. We should honor God and try to be completely like him.
The Church Makes Paul Happy
2Make a place for us in your hearts! We haven't mistreated or hurt anyone. We haven't cheated anyone. 3I am not saying this to be hard on you. But, as I have said before, you will always be in our thoughts, whether we live or die. 4I trust you completely. I am always proud of you, and I am greatly encouraged. In all my trouble I am still very happy.
5 After we came to Macedonia, we didn't have any chance to rest. We were faced with all kinds of problems. We were troubled by enemies and troubled by fears. 6But God cheers up people in need, and this is what he did when he sent Titus to us. 7Of course, we were glad to see Titus, but what really made us glad is the way you cheered him up. He told how sorry you were and how concerned you were about me. And this made me even happier.
8I don't feel bad anymore, even though my letter hurt your feelings. I did feel bad at first, but I don't now. I know that the letter hurt you for a while. 9Now I am happy, but not because I hurt your feelings. It is because God used your hurt feelings to make you turn back to him, and none of you were harmed by us. 10When God makes you feel sorry enough to turn to him and be saved, you don't have anything to feel bad about. But when this world makes you feel sorry, it can cause your death.
11Just look what God has done by making you feel sorry! You sincerely want to prove you are innocent. You are angry. You are shocked. You are eager to see that justice is done. You have proved that you were completely right in this matter. 12When I wrote you, it wasn't to accuse the one who was wrong or to take up for the one who was hurt. I wrote, so God would show you how much you do care for us. 13And we were greatly encouraged.
Although we were encouraged, we felt even better when we saw how happy Titus was, because you had shown he had nothing to worry about. 14We had told him how much we thought of you, and you did not disappoint us. Just as we have always told you the truth, so everything we told him about you has also proved to be true. 15Titus loves all of you very much, especially when he remembers how you obeyed him and how you trembled with fear when you welcomed him. 16It makes me really glad to know I can depend on you.
translation_text:
1Agbene̱, nye mei ní asumoo̱nye, ake̱ noni wó̱ná ne̱ke̱ šiwōi ne̱ hewo̱ le̱, nyehãa wo̱tšūa wo̱he ke̱-dše̱a helo ke̱ mumo̱ fẽ he mũdši mli, ni wo̱gbe hetšemo̱ nā ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ gbeyeišemo̱ mli.
2Nyehãawo̱ gbe̱ ye̱ nyemli! wo̱feko mokomoko efõṅ ko; wo̱fiteko moko, wo̱yeko moko amim. 12,17. Bo̱f. 20,33.
3Mikē̱ē̱ ene̱ ni mike̱-bunye fo̱; edšake̱ mikē̱ *momo ake̱ nyeye wo̱tšuii amli, ní nyeke̱wo̱ agboi ni nyeke̱wo̱ yi aná wala. *6,11-13.
4Mifeo ekā̃ babaō ye̱ nyeno̱, ni asaṅ miſãa mifõo̱ nyeno̱ babaō; miyi obõ ke̱ mīše̱dšemo̱, miyi ke̱-teke no̱ ke̱ mīše̱ ní miyo̱ ye̱ wo̱manehũlũ le̱ fẽ mli le̱.
5Edšake̱ši beni wo̱ba Makedonia le̱ hũ, wo̱náá wo̱hewodšiaṅ dekã kwrā; ši moṅ hefẽhe le̱ amane so̱ṅṅ wo̱naä: wo̱kpono̱gbe̱ le̱ nõmo̱i, wo̱mligbe̱ le̱ gbeyeišemoi. Bo̱f. 20,1. 2.
6Ši Nyoṅmo̱, moni *še̱dšeo̱ mei ní baä ame̱he ši le̱ amī le̱, eke̱ †Tito bā le̱ še̱dše womi; *1,3. 4. †2,18.
7ši dšee ebā le̱ ke̱ke̱, ši moṅ emīše̱dšemo̱ ní aṅõ-še̱dše emī ye̱ nyehewo̱ le̱ hũ, edšake̱ egbawo̱ nyeſẽ le̱ ke̱ nyeṅko̱mo̱yeli le̱ ke̱ mihe mo̱deṅ ní nyebo̱ö̱ le̱, bo̱ni fe ní miná mīše̱ babaō fè tšutšu le̱ ne̱.
8Tše̱ mike̱ miwolo le̱ ehã edo̱nye moṅ, ši kẽle̱ miſaa mihe. Tše̱ edo̱mi kẽ, edšake̱ mina ake̱ nakai wolo le̱ edo̱nye moṅ, ši be kukuō ke̱ke̱ edo̱nye, 2,4.
9kēle̱ agbe̱ne̱ mimī eše̱, dšee do̱ ní edo̱nye hewo̱ ni, ši moṅ ake̱-ní edo̱nye ni ehã nyeſa nyehe le̱ hewo̱ ni; edšake̱ edo̱nye bo̱ni sa Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe, koni ekadše̱ wo̱ ní noko lādšenye.
10Edšake̱ do̱le̱ ní sa Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe le̱ tše̱o̱ heſamo̱ ní ke̱ mo yaä walaheremo̱ mli noni moko ſaa ehe ye̱ hewo̱ le̱; ši *dše ne̱ṅ do̱le̱ le̱ tše̱o̱ gbĕle. *Mat. 27,3-5.
11Edšake̱ na, ne̱ke̱ do̱le̱ ní edo̱nye bo̱ni sa Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe ne̱ noṅṅ le̱, nyekwe̱a nõ mo̱deṅbō̱, nõ henãdšiemo̱, nõ tšuilawō, nõ gbeyeišemo̱, nõ ſẽ, nõ hĩedō̱, nõ oweletō̱ tete ní etše̱ ewo nyemli! nofẽno mli nyeke̱ nyehe tšõwo̱ ye̱, ake̱ nyehe tše ye̱ ne̱ke̱ sane ne̱ mli.
12Nohewo̱ le̱ kē̱ miṅmãnye tete le̱, dšee moni tõ le̱, asaṅ hũ dšee moni atõ eno̱ le̱ hewo̱ṅ, ši moṅ beni afe ní wo̱he mo̱deṅ ní nyebo̱ö̱ le̱ apue faṅṅ ahãnye, ye̱ Nyoṅmo̱ hĩe.
13Nohewo̱ le̱ wo̱mī eše̱. Ši wo̱mīše̱-dšemo̱ le̱ teke no̱ babaō ke̱ mīše̱ ní wo̱ná ye̱ Tito mīše̱ le̱ hewo̱ le̱, edšake̱ nyefẽ nyehã emumo̱ le̱ tšui nyõ emli,
14edšake̱, ké̱ miſãnye mitšõle̱ ye̱ noko mli le̱, nyewoomi hĩegbĕle; ši tamo̱ bo̱ni wo̱wie nibii fē ano̱kwale mli wo̱tšõnye le̱, nakai noṅṅ kẽ wo̱ſā̃ hũ ní wo̱ſã wo̱tšõ Tito le̱ efe ano̱kwale,
15ni eye nyehe tšui babaō fè tšutšu le̱, edšake̱ ekaio̱ nyefẽ *nyetoibō le̱, bo̱ni nyeke̱ gbeyeišemo̱ ke̱ hekpokpomo̱ herele̱ hĩemẽ le̱. *2,9.
16Miná mīše̱ ake̱ miye̱ nyehe tšui ye̱ nofẽno mli.

english_text:
Generous Giving
1 My friends, we want you to know that the churches in Macedonia have shown others God's gift of undeserved grace. 2Although they were going through hard times and were very poor, they were glad to give generously. 3They gave as much as they could afford and even more, simply because they wanted to. 4They even asked and begged us to let them have the joy of giving their money for God's people. 5And they did more than we had hoped. They gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us, just as God wanted them to do.
6Titus was the one who got you started doing this good thing, so we begged him to help you finish what you had begun. 7You do everything better than anyone else. You have stronger faith. You speak better and know more. You are eager to give, and you love us better. Now you must give more generously than anyone else.
8I am not ordering you to do this. I am simply testing how real your love is by comparing it with the concern that others have shown. 9You know our Lord Jesus Christ treated us with undeserved grace by giving up all his riches, so you could become rich.
10A year ago you were the first ones to give, and you gave because you wanted to. So listen to my advice. 11I think you should finish what you started. If you give according to what you have, you will prove you are as eager to give as you were to think about giving. 12It doesn't matter how much you have. What matters is how much you are willing to give from what you have.
13I am not trying to make life easier for others by making life harder for you. But it is only fair 14for you to share with them when you have so much, and they have so little. Later, when they have more than enough, and you are in need, they can share with you. Then everyone will have a fair share, 15 just as the Scriptures say,
“Those who gathered
too much
had nothing left.
Those who gathered
only a little
had all they needed.”
Titus and His Friends
16I am grateful that God made Titus care as much about you as we do. 17When we begged Titus to visit you, he said he would.
