Jɛi Yehowa wo Israelbii lɛ kitã kɛ akpɔ yɛ, ni jɛi hu ekã amɛ yɛ, 26 ni ekɛɛ, “Kɛji nyɛaaye Yehowa, ni ji nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, gbee nɔ kadikadi, ni nyɛaafee nɔ ni ja gbɛ yɛ ehiɛ, ni nyɛaaye ekpɔi kɛ kitãi fɛɛ anɔ lɛ, no lɛ helai ni mihã ye Ijiptbii lɛ eko eko yeŋ nyɛ, ejaakɛ mi ji Yehowa, nyɛtsalɔ lɛ.”
27Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Israelbii lɛ ba Elim, he ni nubui nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ kɛ amitsrɔbi tsei nyɔŋmai kpawo yɔɔ lɛ, ni amɛbato shi yɛ jɛi yɛ nu lɛ he.

english_text:
The Lord Sends Food from Heaven
1On the fifteenth day of the second month after the Israelites had escaped from Egypt, they left Elim and started through the western edge of the Sinai Desert in the direction of Mount Sinai. 2There in the desert they started complaining to Moses and Aaron, 3“We wish the Lord had killed us in Egypt. When we lived there, we could at least sit down and eat all the bread and meat we wanted. But you have brought us out here into this desert, where we are going to starve.”
4 The Lord said to Moses, “I will send bread down from heaven like rain. Tell the people to go out each day and gather only enough for that day. That's how I will see if they obey me. 5But on the sixth day of each week they must gather and cook twice as much.”
6Moses and Aaron told the people, “This evening you will know that the Lord was the one who rescued you from Egypt. 7And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
8Then Moses continued, “You will know it is the Lord when he gives you meat each evening and more than enough bread each morning. He is really the one you are complaining about, not us—we are nobodies—but the Lord has heard your complaints.”
9Moses turned to Aaron and said, “Bring the people together, because the Lord has heard their complaints.”
10Aaron was speaking to them, when everyone looked out toward the desert and saw the bright glory of the Lord in a cloud. 11The Lord said to Moses, 12“I have heard my people complain. Now tell them that each evening they will have meat and each morning they will have more than enough bread. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.”
13That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground. 14After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost. 15 The people had never seen anything like this, and they started asking each other, “What is it?”
Moses answered, “This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat. 16And he orders you to gather about two liters for each person in your family—that should be more than enough.”
17They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less. 18 Everyone had exactly what they needed, just the right amount.
19Moses told them not to keep any overnight. 20Some of them disobeyed, but the next morning what they kept was stinking and full of worms, and Moses was angry.
21Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted. 22However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses, 23 he told them that the Lord had said, “Tomorrow is the Sabbath, a sacred day of rest in honor of me. So gather all you want to bake or boil, and make sure you save enough for tomorrow.”
24The people obeyed, and the next morning the food smelled fine and had no worms. 25“You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today. 26You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
27A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none. 28Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings? 29Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.” 30And so they rested on the Sabbath.
31 The Israelites called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and delicious as wafers made with honey. 32Moses told the people that the Lord had said, “Store up two liters of this manna, because I want future generations to see the food I gave you during the time you were in the desert after I rescued you from Egypt.”
33 Then Moses told Aaron, “Put some manna in a jar and store it in the place of worship for future generations to see.”
34Aaron followed the Lord's instructions and put the manna in front of the sacred chest for safekeeping. 35-36 The Israelites ate manna for 40 years, before they came to the border of Canaan that was a settled land.
translation_text:
Mana kɛ Trakɔkɔi lɛ
1Israelbii asafo lɛ fɛɛ fã kɛjɛ Elim kɛtee Sin ŋa ni kã Elim kɛ Sinai teŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛyashɛ jɛi Ijipt shimɔ lɛ sɛɛ nyɔji enyɔ lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ enumɔ lɛ nɔ. 2 Israelbii asafo muu lɛ fɛɛ wie huhuuhu amɛshi Mose kɛ Aaron yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ. 3 Amɛkɛɛ, “Yehowa hã wɔgboi yɛ Ijipt be ni wɔtara loo kɛ kukwɛii ahe ni wɔyeɔ nii wɔtɔrɔɔ lɛ moŋ kulɛ, ehi fe nɔ ni nyɛjie wɔ kɛba ŋa nɛɛ nɔ, ni nyɛkɛ hɔmɔ abagbe asafo muu nɛɛ fɛɛ nɛɛ.”
4 Ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Naa, mibahã aboloo ajɛ ŋwɛi anɛ ashwie shi ahã nyɛ. Daa gbi lɛ maŋbii lɛ aje kpo ayabua naa bɔ pɛ ni aaashɛ amɛyeli gbi kome. Mikɛ enɛ baaka amɛ makwɛ akɛ amɛaaye mimla lɛ nɔ aloo amɛyeŋ nɔ. 5Shi gbi ni ji ekpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, hã ni amɛsaa nɔ ni amɛbuaa naa daa gbi lɛ falɛ toi enyɔ amɛto.”
6Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛ Aaron kɛɛ Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ akɛ, “Ŋmɛnɛ gbɛkɛ nɛɛ lɛ nyɛaana nyɛle akɛ Yehowa ji mɔ ni jie nyɛ kɛje Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. 7Leebi lɛ nyɛaana Yehowa anunyam lɛ, ejaakɛ enu huhuuhu wiemɔi ni nyɛwieɔ nyɛshiɔ lɛ lɛ, ejaakɛ wɔ lɛ namɛi ji wɔ ni nyɛwieɔ huhuuhu nyɛshiɔ wɔ?” 8Mose tee nɔ ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Kɛji gbɛkɛ lɛ Yehowa hã nyɛ loo nyɛye, ni leebi lɛ ehã nyɛ aboloo nyɛye nyɛtɔrɔ, ejaakɛ enu huhuuhu wiemɔi ni nyɛwieɔ nyɛshiɔ lɛ lɛ, wɔ lɛ nɛgbɛ wɔdamɔ? Jeee wɔ nyɛwieɔ huhuuhu nyɛshiɔ lɛ, shi Yehowa mɔŋ ni.”
9Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛɛ Aaron akɛ, “Kɛɛmɔ Israelbii asafo muu lɛ fɛɛ akɛ, ‘Nyɛtsia nyɛbaa Yehowa hiɛ; enu nyɛ huhuuhu wiemɔi lɛ.’ ” 10 Be ni Aaron kɛ Israelbii asafo muu lɛ fɛɛ wieɔ lɛ, amɛkwɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ gbɛ, ni naa, Yehowa anunyam lɛ epue yɛ atatu lɛ mli. 11Ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, 12“Minu Israelbii lɛ ahuhuuhu wiemɔi lɛ. Kɛɛmɔ amɛ akɛ, ‘Gbɛkɛnaashi lɛ nyɛaaye loo, ni leebi lɛ nyɛaaye aboloo nyɛtɔrɔ, ni nyɛaana nyɛle akɛ mi ji Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.’ ”
13 Gbɛkɛnaashi mli lɛ trakɔkɔi baha Israelbii lɛ ashihilɛhe lɛ. Leebi mli lɛ bɔ nyɔ kɛbɔle Israelbii lɛ ahe fɛɛ kɛkpe kpula. 14Be ni bɔ lɛ kpala lɛ, ana nibii tɛtɛrɛbii kokrobii bibiibii komɛi jwere ŋa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ tamɔ bɔ ni efĩ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. 15 Be ni Israelbii lɛ na nibii nɛɛ, amɛbibii amɛhe akɛ, “Kolɛ mɛni nɛ?” Ejaakɛ amɛleee nɔ ni ji. Mose kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Aboloo ni Yehowa hã nyɛ koni nyɛye lɛ nɛ. 16Ŋmaa nɛɛ he kitã ni Yehowa ewo nɛ: ‘Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ abua bɔ ni eeenyɛ eye naa, shi moŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ naa nii afee tsenesa loo gomer kome falɛ yɛ nyɛyibɔ naa. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ akɔlɔ ahã mɛi abɔ ni ekɛyɔɔ ebuu mli lɛ.’ ”
17Israelbii lɛ fee nakai. Mɛi komɛi kɔlɔ pii, ni mɛi komɛi kɔlɔ fioo. 18 Shi be ni akɛ tsenesa yaasusu lɛ, mɔ ni kɔlɔ pii lɛ enaaa eko yɛ sɛɛ, ni mɔ ni kɔlɔ fioo hu eshwɛɛɛ lɛ eko dani ashɛ. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ na bɔ ni eeenyɛ eye. 19Kɛkɛ ni Mose wo maŋbii lɛ shi ekɛɛ, “Mɔ ko akashwɛ eko ni je miitsɛre nɔ.” 20Shi kɛ̃lɛ mɛi komɛi eyabooo Mose toi ni amɛshwɛ eko. Be ni je tsɛre lɛ ewo gɔgɔmi, ni esha. Enɛ hã Mose mli wo amɛ la. 21No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ daa leebi lɛ Israelbii lɛ yakɔlɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ lɛ, bɔ ni eeenyɛ eye kɛkɛ. Kɛji hulu naa wa lɛ esereɔ.
22Gbi ni ji ekpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛkɔlɔ daa gbi niyenii lɛ falɛ toi enyɔ, mɔ kome nɔ tsenesai enyɔ, ni maŋbii lɛ ateŋ onukpai lɛ babɔ Mose amaniɛ. 23Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛɛ akɛ, “Nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni Yehowa fã: ‘Wɔ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbi ni, Yehowa hejɔɔmɔ gbi krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ ni. Nyɛshãa nɔ ni nyɛyɔɔ shãa, ni nyɛhoa nɔ ni nyɛyɔɔ hoomɔ. Nɔ ni baashwɛ lɛ nyɛkɛtoa ni je atsɛrea nɔ.’ ” 24 Amɛkɛ nii ni shwɛ lɛ to ni je tsɛre nɔ tamɔ bɔ ni Mose kɛɛ amɛ lɛ; niyenii lɛ eshaaa lɛ, ewooo gɔgɔmi hu.
25Ni Mose kɛɛ maŋbii lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛyea enɛ ŋmɛnɛ ejaakɛ Yehowa hejɔɔmɔ gbi ji ŋmɛnɛ, ni no hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɛnɛ nyɛnaŋ eko yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ nyɛkɔlɔ. 26Nyɛbuaa ŋmaa lɛ naa gbii ekpaa ejaakɛ gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbi ni, ni no nɔ lɛ eko baŋ.”
27Gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ, mɛi komɛi je maŋbii lɛ ateŋ tee ŋmaa kɔlɔmɔ, shi amɛyanaaa eko amɛkɔlɔ. 28Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Kɛyaashi mɛɛ beyinɔ nɔŋŋ nyɛaakwa mikitãi kɛ mimlai lɛ? 29Nyɛnaaa akɛ ni Yehowa hã nyɛ hejɔɔmɔgbi lɛ, no hewɔ ni ehãa nyɛ gbii enyɔ niyenii yɛ gbi ni ji ekpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ? Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ahi eshĩa, mɔ ko akaje egbɛhe yɛ gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ.” 30No hewɔ lɛ, Israelbii lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ.
31Israelbii lɛ wo niyenii nɛɛ gbɛi akɛ mana. Edalɛ tamɔ mlɛ bibii, ni eyɛɔ futafuta, ni eŋɔɔmɔ tamɔ akpãanɔɔ kɛ wo. 32Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛɛ maŋ lɛ akɛ, “Kitã ni Yehowa ewo nɛ, ‘Nyɛkɛ niyenii nɛɛ tsenesa kome falɛ atoa nyɛhãa nyɛshwiei koni amɛbana ŋmaa ni mikɛlɛ nyɛ yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ be mli ni mijie nyɛ kɛje Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.’ ” 33 Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛɛ Aaron akɛ, “Wo kpulu ni osusu mana tsenesa kome falɛ owo mli, ni okɛyama Yehowa hiɛ koni akɛto ahã nyɛshwiei yɛ yinɔi fɛɛ mli.” 34Aaron kɛ mana lɛ yama Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ hiɛ tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa fã Mose lɛ koni akɛto. 35Ni Israelbii lɛ ye mana afii nyɔŋmai ejwɛ kɛyashi amɛyanina shikpɔŋ ni amɛaanyɛ nɔ amɛhi. Amɛye mana lɛ kɛyashi beyinɔ ni amɛyashɛ Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ husu naa. 36(“Gomer” loo tsenesa kome feɔ “efa” loo yiteremɔ mlijaa nyɔŋma mli ekome.)

english_text:
The Lord Gives Water from a Rock
1 The Israelites left the desert and moved from one place to another each time the Lord ordered them to. Once they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for them to drink.
2The people started complaining to Moses, “Give us some water!”
Moses replied, “Why are you complaining to me and trying to put the Lord to the test?”
3But the people were thirsty and kept on complaining, “Moses, did you bring us out of Egypt just to let us and our families and our animals die of thirst?”
4Then Moses prayed to the Lord, “What am I going to do with these people? They are about to stone me to death!”
5The Lord answered, “Take some of the leaders with you and go ahead of the rest of the people. Also take along the walking stick with which you struck the Nile River. 6When you get to the rock at Mount Sinai, I will be there with you. Strike the rock with the stick, and water will pour out for the people to drink.” Moses did this while the leaders watched.
7The people had complained and tested the Lord by asking, “Is the Lord really with us?” So Moses named that place Massah, which means “testing” and Meribah, which means “complaining.”
Israel Defeats the Amalekites
8When the Israelites were at Rephidim, they were attacked by the Amalekites. 9So Moses told Joshua, “Have some men ready to attack the Amalekites tomorrow. I will stand on a hilltop, holding this walking stick that has the power of God.”
10Joshua led the attack as Moses had commanded, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur stood on the hilltop. 11The Israelites out-fought the Amalekites as long as Moses held up his arms, but they started losing whenever he lowered them. 12After a while, his arms were so tired that Aaron and Hur got a rock for him to sit on. Then they stood beside him and supported his arms in the same position until sunset. 13That's how Joshua defeated the Amalekites.
14 Afterwards, the Lord said to Moses, “Write an account of this victory and read it to Joshua. I want the Amalekites to be forgotten forever.”
15Moses built an altar and named it “The Lord Gives Me Victory.” 16Then Moses explained, “This is because I depended on the Lord. But in future generations, the Lord will fight the Amalekites again and again.”
translation_text:
Nu jɛ tɛsaa mli
(Numeri 20.1-13)
1Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ fã kɛjɛ Sin ŋa lɛ nɔ. Amɛtotoo shi yɛ gbɛ teŋ yɛ Yehowa famɔ naa kɛyashi amɛyashɛ Refidim; shi nu bɛ jɛi ni maŋ lɛ baanu. 2 No hewɔ lɛ, amɛkɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Hã wɔ nu wɔnu!” Mose here amɛ nɔ, ni ebi amɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ hewɔ nyɛkɛ mi beɔ? Mɛɛ hewɔ nyɛkaa Yehowa?”
3Shi kumai ye maŋ lɛ yɛ jɛi, ni amɛwie huhuuhu amɛshi Mose amɛkɛɛ, “Mɛɛ hewɔ obajie wɔ yɛ Ijipt? Koni okɛ kumai abagbe wɔ kɛ wɔbii kɛ wɔkooloi?”
4 No hewɔ lɛ, Mose bo etsɛ Yehowa ekɛɛ, “Te mafee maŋ nɛɛ mahã tɛŋŋ? Tɛ amɛheɔ amɛtswia mi nɛɛ!”
5Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Halamɔ Israel onukpai lɛ ateiaŋ mɛi komɛi ofata ohe, ni okɔ otso lɛ ni okɛtswa Nilo Faa lɛ mli lɛ ohiɛ odɛ̃, ni okɛ amɛ atsɔ̃ maŋbii lɛ ahiɛ kɛya. 6 Naa, mibadamɔ tɛsaa lɛ nɔ, ni nu baajɛ mli aba koni maŋ lɛ anu.” Ni Mose fee nakai yɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ ahiɛ.
7 Ni Mose wo jɛi gbɛi akɛ Masa kɛ Meriba yɛ shwamɔ ni Israelbii lɛ shwa Yehowa lɛ kɛ nɔ ni amɛwie amɛkɛka lɛ akɛ, “Ni Yehowa yɛ wɔteŋ kɛ̃ nɛ?” lɛ hewɔ.
Israelbii kɛ Amalekbii wu ta
8Amalekbii lɛ fã ta kɛbanina Israelbii lɛ yɛ Refidim, ni amɛkɛ amɛ wu. 9Ni Mose fã Yoshua ekɛɛ, “Halamɔ hii ni amɛya amɛkɛ Amalekbii lɛ ayawu ahã maŋ lɛ. Mi lɛ mibadamɔ gɔŋkpɔ lɛ yiteŋ wɔ, ni mahiɛ Nyɔŋmɔ tso lɛ yɛ midɛ̃.” 10Yoshua fee bɔ ni Mose fã lɛ lɛ, ni amɛtee amɛkɛ Amalekbii lɛ yawu, ni Mose kɛ Aaron kɛ Hur kwɔ gɔŋkpɔ lɛ kɛtee eyiteŋ. 11Kɛji Mose wo enine nɔ kɛtee ŋwɛi pɛ, kɛkɛ lɛ Israelbii lɛ anine miitsɔ̃ Amalekbii lɛ anɔ; shi kɛji Mose kɛ enine ba shi pɛ Amalekbii lɛ anine miitsɔ̃ Israelbii lɛ anɔ. 12Shi Mose niji bɔ̃i lɛ shɔ̃ɔ, ni no hewɔ lɛ, awo tɛ akɛto Mose shishi ni eho eta nɔ, ni Aaron kɛ Hur hiɛ eniji lɛ amli, mɔ kome yɛ biɛ, ni mɔ kome hu yɛ biɛ, ni eniji lɛ ma shi shiŋŋ kɛyashi hulushinyɔɔ mli. 13Ni Yoshua kpãtã Amalek kɛ emaŋ lɛ hiɛ.
14 Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Ŋmaa kunimyeli nɛɛ he sane lɛ owo wolo mli ofɔ̃ shi koni etsɔ̃ kaimɔ nɔ; ni okpã owo Yoshua toiŋ akɛ mibagbe Amalek kwrakwra yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ.” 15Ni Mose ma afɔleshãa latɛ yɛ jɛi, ni ewo lɛ gbɛi akɛ “Yehowa ji miflaŋaa”, 16ni ekɛɛ, “Nyɛwoa Yehowa aflaŋaa lɛ nɔ. Yehowa kɛ Amalek baawu kɛjɛ yinɔ kɛyaashi yinɔ.”

english_text:
Jethro Visits Moses
1Jethro was the priest of Midian and the father-in-law of Moses. He heard what the Lord God had done for Moses and his people, after rescuing them from Egypt.
2-4 In the meantime, Moses had sent his wife Zipporah and her two sons to stay with Jethro, and he had welcomed them. Moses was still a foreigner in Midian when his first son was born, and so Moses said, “I'll name him Gershom.”
When his second son was born, Moses said, “I'll name him Eliezer, because the God my father worshiped has saved me from the king of Egypt.”
5-6While Israel was camped in the desert near Mount Sinai, Jethro sent Moses this message: “I am coming to visit you, and I am bringing your wife and two sons.”
7When they arrived, Moses went out and bowed down in front of Jethro, then kissed him. After they had greeted each other, they went into the tent, 8where Moses told him everything the Lord had done to protect Israel against the Egyptians and their king. He also told him how the Lord had helped them in all of their troubles.
9Jethro was so pleased to hear this good news about what the Lord had done, 10that he shouted, “Praise the Lord! He rescued you and the Israelites from the Egyptians and their king. 11 Now I know that the Lord is the greatest God, because he has rescued Israel from their arrogant enemies.” 12Jethro offered sacrifices to God. Then Aaron and Israel's leaders came to eat with Jethro there at the place of worship.
Judges Are Appointed
(Deuteronomy 1.9-18)
13The next morning Moses sat down at the place where he decided legal cases for the people, and everyone crowded around him until evening. 14Jethro saw how much Moses had to do for the people, and he asked, “Why are you the only judge? Why do you let these people crowd around you from morning till evening?”
15Moses answered, “Because they come here to find out what God wants them to do. 16They bring their complaints to me, and I make decisions on the basis of God's laws.”
17Jethro replied:
That isn't the best way to do it. 18You and the people who come to you will soon be worn out. The job is too much for one person; you can't do it alone. 19God will help you if you follow my advice. You should be the one to speak to God for the people, 20and you should teach them God's laws and show them what they must do to live right.
21You will need to appoint some competent leaders who respect God and are trustworthy and honest. Then put them over groups of 10, 50, 100, and 1,000. 22These judges can handle the ordinary cases and bring the more difficult ones to you. Having them to share the load will make your work easier. 23This is the way God wants it done. You won't be under nearly as much stress, and everyone else will return home feeling satisfied.
24Moses followed Jethro's advice. 25He chose some competent leaders from every tribe in Israel and put them over groups of 10, 50, 100, and 1,000. 26They served as judges, deciding the easy cases themselves, but bringing the more difficult ones to Moses.
27After Moses and his father-in-law Jethro had said goodbye to each other, Jethro returned home.
translation_text:
Yetro yasara Mose
1 Yetro, Midian osɔfo lɛ ni ji Mose shaanuu lɛ nu nibii fɛɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ efee ehã Mose kɛ emaŋ Israel lɛ he, no ji bɔ ni Yehowa jie Israel kɛjɛ Ijipt lɛ. 2Kɛkɛ ni Yetro, Mose shaanuu lɛ, yiŋ etee Mose ŋɔɔ. Eŋɔ Zipora, Mose ŋa lɛ ni Mose hã eku esɛɛ etee Midian lɛ, 3 kɛ Mose bihii enyɔ lɛ efata ehe kɛtee. Bihii nɛɛ ateŋ mɔ kome gbɛi ji Gershom, ejaakɛ Mose kɛɛ, “Miyato gbɔ yɛ maŋsɛɛ”, 4ni mɔ kome lɛ hu gbɛi ji Eliezer ejaakɛ Mose kɛɛ, “Mitsɛ Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ ji mɔ ni wa mi, ni ehe mi kɛje Farao dɛŋ gbele mli.” 5Yetro, Mose shaanuu lɛ, kɛ Mose ŋa lɛ kɛ ebihii enyɔ lɛ ba Mose ŋɔɔ yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ he ni Israelbii lɛ eyato shi yɛ, yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ Gɔŋ lɛ he lɛ. 6Ni Yetro hã ayakɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Mi oshaanuu, mi kɛ oŋa kɛ obihii enyɔ lɛ miiba oŋɔɔ.” 7No hewɔ lɛ, Mose je kpo ekɛ eshaanuu lɛ yakpe. Mose koto lɛ ni eshwɔ enaa; amɛflaflaa amɛhe, ni amɛba Mose buu lɛ mli. 8Ni Mose gba eshaanuu lɛ nibii fɛɛ ni Yehowa fee Farao kɛ Ijiptbii yɛ Israelbii lɛ ahewɔ lɛ. Egba lɛ haomɔi hu ni ba Israelbii lɛ anɔ yɛ amɛgbɛfãa lɛ mli, kɛ bɔ ni fee ni Yehowa jie amɛ yɛ mli. 9Yetro mii shɛ ehe yɛ ejuji fɛɛ ni Yehowa efee yɛ Israelbii lɛ ahewɔ, akɛ ejie amɛ yɛ Ijipt nyɔŋyeli shishi. 10Ni Yetro kɛɛ, “Ajie Yehowa yi, lɛ mɔ ni ejie nyɛ yɛ Farao kɛ Ijiptbii lɛ adɛŋ, ni ejie emaŋ lɛ yɛ Ijiptbii anɔyeli shishi lɛ. 11Kpaako mina mile akɛ Yehowa fe nyɔŋmɔi fɛɛ ejaakɛ eto Ijiptbii lɛ kpa, akɛni amɛwo amɛhe amɛhã Israelbii lɛ, ni Yehowa ba amɛ shi.” 12Ni Yetro, Mose shaanuu lɛ, yashã shãa afɔle kɛ afɔlei krokomɛi ehã Yehowa, ni Aaron kɛ Israel onukpai lɛ fɛɛ ba koni amɛ kɛ Mose shaanuu lɛ abaye nii yɛ he krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ.
Kojolɔiwoo
(Deuteronomio 1.9-18)
13Enɔ jetsɛremɔ leebi lɛ, Mose ho eta shi, ni ekura maŋbii lɛ ateŋ saji, ni maŋ lɛ jwere enɔ kɛjɛ leebi kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. 14Be ni Mose shaanuu lɛ na nibii fɛɛ ni Mose tsuɔ ehãa maŋ lɛ, ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Mɛni ji nɔ ni otsuɔ ohãa maŋ lɛ nɛɛ? Mɛɛba okome too ota shi, ni maŋ lɛ fɛɛ jwere onɔ nɛkɛ leebileebi jenamɔ nɛɛ?”
15Mose hã lɛ hetoo ekɛɛ, “Ebaa lɛ nakai ejaakɛ maŋbii lɛ baa amɛbabiɔ mi Nyɔŋmɔ daaŋ gbee. 16Kɛji amɛna sane ko lɛ amɛkɛbaa miŋɔɔ, ni mikuraa, ni mitsɔ̃ɔ amɛ Nyɔŋmɔ akpɔi kɛ nɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ.”
17Mose shaanuu lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Nɔ ni ofeɔ nɛɛ ehiii. 18 Ebaatɔ bo kɛ maŋ lɛ fɛɛ hu. Nitsumɔ nɛɛ fa tsɔ̃ hã bo; okome too onyɛŋ otsu. 19Agbɛnɛ bo migbee toi; mawo bo ŋaa, ni Nyɔŋmɔ aye abua bo. Bo lɛ feemɔ maŋbii lɛ anaadamɔlɔ yɛ maŋbii lɛ kɛ Nyɔŋmɔ teŋ koni okɛ amɛsaji lɛ ashwie Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ; 20ni otsɔ̃ɔ amɛ Nyɔŋmɔ akpɔi, nɔ ni ekɛɛ lɛ, ni ohã amɛle bɔ ni sa akɛ amɛba amɛjeŋ amɛhã, kɛ nɔ ni sa akɛ amɛfee. 21Ni asaŋ halamɔ maŋ lɛ fɛɛ mli hii ni aaanyɛ atsu gbɛnaa ni abaahã amɛ lɛ he nii, mɛi ni amɛsheɔ Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei hu, ni amɛ ji anɔkwafoi ni heee nyɔɔŋnii, koni oto amɛ kui anɔkwɛlɔi: mɛi nyɔŋmanyɔŋma kui kɛ mɛi nyɔŋmai enumɔenumɔ kui kɛ mɛi ohaoha kui kɛ akpeakpe kui anɔkwɛlɔi. 22Ohã amɛ amɛkura saji ni baaba maŋbii lɛ ateŋ lɛ be fɛɛ be. Sane wulu fɛɛ sane wulu lɛ, no lɛ akɛba ohiɛ; shi saji bibii fɛɛ lɛ kui anɔkwɛlɔi lɛ aye, bɔ ni afee ni amɛkɛmɔ mli amɛhã bo koni efo tsɔ́ ehã bo. 23Bɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ fãa bo nɛ. Kɛji ofee nakai lɛ, ooonyɛ nitsumɔ nɛɛ naa odamɔ, ni maŋbii nɛɛ fɛɛ hu aaayashɛ amɛshɛɛhe yɛ hejɔlɛ mli.”
24Mose bo eshaanuu lɛ toi, ni efee nɔ ni ekɛɛ lɛ lɛ fɛɛ. 25Ehala maŋ lɛ fɛɛ mli hii ni aaanyɛ atsu gbɛnaa ni abaahã amɛ lɛ he nii, ni eto amɛ kui anɔkwɛlɔi: mɛi nyɔŋma nyɔŋma kui kɛ mɛi nyɔŋmai enumɔenumɔ kui kɛ mɛi ohaoha kui kɛ mɛi akpeakpe kui anɔkwɛlɔi. 26Nɔkwɛlɔi nɛɛ kuraa maŋbii lɛ ateŋ saji be fɛɛ be. Saji wuji lɛ amɛkɛbaa Mose ŋɔɔ; shi saji bibii fɛɛ lɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛkuraa.
27Fee sɛɛ lɛ Mose shaanuu Yetro kɛ lɛ ye shɛɛ, ni Yetro ku esɛɛ etee emaŋ.

english_text:
At Mount Sinai
1-2The Israelites left Rephidim and arrived at the desert. Then two months after leaving Egypt, they arrived at the desert near Mount Sinai, where they set up camp at the foot of the mountain. This was two months after they had left Egypt.
3Moses went up the mountain to meet with the Lord God, who told him to say to the people:
4You saw what I did in Egypt, and you know how I brought you here to me, just as a mighty eagle carries its young. 5 Now if you will faithfully obey me, you will be my very own people. The whole world is mine, 6 but you will be my holy nation and serve me as priests.
Moses, that is what you must tell the Israelites.
7After Moses went back, he reported to the leaders what the Lord had said, 8and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded.” So Moses told the Lord about this.
9The Lord said to Moses, “I will come to you in a thick cloud and let the people hear me speak to you. Then they will always trust you.” Again Moses reported to the Lord what the people had said.
10Once more the Lord spoke to Moses:
Go back and tell the people that today and tomorrow they must get themselves ready to meet me. They must wash their clothes 11and be ready by the day after tomorrow, when I will come down to Mount Sinai, where all of them can see me.
12 Warn the people that they are forbidden to touch any part of the mountain. Anyone who does will be put to death, 13either with stones or arrows, and no one must touch the body of the person being put to death in this way. Even an animal that touches this mountain must be put to death. You may go up the mountain only after a signal is given on the trumpet.
14After Moses went down the mountain, he gave orders for the people to wash their clothes and make themselves acceptable to worship God. 15He told them to be ready in three days and not to have sex in the meantime.
The Lord Comes to Mount Sinai
16 On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud covered the mountain, a loud trumpet blast was heard, and everyone in camp trembled with fear. 17Moses led them out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
18Mount Sinai was covered with smoke because the Lord had come down in a flaming fire. Smoke poured out of the mountain just like a furnace, and the whole mountain shook. 19The trumpet blew louder and louder. Moses spoke, and God answered him with thunder.
20The Lord came down to the top of Mount Sinai and told Moses to meet him there. 21Then he said, “Moses, go and warn the people not to cross the boundary that you set at the foot of the mountain. They must not cross it to come and look at me, because if they do, many of them will die. 22Only the priests may come near me, and they must obey strict rules before I let them. If they don't, they will be punished.”
23Moses replied, “The people cannot come up the mountain. You warned us to stay away because it is holy.”
24Then the Lord told Moses, “Go down and bring Aaron back here with you. But the priests and people must not try to push their way through, or I will rush at them like a flood!”
25After Moses had gone back down, he told the people what the Lord had said.
translation_text:
Israelbii lɛ yɛ Sinai Gɔŋ lɛ he
1Gbi ni Israelbii lɛ yiŋ kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, enɔ nyɔji etɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛyashɛ Sinai ŋa lɛ nɔ. 2Refidim ji he ni amɛfã kɛjɛ dani amɛyashɛ Sinai ŋa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni amɛbato shi yɛ Sinai Gɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. 3Kɛkɛ ni Mose kwɔ gɔŋ lɛ kɛtee Nyɔŋmɔ ŋɔɔ. Yehowa jɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ etsɛ Mose, ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kɛɛmɔ Yakob shwiei, ni ji Israelbii, lɛ akɛ, 4 ‘Nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛna nɔ ni mifee Ijiptbii lɛ, kɛ bɔ ni mihiɛ nyɛ kɛ hewalɛ tamɔ okropɔŋ, ni mikɛ nyɛ bashɛ miŋɔɔ yɛ biɛ nɛɛ lɛ. 5 No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ kɛji nyɛaabo mi toi, ni nyɛaaye mikpãŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, no lɛ nyɛaatsɔ̃ mi diɛŋtsɛ minɔ yɛ maji fɛɛ ateŋ; ejaakɛ je lɛ fɛɛ lɛ minɔ ni. 6 Mibafee nyɛ osɔfoi abladei, mibafee nyɛ maŋ krɔŋkrɔŋ. Nɔ ni okɛɛ Israelbii lɛ nɛ.’ ” 7Mose ku esɛɛ eba, ni ebatsɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ, ni ekɛɛ amɛ nɔ ni Yehowa fã akɛ ekɛɛ amɛ lɛ. 8Ni maŋ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ here nɔ shi kome amɛkɛɛ, “Nibii fɛɛ ni Yehowa ekɛɛ lɛ wɔɔfee.” Mose hã Yehowa le hetoo ni maŋ lɛ hã lɛ.
9Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Miiba oŋɔɔ yɛ atatu kpii mli koni kɛ mi kɛ bo miiwie lɛ, maŋ lɛ anu ni amɛhe bo hu amɛye kɛya naanɔ.”
10Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Yaa maŋbii lɛ aŋɔɔ, ni otsuu amɛhe ŋmɛnɛ kɛ wɔ ni ohã amɛfɔ amɛtadei ahe, 11ni amɛsaa amɛhe amɛto gbi ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ, ejaakɛ nakai gbi lɛ Yehowa baakpleke shi kɛba gɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiŋmɛiŋ. 12 Foo akrabatsa okɛtsi maŋ lɛ gbɛ, ni obɔ amɛ kɔkɔ akɛ, ‘Nyɛkwɛa ni ahĩa koni nyɛkakwɔa gɔŋ lɛ, aloo ni nyɛtaa ehusu lɛ he.’ Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaata gɔŋ lɛ he lɛ gbe aaagbe lɛ. 13 Mɔ ko mɔ ko nine akata nakai gbɔmɔ lɛ he, shi atswia lɛ tɛ aloo atsɛ̃rɛ lɛ gãi. Kooloo ni jio, gbɔmɔ ni jio, akahã eyi na wala. Shi kɛji akpã tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ lɛ, ni esɛɛ tsɛ aahu lɛ, no dani amɛba gɔŋ lɛ he.”
14Mose kpeleke shi kɛjɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛba maŋ lɛ ŋɔɔ, ni etsuu maŋ lɛ he, ni amɛfɔfɔɔ amɛtadei ahe. 15 Ni Mose kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Nyɛsaa nyɛhe nyɛtoa hã, wɔ bɛ mli, wɔsɛɛ. Nuu akaya yoo masɛi.”
16 Gbi ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ leebi lɛ ŋwɛi shimɔ, ni srawa gbala ni atatu kpii ko baha gɔŋ lɛ nɔ; tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ ko gbɛɛ waa naakpa, ni mɛi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ shitoohe lɛ fɛɛ kpokpo. 17Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛ maŋ lɛ je kpo kɛjɛ shitoohe lɛ koni amɛkɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ayakpe, ni amɛyadamɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi. 18Sinai Gɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ miije lasu, ejaakɛ Yehowa ekpeleke shi kɛba gɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ la mli. Lasu lɛ fãa kɛyaa ŋwɛi tamɔ flɔnɔɔ mli lasu, ni gɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ hoso waa naakpa. 19 Be ni tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ lɛ yaa nɔ gbɛɔ waa lɛ, kɛkɛ ni Mose wie, ni Nyɔŋmɔ here lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋwɛi shiimɔ. 20Be ni Yehowa kpeleke shi kɛba Sinai Gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ, etsɛ Mose akɛ eba gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ; ni Mose tee. 21Yehowa kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Kpelekemɔ shi ni oyakɛɛ maŋ lɛ kpɔ́kpɔ́ɔkpɔ́ akɛ amɛkatse mli kɛmiiba Yehowa ŋɔɔ amɛbakwɛ nɔ ni yaa nɔ, koni amɛteŋ mɛi pii miiplenee. 22Asaŋ hã osɔfoi lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ Yehowa atsuu amɛhe koni Yehowa akakpãtã amɛhiɛ.”
23Mose kɛɛ Yehowa akɛ, “Maŋ lɛ nyɛŋ Sinai Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ aba ejaakɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ okpã owo wɔtoiŋ akɛ, ‘Nyɛfoa akrabatsa nyɛwoa gɔŋ lɛ he nyɛfea lɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ.’ ”
24Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Kpelekemɔ shi oya ni okɛ Aaron akwɔ kɛba, shi kaahã osɔfoi lɛ kɛ maŋbii lɛ miiteke akrabatsa lɛ kɛkwɔ gɔŋ lɛ kɛba mi, Yehowa, miŋɔɔ koni mikaplene amɛ.” 25Mose kpeleke shi kɛba maŋbii lɛ aŋɔɔ, ni ebakɛɛ amɛ.

english_text:
The Ten Commandments
(Deuteronomy 5.1-21)
1God said to the people of Israel:
2I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
3Do not worship any god except me.
4 Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth. 5 Don't bow down and worship idols. I am the Lord your God, and I demand all your love. If you reject me, I will punish your families for three or four generations. 6But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
7 Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
8 Remember that the Sabbath Day belongs to me. 9 You have six days when you can do your work, 10but the seventh day of each week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your slaves, your animals, or the foreigners who live in your towns. 11 In six days I made the sky, the earth, the oceans, and everything in them, but on the seventh day I rested. That's why I made the Sabbath a special day that belongs to me.
12 Respect your father and your mother, and you will live a long time in the land I am giving you.
13 Do not murder.
14 Be faithful in marriage.
15 Do not steal.
16 Do not tell lies about others.
17 Do not desire to possess anything that belongs to another person—not a house, a wife, a husband, a slave, an ox, a donkey, or anything else.
The People Are Afraid
(Deuteronomy 5.23-33)
18 The people trembled with fear when they heard the thunder and the trumpet and saw the lightning and the smoke coming from the mountain. They stood a long way off 19and said to Moses, “If you speak to us, we will listen. But don't let God speak to us, or we will die!”
20“Don't be afraid!” Moses replied. “God has come only to test you, so that by obeying him you won't sin.” 21But when Moses went near the thick cloud where God was, the people stayed a long way off.
Idols and Altars
22The Lord told Moses to say to the people of Israel:
With your own eyes you saw me speak to you from heaven. 23So you must never make idols of silver or gold to worship in place of me.
24Build an altar out of earth, and offer on it your sacrifices of sheep, goats, and cattle. Wherever I choose to be worshiped, I will come down to bless you. 25 If you ever build an altar for me out of stones, do not use any tools to chisel the stones, because that would make the altar unfit for use in worship. 26And don't build an altar that requires steps; you might expose yourself when you climb up.
translation_text:
Kitãi Nyɔŋma lɛ
(Deuteronomio 5.1-21)
1Ni Nyɔŋmɔ wie wiemɔi nɛɛ fɛɛ ekɛɛ:
2“Mi ji Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, ni mi mijie bo yɛ nyɔŋyeli mli kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.
3 “Kaana nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi yɛ misɛɛ.
4 “Kaafee amãgã ko loo nɔ ko ni tamɔ nii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi loo nii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nii ni yɔɔ nu mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ohã ohe.
5 “Kaaja amɛ, ni kaasɔ̃mɔ amɛ hu, ejaakɛ mi Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ ni yeɔ awuŋã ji mi, ni miwoɔ tsɛmɛi kɛ bii anyɔmɔ yɛ tsɛmɛi lɛ atɔ̃mɔi ahewɔ kɛyashiɔ yinɔ ni ji etɛ̃ kɛ yinɔ ni ji ejwɛ tete ni nyɛɔ mi lɛ nɔ.
6“Shi mɛi akpei abɔ fɛɛ ni sumɔɔ mi, ni amɛyeɔ mikitãi anɔ lɛ, misumɔɔ amɛ kɛ suɔmɔ ni tsakeee, ni minaa amɛ mɔbɔ.
7 “Kaahiɛ Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, gbɛi mli yakayaka, ejaakɛ Yehowa ebuŋ mɔ ni tsɛɔ egbɛi yakayaka lɛ bem.
8 “Ohiɛ ahi hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ nɔ ni oye lɛ akɛ gbi krɔŋkrɔŋ. 9Tsu nii gbii ekpaa ni ofee onii fɛɛ, 10shi gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ, hejɔɔmɔ gbi ni hã Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ. No nɔ lɛ okatsu nɔ ko, bo jio, obinuu jio, obiyoo jio, owenuu jio, oweyoo jio, okooloo jio, ogbɔ ni ebato omaŋ jio. 11 Ejaakɛ gbii ekpaa Yehowa kɛbɔ ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋshɔ kɛ amɛmli nibii fɛɛ; ni gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ ejɔɔ ehe. No hewɔ ni Yehowa jɔɔ hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ, ni efee lɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ.
12 “Wo otsɛ kɛ onyɛ koni owala sɛɛ atsɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi, Yehowa, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, kɛhãa bo lɛ nɔ.
13 “Kaagbe gbɔmɔ.
14 “Kaafite gbãlã.
15“Kaaju.
16 “Kaaye amale odase yɛ onaanyo he.
17“Ohiɛ akakɔ̃ onaanyo nɔ ko nɔ, eshĩa jio, eŋa jio, ewenuu jio, eweyoo jio, etsina jio, eteji jio, enɔ kroko jio, ohiɛ akakɔ̃ nɔ.”
Israelbii lɛ she gbeyei
(Deuteronomio 5.22-33)
18Be ni Israelbii lɛ na bɔ ni ŋwɛi shimɔɔ, ni srawa gbalaa, ni tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ gbɛɔ, ni gɔŋ lɛ fãa lasu lɛ, amɛshe gbeyei, ni amɛkpokpo, ni amɛdamɔ sɛɛ flɛŋŋ. 19Kɛkɛ ni amɛkɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Bo moŋ okɛ wɔ awie, ni wɔɔbo toi, shi kaahã Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ wɔ miiwie ni wɔbagboi.”
20Mose kɛɛ maŋ lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkashea gbeyei, ejaakɛ kaa Nyɔŋmɔ ba nyɛ kaa, bɔ ni afee ni lɛ egbeyeishemɔ ahi nyɛmli daa koni nyɛkafee esha.” 21 Shi maŋ lɛ damɔ sɛɛ flɛŋŋ lolo; kɛkɛ ni Mose tsi ebɛŋkɛ duŋ kpii lɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ.
Afɔleshãa latɛi ahe mlai
22Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Kɛɛmɔ Israelbii lɛ akɛ, ‘Nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛna akɛ ŋwɛi mijɛ mikɛ nyɛ wie nɛɛ. 23Nyɛkafea mihenɔ jwiɛtɛi loo shika amãgãi; nyɛkafea eko eko nyɛhãa nyɛhe koni nyɛja amɛ nyɛfata mihe. 24Nyɛshɔ̃a su afɔleshãa latɛ nyɛhãa mi, ni no nɔ nyɛshãa afɔlei yɛ, shãa afɔlei kɛ shidaa afɔlei kɛ gwantɛŋi kɛ tsinai lɛ yɛ. He fɛɛ he ni mato mahã nyɛ akɛ aja mi yɛ lɛ, maba nyɛŋɔɔ yɛ jɛi ni majɔɔ nyɛ. 25 Kɛji nyɛkɛ tɛ miima afɔleshãa latɛ nyɛhã mi lɛ, akɛ tɛ ni ako akama ejaakɛ ŋaa dade naa ni aaasa tɛ lɛ he pɛ ebule lɛ. 26Ni okafee atrakpoi owo afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he koni akana oyayaiaŋ yɛ atrakpoi lɛ kwɔɔ mli.’ ”

english_text:
Hebrew Slaves
(Deuteronomy 15.12-18)
1The Lord gave Moses the following laws for his people:
2 If you buy a Hebrew slave, he must remain your slave for six years. But in the seventh year you must set him free, without cost to him. 3If he was single at the time you bought him, he alone must be set free. But if he was married at the time, both he and his wife must be given their freedom. 4If you give him a wife, and they have children, only the man himself must be set free; his wife and children remain the property of his owner.
5But suppose the slave loves his wife and children and his owner so much that he won't leave them. 6Then he must stand beside either the door or the doorpost at the place of worship, while his owner punches a small hole through one of his ears with a sharp metal rod. This makes him a slave for life.
7A young woman who was sold by her father doesn't gain her freedom in the same way that a man does. 8If she doesn't please the man who bought her to be his wife, he must let her be bought back. He cannot sell her to foreigners; this would break the contract he made with her. 9If he selects her as a wife for his son, he must treat her as his own daughter.
10If the man later marries another woman, he must continue to provide food and clothing for the one he bought and to treat her as a wife. 11If he fails to do any of these things, she must be given her freedom without paying for it.
Murder and Other Violent Crimes
The Lord said:
12 Death is the punishment for murder. 13 But if you did not intend to kill someone, and I, the Lord, let it happen anyway, you may run for safety to a place that I have set aside. 14If you plan in advance to murder someone, there's no escape, not even by holding on to my altar. You will be dragged off and killed.
15Death is the punishment for attacking your father or mother.
16 Death is the punishment for kidnapping. If you sell the person you kidnapped, or if you are caught with that person, the penalty is death.
17 Death is the punishment for cursing your father or mother.
18Suppose two of you are arguing, and you hit the other with either a rock or your fist, without causing a fatal injury. If the victim has to stay in bed, 19and later has to use a stick when walking outside, you must pay for the loss of time and do what you can to help until the injury is completely healed. That's your only responsibility.
20Death is the punishment for beating to death any of your slaves. 21However, if the slave lives a few days after the beating, you are not to be punished. After all, you have already lost the services of that slave who was your property.
22Suppose a pregnant woman suffers a miscarriage as the result of an injury caused by someone who is fighting. If she isn't badly hurt, the one who injured her must pay whatever fine her husband demands and the judges approve. 23But if she is seriously injured, the payment will be life for life, 24 eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot, 25burn for burn, cut for cut, and bruise for bruise.
26If you hit one of your slaves and cause the loss of an eye, the slave must be set free. 27The same law applies if you knock out a slave's tooth—the slave goes free.
28A bull that kills someone with its horns must be killed and its meat destroyed, but the owner of the bull isn't responsible for the death.
29Suppose you own a bull that has been in the habit of attacking people, but you have refused to keep it fenced in. If that bull kills someone, both you and the bull must be put to death by stoning. 30However, you may save your own life by paying whatever fine is demanded. 31This same law applies if the bull gores someone's son or daughter. 32If the bull kills a slave, you must pay the slave owner 30 pieces of silver for the loss of the slave, and the bull must be killed by stoning.
33Suppose someone's ox or donkey is killed by falling into an open pit that you dug or left uncovered on your property. 34You must pay for the dead animal, and it becomes yours.
35If your bull kills someone else's, yours must be sold. Then the money from your bull and the meat from the dead bull must be divided equally between you and the other owner.
36If you refuse to fence in a bull that is known to attack others, you must replace any animal it kills, but the dead animal will belong to you.
translation_text:
Bɔ ni ahiɛ nyɔji ahã
(Deuteronomio 15.12-18)
1“Agbɛnɛ okɛ mlai nɛɛ ashwie Israelbii lɛ ahiɛ. 2 Kɛji ohe Hebrinyo akɛ nyɔŋ lɛ esɔ̃mɔ afii ekpaa, ni afi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ aŋmɛɛ ehe ni eye ehe tswaa. 3Kɛji ekome eba lɛ, ekome nɔŋŋ eya. Shi kɛji ekɛ eŋa ba lɛ, no lɛ eŋa lɛ kɛ lɛ aya. 4Kɛji enuŋtsɔ lɛ ehã lɛ ŋa, ni ekɛ yoo lɛ efɔ bihii loo biyei lɛ, no lɛ yoo lɛ kɛ ebii lɛ etsɔ̃ enuŋtsɔ lɛ nɔ, ni nuu lɛ kome too aya. 5Shi kɛji nyɔŋ lɛ gba mli kpoo ekɛɛ akɛ, ‘Miisumɔ minuŋtsɔ lɛ kɛ miŋa kɛ mibii lɛ, ni misumɔɔɔ akɛ mashi amɛ maya mayaye mihe lɛ,’ 6 no lɛ enuŋtsɔ lɛ kɛ lɛ aya Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ, ni ehã edamɔ jamɔhe lɛ shinaa lɛ naa loo shinaatso lɛ he, ni enuŋtsɔ lɛ kɛ fitii agbu nyɔŋ lɛ toi, ni nyɔŋ lɛ asɔ̃mɔ enuŋtsɔ lɛ ewala gbii abɔ fɛɛ.
7 “Kɛji nuu ko hɔ̃ɔ ebiyoo akɛ nyɔŋ lɛ, biyoo nɛɛ akatsɔ̃ gbɛ nɔ ni hii nyɔji tsɔ̃ɔ yeɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ eye ehe. 8Kɛ nyɔŋ yoo nɛɛ esaaa enuŋtsɔ lɛ hiɛ akɛ eeeŋɔ lɛ efee eŋa lɛ, no lɛ ehã abakpɔ̃ lɛ. Nuŋtsɔ lɛ bɛ hegbɛ ni ehɔ̃ɔ lɛ ehãa maŋsɛɛnyo, ejaakɛ no lɛ eku eshiwoo mli. 9Kɛji nuŋtsɔ lɛ kɛ nyɔŋ yoo lɛ hã ebinuu gbãlã lɛ, nuŋtsɔ lɛ kɛ nyɔŋ yoo nɛɛ ahi shi akɛ ebiyoo. 10Kɛji nuŋtsɔ lɛ yaŋɔ yoo ni ji enyɔ ebafata nyɔŋyoo lɛ he lɛ, no akahã etse nyɔŋyoo lɛ daaŋ ŋmaa kɛ ehebo kɛ egblãshihilɛ mli gbɛnaa nii nɔ. 11Kɛji nuŋtsɔ lɛ tsuuu nibii etɛ̃ nɛɛ ahe ehãaa nyɔŋ yoo lɛ, no lɛ nyɔŋ yoo lɛ aye ehe tswaa, ni nuŋtsɔ lɛ bɛ hegbɛ akɛ aheɔ eyi shika ko.”
Awuiyeli he mlai
12 “Mɔ ni aaatswa enyɛmi gbɔmɔ nɔ, ni mɔ lɛ aaagbo lɛ, lɛ hu agbe lɛ. 13 Kɛjeee ka eyawo lɛ, shi osharã naa ni, enine kpa yɛ mɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, no lɛ ejo foi eyaba abo yɛ he ko ni mato mahã nyɛ. 14 Shi kɛji mɔ ko to ŋaa fɔŋ yɛ enyɛmi gbɔmɔ he, ni eje gbɛ eyatua lɛ, ni egbe lɛ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ eyaba abo yɛ mifɔleshãa latɛ lɛ naa tete po, ajie lɛ kɛje jɛi ni ayagbe lɛ.
15“Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaagba etsɛ loo enyɛ ma lɛ agbe lɛ.
16 “Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaaju gbɔmɔ lɛ, eyahɔɔ lɛ jio, eto lɛ akɛ nyɔŋ ehã ehe jio, agbe lɛ.
17 “Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaalomɔ etsɛ loo enyɛ lɛ agbe lɛ.
18“Kɛji hii miinɔ ni mɔ kome tswa enaanyo lɛ tɛ aloo ema lɛ atswɛrɛ, ni mɔ lɛ tsɔɔɔ mli gbooo, shi efee lɛ hela kɛkã shi lɛ, 19kɛji helatsɛ lɛ na ete shi ekoŋŋ, ni emɔ tso mli enyiɛ kɛje kpo lɛ, mɔ ni tswa lɛ nɔ lɛ eye ehe, shi moŋ ewo be ni helatsɛ lɛ efite lɛ he nyɔmɔ, ni ekwɛ koni atsa helatsɛ lɛ ni ehe atã kwrakwra.
20“Kɛji mɔ ko kɛ tso tswa enyɔŋ nuu loo nyɔŋ yoo, ni nyɔŋ lɛ nyɔ yɛ enine naa lɛ, ja atɔ nyɔŋ lɛ he owele yɛ nuŋtsɔ lɛ nɔ. 21Shi kɛji je tsɛre nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ lɛ, akatɔ owele yɛ nuŋtsɔ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ nyɔŋ lɛ ni egbo lɛ, lɛ nuŋtsɔ lɛ, eshika ni elaaje ni.
22“Kɛji hii miinɔ ni amɛkɛ nɔmɔ lɛ yapila yoohɔlɔ, ni emusu lɛ fite, shi eyeee lɛ awui kroko kɛfataaa he lɛ, agbe nuu mɔ ni pila yoohɔlɔ lɛ shika gbele. Yoo wu lɛ aaatsɔ̃ɔ nyɔmɔ ni ekɛfɔ̃ɔ nuu lɛ nɔ nɛ, shi moŋ bɔ ni saneyelɔi lɛ aaatsɔ̃ɔ lɛ nakai nuu lɛ awo. 23 Shi kɛji sane fɔŋ ba yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ oweletɔɔ lɛ afee atoŋ kɛ atoŋ, no ji akɛ wala atse wala, 24 ni akɛ hiŋmɛi atse hiŋmɛi, ni akɛ nyanyɔŋ atse nyanyɔŋ, akɛ nane atse nane, 25akɛ la fala atse la fala, akɛ pilamɔ atse pilamɔ, ni akɛ kpelebi naa fala atse kpelebi naa fala.
26“Kɛji mɔ ko tswa enyɔŋ nuu loo nyɔŋ yoo hiŋmɛi nɔ, ni hiŋmɛi lɛ fite lɛ, ehã nyɔŋ lɛ aye ehe tswaa yɛ ehiŋmɛi lɛ hewɔ. 27Kɛji nuŋtsɔ lɛ fã enyɔŋ nuu loo nyɔŋ yoo nyanyɔŋ lɛ, eŋmɛɛ nyɔŋ lɛ he koni eyaye ehe tswaa yɛ enyanyɔŋ lɛ hewɔ.”
Kooloi anuŋtsɔmɛi asɔ̃
28“Kɛji tsina shi nuu loo yoo, ni mɔ lɛ gbo lɛ, atswia tsina lɛ tɛ ni agbe lɛ, ni akaye eloo lɛ, shi tsinatsɛ lɛ aye ehe. 29 Shi kɛji tsina lɛ fɔɔ mɔ shimɔ kɛjɛ jeeŋmɔ, ni abɔ nɔtsɛ lɛ kɔkɔ yɛ he, shi fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ ewooo ekooloo lɛ tsuŋ, ni eyagbe gbɔmɔ lɛ, atswia tsina lɛ tɛ, ni tsinatsɛ lɛ hu agbe lɛ. 30Shi kɛji aahe tsinatsɛ lɛ kpãtãmɔ nii lɛ, no lɛ bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni aheɔ lɛ lɛ, ewo koni ekɛkpɔ̃ esusuma. 31Kɛji tsina lɛ yashi mɔ ko binuu loo biyoo lɛ akɛ tsinatsɛ lɛ aye yɛ mla kome nɛɛ nɔŋŋ naa. 32Kɛji tsina lɛ yashi nyɔŋ nuu loo nyɔŋ yoo lɛ tsinatsɛ lɛ ahã nyɔŋ lɛ nuŋtsɔ lɛ jwiɛtɛi shekel nyɔŋmai etɛ̃, ni no sɛɛ hu lɛ atswia tsina lɛ tɛ.
33“Kɛji mɔ ko shi bu naa eŋmɛ aloo eyatsa bu ni etsiii nɔ, ni tsina loo teji ko yagbee mli lɛ, 34mɔ ni tsa bu lɛ awo koolootsɛ lɛ ekooloo lɛ he nyɔmɔ koni bu tsɛ lɛ aŋɔ kooloo gbonyo lɛ. 35Kɛji mɔ ko tsina pila enaanyo tsina, ni kooloo lɛ gbo lɛ, mɛi enyɔ lɛ ahɔ̃ɔ tsina hiɛkãalɔ lɛ koni amɛja shika lɛ, ni kooloo ni egbo lɛ hu amɛja. 36Shi kɛji ale ato akɛ tsina lɛ fɔɔ mɔshimɔ kɛjɛ jeeŋmɔ, shi tsinatsɛ lɛ wooo tsina lɛ tsuŋ lɛ, no lɛ ekɛ tsina ato mɔ lɛ tsina lɛ najiaŋ ehã lɛ koni mɔ ni tsina yashi lɛ aŋɔ tsina ni egbo lɛ.”

english_text:
Property Laws
The Lord said:
1If you steal an ox and slaughter or sell it, you must replace it with five oxen; if you steal a sheep and slaughter it or sell it, you must replace it with four sheep. 2-4But if you cannot afford to replace the animals, you must be sold as a slave to pay for what you have stolen. If you steal an ox, donkey, or sheep, and are caught with it still alive, you must pay the owner double.
If you happen to kill a burglar who breaks into your home after dark, you are not guilty. But if you kill someone who breaks in during the day, you are guilty of murder.
5If you allow any of your animals to stray from your property and graze in someone else's field or vineyard, you must repay the damage from the best part of your own harvest of grapes and grain.
6If you carelessly let a fire spread from your property to someone else's, you must pay the owner for any crops or fields destroyed by the fire.
7Suppose a neighbor asks you to keep some silver or other valuables, and they are stolen from your house. If the thief is caught, the thief must repay double. 8But if the thief isn't caught, some judges will decide if you are the guilty one.
9Suppose two people claim to own the same ox or donkey or sheep or piece of clothing. Then the judges must decide the case, and the guilty person will pay the owner double.
10Suppose a neighbor who is going to be away asks you to keep a donkey or an ox or a sheep or some other animal, and it dies or gets injured or is stolen while no one is looking. 11If you swear with me as your witness that you did not harm the animal, you do not have to replace it. Your word is enough. 12But if the animal was stolen while in your care, you must replace it. 13If the animal was attacked and killed by a wild animal, and you can show the remains of the dead animal to its owner, you do not have to replace it.
14Suppose you borrow an animal from a neighbor, and it gets injured or dies while the neighbor isn't around. Then you must replace it. 15But if something happens to the animal while the owner is present, you do not have to replace it. If you had leased the animal, the money you paid the owner will cover any harm done to it.
Laws for Everyday Life
The Lord said:
16 Suppose a young woman has never had sex and isn't engaged. If a man talks her into having sex, he must pay the bride price and marry her. 17But if her father refuses to let her marry the man, the bride price must still be paid.
18 Death is the punishment for witchcraft.
19 Death is the punishment for having sex with an animal.
20 Death is the punishment for offering sacrifices to any god except me.
21 Do not mistreat or abuse foreigners who live among you. Remember, you were foreigners in Egypt.
22Do not mistreat widows or orphans. 23If you do, they will beg for my help, and I will come to their rescue. 24In fact, I will get so angry that I will kill your men and make widows of their wives and orphans of their children.
25 Don't charge interest when you lend money to any of my people who are in need. 26 Before sunset you must return any coat taken as security for a loan, 27because that is the only cover the poor have when they sleep at night. I am a merciful God, and when they call out to me, I will come to help them.
28 Don't speak evil of me or of the ruler of your people.
29Don't fail to give me the offerings of grain and wine that belong to me.
Dedicate to me your first-born sons 30and the first-born of your cattle and sheep. Let the animals stay with their mothers for seven days, then on the eighth day give them to me, your God.
31 You are my chosen people, so don't eat the meat of any of your livestock that was killed by a wild animal. Instead, feed the meat to dogs.
translation_text:
Niianajiaŋtoo he mlai
1 “Kɛji mɔ ko yaju tsina loo too, ni eyagbe aloo eyahɔ̃ɔ lɛ, ekɛ tsinai enumɔ ato tsina kome najiaŋ, ni ekɛ toi ejwɛ ato too kome najiaŋ. Shi kɛ ebɛ nɔ ko lɛ, no lɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ koni akɛtse nii ni eju lɛ. 2Kɛji ana kooloo ni eyaju lɛ hiɛkãalɔ yɛ edɛŋ lɛ, tsina ni jio, teji ni jio, too ni jio, eku ebɔ he toi enyɔ eto najiaŋ.
3“Kɛji ana julɔ nyɔɔŋ ni eejwa mɔ ko shinaa ni ebote mli, ni atswa lɛ nɔ ni egbo lɛ, mɔ ni tswa lɛ nɔ lɛ yeee ela yi sɔ̃. 4Shi kɛji shwane agbe lɛ lɛ, no lɛ mɔ ni tswa lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ela yi sɔ̃.
5“Kɛji mɔ ko ŋmɛɛ ekooloo he, ni eyaye ŋmɔ loo waintrom ko mli nii, aloo mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ ekooloo lɛ nɔ, ni ekooloo lɛ yaye mɔ kroko ko ŋmɔshinii lɛ, koolootsɛ lɛ kɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eŋmɔshi loo waintrom mli nii ni hi fe fɛɛ ato nii ni afite lɛ najiaŋ.
6“Kɛji mɔ ko wo la, ni etso kɛyamɔ ŋmeii, ni eshã abele kɛ aboŋo, loo abele ni akuko, loo ŋmɔ lɛ, mɔ ni wo la lɛ ato nii ni hiɛ kpãtã lɛ najiaŋ shishiishi.
7“Kɛji mɔ ko kɛ shika loo nibii hã enaanyo shitoo, ni aju nii lɛ yɛ mɔ lɛ we lɛ, ni amɔ julɔ lɛ, julɔ lɛ kɛ nii ni eju lɛ toi enyɔ ato najiaŋ. 8 Shi kɛji anaaa julɔ lɛ, no lɛ shĩatsɛ lɛ aba Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ ni ebatsɔɔ akɛ enine etako enaanyo lɛ nii lɛ he.
9“Niiaheplemɔ fɛɛ ni aaate shi lɛ, tsina he ejɛ jio, teji he jio, too he jio, atade he jio, nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni eji ni aaapele he ni mɔ ko aaakɛɛ akɛ enɔ ni lɛ, akɛ sane lɛ aba Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ. Mɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ aaabu lɛ fɔ lɛ, ekɛ nɔ lɛ toi enyɔ ato enaanyo lɛ nii lɛ najiaŋ.
10“Kɛji mɔ ko kɛ eteji loo tsina loo too loo kooloo fɛɛ kooloo hã enaanyo shitoo, ni kooloo lɛ gbo, aloo aye lɛ awui, aloo ofɔ̃yelɔi bamɔ lɛ kɛtee, shi anaaa mɔ ko aye he odase lɛ, 11mɔ ni akɛ nɔ lɛ hã shitoo lɛ ayakã Yehowa kitã akɛ enine etako enaanyo lɛ nii lɛ he. Nɔtsɛ lɛ akpɛlɛ̃ nɔ, ni mɔ ni akɛ nii lɛ hã shitoo etoŋ nɔtsɛ lɛ najiaŋ. 12Shi kɛji ju aju nii lɛ yɛ edɛŋ lɛ eto nɔtsɛ lɛ najiaŋ. 13 Kɛji kooloo kakawua ko ni tserɛ kooloo lɛ, ekɛ kooloo gbonyo lɛ abaye odase koni ekato najiaŋ.
14“Kɛji mɔ ko yama kooloo ko yɛ enaanyo dɛŋ, ni eye kooloo lɛ awui, aloo egbo be mli ni nɔtsɛ lɛ bɛ jɛi lɛ, mɔ ni yama kooloo lɛ ato najiaŋ shishiishi; 15shi kɛji nɔtsɛ lɛ yɛ jɛi lɛ, no lɛ akato najiaŋ. Kɛji apaayeli akɛ kooloo lɛ ba lɛ, no lɛ akato najiaŋ ejaakɛ epaayeli nyɔmɔ ni awo hewɔ eba.”
Jeŋba he mlai
16 “Kɛji nuu ko yalaka oblayoo foro ni atsɛko ehe baa, ni ekɛ lɛ wɔ lɛ, nuu lɛ ahã yoo lɛ yinii koni etsɔ̃ eŋa. 17Shi kɛji yoo lɛ tsɛ ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ yoo lɛ kɛ nuu lɛ hãmɔ kwraa lɛ, nuu lɛ ahã bɔ ni ji oblayoo foro yinii kɛ̃.
18 “Akaŋmɛ yoo ŋkunyaayelɔ gbɛ ni ehi jeŋ.
19 “Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni kɛ kooloo aaawɔ lɛ esa akɛ agbe lɛ.
20 “Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaashi Yehowa sɛɛ ni eeeyashã afɔle ehã nyɔŋmɔ kroko ko yɛ Yehowa sɛɛ lɛ akpãtã ehiɛ butubutu.
21 “Akaye gbɔ sane ni ejaaa, ni akawa lɛ yi ejaakɛ nyɛ hu nyɛyatsɔ̃mɔ gbɔi yɛ Ijipt dã. 22 Akawa yoo okulafo loo awusa yi. 23Kɛji awa amɛ yi, ni amɛfo amɛtsɛ mi lɛ, ja mibo amɛyaafo toi. 24Mimlifu naa aaawa naakpa, ni magbe nyɛ yɛ ta mli, ni nyɛŋamɛi aaatsɔ̃mɔ okulafoi, ni nyɛbii aaatsɔ̃mɔ awusai.
25 “Kɛji ofa mimaŋbii ni kɛ bo yɔɔ lɛ ateŋ ohiafo ko shika lɛ, kaaye lɛ wie, ni kaahe hekpa hu. 26 Kɛji eeeba lɛ po akɛ onaanyo kɛ ehebo aaato bo awaba lɛ, okɛ ehebo lɛ aku sɛɛ ohã lɛ dani hulu ayanyɔ shi, 27ejaakɛ no pɛ ji nɔ ni ekɛhaa ehe, ehewolo nɔ mama ni. Mɛni eha kɛwɔ? Kɛji efo etsɛ mi lɛ mabo lɛ toi ejaakɛ mɔbɔnalɔ ji mi.
28 “Kaawie oshi Nyɔŋmɔ, ni kaalomɔ maŋ onukpa.
29 “Kɛji oŋmɔshi nii ba, ni kɛ oŋa owain kɛ omu lɛ, kaashashao shi ni okɛ Nyɔŋmɔ nɔ lɛ abahã lɛ. Jɔɔmɔ obihii ateŋ kromɔ lɛ nɔ ohã mi. 30 Nakai nɔŋŋ hu ofee otsinai kɛ toi. Kooloo kromɔ nuu lɛ ehi enyɛ masɛi gbii kpawo, ni gbi ni ji kpaanyɔ lɛ ojɔɔ enɔ ohã mi.
31“Nyɛaatsɔ̃ mɛi krɔŋkrɔŋ nyɛhã mi. No hewɔ lɛ, loo ni ŋaŋ kooloo etserɛ lɛ lɛ nyɛkayea, ashɛrɛ ashwie ahã gbei.

english_text:
Equal Justice for All
The Lord said:
1 Don't spread harmful rumors or help a criminal by giving false evidence.
2Always tell the truth in court, even if everyone else is dishonest and stands in the way of justice. 3 And don't favor the poor, simply because they are poor.
4 If you find an ox or a donkey that has wandered off, take it back where it belongs, even if the owner is your enemy.
5If a donkey is overloaded and falls down, you must do what you can to help, even if it belongs to someone who doesn't like you.
6 Make sure that the poor are given equal justice in court. 7Don't bring false charges against anyone or sentence an innocent person to death. I won't forgive you if you do.
8Don't accept bribes. Judges are blinded and justice is twisted by bribes.
9 Don't mistreat foreigners. You were foreigners in Egypt, and you know what it is like.
Laws for the Sabbath
The Lord said:
10 Plant and harvest your crops for six years, 11but let the land rest during the seventh year. The poor are to eat what they want from your fields, vineyards, and olive trees during that year, and when they have all they want from your fields, leave the rest for wild animals.
12 Work the first six days of the week, but rest and relax on the seventh day. This law is not only for you, but for your oxen, donkeys, and slaves, as well as for any foreigners among you.
13Make certain that you obey everything I have said. Don't pray to other gods or even mention their names.
Three Annual Festivals
(Exodus 34.18-26; Deuteronomy 16.1-17)
The Lord said:
14Celebrate three festivals each year in my honor.
15 Celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread by eating bread made without yeast, just as I have commanded. Do this at the proper time during the month of Abib, because it is the month when you left Egypt. And make certain that everyone brings the proper offerings.
16 Celebrate the Harvest Festival each spring when you start harvesting your wheat, and celebrate the Festival of Shelters each autumn when you pick your fruit.
17Your men must come to these three festivals each year to worship me.
18Do not offer bread made with yeast when you sacrifice an animal to me. And make sure that the fat of the animal is burned that same day.
19 Each year bring the best part of your first harvest to the place of worship.
Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
A Promise and a Warning
The Lord said:
20I am sending an angel to protect you and to lead you into the land I have ready for you. 21Carefully obey everything the angel says, because I am giving him complete authority, and he won't tolerate rebellion. 22If you faithfully obey him, I will be a fierce enemy of your enemies. 23My angel will lead you into the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will wipe them out. 24Don't worship their gods or follow their customs. Instead, destroy their idols and shatter their stone images.
25Worship only me, the Lord your God! I will bless you with plenty of food and water and keep you strong. 26Your women will give birth to healthy children, and everyone will live a long life.
27I will terrify those nations and make your enemies so confused that they will run from you. 28I will make the Hivites, Canaanites, and Hittites panic as you approach. 29But I won't do all this in the first year, because the land would become poor, and wild animals would be everywhere. 30Instead, I will force out your enemies little by little and give your nation time to grow strong enough to take over the land.
31I will see that your borders reach from the Red Sea to the Euphrates River and from the Mediterranean Sea to the desert. I will let you defeat the people who live there, and you will force them out of the land. 32But you must not make any agreements with them or with their gods. 33Don't let them stay in your land. They will trap you into sinning against me and worshiping their gods.
translation_text:
Jalɛ saneyeli
1 “Kaawie nɔ ni bɛ mli. Kaafi gbɔmɔ fɔŋ sɛɛ kɛmiiye kutumpɔo odase. 2Kaanyiɛ mɛi ni yi fa sɛɛ kɛyafee efɔŋ, ni kaanyiɛ nɔ ni mɛi pii kɛɔ sɛɛ ni okɛɛ nɔ ko ni aaahã atsɔ sane hiɛ abu shi, 3 asaŋ kaasaa ohiafo sane he ohã lɛ yɛ saneyeli mli.
4 “Kɛji ona ohenyɛlɔ tsina loo teji ni edu gbɛ lɛ kplamɔ lɛ obahã lɛ. 5Kɛ oyanina mɔ ni kɛ bo yeee kɛ eteji ni teji lɛ jatsu tsii fe lɛ lɛ, kwɛmɔ ni okaho amɛhe otee, shi moŋ ye obua nɔtsɛ lɛ koni awo kooloo lɛ nɔ adamɔ shi.
6 “Kaatsɔ̃ ohiafo sane hiɛ obu shi yɛ saneyeli mli. 7Kaafo sane ofɔ̃ mɔ nɔ, ni kaagbe jalɔ kɛ mɔ ni he bɛ sane ko mli ejaakɛ mihaŋ efɔŋfeelɔ aye ehe kɔkɔɔkɔ. 8 Kaahe nyɔɔŋnii ejaakɛ nyɔɔŋnii shwilaa nɔkwɛlɔ, ni efiteɔ mɔ ni sane ja sane.
9 “Nyɛkawaa gbɔ yi, akɛ ni nyɛle bɔ ni gbɔ tsui nuɔ nii ahe ehãa lɛ, ejaakɛ nyɛ hu nyɛyatsɔ̃mɔ gbɔi yɛ Ijipt dã.”
Afi ni ji kpawo lɛ kɛ gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ
10 “Ahu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni akpa enɔ nibaanii lɛ kɛyashi afii ekpaa; 11shi afi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ ahã shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe ni ekã shi efolo koni omaŋ lɛ mli ohiafoi lɛ ana enɔ nii amɛkɔlɔ amɛye, ni nɔ ni aaashwɛ lɛ ŋaŋ kooloi hu ana aye. Nakai nɔŋŋ ofee owain trom kɛ omutso trom.
12 “Otsu nii gbi ekpaa, shi gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ okɛjɔɔ ohe, bɔ ni afee ni otsina kɛ oteji ajɔɔ amɛhe, ni nyɔŋ yoo bi kɛ ogbɔ awo amɛtsui.
13“Nibii fɛɛ ni mikɛɛ nyɛ lɛ nyɛyea nɔ. Nyɛkatsĩa nyɔŋmɔi krokomɛi agbɛii ata, akanu yɛ nyɛnaa tete.”
Gbii juji etɛ̃ lɛ
(Ɛksodɔs 34.18-26; Deuteronomio 16.1-17)
14“Daa afi lɛ nyɛyea gbii juji etɛ̃ nyɛhãa mi. 15 Nyɛyea Akpiti Gbijurɔ lɛ. Bɔ ni miwo nyɛ ehe kitã lɛ, nyɛyea aboloo ni akɛ mã akpiti shã. Nyɛyea lɛ gbii kpawo yɛ be ni ato lɛ, ni ji Abib nyɔɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ no nɔ nyɛshi Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No be lɛ mli lɛ mɔ ko akaba mi jamɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ edɛŋ afɔle.
16“Nyɛyea Nikpamɔ Gbijurɔ lɛ ni ji ŋmɔshinii lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ yibii agbijurɔ lɛ; ni nyɛyea Ŋmaa naabuamɔ kɛtoo Gbijurɔ lɛ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee mli, be ni nyɛbuaa ŋmɔshi nii anaa nyɛtoɔ lɛ. 17Daa afi lɛ nyɛteŋ nuu fɛɛ nuu abaja Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ shii etɛ̃ yɛ nɛkɛ gbii juji etɛ̃ nɛɛ anɔ.
18 “Kooloo ni akɛbaashã afɔle ahã mi lɛ, nyɛkɛ masha aboloo akafataa he; ni kooloo ni akɛshã afɔle ahã mi lɛ, nyɛkahãa je miitsɛre emli fɔ lɛ nɔ.
19 “Klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshinii ni nyɛbaakpa lɛ nyɛkɛbaa Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, we lɛ. Akahoo toobi kɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ enyɛ fufɔ mli nu.”
Shiwoi kɛ akpɔi
20 “Naa, miwo bɔfo gbɛ ni enyiɛ nyɛhiɛ koni ebaa nyɛyi yɛ gbɛteŋ koni ekɛ nyɛ ayashɛ he ni misaa mito lɛ. 21Nyɛkwɛa ni ahia yɛ egbɛfaŋ, ni nyɛyea ewiemɔ nɔ. Nyɛkatsea ehiɛ atua; ekɛ ewiemɔ lɛ nɔtɔmɔ ekeŋ nyɛ, ejaakɛ ehiɛ mihewalɛ. 22Shi kɛji nyɛye egbee nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni nyɛfee nɔ ni mikɛɛ nyɛ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ matsɔ̃ henyɛlɔ mahã nyɛhenyɛlɔi, ni mikɛ mɛi ni kɛ nyɛ tswaa baatswa. 23Mibɔfo lɛ aaanyiɛ nyɛhiɛ kɛyanina Amorbii lɛ kɛ Hitbii lɛ kɛ Perizbii lɛ kɛ Kanaanbii lɛ kɛ Hivbii lɛ kɛ Yebusbii lɛ, ni makpãtã amɛhiɛ butubutu. 24 Nyɛkajaa ni nyɛkasɔ̃mɔa amɛnyɔŋmɔi lɛ, asaŋ nyɛkakasea gbɔmɛi nɛɛ anifeemɔ nii hu, shi moŋ nyɛbutua amɛnyɔŋmɔi lɛ, ni nyɛkumɔa amɛshiui lɛ butubutu nyɛshwiea shi. 25 Kɛji nyɛsɔ̃mɔ mi, Yehowa nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, madro nyɛ niyenii kɛ nu, ni makɔ hela yɛ nyɛteŋ mashɛ mafɔ̃ kwraa. 26Yoo sharakeŋ, ni anaŋ yoo kene yɛ nyɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mahã nyɛwala sɛɛ atsɛ.
27“Mahã miheŋmiŋmi atsɔ̃ nyɛhiɛ amɔmɔ maji lɛ fɛɛ dani nyɛaayanina amɛ, ni maŋ fɛɛ maŋ nɔ ni nyɛaashɛ lɛ aaajija yɛ nyɛhiɛ. 28 Matsu sosomootii kɛaatsɔ̃ nyɛhiɛ. Mashwie Hivbii lɛ kɛ Kanaanbii lɛ kɛ Hitbii lɛ yɛ nyɛhiɛ. 29Shi moŋ mishwieŋ amɛ yɛ nyɛhiɛ yɛ afi kome nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akabatsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃, koni ŋaŋ kooloi ayi bafa yɛ nɔ wo nyɛ. 30Fiofio mibashwie amɛ yɛ nyɛhiɛ kɛyaashi beyinɔ ni nyɛyi aaafa, ni nyɛaaŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. 31 Mafo husu mahã nyɛ kɛjɛ Ŋshɔ Tsuru lɛ naa kɛyashi Filistibii lɛ aŋshɔ lɛ naa, agbɛnɛ kɛjɛ shiaŋa lɛ nɔ kɛyashi Eufrate Faa lɛ naa, ejaakɛ mahã nyɛye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii lɛ anɔ kunim koni nyɛshwie amɛ. 32 Amɛ gbɔmɛi lɛ jio, amɛnyɔŋmɔi lɛ jio, nyɛkɛ amɛ akakpãŋa kpãŋmɔ ko. 33 Nyɛkahãa amɛhia shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛmiihã nyɛfee esha nyɛshi mi. Ejaakɛ kɛji nyɛsɔ̃mɔ amɛnyɔŋmɔi lɛ, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ eeetsɔ̃ tsɔne ehã nyɛ.”

english_text:
The People Agree To Obey God
1The Lord said to Moses, “Come up to me on this mountain. Bring along Aaron, as well as his two sons Nadab and Abihu, and 70 of Israel's leaders. They must worship me at a distance, 2but you are to come near. Don't let anyone else come up.”
3Moses gave the Lord's instructions to the people, and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded!” 4Then Moses wrote down what the Lord had said.
The next morning Moses got up early. He built an altar at the foot of the mountain and set up a large stone for each of the twelve tribes of Israel. 5He also sent some young men to burn offerings and to sacrifice bulls as special offerings to the Lord. 6Moses put half of the blood from the animals into bowls and sprinkled the rest on the altar. 7Then he read aloud the Lord's commands and promises, and the people shouted, “We will obey the Lord and do everything he has commanded!”
8 Moses took the blood from the bowls and sprinkled it on the people. Next, he told them, “With this blood the Lord makes his agreement with you.”
9Moses and Aaron, together with Nadab and Abihu and the 70 leaders, went up the mountain 10and saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was something that looked like a pavement made out of sapphire, and it was as bright as the sky.
11Even though these leaders of Israel saw God, he did not punish them. So they ate and drank.
Moses on Mount Sinai
12The Lord said to Moses, “Come up on the mountain and stay here for a while. I will give you the two flat stones on which I have written the laws that my people must obey.” 13Moses and Joshua his assistant got ready, then Moses started up the mountain to meet with God.
14Moses had told the leaders, “Wait here until we come back. Aaron and Hur will be with you, and they can settle any arguments while we are away.”
15When Moses went up on Mount Sinai, a cloud covered it, 16and the bright glory of the Lord came down and stayed there. The cloud covered the mountain for six days, and on the seventh day the Lord told Moses to come into the cloud. 17-18 Moses did so and stayed there 40 days and nights. To the people, the Lord's glory looked like a blazing fire on top of the mountain.
translation_text:
Asɔo Kpãŋmɔ lɛ naa
1 Ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Bo kɛ Aaron kɛ Nadab kɛ Abihu kɛ Israel onukpai lɛ ateŋ mɛi nyɔŋmai kpawo akwɔ gɔŋ lɛ kɛba miŋɔɔ koni nyɛbaja yɛ sɛɛ flɛŋŋ. 2Mose, okome pɛ otsi obɛŋkɛ Yehowa; mɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ akatsi amɛbɛŋkɛ, ni maŋbii lɛ hu kɛ bo akakwɔ kɛmiiba.”
3 Mose ba ni ebajaje Yehowa wiemɔi lɛ kɛ akpɔi lɛ fɛɛ etsɔ̃ɔ maŋ lɛ. Ni maŋ lɛ fɛɛ here nɔ kɛ gbee kome amɛkɛɛ, “Wiemɔi fɛɛ ni Yehowa ewie lɛ wɔɔye nɔ.” 4 Mose ŋmala Yehowa wiemɔi lɛ fɛɛ eshwie shi. Kɛkɛ ni ete shi leebi maŋkpa, ni ema afɔleshãa latɛ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ shishi, ni ehole tɛi nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ edamɔ shi yɛ Israel akutsei nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ lɛ anaa. 5 Ni etsu Israelbii lɛ ateŋ oblahii komɛi, ni amɛkɛ tsina hii yashã afɔle kɛ shidaa afɔle amɛhã Yehowa. 6Mose kɛ lá lɛ fã wo lalakãi amli, ni lá lɛ fã ni shwɛ lɛ efɔ̃ eshwie afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he. 7 Agbɛnɛ ekɔ kpãŋmɔ wolo lɛ, ni ekane yɛ maŋbii lɛ atoiŋ. Kɛkɛ ni maŋbii lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Nii fɛɛ ni Yehowa ekɛɛ lɛ wɔɔfee, ni wɔɔbo lɛ toi.”
8 Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Mose wo lá lɛ, ni ekɛshwã maŋbii lɛ anɔ, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Naa, kpãŋmɔ ni Yehowa kɛ nyɛ ekpãŋ yɛ nɛkɛ wiemɔi nɛɛ fɛɛ he lɛ nɔ lá nɛ.”
9Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛ Aaron kɛ Nadab kɛ Abihu kɛ Israel onukpai nyɔŋmai kpawo lɛ kwɔ gɔŋ lɛ kɛtee, 10 ni amɛyana Israel Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ. Amɛna ni enanemaahei lɛ efee tamɔ he ko ni akɛ safiro tɛ eka; safiro tɛ nɛɛ mlitsemɔ lɛ enɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ. 11 Nyɔŋmɔ efeee Israel onukpai nɛɛ nɔ fɔŋ ko, shi amɛna Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ amɛhiŋmɛi, ni amɛye nii ni amɛnu nɔ ko.
Mose yɛ Sinai Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ
12Ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, “Kwɔɔ kɛba miŋɔɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni obamɛ, ni mikɛ tɛi tɛtɛrɛbii ni maŋmala mlai lɛ kɛ kitãi lɛ yɛ nɔ lɛ baahã bo, ni okɛtsɔ̃ɔ maŋ lɛ nii.” 13Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛ etsulɔ Yoshua te shi, ni Mose kwɔ kɛtee Nyɔŋmɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ. 14Shi ekɛɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛhia biɛ nyɛmɛa wɔ kɛyashi beyinɔ ni wɔɔku wɔsɛɛ kɛba. Aaron kɛ Hur kɛ nyɛ yɛ biɛ. Kɛji mɔ ko hiɛ sane ko lɛ akɛyahã amɛ.”
15Kɛkɛ ni agbɛnɛ Mose kwɔ gɔŋ lɛ kɛtee eyiteŋ, ni atatu lɛ baha gɔŋ lɛ nɔ. 16 Ni Yehowa anunyam la lɛ kpeleke shi kɛba Sinai gɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Atatu lɛ ye gbii ekpaa ni eha gɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ Yehowa jɛ atatu lɛ mli etsɛ Mose. 17 Yehowa anunyam lɛ, kɛji Israelbii lɛ miikwɛ lɛ, amɛnaa lɛ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ tamɔ la grigri ni kpãtãa nii ahiɛ. 18 Mose kwɔ gɔŋ lɛ, ni ebote atatu lɛ mli. Eye nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ kɛ shwaneshwane gbii nyɔŋmai ejwɛ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_text:
The Sacred Tent
(Exodus 35.4-9)
1The Lord said to Moses:
2Tell everyone in Israel who wants to give gifts that they must bring them to you. 3Here is a list of what you are to collect: Gold, silver, and bronze; 4blue, purple, and red wool; fine linen; goat hair; 5tanned ram skins; fine leather; acacia wood; 6olive oil for the lamp; sweet-smelling spices to mix with the incense and with the oil for dedicating the tent and ordaining the priests; 7and onyx stones and other gems for the sacred vest and the breastpiece. 8I also want them to build a special place where I can live among my people. 9Make it and its furnishings exactly like the pattern I will show you.
The Sacred Chest
(Exodus 37.1-9)
The Lord said to Moses:
10Tell the people to build a chest of acacia wood 110 centimeters long, 66 centimeters wide, and 66 centimeters high. 11Cover it inside and out with pure gold and put a gold edging around the lid. 12Make four gold rings and attach one of them to each of the four legs of the chest. 13Make two poles of acacia wood. Cover them with gold 14and put them through the rings, so the chest can be carried by the poles. 15Don't ever remove the poles from the rings. 16When I give you the Ten Commandments written on two flat stones, put them inside the chest.
17 Make the lid of the chest out of pure gold. 18-19Then hammer out two winged creatures of pure gold and fasten them to the lid at the ends of the chest. 20The creatures must face each other with their wings spread over the chest. 21Inside it place the two flat stones with the Ten Commandments on them and put the gold lid on top of the chest. 22I will meet you there between the two creatures and tell you what my people must do and what they must not do.
The Table for the Sacred Bread
(Exodus 37.10-16)
The Lord said:
23Make a table of acacia wood 88 centimeters long, 44 centimeters wide, and 66 centimeters high. 24-25Cover it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it with a border 75 millimeters thick. 26Make four gold rings and attach one to each of the legs 27-28near the edging. The poles for carrying the table are to be placed through these rings and are to be made of acacia wood covered with gold. 29-30 The table is to be kept in the holy place, and the sacred loaves of bread must always be on it. All bowls, plates, jars, and cups for wine offerings are to be made of pure gold and set on this table.
The Lampstand
(Exodus 37.17-24)
The Lord said:
31Make a lampstand of pure gold. The whole lampstand, including its decorative flowers, must be made from a single piece of hammered gold 32with three branches on each of its two sides. 33There are to be three decorative almond blossoms on each branch 34and four on the stem. 35There must also be a blossom where each pair of branches comes out from the stem. 36The lampstand, including its branches and decorative flowers, must be made from a single piece of hammered pure gold. 37The lamp on the top and those at the end of each of its six branches must be made so as to shine toward the front of the lampstand. 38The tongs and trays for taking care of the lamps are to be made of pure gold. 39The lampstand and its equipment will require 35 kilograms of pure gold, 40 and they must be made according to the pattern I showed you on the mountain.
translation_text:
Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ he nikee nii
(Ɛksodɔs 35.4-9)
1Ni Yehowa kɛɛ Mose akɛ, 2 “Bi Israelbii lɛ koni amɛkɛ nikee nii aba. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ he tsui akɛ ehã lɛ, lɛ edɛŋ nikee nii nyɛhea nyɛhãa mi. 3Ni nikee nii ni amɛkɛba lɛ nɛ: shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi kɛ akɔɔble, 4kɛ kuŋtu bluu kɛ kuŋtu afaseo kɛ kuŋtu tsuru fɔɔ kɛ klala kɛ abotia he tsɔi, 5kɛ ojwɛni wolo ni awo lɛ tsofa tsuru kɛ nuŋgbee he wolo kɛ tso. 6Ekrokomɛi hu ji mu ni akɛsuɔ kane, kɛ tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ mu ni akɛfɔɔ mɔ mu mli lɛ. Ekomɛi hu ji tsofai ni akɛfeɔ tsofakɛŋma ni ashãa. 7Abake oniketɛi ni akɛbaamamɔ osɔfonukpa lɛ tsitsinɔhaa nii lɛ kɛ ehewulamɔ nii lɛ eko ni atsɛɔ lɛ efod lɛ amli lɛ. 8Ohã Israelbii lɛ afee Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ ko amɛhã mi koni mahi amɛteŋ. 9 Bɔ ni matsɔ̃ɔ bo Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ su kɛ ehe nibii lɛ fɛɛ hu asu lɛ, nyɛfea lɛ nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ.
Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ
(Ɛksodɔs 37.1-9)
10“Ohã amɛkpɛ tso adeka. Ekɛlɛ afee ninetalɔi enyɔ kɛ fã, ni elɛɛmɔ afee ninetalɔ kome kɛ fã, ni ekwɔlɛ afee ninetalɔ kome kɛ fã. 11Ashwie adeka lɛ mli kɛ ehe fɛɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi, ni akɛ shika abaŋ adeka lɛ naa fɛɛ kɛkpe kpula. 12Ashwie shika gai ejwɛ ato adeka lɛ koji ejwɛ lɛ. Gai enyɔ aye afã kome, ni enyɔ hu aye afã kome lɛ. 13Akɛ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ eko agbɔlɔ tsei bloblobii ni ashwie amɛhe shika. 14Akɛ tsei nɛɛ ahɔlɔ gai ni yɔɔ adeka lɛ ŋmawuiaŋ biɛ kɛ biɛ lɛ amli koni akɛwo. 15Tsei lɛ ahɔlɔ gai lɛ amli, akajie yɛ mli. 16Okɛ odaseyeli tɛi lɛ ni mikɛbaahã bo lɛ awo Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ mli.
17 “Okɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi afee adeka lɛ naanɔ lɛ. Ekɛlɛ afee ninetalɔi enyɔ kɛ fã, ni elɛɛmɔ afee ninetalɔ kome kɛ fã. 18Otswia shika, ni okɛfee kerubim enyɔ omamɔ naanɔ lɛ nɔ koji lɛ anɔ. 19Kerub kome yɛ koŋ kome kɛ ekome hu yɛ koŋ kome lɛ. Sɔomɔ kerubim nɛɛ okpɛtɛ naanɔ lɛ koji enyɔ lɛ. 20Kerubim lɛ agbɛ amɛfiji amli kɛya ŋwɛi ni amɛkɛha naanɔ lɛ nɔ, ni kerub kome akwɛ kerub kome hiɛ, asaŋ amɛmamɔ amɛhiɛ shi amɛkwɛ naanɔ lɛ nɔ. 21 Okɛ odaseyeli tɛi lɛ ni mikɛbaahã bo lɛ awo Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ mli koni okɛ naanɔ lɛ abu naa. 22 Gbɛ ni kã kerubim enyɔ lɛ ateŋ yɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ naanɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsɔ̃ mi kɛ bo kpeehe, ni jɛi majɛ mi kɛ bo aaawie nibii fɛɛ ni mifã bo akɛ okɛɛ Israelbii lɛ.
Okplɔ̃ ni akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ Aboloo lɛ maa nɔ lɛ
(Ɛksodɔs 37.10-16)
23“Okɛ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ eko akpɛ okplɔ̃. Ekɛlɛ afee ninetalɔ kome kɛ fã. 24Oshwie ehe shika ŋmiiŋmi, ni ekoji lɛ okɛ shika abaŋ naa fɛɛ kpula kɛkpe. 25Ogbɔ tso blawa ni elɛɛmɔ tamɔ dɛ̃ lɛɛmɔ koni okɛkpɛtɛ okplɔ̃ lɛ toi kɛbɔle lɛ kɛkpe, ni okɛ shika abaŋ tso blawa nɛɛ naa kpula. 26Feemɔ shika gai ejwɛ okɛwo okplɔ̃ lɛ naji ejwɛ lɛ ahe. 27Gai nɛɛ aye tso blawa lɛ shishi tuuŋtu, ni nomɛi amli akɛ tsei bloblobii ni akɛbaawo okplɔ̃ lɛ ahɔlɔ. 28Okɛ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ eko agbɔlɔ tsei nɛɛ, ni oshwie he shika koni akɛwo okplɔ̃ lɛ. 29Okɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi afee okplɔ̃ lɛ he plɛtei kɛ tsɛnsii ni akɛ tsofakɛŋma baawo amɛmli lɛ, kɛ agbɛnɛ okpolui kɛ kpuji ni akɛbaaye ŋkpai lɛ. 30 Ni okɛ aboloo ni akɛmaa mihiɛ lɛ ama okplɔ̃ lɛ nɔ yɛ mihiɛ daa.
Kanetso lɛ
(Ɛksodɔs 37.17-24)
31“Okɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi ni atswia afee kanetso. Otswia shika ŋmiiŋmi kɛfee eshimaatso lɛ kɛ eshishi nii ni ema nɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Ehe tɔi lɛ kɛ ehe kpɔbii lɛ kɛ ehe fɔfɔi samai lɛ fɛɛ atsa akɛ nɔ muu kome. 32Kanetso lɛ ahiɛ niji ekpaa, niji etɛ̃ aye afã kome nɛɛ, ni niji etɛ̃ hu aye afã kome nɛɛ. 33Afã kome ahiɛ tɔi etɛ̃ ni afee amɛ tamɔ ŋmɛi; tɔ fɛɛ tɔ kɛ ekpɔ kɛ efɔfɔi sama yɛ nine kome he, ni afã kome lɛ hu ahiɛ tɔi etɛ̃ tamɔ ŋmɛi, tɔ fɛɛ tɔ kɛ ekpɔ kɛ efɔfɔi sama yɛ nine kome he. Nakai sɔŋŋ afee niji ekpaa lɛ fɛɛ ni kanetso lɛ egbala lɛ. 34Kanetso lɛ shimaatso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ, ena tɔi ejwɛ ni tamɔ ŋmɛi kɛ amɛhe kpɔbii kɛ fɔfɔi samai. 35Ni kpɔi amãmɔ kanetso lɛ hu niji ntai enyɔnyɔɔnyɔ lɛ ashishi yɛ shimaatso lɛ he, ni tsɔ̃ɔ akɛ niji ekpaa lɛ ateŋ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ kpɔ yɛ eshishi. 36Amɛhe tɔi lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi samai lɛ kɛ shimaatso lɛ fɛɛ atsa akɛ nɔ muu kome, ni akɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi atswia fɛɛ. 37Ofee kanei kpawo omamɔ kanetso lɛ nɔ, koni kɛji asu lɛ amɛkpɛ kɛya hiɛgbɛ. 38Kanetso lɛ he abɛɛlei lɛ kɛ ehe lagbee nii lɛ akɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi afee. 39Aŋmɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi talenta kome koni akɛfee kanetso lɛ kɛ ehe nibii nɛɛ fɛɛ. 40 Kwɛmɔ ni ofee nibii nɛɛ fɛɛ bɔ ni mikɛtsɔ̃ɔ bo yɛ gɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.”

english_text:
Curtains and Coverings for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 36.8-19)
The Lord said to Moses:
1The top of the sacred tent must be made from ten pieces of the finest linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. 2Make each piece twelve meters long and two meters wide 3and sew them together into two panels with five sections each. 4-6Put 50 loops of blue cloth along one of the wider sides of each panel, then fasten the two panels at the loops with 50 gold hooks.
7-8As the material for protecting the tent, use goat hair to weave eleven sections of cloth 13 meters by 2 meters each. 9Sew five of the sections together to make one panel. Then sew the other six together to make a second panel, and fold the sixth section double over the front of the tent. 10Put 50 loops along one of the wider sides of each panel 11and fasten the two panels at the loops with 50 bronze hooks. 12-13The panel of goat hair will be a meter longer than the tent itself, so fold 50 centimeters of the material behind the tent and on each side as a protective covering. 14Make two more coverings—one with tanned ram skins and the other with fine leather.
The Framework for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 36.20-34)
The Lord said:
15Build a framework of acacia wood for the walls of the sacred tent. 16Make each frame 4 meters high and 66 centimeters wide 17with two wooden pegs near the bottom. 18-21Place two silver stands under each frame with sockets for the pegs, so the frames can be joined together. Put 20 of these frames along the south side and 20 more along the north. 22For the back wall along the west side use six frames 23-24with two more at the southwest and northwest corners. Make certain that these corner frames are joined from top to bottom. 25Altogether, this back wall will have eight frames with two silver stands under each one.
26-27Make five crossbars for each of the wooden frames, 28with the center crossbar running the full length of the wall. 29Cover the frames and the crossbars with gold and attach gold rings to the frames to run the crossbars through. 30Then set up the tent in the way I showed you on the mountain.
The Curtain inside the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 36.35-38)
The Lord said:
31-33 Make a curtain to separate the holy place from the most holy place. Use fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. Cover four acacia wood posts with gold and set them each on a silver stand. Then fasten gold hooks to the posts and hang the curtain there.
34Inside the most holy place, put the sacred chest that has the place of mercy on its lid. 35Outside the most holy place, as you face the curtain, put the table for the sacred bread on the right side and the gold lampstand on the left.
36For the entrance to the tent, use a piece of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with fancy needlework. 37Cover five acacia wood posts with gold and set them each on a bronze stand. Then put gold hooks on the posts and hang the curtain there.
translation_text:
Yehowa Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ
(Ɛksodɔs 36.8-38)
1“Okɛ mamai nyɔŋma ni alo kɛ klala yɛŋ futaa kɛ kuŋtu bluu kɛ kuŋtu afaseo kɛ kuŋtu tsuru fɔɔ ni anyɛne afee Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ. Alo kerubim awo mli. 2Mama kome kɛlɛ afee ninetalɔi nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ kpaanyɔ, ni elɛɛmɔ afee ninetalɔi ejwɛ. Mamai lɛ fɛɛ adaramɔ afee ekome. 3Okpɛ mamai lɛ enumɔ otsara, eko tsa eko naa, kɛfee mama muu kome, ni okpɛ enumɔ krokomɛi lɛ hu otsara, eko tsa eko naa, nakai nɔŋŋ kɛfee mama muu kome. 4Okɛ kpãa bluu aŋmɔlɔ aflãi owo mama muu kome naa, ni ofee mama muu kroko lɛ hu nakai nɔŋŋ. 5Oŋmɔlɔ aflãi nɛɛ nyɔŋmai enumɔ yɛ mama muu kome naa kɛ aflãi nyɔŋmai enumɔ hu yɛ mama muu kroko lɛ naa. 6Ofee kpoji nyɔŋmai enumɔ koni okɛlala mamai enyɔ lɛ anaabui lɛ otsara Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ mama lɛ koni etsɔ̃ nɔ muu kome.
7“Okɛ abotia he tsɔi afee mamai nyɔŋma kɛ ekome okɛha Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ nɔ. 8Mama kome kɛlɛ afee ninetalɔi nyɔŋmai etɛ̃, ni elɛɛmɔ afee ninetalɔi ejwɛ. Mamai nyɔŋma kɛ ekome nɛɛ fɛɛ adaramɔ afee ekome. 9Otsara mamai enumɔ aŋklo kɛ mamai ekpaa hu aŋklo. Mama ni ji ekpaa ni baaye buu lɛ hiɛ lɛ odɔ mli enyɔ. 10Oŋmɔlɔ aflãi nyɔŋmai enumɔ yɛ mamai enumɔ ni otsara lɛ aŋklo lɛ naa, kɛ aflãi nyɔŋmai enumɔ hu yɛ mamai ekpaa ni otsara lɛ aŋklo lɛ naa. 11Ofee akɔɔble kpoji nyɔŋmai enumɔ koni okɛlala aflãi lɛ, ni okɛtsara buu mama lɛ koni efee nɔ muu kome. 12Buu mama ni shwɛɔ lɛ, ni ji mama fã lɛ ni dɛŋ nɔ lɛ, odɔ ofɔ̃ nɔ koni ekã nɔ yɛ Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ sɛɛgbɛ. 13Ni buu mamai lɛ akɛlɛ mli ninetalɔ kome ni dɛŋɔ nɔ yɛ afã kome nɛɛ, kɛ ninetalɔ kome hu ni dɛŋɔ nɔ yɛ afã kroko lɛ, ebɔ nɔ koni ekã Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ ŋmawuiaŋ biɛ kɛ biɛ koni eha Buu lɛ he.
14“Okɛ ojwɛni wolo ni awo lɛ tsofa tsuru aha buu lɛ nɔ, ni okɛ nuŋgbee wolo aha yiteŋ oto nɔ.
15“Okɛ tso afee Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ mplaŋi ni baamamɔ shi lɛ. 16Mplaŋ kome kɛlɛ afee ninetalɔi nyɔŋma, ni elɛɛmɔ afee ninetalɔ kome kɛ fã. 17Ojie nyanyɔji enyɔ yɛ mplaŋ fɛɛ mplaŋ he koni onyɛ okɛtsa eko kɛ eko. Bɔ ni omamɔ Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ mplaŋi lɛ fɛɛ nɛ: 18mplaŋi nyɔŋmai enyɔ aye Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ he ni ye wuoyigbɛ. 19Okɛ jwiɛtɛi afee nibii nyɔŋmai ejwɛ owo mplaŋi nyɔŋmai enyɔ lɛ ashishi koni amɛmamɔ nɔ. Mplaŋ fɛɛ mplaŋ ama enyɔ nɔ. 20Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ he ni ye kooyigbɛ lɛ, mplaŋi nyɔŋmai enyɔ aye jɛi, 21kɛ amɛshishi nibii nyɔŋmai ejwɛ ni enyɔ yɛ mplaŋ fɛɛ mplaŋ shishi. 22Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ sɛɛgbɛ, he ni ye kɛyaa anaigbɛ lɛ, mplaŋi ekpaa aye jɛi. 23Okɛ mplaŋi enyɔɔnyɔ ajie Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ sɛɛgbɛ koji enyɔ lɛ. 24Okɛ koŋ kome mplaŋi enyɔ lɛ abɔ he kɛkɛ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ; shi otsa amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ga lɛ yi. Nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni ofee koji enyɔ lɛ mplaŋi lɛ fɛɛ. 25No hewɔ lɛ, abaana mplaŋi kpaanyɔ yɛ sɛɛgbɛ nɛɛ kɛ amɛshishi jwiɛtɛi nibii nyɔŋma kɛ ekpaa ni amɛmamɔ nɔ, mplaŋ fɛɛ mplaŋ ama enyɔ nɔ.
26“Okɛ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ eko afee mlibɛlɛmɔ nii enumɔ ohã mplaŋi ni yɔɔ Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ ŋmawuiaŋ kome, 27ni mplaŋi ni yɔɔ ŋmawuiaŋ kome lɛ hu ana mlibɛlɛmɔ nii enumɔ; ni sɛɛgbɛ, ni ji anaigbɛ, mplaŋi lɛ ana mlibɛlɛmɔ nii enumɔ nakai nɔŋŋ. 28Ni mlibɛlɛmɔ nii ni baaye mplaŋi lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ekã shi emuu kɛjɛ koŋ kome kɛyagbe naa yɛ koŋ kome lɛ. 29 Okɛ shika aha mplaŋi lɛ ahe, ni okɛ shika nɔŋŋ afee gai ni akɛ mlibɛlɛmɔ nii lɛ baahɔlɔ mli lɛ; ni mlibɛlɛmɔ nii lɛ hu okɛ shika aha he. 30Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ bɔ ni ajie atsɔ̃ɔ bo yɛ gɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ, oma lɛ nakai nɔŋŋ.
31 “Okɛ kuŋtu ni alo kɛ kpãa bluu kɛ kpãa afaseo kɛ kpãa tsuru fɔɔ kɛ kpãa yɛŋ futafuta ni anyɛne afee muhɔɔ. Akɛ ŋaa alo kerubim awo muhɔɔ nɛɛ mli. 32Okɛ muhɔɔ lɛ atsotsoro kpoji anaa yɛ tso akulashiŋi ni aha amɛhe shika lɛ ahe. Akɛ shika afee kpoji lɛ, ni akulashiŋ lɛ amãmɔ jwiɛtɛi nibii ejwɛ anɔ. 33 Okɛ kpoji lɛ alala muhɔɔ lɛ kɛtsotsoro shi, ni okɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ abama muhɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni muhɔɔ lɛ afo He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ kɛ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ Fe Fɛɛ lɛ teŋ ahã nyɛ. 34 Okɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ naanɔ lɛ, ni ji kpãtãmɔ sɛi lɛ, abu naa yɛ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ Fe Fɛɛ lɛ. 35 Okɛ okplɔ̃ lɛ ama muhɔɔ lɛ hiɛ yɛ Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ mli kooyigbɛ, ni kanetso lɛ aye Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ mli wuoyigbɛ koni ekwɛ okplɔ̃ lɛ hiɛ.
36“Ni buu lɛ naa shinaa lɛ, okɛ mama ni akɛ kpãa bluu kɛ kpãa afaseo kɛ kpãa tsuru fɔɔ kɛ kpãa yɛŋ futafuta ni anyɛne elo, asaŋ ni akɛ abui elo nii awo mli afee. 37Ni okɛ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ eko afee akulashiŋi enumɔ ohã shinaa lɛ naa mama lɛ. Okɛ shika aha tsei nɛɛ ahe, ni owo amɛhe shika kpoji kɛ amɛshishi akɔɔble nibii ni amɛmamɔ nɔ.”

english_text:
The Altar for Offering Sacrifices
(Exodus 38.1-7)
The Lord said to Moses:
1Use acacia wood to build an altar 2.25 meters square and 1.34 meters high, 2and make each of the four top corners stick up like the horn of a bull. Then cover the whole altar with bronze, including the four horns. 3All the equipment for the altar must also be made of bronze—the pans for the hot ashes, the shovels, the sprinkling bowls, the meat forks, and the fire pans. 4-5Halfway up the altar build a ledge around it, and cover the bottom half of the altar with a decorative bronze grating. Then attach a bronze ring beneath the ledge at the four corners of the altar. 6-7Cover two acacia wood poles with bronze and put them through the rings for carrying the altar. 8Construct the altar in the shape of an open box, just as you were shown on the mountain.
The Courtyard around the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 38.9-20)
The Lord said:
9-15Surround the sacred tent with a courtyard 44 meters long on the south and north and 22 meters wide on the east and west. Use 20 bronze posts on bronze stands for the south and north and 10 for the west. Then hang a curtain of fine linen on the posts along each of these three sides by using silver hooks and rods.
Place three bronze posts on each side of the entrance at the east and hang a curtain 6.67 meters wide on each set of posts. 16Use four more of these posts for the entrance way, then hang on them an embroidered curtain of fine linen nine meters long and woven with blue, purple, and red wool.
17-18Make the curtains that surround the courtyard 2.25 meters high and hang them from the bronze posts with silver hooks and rods. 19Make the rest of the equipment for the sacred tent of bronze, including the pegs for the tent and for the curtain surrounding the courtyard.
The Oil for the Lamp in the Holy Place
(Leviticus 24.1-4)
The Lord said to Moses:
20Command the people of Israel to supply you with the purest olive oil. Do this so the lamp will keep burning 21in front of the curtain that separates the holy place from the most holy place, where the sacred chest is kept. Aaron and his sons are responsible for keeping the lamp burning every night in the sacred tent. The Israelites must always obey this command.
translation_text:
Afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ
(Ɛksodɔs 38.1-7)
1“Okɛ tso lɛ eko akpɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ. Ekɛlɛ afee ninetalɔi enumɔ kɛ elɛɛmɔ hu ninetalɔi enumɔ, ekɛlɛ kɛ elɛɛmɔ aye egbɔ; ekwɔlɛ afee ninetalɔi etɛ̃. 2Feemɔ akloŋtoi omamɔ ekoji ejwɛ lɛ anɔ. Akloŋtoi lɛ kɛ latɛ lɛ fɛɛ afee nɔ muu kome, ni okɛ akɔɔble aha latɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ he. 3Ofee latɛ lɛ he ŋɛsui ni akɛloo elamlu lɛ, asaŋ ofee ehe sofii kɛ ekpolui kɛ fakai kɛ lajee tsɛnsii hu. Okɛ akɔɔble afee nibii nɛɛ fɛɛ. 4Ofee akɔɔble ntaŋ, ni okɛ akɔɔble nɔŋŋ afee gai owo ntaŋ lɛ koji ejwɛ lɛ. 5Okɛ akɔɔble ntaŋ lɛ awo afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ mli ni eyakã latɛ lɛ teŋ tuuŋtu. 6Okɛ tso lɛ eko agbɔlɔ tsei bloblobii, ni oha amɛhe akɔɔble. 7Okɛ tsei nɛɛ ahɔlɔ gai lɛ amli yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ biɛ kɛ biɛ koni akɛwo. 8 Okɛ ŋmoŋmolo akpɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ, ni gbɛ ahi emli. Okpɛ latɛ lɛ bɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ajie atsɔ̃ɔ bo yɛ gɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ.”
Kpee Buu lɛ he afabaŋ lɛ
(Ɛksodɔs 38.9-20)
9“Ofee kpo owo Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ he. Ewuoyigbɛ lɛ akɛ klala kpakpa ni ekɛlɛ feɔ ninetalɔi oha afee muhɔɔ ahã jɛi. 10Amãmɔ muhɔɔ lɛ he akulashiŋi nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ amɛshishi akɔɔble nibii nyɔŋmai enyɔ koni amɛmamɔ nɔ. Akulashiŋi lɛ ahe kpoji lɛ kɛ mlibɛlɛmɔ nii lɛ akɛ jwiɛtɛi afee. 11Ni asaŋ kpo lɛ kɛlɛ nɔ yɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ hu, jɛi muhɔɔ lɛ kɛlɛ afee ninetalɔi oha. Akulashiŋi nyɔŋmai enyɔ nakai nɔŋŋ ahi jɛi kɛ amɛshishi nibii nyɔŋmai enyɔ ni amɛmamɔ nɔ.
