Kɛkɛ ni efɔse lá ni eshwɛ lɛ eshwie afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ koji ejwɛ lɛ he kɛkpe. 25Mose ŋɔ fɔ kɛ lei lɛ ni ewo fɔ lɛ kɛ fɔ fɛɛ ni ha mlinii kɛ mlɛbo lɛ ahe lɛ kɛ sabai enyɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ lɛ kɛ sɛɛ nanejurɔ lɛ. 26Kɛkɛ ni ekɔ aboloo kome yɛ mã akpiti kafu ni akɛmaa Yehowa hiɛ lɛ mli, kɛ aboloo kome ni mu yɔɔ mli kɛ akpãanɔɔ kome, ni ekɛshwie fɔ lɛ kɛ shuɔ jurɔ lɛ nɔ. 27Mose kɛ niyenii nɛɛ fɛɛ wo Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ adɛŋ; ni efɔ̃ kɛtee kɛba akɛ afɔle ni afɔ̃ɔ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ. 28Kɛkɛ ni Mose saa he niyenii lɛ yɛ Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ adɛŋ, ni eshã yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ eshi shãa afɔlei ni ashãa fɛɛ emuu lɛ anɔ. Eji osɔfowoo afɔle ni akɛ la shãa ahãa Yehowa, ni ejeɔ ŋma ewoɔ lɛ. 29Mose kɔ osɔfowoo too ojwɛni lɛ tsitsi lɛ, ni ekɛshã afɔle ehã Yehowa akɛ nɔkee nɔ titri ko. Mose ŋɔ osɔfowoo too ojwɛni tsitsi lɛ akɛ egbɛfaŋnɔ, tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa wo lɛ kitã lɛ.
30Mose ŋɔ mu ni akɛfɔɔ mɔ mu lɛ eko kɛ lá ni yɔɔ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ eko, ni ekɛshwã Aaron kɛ etadei lɛ kɛ ebihii lɛ kɛ amɛtadei lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Ekɛ enɛ fee Aaron kɛ etadei lɛ kɛ Aaron bihii lɛ kɛ amɛtadei lɛ fɛɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ ehã Yehowa.
31Mose kɛɛ Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ akɛ, “Nyɛkɛ loo lɛ ayaa Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ naa koni nyɛyahoa. Nyɛyea loo lɛ kɛ aboloo ni yɔ kafu ni akɛ osɔfowoo afɔlei toɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ yɛ jɛi nɔŋŋ. Nyɛyea tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa wo kitã akɛ, ‘Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ aye lɛ.’ 32Loo kɛ aboloo ni aaashwɛ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, nyɛshãa. 33Nyɛkajea Kpee Buu lɛ mli kɛyashi gbii kpawo ni akɛfeɔ nyɛ osɔfowoo kusum lɛ aaaho; ejaakɛ gbii kpawo akɛfeɔ osɔfowoo kusum lɛ. 34Nɔ ni afee ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ lɛ, Yehowa kɛɛ afee koni akɛjie nyɛhe esha kɛya. 35Nyɛhia Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ naa nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ kɛ shwaneshwane gbii kpawo koni nyɛkɛfee nɔ ni Yehowa efã akɛ afee lɛ. Kɛji nyɛfeee nakai lɛ, nyɛbaagboi. Nakai ji bɔ ni Yehowa wo mi kitã.” 36No hewɔ lɛ, Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ fee nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni Yehowa wo Mose he kitã lɛ.

english_text:
The First Sacrifices Offered by Aaron and His Sons
1Eight days later Moses called together Aaron, his sons, and Israel's leaders. 2Then he said to Aaron:
Find a young bull and a ram that have nothing wrong with them. Offer the bull to the Lord as a sacrifice for sin and the ram as a sacrifice to please him.
3Tell the people of Israel that they must offer sacrifices as well. They must offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin, and a bull and a ram as a sacrifice to please the Lord. The bull and the ram must be a year old and have nothing wrong with them. 4Then the people must offer a bull and a ram as a sacrifice to ask the Lord's blessing and also a grain sacrifice mixed with oil. Do this, because the Lord will appear to you today.
5After the animals and the grain had been brought to the front of the sacred tent, and the people were standing there in the presence of the Lord, 6Moses said:
The Lord has ordered you to do this, so that he may appear to you in all of his glory. 7 Aaron, step up to the altar and offer the sacrifice to please the Lord, then offer the sacrifices for the forgiveness of your sins and for the sins of the people, just as the Lord has commanded.
8Aaron stepped up to the altar and killed the bull that was to be the sacrifice for his sins. 9His sons brought him the blood. He dipped a finger in it, smeared some on the four corners of the bronze altar, and poured out the rest at its foot. 10But he sent up in smoke the fat, the kidneys, and the lower part of the liver, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. 11Then Aaron burned the skin and the flesh outside the camp.
12After Aaron had killed the ram that was sacrificed to please the Lord, Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it against all four sides of the altar. 13They brought him each piece of the animal, including the head, and he burned them all on the altar. 14He washed the insides and the hind legs and also sent them up in smoke.
15Next, Aaron sacrificed the goat for the sins of the people, as he had done with the sacrifice for his own sins. 16And so, he burned this sacrifice on the altar in the proper way. 17He also presented the grain sacrifice and burned a handful of the flour on the altar as part of the morning sacrifice.
18 Finally, he killed the bull and the ram as a sacrifice to ask the Lord's blessing on the people. Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it against the four sides of the altar. 19His sons placed all the fat, as well as the kidneys and the lower part of the liver 20on top of the choice ribs. 21Then Aaron burned the fat on the altar and lifted up the ribs and the right hind leg to show that these were dedicated to the Lord. This was done just as the Lord had instructed Moses.
22 Aaron held out his hand and gave the people his blessing, before coming down from the bronze altar where he had offered the sacrifices. 23He and Moses went into the sacred tent, and when they came out, they gave the people their blessing. Then the Lord appeared to the people in all of his glory. 24The Lord sent fiery flames that burned up everything on the altar, and when everyone saw this, they shouted and fell to their knees to worship the Lord.
translation_text:
Aaron shã afɔle
1Gbi ni agbe osɔfowoo kusumi lɛ anaa lɛ nɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ, Mose tsɛ Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ kɛ Israel onukpai lɛ. 2Mose kɛɛ Aaron akɛ: “Ŋɔɔ tsinanuu fioo kome ni kpa ko bɛ ehe kɛ too ojwɛni kome hu ni kpa ko bɛ ehe ni okɛshã afɔle, ohã Yehowa. Okɛ tsinanuu lɛ ashã esha afɔle ni okɛ too ojwɛni lɛ ashã shãa afɔle. 3Kɛkɛ lɛ okɛɛ Israelbii lɛ akɛ amɛŋɔ too ojwɛni amɛkɛshã esha afɔle; amɛkɛ tsinabi ni eye afi ni kpa ko bɛ ehe kɛ too gwantɛŋbi ni eye afi ni kpa ko bɛ ehe ashã shãa afɔle; 4ni amɛkɛ tsinanuu kɛ too ojwɛni kɛ ŋmãa afɔle ni awo mli mu ashã naanyobɔɔ afɔle. Amɛshã afɔle amɛhã Yehowa, ejaakɛ ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ nɔ Yehowa baajie ehe kpo etsɔ̃ɔ nyɛ.”
5Amɛkɛ nii ni Mose fã amɛ akɛ amɛkɛba lɛ ba Kpee Buu lɛ hiɛ, ni asafo muu lɛ fɛɛ bua amɛhe naa yɛ jɛi koni amɛja Yehowa. 6Mose kɛɛ amɛ akɛ, “Yehowa fã akɛ nyɛfee enɛɛmɛi fɛɛ bɔ ni afee ni enunyam ni kpɛ kaŋkaŋ lɛ ajie ehe kpo atsɔ̃ɔ nyɛ.” 7 Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛɛ Aaron akɛ, “Tsi obɛŋkɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ ni oshã esha afɔle kɛ shãa afɔle ohã ohe koni okɛfɔ ohe esha kɛ maŋ lɛ he esha. Oshã afɔle nɛɛ koni okɛfɔ maŋ lɛ he eshai, tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa wo kitã lɛ.”
8Aaron tsi kɛtee afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he, ni egbe tsinanuu fioo lɛ ekɛshã esha afɔle ehã lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe. 9Ebihii lɛ kɛ lá lɛ ba. Aaron kɛ ewao tsɔ mli, ni ekɛdiki koji ni yɔɔ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he lɛ. Ni lá ni shwɛ lɛ etsi eshwie afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ shishi. 10Kɛkɛ ni eshã fɔ lɛ kɛ sabai lɛ kɛ mlɛbo lɛ he loo ni tsotsoro shi lɛ yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ bɔ ni Yehowa wo Mose kitã lɛ. 11Shi kooloo lɛ kɛ hewolo lɛ eshã yɛ shitoohe lɛ sɛɛ.
12Mose gbe kooloo ni akɛbaashã shãa afɔle lɛ hu. Ebihii lɛ kɛ lá lɛ bahã lɛ, ni ekɛshwã afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ koji ejwɛ lɛ he kɛkpe. 13Amɛkɛ shãa afɔle lɛ hu bahã lɛ, loo ni ashãa lɛ kɛ yitso lɛ fɛɛ hu lɛ, ni eshã yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ. 14Kɛkɛ ni efɔ mlinii lɛ kɛ naji lɛ ahe, ni ekɛshwie shãa afɔle ni jwere afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ, ni eshã fɛɛ.
15Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ekɛ maŋ lɛ afɔlei lɛ ba. Eŋɔ too kpakpo ni akɛbaashã maŋ lɛ he esha afɔle lɛ; egbe lɛ ni ekɛshã afɔle, tamɔ bɔ ni efee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe esha afɔle lɛ. 16Eŋɔ kooloo ni akɛshãa shãa afɔle lɛ hu kɛba, ni ekɛshã afɔle tamɔ bɔ ni gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. 17Ekɛ niyenii afɔle lɛ ba; ni ekpiti emli eko ekɔkɔ obɔ̃ ni ekɛfata shãa afɔle ni ashãa daa leebi lɛ he, ni eshã yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ. 18 Kɛkɛ ni egbe tsinanuu lɛ kɛ too ojwɛni lɛ ekɛshã naanyobɔɔ afɔle ehã maŋ lɛ; ebihii lɛ kɛ lá lɛ bahã lɛ, ni ekɛshwã afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ koji ejwɛ lɛ he kɛkpe. 19Tsinanuu lɛ kɛ too ojwɛni lɛ fɔi lɛ kɛ lei ni ewo fɔ lɛ kɛ fɔ ni ha mlinii lɛ ahe lɛ kɛ sabai lɛ kɛ loo ni tsotsoro mlɛbo lɛ he lɛ, 20Aaron kɛ fɛɛ shwie kooloi lɛ atsitsii lɛ anɔ, ni eshã yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ. 21Ekɛ tsitsii lɛ kɛ sɛɛ ninejurɔ shuɔ naji lɛ hã Yehowa akɛ nikeenii titri ko, tamɔ bɔ ni Mose ewo kitã lɛ.
22 Be ni Aaron eshã esha afɔle kɛ naanyobɔɔ afɔle lɛ egbe naa lɛ, ehole eniji anɔ kɛtee ŋwɛi ni ejɔɔ maŋ lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni ekpeleke shi. 23Agbɛnɛ Mose kɛ Aaron bote Kpee Buu lɛ mli. Be ni amɛje kpo ekoŋŋ lɛ, amɛjɔɔ maŋ lɛ. Ni Yehowa anunyam ni kpɛɔ kaŋkaŋ lɛ jie ehe kpo etsɔ̃ɔ maŋ lɛ fɛɛ. 24 Trukaa lɛ Yehowa hã la ba ni ebashã shãa afɔle lɛ kɛ fɔi lɛ ni yɔɔ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Be ni maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ na lɛ, amɛbolɔ, ni amɛkɛ amɛhiɛ bumɔ shi.

english_text:
Nadab and Abihu
1Nadab and Abihu were two of Aaron's sons, but they disobeyed the Lord by burning incense to him on a fire pan, when they were not supposed to. 2Suddenly the Lord sent fiery flames and burned them to death. 3Then Moses told Aaron that this was exactly what the Lord had meant when he said:
“I demand respect
from my priests,
and I will be praised
by everyone!”
Aaron was speechless.
4Moses sent for Mishael and Elzaphan, the two sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel. Then he told them, “Take these two dead relatives of yours outside the camp far from the entrance to the sacred tent.” 5So they dragged the dead men away by their clothes.
6Then Moses told Aaron and his other two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar:
Don't show your sorrow by messing up your hair and tearing your priestly clothes, or the Lord will get angry. He will kill the three of you and punish everyone else. It's all right for your relatives, the people of Israel, to mourn for those he destroyed by fire. 7But you are the Lord's chosen priests, and you must not leave the sacred tent, or you will die.
Aaron and his two sons obeyed Moses.
8The Lord said to Aaron:
9When you or your sons enter the sacred tent, you must never drink beer or wine. If you do, you will die right there! This law will never change. 10You must learn the difference between what is holy and what isn't holy and between the clean and the unclean. 11You must also teach the people of Israel everything that I commanded Moses to say to them.
12 Moses told Aaron and his two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar:
The grain sacrifice that was offered to give thanks to the Lord is very holy. So make bread without yeast from the part that wasn't sent up in smoke and eat it beside the altar. 13The Lord has said that this belongs to you and your sons, and that it must be eaten in a holy place. 14-15 But the choice ribs and the hind leg that were lifted up may be eaten by your entire family, as long as you do so in an acceptable place. These parts are yours from the sacrifices that the people offer to ask the Lord's blessing. This is what the Lord has commanded, and it will never change.
16When Moses asked around and learned that the ram for the sin sacrifice had already been burned on the altar, he became angry with Eleazar and Ithamar and said, 17 “Why didn't you eat the meat from this sacrifice in an acceptable place? It is very holy, and the Lord has given you this sacrifice to remove Israel's sin and guilt. 18Whenever an animal's blood isn't brought into the sacred tent, I commanded you to eat its meat in an acceptable place, but you burned it instead.”
19Their father Aaron replied, “Today two of my sons offered the sacrifice for sin and the sacrifice to please the Lord, and look what has happened to me! Would the Lord have approved if I had eaten the sacrifice for sin?”
20Moses was satisfied with Aaron's reply.
translation_text:
Nadab kɛ Abihu fee esha
1Shi Aaron bihii ni ji Nadab kɛ Abihu lɛ ateŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ wo elajee ŋɛsu, ni amɛkɛ la wo mli. Amɛkɛ tsofakɛŋma shwie nɔ, ni amɛshã amɛhã Yehowa; shi la ni amɛkɛshã lɛ bɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ, ejaakɛ jeee no he kitã Yehowa wo lɛ. 2 Yehowa hã la ba ebashã amɛ, ni amɛgboi yɛ ehiɛ. 3 Kɛkɛ ni Mose kɛɛ Aaron akɛ, “Enɛ ji nɔ ni Yehowa tsɔ̃ɔ be ni ekɛɛ akɛ, ‘Mɛi fɛɛ ni sɔ̃mɔɔ mi lɛ esa akɛ abu mi akɛ mɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ; majie minunyam lɛ kpo matsɔ̃ɔ maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ.’ ” Shi Aaron mua enaa.
4 Kɛkɛ ni Mose tsɛ Mishael kɛ Elzafan, Aaron tsɛkwɛ Uziel bii lɛ kɛba, ni ekɛɛ amɛ akɛ: “Nyɛbaa nyɛbaholea nyɛnyɛmimɛi lɛ agbohii lɛ kɛjea He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ kɛyaa shitoohe lɛ sɛɛ.” 5Amɛba ni amɛbahole Aaron bihii lɛ kɛ amɛflakai ni amɛwo lɛ kɛje shitoohe lɛ mli, tamɔ bɔ ni Mose kɛɛ lɛ.
6 Mose kɛɛ Aaron kɛ ebihii ni ji Eleazar kɛ Itamar akɛ, “Nyɛkahãa nyɛyiteŋ fea tsaŋtsaŋ aloo nyɛgbalaa nyɛtadei kɛtsɔ̃ɔ akɛ nyɛmiiye ŋkɔmɔ. Kɛ nyɛfee nakai lɛ, nyɛbaagboi, ni Yehowa mli baawo maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ la. Nyɛhãa nyɛwekumɛi, Israel maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ, afoa shãa ni Yehowa ehã la eshã nyɛnyɛmimɛi lɛ ni amɛgboi nɛɛ. 7Nyɛkajea Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ naa hu ni nyɛbagboi, ejaakɛ akɛ Yehowa mufɔɔ mu lɛ efɔ nyɛ mu.” Amɛfee bɔ ni Mose kɛɛ amɛ lɛ.
Mlai ni awo Osɔfoi
8Yehowa kɛɛ Aaron akɛ, 9 “Bo kɛ obihii lɛ, nyɛkanua wain loo dãa ni wa ko be mli ni nyɛyaa Kpee Buu lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ nyɛnu dãa lɛ, nyɛbaagboi. Oshwiei fɛɛ aye akpɔ nɛɛ nɔ. 10Esa akɛ nyɛle srɔto ni kã nɔ ni he tse krɔŋkrɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni buleɔ mɔ teŋ; ni esa akɛ nyɛle srɔto ni yɔɔ nɔ ni he tse kɛ nɔ ni he tseee teŋ. 11Nyɛtsɔ̃a Israelbii lɛ akpɔi fɛɛ ni Yehowa tsɔ̃ Mose nɔ ekɛ amɛ wie he lɛ.”
12 Mose kɛɛ Aaron kɛ ebihii ni eshwɛ ni ji Eleazar kɛ Itamar lɛ akɛ, “Niyenii afɔlei ni shwɛɔ yɛ afɔlei ni ashã ahã Yehowa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, nyɛkɛshãa mã akpiti aboloo ni nyɛyea yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he ejaakɛ afɔle nɛɛ nɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ ni fe fɛɛ ni. 13Nyɛyea yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ, ejaakɛ bo kɛ obihii lɛ, nyɛgbɛnaanii ji niyenii afɔlei nɛɛ ni shwɛɔ yɛ shãa afɔlei ni ashãa ahãa Yehowa lɛ asɛɛ lɛ. Ejaakɛ enɛ ji Yehowa kitã ni ewo mi. 14Shi tsitsi lɛ kɛ shuɔ lɛ ni akɛhãa Yehowa akɛ keenɔ lɛ nyɛyea yɛ he ko ni tse, bo kɛ obihii kɛ obiyei lɛ fɛɛ, ejaakɛ akɛ afɔlei nɛɛ ehã bo kɛ obii lɛ akɛ nyɛgbɛnaanii yɛ naanyobɔɔ afɔlei ni Israelbii lɛ shãa lɛ amli. 15 Akɛ tsitsi lɛ kɛ sɛɛ shuɔ lɛ afata fɔi lɛ ahe kɛba, be mli ni ashãa fɔi lɛ akɛ afɔle ahãa Yehowa akɛ niyenii afɔle lɛ. Tsitsi lɛ kɛ shuɔ lɛ, bo kɛ obihii lɛ agbɛnaanii ni akɛhã nyɛ kɛmiiya naanɔ ni. Nakai ji bɔ ni Yehowa fã akɛ afee.”
16Mose tao too ojwɛni ni akɛshãa esha afɔle lɛ aahu kɛyashi ena ele akɛ ashã momo. Mose mli wo Eleazar kɛ Itamar Aaron bihii ni eshwɛ lɛ la ni ekɛɛ, 17 “Mɛɛba nyɛyeee esha afɔle lɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ? Nɔ ko ni yɔɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ naakpa ji afɔle lɛ ni Yehowa kɛhã nyɛ koni nyɛkɛ kpãtã yɛ Yehowa hiɛ koni nyɛjie maŋ lɛ he esha lɛ kɛya lɛ. 18Akɛni akɛ too ojwɛni lɛ lá lɛ baaa Kpee Buu krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ mli hewɔ lɛ, kulɛ esa akɛ nyɛye afɔle lɛ yɛ jɛi tamɔ bɔ ni mifã lɛ.”
19Aaron to he ehã Mose akɛ, “Maŋbii lɛ shã amɛhe esha afɔle kɛ amɛshãa afɔle lɛ ŋmɛnɛ; ni kɛ̃lɛ oshara ebasharã mi nɛɛ. Eji miye esha afɔle ŋmɛnɛ kulɛ ehi yɛ Yehowa hiɛ?” 20Be ni Mose nu wiemɔ nɛɛ lɛ, ena akɛ eja.

english_text:
Clean and Unclean Animals
(Deuteronomy 14.3-21)
1 The Lord told Moses and Aaron 2to say to the community of Israel:
You may eat 3any animal that has divided hoofs and chews the cud. 4-8But you must not eat animals such as camels, rock badgers, and rabbits that chew the cud but don't have divided hoofs. And you must not eat pigs—they have divided hoofs, but don't chew the cud. All of these animals are unclean, and you are forbidden even to touch their dead bodies.
9-12You may eat anything that lives in water and has fins and scales. But it would be disgusting for you to eat anything else that lives in water, and you must not even touch their dead bodies.
13-19Eagles, vultures, buzzards, crows, ostriches, hawks, sea gulls, owls, pelicans, storks, herons, hoopoes, and bats are also disgusting, and you are forbidden to eat any of them.
20-23The only winged insects you may eat are locusts, grasshoppers, and crickets. All other winged insects that crawl are too disgusting for you to eat.
24-28Don't even touch the dead bodies of animals that have divided hoofs but don't chew the cud. And don't touch the dead bodies of animals that have paws. If you do, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
29-30Moles, rats, mice, and all kinds of lizards are unclean. 31Anyone who touches their dead bodies or anything touched by their dead bodies becomes unclean until evening. 32If something made of wood, cloth, or leather touches one of their dead bodies, it must be washed, but it is still unclean until evening. 33If any of these animals is found dead in a clay pot, the pot must be broken to pieces, and everything in it becomes unclean. 34If you pour water from this pot on any food, that food becomes unclean, and anything drinkable in the pot becomes unclean.
35If the dead body of one of these animals touches anything else, including ovens and stoves, that thing becomes unclean and must be destroyed. 36A spring or a cistern where one of these dead animals is found is still clean, but anyone who touches the animal becomes unclean. 37If the dead body of one of these animals is found lying on seeds that have been set aside for planting, the seeds remain clean. 38But seeds that are soaking in water become unclean, if the dead animal is found in the water.
39If an animal that may be eaten happens to die, and you touch it, you become unclean until evening. 40If you eat any of its meat or carry its body away, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
41-42Don't eat any of those disgusting little creatures that crawl or walk close to the ground. 43If you eat any of them, you will become just as disgusting and unclean as they are. 44 I am the Lord your God, and you must dedicate yourselves to me and be holy, just as I am holy. Don't become disgusting by eating any of these unclean creatures. 45I brought you out of Egypt so that I could be your God. Now you must become holy, because I am holy!
46-47I have given these laws so that you will know what animals, birds, and fish are clean and may be eaten, and which ones are unclean and may not be eaten.
translation_text:
Kooloi ni aaanyɛ aye
1Yehowa kɛ Mose kɛ Aaron wie koni amɛkɛ mlai nɛɛ ahã Israelbii lɛ ni amɛye nɔ. 2Yehowa kɛɛ, “Kooloi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ateŋ nii ni nyɛye ji: 3nii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ koklotoi ni agbala mli aloo aja mli, ni asaŋ amɛgɔiɔ amɛniyenii ni amɛtaa. 4-6Shi nyɛkayea yooma kɛ afutuɔkɔ kɛ kpɛŋkplɛ, ejaakɛ amɛhe tseee. Amɛgɔiɔ amɛniyenii, ni amɛtaa moŋ, shi agbalako amɛkoklotoi amli. 7Nyɛkayea kplotoo, ejaakɛ ehe tseee. Eyɛ koklotoi ni agbala mli moŋ, shi egɔiii eniyenii etaaa. 8Nyɛkayea kooloi nɛɛ aloo; nyɛkataa amɛgbohii ahe hu, ejaakɛ amɛhe tseee.
9“Yɛ nu mli loi ateŋ lɛ, nyɛyea nii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ fiji kɛ totoi ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ kɛ fai amli fɛɛ. 10Shi nii fɛɛ ni bɛ fiji kɛ totoi ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ mli loo fai amli, bɔɔnii bibii ni ebua amɛhe naa tɔo kɛnyiɛ nu mli jio, bɔɔnii ni yɔɔ nu mli ni dara fe nomɛi jio, nyɛhia amɛ. 11Nihiinii ji amɛ; nyɛkayea amɛloo, ni nyɛhia amɛgbohii lɛ tete. 12Nii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ nu mli ni amɛbɛ fiji loo totoi lɛ, nii ni ahiɔ ni. 13Yɛ loofɔji ateŋ lɛ, nii ni nyɛhia ni nyɛkayea nɛ: okropɔŋ kɛ akpaŋa 14kɛ ŋshɔŋ okropɔŋ kɛ laalɔɔ kɛ osansa henɔi srɔtoi lɛ 15kɛ kwãakwãalabite henɔi srɔtoi fɛɛ, 16kɛ duguma kɛ nyɔɔŋ akroma kɛ faanaa oka, kɛ akroma henɔi srɔtoi lɛ fɛɛ, 17kɛ patu kɛ ŋshɔŋ patu, kɛ patu bibioo 18kɛ dɔkɔdɔkɔ kɛ kpokukpoku kɛ guŋ 19kɛ klitso kɛ ehenɔi srɔtoi lɛ fɛɛ, kɛ obleku kɛ aputupata.
20“Kooloi bibii fɛɛ ni filikiɔ ni amɛwamɔɔ ni amɛnyiɛɔ yɛ amɛnaji ejwɛjwɛ nɔ lɛ, nyɛkayea. 21Shi kɛ̃lɛ enɛɛmɛi ateŋ nii ni yɔɔ shɔji enyɔɔnyɔ ni tsara amɛnane tokota nɔ ni amɛkɛtumɔɔ lɛ, nyɛyea. 22Kooloi nɛɛ ji baalabii kɛ amɛhenɔi lɛ, ligɔligɔ kɛ ehenɔi lɛ, kɛ agã kɛ ehenɔi, 23filikilɔi krokomɛi fɛɛ ni eshwɛ ni wamɔɔ ni amɛyɔɔ naji ejwɛɛjwɛ lɛ nyɛkayea, ejaakɛ amɛhe tseee. 24 Ni enɛɛmɛi buleɔ nyɛ. Kɛ nyɛye lɛ nyɛkɛbaabule nyɛhe. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni taa kooloi nɛɛ agbohii ahe lɛ, ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. 25Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaakɔ kooloi nɛɛ ateŋ eko ni egbo he nɔ ko ehiɛ yɛ edɛ̃ lɛ, efɔ etadei lɛ ahe; ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. 26Kooloo fɛɛ kooloo ni yɔɔ koklotoi ni agbalako mli, ni asaŋ egɔiii nii ni eye momo lɛ, ehe tseee. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaata eko he lɛ, mɔ lɛ he tseee. 27Kooloi fɛɛ ni kɛ amɛniji nyiɛɔ yɛ kooloi naji ejwɛɛjwɛtsɛmɛi ateŋ lɛ, amɛhe tseee. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni taa eko gbonyo he lɛ, ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. 28Mɔ ni aaawo kooloi nɛɛ ateŋ eko gbonyo lɛ, efɔ etadei ahe; shi ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. Nyɛbua kooloi nɛɛ akɛ kooloi ni ahe tseee.
29“Kooloi ni eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ, nii ni he tseee ji obishi kɛ kwakwe kɛ odaaklɔ kɛ ehenɔi, 30kɛ mampam kɛ odiŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsunyɛ kɛ kɔ̃dɔ̃ kɛ obosumaketeo. 31Nyɛbua enɛɛmɛi akɛ nii ni he tseee yɛ kooloi ni eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ lɛ ateŋ. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni taa eko ni egbo he lɛ, ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. 32Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni kooloi nɛɛ ateŋ eko ni egbo aaagbee enɔ lɛ, ehe tseee; nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni akɛ tso loo mama loo kooloo hewolo fee, loo kpekpe loo nɔ fɛɛ nɔ kɛkɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jio, eko fɛɛ eko lɛ akɛwo nu mli. Shi ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. No sɛɛ dani ehe aaatse. 33Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni akɛ sũ fee ni kooloi nɛɛ ateŋ eko aaagbee mli lɛ, nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he tseee. Ajwa sũnɔ ni nii lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ. 34Niyenii fɛɛ ni ayeɔ ni aaatsɔ̃ nu ni jɛ sũnɔ nɛɛ mli aaashwie nɔ lɛ, ehe tseee; ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni anuɔ ni yɔɔ nɛkɛ sũnɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ, ehe tseee. 35Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni kooloi nɛɛ ateŋ eko gbonyo aaagbee nɔ lɛ, ehe tseee. Kɛ flɔnɔɔ loo latɛ nɔ egbee lɛ, akumɔ, ejaakɛ ehe tseee, ni nyɛbua lɛ akɛ nɔ ni he tseee. 36Shi kɛ nu hiŋmɛi loo dudɔ ni akɛ nu toɔ mli ni lɛ, no lɛ ehe tse; shi kɛ eko he aaasa kooloo gbonyo he lɛ, ehe tseee. 37Kɛji kooloi nɛɛ ateŋ eko gbonyo gbee wu ni abaadu nɔ lɛ, wu lɛ he tse lolo. 38Shi kɛ aafɔ dumɔnii lɛ yɛ nu mli, ni gbonyo lɛ gbee nɔ lɛ, wu lɛ he tseee.
39“Kɛ kooloi ni ayeɔ lɛ eko gbo lɛ, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni taa egbonyo lɛ he lɛ, ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. 40 Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yeɔ kooloo ni egbo lɛ loo lɛ eko lɛ, efɔ etadei ahe; ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. Mɔ ni woɔ kooloo lɛ gbonyo lɛ, efɔ etadei ahe, ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.
41“Kooloi bibii fɛɛ ni eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ lɛ, nyɛkayea, ejaakɛ nii ni ahiɔ ni. 42Kooloi fɛɛ ni wamɔɔ yɛ amɛmusu nɔ aloo amɛnyiɛɔ yɛ amɛnaji ejwɛ nɔ, aloo amɛyɔɔ naji piipii, kooloi bibii fɛɛ ni eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ lɛ, nyɛkayea, ejaakɛ amɛbuleɔ mɔ. 43Nyɛkayea koni nyɛkɛ no bule nyɛhe ni nyɛkɛwo nyɛhe muji. 44 Mi ji Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛfea nyɛhe krɔŋkrɔŋ; nyɛtoa nyɛhe krɔŋkrɔŋ, ejaakɛ mɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ ji mi. No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛkɛ nibii ni eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ̃ lɛ eko eko akabulea nyɛhe. 45Mi ji Yehowa mɔ ni jie nyɛ kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, koni matsɔ̃ nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛfea nyɛhe krɔŋkrɔŋ, ejaakɛ mɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ ji mi.
46“Belɛ enɛ ji mla ni kã shi yɛ kooloi kɛ loofɔji kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni hiɔ nu mli kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni hiɛ kã ni nyiɛɔ ni eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ lɛ he. 47Awo mla lɛ koni akɛna srɔto ni yɔɔ kooloi ni he tse kɛ nii ni he tseee teŋ, kɛ kooloi ni ayeɔ kɛ nii ni ayeee teŋ.”

english_text:
What Women Must Do after Giving Birth
1The Lord told Moses 2to say to the community of Israel:
If a woman gives birth to a son, she is unclean for seven days, just as she is during her monthly period. 3 Her son must be circumcised on the eighth day, 4but her loss of blood keeps her from being completely clean for another 33 days. During this time she must not touch anything holy or go to the place of worship. 5Any woman who gives birth to a daughter is unclean for two weeks, just as she is during her period. And she won't be completely clean for another 66 days.
6When the mother has completed her time of cleansing, she must come to the front of the sacred tent and bring to the priest a year-old lamb as a sacrifice to please me and a dove or a pigeon as a sacrifice for sin. 7After the priest offers the sacrifices to me, the mother will become completely clean from her loss of blood, whether her child is a boy or a girl. 8 If she cannot afford a lamb, she can offer two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice to please me and the other as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_text:
Yei ahetsuumɔ yɛ bifɔmɔ sɛɛ
1Yehowa kɛ Mose wie 2koni ekɛɛ Israelbii lɛ akɛ, “Kɛji yoo ko na musu, ni efɔ binuu lɛ, ehe tseee gbii kpawo, tamɔ bɔ ni ehe tseee yɛ eyei aniifeemɔ be mli lɛ. 3 Gbi ni ji kpaanyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, afo gbekɛ lɛ ketia. 4Yoo lɛ aŋɔ gbii nyɔŋmai etɛ̃ kɛ etɛ̃ ni ekɛtsuu ehe, ni ekɛjie ehe lá muji lɛ. Nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ekata nɔ ko ni yɔɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ he, ni ekaya Kpee Buu krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi gbi ni eeegbe ehetsuumɔ lɛ naa.
5“Kɛ yoo ko fɔ biyoo lɛ, ehe tseee otsii enyɔ, tamɔ be ni efee yeianii lɛ. Eŋɔ gbii nyɔŋmai ekpaa kɛ ekpaa sɔŋŋ ni ekɛtsuu ehe, ni ekɛjie ehe lá muji lɛ.
6“Kɛji gbii ni ekɛtsuɔ ehe lɛ, yɛ binuu loo biyoo hewɔ lɛ ho lɛ, ekɛ too gwantɛŋ bi ni eye afi aba abahã ni akɛshã shãa afɔle, kɛ shĩa okpo loo kosɛɛ okpo ni akɛshã esha afɔle. Ekɛba Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ naa ekɛbahã osɔfo lɛ. 7Osɔfo lɛ kɛ afɔle lɛ aba Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ ni ekpãtã ehã yoo lɛ, koni ehe atse yɛ lá ni hoɔ lɛ lɛ gbɛfaŋ. Enɛ ji mla ni kã shi hã yoo ni fɔɔ nuu loo yoo lɛ.
8 “Shi kɛji yoo lɛ naaa too gwantɛŋbi yinii lɛ, no lɛ ekɛ kosɛɛ okpoi enyɔ loo shĩa okpoi enyɔ aba. Akɛ ekome ashã shãa afɔle, koni akɛ ekome hu ashã esha afɔle. Osɔfo lɛ akpãtã ahã lɛ, ni ehe aaatse yɛ lá ni hoɔ lɛ gbɛfaŋ.”

english_text:
Skin Diseases
1The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
2If sores or boils or a skin rash should break out and start spreading on your body, you must be brought to Aaron or to one of the other priests. 3If the priest discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
4But if the infected area is white and only skin deep, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, the priest will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 5If the disease hasn't spread by that time, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days. 6Then if the disease hasn't become any worse or spread, the priest will say, “You are clean. It is only a sore. After you wash your clothes, you may go home.”
7However, if the disease comes back, you must return to the priest. 8If it is discovered that the disease has started spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
9Any of you with a skin disease must be brought to a priest. 10If he discovers that the sore spot is white with pus and that the hair around it has also turned white, 11he will say, “This is leprosy. You are unclean and must stay away from everyone else.” 12-13But if the disease has run its course and only the scars remain, he will say, “You are clean.” 14-15If the sores come back and turn white again, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
16-17However, if the sores heal and only white spots remain, the priest will say, “You are now clean.”
18-19If you have a sore that either swells or turns reddish-white after it has healed, then you must show it to a priest. 20If he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 21But if the white area is only on the surface of the skin and hasn't become any worse, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
22If the sore begins spreading during this time, the priest will say, “You are unclean because you have a disease.” 23But if it doesn't spread, and only a scar remains, he will say, “You are now clean.”
24If you have a burn that gets infected and turns red or reddish-white, 25a priest must examine it. Then if he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “The burn has turned into leprosy, and you are unclean.” 26But if the priest finds that the hair in the infected area hasn't turned white and that the sore is only skin deep and it is healing, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 27On the seventh day the priest will examine you again, and if the infection is spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 28However, if the infection hasn't spread and has begun to heal, and if only a scar remains, he will say, “Only a scar remains from the burn, and you are clean.”
29If you have a sore on your head or chin, 30it must be examined by a priest. If the infection seems more than skin deep, and the hair in it has thinned out and lost its color, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 31On the other hand, if he discovers that the itchy spot is only skin deep, but that the hair still isn't healthy, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 32By that time, if the itch hasn't spread, if the hair seems healthy, and if the itch is only skin deep, 33you must shave off the hair around the infection, but not those on it. Then the priest will tell you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days. 34By that time, if the itch hasn't spread and seems no more than skin deep, he will say, “You are clean; now you must wash your clothes.”
35-36Later, if the itch starts spreading, even though the hair is still healthy, the priest will say, “You are unclean.” 37But if he thinks you are completely well, he will say, “You are clean.”
38If white spots break out on your skin, 39but the priest discovers that it is only a rash, he will say, “You are clean.”
40-41If you become bald on any part of your head, you are still clean. 42-43But if a priest discovers that a reddish-white sore has broken out on the bald spot and looks like leprosy, he will say, 44“This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
45If you ever have leprosy, you must tear your clothes, leave your hair uncombed, cover the lower part of your face, and go around shouting, “I'm unclean! I'm unclean!” 46As long as you have the disease, you are unclean and must live alone outside the camp.
47-50If a greenish or reddish spot appears anywhere on any of your clothing or on anything made of leather, you must let the priest examine the clothing or the leather. He will put it aside for seven days, 51and if the mildew has spread in that time, he will say, “This is unclean 52because the mildew has spread.” Then he will burn the clothing or the piece of leather.
53If the priest discovers that the mildew hasn't spread, 54he will tell you to wash the clothing or leather and put it aside for another seven days, 55after which he will examine it again. If the spot hasn't spread, but is still greenish or reddish, the clothing or leather is unclean and must be burned. 56But if the spot has faded after being washed, he will tear away the spot. 57Later, if the spot reappears elsewhere on the clothing or the leather, you must burn it. 58Even if the spot completely disappears after being washed, it must be washed again before it is clean.
59These are the rules for deciding if clothing is clean or unclean after a spot appears on it.
translation_text:
Mlai ni kɔɔ hewolo nɔ helai ahe
1Yehowa kɛ mlai nɛɛ hã Mose kɛ Aaron. 2“Kɛji nɔ ko fũu yɛ mɔ ko hewolo nɔ loo fala ko loo gbɛ̃ ko, ni fee sɛɛ lɛ elɛɛ shi, ni etsɔ̃ tamɔ kpiti hela lɛ, akɛ mɔ lɛ aba Osɔfo Aaron loo ebihii osɔfoi lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko ŋɔɔ. 3 Osɔfo lɛ akwɛ he ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ ekwɛ ni tsɔi ni yɔɔ jɛi lɛ etsɔ̃ eyɛŋ, ni jɛi enyɔ mli voo fe hewolo ni bɔle he ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ, belɛ kpiti ni; ni be ni osɔfo lɛ ekwɛ helatsɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ekɛɛ akɛ helatsɛ lɛ he tseee. 4Shi kɛji hewolo nɔ he ni akwɛ lɛ yɛ eyɛŋ ni enyɔko mli voo fe hewolo ni bɔle he lɛ, ni emli tsɔi lɛ hu tsɔ̃ko eyɛŋ lɛ, no lɛ osɔfo lɛ aŋa helatsɛ lɛ yi gbii kpawo. 5Gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ osɔfo lɛ akwɛ, ni kɛ hela lɛ yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ heloo lɛ hiɛ, ni elɛɛko yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ lɛ, no lɛ osɔfo lɛ asaa aŋa eyi gbii kpawo ekoŋŋ. 6Kɛji gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ osɔfo lɛ kwɛ ekoŋŋ, ni kɛ hela lɛ elaaje, ni elɛɛko yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ lɛ, no lɛ osɔfo lɛ aŋɔ gbɔmɔ lɛ akɛ mɔ ko ni he tse; hela lɛ gbɛ̃i ni. Helatsɛ lɛ afɔ etadei ahe, koni ehe atse. 7Shi kɛji gbɛ̃i lɛ miilɛɛ yɛ ehewolo lɛ nɔ be ni osɔfo lɛ ekwɛ lɛ ni ekɛɛ akɛ ehe tse lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ gbɔmɔ lɛ kɛ ehe ayatsɔɔ osɔfo lɛ, nɔ ni ji shii enyɔ. 8Kɛ osɔfo lɛ kwɛ, ni gbɛ̃i lɛ miilɛɛ yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ lɛ, osɔfo lɛ akɛɛ akɛ mɔ lɛ he tseee; hela lɛ kpiti ni.
9“Kɛji kpiti shwie mɔ ko he lɛ, akɛ lɛ aba osɔfo lɛ ŋɔɔ. 10Osɔfo lɛ akwɛ lɛ. Kɛ nɔ ko yɛŋ ewo yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ, ni ehã jɛi tsɔi lɛ etsɔ̃ eyɛŋ, ni loo ŋmɔŋ tɔ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ ni efuu lɛ mli lɛ, 11belɛ kpiti momo yɔɔ ehewolo lɛ mli lɛ. Osɔfo lɛ akɛɛ akɛ nɔ ko ni he tseee ni. Osɔfo lɛ akaŋa eyi, ejaakɛ ekã shi faŋŋ akɛ ehe tseee. 12Shi kɛji hela lɛ je kpo yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ, ni nɔ ni osɔfo lɛ naa kɛkɛ ji hela lɛ eshwie helatsɛ lɛ hewolo nɔ fɛɛ, kɛjɛ eyiteŋ kɛyashi enaji ahe lɛ, 13osɔfo lɛ akwɛ helatsɛ lɛ; ni kɛ ena akɛ hela lɛ eha ehewolo nɔ fɛɛ lɛ, ekɛɛ akɛ helatsɛ lɛ he tse. Ni kɛ helatsɛ lɛ he fɛɛ eyɛ futaa lɛ, ehe tse. 14Shi gbi nɔ ni aaana fala ŋmɔŋ yɛ helatsɛ lɛ he lɛ, ehe tseee. 15Osɔfo lɛ akwɛ helatsɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ; ni kɛ ena lɛ ekɛɛ akɛ helatsɛ lɛ he tseee; hela lɛ kpiti ni. 16Shi kɛji fala lɛ tã, ni eesaa etsɔ̃ eyɛŋ ekoŋŋ lɛ, helatsɛ lɛ aba osɔfo lɛ ŋɔɔ. 17Osɔfo lɛ akwɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ. Kɛ ena akɛ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ etsɔ̃ eyɛŋ lɛ, helatsɛ lɛ he tse; ni osɔfo lɛ akɛɛ akɛ ehe tse.
18“Kɛji asane tsɛ̃ mɔ ko hewolo nɔ ni etã, 19ni fee sɛɛ lɛ nɔ ko yɛŋ bawo yɛ he ni asane lɛ tsɛ̃ lɛ yɛ lɛ, aloo nɔ ko yɛŋ ni tsuɔo ba jɛi lɛ, no lɛ mɔ lɛ aya osɔfo lɛ ŋɔɔ. 20Osɔfo lɛ akwɛ lɛ. Kɛji he ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ enyɔ mli voo fe hewolo ni bɔle jɛi lɛ, ni emli tsɔi lɛ etsɔ̃ eyɛŋ lɛ, osɔfo lɛ akɛɛ akɛ ehe tseee; kpiti ebote asane lɛ mli. 21Shi kɛji osɔfo lɛ kwɛ, ni ena akɛ tsɔi yɛŋ bɛ mli, ni jɛi enyɔko mli voo fe hewolo ni bɔle lɛ lɛ, ni enaa miilaaje lɛ, no lɛ osɔfo lɛ aŋa helatsɛ lɛ yi gbii kpawo. 22Kɛji hela lɛ miilɛɛ shi fe bɔ ni kulɛ eyɔɔ lɛ, osɔfo lɛ akɛɛ akɛ helatsɛ lɛ he tseee; hela lɛ kpiti ni. 23Shi kɛji nɔ ko yɛŋ lɛ elɛɛɛ shi, ni eyɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, no lɛ fladoku ni; asane lɛ shishi ni. Osɔfo lɛ akɛɛ akɛ helatsɛ lɛ he tse.
24“Kɛji la shã mɔ ko, ni la fala lɛ fee nɔ ko yɛŋ aloo nɔ ko yɛŋ ni etsuru fioo futu mli lɛ, 25osɔfo lɛ akwɛ mɔ lɛ. Kɛji tsɔi ni yɔɔ la fala lɛ mli etsɔ̃ eyɛŋ, ni jɛi enyɔ mli voo fe hewolo ni bɔle lɛ lɛ, belɛ kpiti ebote la fala lɛ mli. Osɔfo lɛ akɛɛ akɛ helatsɛ lɛ he tseee; hela lɛ kpiti ni. 26Shi kɛ osɔfo lɛ kwɛ lɛ, ni ena akɛ tsɔi yɛŋ bɛ fala lɛ mli ni jɛi enyɔko mli voo fe hewolo ni bɔle lɛ lɛ, no lɛ osɔfo lɛ aŋa helatsɛ lɛ yi gbii kpawo. 27Osɔfo lɛ akwɛ helatsɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ. Kɛji fala lɛ elɛɛ yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni kulɛ eyɔɔ lɛ, osɔfo lɛ akɛɛ akɛ mɔ lɛ he tseee; hela lɛ kpiti ni. 28Shi kɛji he ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ, ni elɛɛko shi efatako he, shi moŋ enaa miilaaje lɛ, belɛ la fala lɛ kɛkɛ ni ehã jɛi efuu lɛ. Osɔfo lɛ akɛɛ akɛ helatsɛ lɛ he tse, ejaakɛ fala doku kɛkɛ ni.
29“Kɛji fala fee nuu loo yoo ko yiteŋ loo etsɛŋ mli lɛ, osɔfo lɛ akwɛ. 30Kɛji he ni fala lɛ yɔɔ lɛ enyɔ mli voo fe hewolo ni bɔle jɛi lɛ, ni tsɔi ni yɔɔ jɛi lɛ yɛ hwiaahwiaa ni ehiɛ wuɔfɔ su lɛ, osɔfo lɛ akɛɛ akɛ mɔ lɛ he tseee; hela lɛ fafale ni; efeɔ yiteŋ loo tsɛŋ mli. 31Kɛji be ni osɔfo lɛ kwɛ helatsɛ lɛ ena akɛ he ni fafale lɛ yɔɔ lɛ enyɔko mli voo fe hewolo ni bɔle lɛ lɛ, shi kɛ̃lɛ tsɔi ni yɔɔ jɛi lɛ bɛ ediŋ lɛ, eŋa helatsɛ lɛ yi ewo tsuŋ gbii kpawo. 32Gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ osɔfo lɛ asaa akwɛ fafale lɛ ekoŋŋ. Kɛji fafale lɛ elɛko, ni tsɔi ni hiɛ wuɔfɔ su ekwɛ̃ko yɛ mli, ni fala lɛ enyɔko hewolo lɛ mli voo fe hewolo ni bɔle lɛ lɛ, 33ahã mɔ lɛ ashɛ ehe tsɔi fɛɛ fe he ni fafale lɛ yɔɔ pɛ eshi. Osɔfo lɛ aŋa mɔ lɛ yi awo tsuŋ gbii krokomɛi kpawo. 34Gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ, osɔfo lɛ akwɛ fafale lɛ ekoŋŋ. Kɛji elɛɛko ni enyɔko mli voo fe hewolo ni bɔle lɛ lɛ, ekɛɛ akɛ mɔ lɛ he tse. Mɔ lɛ afɔ etadei ahe koni ehe atse. 35Shi kɛji fafale lɛ elɛɛ, yɛ be ni akɛɛ akɛ mɔ lɛ he tse lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, 36Osɔfo lɛ akwɛ helatsɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ. Kɛji fafale lɛ esaa elɛɛ lɛ, ehe ehiaaa akɛ osɔfo lɛ akwɛ akɛ eeena tsɔi ni hiɛ wuɔfɔ su lo; nɔ ni kã shi faŋŋ kɛkɛ ji mɔ lɛ he tseee. 37Shi kɛji ekwɛ lɛ esusuɔ akɛ fafale lɛ yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ, ni tsɔi diŋ ekwɛ̃ yɛ mli lɛ, belɛ fafale lɛ etã. Helatsɛ lɛ he etse; ni osɔfo lɛ akɛɛ akɛ ehe tse.
38“Kɛji nii yɛji hãlãhãlã komɛi ba nuu loo yoo ko hewolo nɔ lɛ, 39osɔfo lɛ akwɛ. Kɛji nibii yɛji hãlãhãlã nɛɛ ejeee shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ lɛ, belɛ aflimata eshwie mɔ lɛ hewolo nɔ lɛ; mɔ lɛ he tse.
40“Kɛji nuu ko yi kpa yɛ eyisɛɛ lɛ, yikpataatsɛ ji lɛ, shi ehe tse. 41Kɛji ehiɛnaa gbɛ kɛkɛ eyi lɛ kpa yɛ lɛ, hiɛnaa kpataa tsɛ ji lɛ, shi ehe tse. 42Shi kɛji nɔ ko yɛŋ ni tsuɔ oo shwie eyiteŋ loo ehiɛnaa he ni ekpa lɛ, kpiti ji nɔ ni yɔɔ jɛi lɛ. 43Osɔfo lɛ akwɛ mɔ lɛ. Kɛji osɔfo lɛ na fafale yɛŋ ni tsuɔ oo yɛ eyisɛɛ loo ehiɛnaa he ni ekpa lɛ, ni etamɔ kpiti yɛ hewolo nɔ lɛ, 44osɔfo lɛ akɛɛ akɛ eji mɔ ko ni he tseee yɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ eyiteŋ lɛ hewɔ.
45“Mɔ ni yeɔ kpiti lɛ egbala etadei, ni ehiɛ eyitso efolo. Eha enaabu nɔ, ni ebolɔ akɛ, ‘Mihe tseee, mihe tseee!’ 46Gbii abɔ ni hela lɛ yɔɔ ehe lɛ, ehe tseee kwraa. Ekome too ehi shi, ni eshihilɛhe lɛ ahi shitoohe lɛ sɛɛ.
47“Kɛji kpiti ekadi kuŋtu loo klala atade ko mli, 48aloo ekadi kuŋtu loo klala kpãi ni akɛlo atade lɛ mli, loo kooloo wolo loo nɔ ko ni akɛ kooloo wolo fee lɛ mli, 49ni kadimɔ lɛ su eŋɔli loo etsuru yɛ atade loo kooloo wolo loo kpãi ni akɛlo atade lɛ, loo nɔ ko ni akɛ kooloo wolo fee lɛ mli lɛ, no lɛ kpiti he okadi ni; ni esa akɛ akɛtsɔ̃ɔ osɔfo lɛ. 50Osɔfo lɛ akwɛ nɔ ni ekadi mli lɛ, ni ekɛ nɔ ni mli ni ekadi lɛ ato gbii kpawo. 51Gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ ekwɛ ekoŋŋ. Kɛji nɔ ni ekadi mli lɛ elɛɛ yɛ atade lɛ loo kpãi ni akɛlo atade lɛ loo kooloo wolo lɛ loo nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni akɛ kooloo wolo lɛ fee lɛ mli lɛ, belɛ kpiti ni fiteɔ nii eshwie he lɛ; ni nɔ mli ni ekadi lɛ he tseee. 52Osɔfo lɛ ashã atade ni kpiti lɛ ekadi mli lɛ, loo kpãi ni akɛlo kuŋtu loo klala atade lɛ loo nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni akɛ kooloo wolo fee ni akadi mli lɛ; ejaakɛ eji kpiti ni fiteɔ nii; ni esa akɛ akɛ la ashã.
53“Shi kɛji osɔfo lɛ kwɛ, ni ena akɛ nɔ ni ekadi mli lɛ elɛɛko yɛ atade lɛ loo kpãi ni akɛlo lɛ, loo nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni akɛ kooloo wolo fee lɛ mli lɛ, 54no lɛ osɔfo lɛ afã akɛ afɔ nɔ ni kpiti lɛ ekadi mli lɛ he, ni esaa eŋa eyi gbii kpawo ekoŋŋ. 55Gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ osɔfo lɛ akwɛ; ni kɛ ena akɛ kadimɔ lɛ su tsakeko be ni afɔ he sɛɛ, ni elɛko hu efatako he lɛ, belɛ nɔ ni kpiti lɛ ekadi mli lɛ he tseee. Akɛ la ashã; hiɛgbɛ ekadi jio, sɛɛgbɛ jio, no kɔɔɔ he eko. 56Shi kɛji osɔfo lɛ kwɛ ni ena akɛ nɔ ni ekadi nii lɛ mli lɛ miilaaje be ni afɔ he sɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ etse he ni kadimɔ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ yɛ atade lɛ loo kooloo wolo lɛ loo kpãi ni akɛlo atade lɛ he. 57Shi kɛji aana kadimɔ lɛ lolo yɛ atade lɛ loo kpãi ni akɛlo atade lɛ mli, loo nɔ ni akɛ kooloo wolo fee lɛ mli lɛ, no lɛ nɔ ni ekadi nii lɛ mli lɛ miiku esɛɛ ekoŋŋ, akɛ la ashã nɔ ni mli ni ekadi lɛ. 58Atade lɛ loo kpãi ni akɛlo lɛ loo kooloo wolo nɔ lɛ ni afɔ he lɛ, kɛ nɔ ni ekadi mli lɛ je mli lɛ, afɔ he ekoŋŋ koni ehe atse.
59“Enɛ ji mla ni kã shi hã kpiti ni eshwie kuŋtu loo odonti mama loo kpãi ni akɛloɔ mama lɛ loo nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni akɛ kooloo wolo fee he lɛ. Eji mla hu ni akɛnaa akɛ nɔ ni kpiti eshwie he lɛ he tse aloo ehe tseee.”

english_text:
The Ceremony for People Healed of Leprosy
1The Lord told Moses to say to the people:
2-3 After you think you are healed of leprosy, you must ask for a priest to come outside the camp and examine you. And if you are well, 4he will order someone to bring out two live birds that are acceptable for sacrifice, together with a stick of cedar wood, a piece of red yarn, and a branch from a hyssop plant. 5The priest will order someone to kill one of the birds over a clay pot of spring water. 6Then he will dip the other bird, the cedar, the red yarn, and the hyssop in the blood of the dead bird. 7Next, he will sprinkle you seven times with the blood and say, “You are now clean.” Finally, he will release the bird and let it fly away.
8After this you must wash your clothes, shave your entire body, and take a bath before you are completely clean. You may move back into camp, but you must not enter your tent for seven days. 9Then you must once again shave your head, face, and eyebrows, as well as the hair on the rest of your body. Finally, wash your clothes and take a bath, and you will be completely clean.
10On the eighth day you must bring to the priest two rams and a year-old female lamb that have nothing wrong with them; also bring 300 milliliters of olive oil and 3 kilograms of your finest flour mixed with oil. 11Then the priest will present you and your offerings to me at the entrance to my sacred tent. 12There he will offer one of the rams, together with the oil, as a sacrifice to make things right. He will also lift them up to show that they are dedicated to me. 13This sacrifice is very holy. It belongs to the priest and must be killed in the same place where animals are killed as sacrifices for sins and as sacrifices to please me.
14The priest will smear some of the blood from this sacrifice on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot. 15He will then pour some of the olive oil into the palm of his left hand, 16dip a finger of his right hand into the oil, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred tent. 17Next, the priest will smear some of the oil on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot, 18-20and he will pour the rest of the oil from his palm on your head. Then he will offer the other two animals—one as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me, together with a grain sacrifice. After this you will be completely clean.
21If you are poor and cannot afford to offer this much, you may offer a ram as a sacrifice to make things right, together with 300 milliliters of olive oil and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil as a grain sacrifice. The priest will then lift these up to dedicate them to me. 22Depending on what you can afford, you must also offer either two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me. 23The priest will offer these to me in front of the sacred tent on the eighth day.
24-25The priest will kill this ram for the sacrifice to make things right, and he will lift it up with the olive oil in dedication to me. Then he will smear some of the blood on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot.
26The priest will pour some of the olive oil into the palm of his left hand, 27then dip a finger of his right hand in the oil and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred tent. 28He will smear some of the oil on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot, just as he did with the blood of the sacrifice to make things right. 29-31And he will pour the rest of the oil from his palm on your head.
Then, depending on what you can afford, he will offer either the doves or the pigeons together with the grain sacrifice. One of the birds is the sacrifice for sin, and the other is the sacrifice to please me. After this you will be completely clean.
32These are the things you must do if you have leprosy and cannot afford the usual sacrifices to make you clean.
When There Is Mildew in a House
33The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
34After I have given you the land of Canaan as your permanent possession, here is what you must do, if I ever put mildew on the walls of any of your homes. 35First, you must say to a priest, “I think there is mildew on the wall of my house.”
36The priest will reply, “Empty the house before I inspect it, or else everything in it will be unclean.”
37If the priest discovers greenish or reddish spots that go deeper than the surface of the walls, 38he will have the house closed for seven days. 39Then he will return and check to see if the mildew has spread. 40-41If so, he will order someone to scrape the plaster from the walls, remove the stones covered with mildew, then haul everything off and dump it in an unclean place outside the town. 42Afterwards the wall must be repaired with new stones and fresh plaster.
43If the mildew appears a second time, 44the priest will come and say, “This house is unclean. It's covered with mildew that can't be removed.” 45Then he will have the house torn down and every bit of wood, stone, and plaster hauled off to an unclean place outside the town. 46Meanwhile, if any of you entered the house while it was closed, you will be unclean until evening. 47And if you either slept or ate in the house, you must wash your clothes.
48On the other hand, if the priest discovers that mildew hasn't reappeared after the house was newly plastered, he will say, “This house is clean—the mildew has gone.” 49Then, to show that the house is now clean, he will get two birds, a stick of cedar wood, a piece of red yarn, and a branch from a hyssop plant and bring them to the house. 50He will kill one of the birds over a clay pot of spring water 51-52and let its blood drain into the pot. Then he will dip the cedar, the hyssop, the yarn, and the other bird into the mixture of blood and water. Next, he will sprinkle the house seven times with the mixture, then the house will be completely clean. 53Finally, he will release the bird and let it fly away, ending the ceremony for purifying the house.
54-57These are the things you must do if you discover that you are unclean because of an itch or a sore, or that your clothing or house is unclean because of mildew.
translation_text:
Mɔ ni eye hewolo nɔ hela hetsuumɔ
1Yehowa kɛ Mose wie ni ekɛ mlai ni abaatsi tã nɛɛ hã lɛ. 2 Mlai nɛɛ kã shi hã mɔ ni eye kpiti ni ehe etã hetsuumɔ. Gbi nɔ ni aaakɛɛ akɛ ehe etse lɛ, akɛ lɛ aba osɔfo lɛ ŋɔɔ. 3Osɔfo lɛ kɛ lɛ aje kpo kɛya nsra lɛ sɛɛ ni eyakwɛ lɛ. Kɛji kpiti ni shwie helatsɛ lɛ etã yɛ ehe lɛ, 4osɔfo lɛ afã mɔ ni abaatsuu ehe lɛ koni ekɛ loofɔji hiɛkãalɔi enyɔ ni he tse kɛ tsenedru tso kɛ kpãa tsuru kɛ hisopo aba. 5Osɔfo lɛ afã ni agbe loofɔji lɛ ateŋ ekome yɛ kã ni nu ŋmɔŋ yɔɔ mli nɔ. 6Osɔfo lɛ amɔ loofɔlɔ ni hiɛ kã lɛ. Ekɛ tsenedru tso lɛ kɛ kpãa tsuru lɛ kɛ hisopo lɛ afata he ni ekɛ fɛɛ atsɔ loofɔlɔ ni agbe lɛ yɛ kã ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ lá lɛ mli. 7 Etsɔ la lɛ eshwã kpitiyelɔ ni abaatsuu ehe lɛ nɔ shii kpawo koni ekɛtsuu ehe. Eŋmɛɛ loofɔlɔ ni hiɛ kã lɛ he ni eya ŋa lɛ nɔ. 8 Mɔ ni atsuɔ ehe lɛ afɔ etadei lɛ ahe. Eshɛ eyiteŋ tsɔi fɛɛ, ni ekɛ nu aju ehe koni ehe atse. No sɛɛ lɛ, eba shitoohe lɛ mli, shi ekabote ebuu lɛ mli gbii kpawo. 9Gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ esaa eshɛ eyiteŋ tsɔi ekoŋŋ kɛ etsɛŋ kɛ ehiŋmɛi sɛɛ tsɔi kɛ ehe tsɔi fɛɛ. Efɔ etadei ahe, ni ekɛ nu aju ehe; kɛkɛ lɛ ehe baatse.
10Gbi ni ji kpaanyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mɔ ni atsuɔ ehe lɛ kɛ gwantɛŋbii enyɔ ni kpa ko bɛ amɛhe kɛ gwantɛŋ yoo kome ni eye afi ni kpa ko bɛ ehe kɛ ŋmãa mamu kiloi etɛ̃ ni akɛ mu ewo mli kɛ mu lita mlijai etɛ̃ mli ekome aba. 11Osɔfo ni tsuuɔ gbɔmɔ lɛ he lɛ aŋɔ lɛ kɛ nibii nɛɛ fɛɛ kɛba Yehowa hiɛ yɛ Kpee Buu shinaa lɛ naa. 12Emɔ gwantɛŋbii lɛ ateŋ ekome ekɛbahã akɛ sɔ̃ afɔle kɛ mu lita mlijai etɛ̃ mli ekome lɛ hu, koni ekɛba Yehowa hiɛ akɛ keenii titri ko. 13 Egbe gwantɛŋbi lɛ yɛ he ni agbeɔ esha afɔle kɛ shãa afɔle lɛ yɛ lɛ, yɛ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ, ejaakɛ sɔ̃ afɔle lɛ jio, esha afɔle lɛ jio, fɛɛ lɛ osɔfo lɛ nɔ ni; eji nɔ ko krɔŋkrɔŋ naakpa. 14 Agbɛnɛ osɔfo lɛ kɛ sɔ̃ afɔle lɛ lá lɛ eko asa mɔ ni atsuɔ ehe lɛ ninejurɔ toi naa kɛ eninejurɔ gɔnti naa, kɛ enanejurɔ gɔnti naa. 15Kɛkɛ lɛ osɔfo lɛ awo mu lɛ ni efo eko ewo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ enine abɛku kɔkɔ mli. 16Ekɛ eninejurɔ wao atsɔ mu ni yɔɔ ebɛku lɛ mli lɛ eko eshwã shii kpawo yɛ Yehowa hiɛ. 17Osɔfo lɛ kɛ mu ni eshwɛ yɛ edɛŋ lɛ eko asa mɔ ni atsuɔ ehe lɛ ninejurɔ toi naa kɛ eninejurɔ gɔnti naa kɛ enanejurɔ gɔnti naa he ni akɛ sɔ̃ afɔle lɛ lá lɛ sa lɛ. 18Mu ni eshwɛ yɛ osɔfo lɛ dɛŋ lɛ, efɔse eshwie mɔ ni atsuuɔ ehe lɛ yiteŋ koni osɔfo lɛ akpãtã ahã lɛ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ.
19Kɛkɛ lɛ osɔfo lɛ ashã esha afɔle lɛ koni ekɛjie mɔ ni atsuuɔ ehe lɛ he muji lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, osɔfo lɛ agbe too ni akɛ baashã shãa afɔle lɛ; 20no sɛɛ lɛ osɔfo lɛ ashã shãa afɔle kɛ niyenii afɔle lɛ yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ, koni ekɛtsuu mɔ lɛ he; kɛkɛ lɛ ehe baatse. 21Shi kɛ eji ohiafo ni enaaa enɛɛmɛi lɛ, no lɛ ekɛ gwantɛŋbi kome aba akɛ sɔ̃ afɔle, keenii titri ko ni akɛkpãtã ahã lɛ ni. Ekɛ ŋmãa mamu kilo kome ni awo mli mu hu aba akɛ niyenii afɔle, kɛ mu lita mlijai etɛ̃ mli ekome. 22Asaŋ ekɛ kosɛɛ okpoi enyɔ loo shĩa okpoi bibii enyɔ aba; emli eko fɛɛ eko ni enine aaashɛ nɔ. Akɛ ekome afee esha afɔle, ni akɛ ekome hu afee shãa afɔle. 23Ehetsuumɔ gbi ni ji kpaanyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ekɛ nibii nɛɛ aba abahã osɔfo lɛ yɛ Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ naa yɛ Yehowa hiɛ. 24Osɔfo lɛ aŋɔ gwantɛŋbi lɛ ni akɛshãa sɔ̃ afɔle lɛ kɛ mu lita mlijai etɛ̃ mli ekome lɛ ni ekɛba Yehowa hiɛ akɛ keenii titri ko. 25Osɔfo lɛ agbe gwantɛŋbi ni akɛshãa sɔ̃ afɔle lɛ. Ekɛ toobi lɛ lá lɛ eko asa mɔ ni atsuuɔ ehe lɛ ninejurɔ toi naa kɛ eninejurɔ gɔnti naa kɛ enanejurɔ gɔnti naa. 26Osɔfo lɛ afo mu lɛ eko awo enine abɛku kɔkɔ mli. 27Ekɛ eninejurɔ wao atsɔ mu ni yɔɔ ebɛku lɛ eko eshwã shii kpawo yɛ Yehowa hiɛ. 28Osɔfo lɛ kɛ mu ni yɔɔ edɛŋ lɛ eko asa mɔ ni atsuuɔ ehe lɛ ninejurɔ toi naa, kɛ eninejurɔ gɔnti naa, kɛ enanejurɔ gɔnti naa, eko fɛɛ eko lɛ akɛsa he ni lá ni akɛshã sɔ̃ afɔle lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. 29Mu ni eshwɛ yɛ osɔfo lɛ dɛŋ lɛ, efɔse eshwie mɔ ni atsuuɔ ehe lɛ yiteŋ, koni ekɛkpãtã ehã lɛ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ. 30Enɛ sɛɛ lɛ, okpoi lɛ ateŋ eko fɛɛ eko nɔ, ni enine aaashɛ, kosɛɛ okpoi jio, shĩa okpoi jio, 31osɔfo lɛ kɛ ekome afee esha afɔle, ni ekɛ ekome hu afee shãa afɔle efata niyenii afɔle lɛ he. Efee enɛ ni ekɛkpãtã ehã mɔ ni atsuuɔ ehe lɛ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ. 32Enɛ ji mla ni kã shi hã mɔ ni yeɔ kpiti ni enine shɛɛɛ nii ni akɛbaatsuu ehe lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ.
Kpiti yɛ shĩai amli
33Yehowa kɛ mlai ni abaatsi tã nɛɛ hã Mose kɛ Aaron. 34Kɛ nyɛshɛ Kanaan shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mi diɛŋtsɛ mikɛhã nyɛ ni nyɛye nɔ lɛ nɔ, ni mihã kpiti shwie shĩa ko he yɛ nyɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, 35 no lɛ nakai shĩa lɛ tsɛ lɛ aya ni eyakɛɛ osɔfo lɛ akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ko tamɔ kpiti eshwie eshĩa lɛ he. 36Osɔfo lɛ afã ni ajie shĩa lɛ mli nii kɛje kpo dani osɔfo lɛ abote shĩa lɛ mli ni eyakwɛ nɔ ni eshwie he lɛ. Kɛji afeee nakai lɛ, no lɛ shĩa lɛ mli nii fɛɛ baatsɔ̃ nii ni he tseee. 37 Kɛ osɔfo lɛ yakwɛ, ni ena akɛ nɔ ni eshwie shĩa lɛ gbogboi lɛ ahe lɛ, fɔji ŋɔlii kɛ etsuji ni, ni amɛmiikpe kɛmiibote gbogboi lɛ amli lɛ, 38no lɛ eje kpo ni eŋmɛ agbo lɛ mli kɛyashi gbii kpawo. 39Gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ osɔfo lɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Kɛji ekwɛ, ni ena akɛ fɔji lɛ elɛɛlɛɛ yɛ gbogboi lɛ ahe lɛ, 40no lɛ efã ni ajie tɛi ni hela lɛ eshwie he lɛ koni ashɛrɛ ashwie maŋ lɛ sɛɛ he ko ni tseee. 41No sɛɛ lɛ, aŋmala shĩa lɛ mligbɛ gbogboi lɛ fɛɛ he kɛ kpe, ni akɛ su ni aŋmala lɛ ayashwie maŋ lɛ sɛɛ yɛ he ko ni tseee. 42Akɛ tɛi krokomɛi ahɔlɔ tɛi ni afamɔ lɛ anajiaŋ, ni akɛ su hee ama gbogboi lɛ ahe.
43Kɛji hela lɛ ku sɛɛ eshwie gbogboi lɛ ahe ekoŋŋ, ni eje shi faŋŋ yɛ he ni afamɔ tɛi lɛ ni aŋmala gbogboi lɛ ahe ni ama he yɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, 44osɔfo lɛ aya ni eyakwɛ. Kɛji ena akɛ nɔ ni eshwie shĩa lɛ he lɛ miilɛɛ yɛ gbogboi lɛ ahe ekoŋŋ lɛ, belɛ hela ko ni tamɔ kpiti ni fiteɔ nii yɛ shĩa lɛ; shĩa lɛ he tseee. 45Akumɔ shĩa lɛ ashwie shi, etɛi lɛ kɛ mplaŋi lɛ kɛ shĩa lɛ sũ lɛ fɛɛ, ni aloo kɛje maŋ lɛ mli kɛyashwie he ko ni tseee. 46 Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni boteɔ shĩa lɛ mli be mli ni ala agbo lɛ mli lɛ, ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ; 47ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaawɔ shĩa lɛ afɔ etadei ahe; ni mɔ ni aaaye nii yɛ shĩa lɛ afɔ etadei ahe.
48Shi kɛji osɔfo lɛ ba shĩa lɛ ni ebakwɛ, ni ena akɛ nɔ ni shwie he lɛ ekuko esɛɛ eshwieko shĩa lɛ he kɛjɛ be ni ama shĩa lɛ he ekoŋŋ nɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ ekɛɛ akɛ, shĩa lɛ he tse, ejaakɛ nɔ ni shwie he lɛ etã kwraa. 49Osɔfo lɛ kɛ loofɔji enyɔ kɛ tsenedru tso kɛ kpãa tsuru kɛ hisopo ashã esha afɔle kɛjwira shĩa lɛ. 50Egbe loofɔji lɛ ateŋ ekome yɛ kã ni nuhiŋmɛi ni hoɔ mli nu yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. 51Ekɛ tsenedru tso lɛ kɛ hisopo lɛ kɛ kpãa tsuru lɛ kɛ loofɔlɔ ni hiɛ kã lɛ fɛɛ atsɔ loofɔlɔ ni agbe lɛ lá lɛ kɛ nuhiŋmɛi ni hoɔ mli nu ni yɔɔ kã lɛ mli lɛ mli koni ekɛshwã shĩa lɛ shii kpawo. 52Kɛ efee nɛkɛ lɛ, belɛ ekɛ loofɔlɔ lɛ lá lɛ kɛ nuhiŋmɛi ni hoɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛ loofɔlɔ ni hiɛ kã lɛ kɛ tsenedru tso lɛ kɛ hisopo lɛ kɛ kpãa tsuru lɛ ejwra shĩa lɛ. 53Agbɛnɛ eŋmɛɛ loofɔlɔ ni hiɛ kã lɛ he, yɛ maŋ lɛ agbo lɛ naa, koni efiliki kɛya ŋa lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ nɔ ni osɔfo lɛ atsɔ kɛkpãtã ehã shĩa lɛ nɛ, koni shĩa lɛ he atse. 54Enɛ ji mla ni kã shi hã hewolo nɔ helai srɔtoi ni tamɔ kpiti henɔ: 55-56fala, fafale, loosule, gbɛ̃, fuumɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli muji ni kaa mama mli kɛ gbogbo he mla. 57Eji mla ni akɛnaa nɔ ni he tseee kɛ nɔ ni he tse; hela ni tamɔ kpiti kɛ ehenɔi ahe mla nɛ.

english_text:
Sexual Uncleanness
1The Lord told Moses and Aaron 2to say to the community of Israel:
Any man with an infected penis is unclean, 3whether it is stopped up or keeps dripping. 4Anything that he rests on or sits on is also unclean, 5-7and if you touch either these or him, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening.
8If you are spit on by the man, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 9-10Any saddle or seat on which the man sits is unclean. And if you touch or carry either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 11If the man touches you without first washing his hands, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 12Any clay pot that he touches must be destroyed, and any wooden bowl that he touches must be washed.
13Seven days after the man gets well, he will be considered clean, if he washes his clothes and takes a bath in spring water. 14On the eighth day he must bring either two doves or two pigeons to the front of my sacred tent and give them to a priest. 15The priest will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me, then I will consider the man completely clean.
16Any man who has a flow of semen must take a bath, but he still remains unclean until evening. 17If the semen touches anything made of cloth or leather, these must be washed, but they still remain unclean until evening. 18After having sex, both the man and the woman must take a bath, but they still remain unclean until evening.
19When a woman has her monthly period, she remains unclean for seven days, and if you touch her, you must take a bath, but you remain unclean until evening. 20-23Anything that she rests on or sits on is also unclean, and if you touch either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 24Any man who has sex with her during this time becomes unclean for seven days, and anything he rests on is also unclean.
25Any woman who has a flow of blood outside her regular monthly period is unclean until it stops, just as she is during her monthly period. 26Anything that she rests on or sits on during this time is also unclean, just as it would be during her period. 27If you touch either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening.
28Seven days after the woman gets well, she will be considered clean. 29On the eighth day, she must bring either two doves or two pigeons to the front of my sacred tent and give them to a priest. 30He will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me; then I will consider the woman completely clean.
31When any of you are unclean, you must stay away from the rest of the community of Israel. Otherwise, my sacred tent will become unclean, and the whole nation will die.
32-33These are the things you men must do if you become unclean because of an infected penis or if you have a flow of semen. And these are the things you women must do when you become unclean either because of your monthly period or an unusual flow of blood. This is also what you men must do if you have sex with a woman who is unclean.
translation_text:
Gbɔmɔtso mli nu ni he tseee
1Yehowa kɛ mlai ni abaatsi tã nɛɛ hã Mose kɛ Aaron 2 ni amɛkɛhã Israelbii lɛ. Kɛji nu miiho yɛ nuu ko nuutso mli lɛ, nu ni hoɔ lɛ he tseee. 3Nu lɛ kã he eeho jio, nuutso lɛ etsi enaa ni ehã ekpa hoo jio, gbɔmɔ lɛ he tseee. 4Saa fɛɛ saa ni mɔ ni he hoɔ nu lɛ kãa nɔ lɛ he tseee, ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni etaa nɔ lɛ he tseee. 5Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni taa saa lɛ he lɛ afɔ etadei ahe ni ekɛ nu aju ehe; ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.
6Mɔ ni taa mɔ ni he hoɔ nu lɛ sɛi nɔ lɛ afɔ etadei ahe, ni ekɛ nu aju ehe; ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. 7Mɔ ni taa mɔ ni he hoɔ nu lɛ he lɛ, efɔ etadei ahe, ni ekɛ nu aju ehe; ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. 8Kɛji mɔ ni he hoɔ nu lɛ tsɛ̃ lajɔ̃ eshwie mɔ ni he tse he lɛ, mɔ ni atsɛ̃ lajɔ̃ ashwie ehe lɛ afɔ etadei ahe, ni ekɛ nu aju ehe; ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. 9Sɛi ni mɔ ni he hoɔ nu lɛ taa nɔ yɛ shwiili mli loo kooloo nɔ lɛ he tseee. 10Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni taa nɔ ko ni mɔ ni he hoɔ nu lɛ eta nɔ lɛ he lɛ, ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni woɔ nɔ ko ni tamɔ nakai lɛ, efɔ etadei ahe, ni ekɛ nu aju ehe; ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. 11Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni mɔ ni he hoɔ nu ni efɔko edɛ aaata ehe lɛ, efɔ etadei ahe, ni ekɛ nu aju ehe; ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. 12 Sũ nii ni mɔ ni he hoɔ nu lɛ aaata he lɛ, ajwa; ni tso nii fɛɛ tso nii ni eeeta he lɛ, akɛ nu afɔ mli.
13Kɛji mɔ ni he hoɔ nu lɛ hela lɛ tã lɛ, emɛ gbii kpawo. Efɔ etadei ahe ni ekɛ nuhiŋmɛi ni hoɔ mli nu aju ehe; kɛkɛ lɛ ehe baatse. 14 Gbi ni ji kpaanyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ekɛ kosɛɛ okpoi enyɔ loo shĩa okpoi enyɔ aya Yehowa hiɛ yɛ Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ naa ni ekɛyahã osɔfo lɛ. 15Osɔfo lɛ kɛ ekome afee esha afɔle ni ekɛ ekome hu afee shãa afɔle, koni ekpãtã ehã lɛ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ yɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ.
16 Kɛji nuu ko shwie ehe shi lɛ, ekɛ nu aju ehe fɛɛ; ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. 17Mama fɛɛ mama kɛ kooloo wolo fɛɛ kooloo wolo ni nu nɛɛ eko aaatee mli lɛ akɛ nu afɔ he; ni ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. 18Kɛji nuu ko kɛ yoo ko wɔ, ni nuu lɛ henu je emli lɛ, amɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ amɛkɛ nu aju amɛhe; amɛhe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.
19 Kɛji yoo ko fee yeianii ni ehe miiho lá lɛ, ehe tseee gbii kpawo. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni taa ehe lɛ he tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. 20Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yoo lɛ ekã nɔ gbii abɔ ni etee tsuiasɛɛ lɛ he tseee; ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni eta nɔ hu he tseee. 21Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni taa yoo ni etee tsuiasɛɛ lɛ saa he lɛ, afɔ etadei ahe, ni ekɛ nu aju ehe; ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. 22Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni taa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yoo lɛ eta nɔ lɛ he lɛ afɔ etadei ahe, ni ekɛ nu aju ehe; ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. 23Kɛji mɔ ko ta nɔ ko ni yɔɔ yoo lɛ saa nɔ loo nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni eta nɔ lɛ he lɛ, ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. 24Kɛji nuu ko kɛ yoo lɛ na bɔlɛ ni lá ni hoɔ yɛ yoo lɛ he lɛ eko tee ehe lɛ, no lɛ ehe tseee gbii kpawo, ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ekã nɔ lɛ he tseee.
25Kɛji yoo ko he ho lá gbii pii be ni eshɛko etsuiasɛɛyaa be lɛ, aloo ehe ho lá yɛ etsuiasɛɛyaa be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ gbii abɔ fɛɛ ni ehe hoɔ la lɛ ehe tseee, tamɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ yɛ etsuiasɛɛyaa gbii lɛ amli lɛ pɛ. 26Saa fɛɛ saa ni ekã nɔ gbii abɔ ni ehe hoɔ lá lɛ tamɔ etsuiasɛɛyaa saa lɛ pɛ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni eta nɔ lɛ he tseee tamɔ bɔ ni ehe tseee yɛ etsuiasɛɛyaa be lɛ mli lɛ. 27Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni taa nibii nɛɛ eko he lɛ, ehe tseee. Efɔ etadei ahe, ni ekɛ nu aju ehe; ehe tseee kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. 28Kɛji lá ni hoɔ yɛ yoo lɛ he lɛ sɛɛ fo lɛ, ekane gbii kpawo ehã ehe; no sɛɛ lɛ ehe aaatse. 29Gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ ekɛ kosɛɛ okpoi enyɔ loo shĩa okpoi bibii enyɔ aba abahã osɔfo lɛ yɛ Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ naa. 30Osɔfo lɛ kɛ okpoi lɛ ateŋ ekome afee esha afɔle, ni ekɛ ekome hu afee shãa afɔle ni ekɛkpãtã ehã lɛ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ ni ehe aaatse.
31Yehowa kɛɛ Mose koni ebɔ Israelbii lɛ kɔkɔ yɛ amɛhe ni tseee lɛ hewɔ koni amɛkabule miKpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ ni amɛbagboi.
32Enɛ ji mla ni kã shi hã mɔ ni he hoɔ nu kɛ mɔ ni nu jeɔ emli ni no hãaa ehe atse. 33Mla nɛɛ kã shi hã mɔ ni kɛ yoo ni miifee yeianii wɔɔ kɛ nuu ko ni kɛ yoo ni he tseee naa bɔlɛ.

english_text:
The Great Day of Forgiveness
1-2 Two of Aaron's sons had already lost their lives for disobeying the Lord, so the Lord told Moses to say to Aaron:
I, the Lord, appear in a cloud over the place of mercy on the sacred chest, which is behind the inside curtain of the sacred tent. And I warn you not to go there except at the proper time. Otherwise, you will die!
3 Before entering this most holy place, you must offer a bull as a sacrifice for your sins and a ram as a sacrifice to please me. 4You will take a bath and put on the sacred linen clothes, including the underwear, the robe, the sash, and the turban. 5Then the community of Israel will bring you a ram and two goats, both of them males. The goats are to be used as sacrifices for sin, and the ram is to be used as a sacrifice to please me.
6Aaron, you must offer the bull as a sacrifice of forgiveness for your own sins and for the sins of your family. 7Then you will lead the two goats into my presence at the front of the sacred tent, 8where I will show you which goat will be sacrificed to me and which one will be sent into the desert to the demon Azazel. 9After you offer the first goat as a sacrifice for sin, 10the other one must be presented to me alive, before you send it into the desert to take away the sins of the people.
11You must offer the bull as a sacrifice to ask forgiveness for your own sins and for the sins of your family. 12Then you will take a fire pan of live coals from the bronze altar, together with two handfuls of finely ground incense, into the most holy place. 13There you will present them to me by placing the incense on the coals, so that the place of mercy will be covered with a cloud of smoke. Do this, or you will die right there! 14Next, use a finger to sprinkle some of the blood on the place of mercy, which is on the lid of the sacred chest; then sprinkle blood seven times in front of the chest.
15 Aaron, you must next sacrifice the goat for the sins of the people, and you must sprinkle its blood inside the most holy place, just as you did with the blood of the bull. 16By doing this, you will take away the sins that make both the most holy place and the people of Israel unclean. Do the same for the sacred tent, which is here among the people. 17Only you are allowed in the sacred tent from the time you enter until the time you come out. 18After leaving the tent, you will purify the bronze altar by smearing each of its four corners with some of the blood from the bull and from the goat. 19Use a finger to sprinkle the altar seven times with the blood, and it will be completely clean from the sins of the people.
20After you have purified the most holy place, the sacred tent, and the bronze altar, you must bring the live goat to the front of the tent. 21 There you will lay your hands on its head, while confessing every sin the people have committed, and you will appoint someone to lead the goat into the desert, so that it can take away their sins. 22Finally, this goat that carries the heavy burden of Israel's sins must be released deep in the desert.
23-24 Aaron, after this you must go inside the sacred tent, take a bath, put on your regular priestly clothes, and leave there the clothes you put on before entering the most holy place. Then you will come out and offer sacrifices to please me and sacrifices for your sins and for the sins of the people. 25The fat from these sacrifices for sin must be sent up in smoke on the bronze altar.
26The one who led the goat into the desert and sent it off to the demon Azazel must take a bath and wash his clothes before coming back into camp. 27 The remains of the bull and the goat whose blood was taken into the most holy place must be taken outside the camp and burned. 28And whoever does this must take a bath and change clothes before coming back into camp.
The Lord told Moses to say to the people:
29 On the tenth day of the seventh month of each year, you must go without eating to show sorrow for your sins, and no one, including foreigners who live among you, is allowed to work. 30This is the day on which the sacrifice for the forgiveness of your sins will be made in my presence, 31and from now on, it must be celebrated each year. Go without eating and make this a day of complete rest just like the Sabbath. 32The high priest must offer the sacrifices for cleansing from sin, while wearing the sacred linen clothes. 33He will offer these sacrifices for the most holy place, the sacred tent, the bronze altar, all the priests, and for the whole community. 34You must celebrate this day each year—it is the Great Day of Forgiveness for all the sins of the people of Israel.
Moses did exactly as the Lord had commanded.
translation_text:
Najiaŋtoo gbi
1 Yehowa kɛ Mose wie yɛ Aaron bihii enyɔ ni kɛ la ni bɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ tee Yehowa hiɛ ni amɛgboi lɛ agbele lɛ sɛɛ, ni ekɛɛ, 2 “Okɛ onyɛmi Aaron awie koni ekabote He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ mli kɛmiiya muhɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ mɔbɔnalɛ sɛi ni bu Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ, be fɛɛ be kɛkɛ, koni ekagbo, ejaakɛ mapue yɛ atatu mli yɛ naanɔ ni bu Adeka lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. 3 Nii ni Aaron kɛbote He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ nɛ: tsinanuu oblanyo ni akɛfee esha afɔle kɛ ojwɛni ni akɛfee shãa afɔle.
4 “Aaron kɛ nu aju ehe, ni ewo klala flaka krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ kɛ klala tswakotoi lɛ. Ekɛ klala mlifiinii lɛ afi emli, ni ekɛ klala tɔɔbaŋ afi eyitso. Atadei ni yɔɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ nɛ. 5Israel asafo ku lɛ ahã Aaron too kpakpoi enyɔ ni akɛbaashã esha afɔle, kɛ ojwɛni kome ni akɛbaafee eshãa afɔle. 6 Aaron kɛ tsinanuu ni ji lɛ diɛŋtsɛ enɔ lɛ abashã esha afɔle kɛjie lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe eshai kɛ ewe lɛ he eshai. 7Agbɛnɛ ekɛ too kpakpoi enyɔ lɛ abadamɔ Yehowa hiɛ yɛ Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ naa. 8Efɔ̃ amɛnɔ oshiki; oshiki kome hã Yehowa kɛ oshiki kome hã Azazel. 9Aaron kɛ too kpakpo ni Yehowa oshiki lɛ gbee enɔ lɛ aba ni ekɛbashã esha afɔle. 10Shi too kpakpo ni Azazel oshiki lɛ gbee enɔ lɛ, ekɛ lɛ abadamɔ Yehowa hiɛ ni kooloo lɛ hiɛ kã. Eŋmɛɛ kooloo lɛ he ehã Azazel yɛ ŋa kplanaa lɛ nɔ koni ewo maŋ lɛ he eshai lɛ kɛya.
11“Aaron kɛ etsinanuu lɛ aba akɛ esha afɔle ahã lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe kɛ ewe lɛ, ni egbe. 12Eloo ŋai kɛ la ŋɛsu obɔ̃ yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ, yɛ Yehowa hiɛ, kɛ tsofakɛŋma ni ashi bɔdɔbɔdɔ ekɔkɔi obɔbɔi enyɔ, ni ekɛbote muhɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ. 13Ekɛ ohɛ lɛ ashwie la lɛ nɔ yɛ Yehowa hiɛ yɛ jɛi, ni ohɛ lɛ he lasu kumɔŋŋ lɛ baaha mɔbɔnalɛ sɛi lɛ ni bu Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ nɔ lɛ he, koni Aaron akana ni egbo. 14Ekɛ ewao atsɔ tsinanuu lɛ lá lɛ eko koni ekɛshwã mɔbɔnalɛ sɛi lɛ hiɛgbɛ; ni ekɛ ewao atsɔ lá lɛ eko hu ni ekɛshwã Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ hiɛ shii kpawo.
15 “No sɛɛ lɛ, egbe too kpakpo ni ji maŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛbaashã esha afɔle lɛ. Ekɛ lá lɛ abote He Krɔŋkrɔŋ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli, ni etsɔ eko eshwã mɔbɔnalɛ sɛi lɛ hiɛgbɛ kɛ Kpãŋmɔ Adeka lɛ hiɛgbɛ tamɔ bɔ ni ekɛ tsina lá lɛ fee lɛ. 16 Ni akɛjwira He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ yɛ Israelbii lɛ ahe ni tseee kɛ amɛtũatsemɔi kɛ amɛhe eshai lɛ fɛɛ ahewɔ. Aaron afee nakai nɔŋŋ ehã Kpee Buu lɛ ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ; efee yɛ amɛmuji nii lɛ ahewɔ. 17Be ni Aaron boteɔ Kpee Buu lɛ mli koni eyakpãtã ehã maŋ lɛ, mɔ ko mɔ ko akahi jɛi kɛyashi beyinɔ ni eeeje kpo. Aaron akpãtã ahã lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe kɛ ewe lɛ kɛ Israel maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. 18 No sɛɛ lɛ, eje kpo kɛya afɔleshãa latɛ ni ma Yehowa hiɛ lɛ he, ni etsuu he. Ekɛ tsinanuu lɛ lá lɛ eko kɛ too kpakpo lɛ lá lɛ eko asra koji ni yɔɔ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he lɛ ahe kɛkpe. 19Ekɛ ewao atsɔ lá lɛ eko eshwã afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ shii kpawo koni ekɛtsuu he efee lɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ yɛ Israelbii lɛ ahe eshai lɛ ahewɔ.
20“Kɛ Aaron egbe He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ kɛ Kpee Buu lɛ kɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ jwiramɔ lɛ naa lɛ, ekɛ too kpakpo ni hiɛ kã lɛ aba. 21Ekɛ eniji enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ashwie too kpakpo ni hiɛ kã lɛ yiteŋ, ni ejaje Israelbii lɛ atɔ̃mɔi kɛ amɛmla tɔ̃mɔi ni ji amɛhe eshai lɛ fɛɛ eshwie too kpakpo lɛ yiteŋ. Etu lɛ ewo nuu ko ni mɛɔ yɛ jɛi lɛ dɛŋ koni eyaŋmɛɛ ehe ni eya ŋa lɛ nɔ. 22Too kpakpo lɛ baatere amɛtɔ̃mɔi lɛ fɛɛ kɛya ŋa nɔ he ko kplanaa ni mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ, ni jɛi nuu lɛ aŋmɛɛ ehe yɛ. 23 Agbɛnɛ Aaron abote Kpee Buu lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ejie klala atadei ni ewo be ni ebote He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛŋ lɛ, ni eshi yɛ jɛi. 24Eju ehe kɛ nu yɛ He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ, ni ekɔlɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etadei lɛ. Eje kpo ni eyashã lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshãa afɔle lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ shãa afɔle kooloo lɛ koni ekɛkpãtã ehã lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe kɛ maŋ lɛ hu. 25Eshã fɔ ni yɔɔ esha afɔle lɛ he lɛ yɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ. 26Agbɛnɛ mɔ ni kɛ too kpakpo lɛ tee eya ŋmɛɛ ehe ehã Azazel lɛ afɔ etadei ahe, ni ekɛ nu aju ehe dani eba nsra lɛ mli. 27 Akɛ tsinanuu lɛ kɛ too kpakpo lɛ ni akɛshã esha afɔle lɛ ni akɛ amɛlá lɛ tee He Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ mli ni akɛyakpãtã lɛ, aje nsra lɛ mli ni akɛ la ayashã. Ashã amɛloo kɛ amɛhewoji kɛ amɛwamɔ lɛ fɛɛ. 28Mɔ ni yashã lɛ afɔ etadei ahe, ni ekɛ nu aju ehe; no sɛɛ fɛɛ dani eba shitoohe lɛ mli.”
Kpãtãmɔ gbi wulu lɛ
29“Enɛ afee akpɔ ahã nyɛ kɛmiiya naanɔ. Nyɔɔŋ ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma lɛ nɔ lɛ, nyɛgbea nyɛhe hɔmɔ. Nyɛkatsua nitsumɔ ko, nyɛmaŋ lɛ mli bii jio, gbɔ ni ebato nyɛ jio. 30 Ejaakɛ nakai gbi lɛ abaakpãtã ahã nyɛ koni akɛtsuu nyɛhe ni akɛhã nyɛhe atse yɛ Yehowa hiɛ. 31Hejɔɔmɔ gbi wulu ni hã nyɛ. Nyɛgbea nyɛhe hɔmɔ. Akpɔ ni yɔɔ kɛmiiya naanɔ nɛ. 32Kusum ni abaafee kɛkpãtã lɛ, mɔ ni afɔ lɛ mu ni awo lɛ osɔfo koni eye etsɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ewo klala atadei ni ji atadei ni yɔɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ ni efee. 33Ejwra He Krɔŋkrɔŋ fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛ Kpee Buu lɛ kɛ afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ, ni ekpãtã ehã osɔfoi lɛ kɛ maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. 34Enɛ atsɔ̃ akpɔ ni kã shi hã nyɛ kɛmiiya naanɔ, koni akɛkpãtã ahã Israelbii lɛ daa afi shi kome yɛ amɛhe eshai lɛ fɛɛ hewɔ.”
Mose fee bɔ ni Yehowa wo lɛ kitã lɛ.

english_text:
Where To Offer Sacrifices
1The Lord told Moses 2to tell Aaron, his sons, and everyone else in Israel:
3-4Whenever you kill any of your cattle, sheep, or goats as sacrifices to me, you must do it at the entrance to the sacred tent. If you don't, you will be guilty of pouring out blood, and you will no longer belong to the community of Israel. 5And so, when you sacrifice an animal to ask my blessing, it must not be done out in a field, 6but in front of the sacred tent. Then a priest can splatter its blood against the bronze altar and send its fat up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 7Don't ever turn from me again and offer sacrifices to goat-demons. This law will never change.
8Remember! No one in Israel, including foreigners, is to offer a sacrifice anywhere 9except at the entrance to the sacred tent. If you do, you will no longer belong to my people.
Do Not Eat Blood
The Lord said:
10 I will turn against any of my people who eat blood. This also includes any foreigners living among you. 11 Life is in the blood, and I have given you the blood of animals to sacrifice in place of your own. 12That's also why I have forbidden you to eat blood. 13Even if you should hunt and kill a bird or an animal, you must drain out the blood and cover it with soil.
14The life of every living creature is in its blood. That's why I have forbidden you to eat blood and why I have warned you that anyone who does will no longer belong to my people.
15If you happen to find a dead animal and eat it, you must take a bath and wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening. 16If you don't take a bath, you will suffer for what you did wrong.
translation_text:
Krɔŋkrɔŋ nɔ ko ji lá
1Yehowa fã Mose, 2koni ekɛ mlai ni abaatsi tã nɛɛ ahã Aaron kɛ ebihii lɛ kɛ Israelbii lɛ fɛɛ. 3“Israelnyo fɛɛ Israelnyo ni gbeɔ tsina loo gwantɛŋ loo abotia yɛ shitoohe lɛ mli loo shitoohe lɛ sɛɛ, 4 ni ekɛbaaa Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ shinaa lɛ naa koni akɛshã afɔle ahã Yehowa yɛ Yehowa Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ, eye lá yi sɔ̃. Lá efɔse eshwie shi lɛ, ni abuŋ lɛ ashiŋ Yehowa bii anɔ dɔŋŋ. 5Mla nɛɛ oti ji akɛ kooloi ni Israelbii lɛ gbeɔ yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ amɛkɛba ni amɛkɛbahã osɔfo lɛ yɛ Yehowa Kpee Buu Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ shinaa lɛ naa koni amɛgbe amɛkɛshã naanyobɔɔ afɔlei amɛhã Yehowa. 6Osɔfo lɛ atsi lá lɛ eshwie afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ he, yɛ Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ shi, ni eshã fɔ lɛ koni eje ŋma ni Yehowa sumɔɔ lɛ. 7 Israelbii lɛ akafee amɛhe mɛi ni yeee Yehowa anɔkwa ni amɛshãa afɔlei amɛhãa wɔji ni amɛnyiɛɔ amɛsɛɛ. Enɛ atsɔ̃ akpɔ ni yɔɔ ni kã shi hã amɛ kɛ yinɔi fɛɛ ni baaba yɛ amɛsɛɛ kɛmiiya naanɔ.
8“Israelnyo fɛɛ Israelnyo loo gbɔ ni ebato Israelbii lɛ ni shãa shãa afɔle loo 9 afɔle kroko ehãa Yehowa yɛ he kroko ni ekɛbaaa Kpee Buu lɛ shinaa lɛ naa lɛ, abuŋ lɛ ashiŋ Nyɔŋmɔ maŋbii lɛ anɔ.
10 Israelnyo fɛɛ Israelnyo loo gbɔ ni ebato Israelbii akaye loo lɛ mli lá, no lɛ majie mihiɛ maka nakai gbɔmɔ lɛ, ni mi kɛ lɛ baafo takoŋ. 11 Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni hiɛ kã lɛ, elá lɛ mli ewala yɔɔ, ni no hewɔ ni Yehowa fã akɛ afɔse lá lɛ fɛɛ ashwie afɔleshãa latɛ lɛ nɔ koni akɛjie maŋ lɛ he eshai lɛ. Ejaakɛ lá ni ji wala lɛ akɛjieɔ eshai yɛ gbɔmɔ he. 12No hewɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Israelbii lɛ akɛ amɛ jio, gbɔ ni ebato amɛ jio, amɛkaye loo ni lá yɔɔ mli lɛ.
13“Israelnyo fɛɛ Israelnyo kɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni ebato gbɔ yɛ Israel lɛ, kɛji eyagbɔbi ni egbe kooloo loo loofɔlɔ ni ayeɔ lɛ, efɔse elá lɛ eshwie shi, ni ekɛ sũ atsi nɔ, 14 ejaakɛ bɔɔ nii fɛɛ ni hiɛ kã lɛ, amɛlá lɛ mli amɛwala yɔɔ; ni no hewɔ ni mikɛɛ Israelbii lɛ akɛ amɛkaye loo ko loo ko lá lɛ. Bɔɔnɔ fɛɛ bɔɔnɔ lɛ elá mli ewala yɔɔ. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yeɔ lá lɛ abuŋ lɛ ashiŋ Nyɔŋmɔ webii anɔ.
15 “Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yeɔ kooloo ni egbo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ edɛŋ gbele aloo kooloo ni kooloo awuyelɔ ko tserɛ emli lɛ, Israelnyo ji lɛ jio, gbɔ ni ebato Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ji lɛ jio, efɔ etadei ahe ni ekɛnu aju ehe; ebaahi shi kɛyashi gbɛkɛ dani ehe baatse. 16Kɛji efɔɔɔ etadei ahe, ni ejuuu ehe lɛ, no lɛ esɔ̃ akã lɛ diɛŋtsɛ enɔ.”

english_text:
Forbidden Sex
1The Lord told Moses 2to tell the people of Israel:
I am the Lord your God! 3So don't follow the customs of Egypt where you used to live or those of Canaan where I am bringing you. 4I am the Lord your God, and you must obey my teachings. 5 Obey them and you will live. I am the Lord.
6Don't have sex with any of your close relatives, 7especially your own mother. This would disgrace your father. 8 And don't disgrace him by having sex with any of his other wives. 9 Don't have sex with your sister or stepsister, whether you grew up together or not. 10Don't disgrace yourself by having sex with your granddaughter 11or half sister 12-13 or a sister of your father or mother. 14Don't disgrace your uncle by having sex with his wife. 15 Don't have sex with your daughter-in-law 16 or sister-in-law. 17 And don't have sex with the daughter or granddaughter of any woman that you have earlier had sex with. You will be having sex with her closest relatives, and that would make you unclean. 18As long as your wife is alive, don't cause trouble for her by taking one of her sisters as a second wife.
19 When a woman is having her monthly period, she is unclean, so don't have sex with her.
20 Don't have sex with another man's wife—that would make you unclean.
21 Don't sacrifice your children on the altar fires to the god Molech. I am the Lord your God, and that would disgrace me.
22 It is disgusting for a man to have sex with another man.
23 Anyone who has sex with an animal is unclean.
24Don't make yourselves unclean by any of these disgusting practices of those nations that I am forcing out of the land for you. They made themselves 25and the land so unclean, that I punished the land because of their sins, and I made it vomit them up. 26-27Now don't do these sickening things that make the land filthy. Instead, obey my laws and teachings. 28Then the land won't become sick of you and vomit you up, just as it did them. 29-30If any of you do these vulgar, disgusting things, you will be unclean and no longer belong to my people. I am the Lord your God, and I forbid you to follow their sickening way of life.
translation_text:
Nuu kɛ yoo bɔlɛ ni ahiɔ
1Yehowa kɛ Mose wie ni ekɛɛ, 2“Mi ji Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ. 3 Nyɛkabaa nyɛjeŋ tamɔ bɔ ni abaa jeŋ yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni nyɛhi tsutsu lɛ. Asaŋ nyɛkabaa nyɛjeŋ tamɔ bɔ ni abaa jeŋ yɛ Kanaan shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ nyɛ yaa nɔ nɛɛ lɛ. Amɛkusum lɛ nyɛkafea. 4Nyɛyea mimlai kɛ migbɛjianɔtoi lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be. Mi ji Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ. 5 Nyɛyea migbɛjianɔtoi kɛ mimlai lɛ anɔ; nɔ ni kɛji gbɔmɔ ye nɔ ni enaa wala lɛ. Mi ji Yehowa. 6Nuu ko nuu ko akabɛŋkɛ ewekunyo ni ekɛ lɛ na bɔlɛ. Mi ji Yehowa. 7Okɛ onyɛ akawɔ ni okɛshwie otsɛ hiɛ shi; onyɛ ni, kaahã ehiɛ miishwie shi. 8 Okɛ otsɛ ŋa akawɔ; obaashwie otsɛ hiɛ shi. 9 Okɛ onyɛmi yoo ni ji otsɛ loo onyɛ bi akawɔ; alɛ lɛ yɛ nyɛshĩa lɛ mli jio, shĩa kroko mli jio, okɛ lɛ akawɔ. 10Okɛ obinuu biyoo loo obiyoo biyoo akawɔ. Eji nɔ ko ni baashwie bo diɛŋtsɛ ohiɛ shi. 11Okɛ otsɛ ŋa biyoo ni otsɛ fɔ lɛ akawɔ. Onyɛmi yoo ni, ni esaaa akɛ ohãa ehiɛ shwieɔ shi. 12 Okɛ otsɛ nyɛmi yoo akawɔ: otsɛ lá ji lɛ. 13Okɛ onyɛ nyɛmi yoo akawɔ: onyɛ lá ji lɛ. 14Kaabɛŋkɛ otsɛ nyɛmi nuu ŋa ni okɛshwie otsɛ hiɛ shi: onyɛkwɛ ni. 15 Okɛ onyɛmi nuu ŋa akawɔ: ebaahã onyɛmi nuu lɛ hiɛ ashwie shi. 16 Okɛ onyɛmi nuu ŋa akawɔ ni okɛshwie onyɛmi nuu lɛ hiɛ shi. 17 Okɛ yoo kɛ ebiyoo fɛɛ akawɔ, ni asaŋ okaŋɔ obinuu biyoo loo ebiyoo lɛ biyoo ni okɛ lɛ yawɔ. Yoo lɛ lá ji amɛ, ni jeŋba ni tamɔ nakai bɛ fɛo. 18Kaaŋɔ oŋa nyɛmi yoo ofee oŋa bienyɛ; ni okɛ lɛ na bɔlɛ be mli ni oŋa hiɛ kã lolo.
19 “Kaaya yoo ŋɔɔ ni okɛ lɛ ayawɔ be mli ni etee tsuiasɛɛ, ejaakɛ ehe tseee. 20 Okɛ onaanyo ŋa akawɔ ni okɛwo ohe muji. 21 Kaaŋmɛɛ obii lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko he ohã ni akɛ lɛ ja Molek ni akɛ no wo oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ gbɛi he muji. Mi ji Yehowa. 22 Okɛ nuu akawɔ tamɔ okɛ yoo wɔɔ lɛ; aahi. 23 Okɛ kooloo ko kooloo ko akawɔ ni okɛwo ohe muji. Nakai nɔŋŋ esaaa akɛ yoo ko kɛ ehe hãa kooloo ko. 24Nyɛkɛ nii nɛɛ ateŋ eko eko akawoa nyɛhe muji; ejaakɛ enɛɛmɛi fɛɛ jeŋmaji ni mibashwie mahã nyɛ lɛ kɛwoɔ amɛhe muji lɛ. 25Gbɛ nɔ ni tsɔ̃ ni shikpɔŋ fee shikpɔŋ ni he tseee nɛ. Mibagbala etoii yɛ enishaianii lɛ hewɔ, ni ebaafɛ̃ mɛi ni yɔɔ enɔ lɛ eshwie. 26-27Mɛi ni nyiɛ nyɛhiɛ lɛ fee nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ fɛɛ, ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ he muji. Shi nyɛ lɛ nyɛkafea nɛkɛ nihii nii nɛɛ ateŋ eko eko. Maŋnyo jio, gbɔ ni ebato gbɔ jio, nyɛyea Yehowa mlai lɛ kɛ akpɔi lɛ anɔ, 28koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akafɛ̃ nyɛ hu eshwie tamɔ bɔ ni efɛ̃ jeŋmaŋ ni tsɔ nyɛhiɛ lɛ eshwie lɛ. 29Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni feɔ nɛkɛ nihiinii nɛɛ eko lɛ, abuŋ lɛ dɔŋŋ ashiŋ Nyɔŋmɔ mɛi lɛ anɔ.
30“No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛyea nii ni mifã akɛ nyɛfee lɛ anɔ, ni nyɛkafea kusumi ni ahiɔ ni afeɔ dani nyɛba lɛ, koni nyɛkɛkawo nyɛhe muji. Mi ji Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.”

english_text:
Moral and Religious Laws
1The Lord told Moses 2 to say to the community of Israel:
I am the Lord your God. I am holy, and you must be holy too! 3-4 Respect your father and your mother, honor the Sabbath, and don't make idols or images. I am the Lord your God.
5When you offer a sacrifice to ask my blessing, be sure to follow my instructions. 6You may eat the meat either on the day of the sacrifice or on the next day, but you must burn anything left over on the third day. 7If you eat any of it on the third day, the sacrifice will be disgusting to me, and I will reject it. 8In fact, you will be punished for not respecting what I say is holy, and you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
9 When you harvest your grain, always leave some of it standing along the edges of your fields and don't pick up what falls on the ground. 10Don't strip your grapevines clean or gather the grapes that fall off the vines. Leave them for the poor and for those foreigners who live among you. I am the Lord your God.
11 Do not steal or tell lies or cheat others.
12 Do not misuse my name by making promises you don't intend to keep. I am the Lord your God.
13 Do not steal anything or cheat anyone, and don't fail to pay your workers at the end of each day.
14 I am the Lord your God, and I command you not to make fun of the deaf or to cause a blind person to stumble.
15 Be fair, no matter who is on trial—don't favor either the poor or the rich.
16Don't be a gossip, but never hesitate to speak up in court, especially if your testimony can save someone's life.
17 Don't hold grudges. On the other hand, it's wrong not to correct someone who needs correcting. 18 Don't be angry or try to take revenge. I am the Lord, and I command you to love others as much as you love yourself.
19 Breed your livestock animals only with animals of the same kind, and don't plant two kinds of seed in the same field or wear clothes made of different kinds of material.
20If a man has sex with a slave woman who is promised in marriage to someone else, he must pay a fine, but they are not to be put to death. After all, she was still a slave at the time. 21-22The man must bring a ram to the entrance of the sacred tent and give it to a priest, who will then offer it as a sacrifice to me, so the man's sins will be forgiven.
23After you enter the land, you will plant fruit trees, but you are not to eat any fruit from them for the first three years. 24In the fourth year the fruit must be set apart, as an expression of thanks 25to me, the Lord God. Do this, and in the fifth year, those trees will produce an abundant harvest of fruit for you to eat.
26 Don't eat the blood of any animal.
