18That servant was still speaking, when a fourth one dashed up and said, “Your children were having a feast and drinking wine at the home of your oldest son, 19when suddenly a windstorm from the desert blew the house down, crushing all of your children. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
20When Job heard this, he tore his clothes and shaved his head because of his great sorrow. He knelt on the ground, then worshiped God 21 and said:
“We bring nothing at birth;
we take nothing
with us at death.
The Lord alone gives and takes.
Praise the name of the Lord!”
22In spite of everything, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing wrong.
translation_text:
Abonsam ka Hiob ekwɛ
1 Nuu ko hi shi yɛ Uz shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; egbɛi ji Hiob. Esheɔ Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei, ni ewiɔ ehe yɛ efɔŋ he. Eji gbɔmɔ ni shwamɔ ko bɛ ehe, asaŋ efeɔ nii ni ja hu. 2Hiob fɔ bihii kpawo kɛ biyei etɛ̃. 3Eyɛ toi akpei kpawo kɛ yoomai akpei etɛ̃ kɛ tsinai akpe kɛ teji yei ohai enumɔ kɛ tsuji babaoo diɛŋtsɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, Hiob ji bokãgbɛbii lɛ ateŋ niiatsɛ fe fɛɛ.
4Hiob bihii lɛ toɔ naa ekomekome ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛhe okplɔ̃. Kɛji eshɛ mɔ ko nɔ lɛ, ebihii krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ yaa mɔ lɛ we lɛ. Hii lɛ tsuɔ kɛyaa, ni ayatsɛɔ amɛnyɛmimɛi yei etɛ̃ lɛ hu kɛbaa, ni amɛkɛ amɛ bayeɔ nii, ni amɛnuɔ dãa. 5Kɛji aŋmɛ okplɔ̃ lɛ kɛbɔle bihii lɛ anɔ kɛkpe lɛ, Hiob teɔ shi daa leebi maŋkpa, ni eyashãa shãa afɔlei ehãa ebii lɛ ateŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ, yɛ amɛyibɔ naa koni akɛtsuu amɛhe. Ejaakɛ Hiob kɛɔ akɛ, “Benɛ mibihii lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko efee esha ko ni aleee, ni ekwa Nyɔŋmɔ yɛ etsuiŋ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni Hiob feɔ daa.”
6 Be ko lɛ ŋwɛi bɔfoi lɛ ni sɔmɔɔ Nyɔŋmɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ tee Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ. Abonsam futu amɛ kɛtee, ni lɛ hu eyadamɔ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ eko. 7Nyɔŋmɔ bi Abonsam akɛ, “Nɛgbɛ ojɛ obaa nɛɛ?”
Abonsam to he akɛ, “Mijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpaa kɛ shisharamɔ yɛ nɔ.”
8Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa bi Abonsam akɛ, “Osusu mitsulɔ Hiob he akɛ mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni tamɔ lɛ ni eji nuu anɔkwafo ni sheɔ Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei, ni ewiɔ ehe yɛ efɔŋ he, ni shwamɔ ko bɛ ehe, ni efeɔ nɔ ni ja?”
9Abonsam kɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Ani yaka Hiob sheɔ bo, Nyɔŋmɔ, gbeyei lɛ? 10Bɛ ofo afabaŋ okɛbaa lɛ kɛ ewe kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ yi shweshweeshwe. Ojɔɔ eninenaa nitsumɔ nɔ, ni ekooloi eshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. 11 Shi agbɛnɛ bo lɛ kpã onine mli ofite enii ni eyɔɔ lɛ, koni okwɛ akɛ ekwaŋ bo yɛ ohiɛ lo.”
12Ni Yehowa kɛɛ Abonsam akɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ, mijɔɔ enii fɛɛ ni eyɔɔ nɔ miwo odɛ̃ŋ. Lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe kɛkɛ ni okɛ onine akasa.” Kɛkɛ ni Abonsam je Yehowa hiɛ ni etee.
Hiob bii lɛ kɛ ejwetri hiɛ kpãtã
13Gbi ko lɛ Hiob bihii lɛ kɛ ebiyei lɛ eyakpe, ni amɛmiiye nii, ni amɛmiinu wain yɛ amɛnyɛmi nuu onukpa lɛ we lɛ mli. 14Bɔfo ko ba Hiob ŋɔɔ ni ebakɛɛ lɛ akɛ, “Tsinai lɛ miihu, ni teji yei lɛ hu miiye nii yɛ amɛmasɛi. 15 Trukaa ni Sabiabii batua amɛ, ni amɛmɔmɔ kooloi lɛ kɛtee; amɛgbe otsuji lɛ kɛ klante; mikome too pɛ mihe je mli, ni miba mibatswa bo adafi nɛɛ.”
16Tsulɔ lɛ hiɛ wiemɔ lɛ mli lolo kɛkɛ ni tsulɔ kroko ko ba, ni ebakɛɛ akɛ, “Srawa gba kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ni ebayi toi lɛ kɛ tsuji lɛ anɔ, ni eplene amɛ fɛɛ; mikome too pɛ mihe je mli, ni miba mibatswa bo adafi nɛɛ.”
17 Be ni lɛ hu ewieɔ lolo lɛ, tsulɔ kroko ko hu bashɛ shi, ni ebakɛɛ akɛ, “Kaldeabii ba kɛ kui etɛ̃ amɛbatua yoomai lɛ, ni amɛmɔmɔ amɛ kɛtee, ni amɛkɛ klante gbe tsuji lɛ, mikome too pɛ mihe je mli, ni miba mibatswa bo adafi nɛɛ.”
18Tsulɔ lɛ wiemɔ lɛ ma enaa lolo kɛkɛ lɛ naa tsulɔ kroko ko hu eba, ni ebakɛɛ akɛ, “Obihii lɛ kɛ obiyei lɛ miiye nii, ni amɛmiinu wain yɛ amɛnyɛmi nuu nukpa lɛ we lɛ mli 19kɛkɛ ni ahum kpele ko tswa kɛjɛ shiaŋa lɛ nɔ gbɛ, ni ebabote shĩa lɛ mli, ni eshimɔ shĩa lɛ koji ejwɛ lɛ, ni eshĩa lɛ wule eshwie oblahii lɛ anɔ, ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛgboi; mikome too pɛ mihe je mli ni miba mibatswa bo adafi nɛɛ.”
20Kɛkɛ ni Hiob te shi, ni ekɛ awerɛho gbala ehe atade lɛ, eshɛ eyi, ni eho ebu shikpɔŋ, ni esɔle. 21 Ekɛɛ akɛ, “Yayai mikɛjɛ minyɛ musuŋ miba, ni yayai mikɛaaku misɛɛ kɛaatee. Yehowa ni ŋɔ hã, ni Yehowa ebaŋɔ kɛtee; aaajie Yehowa gbɛi lɛ yi kɛ̃!”
22Saji ni ba nɛɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ Hiob shwaaa Nyɔŋmɔ ni no atsɔ̃ esha ahã lɛ.

english_text:
Job Loses His Health
1When the angels gathered around the Lord again, Satan was there with them, 2and the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?”
Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
3Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil. And he hasn't changed, even though you persuaded me to destroy him for no reason.”
4Satan answered, “There's no pain like your own. People will do anything to stay alive. 5Try striking Job's own body with pain, and he will curse you to your face.”
6“All right!” the Lord replied. “Make Job suffer as much as you want, but just don't kill him.” 7Satan left and caused painful sores to break out all over Job's body—from head to toe.
8Then Job sat on the ash-heap to show his sorrow. And while he was scraping his sores with a broken piece of pottery, 9his wife asked, “Why do you still trust God? Why don't you curse him and die?”
10Job replied, “Don't talk like a fool! If we accept blessings from God, we must accept trouble as well.” In all that happened, Job never once said anything against God.
Job's Three Friends
11Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah were three of Job's friends, and they heard about his troubles. So they agreed to visit Job and comfort him. 12When they came near enough to see Job, they could hardly recognize him. And in their great sorrow, they tore their clothes, then sprinkled dust on their heads and cried bitterly. 13For seven days and nights, they sat silently on the ground beside him, because they realized what terrible pain he was in.
translation_text:
Abonsam ka Hiob ekwɛ ekoŋŋ
1Be ni eshɛ gbi ko ni ŋwɛi bɔfoi ni sɔmɔɔ Nyɔŋmɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ tee amɛyadamɔ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ, Abonsam futu amɛ kɛtee, ni lɛ hu eyadamɔ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ eko.
2Yehowa bi Abonsam akɛ, “Nɛgbɛ ojɛ obaa nɛ?”
Abonsam to he akɛ, “Mijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; miyakpa nɔ; ni miyashara shi yɛ nɔ.”
3Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa bi Abonsam akɛ, “Osusu mitsulɔ Hiob he akɛ mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni tamɔ lɛ, ni anɔkwafo ni, ni esheɔ Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei, ni ewiɔ ehe yɛ efɔŋ he; ni shwamɔ ko bɛ ehe, ni efeɔ nɔ ni ja? Ehiɛ enɔkwayeli lɛ mli kpɛŋŋ lolo tsɛbelɛ ohã mite shi miwo lɛ koni mikpãtã ehiɛ yakatswaa!”
4Abonsam to he hã Yehowa akɛ, “Gbɔmɔ baaŋmɛɛ nii fɛɛ ni eyɔɔ he bɔ ni afee kɛkɛ ni eyi ana wala. 5Shi bo lɛ taa egbɔmɔtso he kɛkɛ okwɛ akɛ ekwaŋ bo yɛ ohiɛ lo?”
6Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ Abonsam akɛ, “Ojogbaŋŋ, mijɔɔ enɔ miwo odɛ̃ŋ; shi obaa ewala yi kɛkɛ.”
7No hewɔ lɛ, Abonsam shi Yehowa hiɛ, ni etee; ni ehã asane ni waa mɔ he waa tsɛ̃rɛ Hiob kɛjɛ enaneshi aahu kɛyashi epampam. 8Hiob kɛ ŋɛsuko wamɔɔ ehe, ni eho eta mlu mli. 9Hiob ŋa bi lɛ akɛ, “Ohiɛ anɔkwayeli nɛɛ mli kpɛŋŋ lolo? Mɛɛba okwaaa Nyɔŋmɔ koni ogbo?”
10Hiob kɛɛ eŋa lɛ akɛ, “Oowie tamɔ bɔ ni yei kwashiai lɛ wieɔ lɛ. Nɔ kpakpa lɛ wɔhe kɛjɛ Nyɔŋmɔ dɛŋ. Mɛɛba ni nɔ fɔŋ lɛ wɔkahe?” Enɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, Hiob naa tɛɛɛ shi, ni ewieee wiemɔ gbonyo ko.
Hiob nanemɛi ba eŋɔɔ
11 Be ni nanemɛi etɛ̃ komɛi ni Hiob yɔɔ lɛ nu amanehulu fɛɛ ni eba Hiob nɔ lɛ he lɛ, amɛjɛjɛɛ amɛshihilɛhei amɛba Hiob ŋɔɔ. Enaanyo Elifaz jɛ Teman, ni Bildad jɛ Shua, ni Zofar jɛ Naama. Nanemɛi nɛɛ ye fua akɛ amɛaatee kutuu amɛyaye Hiob ŋkɔmɔ, ni amɛshɛje emii. 12Nanemɛi nɛɛ na Hiob yɛ shɔŋŋ, shi amɛyooo lɛ. Shi be ni amɛyoo Hiob lɛ, amɛfo waa; amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ kɛ dɔlɛ gbala ehe atade, ni amɛloo mlu amɛwo amɛyiteiaŋ. 13Nanemɛi lɛ ho amɛta Hiob masɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ, shwaneshwane kɛ nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ gbii kpawo sɔŋŋ. Amɛteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko kɛ Hiob ewieee wiemɔ kome nɛkɛ, ejaakɛ amɛna akɛ eena nɔ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ.

english_text:
Job's First Speech
Blot Out the Day of My Birth
1 Finally, Job cursed the day
of his birth
2by saying to God:
3Blot out the day of my birth
and the night when my parents
created a son.
4Forget about that day,
cover it with darkness,
5and send thick, gloomy shadows
to fill it with dread.
6Erase that night from the calendar
and conceal it with darkness.
7Don't let children be created
or joyful shouts be heard
ever again in that night.
8Let those with magic powers
place a curse on that day.
9Darken its morning stars
and remove all hope of light,
10because it let me be born
into a world of trouble.
Why Didn't I Die at Birth?
11Why didn't I die at birth?
12Why was I accepted
and allowed to nurse
at my mother's breast?
13Now I would be at peace
in the silent world below
14with kings and their advisors
whose palaces lie in ruins,
15and with rulers once rich
with silver and gold.
16I wish I had been born dead
and then buried, never to see
the light of day.
17In the world of the dead,
the wicked and the weary rest
without a worry.
* 18Everyone is there—
19where captives and slaves
are free at last.
Why Does God Let Me Live?
20Why does God let me live
when life is miserable
and so bitter?
21 I keep longing for death
more than I would seek
a valuable treasure.
22Nothing could make me happier
than to be in the grave.
23Why do I go on living
when God has me surrounded,
and I can't see the road?
24Moaning and groaning
are my food and drink,
25and my worst fears
have all come true.
26I have no peace or rest—
only troubles and worries.
translation_text:
Hiob kɛ esane ŋmɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ
1 Be nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Hiob gbele enaa, ni elomɔ gbi ni afɔ lɛ lɛ. 2Hiob kɛɛ akɛ,
3“Oo Nyɔŋmɔ, hã gbi nɔ
ni afɔ mi lɛ hiɛ akpãtã;
hã gbi gbɛkɛ ni akɛɛ akɛ,
‘Ana binuu musu lɛ hiɛ akpãtã.’
4Hã jeŋ awo duŋ nakai gbi lɛ.
Nyɔŋmɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akatiu esɛɛ,
ni jeŋ akatse yɛ nɔ.
5Hã enɔ atsi kpii kɛ duŋ;
hã atatu kabitii atsi yɛ enɔ,
hã duŋ ni ewo kpii shwane lɛ
awo ehe gbeyei.
6Hã duŋ kpii awo nakai nyɔŋ lɛ mli;
kaahã emii shɛ ehe yɛ afi lɛ mli
gbii lɛ ateŋ eko nɔ;
akabu lɛ ashi afi lɛ mli nyɔji lɛ anɔ.
7Hɛɛ, hã nakai gbi lɛ
atsɔ̃ tamɔ yoo kene;
akanu miishɛɛ gbee he yɛ nɔ!
8Hã mɛi ni lomɔɔ gbi alomɔ lɛ,
mɛi ni le bonso hiɛlawoo lɛ.
9 Hã emaŋkɛ̃ ŋulamii lɛ afɔ̃ɔ kpɛmɔ;
hã etao la, shi ekana eko;
ni ekana hulu haaigbalamɔ.
10Ejaakɛ eŋmɛ gbɛ ni afɔ mi
ni etsiii minyɛ musu naa,
ni ehã miina jaramɔ.
11“Mɛɛba migbooo yɛ mifɔmɔ mli;
mɛɛba minyɔɔɔ be ni ashwie
mi shi lɛ?
12Mɛɛba shuɔ he mi fɔ̃ enɔ;
ni mɛɛba fufɔ hã mina
lɛ miye?
13Kulɛ benɛ miho mikã shi kpoo;
kulɛ bɛ miwɔ ni kulɛ
benɛ mihe ejɔ mi
14kɛkã maŋtsɛmɛi kɛ jeŋ ajinafoi lɛ,
mɛi ni saa mamɔɔ mɔji
ni ekumɔ hãa amɛhe lɛ,
15loo tamɔ lumɛi shikatsɛmɛi,
mɛi ni shĩaiaŋ eyimɔ kɛ jwiɛtɛi lɛ ateŋ.
16Aloo mɛɛba mitsɔ̃ɔɔ sharakemɔ bi
ni enãaa hulu la lɛ?
17Jɛi lɛ yitsoŋwalɔi kpaa
mɔ haomɔ;
ni mɛi ni etɔ amɛ woɔ amɛtsui.
18Gboklɛfoi fɛɛ ahe jɔɔ amɛ
yɛ jɛi;
ni amɛnuuu kpalalɔ gbee dɔŋŋ.
19Mɔ bibioo kɛ mɔ wulu feɔ pɛ
yɛ jɛi,
ni nyɔŋ yeɔ ehe yɛ enuŋtsɔ dɛŋ.
20“Mɛɛba ahãa mɔ ni yɔɔ haomɔ
mli lɛ lá;
ni ahãa mɔ ni werɛ eho ehe wala?
21 Mɔ ni shweɔ gbele, shi gbele baaa lɛ,
ni etsaa shi etaoɔ gbele fe bɔ ni atsaa shi
ataoɔ jwetri ni akɛtee lɛ;
22mɔ ni mii shɛɔ fe nine,
ni enyaaa kɛji ena gbonyobu lɛ.
23Mɛɛba ahãa gbɔmɔ ni aŋɔ
ewala atee,
gbɔmɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ esa eyi lɛ la?
24Ŋkɔmɔyeli etsɔ̃ miniyenii,
ni mifɔseɔ mligbigblimɔ mishwieɔ shi
tamɔ nu.
25Ejaakɛ nɔ gbeyei ni misheɔ lɛ,
no nɔŋŋ baa minɔ,
ni nɔ ni mitsui fãa yɛ he lɛ,
no ji nɔ ni minaa.
26Mihe ejɔko mi,
ni minako miyitso toohe;
mibɛ hejɔlɛ
shi haomɔ miiba lolo.”

english_text:
Eliphaz's First Speech
Please Be Patient and Listen
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
2Please be patient and listen
to what I have to say.
* 3Remember how your words
4have guided and encouraged
many in need.
5But now you feel discouraged
when struck by trouble.
6You respect God and live right,
so don't lose hope!
7No truly innocent person
has ever died young.
8In my experience, only those
who plant seeds of evil
harvest trouble,
9and then they are swept away
by the angry breath of God.
10They may roar and growl
like powerful lions.
But when God breaks their teeth,
11they starve, and their children
are scattered.
A Secret Was Told to Me
12A secret was told to me
in a faint whisper—
13 I was overcome by sleep,
but disturbed by dreams;
14I trembled with fear,
15and my hair stood on end,
as a wind blew past my face.
16It stopped and stood still.
Then a form appeared—
a shapeless form.
And from the silence,
I heard a voice say,
17“No humans are innocent
in the eyes of God
their Creator.
18He finds fault with his servants
and even with his angels.
19Humans are formed from clay
and are fragile as moths,
so what chance do you have?
20Born after daybreak,
you die before nightfall
and disappear forever.
21Your tent pegs are pulled up,
and you leave this life,
having gained no wisdom.”
translation_text:
Klɛŋklɛŋ sanegbaa lɛ
(4.1—14.22)
Elifaz wiemɔ
1Kɛkɛ ni Elifaz, Temannyo lɛ, hã Hiob hetoo ekɛɛ,
2“Kɛji aka bo kɛ wiemɔ lɛ, eeefee bo mlifu lo?
Shi kɛ̃lɛ namɔ aaanyɛ enaa emua?
3Naa, otsɔ̃ɔ mɛi babaoo anii kɛho,
ni owo mɛi hu ni nijiaŋ eje wui
hewalɛ.
4Owiemɔ ehere mɔ ni etɛ́
ni eyaagbee shi;
mɛi ni nakutseiaŋ egbɔjɔ lɛ,
owo amɛ hewalɛ;
ni amɛnyɛ shi amɛdamɔ.
5Shi agbɛnɛ lɛ eshɛ onɔ,
shi onaaa tsui;
esa ohe, no ojijaa nɛɛ.
6Kwɛ jeee Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei ni osheɔ lɛ
no nɔ ohiɛ kã,
ni onɔkwayeli jeŋba lɛ
ji ohiɛnɔkãmɔ?
7“Kɛ ohiɛ awo mli okwɛ!
Namɔ hiɛ ekpãtã pɛŋ
be mli ni efeko efɔŋ ko?
Aloo nɛgbɛ aplene mɛi ni
feɔ jalɛnii yɛ pɛŋ?
8 Bɔ pɛ ni mina nɛ:
Mɛi ni huɔ nɔsha ŋmɔ,
ni amɛduɔ yiwalɛ wui lɛ
nomɛi nɔŋŋ amɛkpaa.
9Nyɔŋmɔ mumɔ ni shwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ
kpãtãa amɛhiɛ,
ni emlifu kɔɔyɔɔ pleneɔ amɛ.
10Ajɔɔ jata huumɔ kɛ oloowɔ gbee he,
ni akumɔ jatabii atsoji fɛɛ.
11Jata ni he wa gboɔ
kɛ enaaa kooloo emɔ ni eye,
ni jata yoo bii gbɛɔ shwãa.
12“Be ko lɛ, minu wiemɔ ko;
efo mitoi naa nyɔɔŋ
13 be ni wɔ ni tsii nyɔɔ mɛi anɔ,
ni ninai ahejwɛŋmɔ
14hã ŋmiŋmi mɔ mi,
ni mikpokpo kɛshɛ miwuiaŋ tɔ̃ɔ.
15Mumɔ ko bafo mihiɛ;
mihe tsɔi te shi damɔ shi.
16Mumɔ lɛ wa edamɔ shi keŋŋ;
shi miyooo esu.”
Shi su ko badamɔ mihiɛ,
jɛi fee koniŋŋ,
kɛkɛ ni minu gbee ko:
17“Aso adesa ko aaaja yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ?
Aso adesa ko he aaatse yɛ ebɔlɔ lɛ hiɛ?
18Kɛji Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ ehe efɔ̃ɔɔ etsuji anɔ,
ni enaa tɔ̃mɔ yɛ ebɔfoi tete ahe lɛ,
19ani osusuɔ akɛ ekɛ ehe
baafɔ gbɔmɔ adesa nɔ,
gbɔmɔ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ su mli
ni afufluɔ lɛ tamɔ omlɛgɛ?
20Gbɔmɔ hiɛ kãa leebi,
shi egboɔ trukaa gbɛkɛnaashi.
Ehiɛ kpãtãa, ni mɔ ko ebuuu
ehe akɔntaa.
21Kɛji atserɛ emli fãi lɛ;
aso amɛgboiii yɛ be mli
ni amɛnako jwɛŋmɔ lolo lɛ?”

english_text:
Eliphaz Continues
Call Out for Help
1Job, call out for help
and see if an angel comes!
2Envy and jealousy
will kill a stupid fool.
3I have seen fools take root.
But God sends a curse,
suddenly uprooting them
4and leaving their children
helpless in court.
5Then hungry and greedy people
gobble up their crops
and grab their wealth.
6Our suffering isn't caused
by the failure of crops;
7it's all part of life,
like sparks shooting skyward.
8Job, if I were you,
I would ask God for help.
9 His miracles are marvelous,
more than we can count.
10God sends showers on earth
and waters the fields.
11He protects the sorrowful
and lifts up those
who have been disgraced.
* 12God swiftly traps the wicked
13 in their own evil schemes,
and their wisdom fails.
14Darkness is their only companion,
hiding their path at noon.
15God rescues the needy
from the words of the wicked
and the fist of the mighty.
16The poor are filled with hope,
and injustice is silenced.
Consider Yourself Fortunate
17 Consider yourself fortunate
if God All-Powerful
chooses to correct you.
18 He may cause injury and pain,
but he will bandage and heal
your cuts and bruises.
19God will protect you from harm,
no matter how often
trouble may strike.
20In times of war and famine,
God will keep you safe.
21You will be sheltered,
without fear of hurtful words
or any other weapon.
22You will laugh at the threat
of destruction and famine.
And you won't be afraid
of wild animals—
23they will no longer be fierce,
and your rocky fields
will become friendly.
24Your home will be secure,
and your sheep will be safe.
25You will have more descendants
than there are blades of grass
on the face of the earth.
26You will live a very long life,
and your body will be strong
until the day you die.
27Our experience has proven
these things to be true,
so listen and learn.
translation_text:
1“Agbɛnɛ Hiob, boo ni otsɛ
akɛ mɔ ko kwraa yɛ ni aaahere
bo nɔ lo?
Bɔfoi lɛ ateŋ namɔ ŋɔɔ oootee?
2Eji anɔkwale sane
akɛ mlila sɔŋŋ gbeɔ kwashia,
ni awuŋayeli gbeɔ mɔ ni hiɛ etɛ̃ɛɛ.
3 Mina kwashiai ni miihe shi ahe dã;
shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni milomɔ amɛwe lɛ.
4Amɛbii kɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ teŋ jɛkɛ,
anaanaa amɛnɔ yɛ koishi,
ni mɔ ko kwraa bɛ
ni aaahere amɛ.
5Hɔmɔwɔlɔi aaaye enikpamɔ nii,
ŋmei ateŋ nii eeena ekɔlɔ;
mɛi aaaye enii he kumai.
6Amanehulu jɛɛɛ mlu mli
baaa,
ni haomɔ hu ekwɛ̃ɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ
shikpɔŋ;
7shi gbɔmɔ lɛ, afɔ lɛ ahã haomɔ,
tamɔ bɔ ni lalilɛi tsɛ̃rɛɔ
kɛjɛɔ la mli kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.
8“Mi ji bo kulɛ, matao Nyɔŋmɔ sɛɛgbɛ,
ni Nyɔŋmɔ dɛŋ matu misane lɛ mawo,
9lɛ mɔ ni efeɔ nibii wuji
ni anaaa naa,
kɛ naakpɛɛ nibii hu ni ehiii kanemɔ lɛ.
10Ehãa nu nɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ,
ni eshwieɔ ŋmɔji anɔ nu;
11 Eholeɔ humii anɔ grɔŋŋ,
ni eshɛjeɔ ŋkɔmɔyelɔi amii.
12Efiteɔ ŋai ni hiɛtɛ̃lɔi tsɔ̃ɔ,
ni ehãa amɛnine nyɛɔ shi.
13 Ekɛ ŋaatsɔlɔi nɔŋŋ aŋaa duɔ amɛ,
ni efiteɔ mɛi fɔ̃ji ayiŋtoi fɔ̃ji lɛ.
14Duŋ woɔ amɛ shwane fintiŋŋ,
ni amɛgbugbuɔ shi shwane mlemle
tamɔ mɛi ni nyiɛɔ nyɔɔŋ.
15Ehereɔ awusai ayiwala
kɛjeɔ mɛi fɔ̃ji adaaŋ,
ni ehereɔ ohiafo yɛ yiwalɔ dɛŋ.
16No hewɔ lɛ, ohiafo yɛ hiɛnɔkãmɔ,
ni toikɔdɔmɔ saneyeli muɔ shi kɔ̃i.
17 “Naa, ajɔɔ mɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ kãa lɛ lɛ,
no hewɔ lɛ, ekafee bo dɔlɛ
kɛji Ofe lɛ kã bo.
18 Ejaakɛ epilaa mɔ, shi lɛ nɔŋŋ efiɔ nɔ,
etswaa mɔ nɔ, ni enine nɔŋŋ tsaa.
19Ebaajie bo yɛ amanehului babaoo amli hu,
nɔ ko nɔ ko efeŋ bo.
20Hɔmɔ be mli lɛ
ebaajie bo yɛ gbele mli,
ni ta mli hu lɛ,
oooje klante naa.
21Nyɔŋmɔ baabaa oyi
kɛjɛ gbɔmɔ naabu fitemɔ mli;
ni kɛji hiɛkpãtãmɔ miiba lɛ
osheŋ gbeyei.
22Oooŋmɔ hiɛkpãtãmɔ kɛ hɔmɔ fɛɛ,
ni osheŋ ŋaŋ kooloi agbeyei.
23Tɛi ehiŋ shikpɔŋ ni ohuɔ nɔ,
ni ŋaŋ kooloi kɛ bo aaahi
shi kpoo.
24Enɛ aaahã ole akɛ owe
lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe,
ni oookpa otoi anaa,
ni ooona akɛ amɛyɛ shweshweeshwe.
25Ooona hiɛnɔkãmɔ akɛ oshwiei
ayi aaafa tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ
jwɛi.
26Ooogbɔ kotokoto dani ooogbo,
tamɔ bɔ ni ŋmãa tsɛɔ ni esaa
dani ebashɛɔ ŋmãagbeemɔhe lɛ.
27Hiob, nɔ ni wɔkpa shi wɔna nɛ.
Anɔkwale ni, no hewɔ lɛ, okɛbu ohe.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
It's Impossible
1Job said:
2It's impossible to weigh
my misery and grief!
3They outweigh the sand
along the beach,
and that's why I have spoken
without thinking first.
4The fearsome arrows
of God All-Powerful
have filled my soul
with their poison.
5Do oxen and wild donkeys
cry out in distress
unless they are hungry?
6What is food without salt?
What is more tasteless
than the white of an egg?
7That's how my food tastes,
and my appetite is gone.
* 8How I wish that God
would answer my prayer
9and do away with me.
10Then I would be comforted,
knowing that in all of my pain
I have never disobeyed God.
11Why should I patiently hope
when my strength is gone?
12I am not strong as stone
or bronze,
13and I have finally reached
the end of my rope.
My Friends, I Am Desperate
14My friends, I am desperate,
and you should help me,
even if I no longer respect
God All-Powerful.
* 15But you are treacherous
16like streams that swell
with melting snow,
17then suddenly disappear
in the summer heat.
18I am like a caravan,
lost in the desert
while searching for water.
19Caravans from Tema and Sheba
20thought they would find water.
But they were disappointed,
21just as I am with you.
Only one look at my suffering,
and you run away scared.
What Have I Done Wrong?
22Have I ever asked any of you
to give me a gift
23or to purchase my freedom
from brutal enemies?
24What have I done wrong?
Show me,
and I will keep quiet.
25The truth is always painful,
but your arguments
prove nothing.
26Here I am desperate,
and you consider my words
as worthless as wind.
27Why, you would sell an orphan
or your own neighbor!
28Look me straight in the eye;
I won't lie to you.
29Stop accusing me falsely;
my reputation is at stake.
30I know right from wrong,
and I am not telling lies.
translation_text:
Hiob wiemɔ
1Hiob here nɔ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ,
2“Oo, mina ni aŋmɛ minaagbai
kɛ mihejaramɔ fɛɛ yɛ nsɛni mli.
3Ejaakɛ aaana akɛ etsii fe ŋshɔnaa shia,
ni no hewɔ ni minaa wiemɔi
lɛ efeŋ yiŋ flɛflɛ lɛ.
4 Ejaakɛ Ofe lɛ etsɛ̃rɛ mi gãi,
ni miinu gãimlibii lɛ anaa ebɔɔ lɛ he yɛ mimli;
Nyɔŋmɔ he ŋmiŋmi emɔ mi emuu.
5Ani ŋaŋ teji bolɔɔ be ni ena jwɛi eekpe,
aloo tsina bolɔɔ yɛ eniyeniiashi?
6Ani ayeɔ nii mutɛ
ni ŋoo bɛ mli?
Aloo mɛɛ ŋɔɔmɔ yɔɔ wuɔwɔlɔ mli
eyɛŋ lɛ mli?
7Nii ni misusuma sumɔɔɔ
akɛ eyeɔ lɛ
nomɛi nɔŋŋ etsɔ̃ miniyenii
ni minyaŋeɔ nɛɛ.
8“Oo, mina ni kulɛ mina mitaomɔnii;
ni Nyɔŋmɔ hã mi mishweenii.
9Mina ni kulɛ Nyɔŋmɔ akpãtã mihiɛ;
eeeŋmɛ enine gbɛ ni
etsɛ̃rɛ mimli!
10Kulɛ mimii aaashɛ mihe,
mimli aaafli mi pam
yɛ minɔnaa ni akɛfaaa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ,
ejaakɛ mikwako Mɔ Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ
wiemɔi lɛ.
11Mihewalɛ enyiɛ hewɔ ni mamia
mihiɛ mamɛ?
Mɛɛ ji minaagbee hewɔ ni
mato mitsui shi?
12Ani mihewalɛ lɛ tɛ hewalɛ ni?
Loo miheloo lɛ akɔɔble ni?
13Anɔkwa, mibɛ hewalɛ ko dɔŋŋ,
minyɛmɔ fɛɛ etã.
14“Mɔ ni kwaa enaanyo ejurɔfeemɔ lɛ,
esheee Ofe lɛ gbeyei.
15 Minyɛmimɛi lɛ yeee anɔkwale
tamɔ faa ni hoɔ,
tamɔ jɔɔ mli faa ni hoɔ kɛyaa ni eŋalaa;
16amɛhiɛ diɔ oookɛɛ aisi,
ni amɛyi tɔ kɛ nyɔŋmɔŋtɛ yɛŋ muɛmuɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ snoo.
17Kɛji dɔlɛ ba pɛ amɛlaaje;
kɛ jeŋ dɔ pɛ amɛmii.
18Gbɛnyiɛlɔi asafo gbaa afã kɛjeɔ amɛgbɛ nɔ,
amɛyafoɔ shi kɛtaoɔ nu yɛ shiaŋa lɛ nɔ
ni amɛhiɛ kpãtãa.
19Tema kɛ Sheba gbɛfalɔi asafoi
taoɔ kɛ hiɛnɔkãmɔ,
20shi amɛhiɛ gboiɔ akɛ
amɛŋɔ amɛhiɛ amɛfɔ nɔ;
ejaakɛ kɛji amɛshɛ he pɛ,
amɛhiɛ shwieɔ shi.
21Bɔ pɛ ni nyɛ ji nyɛhã mi nɛ,
mimanehulu ni nyɛna lɛ,
ehã nyɛmiishe gbeyei.
22Ani mibi akɛ nyɛke mi nɔ ko,
aloo nyɛkɛ nyɛnii ni nyɛyɔɔ
ayawo mɔ ko daaŋnii ahã mi?
23Aloo nyɛhere mi yɛ henyɛlɔ lɛ dɛŋ,
aloo nyɛkpɔ̃ mi yɛ yiwalɔi adɛŋ?
24Nyɛtsɔa mi; nyɛhãa manua shishi,
koni nɔ mli ni mitɔ̃ yɛ lɛ,
mafee diŋŋ.
25Anɔkwa wiemɔ yɛ hewalɛ;
shi mɛni kãmɔ ni nyɛkãa mi lɛ
baanyɛ etsu?
26Ani nyɛsusuɔ akɛ nyɛaanyɛ nyɛkã
gbɔmɔ yɛ wiemɔ hewɔ,
be mli ni mɔ ni bɛ hiɛnɔkãmɔ
wiemɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni lɛ?
27Nyɛaafɔ̃ awusa nɔ oshiki,
ni nyɛaaye nyɛnaanyo yi jara.
28Shi agbɛnɛ, nyɛtɛjea nyɛhiɛ
nyɛkwɛa mi;
ejaakɛ mimaleŋ
mitsɔŋ nyɛ kɔkɔɔkɔ!
29Nyɛfainɛ, awa jɛi!
Nyɛkafea esha;
awa jɛi, misane lɛ ja.
30Ani wiemɔ ko ni ejaaa
eje minaa dã?
Ani mileee nɔ kpakpa
yɛ nɔ fɔŋ he?”

english_text:
Job Continues
Why Is Life So Hard?
1Why is life so hard?
Why do we suffer?
2We are slaves in search of shade;
we are laborers longing
for our wages.
3God has made my days drag on
and my nights miserable.
4I pray for night to end,
but it stretches out
while I toss and turn.
5My parched skin is covered
with worms, dirt, and sores,
6and my days are running out
quicker than the thread
of a fast-moving needle.
Don't Forget!
7I beg you, God, don't forget!
My life is just a breath,
and trouble lies ahead.
8I will vanish from sight,
and no one, including you,
will ever see me again.
9 I will disappear in the grave
or vanish from sight
like a passing cloud.
10Never will I return home;
soon I will be forgotten.
11And so, I cry out to you
in agony and distress.
12Am I the sea or a sea monster?
Is that why you imprison me?
13I go to bed, hoping for rest,
14but you torture me
with terrible dreams.
* 15I'd rather choke to death
than live in this body.
16Leave me alone and let me die;
my life has no meaning.
17 What makes you so concerned
about us humans?
18Why do you test us
from sunrise to sunset?
19Won't you look away
just long enough
for me to swallow?
20Why do you watch us so closely?
What's it to you, if I sin?
Why am I your target
and such a heavy burden?
21Why do you refuse to forgive?
Soon you won't find me,
because I'll be dead.
translation_text:
1“Ani gbɔmɔ wala yɛ shikpɔŋ
nɛɛ nɔ jeee tɔlɛ kɛ deŋmegbomɔ?
Ani ewala gbii tamɔɔɔ
apaafonyo wala gbii?
2Ani etamɔɔɔ bɔ ni apaafonyo
kwɛɔ epaabɔɔnii gbɛ lɛ?
3Nakai mihi shi shwɛm nyɔji abɔ
ni mikã jaramɔ mli nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ fɛɛ.
4Kɛji miho mikã shi lɛ,
bɔ ni mibablaa shi nɛ.
No hewɔ lɛ, nyɔɔŋ hu
sɛɛ jɛkɛɔ,
ni mibiɔ mihe akɛ,
mɛɛbe je aaatsɛre ni mate shi?”
5Miheloo ewo gɔgɔmi kɛ muji;
miheloo lɛ hiɛ gbiɔ
kɛkɛ lɛ eflɛ.
6Migbii lɛ hoɔ oyayaaya
fe mamalolɔ akokrowa tete,
ni amɛmiitã ni hiɛnɔkãmɔ ko bɛ.
7“Nyɔŋmɔ, kaimɔ akɛ miwala lɛ
kɔɔyɔɔ ni,
ni nɔ kpakpa bɛ
ni mihiŋmɛi baana dɔŋŋ.
8Mɔ hiŋmɛi ni naa mi nɛɛ,
enaŋ mi dɔŋŋ.
Ookwɛ mi nɛkɛ nɔŋŋ,
ni malaaje.
9Bɔ ni atatu tseɔ, ni elaajeɔ lɛ,
nakai mɔ ni yaa gbohiiaje
ekuuu esɛɛ ebaaa dɔŋŋ;
10ekuuu esɛɛ ebaaa ewe dɔŋŋ,
ni hiɛ kpaa enɔ kwraa.
11No hewɔ lɛ, mimuaŋ minaa!
Mikɛ mimumɔŋ hejaramɔ baawie;
mibawie misusuma nidɔɔnii.
12Ani ŋshɔ loo bonso ji mi
hewɔ ni otoɔ mɔ ko ni
ebu mihe lɛ?”
13Kɛji mikɛɛ akɛ, “Misaa
aaashɛje mimii,
ni mipiŋmɔ he aaajɔ yɛ misaa nɔ lɛ,
14kɛkɛ lɛ okɛ lamɔi miiwo mihe gbeyei,
ni okɛ ninai hãa ŋmiŋmi mɔɔ mi.
15Ni no hewɔ lɛ, masumɔ
ni amia misɛ̃ ni magbo moŋ
fe nɔ ni makã lootãa wuiwui nɛɛ amli.
16 Jeŋhilɛ eje mitsine;
mihiŋ shi kɛyaŋ naanɔ.
Ŋmɛɛmɔ mihe,
ejaakɛ miwala tamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ.
17 Namɔ ji gbɔmɔ, hewɔ ni obuɔ ehe
akɔntaa nɛkɛ,
ni ojwɛŋɔ ehe kwraa po;
18ni osaraa lɛ daa leebi,
ni okaa lɛ okwɛɔ hiŋmɛitswaa
fɛɛ hiŋmɛitswaa nɛɛ?
19Mɛɛ beyinɔ okpaŋ nii kwɛmɔ;
mɛɛbe po oooŋmɛɛ mihe,
koni mana be mami misɛŋ nu?
20Bo adesai ahebulɔ,
kɛji mifee esha lɛ,
mɛni po mina mifee bo?
Mɛɛba ni ojie ohiɛ oka mi?
Mɛɛba mitsɔ̃ jatsu mihã mi diɛŋtsɛ
nɔŋŋ mihe nɛɛ?
21Mɛɛba okɛ mitɔ̃mɔi lɛ efaaa mi
koni ofɔ minɔsha lɛ yɛ mihe?
Ejaakɛ agbɛnɛ su mli makã
ni obaatao mi,
shi onaŋ mi yɛ he ko he ko.”

english_text:
Bildad's First Speech
How Long Will You Talk?
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2How long will you talk
and keep saying nothing?
3Does God All-Powerful
stand in the way of justice?
4He made your children pay
for their sins.
5So why don't you turn to him
6and start living right?
Then he will decide
to rescue and restore you
to your place of honor.
7Your future will be brighter
by far than your past.
Our Ancestors Were Wise
8 Our ancestors were wise,
so learn from them.
9Our own time has been short,
like a fading shadow,
and we know very little.
10But they will instruct you
with great understanding.
11Papyrus reeds grow healthy
only in a swamp,
12and if the water dries up,
they die sooner than grass.
13Such is the hopeless future
of all who turn from God
14and trust in something as frail
as a spider's web—
15they take hold and fall
because it's so flimsy.
16Sinful people are like plants
with spreading roots and plenty
of sun and water.
17They wrap their roots tightly
around rocks.
18But once they are pulled up,
they have no more place;
19their life slips away,
and other plants grow there.
20We know God doesn't reject
an innocent person
or help a sinner.
21And so, he will make you happy
and give you something
to smile about.
22But your evil enemies
will be put to shame
and disappear forever.
translation_text:
1Kɛkɛ ni Bildad, Shuhinyo lɛ, here Hiob nɔ ekɛɛ:
2“Mɛɛbe po ooohiɛ nɛkɛ wiemɔi nɛɛ amli
kɛyashi,
onaa wiemɔi ni tamɔ ahum
wulu nɛɛ?
3Ani Nyɔŋmɔ tsɔ̃ɔ jalɛ hiɛ ebuɔ shi?
Aloo Ofe lɛ kɔdɔ̃ɔ etoi eyeɔ sane?
4Kɛji obii lɛ tɔ̃ enɔ lɛ,
no lɛ egbala amɛtoi bɔ ni sa amɛ.
5Kɛji obaatao Nyɔŋmɔ sɛɛgbɛ
ni okpa Ofe lɛ fai,
6ni kɛji ohe tse ni oja lɛ,
no lɛ anɔkwa, Nyɔŋmɔ baaye ebua bo,
ni ebaaduro bo we kpakpa ekoŋŋ.
7Osa shihilɛ lɛ baafee nɔ ko bibioo,
shi owɔsɛɛ shihilɛ baafe nɔ wulu.
8“Ofainɛ, bo lɛ bi tsutsu yinɔbii,
ni obo nɔ ni amɛtsɛmɛi ekpa shi
ni amɛna lɛ toi.
9 Ejaakɛ wɔ lɛ, nyɛ kpaakpa nyɛ afɔ wɔ,
ni wɔleee nɔ ko nɔ ko,
ejaakɛ wɔgbii yɛ jeŋ tamɔ hɔ̃ɔŋ.
10Ani blematsɛmɛi nɛɛ etsɔŋ bo nii;
ani amɛgbaŋ bo, ani amɛwieŋ
amɛnilee mli wiemɔi?
11“Ani adã kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni
ŋmiamɔ bɛ lo?
Ani glã shwereɔ yɛ he ni nu bɛ?
12Be mli ni amɛgba afofro,
ni anako afolɔ lɛ,
amɛŋalaa amɛshiɔ jwɛi krokomɛi fɛɛ.
13Mɛi fɛɛ ni hiɛ kpaa Nyɔŋmɔ nɔ lɛ,
bɔ ni amɛnaagbee yɔɔ nɛ;
mɔ ni sheee Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei lɛ,
ehiɛnɔkãmɔ aaafite.
14Ehiɛnɔkãmɔ mli tserɛɔ,
ehiɛnɔkãmɔ lɛ tamɔ anaanu ntaŋ.
15Ehoɔ ekpasaa ewe lɛ,
shi ewe lɛ nyɛɛɛ shi ema;
emɔɔ mli waa;
shi no nyɛɛɛ lɛ asɔo.”
16Gbɔmɔ shwereɔ yɛ hulu hiɛ,
ni niji ni etsɛ̃rɛ lɛ haa
etrom lɛ nɔ.
17Efãi blaa tɛi kui,
etsɔ̃ɔ tɛsai amli tete.
18Kɛji akpãtã ehiɛ yɛ he ni
eyɔɔ lɛ,
no lɛ he ni ehi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ
baatso yɛ ehe ekɛɛ akɛ,
“Minako bo dã!”
19Shi naa, miishɛɛ ni eyɔɔ
ji akɛ gbɔmɛi krokomɛi
baakwɛ̃ kɛnyiɛ esɛɛ.
20“Naa, Nyɔŋmɔ kwaaa
mɔ ni tɔ̃mɔ ko bɛ ehe;
ni asaŋ etooo he nine
ehãaa efɔŋfeelɔi.
21Ebaahã odaa aaayi obɔ̃ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ,
ni odaa ayi obɔ kɛ oshebɔɔ.
22Ohenyɛlɔi ahiɛ aaagboi,
ni yiwalɔi awei aaalaaje.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
What You Say Is True
1Job said:
2 What you say is true.
No human is innocent
in the sight of God.
3Not once in a thousand times
could we win our case
if we took him to court.
4God is wise and powerful—
who could possibly
oppose him and win?
5When God becomes angry,
he can move mountains
before they even know it.
6God can shake the earth loose
from its foundations
7 or command the sun and stars
to hold back their light.
8God alone stretched out the sky,
stepped on the sea,
9 and set the stars in place—
the Big Dipper and Orion,
the Pleiades and the stars
in the southern sky.
10Of all the miracles God works,
we cannot understand a one.
11God walks right past me,
without making a sound.
12And if he grabs something,
who can stop him
or raise a question?
13When God showed his anger,
the servants of the sea monster
fell at his feet.
14How, then, could I possibly
argue my case with God?
Though I Am Innocent
15Even though I am innocent,
I can only beg for mercy.
16And if God came into court
when I called him,
he would not hear my case.
17He would strike me with a storm
and increase my injuries
for no reason at all.
18Before I could get my breath,
my miseries would multiply.
19God is much stronger than I am,
and who would call me into court
to give me justice?
20Even if I were innocent,
God would prove me wrong.
21I am not guilty,
but I no longer care
what happens to me.
22What difference does it make?
God destroys the innocent
along with the guilty.
23When a good person dies
a sudden death,
God sits back and laughs.
24And who else but God
blindfolds the judges,
then lets the wicked
take over the earth?
My Life Is Speeding By
25My life is speeding by,
without a hope of happiness.
26Each day passes swifter
than a sailing ship
or an eagle swooping down.
27Sometimes I try to be cheerful
and to stop complaining,
28but my sufferings frighten me,
because I know that God
still considers me guilty.
29So what's the use of trying
to prove my innocence?
30Even if I washed myself
with the strongest soap,
31God would throw me into a pit
of stinking slime, leaving me
disgusting to my clothes.
32God isn't a mere human like me.
I can't put him on trial.
33Who could possibly judge
between the two of us?
34Can someone snatch away
the stick God carries
to frighten me?
35Then I could speak up
without fear of him,
but for now, I cannot speak.
translation_text:
Hiob wiemɔ
1Kɛkɛ ni Hiob hã Bildad hetoo ekɛɛ:
2 Mile lɛɛlɛŋ akɛ nakai ji sane lɛ,
shi te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni adesa
aja yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛŋ?
3Kɛji mɔ ko kɛɛ ekɛ Nyɔŋmɔ
aaataa naa lɛ, mɔ lɛ
nyɛŋ Nyɔŋmɔ saji akpe mli
ekome kɛkɛ naa ejie.
4Nilelɔ ji lɛ, ni eyɛ hewalɛ;
namɔ ete shi ewo lɛ,
ni eye kunim pɛŋ?
5Efãmɔɔ gɔji, ni amɛleee kwraa
kɛji etsɔ̃mɔ amɛ ebu shi
yɛ emlifu mli.
6Ehosoɔ je lɛ kɛmɔɔ eshishitoo;
ni ekulashiŋi ni tere je lɛ hosoɔ.
7Efãa hulu, ni ehiii lɛ shitee;
ni esɔoɔ ŋulamii anaa, ni amɛkpɛɛɛ.
8 Lɛ ekoome ekpã ŋwɛi mli
elɛɛ shi,
ni enaanaa bonso nɔ yɛ ŋshɔŋ.
9 Lɛ ebɔ Jeŋ kpawo kɛ Oŋwɛ
kɛ Wuɔ kɛ ebii kɛ wuoyigbɛ ŋulamii lɛ.
10Efeɔ nibii wuji ni anaaa naa;
kɛ naakpɛɛnii ni aleee amɛyibɔ.
11Naa Nyɔŋmɔ tsɔ̃ɔ mihe kɛhoɔ,
ni minaaa lɛ;
ehoɔ eyaa, ni miyooo lɛ.
12Naa, nɔ ni etaoɔ lɛ ekɔɔ;
namɔ aaanyɛ enaa atsi?
Namɔ aaanyɛ akɛɛ lɛ akɛ,
“Mɛni ofeɔ nɛɛ?
13Nyɔŋmɔ eŋmɛŋ emlifu lɛ he,
ni mɛi ni ye bua Rahab lɛ aaabakua lɛ.
14Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã lɛ hetoo hu?
Mɛɛ wiemɔi anɔ matsɔ̃
mi kɛ lɛ awie?
15Yɛ mli akɛ tɔ̃mɔ ko bɛ mihe moŋ,
shi minyɛŋ lɛ hetoo mahã;
hewɔ lɛ fai moŋ makpa mikojolɔ lɛ.
16Kɛji mitsɛ lɛ ni ehere minɔ po,
miheŋ miyeŋ akɛ eebo mi toi.
17Ejaakɛ ekɛ ahum kumɔɔ mi,
ni ehãa mifaji lɛ faa yakatswaa.
18Ehãaa mana mumɔhe,
shi ewoɔ mi jaramɔ moŋ.
19Kɛji aaye lɛ hewalɛ naa lɛ,
naa, lɛ nɛ;
ni kɛji aafee jalɛnii lɛ,
namɔ kɛ lɛ kedeɔ?
20Yɛ mli akɛ tɔ̃mɔ ko bɛ mihe,
kɛ̃lɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ minaa wiemɔ
baabu mi fɔ.
Shwamɔ ko bɛ mihe moŋ nɛ,
shi eeetsɔ̃ɔ akɛ mihiii.
21Shwamɔ ko bɛ mihe,
shi mitsɛɛɛ mihe nɔ ko.
Jeŋshihilɛ eje mitsine.
22Fɛɛ ekome!”
No hewɔ lɛ, miikɛɛ akɛ,
“Jeŋshihilɛ eje mitsine;
mɔ ni shwamɔ bɛ ehe,
kɛ mɔ fɔŋ lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ
baakpãtã amɛ fɛɛ amɛhiɛ.
23Kɛji osharã gbe mɔ ko
ni tɔ̃mɔ bɛ ehe lɛ,
Nyɔŋmɔ ŋmɔɔ.
24Ekɛ je lɛ ewo mɔ fɔŋ dɛŋ;
eha enɔ kojolɔi ahiɛ.
Kɛjeee Nyɔŋmɔ ni lɛ,
namɔ ni mɔ?
25“Migbii lɛ ahe yɛ oya fe foijolɔ,
amɛhoɔ amɛyaa,
ni amɛnaaa nɔ kpakpa ko.
26Amɛhoɔ amɛyaa shwiaa
tamɔ glã lɛji,
tamɔ okropɔŋ gbaa eyiɔ kooloo nɔ.
27Kɛji mikɛɛ majie mihiɛ yɛ mikɔmɔi lɛ anɔ,
ni masaa mihiɛ, ni mana tsui lɛ,
28mipiŋmɔi lɛ aaawo mihe gbeyei moŋ,
ejaakɛ mile akɛ obuŋ mi bem.
29Ni abaabu mi fɔ kɛ̃;
mɛɛba mɔ magba mihe naa yaka?
30Kɛji miju mihe kɛ snoo nu,
ni mifɔ midɛ̃ hu kɛ samla lɛ,
31kɛ̃lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ, oootsi mi
owo bu mli;
ni mi diɛŋtsɛ mihe atade tete
aaahã mihe anyaŋe mi.
32Ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ jeee adesa tamɔ mi
koni mahã lɛ hetoo;
ni wɔya ni akojo wɔ yɛ kojomɔhe.
33Mɔ ko bɛ ni aaadamɔ wɔteŋ,
ni eeeŋɔ enine efɔ̃ wɔyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ wɔnɔ,
ni ekpãtã wɔteŋ.
34Hã ekpa mi piŋmɔ,
koni ehe ŋmiŋmi akamɔ mi.
35Kɛkɛ lɛ mawie, ni lɛ gbeyeishemɔ
bɛ mli;
ejaakɛ jeee nakai miyɔɔ.”

english_text:
Job Complains to God
I Am Sick of Life!
1I am sick of life!
And from my deep despair,
I complain to you, my God.
2Don't just condemn me!
Point out my sin.
3Why do you take such delight
in destroying those you created
and in smiling on sinners?
4Do you look at things
the way we humans do?
5Is your life as short as ours?
6Is that why you are so quick
to find fault with me?
7 You know I am innocent,
but who can defend me
against you?
8Will you now destroy
someone you created?
9Remember that you molded me
like a piece of clay.
So don't turn me back
into dust once again.
10 As cheese is made from milk,
you created my body
from a tiny drop.
11Then you tied my bones together
with muscles and covered them
with flesh and skin.
12You, the source of my life,
showered me with kindness
and watched over me.
You Have Not Explained
13You have not explained
all of your mysteries,
14but you catch and punish me
each time I sin.
15Guilty or innocent,
I am condemned and ashamed
because of my troubles.
16No matter how hard I try,
you keep hunting me down
like a powerful lion.
17You never stop accusing me;
you become furious and attack
over and over again.
18Why did you let me be born?
I would rather have died
before birth
19and been carried to the grave
without ever breathing.
20I have only a few days left.
Why don't you leave me alone?
Let me find some relief,
* 21before I travel to the land
22of darkness and despair,
the place of no return.
translation_text:
1“Mijeŋshihilɛ eje mitsine.
Mikɛ mikɔmɔi lɛ baashwie shi
kpookpoo.
Mibawie mitsui mli dɔlɛ fɛɛ.
2Mibakɛɛ Nyɔŋmɔ akɛ, ‘Kaabu mi
fɔ!’
Tsɔɔmɔ mi nɔ hewɔ ni
okɛ mi ena nɛɛ.
3Aso eja gbɛ yɛ ohiɛ,
akɛ owa mɔ yi, ni onyaŋe
bo diɛŋtsɛ oninenaa nitsumɔnii.
Ni ona mɛi fɔ̃ji ayiŋtoi
moŋ ahe tsuijurɔ lo?
4Ani adesa hiŋmɛi ohiɛ,
ni okwɛɔ nii tamɔ adesa?
5Ani ogbii tamɔ adesa gbii,
loo ofii tamɔ adesa afii;
6hewɔ ni otiuɔ mitɔ̃mɔi asɛɛ,
ni odiɔ esha ni mifee sɛɛ;
7tsɛbelɛ ole akɛ miyeee fɔ,
ni mɔ ko bɛ ni aaanyɛ ashɔ̃
mi yɛ odɛ̃ŋ?
8Oniji shɔ̃ mi, ni amɛbɔ mi,
ni agbɛnɛ ofo ohe,
ni okɛ nakai niji lɛ nɔŋŋ
miikpãtã mihiɛ.
9 Kaimɔ akɛ okɛ sũ bɔ mi.
Ani oohã matsɔ̃ sũ ekoŋŋ?
10Ohã mitsɛ hewalɛ, ni ekɛfɔ mi,
ni ohã mida yɛ minyɛ musuŋ.
11Okɛ wui kɛ fãi tsara migbɔmɔtso,
ni okɛ loo kɛ hewolo ha mihe.
12Oduro mi wala, ni suɔmɔ ni okɛsumɔ mi sɛɛ efooo,
ni odɛ̃ŋ kwɛmɔ ebaa miyi.
13Kɛ̃lɛ okɛ nibii ni eba minɔ nɛɛ tee mi yɛ otsui mli,
yɛ oyiŋtoo naa.
14Kɛji mifee esha lɛ, okadiɔ ohãa mi,
ni okɛ mitɔmɔ lɛ efaaa.
15Kɛji mifee nɔ fɔŋ lɛ, kpoo hã mi!
Kɛji mifee nɔ ni ja tete lɛ,
minyɛɛɛ miyi nɔ mawo,
ejaakɛ mihiɛ egbo kpɔtɔɔ,
ni miikwɛ mihejaramɔ lɛ moŋ.
16 Kɛji mikanya mihe lɛ,
ogbɔbiɔ mi tamɔ jata,
ni ofeɔ naakpɛɛ nibii oshiɔ mi.
17Otsakeɔ odasefoi ni wieɔ shiɔ mi,
ni ohãa omlifu naa waa yɛ minɔ,
ni ohãa ta nyiɛɔ ta sɛɛ kɛtuaa mi.
18Nyɔŋmɔ, mɛɛba oŋmɛ gbɛ ni afɔ mi mɔ?
Mina ni migbo dani hiŋmɛi ko
na mi;
19ni kɛjɛ musuŋ lɛ
awo mi ayafu,
ni mitsɔ̃ tamɔ mɔ ko
ni afɔko lɛ kwraa.
20Te miwala gbii faaa?
Ŋmɛɛmɔ mihe koni mawo mitsui fioo,
21dani maya he ni kɛ mitee,
ni mijɛŋ jɛi mibaŋ dɔŋŋ,
he ni ji duŋ kpii kɛ gbele hɔ̃ɔŋ
shikpɔŋ lɛ,
22duŋ kpii shikpɔŋ kɛ enɔ sakasaka,
he ni la ji duŋ lɛ.”

english_text:
Zophar's First Speech
So Much Foolish Talk
1Zophar from Naamah said:
2So much foolish talk
cannot go unanswered.
3Your words have silenced others
and made them ashamed;
now it is only right for you
to be put to shame.
4You claim to be innocent
and argue that your beliefs
are acceptable to God.
5But I wish God would speak
6and let you know that wisdom
has many different sides.
You would then discover
that God has punished you
less than you deserve.
7Can you understand the mysteries
surrounding God All-Powerful?
8They are higher than the heavens
and deeper than the grave.
So what can you do
when you know so little,
9and these mysteries outreach
the earth and the ocean?
10If God puts you in prison
or drags you to court,
what can you do?
11God has the wisdom to know
when someone is worthless
and sinful,
12but it's easier to tame
a wild donkey
than to make a fool wise.
Surrender Your Heart to God
13Surrender your heart to God,
turn to him in prayer,
14and give up your sins—
even those you do in secret.
15Then you won't be ashamed;
you will be confident
and fearless.
16Your troubles will go away
like water beneath a bridge,
17and your darkest night
will be brighter than noon.
18You will rest safe and secure,
filled with hope
and emptied of worry.
19You will sleep without fear
and be greatly respected.
20But those who are evil
will go blind and lose their way.
Their only escape is death!
translation_text:
Zofar wiemɔ
1Kɛkɛ ni Zofar, Naamanyo lɛ here Hiob nɔ, ni ekɛɛ,
2“Ani awieɔ babaoo nɛkɛ
ni ahãaa hetoo,
ni ahãa naafuutsɛ ŋɔɔ ehe eyeɔ?
Ani naafuu wiemɔ
hãa mɔ sane jaa?
3Hiob, aso owiemɔi babaoo nɛɛ
aaahã mɛi afee dioo?
Ni kɛji oye mɛi ahe fɛo lɛ,
mɔ ko akawo bo hiɛgbele?
4Okɛɛ nɔ ni owieɔ lɛ anɔkwale ni,
ni yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ lɛ ohe tse.
5Oo, kulɛ Nyɔŋmɔ awie,
egbɛ edaaŋ ekɛ bo awie,
6koni egbele teemɔŋ nilee hiɛ
etsɔ̃ɔ bo,
ejaakɛ enilee yɛ naakpɛɛ.
Na ole akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ bo yeko
bɔ ni sa otɔ̃mɔ lɛ.
7Ani ooonyɛ ona Nyɔŋmɔ
teemɔŋ nibii anaa?
Ani ooonyɛ ole he ni Ofe lɛ hewalɛ yatãa?
8Nyɔŋmɔ nɔ kwɔ fe ŋwɛii amli ŋwɛi;
mɛni obaanyɛ ofee yɛ he?
Ni emli kwɔ voo fe gbohiiaje;
mɛni obaanyɛ ofee yɛ he?
9Ekɛ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛlɛ,
ni elɛɛ fe ŋshɔ.
10Kɛji Nyɔŋmɔ ba,
ni ebamɔ bo ewo kpabuŋ,
ni etsɛ bo kojomɔ lɛ,
namɔ aaanyɛ enaa atsi?
11Akɛni Nyɔŋmɔ le mɛi ni ji yakagbɔmɛi lɛ,
kɛji ena nɔ sha lɛ,
aso eeeku ehiɛ efɔ̃ nɔ?
12Kwashiai baabɔ̃i jwɛŋmɔ namɔ,
be ni ŋaŋ teji baafɔ bi
ni he jɔ tamɔ gbɔmɔ.
13Kɛji osaa otsuiŋ ekpakpa lɛ,
ooohole oniji anɔ yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ.
14Kɛji nɔ sha ko yɛ odɛ̃ŋ lɛ,
hã eya sɛɛ flɛŋŋ
ni ogu nɔ ni ejaaa gbɛ
yɛ owe lɛ mli.
15Kɛkɛ lɛ, anɔkwa, ooonyɛ
ohiɛ nɔ owo,
ni kpa ko bɛ ohe,
ni ooona ekãa
ni osheŋ gbeyei.
16Ejaakɛ ohiɛ aaakpa ohaomɔi
lɛ fɛɛ nɔ;
obaakai haomɔi lɛ tamɔ faaŋ
nu ni eho etee kɛkɛ.
17Owala be mli aaatse fe shwane,
ni kɛji duŋ wo yɛ mli tete lɛ,
eeetsɔ tamɔ leebi.
18Otsui aaakã omli, ejaakɛ oyɛ
hiɛnɔkãmɔ;
Nyɔŋmɔ aaabu ohe, ni ooojɔɔ ohe,
ni ooofee shweshweeshwe.
19Oookã shi, ni mɔ ko woŋ ohe gbeyei;
mɛi babaoo aaababi odɛ̃ŋ wamɔ.
20Shi mɛi fɔ̃ji lɛ aaashwila,
ni amɛnaŋ foijeehe.
Amɛhiɛnɔkãmɔ pɛ ji gbele.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Zophar
You Think You Are So Great
* 1Job said to his friends:
2You think you are so great,
with all the answers.
3But I know as much as you do,
and so does everyone else.
4I have always lived right,
and God answered my prayers;
now friends make fun of me.
5It's easy to condemn
those who are suffering,
when you have no troubles.
6Robbers and other godless people
live safely at home and say,
“God is in our hands!”
If You Want To Learn
7If you want to learn,
then go and ask
the wild animals and the birds,
8the flowers and the fish.
9Any of them can tell you
what the Lord has done.
10Every living creature
is in the hands of God.
11We hear with our ears,
taste with our tongues,
12and gain some wisdom from those
who have lived a long time.
13But God is the real source
of wisdom and strength.
14No one can rebuild
what he destroys, or release
those he has imprisoned.
15God can hold back the rain
or send a flood,
16just as he rules over liars
and those they lie to.
17God shames counselors,
turns judges into fools,
18and makes slaves of kings.
19God removes priests and others
who have great power—
20he confuses wise,
experienced advisors,
21puts mighty kings to shame,
and takes away their power.
22God turns darkness to light;
23he makes nations strong,
then shatters their strength.
24God strikes their rulers senseless,
then leaves them to roam
through barren deserts,
25lost in the dark, staggering
like someone drunk.
translation_text:
Hiob Wiemɔ
1Kɛkɛ ni Hiob here nɔ ni ekɛɛ akɛ,
2“Ŋwanejee bɛ he akɛ nyɛ ji maŋ lɛ,
ni kɛji nyɛgboi pɛ,
nilee hu egbo.
3Shi mi hu miyɛ jwɛŋmɔ tamɔ nyɛ nɔŋŋ;
Nyɛfeee mi nilee.
Namɔ leee wiemɔi ni nyɛwie nɛɛ?
4Naa mi ni mitsɔ̃ hefɛoyeli nɔ
mihã minanemɛi.
Mi ni mitsɛɔ Nyɔŋmɔ,
ni ehereɔ mi nɔ,
ni miyeɔ jalɛ sane,
ni shwamɔ ko bɛ mihe lɛ;
mi, mitsɔ̃ hefɛoyeli nɔ nɛɛ.
5Mɔ ni he ejɔ lɛ lɛ,
ejwɛŋmɔ ji akɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ amanehulu mli lɛ
esa ehefɛoyeli.
No ji nɔ ni sa mɔ ni eshane
ni eyaagbee shi lɛ.
6Julɔi atoiiaŋ ejɔ amɛ yɛ amɛshĩai amli,
ni mɛi ni woɔ Nyɔŋmɔ mli la hu
yɛ shweshweeshwe,
tsɛbelɛ amɛhewalɛ ji amɛnyɔŋmɔ.
7Bo lɛ bi kooloi, ni amɛaatsɔ̃ɔ bo nii;
bi loofɔji, ni amɛaagba bo sane;
8loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei,
ni amɛaatsɔ̃ɔ bo nii;
ni ŋshɔŋ loi hu aaagba bo sane.
9Te nibii nɛɛ ateŋ nɔ ni leee
akɛ Yehowa nine ji nɔ ni bɔ lɛ lɛ?
10 Lɛ edɛŋ nibii fɛɛ ni muɔ awala
kɛ adesa mumɔ fɛɛ yɔɔ.
11Bɔ ni toi kaa wiemɔi ekwɛɔ lɛ,
nakai lilɛi hu saa niyenii naa ekwɛɔ.
12Nilee yɛ onukpai adɛŋ,
shi walasɛɛtsɛlɛ mli jwɛŋmɔ yɔɔ.
13Shi Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, eyɛ nilee kɛ hewalɛ
kɛ ŋaawoo kɛ jwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ.
14Kɛji ekumɔ nɔ ko eshwie shi lɛ,
mɔ ko bɛ ni baanyɛ esaa etswa ema shi;
ni kɛji eŋa mɔ ko yi lɛ,
mɔ ko nyɛŋ agbele mɔ lɛ.
15 Kɛji etsi nunɛmɔ naa lɛ,
fai miiɔ;
ni kɛji eŋmɛɛ he lɛ fai yimɔɔ,
ni amɛjeɔ ŋa kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.
16Lɛ edɛŋ hewalɛ kɛ nilee fɛɛ yɔɔ;
mɔ ni eshishiuɔ mɔ kɛ
mɔ ni ashishiuɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ,
enɔ ji amɛ fɛɛ.
17Ehãa nilee ŋmɛɔ ajinafoi,
ni ehãa kojolɔi tsɔ̃ɔ kwashiai.
18Ekpaa maŋtsɛmɛi,
ni ekɛ kpãa fimɔɔ amɛhɛ.
19Ekpɔlɔɔ osɔfoi ahewulamɔnii yɛ amɛhe,
ni ebaa mɛi ni hiɛ hewalɛ shi.
20Ehãa wiemɔ tete ŋmɛɔ mɛi
ni hiɛ kã amɛnɔ,
ni eshɔ̃ɔ hiimeji anilee yɛ amɛdɛŋ.
21Ehãa lumɛi ahe guɔ gboɔ,
ni efoɔ hewalɔi ahewalɛ sɛɛ.
22Ejieɔ nibii ni hɔlɔ dujiaŋ lɛ kpo,
ni ehãa la kpɛɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ.
23Ehãa maji jeɔ agbo,
ni lɛ nɔŋŋ ekpãtãa amɛhiɛ.
Elɛɔ maji amli, ni amɛdaraa,
ni lɛ nɔŋŋ ekpãtãa amɛhiɛ.
24Eshɔ̃ɔ nilee yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii
amaŋtsɛmɛi adɛŋ;
ni ehãa amɛtsomloɔ yɛ ŋa nɔ
he ni nanegbɛ tete bɛ.
25Amɛgbugbuɔ shi yɛ duŋ
ni la ko bɛ mli lɛ mli,
ni ehãa amɛdidãa tamɔ dãatɔlɔi.

english_text:
Job Continues
I Know and Understand
1I know and understand
every bit of this.
2None of you are smarter
than I am;
there's nothing you know
that I don't.
3But I prefer to argue my case
with God All-Powerful—
4you are merely useless doctors,
who treat me with lies.
5The wisest thing you can do
is to keep quiet 6and listen
to my argument.
7Are you telling lies for God
8and not telling the whole truth
when you argue his case?
9If he took you to court,
could you fool him,
just as you fool others?
10If you were secretly unfair,
he would correct you,
11and his glorious splendor
would make you terrified.
12Your wisdom and arguments
will blow away like dust.
Be Quiet While I Speak
13Be quiet while I speak,
and we'll see what happens.
14I will be responsible
for what happens to me.
15God may kill me, but still
I will trust him
and offer my defense.
16This may be what saves me,
because no guilty person
would come to his court.
17Listen carefully to my words!
18I have prepared my case well,
and I am certain to win.
19If you can prove me guilty,
I will give up and die.
Job Prays
I Ask Only Two Things
20I ask only two things
of you, my God,
and I will no longer
hide from you—
21stop punishing
and terrifying me!
22Then speak, and I will reply;
or else let me speak,
and you reply.
23Please point out my sins,
so I will know them.
24Why have you turned your back
and count me your enemy?
25Do you really enjoy
frightening a fallen leaf?
26Why do you accuse me
of horrible crimes
and make me pay for sins
I did in my youth?
27 You have tied my feet down
and keep me surrounded;
28I am rotting away like cloth
eaten by worms.
translation_text:
1Naa, mina nibii nɛɛ fɛɛ
kɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mihiŋmɛi,
ni mitoi hu enu, ni minu shishi.
2Nɔ ni nyɛle lɛ, mi hu mile;
nyɛfeee mi yɛ enɛɛmɛi agbɛfaŋ.
3Shi mi lɛ Ofe lɛ mitaoɔ mikɛwie,
Nyɔŋmɔ ji mɔ ni mitaoɔ mikɛyiyi
ni matsɔ̃ɔ lɛ misane lɛ naa.
4Shi nyɛ lɛ, nyɛkɛ abla eto nyɛhiɛ,
tsofatsɛmɛi ni bɛ nɔ ko mli ji nyɛ fɛɛ.
5Oo, nyɛmuaa nyɛnaa moŋ kulɛ eeehi pam,
ejaakɛ no aaatsɔ̃ nyɛnilee.
6Agbɛnɛ nyɛboa misane lɛ toi,
ni nyɛfea toi nyɛhãa minaajiemɔ lɛ.
7Ani nyɛaato abla nyɛwo Nyɔŋmɔ naa,
ni nyɛaawie nɔ ni bɛ mli nyɛhã lɛ?
8Ani nyɛmiiwie kɛmiifã Nyɔŋmɔ he lo?
Ani nyɛbaawie nyɛhã Nyɔŋmɔ?
9Ani kɛji Nyɔŋmɔ tao nyɛsaji amli lɛ,
nyɛaaye nyɛhe?
Ani nyɛaanyɛ nyɛlaka Nyɔŋmɔ
tamɔ alakaa adesa lo?
10Anɔkwa, Nyɔŋmɔ baakã nyɛhiɛ
kɛji nyɛkwɛ hiɛiaŋ yɛ dujiaŋ tete.
11Aso egbojee lɛ woŋ nyɛhe gbeyei
ni ehe ŋmiŋmi hu mɔŋ nyɛ?
12Abɛi ni nyɛbubuɔ lɛ tamɔ lamlu;
wiemɔi ni nyɛkɛfãa nyɛhe lɛ
tamɔ magbɛ.
13Nyɛfea dioo koni manyɛ mawie,
ni nɔ ni aaaba minɔ lɛ aba.
14Mɛɛ hewɔ maŋɔ miheloo makɔ̃ minaa
koni mahiɛ miwala yɛ midɛŋ?
15Naa, kɛji eeegbe mi tete lɛ,
mibɛ sane ko;
mibafã mijeŋba he yɛ ehiɛ kɛ̃.
16Enɛ nɔŋŋ aaatsɔ̃ miyiwalaheremɔ,
ejaakɛ mɔ fɔŋ nyɛŋ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ aba.
17Nyɛboa nɔ ni mawie nɛɛ toi jogbaŋŋ,
ni nyɛhãa minaajiemɔ lɛ
aya nyɛtoiiaŋ.
18Naa, misaa minaajiemɔ mito;
mile akɛ abaabu mi bem.
19Namɔ yɔɔ jɛi ni ekɛ mi
batao naa?
Kɛji Nyɔŋmɔ ni lɛ,
no lɛ mibafee diŋŋ
koni magbo kɛkɛ.
20Feemɔ nibii enyɔ nɛɛ pɛ
ohã mi,
ni miteŋ mihe yɛ ohiɛ.
21Suu onine yɛ mihe kwraa,
ni kaahã ohe ŋmiŋmi miimɔ mi.
22Oo Nyɔŋmɔ, tsɛ mi, ni mibahere bo nɔ,
aloo ŋmɛɛ mi gbɛ koni mawie
ni ohã mi hetoo.
23Minishaianii kɛ mihe eshai lɛ, enyiɛ ni?
Hã male minishaianii kɛ mihe eshai lɛ.
24Mɛɛba okɛ ohiɛ teɔ mi,
ni obuɔ mi akɛ ohenyɛlɔ lɛ?
25Aso obaafã baa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ehuu lɛ tsui;
ni obaanyiɛ abele shishi tutuu sɛɛ?
26Ejaakɛ okɛ saji ni naa wa miishi mi,
ootsɛ miblahiaŋ tɔ̃mɔi tete asɛɛ.
27 Obɔ minaji apã,
ni ohiŋmɛi kã nɔ fɛɛ nɔ
ni mifeɔ he;
minanefaamɔi hu owo he husu.
28Adesa tamɔ nɔ ko ni ekpɔtɔ,
etamɔ mama ni omlɛgɛ eye.

english_text:
Job Continues His Prayer
Life Is Short and Sorrowful
1 Life is short and sorrowful
for every living soul.
2We are flowers that fade
and shadows that vanish.
3And so, I ask you, God,
why pick on me?
4There's no way a human
can be completely pure.
5Our time on earth is brief;
the number of our days
is already decided by you.
6Why don't you leave us alone
and let us find some happiness
while we toil and labor?
When a Tree Is Chopped Down
7When a tree is chopped down,
there is always the hope
that it will sprout again.
8Its roots and stump may rot,
9but at the touch of water,
it sprouts once again.
10Humans are different—
we die, and that's the end.
11We are like streams and lakes
after the water has gone;
12we fall into the sleep of death,
never to rise again,
until the sky disappears.
13Please hide me, God,
deep in the ground—
and when you are angry no more,
remember to rescue me.
Will We Humans Live Again?
14Will we humans live again?
I would gladly suffer
and wait for my time.
15My Creator, you would want me;
you would call out,
and I would answer.
16You would take care of me,
but not count my sins—
17you would put them in a bag,
tie it tight,
and toss them away.
18But in the real world,
mountains tumble,
and rocks crumble;
19streams wear away stones
and wash away soil.
And you destroy our hopes!
20You change the way we look,
then send us away,
wiped out forever.
21We never live to know
if our children are praised
or disgraced.
22We feel no pain but our own,
and when we mourn,
it's only for ourselves.
translation_text:
1Gbɔmɔ ni yoo fɔ lɛ yɔɔ nɛɛ,
kukuoo kɛkɛ ji ewala be lɛ;
ni emli eyi tɔ kɛ haomɔ sɔŋŋ.
2Ewala nɛɛ tamɔ fɔfɔi;
ekwɛ̃ɔ, ni eŋalaa shwiaa;
ehoɔ tamɔ hɔ̃ɔŋ, ni etsɛɛɛ.
3Gbɔmɔ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ lɛ
ona be ookwɛ lɛ,
ni ootao okɛ lɛ aye sane lo?
4Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ana nɔ ni
he tse kɛ nɔ ni he tseee
teŋ srɔto lɛ?
5Akɛni ato ewala be lɛ,
ni nyɔji abɔ ni ebaaye yɛ odɛ̃ŋ lɛ,
belɛ owo ewala he husu momo.
6Jiemɔ ohiɛ yɛ enɔ; kaafo edaaŋ
koni emii ashɛ ehe yɛ ewala mli
tamɔ apaafonyo.
7Tso tete yɛ hiɛnɔkãmɔ
akɛ kɛji atoo lɛ lɛ,
eeehere ekoŋŋ, ni niji
ni ebaatsɛ̃rɛ lɛ baadara, amɛgboiŋ.
8Yɛ mli akɛ efãi baatsɛ̃
yɛ sũ mli
ni etsoku lɛ baagbo yɛ suŋ,
9shi nu ni eeena nɛkɛ pɛ,
eeetsɛ̃ ekoŋŋ, ni eeetsɛ̃rɛ niji
tamɔ tso ŋmɔŋ.
10Shi gbɔmɔ gboɔ, ni enyɔɔ shi.
Kɛji mumɔ na fã yɛ emli lɛ,
nɛgbɛ lɛ yɔɔ dɔŋŋ?
11Bɔ ni nu tãa yɛ kpaakpo mli,
ni faa miiɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ,
12nakai gbɔmɔ hoɔ ekãa shi
ni eteee shi dɔŋŋ.
Kɛyaashi beyinɔ ni ŋwɛi aaaho aya lɛ,
ehiɛ etsɛŋ, ni atsiɛŋ lɛ yɛ wɔ lɛ mli.
13Mina ni kulɛ oŋɔ mi otee
yɛ gbohiiaje,
ni oŋɔ mi ohɔ shi
kɛyashi beyinɔ ni
omlifu lɛ aaaho,
koni oto be ohã mi,
ni okai mi.
14Kɛji gbɔmɔ gbo lɛ,
ehiɛ aaakã ekoŋŋ?
Mibato mitsui shi mamɛ yɛ
misɔ̃ɔmɔ be lɛ mli
kɛyaashi be aaashɛ
ni aaaŋmɛ̃ɛ mihe.
15Kɛkɛ lɛ ooobo otsɛ mi, ni mahere bo nɔ;
ni oootao oninenaa bɔɔnii
lɛ sɛɛgbɛ.
16Ni ohiŋmɛi baakã minyiɛmɔ he,
ni obuŋ minifɔɔjianii ahe akɔntaa;
17aaasɔo minifɔɔjianii anaa awo
kotoku mli,
ni obaatsimɔ minifɔɔjianii lɛ anɔ.
18Shi bɔ ni gɔŋ tete gbeɔ shi,
ni efufluɔ,
ni atsiɔ tɛsaa kɛjeɔ eshimaahe,
19 ni nu yeɔ tɛi ahe,
ni eloɔ shikpɔŋ su kɛyaa lɛ,
nakai ofiteɔ gbɔmɔ adesa hiɛnɔkãmɔ.
20Oyeɔ gbɔmɔ hewalɛ nɔ kɛyaa naanɔ,
otsakeɔ ehiɛ, ni oshwieɔ lɛ kɛyaa,
ni ehoɔ eyaa.
21Kɛji ebii ahiɛ miiba nyam lɛ, eleee;
ni kɛji amɛhiɛ miishwie shi hu
eleee.
22Lɛ diɛŋtsɛ pɛ egbɔmɔtsoŋ piŋmɔ
he enuɔ,
ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ pɛ ehe ŋkɔmɔ eyeɔ.”

english_text:
Eliphaz's Second Speech
If You Had Any Sense
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
* 2Job, if you had any sense,
3you would stop spreading
all of this hot air.
4Your words are enough
to make others turn from God
and lead them to doubt.
5And your sinful, scheming mind
is the source of all you say.
6I am not here as your judge;
your own words are witnesses
against you.
7Were you the first human?
Are you older than the hills?
8Have you ever been present
when God's council meets?
Do you alone have wisdom?
9Do you know and understand
something we don't?
10We have the benefit of wisdom
older than your father.
11And you have been offered
comforting words from God.
Isn't this enough?
12Your emotions are out of control,
making you look fierce;
13that's why you attack God
with everything you say.
14 No human is pure and innocent,
15and neither are angels—
not in the sight of God.
If God doesn't trust his angels,
16what chance do humans have?
We are so terribly evil
that we thirst for sin.
Just Listen to What I Know
17Just listen to what I know,
and you will learn
18wisdom known by others
since ancient times.
19Those who gained such insights
also gained the land,
and they were not influenced
by foreign teachings.
20But suffering is in store
each day for those who sin.
21Even in times of success,
they constantly hear
the threat of doom.
22Darkness, despair, and death
are their destiny.
23They scrounge around for food,
all the while dreading
the approaching darkness.
24They are overcome with despair,
like frightened soldiers facing
a fearsome king in battle.
25This is because they rebelled
against God All-Powerful
26and have attacked him
with their weapons.
27They may be rich and fat,
28but they will live in the ruins
of deserted towns.
29Their property and wealth
will shrink and disappear.
30They won't escape the darkness,
and the blazing breath of God
will set their future aflame.
* 31They have put their trust
in something worthless;
now they will become worthless
32like a date palm tree
without a leaf.
33Or like vineyards or orchards
whose blossoms and unripe fruit
drop to the ground.
34Yes, the godless and the greedy
will have nothing but flames
feasting on their homes,
35because they are the parents
of trouble and vicious lies.
translation_text:
Sanegbaa ni ji enyɔ lɛ
(15.1—21.34)
Elifaz wiemɔ
1Kɛkɛ ni Elifaz, Temannyo lɛ, here nɔ ni ekɛɛ akɛ,
2“Aso nilelɔ hãa sane hetoo
kɛ wiemɔ huu nɛkɛ,
ni ehãa emusu ayi obɔ̃ kɛ
bokã kɔɔyɔɔ?
3Aso ekɛ wiemɔ ni he bɛ sɛɛnamɔ
baajie enaa;
aloo eeejie enaa kɛ wiemɔ
ni shishinumɔ bɛ he?
4Ojie Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyeishemɔ yɛ ojwɛŋmɔŋ,
ni ootsi sɔlemɔ naa yɛ ehiɛ;
5ejaakɛ odaaŋ wiemɔ miijie onifɔ̃jianii
lɛ kpo,
ni ohiɛ shishiulɔi alilɛi.
6Bo diɛŋtsɛ odaaŋ wiemɔ miibu bo fɔ,
shi jeee mi;
bo diɛŋtsɛ odaaŋ wiemɔ miiye odase
miishi bo.
7Ani bo ji klɛŋklɛŋ gbɔmɔ ni afɔ
yɛ je nɛɛŋ?
Aloo aŋɔ bo hɔ dani abɔ gɔji lɛ?
8Ani ona onu Nyɔŋmɔ ajinaŋ sane?
Ani bo pɛ odɛ̃ŋ nilee yɔɔ?
9Mɛni kwraa ole ni wɔ lɛ wɔleee?
Mɛni shishi onu, ni wɔ lɛ efeko faŋŋ
ehãko wɔ lolo?
10Wajiatsɛmɛi kɛ hiimeji fɛɛ yɛ wɔteŋ
ni amɛye otsɛ ni fɔ bo onukpa kwraa.
11Omii ni Nyɔŋmɔ shɛjeɔ lɛ, efaaa lo?
Aloo wiemɔ ni akɛ bo wieɔ
kɛ naajɔlɛ lɛ jeee nɔ ko hã bo?
12Mɛɛba otsui sha bo,
ni mɛɛba ohiŋmɛii tswaa kpɛlɛkpɛlɛ,
13ni ote shi owo Nyɔŋmɔ
yɛ omumɔ mli,
ni ohãa wiemɔi ni tamɔ enɛɛmɛi
jeɔ onaa?
14 Namɔ ji adesa ni ehe aaatse,
loo gbɔmɔ ni jɛ yoo musuŋ
ni eeefee nɔ ni ja?
15Naa, Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ ehe efɔ̃ɔɔ
emɛi krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ tete anɔ;
ni ŋwɛi tete he tseee yɛ ehiɛ.
16Te aaafee tɛŋŋ mɔ,
ni mɔ ni feɔ musubɔɔnii,
asaŋ ni efite
adesa ni nifɔɔjianiifeemɔ
ji enu ni enuɔ lɛ,
ekɛ ehe aaafɔ̃ enɔ lɛ?
17Hiob, bo mi toi;
mibagba bo nɔ ni mina yɛ jeŋ,
18nɔ ni nilelɔi egba,
ni ji nɔ ni amɛtsɛmɛi kɛteee amɛ lɛ.
19Amɛ tuuŋtu aŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ahã;
gbɔi futuuu amɛ.
20 Yiwalɔ, mɔ ni waa mɛi krokomɛi ayi lɛ,
piŋɔ ewala gbii abɔ fɛɛ.
21Gbee ni yɔɔ gbeyei gbɛɔ yɛ etoiiaŋ,
ni julɔ batuaa lɛ be mli ni
ehe ejɔ lɛ.
22Eheee eyeee akɛ eeeku esɛɛ
kɛaajɛ duŋ mli,
ni klante ji nɔ ni aaagbe lɛ,
23ni akpaŋai miimɛ ni amɛye eloo.
Ele akɛ gbi fɔŋ lɛ ebɛŋkɛ lɛ etã.
24Jaramɔ kɛ fimɔ woɔ ehe gbeyei;
amɛyeɔ enɔ tamɔ maŋtsɛ ni efã ta.
25Ete shi ewo Nyɔŋmɔ,
ni ewo ehe nɔ yɛ Ofe lɛ nɔ.
26Ehiɛ tsɛŋ kpakpataa, ni etsɛ̃
kɛ kuɛŋtimɔ kɛba Nyɔŋmɔ nɔ.
27Eshwi kɛbamɔ ehiɛ fɛɛ.
28Maji amaŋfɔ̃i amli ehi,
yɛ shĩai ni esaaa akɛ gbɔmɔ
aaahi mli,
hei ni baatsɔmɔ koikoi lɛ.
29Enaŋ nii, ni enii ni eyɔɔ lɛ
tete etsɛŋ,
asaŋ etsɛ̃ŋ fã yɛ su mli.
30Ejeŋ duŋ lɛ mli; la baashã
niji ni etsɛ̃rɛ lɛ;
ni kɔɔyɔɔ baakpala efɔfɔi ashwie.
31Ekaŋɔ ehiɛ efɔ̃ yakanii anɔ
ni ekɛmiilaka ehe,
ejaakɛ yakanii nɔŋŋ ebaakpa.
32Eshɛŋ ebe ni ebaaŋala
tamɔ tso nine,
ni eyi baa frɔkeŋ dɔŋŋ.
33Eyibii ŋmilikiti lɛ eeekpala eshwie shi
tamɔ waintso;
34Ejaakɛ mɛi fɔ̃ji woŋ shwiei,
ni shĩai ni akɛ nyɔɔŋnihemɔ
mamɔ lɛ, la aaakpãtã hiɛ.
35Nifɔ̃ji ahe ŋaa amɛtoɔ,
ni amɛfeɔ nifɔ̃jianii;
ni mɔshishiumɔ eyi
amɛtsuiiaŋ tɔ.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
I Have Often Heard This
1Job said:
2I have often heard this,
and it offers no comfort.
3So why don't you keep quiet?
What's bothering you?
4If I were in your place,
it would be easy to criticize
or to give advice.
5But I would offer hope
and comfort instead.
6If I speak, or if I don't,
I hurt all the same.
My torment continues.
7God has worn me down
and destroyed my family;
8my shriveled up skin proves
that I am his prisoner.
9God is my hateful enemy,
glaring at me and attacking
with his sharp teeth.
10Everyone is against me;
they sneer and slap my face.
11And God is the one
who handed me over
to this merciless mob.
Everything Was Going Well
12Everything was going well,
until God grabbed my neck
and shook me to pieces.
God set me up as the target
13for his arrows,
and without showing mercy,
he slashed my stomach open,
spilling out my insides.
14God never stops attacking,
15and so, in my sorrow
I dress in sackcloth
and sit in the dust.
16My face is red with tears,
and dark shadows
circle my eyes,
17though I am not violent,
and my prayers are sincere.
18If I should die,
I beg the earth not to cover
my cry for justice.
19 Even now, God in heaven
is both my witness
and my protector.
20My friends have rejected me,
but God is the one I beg
21to show that I am right,
just as a friend should.
22Because in only a few years,
I will be dead and gone.
translation_text:
Hiob wiemɔ
1Kɛkɛ ni Hiob to he akɛ,
2“Minu saji ni tamɔ enɛɛmɛi aahu;
miishɛjelɔ gbohii ji nyɛ fɛɛ.
3Aso yaka wiemɔi nɛɛ agbeŋ naa?
Ni mɛni ta omli
hewɔ ni ohere wiemɔ lɛ nɔ nɛɛ?
4Eji nyɛgbɔmɔtso baje migbɔmɔtso
mli jikulɛ,
mi hu mawie tamɔ nyɛwieɔ nɛɛ;
mawie mashi nyɛ,
ni mahoso miyitso mawo nyɛ.
5Nakai nɔŋŋ kulɛ mawo nyɛ hewalɛ
kɛ midaaŋ wiemɔ,
ni midaaŋ wiemɔ baahã
nyɛwerɛho lɛ naa aba shi.
6Kɛji miwie lɛ, mipiŋmɔ lɛ ejɔɔɔ,
ni kɛji mifee dioo hu,
enɔ enyiɛ po ni gbɔɔ?
7Anɔkwa, Nyɔŋmɔ ehã eje mitsine;
ehã mihe gbɔmɛi fɛɛ etã.
8Ehã mikũakũai
ni enɛ yeɔ odase eshiɔ mi;
milootãa lɛ yeɔ odase shiɔ mi faŋŋ.
9Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ mlifu etserɛ mimli;
ebɛ mi ewo emli;
ekpe enyanyɔji ashi ewo mi;
etsu ehiŋmɛi eshwie minɔ
tamɔ henyɛlɔ feɔ.
10Mɛi gbɛɔ amɛdaaŋ
amɛwoɔ mi kɛ naakpɛɛ;
amɛgbalaa mitoiiaŋ ma
kɛbɔɔ mi ahora;
amɛbuaa amɛhe naa amɛwoɔ mi.
11Nyɔŋmɔ eŋɔ mi ehã mɛi fɔ̃ji,
ni etu mi ewo yiwalɔi adɛŋ.
12Kulɛ mihe ejɔ mi,
ni Nyɔŋmɔ kɔ miyinɔ tɛ;
emɔ mikuɛ, ni ekɛ mi tswia shi,
ni ekumɔ mi dukuduku.
13Egãitsɛ̃lɔi lɛ bɔle mi kɛkpe kpula;
ekɛ kakla gbala misabai amli,
ni ekɔ̃ɔɔ efiliii kwraa;
efɔse midrɔ eshwie shikpɔŋ.
14Epila mihei srɔtoi;
ni etsɛ̃ kɛba minɔ oookɛɛ
henyɛlɔ tabilɔ.
15Mikpɛ kpekpe miha miheloo he.
Naa mi, mita mlu mli
tamɔ mɔ ni aye enɔ kunim.
16Yaafo ehã mihiɛ etsu fɔɔ,
ni mihiŋmɛii anaa etitii,
ni edi tuŋŋ;
17tsɛbelɛ mikɛ minine yeko awui ko,
ni misɔleɔ mikpaa Nyɔŋmɔ fai kɛ tsui krɔŋŋ.
18Oo shikpɔŋ, kaaha milá lɛ nɔ!
Oo, shikpɔŋ, kaatsimɔ sane fɔŋ
ni aye mi lɛ nɔ;
hã miyaafo ashɛ hei fɛɛ.
19 Naa, amrɔmrɔ nɛɛ tete
midasefonyo yɛ ŋwɛi;
mɔ ni baawie ehã mi lɛ
yɛ ŋwɛi flooflo.
20Minanemɛi miiye mihe fɛo;
shi miifo miitsɔ̃ɔ Nyɔŋmɔ.
21Mina mɔ ko ni ekɛ Nyɔŋmɔ awie
ahã mi,
tamɔ bɔ ni gbɔmɔ damɔɔ mli hãa
enaanyo gbɔmɔ lɛ.
22Ejaakɛ biɛ afii fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ,
mibaya he ni
mikuŋ misɛɛ kɛjɛŋ kɛbaŋ dɔŋŋ.

english_text:
Job Complains to God
My Hopes Have Died
1My hopes have died,
my time is up,
and the grave is ready.
2All I can see are angry crowds,
making fun of me.
3If you, Lord, don't help,
who will pay the price
for my release?
4My friends won't really listen,
all because of you,
and so you must be the one
to prove them wrong.
5They have condemned me,
just to benefit themselves;
now blind their children.
6You, God, are the reason
I am insulted and spit on.
7I am almost blind with grief;
my body is a mere shadow.
8People who are truly good
would feel so alarmed,
that they would become angry
with my worthless friends.
9They would do the right thing
and because they did,
they would grow stronger.
10But none of my friends
show any sense.
11My life is drawing to an end;
hope has disappeared.
12But all my friends can do
is offer empty hopes.
13I could tell the world below
to prepare me a bed.
14Then I could greet the grave
as my father
and say to the worms,
“Hello, mother and sisters!”
15But what kind of hope is that?
16Will it keep me company
in the world of the dead?
translation_text:
1“Misusuma etɔ bahao;
miwala gbii lɛ etã,
gbonyobu miimɛ mi!
2Anɔkwa ji akɛ hefɛoyelɔi ebɔle mi,
ni mihiŋmɛii jwere mlilawoo
nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ anɔ.
3Miiye bo anɔkwa, Nyɔŋmɔ, he mi oye!
4Akɛni oŋamɔ amɛjwɛŋmɔi anaa
koni amɛkanu sane shishi hewɔ lɛ,
ohaŋ amɛye minɔ kunim ko.
5Mɔ ni tsɔ̃ɔ enanemɛi asɛɛgbɛ,
bɔ ni afee ni kɛji aja amɛnii lɛ,
ena eko lɛ, ebii ahiŋmɛii tete aaafite.
6Efee mi nɔ ni akɛbuɔ abɛ
ehã maŋbii,
ni mitsɔ̃ mɔ ni afɛ̃ɔ lajɔ̃
ashwieɔ ehiɛ.
7 Awerɛho sɔŋŋ ehã mihiŋmɛi
nɔ efee kusuu,
ni miniji kɛ mi naji efee kanyakanya,
amɛtsɔ̃ tamɔ hɔ̃ɔŋ.
8Enɛ hãa mɛi ni feɔ jalɛ nii
ahe jɔ̃ɔ amɛhe;
ni mɔ ni efeko nɔ fɔŋ griɔ
ewoɔ mɔ fɔŋ.
9Kɛ̃lɛ jalɔ lɛ fiɔ shi yɛ egbɛ lɛ nɔ,
ni mɔ ni niji ahe tse hewalɛ shwereɔ
kɛyaa naanɔ.
10Shi nyɛ, nyɛ fɛɛ,
nyɛkua nyɛsɛɛ kɛbaa;
shi minaŋ nilelɔ ko nilelɔ ko yɛ nyɛteŋ.
11Migbii lɛ eho etee;
miyiŋtoi, ni ji nɔ ni mitsui shwe
lɛ, fɛɛ efee yaka.
12Amɛkɛ gbɛkɛ feɔ shwane,
ni amɛkɛɔ akɛ,
“La ebɛŋkɛ”.
13Kɛji miŋɔ miwe lɛ akɛ gbohiiaje,
kɛ miŋmɛ misaa lɛ yɛ duŋ lɛ mli,
14ni kɛji mikɛɛ bu lɛ akɛ, “Mitsɛ ji bo”,
ni mikɛɛ gɔgɔmi akɛ, “Minyɛ loo
minyɛmi yoo ji bo lɛ”,
15no lɛ nɛgbɛ mihiɛnɔkãmɔ yɔɔ?
Namɔ baana mihiɛnɔkãmɔ lɛ?
16Ani hiɛnɔkãmɔ hu aaaya Gbohiiaje?
Ani wɔ kɛ lɛ fɛɛ baakpleke shi
kɛya su mli lo?”

english_text:
Bildad's Second Speech
How Long Will You Talk?
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2How long will you talk?
Be sensible! Let us speak.
3Or do you think that we
are dumb animals?
4You cut yourself in anger.
Will that shake the earth
or even move the rocks?
* 5 The lamps of sinful people
soon are snuffed out,
6leaving their tents dark.
7Their powerful legs become weak,
and they stumble on schemes
of their own doing.
* 8Before they know it,
9they are trapped in a net,
10hidden along the path.
11Terror strikes and pursues
from every side.
12Starving, they run,
only to meet disaster,
13then afterwards to be eaten alive
by death itself.
14Those sinners are dragged
from the safety of their tents
to die a gruesome death.
15Then their tents and possessions
are burned to ashes,
16and they are left like trees,
dried up from the roots.
17They are gone and forgotten,
18thrown far from the light
into a world of darkness,
19without any children
to carry on their name.
20Everyone, from east to west,
is overwhelmed with horror.
21Such is the fate of sinners
and their families
who don't know God.
translation_text:
Bildad wie
1Kɛkɛ ni Bildad, Shuhinyo lɛ,
here Hiob nɔ ni ekɛɛ,
2“Mɛɛ beyinɔ nɔŋŋ ooogbe wiemɔ naa?
Susumɔ he koni wɔwie.
3Mɛɛba obuɔ wɔ tamɔ tsinai?
Mɛɛba wɔtamɔ mɛi ni bɛ yitseiaŋ
yɛ ohiɛ lɛ?
4Bo diɛŋtsɛ okɛ omlifu yeɔ bo nɔŋŋ
ohe awui.
Aso ootao akɛ ashi je lɛ ahã bo,
aloo ohewɔ lɛ abaafamɔ tɛsai
ashwie?
5Hɛɛ, abaagbe mɔ fɔŋ kane lɛ,
ni ela lɛ etsoŋ dɔŋŋ!
6 Ewe lɛ mli kane egbo,
ni agbe kane ni ye eyiteŋ lɛ.
7Enaji ni efamɔɔ waawaa lɛ
nɔ baagbɔ,
ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eyiŋtoi
baatsi lɛ atswa shi.
8Ejaakɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ enyiɛɔ
kɛyaboteɔ yaa mli,
ni yaa lɛ duɔ lɛ.
9Enanetsitsi aaadu jwao,
ni kpãa ni akɛtsɔ tsɔne
aaadu lɛ.
10Akɛ kpãa etee sũ mli eto lɛ,
ni atsɔ̃ lɛ akpa yɛ gbɛteŋ.
11Ehewɔ nibii fɛɛ ni bɔle lɛ
ehã ŋmiŋmi emɔ lɛ,
ni amɛnyiɛ esɛɛ kpaakpa.
12Ehewalɛ baatã,
ni amanehulu efee kralo eto
etɛmɔ kɛ shigbeemɔ.
13Hela baakpãtã ehewolo hiɛ,
gbele kromɔbi lɛ baaye eniji kɛ enaji.
14Aaakpɔ lɛ yɛ shĩa
ni ehiɛ kã nɔ lɛ mli;
ni akɛ lɛ aaatee maŋtsɛ
ni hãa ŋmiŋmi mɔɔ lɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ.
15Mɔkpɔŋ aaayahi ewe lɛ mli
kɛji ashwã mli swɔɔ
kɛgbe emli muawa sɛɛ.
16Eshishifãi lɛ aaagbi yɛ shishigbɛ
ni eniji hu aaaŋala yɛ eyiteŋ.
17Akaiŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ,
ni atsiŋ egbɛi atã yɛ blohuŋ.
18Ashwie lɛ kɛje la hiɛ kɛtee duŋ mli,
ni ashwie lɛ kɛje jeŋ.
19Ebi loo eshwie bɛ emaŋbii ateŋ,
ni eshwɛko mɔ ko mɔ ko yɛ shihilɛhe lɛ mli.
20 Anaigbɛbii ahe aaajɔ̃ amɛhe,
yɛ nɔ ni eba enɔ lɛ hewɔ,
ni ŋmiŋmi aaamɔmɔ bokãgbɛbii hu.
21Anɔkwa, bɔ pɛ ni mɛi ni sheee
Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei ashĩai feɔ nɛ;
mɔ ni leee Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ
nɛkɛ eshihilɛhe tsɔ̃ɔ.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
How Long Will You Torture Me?
1Job said:
2How long will you torture me
with your words?
3Isn't ten times enough
for you to accuse me?
Aren't you ashamed?
4Even if I have sinned,
you haven't been harmed.
5You boast of your goodness,
claiming I am suffering
because I am guilty.
6But God is the one at fault
for finding fault with me.
7Though I pray to be rescued
from this torment,
no whisper of justice
answers me.
8God has me trapped
with a wall of darkness
9and stripped of respect.
10God rips me apart,
uproots my hopes,
11and attacks with fierce anger,
as though I were his enemy.
12His entire army advances,
then surrounds my tent.
I Am Forgotten
* 13God has turned relatives
and friends against me,
14and I am forgotten.
15My guests and my servants
consider me a stranger,
16and when I call my servants,
they pay no attention.
17My breath disgusts my wife;
everyone in my family
turns away.
18Young children can't stand me,
and when I come near,
they make fun.
19 My best friends and loved ones
have turned from me.
20I am skin and bones—
just barely alive.
21My friends, I beg you for pity!
God has made me his target.
22Hasn't he already done enough?
Why do you join the attack?
23I wish that my words
could be written down
24or chiseled into rock.
25I know that my Protector lives,
and at the end
he will stand on this earth.
26My flesh may be destroyed,
yet from this body
I will see God.
27Yes, I will see him for myself,
and I long for that moment.
28My friends, you think up ways
to blame and torment me, saying
I brought it on myself.
29But watch out for the judgment,
when God will punish you!
translation_text:
Hiob wiemɔ
1Kɛkɛ ni Hiob here nɔ akɛ,
2“Mɛɛ beyinɔ nyɛaagba minaa,
ni nyɛkɛ wiemɔ aaasu mitsui
kɛaayashi?
3Shii abɔ nɛɛ fɛɛ lɛ,
nyɛmiibɔ mi ahora;
efeee nyɛ hiɛgbele akɛ nyɛmiitɔ̃ minɔ?
4Kɛji eyɛ mli tete akɛ mifee efɔŋ lɛ,
mɛni no kɔɔ yɛ nyɛhe?
5Kɛji nyɛmiiwo nyɛhe nɔ yɛ minɔ,
ni nyɛmiiŋɔ mimanehului lɛ
akɛ minɔ fɔŋ lɛ he okadi lɛ,
6no lɛ nyɛnaa nyɛlea
akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ni ebu mi fɔ,
ni ekɛ eyaa lɛ ebɔle mi kɛsa miyi.
7Naa, mibolɔɔ akɛ aawa mi yi,
shi ahereee mi nɔ;
miboɔ koni aye abua mi,
shi ayeee mi jalɛ sane.
8 Etswa gbogbo ekɛsa minaa,
ni no hewɔ lɛ, minyɛɛɛ maho;
ni ehã migbɛ lɛ nɔ ewo duŋ.
9Ekpakpla mininamɔ fɛɛ yɛ mihe,
ni efo minunyam fɛɛ sɛɛ.
10Ekpãtã mihiɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he,
ni egbe naa ehã mi;
ni efo mihiɛnɔkãmɔ lɛ efɔ̃ shi
tamɔ atoɔ tso.
11Nyɔŋmɔ mli ewo la ewo mi,
ni ebuɔ mi akɛ ehenyɛlɔ.
12Etabilɔi lɛ ba kutuu,
amɛfo sa amɛwo mihe,
ni amɛbɔle miwe lɛ kɛkpe.
13Nyɔŋmɔ ehã minyɛmimɛi ekwa mi,
ni mɛi ni le mi etsɔ̃mɔ amɛhe
mɛi kpɔji amɛhã mi.
14Miwekumɛi egbala amɛhe shi,
mishieŋtsɛmɛi fɛɛ ahiɛ ekpa minɔ;
15mishĩa mli gbɔi ahiɛ ekpa minɔ,
mitsuji yei buɔ mi akɛ gbɔ,
mitsɔ̃ mɔkpɔŋ yɛ amɛhiɛ.
16Kɛji mitsɛ mitsulɔ lɛ, efooo midaaŋ;
kɛji mikpa lɛ fai tete, nakai nɔŋŋ.
17Midaaŋ lamɔ eje fu ewo miŋa,
minyɛ musuŋbii tete nyɛɛɛ
mihe fu naa amɛdamɔ.
18Mihe guɔ egbo yɛ gbekɛbii
tete ahiɛ,
ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔlɔ
kɛji amɛna mi.
19Mishieŋtsɛmɛi fɛɛ miinyaŋe mi,
ni mɛi ni misumɔɔ
etsɔ̃mɔ amɛhiɛ amɛwo mi.
20 Miwui ekpɛtɛ mihewolo,
ni dromɔ naa kɛkɛ ni miyɔɔ
wala mli nɛɛ.
21 Oo, minanemɛi, nyɛnaa mi mɔbɔ!
Nyɛnaa mi mɔbɔ,
ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ nine eta mihe!
22 Mɛɛba nyɛwaa mi yi
tamɔ bɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ efee mi lɛ?
23Oo, mina ni kulɛ aŋmã
minaa wiemɔi lɛ!
Oo, mina ni kulɛ aŋmã awo wolo mli!
24Mina ni kulɛ akɛ pɛi kpɛ
wiemɔ lɛ,
ni akɛ sumui wo mli
yɛ tɛsaa nɔ,
koni ehi shi kɛya naanɔ.
25 Ejaakɛ mile akɛ,
mikpɔlɔ lɛ hiɛ kã,
ni naagbee mli lɛ
eeedamɔ misɛɛ;
26 ni kɛji mihewolo hiɛ kpãtã
nɛkɛ sɛɛ,
ni heloo bɛ mihe lɛ, mana Nyɔŋmɔ.
27 Lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛ̃ mana, ni mayoo lɛ;
ejeee mɔkpɔŋ ko.
Mitsui miitse yɛ mimli!
28Kɛji nyɛmiikɛɛ akɛ,
“Bɔ ni wɔɔtsɔ̃ wɔwa lɛ yi!”
Kɛ “Sane tso muu fɛɛ lɛ jɛ lɛ” lɛ,
29nyɛshea klante gbeyei,
klante lɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ mlifu
kɛ kojomɔ kɛbaa lɛ,
koni nyɛna nyɛle akɛ
kojomɔ ko yɛ.”

english_text:
Zophar's Second Speech
Your Words Are Disturbing
1Zophar from Naamah said:
2Your words are disturbing;
now I must speak.
3You have accused
and insulted me,
and reason requires a reply.
4Since the time of creation,
everyone has known
5that sinful people are happy
for only a while.
6Though their pride and power
may reach to the sky,
7they will disappear like dust,
and those who knew them
will wonder what happened.
8 They will be forgotten
like a dream
9and vanish from the sight
of family and friends.
10Their children will have to repay
what the parents took
from the poor.
11Indeed, the wicked will die
and go to their graves
in the prime of life.
Sinners Love the Taste of Sin
12Sinners love the taste of sin;
they relish every bite
13and swallow it slowly.
14But their food will turn sour
and poison their stomachs.
15Then God will make them lose
the wealth they gobbled up.
16They will die from the fangs
of poisonous snakes
17and never enjoy rivers flowing
with milk and honey.
18Their hard work will result
in nothing gained,
19because they cheated the poor
and took their homes.
20Greedy people want everything
and are never satisfied.
21But when nothing remains
for them to grab,
they will be nothing.
22Once they have everything,
distress and despair
will strike them down,
23and God will make them swallow
his blazing anger.
24 While running from iron spears,
they will be killed
by arrows of bronze,
25whose shining tips go straight
through their bodies.
They will be trapped by terror,
26and what they treasure most
will be lost in the dark.
God will send flames
to destroy them in their tents
with all their property.
27The heavens and the earth
will testify against them,
28and all their possessions
will be dragged off
when God becomes angry.
29This is what God has decided
for those who are evil.
translation_text:
1Kɛkɛ ni Zofa, Naamanyo lɛ, here Hiob nɔ ni ekɛɛ,
2“Miyiŋ kɛ mi ewie,
ni mihe miitswa shi ni mahã bo hetoo.
3Minu jɛmɔi ni ojɛ mi lɛ,
ni mile hetoo ni mahã bo.
4Aso oleee kɛjɛ teteete,
kɛjɛ beyinɔ ni abɔ gbɔmɔ
adesa ato shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ,
5akɛ efɔŋfeelɔi anyamɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ,
ni mɛi ni sheee Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei
amiishɛɛ yeɔ hiŋmɛitswaa kɛkɛ!
6 Egbojee aaakwɔ kɛshɛ ŋwɛi,
ni eyitso tete aaashɛ atatuiaŋ;
7 kɛ̃lɛ amɛhiɛ aaakpãtã kɛya naanɔ
tamɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwamɔ.
Mɛi ni ena amɛ pɛŋ lɛ aaabi akɛ,
‘Nɛgbɛ amɛtee?’
8Ebaalaaje tamɔ lamɔ,
ni anaŋ lɛ;
ebaalaaje tamɔ nyɔɔŋ ninaa.
9 Mɛi ni ena lɛ lɛ, enaŋ lɛ dɔŋŋ,
ni eshihilɛhe lɛ enaŋ
lɛ dɔŋŋ.
10 Ekɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ eniji baadãi
enii ni ena kɛjɛ ohiafoi adɛŋ
lɛ ehã amɛ.
Ebii baatao koni ohiafoi ana
amɛhe tsuijurɔ.
11Egbɔmɔtso yɛ kpiŋtiŋkpliŋŋ kɛ
oblahiiaŋ hewalɛ nɛ,
shi fɛɛ baatsɔ̃ sũ.
12Yɛ mli akɛ nɔfɔŋfeemɔ ŋɔɔ enaa,
ni ekɛteɔ yɛ elilɛi shishi,
13ni emiii akɛ eŋmɛɔ he,
shi etsiɔ̃ naa yɛ edaaŋ;
14kɛ̃lɛ eniyenii lɛ tsakeɔ
yɛ emusuŋ, ni etsɔ̃ɔ
tamɔ shinɔi adrɔ yɛ emli.
15Emimiɔ mɛi ajwetrii
shi eshweɔ fɛɛ ekoŋŋ.
Nyɔŋmɔ jieɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ emusuŋ.
16Eeeshwɔ shinɔi anaa ebɔɔ,
ni no aaagbe lɛ
tamɔ nɔ ni blikã ekɔ̃ lɛ.
17Ehiŋmɛi enaŋ fai lɛ ekwɛ,
fai ni hoɔ
ni eyi kɛ wo kɛ fufɔ lɛ.
18 Eeedãi nibii ni egbo he deŋme
fɛɛ ehã,
ni enaŋ hegbɛ eye eninenaa nitsumɔ
mli ŋɔɔmɔ,
19ejaakɛ ewa ohiafoi ayi, ni ekwa amɛ,
ni shĩa ni jeee lɛ ema lɛ,
eshɔ̃ɔ ekãa naa.
20Akɛni fufeemɔ leee mitɔ hewɔ lɛ,
eyeee nii ni ŋɔɔ enaa ni eshwɛ eko.
21Kɛji eye nii lɛ eshwɛɛɛ eko,
no hewɔ lɛ, eninamɔ sɛɛ etsɛŋ.
22Enii ni ena babaoo lɛ mli po,
eeefĩ lɛ,
ni hejaramɔ ni baaba enɔ lɛ
naa baawa pam.
23Nyɔŋmɔ baahã emlifu ni naa wa
lɛ anina lɛ, ni ebaanɛ eshwie enɔ,
ni ebaatsɔ̃ eniyenii ni aaayi emusu obɔ̃.
24Ebaajo dade tawuunii anaa foi;
shi akɔɔble gãi aaagbu emli kɛho.
25 Abaagbala gãi lɛ, ni ebaaje kpo
yɛ egbɔmɔtso lɛ mli;
gãi lɛ naa kaŋkaŋ lɛ fãa kɛjɛɔ
edɔrɔ mli;
ni gbele ŋmiŋmi mɔɔ lɛ.
26 Ejwetri ni ena fɛɛ hiɛ aaakpãtã;
la ni mɔ ko mɔ ko huuu
baashã enii ni eshwɛ yɛ eshĩa mli fɛɛ.
27Ŋwɛi aaajie enifɔɔji anii kpo etsɔ̃ɔ,
ni je lɛ aaate shi awo lɛ.
28Enii ni ena fɛɛ hiɛ aaakpãtã,
yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ mlifu gbi lɛ nɔ.
29Nɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ eto ehã gbɔmɔ
fɔŋ nɛ,
gboshinii ni Nyɔŋmɔ yɔɔ hã lɛ nɛ.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Zophar
If You Want To Offer Comfort
1Job said:
2If you want to offer comfort,
then listen to me.
3And when I have finished,
you can start your insults
all over again.
4My complaint is against God;
that's why I am impatient.
5Just looking at me is enough
to make you sick,
6and the very thought of myself
fills me with disgust.
7Why do evil people live so long
and gain such power?
8Why are they allowed to see
their children grow up?
9They have no worries at home,
and God never punishes them.
10Their cattle have lots of calves
without ever losing one;
11their children play and dance
safely by themselves.
12These people sing and celebrate
to the sound of tambourines,
small harps, and flutes,
13and they are successful,
without a worry,
until the day they die.
Leave Us Alone!
14Those who are evil say
to God All-Powerful,
“Leave us alone! Don't bother us
with your teachings.
15What do we gain from praying
and worshiping you?
16We succeeded all on our own.”
And so, I keep away from them
and their evil schemes.
17How often does God become angry
and send disaster and darkness
to punish sinners?
18How often does he strike them
like a windstorm
that scatters straw?
19You say, “God will punish
those sinners' children
in place of those sinners.”
But I say, “Let him punish
those sinners themselves
until they really feel it.
20Let God All-Powerful force them
to drink their own destruction
from the cup of his anger.
21Because after they are dead,
they won't care what happens
to their children.”
Who Can Tell God What To Do?
22Who can tell God what to do?
He judges powerful rulers.
* 23Some of us die prosperous,
24enjoying good health,
25while others die in poverty,
having known only pain.
26But we all end up dead,
beneath a blanket of worms.
27My friends, I know that you
are plotting against me.
28You ask, “Where is the home
of that important person
who does so much evil?”
29Everyone, near and far, agrees
30that those who do wrong
never suffer disaster,
when God becomes angry.
31No one points out their sin
or punishes them.
32Then at their funerals,
they are highly praised;
33the earth welcomes them home,
while crowds mourn.
34But empty, meaningless words
are the comfort you offer me.
translation_text:
1Kɛkɛ ni Hiob hã hetoo ekɛɛ:
2“Nyɛboa nɔ ni miyɔɔ kɛɛmɔ toi jogbaŋŋ,
ni no afee nɔ ni nyɛkɛaashɛje mimii.
3Nyɛnaa tsui nyɛhãa mi, ni mi hu mawie;
ni kɛji miwie migbe naa lɛ,
koni nyɛye mihe fɛo.
4Ani gbɔmɔ mikɛna lɛ?
Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato tsui shi?
5Nyɛkwɛa mi, ni nyɛhe aaajɔ̃ nyɛhe;
ni nyɛkɛ nyɛnine aaato nyɛnaabu.
6Kɛji mijwɛŋ he lɛ, miwerɛ hoɔ,
ni ŋmiŋmi mɔɔ mi.
7 Mɛni hewɔ mɛi fɔ̃ji ayi naa wala,
amɛgbɔlɔɔ, ni amɛjeɔ agbo
kɛ hewalɛ?
8Amɛnaa amɛbii ashweremɔ,
ni amɛnabii daraa yɛ amɛhiɛ.
9Asheee gbeyei yɛ amɛshĩai amli,
ni Nyɔŋmɔ edɔɔɔ kpãa etooo amɛnɔ.
10Amɛtsina hii lɛ kwɔɔ; ni efeee yaka,
ni amɛtsina yei lɛ sharakeee.
11Amɛhãa amɛbii jeɔ kpo, ni
amɛtumɔɔ kɛ shwɛmɔ tamɔ toobii.
12Amɛlaa kɛnyiɛɔ milɛ̃ kɛ saŋku sɛɛ;
ni amɛnyaa kɛji blɛ gbɛɛ.
13Amɛyeɔ ejurɔ yɛ amɛwala mli,
ni amɛyaa gbohiiaje kpoo kɛ toiŋjɔlɛ.
14 Yiwalɔi kɛɔ Nyɔŋmɔ akɛ, “Jee wɔnɔ!
Wɔtaooo wɔle bɔ ni otaoɔ akɛ
aba jeŋ ahã.
15Namɔ ji Ofe lɛ, ni esa akɛ
wɔsɔmɔ lɛ lɛ?
Ni mɛni sɛɛ wɔɔna kɛji
wɔsɔle wɔkpa lɛ fai?”
16 Naa, amɛshweremɔ lɛ aso
jeee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ mli eyɔɔ?
Shi yiwalɔi asusumɔ nɛɛ lɛ,
mi lɛ miŋɔɔɔ nɔ.
17 Shii enyiɛ agbe mɛi fɔ̃ji akane lɛ,
ni amanehulu eba amɛnɔ,
aloo Nyɔŋmɔ ehã amɛpiŋ
yɛ emlifu naa
18 ni amɛtsɔ̃ tamɔ jwɛi
yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa,
loo tutuu ni kɔɔyɔɔ loɔ kɛyaa?
19 Nyɛkɛɔ akɛ, ‘Nyɔŋmɔ etĩa amɛnifɔɔjianii
lɛ anaa eto ehã amɛbii.
Dabida! Nyɔŋmɔ baagbala
efɔŋfeelɔ toi yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ
enɔ fɔŋ lɛ hewɔ,
koni amɛna amɛle nɔ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee lɛ.’
20Hã ena lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehiɛkpãtãmɔ
kɛ ehiŋmɛii
ni esa enaa Ofe lɛ mlifu lɛ eko.
21Ejaakɛ mɛɛ ŋkɔmɔ eyeɔ
yɛ ebii ni eshi he,
kɛji egbii asɛɛ efo yɛ jeŋ?
22 Aso mɔ ko aaanyɛ Nyɔŋmɔ nilee etsɔ̃ɔ,
lɛ mɔ ni ekojoɔ ŋwɛibii tete po lɛ?
23Mɔ ko gboɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ kpiŋtiŋkpliŋŋ
be mli ni eyɔɔ hejɔlɛ,
ni etoiŋ hu ejɔ lɛ,
24ni egbɔmɔtso eshwi
ni ewui amli eyi
obɔ̃ kɛ fɔ tsɔtsɔɔ tsɔ lɛ.
25Mɔ ko hu gboɔ yɛ awerɛhoo mli,
ni eyeko ŋɔɔmɔ ko kwraa dã.
26 Amɛ fɛɛ amɛyajwereɔ su mli,
ni gɔgɔmii haa amɛhe.
27Naa, mile nyɛjwɛŋmɔi
kɛ ŋaa ni nyɛtsɔ̃ɔ kɛgba minaa fɛɛ.
28Ejaakɛ nyɛbiɔ akɛ,
‘Nɛgbɛ lumɔ lɛ we lɛ yɔɔ agbɛnɛ,
gbɔmɔ ni ji yiwalɔ lɛ?’
29Nyɛbiko gbɛfalɔi lɛ anii,
ni odase ni amɛyeɔ lɛ nyɛŋɔɔɔ nɔ,
30akɛ abaa yiwalɔ yi
yɛ amanehulu gbi lɛ nɔ;
ni mlifu gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ ahereɔ
eyiwala?
31Namɔ kãa yiwalɔ hiɛ,
ni namɔ woɔ lɛ nɔ ni
efee he nyɔmɔ?
32Kɛji atere lɛ ni ayaafu lɛ,
abuɔ esaŋ lɛ he tete.
33Nakai mɛi fɛɛ aaanyiɛ esɛɛ;
ni mɛi ni etsɔ̃ ehiɛ kɛtee
ayifa babaoo.
34Mɛɛba mɔ nyɛaasumɔ akɛ
nyɛkɛ yaka wiemɔi ashɛje mimii lɛ?
Nyɛwiemɔi lɛ amale sɔŋŋ ni.”

english_text:
Eliphaz's Third Speech
What Use Are We Humans to God?
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
2 What use are we humans
to God,
even the wisest of us?
3If you were completely sinless,
that would still mean nothing
to God All-Powerful.
4Is he correcting you
for worshiping him?
5No! It's because of
your terrible and endless sins.
6To guarantee payment of a debt,
you have taken clothes
from innocent people.
7And you refused bread and water
to the hungry and thirsty,
8although you were rich,
respected, and powerful.
9You have turned away widows
and have broken the arms
of orphans.
10That's why you were suddenly
trapped by terror,
11blinded by darkness,
and drowned in a flood.
God Lives in the Heavens
12God lives in the heavens
above the highest stars,
where he sees everything.
13Do you think the deep darkness
hides you from God?
14Do thick clouds cover his eyes,
as he walks around heaven's dome
high above the earth?
15Give up those ancient ideas
believed by sinners,
16who were swept away
without warning.
17They rejected God All-Powerful,
feeling he was helpless,
18although he had been kind
to their families.
The beliefs of these sinners
are truly disgusting.
19When God's people see
the godless swept away,
they celebrate, 20saying,
“Our enemies are gone,
and fire has destroyed
their possessions.”
Surrender to God All-Powerful
21Surrender to God All-Powerful!
You will find peace
and prosperity.
22Listen to his teachings
and take them to heart.
23If you return to God
and turn from sin,
all will go well for you.
24So get rid of your finest gold,
as though it were sand.
25Let God All-Powerful
be your silver and gold,
26and you will find happiness
by worshiping him.
27God will answer your prayers,
and you will keep the promises
you made to him.
28He will do whatever you ask,
and life will be bright.
29When others are disgraced,
God will clear their names
in answer to your prayers.
30Even those who are guilty
will be forgiven,
because you obey God.
translation_text:
Sanegbaa ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ
(22.1—27.23)
Elifaz wiemɔ
1Kɛkɛ ni Elifaz, Temannyo lɛ, here Hiob nɔ ekɛɛ,
2“Aso adesa ko he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ
hã Nyɔŋmɔ?
Anɔkwa, nilelɔ lɛ, lɛ diɛŋtsɛ
ehe sɛɛ enaa.
3 Ani eji miishɛɛ sane hã Ofe lɛ
kɛji ofeɔ nii ni ja?
Aloo Nyɔŋmɔ naa he sɛɛ
kɛji ohi shi ni shwamɔ ko bɛ ohe?
4Ani gbeyei ni osheɔ lɛ hewɔ
ni Nyɔŋmɔ kãa ohiɛ,
ni ekojoɔ bo nɛɛ?
5Ani jeee oyiwalɛ nifeemɔi ni naa wa
kɛ onifɔɔjianii ni aleee naa lɛ
hewɔ ekɛ bo yeɔ nɛɛ?
6 Ejaakɛ onyɛ onyɛmimɛi anɔ,
ni amɛto bo awaba yakatswaa;
ni oshɔ̃ amɛheboi oŋmɛ amɛyayai.
7Mɔ ni etɔ lɛ lɛ,
ohãaa lɛ nu ni enu;
ni mɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ hu
okamaa lɛ niyenii.
8Mɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ,
lɛ eŋɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ,
ni mɔ ni hiɛ yɔɔ nyam lɛ,
lɛ ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.
9 Yei okulafoi lɛ, ashwieɔ amɛ,
amɛyaa kɛ amɛdɛ̃ folo.
10No hewɔ lɛ, tsɔnei ebɔle bo kɛkpe,
ni ŋmiŋmi emɔ bo trukaa,
11duŋ ewo bo, ni no hewɔ lɛ,
onaaa nii,
ni nu afua eha onɔ.
12Aso Nyɔŋmɔ bɛ ŋwɛi shɔŋŋ?
Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni ŋulamii lɛ
ekomɛi yɔɔ shɔŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ hã.
13No hewɔ lɛ, okɛɔ akɛ,
‘Mɛni ji nɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ le?
Ani eeenyɛ etsɔ̃ duŋ kpii
lɛ mli ekojo lo?’
14Osusuɔ akɛ atatui kabitii etsimɔ enɔ,
ni no hewɔ lɛ, enaaa nii,
ni ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ
husu lɛ naa esharaa shi yɛ?
15Ani obaaba blema jeŋba gbonyo
ni yiwalɔi lɛ ba lɛ eko?
16 Mɛi ni ashara amɛ kɛtee dani
eshɛ amɛbe,
ni afɔ amɛshishitoo ashwie kɛ nu?
17 Amɛkɛɛ Nyɔŋmɔ akɛ,
‘Jee wɔnɔ!’
Ni ‘Mɛni Ofe lɛ baanyɛ wɔ efee?’
18 Tsɛbelɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ji mɔ ni
hã amɛshĩai shwere kɛ nii.
Minuuu mɛi fɔ̃ji lɛ ashishi!
19 Mɛi ni feɔ jalɛnii naa,
ni efeɔ amɛ miishɛɛ;
mɛi ni efeko efɔŋ ko lɛ
yeɔ amɛhe fɛo.
20Amɛkɛɔ akɛ, ‘Anɔkwa, akpãtã
wɔhenyɛlɔi lɛ ahiɛ,
ni nii ni amɛshi hu
la ekpãtã hiɛ.’
21Okɛ Nyɔŋmɔ akpãtã,
koni otoiŋ ajɔ bo;
no nɔ aaatsɔ̃ ni oooye ejurɔ.
22No hewɔ lɛ, mɔ enaa wiemɔi lɛ amli,
ni okɛ ewiemɔi lɛ ato otsuiŋ.
23 Kpalemɔ kɛya Ofe lɛ ŋɔɔ,
ni oba ohe shi.
Kpa nibii ni ejaaa feemɔ lɛ
yɛ owe lɛ mli.
24 Kɛ okɛ oshika yawo mlu mli,
ni okɛ Ofir shika yawo
faa ni hoɔ shishi tɛi amli,
25ni oŋɔ Ofe lɛ ofee oshika,
kɛ ojwiɛtɛi ni jara wa lɛ,
26 no dani omli aaafli bo
yɛ Ofe lɛ hiɛ,
ni ooowo ohiɛ nɔ okwɛ Nyɔŋmɔ!
