27 Sɔlemɔ okpa lɛ fai
ni eeebo bo toi;
ni oooye oshiwoi lɛ anɔ.
28Nɔ ni oooto oyiŋ akɛ ooofee lɛ
eeeye omanye ehã bo,
ni la aaakpɛ ahã bo yɛ ogbɛ nɔ!
29 Ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ baa mɔ ni
woɔ ehe nɔ shi,
ni heshibalɔ lɛ, ehereɔ
eyiwala.
30 Ehereɔ mɔ ni efeko efɔŋ ko yiwala.
Eeehere oyiwala kɛji ofeko esha.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
Today I Complain Bitterly
1Job said:
2Today I complain bitterly,
because God has been cruel
and made me suffer.
3If I knew where to find God,
I would go there
4and argue my case.
5Then I would discover
what he wanted to say.
6Would he overwhelm me
with his greatness?
No! He would listen
7because I am innocent,
and he would say,
“I now set you free!”
8I cannot find God anywhere—
in front or back of me,
9to my left or my right.
God is always at work,
though I never see him.
10But he knows what I am doing,
and when he tests me,
I will be pure as gold.
* 11I have never refused to follow
any of his commands,
12and I have always treasured
his teachings.
13But he alone is God,
and who can oppose him?
God does as he pleases,
14and he will do exactly
what he intends with me.
* 15Merely the thought
of God All-Powerful
16makes me tremble with fear.
17God has covered me
with darkness,
but I refuse to be silent.
translation_text:
Hiob wiemɔ
1Kɛkɛ ni Hiob here nɔ akɛ,
2“Ŋmɛnɛ hu mikɔmɔyeli lɛ naa wa;
minyɛɛɛ mitsɔidɔɔmɔ lɛ naa mamɔ.
3Oo, mile he ni mana lɛ yɛ kulɛ
maya esɛi lɛ hiɛ tɔ̃ɔ.
4Mikɛ misane lɛ baafɔ̃ ehiɛ,
ni mibakɔlɔ misane lɛ fɛɛ yɛ ehiɛ.
5Mana male nɔ hetoo ni eeehã mi
ni mana manu nɔ ni eeekɛɛ mi lɛ shishi.
6Aso Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ mi aaatao naa
yɛ ehewalɛ kpeteŋkple lɛ naa?
Dabida; eeebo mi toi kɛ̃.
7Mɔ ni feɔ jalɛnii kɛ Nyɔŋmɔ aaayiyi yɛ jɛi;
ni mikojolɔ lɛ aaabu mi bem
ni maye mihe kɛaatee naanɔ.
8Naa, kɛji mitee bokãgbɛ lɛ, ebɛ jɛi,
ni miba anaigbɛ hu, minaaa lɛ.
9Mitao lɛ yɛ kooyigbɛ,
shi minaaa lɛ;
mitsɔ̃ mihe kɛtee wuoyigbɛ hu,
shi mihiŋmɛi gbaaa enɔ.
10 Shi Nyɔŋmɔ le minanefaamɔi fɛɛ;
kɛji eka mi ekwɛ lɛ
ebaana mi akɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi.
11Minyiɛ enanefãamɔ sɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ;
no mli minyiɛ; migbako afã.
12Mitswako Nyɔŋmɔ naa wiemɔ ko
mifɔ̃ko afã dã;
mikɛto mitsui shishi tɔ̃ɔ.
13Etsakeee; ni
Lɛ lɛ eyɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ kɛjɛ sa,
ni namɔ aaanyɛ enaa eku.
Nɔ ni esumɔɔ lɛ, no efeɔ.
14Nɔ ni eto ehã mi lɛ,
ebaafee kɛgbe naa;
ni nibii ni tamɔ enɛɛmɛi
pii yɛ eyiŋ.
15No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmiŋmi mɔɔ mi
yɛ ehiɛ;
kɛji mishwie miyiŋ lɛ,
misheɔ lɛ gbeyei.
16Nyɔŋmɔ ehã mitsui efã;
Ofe lɛ ewo mihe gbeyei,
17ejaakɛ duŋ ebɔle mi kɛkpe
ni duŋ kabitii ha mihiɛ.

english_text:
Job Continues
Why Doesn't God Set a Time?
1Why doesn't God
set a time for court?
Why don't his people know
where he can be found?
2Sinners remove boundary markers
and take care of sheep
they have stolen.
3They cheat orphans and widows
by taking their donkeys
and oxen.
4The poor are trampled
and forced to hide
5in the desert,
where they and their children
must live like wild donkeys
and search for food.
6If they want grain or grapes,
they must go to the property
of these sinners.
7They sleep naked in the cold,
because they have no cover,
8and during a storm
their only shelters are caves
among the rocky cliffs.
9Children whose fathers have died
are taken from their mothers
as payment for a debt.
10Then they are forced to work
naked in the grain fields
because they have no clothes,
and they go hungry.
11They crush olives to make oil
and grapes to make wine—
but still they go thirsty.
12And along the city streets,
the wounded and dying cry out,
yet God does nothing.
Some Reject the Light
13Some rebel and refuse
to follow the light.
14Soon after sunset they murder
the poor and the needy,
and at night they steal.
15Others wait for the dark,
thinking they won't be seen
if they sleep with the wife
or husband of someone else.
16Robbers hide during the day,
then break in after dark
because they reject the light.
17They prefer night to day,
since the terrors of the night
are their friends.
Sinners Are Filthy Foam
18Those sinners are filthy foam
on the surface of the water.
And so, their fields and vineyards
will fall under a curse
and won't produce.
19Just as the heat of summer
swallows the snow,
the world of the dead
swallows those who sin.
20Forgotten here on earth,
and with their power broken,
they taste sweet to worms.
21Sinners take advantage of widows
and other helpless women.
22But God's mighty strength
destroys those in power.
Even if they seem successful,
they are doomed to fail.
23God may let them feel secure,
but they are never
out of his sight.
24Great for a while; gone forever!
Sinners are mowed down
like weeds,
then they wither and die.
25If I haven't spoken the truth,
then prove me wrong.
translation_text:
Hiob wiemɔ
1“Mɛɛba Ofe lɛ etooo be pɔtɛ̃ɛ
ni ekojoɔ,
ni mɛɛba mɛi ni sɔmɔɔ lɛ
tete leee ekojomɔ bei lɛ?
2 Mɛi tsirɛɔ husui kɛyaa sɛɛ,
amɛshɔ̃ɔ mɛi akooloi
ni amɛkɛshiɔ amɛkooloi anɔ
amɛlɛɔ.
3Amɛshɔ̃ɔ awusãi atejii yɛ amɛdɛŋ
kɛyaa;
amɛhãa okulafo kɛ etsina
toɔ amɛ awaba.
4Amɛtsirɛɔ ohiafoi kɛjeɔ gbɛteŋ,
ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shitswialɔi fɛɛ
teeteɔ amɛhe.
5No hewɔ lɛ, naa, ohiafoi lɛ
nyiɛ ŋa nɔ ni amɛmiitao
niyenii tamɔ ŋaŋ teji
amɛhã amɛbii koni amɛye.
6Ŋa nɔ amɛfolɔɔ kooloi aniyenii yɛ;
ni yiwalɔi awaintromi amli
amɛyeɔ kpɛkpɛo yɛ.
7Amɛkamɔɔ shi nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ fɛɛ
kɛ amɛhe yayai,
ni fɛ̃i be hu amɛbɛ
hehaanɔ.
8Gɔji lɛ anɔ nyɔŋmɔ eyi amɛ,
ni amɛhɔlɔ tɛkploi amli,
ejaakɛ amɛbɛ abobaahe
yɛ he ko he ko.
9Amɛteŋ mɛi komɛi tseɔ
abifao ni kã fufɔ naa awusã;
ni amɛbiɔ, ni ohiafo kɛ ebi abifao
tete batoɔ amɛ awaba.
10Ohiafoi nyiɛ yayai
ni mama bɛ amɛhe;
ni amɛtereɔ jatsu kɛ hɔmɔ.
11 Amɛfeɔ mu yɛ yiwalɔi amutsei ateŋ;
amɛŋaa wain kɛ wain tsɔnei nɛ,
shi kumai yeɔ amɛ.
12Aanu mɛi ni miigboi akɛ̃ɛmɔ
kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli,
ni pilafoi miibolɔ kɛmiitsɛ yelikɛbuamɔ;
kɛ̃lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ booo amɛfaikpamɔ toi.
13Mɛi yɛ ni amɛkwa la lɛ,
amɛnuuu egbɛjianɔtoo shishi,
ni amɛhiii shi yɛ egbɛi lɛ anɔ hu.
14Gbɔmɔgbelɔ lɛ teɔ shi leebi mra
ni eyaa eyagbeɔ ohiafo kɛ shitswialɔ,
ni kɛji je na hu lɛ etsɔ̃ɔ tamɔ julɔ.
15Ni gbãlãfitelɔ hu mɛ̃ɔ hiɛbulɛ
ni ekɛ nɔhaanɔ haa ehiɛ
ni ekɛɔ akɛ, “Mɔ ko yooŋ mi.”
16Amɛjwaraa shĩai yɛ duŋ mli nyɔɔŋ;
ni shwaneshwane lɛ
amɛŋmɛɔ amɛyi amɛwoɔ tsuŋ;
ni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ bɛ sane ko.
17Ejaakɛ nyɔɔŋ duŋ kpii lɛ
ji amɛleebi;
ejaakɛ duŋ kpii mli gbeyei nibii
lɛ ji amɛnanemɛi.
[Zofa]
18 Yiwalɔ lɛ, faa shaa lɛ kɛyaa shwiaa,
ni Nyɔŋmɔ lomɔɔ eshikpɔŋ ni eshi lɛ;
eyaaa ewaintrom lɛ mli gbɛ dɔŋŋ
eyaŋaaa wain.
19Jeŋ gbimɔ kɛ dɔlɛ hereŋŋ hãa snoo nu miiɔ,
nakai gbohiiaje hu loɔ eshafeelɔi kɛyaa.
20Hiɛkpaa amɛ nɔ yɛ blohuiaŋ,
akaiii amɛgbɛii tete dɔŋŋ;
ni no hewɔ lɛ, akuɔ yiwalɛ mli
tamɔ tso.
21Amɛyeɔ yoo kene ni bɛ bi dɛŋ nii,
ni amɛfeee yoo okulafo ejurɔ ko kwraa.
22Kɛ̃lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ tsɔ̃ɔ ehewalɛ nɔ
ehãa hewalɔi awala sɛɛ tsɛɔ;
amɛteɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ, kɛji
jeŋshihilɛ je amɛtsine.
23Nyɔŋmɔ hãa amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe,
ni amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ no nɔ,
shi ehiŋmɛi kã amɛjeŋba he daa.
24Awoɔ amɛ nɔ be kukuoo ko,
kɛkɛ lɛ amɛlaaje;
amɛgbiɔ tamɔ jwɛi, ni afolɔɔ
amɛ ashwieɔ tamɔ akuɔ abele.
25Kɛji jeee nakai ji sane lɛ,
namɔ baanyɛ ekɛɛ akɛ
amalelɔ ji mi,
asaŋ ni etsɔ̃ɔ akɛ miwiemɔi lɛ
ekome nɛkɛ bɛ mli?”

english_text:
Bildad's Third Speech
God Is the One To Fear
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2God is the one to fear,
because God is in control
and rules the heavens.
3Who can count his army of stars?
Isn't God the source of light?
4How can anyone be innocent
in the sight of God?
5To him, not even the light
of the moon and stars
can ever be pure.
6So how can we humans,
when we are merely worms?
translation_text:
1Kɛkɛ ni Bildad, Shuhinyo lɛ, here nɔ ni ekɛɛ,
2“Nyɔŋmɔ dɛŋ hewalɛ fɛɛ yɔɔ,
mɛi fɛɛ ashe lɛ gbeyei;
ehã toiŋjɔlɛ ehe shi yɛ eŋwɛi
maŋtsɛyeli lɛ mli.
3Ani aaanyɛ etabilɔi ayibɔ akane?
Namɔ kwraa nɔ ela lɛ etsooo yɛ?
4Te aaafee tɛŋŋ hu ni adesa
aaaja yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ hu?
Te aaafe tɛŋŋ ni gbɔmɔ
ni jɛ yoo musuŋ lɛ he aaatse hu?
5Naa, yɛ ehiɛ lɛ
nyɔɔŋtsere kpɛɛɛ,
ni ŋulamii lɛ hu ahe tseee;
6mbasroo adesa ni ji omlɛgɛ,
adesa fɔmɔbi ni ji gɔgɔmi nɛɛ?”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
You Have Really Been Helpful
1Job said:
2You have really been helpful
to someone weak and weary.
3You have given great advice
and wonderful wisdom
to someone truly in need.
4How can anyone possibly speak
with such understanding?
5Remember the terrible trembling
of those in the world of the dead
below the mighty ocean.
6Nothing in that land
of death and destruction
is hidden from God,
7who hung the northern sky
and suspended the earth
on empty space.
8God stores water in clouds,
but they don't burst,
9and he wraps them around
the face of the moon.
10On the surface of the ocean,
God has drawn a boundary line
between light and darkness.
11And columns supporting the sky
tremble at his command.
12By his power and wisdom,
God conquered the force
of the mighty ocean.
13The heavens became bright
when he breathed,
and the escaping sea monster
died at his hands.
14These things are merely a whisper
of God's power at work.
How little we would understand
if this whisper
ever turned into thunder!
translation_text:
Hiob wiemɔ
1Kɛkɛ ni Hiob here nɔ ni ekɛɛ,
2“Ei, bɔ ni oyeɔ obuaa
mɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ nɛ?
Ei, bɔ ni ohereɔ mɔ ni
egbɔjɔ lɛ yiwala nɛ?
3Kwɛ, bɔ ni owoɔ mɔ ni
bɛ jwɛŋmɔ lɛ ŋaa
ni ojieɔ nilee babaoo kpo
otsɔ̃ɔ nɛ?
4Namɔ wa bo kɛwie lɛ,
ni namɔ mumɔ jɛ omli je kpo nɛɛ?
[Bildad]
5Gbohii asusumai lɛ miikpokpo,
ni fai lɛ kɛ amɛmli nibii fɛɛ miikpokpo.
6 Gbohiiaje kã shi kpetekplee
yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ;
nɔ ko nɔ ko ehaaa nɔ
yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ.
7Elɛɛ kooyigbɛ ŋwɛi lɛ mli
eha shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli,
ni eŋɔ je lɛ etsotsoro shi
ni etsotsorooo nɔ ko nɔ ko nɔ.
8 Nyɔŋmɔ tiaa nu naa yɛ atatu
mli,
kɛ̃lɛ nu lɛ tsiimɔ fɛɛɛ atatu lɛ.
9Ehãa atatu lɛɔ shi,
ni ehaa nyɔɔŋtsere hiɛ fɛɛ.
10 Efo akrabatsa yɛ ŋshɔ sɛɛ
ni no etsɔ̃ husu ni kã
la kɛ duŋ lɛ teŋ.
11Akulashiŋi ni hiɛ ŋwɛi lɛ
ahe kpokpoɔ,
ni amɛhe jɔ̃ɔ amɛhe
kɛji ekã amɛhiɛ lɛ.
12Ejɔɔ ŋshɔ he yɛ ehewalɛ naa,
ni ekɛ enilee kpãtãa sasabonsam lɛ hiɛ.
13 Emumɔ ji nɔ ni hãa ŋwɛi tseɔ,
ni ekɛ enine kpãtãa onufu
ni miijo foi ni eya lɛ hiɛ.
14Naa, ehewalɛ lɛ he okadii
nyɔkɔsiɔ̃ɔi komɛi kɛkɛ nɛ;
ni ewiemɔ ablɛbi fioo kɛkɛ
wɔnuɔ lɛ.
Shi namɔ aaanyɛ ele
Nyɔŋmɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛwula shi.”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Am Desperate
1Job said:
2I am desperate because
God All-Powerful refuses
to do what is right.
As surely as God lives,
3and while he gives me breath,
4I will tell only the truth.
5Until the day I die,
I will refuse to do wrong
by saying you are right,
6because each day my conscience
agrees that I am innocent.
7I pray that my enemies
will suffer no less
than the wicked.
8Such people are hopeless,
and God All-Powerful
will cut them down,
9without listening
when they beg for mercy.
10And that is what God should do,
because they don't like him
or ever pray.
11Now I will explain in detail
what God All-Powerful does.
12All of you have seen these things
for yourselves.
So you have no excuse.
How God Treats the Wicked
13Here is how God All-Powerful
treats those who are wicked
and brutal.
14They may have many children,
but most of them will go hungry
or suffer a violent death.
15Others will die of disease,
and their widows
won't be able to weep.
16The wicked may collect riches
and clothes in abundance
as easily as clay.
17But God's people will wear
clothes taken from them
and divide up their riches.
18No homes built by the wicked
will outlast a cocoon
or a shack.
19Those sinners may go to bed rich,
but they will wake up poor.
20Terror will strike at night
like a flood or a storm.
21Then a scorching wind
will sweep them away
22without showing mercy,
as they try to escape.
23At last, the wind will celebrate
because they are gone.
translation_text:
Hiob wie ekoŋŋ
1Kɛkɛ ni Hiob wo ewiemɔ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ, ni ekɛɛ,
2“Mina Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ lɛ,
mɔ ni tswa misane lɛ efɔ̃ lɛ,
kɛ Ofe lɛ, mɔ ni hã
miwerɛ ho mihe lɛ, akɛ,
3gbii abɔ ni wala yɔɔ mimli,
ni Nyɔŋmɔ mumɔ hãa mimuɔ nɛɛ,
4 amale ejeŋ minaa,
ni mililɛi lakaŋ mɔ ko.
5Enɛ akagbale mi akɛ mabu
nyɛ bem;
kɛyaashi magbo lɛ, miŋmɛŋ
mibemyeli lɛ he.
6 Mihiɛ mijalɛ lɛ mli kpɛŋŋ,
ni miŋmɛŋ he;
mihenilee ebuuu mi fɔ
yɛ miwalaŋ
gbii lɛ eko kwraa ahe.
7Hã mihenyɛlɔ atsɔ̃ tamɔ yiwalɔ,
ni hã mɔ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ mi lɛ
atsɔ̃ tamɔ mɔ fɔŋ.
8 Ejaakɛ mɛni ji mɔ ni sheee Nyɔŋmɔ
gbeyei lɛ hiɛnɔkãmɔ,
be ni Nyɔŋmɔ efo ewala sɛɛ,
ni eshɔ̃ ewala yɛ edɛŋ lɛ?
9Kɛji fimɔ ba enɔ lɛ, ani
Nyɔŋmɔ aaabo ebolɔmɔ toi?
10Ani emii shɛɔ yɛ Ofe lɛ hewɔ,
aloo esɔleɔ ebiɔ Nyɔŋmɔ dɛŋ yelikɛbuamɔ
be fɛɛ be?
11Matsɔ̃ɔ nyɛ nɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ;
mikɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ Ofe lɛ he eteŋ nyɛ.
12Naa, nyɛ fɛɛ tswɛm nyɛna;
mɛɛ hewɔ mɔ ni nyɛwieee
wiemɔi ni ahe yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ?
13Nɔ ni mɔfɔŋ naa yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ
dɛŋ nɛ;
nɔ ni Ofe lɛ yɔɔ hã yiwalɔ nɛ.
14 Kɛji ebii ayi fa babaoo lɛ,
klante amɛyi fa amɛhã,
ni eshwiei lɛ aboloo shɛŋ amɛnaa.
15Bii ni eshiɔ yɛ esɛɛ lɛ,
gbele hela gbeɔ amɛ;
ni amɛkulafoi lɛ foŋ amɛ tete.
16Yiwalɔ buaa jwiɛtɛi naa tamɔ mlu,
ni eeebua atadei anaa eto tamɔ mɛ;
17 eeebua naa nɛ, shi mɔ ni baawo ji jalɔ,
ni mɔ ni fɔbuu bɛ ehe
ji mɔ ni baaja ejwiɛtɛi lɛ.
18Shĩa ni emaa lɛ etamɔ
anaanu ntaŋ, loo
asese ni bulɔ efee.
19Eyakãa shi akɛ niiatsɛ,
shi ebaŋ lɛ nakai dɔŋŋ;
be ni eeegbele ehiŋmɛi lɛ
enii ni eyɔɔ lɛ bɛ dɔŋŋ.
20Ŋmiŋmi mɔɔ lɛ tamɔ faa
ni eje ŋa loɔ nibii;
ahum woɔ lɛ kɛyaa nyɔɔŋ.
21Bokã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ woɔ lɛ kɛyaa,
ebɛɔ lɛ kɛjeɔ eshĩaŋ kɛyaa.
22Nyɔŋmɔ tsɛ̃ɔ kɛbaa enɔ
ni enaaa lɛ mɔbɔ,
be ni etaoɔ foi ejo kɛjɛ edɛŋ lɛ.
23Nyɔŋmɔ tswaa edɛŋ eshwieɔ enɔ,
ni eboɔ lɛ ‘tsiaa!’ kɛjɛ eshihilɛhe lɛ mli.

english_text:
Job Continues
Gold and Silver Are Mined
1Gold and silver are mined,
then purified;
2the same is done
with iron and copper.
3Miners carry lanterns
deep into the darkness
to search for these metals.
4They dig tunnels
in distant, unknown places,
where they dangle by ropes.
5Far beneath the grain fields,
fires are built
to break loose those rocks
6that have jewels or gold.
7Miners go to places unseen
by the eyes of hawks;
8they walk on soil unknown
to the proudest lions.
9With their own hands
they remove sharp rocks
and uproot mountains.
10They dig through the rocks
in search of jewels
and precious metals.
11They also uncover
the sources of rivers
and discover secret places.
Where Is Wisdom Found?
12 But where is wisdom found?
13 No human knows the way.
14Nor can it be discovered
in the deepest sea.
* 15It is worth much more
than silver or pure gold
16or precious stones.
17Nothing is its equal—
not gold or costly glass.
18Wisdom is worth much more than
coral, jasper, or rubies.
19All the topaz of Ethiopia
and the finest gold
cannot compare with it.
20Where then is wisdom?
21It is hidden from human eyes
and even from birds.
22Death and destruction
have merely heard rumors
about where it is found.
23 God is the only one who knows
the way to wisdom;
24he alone sees everything
beneath the heavens.
25When God divided out
the wind and the water,
26and when he decided the path
for rain and lightning,
27 he also determined the truth
and defined wisdom.
28 God told us, “Wisdom means
that you respect me, the Lord,
and turn from sin.”
translation_text:
Nilee kafomɔ
1“Anɔkwa, bui yɛ ni atsaa
jwiɛtɛi yɛ mli,
ni hei yɛ ni anaa shika
ni asereɔ yɛ.
2Atsaa dade yɛ shikpɔŋ
ni asereɔ akɔɔble kɛjɛɔ tɛ mli.
3Mɛi sheee duŋ gbeyei, ni amɛboteɔ duŋ
mli amɛyataoɔ tɛi ni yɔɔ
duŋ kabitii lɛ mli kɛyaa
duŋ lɛ shishi tɔ̃ɔ.
4Mɛi yatsaa shika bui
yɛ hei ni gbɔmɔ bɛ.
Gbɛfalɔi ahiɛ kpaa amɛnɔ;
amɛtsotsoroɔ kpãa naa
kɛyaa kɛbaa yɛ shika bui
lɛ amli.
5Shikpɔŋ mli niyenii jɛɔ;
shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ shishi lɛ,
efee tamɔ nɔ ni
la eshã.
6Emli tɛi amli anaa safiro yɛ,
ni shika futru hu yɛ mli.
7Okropɔŋ leee jɛigbɛ lɛ,
akroma ko hiŋmɛi enako jɛi dã.
8Kooloi kakawuai lɛ eko kwraa
nane yiko gbɛ lɛ nɔ dã,
ni jata tsɔ̃ko enɔ kɛhoko dã.
9Gbɔmɔ kɛ enine tsaa tswɛrɛbo tɛ,
ni etsaa gɔji ashishi ekɛwuleɔ
amɛ eshwieɔ shi.
10Be mli ni ekpɛɔ gbɛ
kɛtsɔ̃ɔ tɛsai amli lɛ,
ehiŋmɛi naa ojarawatɛi fɛɛ.
11Etsĩɔ fai anaa koni
amɛkanyɛ amɛho,
ni nii ni akɛtee shishi lɛ,
ejieɔ lɛ kpo etsɔ̃ɔ.
12Shi nɛgbɛ abaana nilee yɛ?
Ni nɛgbɛ ji he ni niiashishinumɔ yɔɔ?
13Gbɔmɔ leee ejarawalɛ;
ni anaaa lɛ yɛ hiɛkãalɔi
ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.
14Ŋshɔŋ bu kwɔŋkwɔŋ lɛ kɛɛ, ‘Ebɛ mimli!’
Ni ŋshɔ hu kɛɛ, ‘Ebɛ miŋɔɔ!’
15 Atseee shika aheee,
ni anyɛŋ aŋmɛ jwiɛtɛi ni baashɛ enyɔmɔwo.
16 Ofir shika shɛɛɛ ejara;
nakai nɔŋŋ ji ojarawatɛ onike loo safiro.
17Shika kɛ ashwishwɛ kɛ lɛ yeee hegbɔ;
ni akɛtsakeŋ shika jwinei kpakpai diɛŋtsɛ.
18Atsiŋ tɛ̃ŋlɛ̃o kɛ kɔli tã yɛ he ni eyɔɔ;
nilee jara wa fe adiagba.
19 Etiopia ojarawatɛ topasiɔn kɛ lɛ yeee hegbɔ,
ni anyɛŋ aŋmɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi ni baashɛ ejara.
20Belɛ nɛgbɛ nilee jɛɔ mɔ,
ni nɛgbɛ ji he ni niiashishinumɔ yɔɔ?
21Aŋɔ tee, ni hiɛkãalɔ ko hiŋmɛi enaŋ;
akɛtee loofɔji ni filikiɔ yɛ ŋwɛi tete.
22Gbele kɛ hiɛkpãtãmɔ kɛɛ,
‘He kɛkɛ wɔnu kɛ wɔtoi ni aawie.’
23 Nyɔŋmɔ pɛ ni le gbɛ ni kã kɛyaa he;
ni lɛ ele he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.
24Ejaakɛ lɛ lɛ, enaa jeŋ naagbee hei bluublu,
ni enaa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shishi.
25 Be ni eŋmɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hewalɛ ehã lɛ,
ni esusu ŋshɔi kɛ fai afalɛ,
26be ni etsɔ̃ɔ bɔ ni nu anɛ ahã,
kɛ bɔ ni srawa agba kɛnyiɛ ŋwɛi ahã lɛ;
27no mli Nyɔŋmɔ na nɔ krɛdɛɛ ni ji nilee;
ni eka etɛ naa ekwɛ ni eŋɔ nɔ.
28 Kɛkɛ ni ekɛɛ adesã akɛ,
‘Naa, Nuŋtsɔ lɛ gbeyeishemɔ lɛ, no ji nilee,
ni hewii kɛ efɔŋ hejee ji jwɛŋmɔ.’ ”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Long for the Past
1Job said:
2I long for the past,
when God took care of me,
3and the light from his lamp
showed me the way
through the dark.
4I was in the prime of life,
God All-Powerful
was my closest friend,
5and all of my children
were nearby.
6My herds gave enough milk
to bathe my feet,
and from my olive harvest
flowed rivers of oil.
* 7When I sat down at the meeting
of the city council,
8the young leaders stepped aside,
* 9while the older ones stood
10and remained silent.
Everyone Was Pleased
11Everyone was pleased
with what I said and did.
12When poor people or orphans
cried out for help,
I came to their rescue.
13And I was highly praised
for my generosity to widows
and others in poverty.
14Kindness and justice
were my coat and hat;
15I was helpful to the blind
and to the lame.
16I was a father to the needy,
and I defended them in court,
even if they were strangers.
17When criminals attacked,
I broke their teeth
and set their victims free.
18I felt certain that I would live
a long and happy life,
then die in my own bed.
19In those days I was strong
like a tree with deep roots
and with plenty of water,
20or like an archer's new bow.
21Everyone listened in silence
to my welcome advice,
22and when I finished speaking,
nothing needed to be said.
23My words were eagerly accepted
like the showers of spring,
24and the smile on my face
renewed everyone's hopes.
25My advice was followed
as though I were a king
leading my troops,
or someone comforting
those in sorrow.
translation_text:
Hiob naagbee naajiemɔ
1Hiob bɔ̃i wiemɔ ekoŋŋ, ni ekɛɛ,
2“Oo, mina ni kulɛ mitsɔ̃ tamɔ
bɔ ni miyɔɔ be ko ni eho lɛ,
be mli ni Nyɔŋmɔ buɔ mihe lɛ,
3 be ni ela lɛ kpɛɔ yɛ miyiteŋgbɛ
ni minaa nii yɛ duŋ mli lɛ.
4 No be mli lɛ, minibii shwere,
ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ naanyobɔɔ bu miwe lɛ he.
5Ofe lɛ kɛ mi yɛ,
ni mimusuŋbii hu bɔle mihe kɛkpe.
6Mitsinai kɛ mitoi hãa mi fufɔ babaoo,
ni mimutsei shwere yɛ tɛsai amli.
7Kɛji mije kpo kɛtee maŋ koi lɛ shi,
ni miyata shi yɛ blohuŋ lɛ,
8oblahii lɛ hãa mi gbɛ kɛji amɛna mi,
ni onukpai lɛ teɔ shi hãa mi,
9lumɛi tete fɔ̃ɔ wiemɔ,
ni amɛkɛ amɛniji toɔ amɛnaabu;
10abladei agbei laajeɔ,
ni amɛlilɛi kpɛtɛɔ amɛdaaŋ.
11Mɛi fɛɛ ni nuɔ mihe lɛ jɔɔ mi,
ni kɛji amɛna mi lɛ, amɛkafoɔ mi.
12 Ejaakɛ mihereɔ ohiafo ni foɔ
kɛ awusã ni bɛ bualɔ lɛ.
13Mɔ ni hiɛ heɔ akpãtã lɛ jɔɔmɔ baninaa mi,
ni mihãa okulafo tsui nyɔɔ emli kɛ nyamɔ.
14Jalɛ ji mimama ni mibuɔ,
ni mijalɛ saneyeli ji mitade kɛ akekre.
15Mitsɔ̃ hiŋmɛi mihã shwilafo,
ni mitsɔ̃ naji mihã obubuafo.
16Mitsɔ̃ tsɛ mihã ohiafoi
ni mɛi ni mileee amɛ tete
mitao amɛsaji amli mihã amɛ.
17 Mikumɔ mɔfɔŋ lɛ nyanyɔji yɛ edaaŋ,
ni ehã eŋmɛɛ nɔ ni kɔ̃ enaa
ni eyaaye lɛ he efɔ̃ shi.
18Kɛkɛ ni mikɛɛ mihe akɛ,
“Mishĩa teŋ magbo yɛ
ni migbii baafa tamɔ shia.
19Mitamɔ tso ni efãi etsɛ̃rɛ
kɛtee kɛyanina nu,
ni bɔ nyɔɔ ebai anɔ
nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ fɛɛ.
20Mɛi ahiɛ sɔɔ mi be fɛɛ be,
ni migãi lɛ hu naa hewalɛ hee yɛ midɛŋ.”
21Mɛi bo mi toi, ni amɛmɛ,
ni amɛfee kpoo kɛmɛ nɔ ni miyɔɔ kɛɛmɔ.
22Kɛji miwie sɛɛ lɛ,
mɔ ko ewieee dɔŋŋ;
ni miwiemɔi lɛ boteɔ amɛmli.
23Amɛkwɛɔ miwiemɔ gbɛ
tamɔ okwaafonyo kwɛɔ nunɛmɔ gbɛ.
24Miŋmɔɔ kɛji mina akɛ amɛtsui miiye,
ni mihiɛ ŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ amɛ hewalɛ.
25Mi, mito amɛshihilɛ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ,
ni mihi shi mihã amɛ akɛ yitso;
mihi shi yɛ etabilɔi ateŋ akɛ maŋtsɛ.
Mihi shi akɛ mɔ ni shɛjeɔ ŋkɔmɔyelɔi amii.

english_text:
Job Continues
Young People Now Insult Me
1Young people now insult me,
although their fathers
would have been a disgrace
to my sheep dogs.
2And those who insult me
are helpless themselves.
3They must claw the desert sand
in the dark for something
to satisfy their hunger.
4They gather tasteless shrubs
for food and firewood,
5and they are run out of towns,
as though they were thieves.
6Their only homes are ditches
or holes between rocks,
7where they bray like donkeys
gathering around shrubs.
8And like senseless donkeys
they are chased away.
Those Worthless Nobodies
9Those worthless nobodies
make up jokes and songs
to disgrace me.
10They are hateful
and keep their distance,
even while spitting
in my direction.
11God has destroyed me,
and so they don't care
what they do.
12Their attacks never stop,
though I am defenseless,
and my feet are trapped.
13Without any help,
they prevent my escape,
destroying me completely
14and leaving me crushed.
15Terror has me surrounded;
my reputation and my riches
have vanished like a cloud.
I Am Sick at Heart
16I am sick at heart!
Pain has taken its toll.
17Night chews on my bones,
causing endless torment,
18and God has shrunk my skin,
choking me to death.
19I have been thrown in the dirt
and now am dirt myself.
20I beg God for help,
but there is no answer;
and when I stand up,
he simply stares.
21God has turned brutal,
22stirring up a windstorm
to toss me about.
23Soon he will send me home
to the world of the dead,
where we all must go.
24No one refuses help to others,
when disaster strikes.
25I mourned for the poor
and those who suffered.
26But when I beg for relief
and light,
all I receive are disaster
and darkness.
27My stomach is tied in knots;
pain is my daily companion.
28My days are dark and gloomy
and in the city council
I stand and cry out,
29making mournful sounds
like jackals and owls.
30My skin is so parched,
that it peels right off,
and my bones are burning.
31My only songs are sorrow
and sadness.
translation_text:
1 Shi agbɛnɛ mɛi ni miye amɛ onukpa miiŋmɔ mi;
mɛi ni mibuŋ amɛtsɛmɛi bɔ ni maŋɔ amɛ mafata
gbei ni buɔ tookui tete ahe lɛ anɔ.
2Mɛɛ sɛɛ mibana yɛ mɛi ni egbɔlɔ ahe?
3Ohia kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa
hãa amɛkpeɔ ŋa gbiŋ nɔ tsei ashishifãi.
4Amɛfamɔɔ shiaŋaŋ tsei,
ni amɛtsɛrɛɔ koowie bai
ni amɛshɛreɔ blɔtsei amɛwereɔ.
5Ashwieɔ amɛ kɛjeɔ gbɔmɛi ateŋ,
ni awɔɔ amɛyi tamɔ awɔɔ julɔ yi.
6Nujɔi ajɔi amli kɛ shikpɔŋ bui
kɛ tɛkploi amli amɛaahi.
7Koowiei ashishi amɛbolɔɔ yɛ;
sɔŋsrɔ shishi amɛbuaa amɛhe naa yɛ.
8Kwashiai yakagbɔmɛi abii;
ayi amɛ, ashwie amɛ kɛje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.
9Shi agbɛnɛ, mitsɔ̃ amɛdaaŋ kotsa,
ni mitsɔ̃ fɛoyeli wiemɔ mihã amɛ.
10 Amɛnyaŋeɔ mi;
amɛwiɔ amɛhe yɛ mihe,
kɛji amɛna mi lɛ amɛtsɛ̃ɔ lajɔ̃.
11Akɛni Nyɔŋmɔ ehã migbɔjɔ
ni eba mi shi hewɔ lɛ,
amɛhiɛ gbooo nɔ ni amɛfeɔ he yɛ mihiɛ.
12Yakagbɔmɛi teɔ shi yɛ mininejurɔ nɔ,
ni amɛshwieɔ mi kɛyaa sɛɛ,
ni amɛkaa mihiɛ kpãtãmɔ tete.
13Amɛtsimɔɔ migbɛ ni matsɔ̃ nɔ lɛ,
ni amɛbɔɔ mihiɛkpãtãmɔ he mɔdɛŋ,
ni mɔ ko ebooo amɛ tswai!
14Amɛkeɔ kɛbaa tamɔ mɛi
ni egbu gbogbo ewo mli
ni amɛbashwieɔ minɔ.
15Adɔ gbeyei nibii ayi kɛba minɔ,
minunyam etã oookɛɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni etswa kɛtee;
kɔɔyɔɔ etswa nii ni mina fɛɛ kɛtee tamɔ atatu.
16 Agbɛnɛ eshɛ migbele be,
ni mikã nɔnaa mli gbii abɔ nɛɛ.
17Duŋ lɛ hãa miwui amli kpeɔ mi,
mipiŋmɔ lɛ ejɔɔɔ.
18 Enaawalɛ lɛ kpitiɔ mitade lɛ:
efiɔ lɛ kɛmɔɔ misɛ̃.
19Nyɔŋmɔ eshɛ mi efɔ̃ ŋmɔtɔ mli,
ni mitsɔ̃ tamɔ mlu kɛ lamlu.
20 Mibolɔɔ mitsɛɔ bo, shi ohereee mi nɔ;
mihoɔ midamɔɔ shi misɔleɔ;
shi okwɛɛɛ mi po.
21Oowa mi yi;
okɛ ohewalɛ fɛɛ miipiŋ mi.
22Owoɔ mi owoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli,
ni etswaa mi kɛfoɔ shi;
ni otswiaa mi shi kɛbɔleɔ shi yɛ ahum mli.
23Hɛɛ, mile akɛ okɛ mi baaya ayahã gbele,
ni ji shĩa ni ato ahã hiɛkãalɔi fɛɛ lɛ.
24Kɛ̃lɛ aso mɔ ni kã hiɛkpãtãmɔ mli kpãaa enineŋ
yɛ emanehulu lɛ mli ni ebi yelikɛbuamɔ lo?
25Ani mifooo mihãaa mɔ ni yɔɔ haomɔ mli?
Ani misusuma werɛ hooo hãaa ohiafo?
26 Shi be ni mikwɛ nɔ kpakpa gbɛ lɛ,
nɔ fɔŋ moŋ ni ba;
ni be ni mimɛ la lɛ, duŋ moŋ wo mi.
27Mitsui miitswa kɛ hejaramɔ,
ni enyɔɔɔ shi;
amanehulu gbii enina mi.
28Duŋ ewo mi kɛmiiya kɛmiiba;
ni hulu etsooo ehãaa mi kwraa,
mihoɔ midamɔɔ shi yɛ maŋ,
ni mibiɔ yelikɛbuamɔ.
29Mitsɔ̃ ŋaŋgbei anyɛmi
kɛ okpɔŋɔloofɔji anaanyo.
30Mihewolo edĩ, ni eekpɔlɔ yɛ mihe eeshwie shi;
ni miwui amli miishã mi.
31 Mikpãa saŋku lɛ gbɛɛmɔ etsɔ̃ ŋkɔmɔyeli,
ni mibɛlɛ gbɛɛmɔ etsɔ̃ yaafolɔi agbee.

english_text:
Job Continues
I Promised Myself
1I promised myself
never to stare with desire
at a young woman.
2God All-Powerful punishes
men who do that.
3In fact, God sends disaster
on all who sin,
4and he keeps a close watch
on everything I do.
5I am not dishonest or deceitful,
6and I beg God to prove
my innocence.
7If I have disobeyed him
or even wanted to,
8then others can eat my harvest
and uproot my crops.
9If I have desired someone's wife
and chased after her,
10then let some stranger
steal my wife from me.
11If I took someone's wife,
it would be a horrible crime,
12sending me to destruction
and my crops to the flames.
13When my servants
complained against me,
I was fair to them.
14Otherwise, what answer
would I give to God
when he judges me?
15After all, God is the one
who gave life to each of us
before we were born.
I Have Never Cheated Anyone
16 I have never cheated widows
or others in need,
17and I have always shared
my food with orphans.
18Since the time I was young,
I have cared for orphans
and helped widows.
19I provided clothes for the poor,
20and I was praised
for supplying woolen garments
to keep them warm.
21If I have ever raised my arm
to threaten an orphan
when the power was mine,
22I hope that arm will fall
from its socket.
23I could not have been abusive;
I was terrified at the thought
that God might punish me.
24 I have never trusted
the power of wealth,
25or taken pride in owning
many possessions.
* 26I have never openly or secretly
27worshiped the sun or moon.
28Such horrible sins
would have deserved
punishment from God.
29I have never laughed
when my enemies
were struck by disaster.
30Neither have I sinned
by asking God
to send down on them
the curse of death.
31No one ever went hungry
at my house,
32and travelers
were always welcome.
33Many have attempted to hide
their sins from others—
but I refused.
34And the fear of public disgrace
never forced me to keep silent
about what I had done.
Why Doesn't God Listen?
35Why doesn't God All-Powerful
listen and answer?
If God has something against me,
let him speak up
or put it in writing!
36Then I would wear his charges
on my clothes and forehead.
37And with my head held high,
I would tell him everything
I have ever done.
38I have never mistreated
the land I farmed
and made it mourn.
39Nor have I cheated
my workers
and caused them pain.
40If I had, I would pray
for weeds instead of wheat
to grow in my fields.
After saying these things,
Job was silent.
translation_text:
1 Mikã mihiŋmɛi kitã
ni no hewɔ lɛ, te aaafee tɛŋŋ mahã oblayoo foro he
afee mi akɔnɔ hu?
2Mɛni mana kɛaajɛ Nyɔŋmɔ
ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi nɛɛ dɛŋ?
Ni mɛni aaafee migbɛfaŋ nɔ
ni Ofe ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baahã mi?
3Ani jeee hiɛkpãtãmɔ kã shi
hã mɛi ni feɔ nɔ fɔŋ?
Kɛ osharã hã mɛi ni feɔ nishaianii?
4 Ani Nyɔŋmɔ leee mijeŋba,
ni ekaneee minanefaamɔi?
5Kɛji miba mijeŋ kɛ kutumpɔo,
ni miye oyai mishishiu mɔ ko lɛ,
6no lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ nsɛni ni ja aŋmɛ mi
koni ena akɛ kpako bɛ mihe.
7 Kɛji migba afã yɛ minyiɛmɔŋ,
ni mitsui eyadi mihiŋmɛi sɛɛ,
ni muji ko kpɛtɛ miniji ahe lɛ,
8no lɛ nii ni madu lɛ,
mɔ kroko aaaye,
ni ŋmɔshinii ni aaakwɛ̃ ahã mi lɛ, afãmɔ ashwie.
9Kɛji minaanyo ŋa he efee mi akɔnɔ pɛŋ,
ni miyawo ka yɛ minaanyo shinaa shi pɛŋ lɛ,
10 no lɛ hã miŋa ahoo nii ahã nuu kroko,
ni mɛi krokomɛi kɛ lɛ ana bɔlɛ.
11Ejaakɛ hiɛgbeji asane kpeteŋkple ni;
eji nɔ fɔŋ ni kojolɔi lɛ baagbala etoi,
12ejaakɛ tɔ̃mɔ lɛ baatsɔ̃ la ni baashã
nii kɛshɛ abonsamiiaje,
ni ebaashã nii ni miyɔɔ fɛɛ wɛɛ kɛmɔ shi.
13Kɛji miyeee mitsulɔ nuu loo mitsulɔ yoo
jalɛ sane be ni amɛ kɛ mi ena lɛ,
14no lɛ te mafee tɛŋŋ
kɛji Nyɔŋmɔ te shi wo mi lɛ?
Kɛji eba kojomɔ lɛ,
te majie minaa makɛɛ tɛŋŋ?
15 Ani mɔ ni bɔ mi ewo musuŋ lɛ
jeee lɛ nɔŋŋ ebɔ amɛ?
Ani jeee mɔ koome shɔ̃ wɔ fɛɛ yɛ musuŋ?
16 Kɛji mikãma ohiafoi anii ni amɛtaoɔ,
aloo mihã jeŋ fee okulafo awerɛho,
17aloo miye nii mikome pɛ,
ni mihãaa awusãi eko
18tsɛbelɛ mi mihiɛ lɛ akɛ tsɛ kɛjɛ eblahiiaŋ,
ni kɛjɛ enyɛ musuŋ beebe lɛ mi miwa lɛ.
19 Kɛji mina mɔ ko ni efĩ lɛ ni mama bɛ ehe,
loo ohiafo ko ni bɛ nɔ ni ehaa lɛ,
20no lɛ mahã lɛ mama
ni akɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mitoo he tsɔi lo
koni ehe afee kulɔɔ,
kɛkɛ lɛ ebaajie miyi kɛ etsuiŋ fɛɛ.
21 Kɛji miwo minine nɔ yɛ awusã ko nɔ,
ejaakɛ mile akɛ abaabu mi bem yɛ kojomɔhe lɛ,
22no lɛ mikɔ̃ŋ lɛ akpɔ yɛ mikɔ̃ŋ wu lɛ he,
ni minine hu atse kɛje kɔ̃ŋ wu lɛ he.
23 Ejaakɛ misheɔ Ofe lɛ dɛŋ hiɛkpãtãmɔ lɛ gbeyei.
Ni minyɛŋ Ofe lɛ hiɛ madamɔ.
24Kɛji miŋɔ shika mifee mihiɛnɔkãmɔ,
aloo mitsɛ shika ŋmiiŋmi mihiɛnɔkãmɔ,
25ni minya ejaakɛ minii ni mina fa babaoo,
ni minine eshɛ nii babaoo nɔ
26 kɛji mikwɛ hulu ni eetso,
loo nyɔɔŋtsere bɔ ni ekpɛɔ fɛɛfɛo kɛhoɔ.
27 Kɛji nɔ ko elaka mitsui
ni miwo amɛ yɛ teemɔŋ
ni mishwɔ minine naa
kɛ hiɛsɔlɛ mihã amɛ lɛ,
28no hu nifɔɔjianii ni esa akɛ
kojolɔi lɛ awo he nyɔmɔ ni.
Ejaakɛ kulɛ miyeko Nyɔŋmɔ
ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔkwa.
29 Minyako yɛ osharã ni esharã
mihenyɛlɔ hewɔ,
ni mimli efiliko mi
be ni amanehulu eba enɔ.
30 Miŋmɛko minaabu gbɛ ni efee esha,
ni mitaoko egbele kɛ kitãkãmɔ.
31Mishĩaŋbii ekɛŋ akɛ,
‘Wɔteŋ namɔ yeko edɛŋ niyenii
etɔko dã?’
32 Gbɔ ko gbɔ ko etooo blohuŋ;
migbeleɔ mishinaa mihãa gbɔ be fɛɛ be.
33Mitsimɔko mitɔ̃mɔi anɔ
tamɔ Adam,
ni mikɛ minɔsha lɛ etoko mimli.
34Miishe mɛi asafo lɛ gbeyei,
ni bɔ ni wekui baanyaŋe mi hu
woɔ mihe gbeyei,
ni no hewɔ ni mifee diŋŋ,
ni mishiii shĩa mijeee kpo
ejaakɛ miishe amɛ gbeyei.
35 Oo, mina mɔ ko ni aaabo mi toi!
Naa, minine naa okadi!
Ofe lɛ ahã mi hetoo!
Oo, mina ni kulɛ mɔ ni kɛ mi ena lɛ
eŋmala saji ni ekɛshiɔ mi lɛ
ewo wolo hiɛ!
36Anɔkwa, kulɛ makɔ matswa
mikɔŋ,
ni mikɛbaafee akekre mafi miyitso.
37Kulɛ matsɔ̃ɔ Nyɔŋmɔ nibii fɛɛ
ni mifee,
ni matsi mabɛŋkɛ lɛ tamɔ lumɔ
38kɛji shikpɔŋ ni mihu nɔ bolɔ wo mi
ni enɔ akofii wo yara kutuu;
39 kɛji mikpa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yibii miye
ni miwooo nyɔmɔ,
ni no nɔ tsɔ̃ ni nɔtsɛmɛi lɛ gboi lɛ,
40no lɛ ŋmei akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmãa najiaŋ,
ŋmei gbohii akwɛ̃ yɛ abele najiaŋ.”
Hiob wiemɔ lɛ naagbee nɛ.

english_text:
Elihu Is Upset with Job's Friends
1Finally, these three men stopped arguing with Job, because he refused to admit he was guilty.
2Elihu from Buz was there, and he had become upset with Job for blaming God instead of himself. 3He was also angry with Job's three friends for not being able to prove that Job was wrong. 4Elihu was younger than these three, and he let them speak first. 5But he became irritated when they could not answer Job, 6and he said to them:
I am much younger than you,
so I have shown respect
by keeping silent.
7I once believed age
was the source of wisdom;
8now I truly realize
wisdom comes from God.
9Age is no guarantee of wisdom
and understanding.
10That's why I ask you
to listen to me.
I Eagerly Listened
* 11I eagerly listened
to each of your arguments,
12but not one of you proved
Job to be wrong.
13You shouldn't say,
“We know what's right!
Let God punish him.”
14Job hasn't spoken against me,
and so I won't answer him
with your arguments.
15All of you are shocked;
you don't know what to say.
16But am I to remain silent,
just because you
have stopped speaking?
17No! I will give my opinion,
18because I have so much to say,
that I can't keep quiet.
19I am like a swollen wineskin,
and I will burst
20if I don't speak.
* 21I don't know how to be unfair
or to flatter anyone—
22if I did, my Creator
would quickly destroy me!
translation_text:
Elihu wiemɔ
1Kɛkɛ ni hii etɛ̃ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ Hiob hetoohãmɔ, ejaakɛ amɛna akɛ Hiob wiemɔ lɛ miitsɔ̃ɔ akɛ efeko nɔ fɔŋ ko. 2 Kɛkɛ ni Elihu, Buznyo Barakel ni jɛ Ram weku lɛ mli lɛ, mli wo la. Emli wo la ewo Hiob, ejaakɛ Hiob bu ehe jalɔ ni eshwa Nyɔŋmɔ. 3 Emlifu Hiob nanemɛi etɛ̃ lɛ hu, ejaakɛ amɛnaaa hetoo ko amɛhã Hiob, tsɛbelɛ amɛtsɔ̃ hiɛ amɛbua he akɛ Hiob yeɔ fɔ. 4Elihu mɛ be fioo dani ekɛ Hiob wie, ejaakɛ Hiob nanemɛi lɛ ye lɛ onukpa. 5Be ni Elihu na akɛ hii etɛ̃ nɛɛ bɛ nɔ ko dɔŋŋ ni amɛkɛɔ Hiob lɛ, emli wo la.
6Kɛkɛ ni Elihu, Buznyo Barakel bi lɛ, here nɔ ni ekɛɛ akɛ,
“Gbekɛ ji mi yɛ afii amli,
shi nyɛ lɛ nyɛdara;
no hewɔ lɛ, mishe gbeyei
ni mikɛ misusumɔ aŋmɛ
nyɛhiɛ.
7 Mikɛɛ mihe akɛ nyɛ ji mɛi
ni esa akɛ nyɛwie;
nyɛ waŋtsɛmɛi nyɛwieɔ
ni akaseɔ nii kɛjɛɔ nyɛdɛŋ.
8Shi kɛ̃lɛ mumɔ ni yɔɔ adesa mli,
Ofe lɛ mumɔ ni ekɛmuɔ lɛ,
no hãa enaa jwɛŋmɔ.
9Jeee dalɛ ni hãa mɔ leɔ nii,
ni jeee gbɔlɛ hu ni hãa
anuɔ sane shishi.
10No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛboa mi toi
koni mi hu mawie mijwɛŋmɔ.
11Naa, mito mitsui shi mibo
nyɛwiemɔi lɛ atoi,
mimɛ beiaŋ ni nyɛtaoɔ
nɔ ni nyɛaakɛɛ lɛ.
12Mibo nyɛ toi aahu;
ni naa, nyɛteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko
ekuuu ewooo Hiob naa;
aloo nyɛteŋ mɔ ko ehã ewiemɔi lɛ ahetoo.
13Nyɛkwɛa ni nyɛkakɛa akɛ,
‘Wɔle nii. Nyɔŋmɔ ni
aaaku enaa, shi jeee gbɔmɔ.’
14Ewieko eshiko mi,
ni mikɛ nyɛnaa wiemɔi lɛ
haŋ lɛ hetoo.
15Ashi amɛ shi, amɛhãaa
hetoo dɔŋŋ;
amɛbɛ nɔ ko ni amɛkɛɔ dɔŋŋ.
16Ni esa akɛ mimɛɔ
ejaakɛ amɛwieee;
amɛdamɔ shi diŋŋ
ni amɛhãaa wiemɔ ko hetoo dɔŋŋ?
17Mi hu makɛɛ minɔ;
ni mi hu mawie nɔ ni misusuɔ.
18Ejaakɛ minyɛɛɛ mamua minaa
dɔŋŋ;
mumɔ ni yɔɔ mimli lɛ ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ
mi dɔŋŋ.
19Naa, mitsui etsɔ̃ tamɔ wain
ni atsi naa kpɛŋŋ,
ni ebɛ mumɔhe,
etamɔ wain wolotɔi hei
ni heɔ aflɛ.
20Mawie koni mana hejɔlɛ.
Ja migbele minaa mihã hetoo.
21Mikwɛŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko hiɛ,
ni midɔkɔŋ minaa mihaŋ mɔ ko.
22Ejaakɛ mileee mɔhɔlɔmɔ;
nakai ni kulɛ Nyɔŋmɔ, miBɔlɔ lɛ,
aaafo miwala sɛɛ biɛ be kukuoo mli.”

english_text:
Elihu Speaks
Job, Listen to Me!
1Job, listen to me!
Pay close attention.
* 2Everything I will say
3is true and sincere,
4just as surely as the Spirit
of God All-Powerful
gave me the breath of life.
5Now line up your arguments
and prepare to face me.
6We each were made from clay,
and God has no favorites,
7so don't be afraid of me
or what I might do.
I Have Heard You Argue
8I have heard you argue
9that you are innocent,
guilty of nothing.
10You claim that God
has made you his enemy,
11 that he has bound your feet
and blocked your path.
12But, Job, you're wrong—
God is greater
than any human.
13So why do you challenge God
to answer you?
14God speaks in different ways,
and we don't always
recognize his voice.
* 15 Sometimes in the night,
he uses terrifying dreams
16to give us warnings.
17God does this to make us turn
from sin and pride
18and to protect us
from being swept away
to the world of the dead.
19Sometimes we are punished
with a serious illness
and aching joints.
20Merely the thought
of our favorite food
makes our stomachs sick,
21and we become so skinny
that our bones stick out.
22We feel death and the grave
taking us in their grip.
23One of a thousand angels
then comes to our rescue
by saying we are innocent.
24The angel shows kindness,
commanding death to release us,
because the price was paid.
25Our health is restored,
we feel young again,
26and we ask God to accept us.
Then we joyfully worship God,
and we are rewarded
because we are innocent.
27When that happens,
we tell everyone,
“I sinned and did wrong,
but God forgave me
28and rescued me from death!
Now I will see the light.”
29God gives each of us
chance after chance
30to be saved from death
and brought into the light
that gives life.
31So, Job, pay attention
and don't interrupt,
32though I would gladly listen
to anything you say
that proves you are right.
33Otherwise, listen in silence
to my wisdom.
translation_text:
1“Ni agbɛnɛ, Hiob, bo toi,
ni ofee toi ohã miwiemɔi lɛ fɛɛ.
2Naa, migbele minaa
ni mawie nɔ ni misusuɔ.
3Wiemɔi fɛɛ ni mawie lɛ
jɛ mitsui mli krɔŋŋ;
ni mawie nɔ ni mile anɔkwaleŋ.
4Nyɔŋmɔ mumɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni bɔ mi,
ni Ofe lɛ mumɔ lɛ hãa
miyi naa wala.
5Kɛji ooonyɛ lɛ, too he ohã mi;
saamɔ ohe; saamɔ nɔ ni obaakɛɛ lɛ oto.
6Naa, mi kɛ bo yeɔ hegbɔ
yɛ Yehowa gbɛfaŋ;
mi hu sũ nɔŋŋ akɛshɔ̃ mi.
7Naa, mihe ŋmiŋmi akawo
ohe gbeyei;
minyɛŋ onɔ.
8Lɛɛlɛŋ, owie owo mitoiiaŋ,
ni minu owiemɔi lɛ.
9Okɛɛ akɛ, ‘Mihe tse,
tɔ̃mɔ ko bɛ mihe;
miyeɔ bem, ni mifeko esha ko.
10 Naa, eetao sane efo eŋmɛ minɔ;
ebuɔ mi akɛ ehenyɛlɔ.
11 Ebɔ minaji apã,
ejie ehiɛ eka mi.’
12Naa, miikɛɛ bo akɛ,
enɛ mli lɛ osane lɛ ejaaa; ejaakɛ
Nyɔŋmɔ da aahu fe adesa.
13Mɛni hewɔ oshwaa Nyɔŋmɔ
ni okɛɔ akɛ, ‘Ehãaa miwiemɔi
lɛ eko kwraa hetoo lɛ.’
14Ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ wieɔ shii abɔ,
fɛɛ ni adesa ediii sɛɛ.
15 Nyɔɔŋ be ni wɔ ni tsii
enyɔ adesai anɔ
yɛ amɛsai amli lɛ,
Nyɔŋmɔ tsɔ̃ɔ lamɔ kɛ nyɔɔŋ
ninaa nɔ
16 ni egbeleɔ adesai atoiiaŋ
ni ekɛ kɔkɔbɔɔ woɔ amɛhe gbeyei
17 koni ehã adesa akpale
kɛjɛ enifeemɔnii ahe,
ni ehã adesa akpa ehenɔwomɔ lɛ.
18Etsiɔ adesa susuma naa
koni ekayagbee bu kwɔŋkwɔŋ lɛ mli;
ebuɔ ewala hu he koni akakpãtã
hiɛ kɛ klante.
19Nyɔŋmɔ gbalaa adesa toi
kɛ saa mli piŋmɔ
kɛ ewuiaŋ kpemɔ,
20ni no hãa edaaŋ gboɔ kɛ niyeli,
ni ekpoɔ niyenii ni kpɔɔ ewɔlɔmɔ tete.
21Etãa loo ni ehiii lɛ kwɛmɔ,
ni egbɔmɔtsoŋ wui ni kulɛ
anaaa lɛ bajwereɔ shi faŋŋ.
22Ebɛŋkɛɔ gbohiiaje, ni ewala
bɛŋkɛɔ gbele bɔfoi lɛ.
23 Kɛji ena bɔfoi akpe
lɛ ateŋ eko damɔ mli hã lɛ,
ni etsɔ̃ɔ gbɔmɔ nɔ ni hi hã lɛ,
24ni ena gbɔmɔ mɔbɔ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ,
‘Jiemɔ lɛ kɛjɛ gbohiiajeyaa mli,
mina eyinii ni akɛkpɔ̃ lɛ.’
25No lɛ eheloo aaatsɔ̃ efɔ́ tamɔ
gbekɛ nɔ,
ni eeeku sɛɛ etsɔ̃ oblanyo ekoŋŋ.
26Eeekpa Nyɔŋmɔ fai, ni eeeduro lɛ;
ni eeeba Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ kɛ nyamɔ.
Eeegba eyiwalaheremɔ lɛ etsɔ̃ɔ mɛi.
27Ni eeela yɛ adesai ahiɛ,
ni eeekɛɛ akɛ, ‘Mifee esha,
ni mikɔ̃dɔ̃ nɔ ni ja;
ni akɛ mihe fa mi;
28Ehere misusuma kɛjɛ gbohiiaje
ni mihiɛ kã lolo.’
29Naa, Nyɔŋmɔ feɔ nɛkɛ nii nɛɛ
shii abɔ ehãa gbɔmɔ,
30 koni ehere eyiwala kɛjɛ gbohiiaje,
koni wala afee enɔ.
31Oo Hiob, ka otoi!
Bo mi toi, feemɔ diŋŋ,
mibawie!
32Kɛji oyɛ nɔ ko ni oookɛɛ lɛ,
kɛɛmɔ mi!
Wiemɔ, shi miitao bo bem mabu.
33Kɛjeee nakai lɛ,
bo moŋ bo mi toi;
feemɔ diŋŋ, ni matsɔ̃ɔ bo nilee.”

english_text:
Elihu Continues
You Men Think You Are Wise
1Elihu said:
2You men think you are wise,
but just listen to me!
3Think about my words,
as you would taste food.
4Then we can decide the case
and give a just verdict.
5Job claims he is innocent
and God is guilty
of mistreating him.
6Job also argues that God
considers him a liar
and that he is suffering severely
in spite of his innocence.
7But to tell the truth,
Job is shameless!
8He spends his time with sinners,
9because he has said,
“It doesn't pay to please God.”
If Any of You Are Smart
10If any of you are smart,
you will listen and learn
that God All-Powerful
does what is right.
11 God always treats everyone
the way they deserve,
12and he is never unfair.
13From the very beginning,
God has been in control
of all the world.
14If God took back the breath
that he breathed into us,
15we humans would die
and return to the soil.
16So be smart and listen!
17The mighty God is the one
who brings about justice,
and you are condemning him.
18Indeed, God is the one
who condemns unfair rulers.
19And God created us all;
he has no favorites,
whether rich or poor.
20Even powerful rulers die
in the darkness of night
when they least expect it,
just like the rest of us.
God Watches Everything We Do
21God watches everything we do.
22No evil person can hide
in the deepest darkness.
23And so, God doesn't need
to set a time for judgment.
24Without asking for advice,
God removes mighty leaders
and puts others in their place.
25He knows what they are like,
and he wipes them out
in the middle of the night.
26And while others look on,
he punishes them
because they were evil
27and refused to obey him.
28The persons they mistreated
had prayed for help,
until God answered
their prayers.
29When God does nothing,
can any person or nation
find fault with him?
30But still, he punishes rulers
who abuse their people.
31Job, you should tell God
that you are guilty
and promise to do better.
32Then ask him to point out
what you did wrong,
so you won't do it again.
33Do you make the rules,
or does God?
You have to decide—
I can't do it for you;
now make up your mind.
34Job, anyone with good sense
can easily see
35that you are speaking nonsense
and lack good judgment.
36So I pray for you to suffer
as much as possible
for talking like a sinner.
37You have rebelled against God,
time after time,
and have even insulted us.
translation_text:
1Kɛkɛ ni Elihu kɛɛ akɛ,
2“Nyɛ nilelɔi kɛ jwɛŋlɔi,
nyɛboa miwiemɔ toi,
nyɛfea toi nyɛhãa mi,
3 ejaakɛ toi akɛŋmɛɔ wiemɔ akwɛɔ,
tamɔ bɔ ni akɛ lilɛi saa niyenii
anaa akwɛɔ lɛ.
4Nyɛhãa wɔkɔa nɔ ni ja,
nyɛhãa wɔsusua he yɛ wɔteŋ
wɔna nɔ ni hi.
5Ejaakɛ Hiob ekɛɛ akɛ, ‘Miyeɔ bem’
shi Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ mi yeee yɛ jalɛ naa;
6bem ni miyeɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ,
abu mi amalelɔ:
Mifala lɛ bɛ tsabaa,
tsɛbelɛ tɔ̃mɔ ko bɛ mihe.
7Namɔ ena mɔ ko tamɔ Hiob,
mɔ ni bɔɔ musu tamɔ anuɔ nu pɛŋ?
8Mɔ ni kɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ nishaianii
bɔɔ naanyo,
ni ekɛ gbɔmɛi fɔ̃ji nyiɛɔ?
9Ejaakɛ ekɛɛ akɛ, ‘Ehe bɛ sɛɛnamɔ
hã gbɔmɔ akɛ ekɛ Nyɔŋmɔ
aaabɔ naanyo!’
10No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛ mɛi ni nyɛyɔɔ jwɛŋmɔ lɛ,
nyɛboa mi toi.
Enɛ akagbale Nyɔŋmɔ fɔɔŋfɔ akɛ eeefee nɔ fɔŋ,
aloo Ofe lɛ, eeefee nɔ ko ni ejaaa hu.
11 Ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ woɔ gbɔmɔ nyɔmɔ
yɛ enitsumɔ naa,
ni ekɛ gbɔmɔ yeɔ yɛ ejeŋba naa.
12 Anɔkwa, Nyɔŋmɔ yeee
toikɔdɔmɔ sane;
ni Ofe lɛ tsɔ̃ɔɔ sane hiɛ ebuuu shi.
13Namɔ ji mɔ ni kɛ je lɛ
nɔkwɛmɔ hã lɛ?
Namɔ kɛ jeŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ
hã lɛ?
14Kɛji eeeŋɔ emumɔ lɛ yɛ je lɛŋ,
ni eeehã mumɔ lɛ akpale kwraa
kɛba eŋɔɔ lɛ,
15 no lɛ heloo fɛɛ heloo hiɛ aaakpãtã;
ni gbɔmɔ aaatsɔ̃ sũ ekoŋŋ.
16Kɛji oyɛ jwɛŋmɔ lɛ bo toi!
Bo nɔ ni makɛɛ lɛ toi!
17Ani mɔ ni taooo jalɛ saneyeli
baanyɛ mɛi anɔ eye?
Ani ooobu mɔ ni ja
ni eyɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɔ?
18Ani ooobu mɔ ni kɛɔ maŋtsɛ akɛ ‘Yakagbɔmɔ’
kɛ lumɛi hu akɛ, ‘Yitsoŋwalɔi?’
19Ni ekwɛɛɛ lumɛi ahiɛ
ni ebuuu niiatsɛ fe ohiafo,
ejaakɛ lɛ eninenaa nitsumɔnii
ji amɛ fɛɛ kwa lɛ bem?
20Trukaa gbɔmɔ gboɔ;
ahosoɔ gbɔmɔ nyɔɔŋ,
ni ehoɔ eyaa;
hewalɔi hoɔ amɛyaa,
ni amɛtsɔ̃ɔɔ adesa nine nɔ.
21 Ejaakɛ ohiŋmɛi jwere
gbɔmɔ adesa jeŋba nɔ,
ni onaa enyiɛmɔhei fɛɛ.
22 Duŋ kabitii bɛ he ko he ko
ni mɛi ni tsuɔ nishaianii
aaanyɛ atee amɛhe yɛ mli.
23Ejaakɛ etoko be pɔtɛɛ ko
ehãko adesa ko
ni eeeya kojomɔ yɛ lɛ ehiɛ.
24Ekpãtãa hewalɔi ahiɛ
ni etaooo amɛsaji amli,
ni eholeɔ mɛi krokomɛi
etoɔ amɛnajiaŋ.
25Akɛni ele amɛnifeemɔnii lɛ,
ebutuɔ amɛ nyɔɔŋ,
ni amɛhiɛ kpãtãa.
26Egbalaa mɛi fɔ̃ji atoi
yɛ mɛi fɛɛ ahiɛ.
27Ejaakɛ amɛkpale yɛ esɛɛ,
ni amɛbuuu egbɛi lɛ ekoeko;
28 ni no hewɔ lɛ, amɛhã
ohiafoi ayaafo yashɛ eŋɔɔ;
ni enu mɛi ni efĩ amɛ lɛ abolɔmɔ.
29Kɛji Nyɔŋmɔ fee diŋŋ lɛ,
namɔ baanyɛ lɛ ashwa?
Kɛji ekɛ ehiɛ tee lɛ
namɔ baanyɛ ehiɛ lɛ ena?
30Nɔ ko bɛ ni aaanyɛ afee
koni gbɔmɔ fɔŋ akaye maŋ nɔ,
ni ekahã maŋbii bote kaa mli.
31Ejaakɛ ani mɔ ko ekɛɛ Nyɔŋmɔ
dã akɛ ‘Agbala mitoi. Mifeŋ nɔ ni
ehiii dɔŋŋ;
32tsɔ̃ɔmɔ mi nibii ni minaaa;
koni kɛji mifee nɔ ni ehiii lɛ
mikafee nakai dɔŋŋ?’
33Akɛni okwa egbɛi lɛ,
ani Nyɔŋmɔ baafee nɔ ni
otaoɔ ehã bo lo?
Kɛɛmɔ nɔ ni ole lɛ,
ejaakɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ esa akɛ
okɔɔ nɔ ni osumɔɔ;
shi jeee mi matsɔ̃ɔ bo.
34Mɛi ni nuɔ nii ashishi lɛ
baakɛɛ mi;
ni nilelɔi ni nuɔ nɔ ni
miwieɔ lɛ baakɛɛ akɛ,
35‘Hiob wieɔ ni jwɛŋmɔ bɛ mli;
nilee bɛ ewiemɔ mli.’
36Mina ni kulɛ aka Hiob
akwɛ kɛyashi naagbee,
ejaakɛ hetoi ni ehãa lɛ
tamɔ mɛi fɔ̃ji anaa wiemɔ.
37Ejaakɛ eetse atua efata
esha ni efee lɛ he,
eetswa edɛ̃ eshwie wɔnɔ
ni eewie babaoo eeshi Nyɔŋmɔ.”

english_text:
Elihu Continues
Are You Really Innocent?
1Elihu said:
2Job, are you really innocent
in the sight of God?
3Don't you honestly believe
it pays to obey him?
4I will give the answers
to you and your friends.
* 5Look up to the heavens
6 and think!
Do your sins hurt God?
7Is any good you may have done
at all helpful to him?
8The evil or good you do
only affects other humans.
9In times of trouble,
everyone begs the mighty God
to have mercy.
10But after their Creator
helps them through hard times,
they forget about him,
11though he makes us wiser
than animals or birds.
12God won't listen to the prayers
of proud and evil people.
13If God All-Powerful refuses
to answer their empty prayers,
14he will surely deny
your impatient request
to face him in court.
15Job, you were wrong to say
God doesn't punish sin.
16Everything you have said
adds up to nonsense.
translation_text:
1Kɛkɛ ni Elihu saa kɛɛ ekoŋŋ akɛ,
2“Aso osusuɔ akɛ eja gbɛ
akɛ oookɛɛ akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ lɛ
tɔ̃mɔ ko bɛ ohe,
3hewɔ ni okɛɔ akɛ,
‘Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he?
Mɛɛ ejurɔ miyeɔ kɛji
mifee esha lɛ?’
4Mahã bo kɛ onanemɛi ni fata ohe lɛ fɛɛ hetoo.
5Kwɛmɔ ŋwɛi!
Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni atatui lɛ
yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔŋŋ yɛ oyiteŋ!
6Kɛji ofee esha lɛ,
mɛni ona ofee Nyɔŋmɔ?
Kɛji ofee esha lɛ shii abɔ po,
mɛɛ awui no yeɔ Nyɔŋmɔ?
7Kɛji jalɔ ji bo lɛ,
mɛni okɛwa Nyɔŋmɔ,
aloo mɛni enaa kɛjɛɔ odɛ̃ŋ?
8 Esha ni ofeɔ lɛ, adesa tamɔ bo
awui eyeɔ,
ni ojalɛ lɛ, gbɔmɔ eyeɔ ebuaa.
9Yiwaa babaoo hãa maŋbii
lɛ bolɔɔ;
amɛbolɔɔ amɛtsɛɔ yelikɛbuamɔ
yɛ ojei ayiwalɛ nifeemɔnii ahewɔ.
10 Shi mɔ ko kwraa ekɛɛɛ akɛ,
‘Nɛgbɛ Nyɔŋmɔ, miBɔlɔ lɛ yɔɔ,
mɔ ni hãa hiɛnɔkãmɔ
yɛ fĩmɔbe mli kɛ
11mɔ ni tsɔ̃ɔ wɔ nii
fe bɔ ni etsɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ
nɔ kooloi lɛ,
ni ehãa wɔleɔ nii fe ŋwɛi loofɔji lɛ?’
12Amɛbolɔɔ amɛtsɛɔ yelikɛbuamɔ
shi Nyɔŋmɔ efooo amɛdaaŋ
yɛ amɛnifɔɔjianii kɛ
amɛhenɔwomɔ hewɔ.
13 Anɔkwa, Nyɔŋmɔ booo yaka yaafo toi,
ni Ofe lɛ ebuuu hu.
14Nɔ ni wa fe fɛɛ ji akɛ,
oookɛɛ akɛ onaaa lɛ,
ni sane lɛ kã ehiɛ,
ni oomɛ lɛ.
15 Shi agbɛnɛ, akɛni Nyɔŋmɔ mlifu
gbalaaa mɔ toi, ni ediii
tɔ̃mɔ sɛɛ yrɛdɛɛ hewɔ lɛ,
16Hiob, oowie huu,
oowie babaoo ni nilee bɛ mli.”

english_text:
Elihu Continues
Be Patient a While Longer
1Elihu said:
2Be patient a while longer;
I have something else to say
in God's defense.
3God always does right—
and this knowledge
comes straight from God.
4You can rest assured
that what I say is true.
5Although God is mighty,
he cares about everyone
and makes fair decisions.
6The wicked are cut down,
and those who are wronged
receive justice.
7God watches over good people
and places them in positions
of power and honor forever.
8But when people are prisoners
of suffering and pain,
* 9God points out their sin
and their pride,
10then he warns them
to turn back to him.
11And if they obey,
they will be successful
and happy from then on.
12But if they foolishly refuse,
they will be rewarded
with a violent death.
Godless People Are Too Angry
13Godless people are too angry
to ask God for help
when he punishes them.
14So they die young
in shameful disgrace.
15Hard times and trouble
are God's way
of getting our attention!
16And at this very moment,
God deeply desires
to lead you from trouble
and to spread your table
with your favorite food.
17Now that the judgment
for your sins
has fallen upon you,
18don't let your anger
and the pain you endured
make you sneer at God.
19Your reputation and riches
cannot protect you
from distress,
20nor can you find safety
in the dark world below.
21Be on guard! Don't turn to evil
as a way of escape.
22God's power is unlimited.
He needs no teachers
23to guide or correct him.
Others Have Praised God
24Others have praised God
for what he has done,
so join with them.
25From down here on earth,
everyone has looked up and seen
26how great God is—
God is more than we imagine;
no one can count the years
he has lived.
* 27God gathers moisture
into the clouds
28and supplies us with rain.
29Who can understand
how God scatters the clouds
and speaks from his home
in the thunderstorm?
30And when God sends lightning,
it can be seen
at the bottom of the sea.
31By producing such rainstorms,
God rules the world
and provides us with food.
32Each flash of lightning
is one of his arrows
striking its target,
33and the thunder tells
of his anger against sin.
translation_text:
1Elihu tee ewiemɔ lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛɛ akɛ,
2“Na tsui ohã mi fioo,
ni matsɔ̃ɔ bo nɔ ko naa,
ejaakɛ miyɛ nɔ ko lolo
ni mibawie mahã Nyɔŋmɔ.
3Minilee babaoo lɛ mli majɛ
matsɔ̃ɔ akɛ miBɔlɔ lɛ
yeɔ jalɛ sane.
4Ejaakɛ anɔkwa wiemɔ miwieɔ lɛ.
Mɔ ko ni le nii jogbaŋŋ
damɔ ohiɛ nɛɛ.
5Naa, Nyɔŋmɔ je agbo,
ni enyaŋeee mɔ ko mɔ ko;
eniiashishinumɔ naa wa jogbaŋŋ.
6 Ehãaa mɔ fɔŋ yi ana wala,
shi ohiafoi kɛ mɛi ni naa amanehulu lɛ
eyeɔ amɛsane ehãa amɛ.
7Ehiŋmɛi kãa jalɔ he,
ni ehãa amɛtsɔ̃mɔɔ tamɔ
maŋtsɛmɛi ni tara sɛii anɔ
ni awoɔ amɛnɔ gojoo.
8Kɛji awo amɛ gboklɛi
ni amanehulu efĩmɔ amɛ lɛ,
9kɛkɛ lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ tsɔ̃ɔ amɛ
nɔ fɔŋ ni amɛfee, amɛtɔ̃mɔi
kɛ amɛhenɔwomɔ lɛ.
10 Egbeleɔ amɛtoiiaŋ, ni amɛnuɔ
kãmɔ ni ekãa amɛ akɛ
amɛkpa nishaianii feemɔ lɛ.
11Kɛji amɛbo Nyɔŋmɔ toi, ni amɛsɔ̃mɔ lɛ lɛ,
amɛaaye amɛwala be lɛ
yɛ ejurɔyeli mli,
kɛ amɛfii lɛ hu yɛ miishɛɛ mli.
12Shi kɛji amɛbooo toi lɛ,
no lɛ amɛleŋ nii, ni amɛaagboi
yɛ klante naa.
13Mɛi ni sheee Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei lɛ,
eŋmɛ̃ɛɛ mlifu he;
kɛji efĩ amɛ tete lɛ
amɛbiii Nyɔŋmɔ dɛŋ yelikɛbuamɔ.
14Amɛgboiɔ yɛ amɛblahiiaŋ,
ni amɛwala sɛɛ foɔ
kɛ hiɛgbele kɛ tɔlɛ.
15Nyɔŋmɔ tsɔseɔ gbɔmɔ kɛtsɔ̃ɔ
amanehulu nɔ,
ni ekɛ nɔnaa gbeleɔ mɔ hiŋmɛi.
16Nyɔŋmɔ jie bo kɛje jaramɔ mli
kɛba he ko ni ohe jɔ bo yɛ,
ni okplɔ̃ lɛ nɔ eyi tɔ kɛ niyenii.
17Shi agbɛnɛ aagbala otoi
bɔ ni sa bo pɛpɛɛpɛ;
aagbala otoi yɛ jalɛ naa.
18Kwɛmɔ ni ahi koni akɛ
nyɔɔŋnihamɔ akalaka bo;
ni kaahã ninamɔ miihã oodu gbɛ.
19Aso oyaafo baanyɛ bo ahere,
aloo ohewalɛ kɛ oshika
aaanyɛ nɔ ko afee?
20Kaashwe ni duŋ awo,
be ni maji ahiɛ aaakpãtã lɛ.
21Kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okabɔ̃i
eshafeemɔ:
ejaakɛ oosumɔ enɛ moŋ
fe nɔnaa.
22 Naa, Nyɔŋmɔ je agbo
yɛ ehewalɛ lɛ naa;
ni mɛɛ tsɔɔlɔ kɛ lɛ yeɔ hegbɔ?
23Namɔ baanyɛ etsɔ̃ɔ Nyɔŋmɔ
nɔ ni sa akɛ efee,
aloo namɔ aaanyɛ akɛɛ Nyɔŋmɔ
akɛ, ‘Ofee nɔ ko ni ejaaa’.
24Kaimɔ koni okafo enifeemɔ
ni adesai fɛɛ ewo he lala lɛ.
25Adesai fɛɛ miikwɛ enifeemɔ
kɛmiijɛ shɔŋŋ;
shi kɛ̃lɛ adesa nuuu shishi.
26Naa, Nyɔŋmɔ da, shi
wɔleee lɛ;
ni wɔnyɛŋ efii ni eye wɔkane.
27Ejaakɛ egbalaa nu kulibii
kɛyaa ŋwɛi,
ni ehãa afua tsɔ̃ɔ nu,
28ni ŋwɛi fɔseɔ shwieɔ shi,
ni ebashwieɔ adesai fɛɛ anɔ babaoo.
29 Ani mɔ ko aaanyɛ anu
bɔ ni atatui ha ŋwɛi lɛ shishi,
aloo eeenu ŋwɛi shiimɔ shishi?
30Naa, egbɛ ŋwɛi srawa mli kɛbɔle ehe;
shi ehã ŋshɔ shishi wo duŋ.
31Ejaakɛ gbɛ nɔ ni etsɔ̃ɔ
elɛɔ adesai nɛ,
ni ekumaa amɛ niyenii babaoo.
32Ekɛ enine mɔɔ ŋwɛi srawa mli
ni etsɔ̃ɔ lɛ he ni egba kɛyayi.
33Ŋwɛi srawa gbɛɛmɔ lɛ tsɔ̃ɔ
bɔ ni eji,
akɛ mɔ ko ni mli fũɔ yɛ
nishaianii hewɔ.”

english_text:
Elihu Continues
I Am Frightened
1I am frightened
and tremble all over,
2when I hear the roaring voice
of God in the thunder,
3and when I see his lightning
flash across the sky.
4God's majestic voice
thunders his commands,
5creating miracles too marvelous
for us to understand.
6Snow and heavy rainstorms
7make us stop and think
about God's power,
8and they force animals
to seek shelter.
9The windstorms of winter strike,
10and the breath of God
freezes streams and rivers.
11Rain clouds filled with lightning
appear at God's command,
12traveling across the sky
13to release their cargo—
sometimes as punishment for sin,
sometimes as kindness.
Consider Carefully
14Job, consider carefully
the many wonders of God.
15Can you explain why lightning
flashes at the orders
16of God who knows all things?
Or how he hangs the clouds
in empty space?
17You almost melt in the heat
of fierce desert winds
when the sky is like brass.
18God can hammer out the clouds
in spite of the oppressive heat,
but can you?
19Tell us what to say to God!
Our minds are in the dark,
and we don't know how
to argue our case.
20Should I risk my life
by telling God
that I want to speak?
21No one can stare at the sun
after a breeze has blown
the clouds from the sky.
22Yet the glorious splendor
of God All-Powerful
is brighter by far.
23God cannot be seen—
but his power is great,
and he is always fair.
24And so we humans fear God,
because he shows no respect
for those who are proud
and think they know so much.
translation_text:
1“Ŋwɛi shiimɔ lɛ hãa mitsui tswaa
ni tse po eheɔ etse yɛ mimli nɛɛ.
2 Nyɛboa Nyɔŋmɔ gbee ni ji ŋwɛi shiimɔ
lɛ toi,
kɛ shiimɔ ni jɛ edaaŋ lɛ.
3Eŋmɛɔ he ewoɔ ŋwɛi shishi fɛɛ,
ni ŋwɛi srawa gbalaa kɛyaa
shikpɔŋ lɛ koji ejwɛ lɛ fɛɛ.
4Ŋwɛi shiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ,
ewoɔ egbee kɛ agbojee;
ni etsiii srawa naa
be mli ni eshiɔ lɛ.
5Nyɔŋmɔ gbeeshiimɔ yɛ naakpɛɛ
ni efeɔ nibii wuji ni wɔjwɛŋmɔ
shɛɛɛ he.
6 Ekɛɔ snoo akɛ, ‘Nɛɛ oshwie
shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ;
ni ekɛɔ nu kɛ futufuli akɛ, nɛɛ waa!’
7Ejieɔ gbɔmɔ nine yɛ
nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni efeɔ lɛ he,
koni adesai fɛɛ ana ale
akɛ lɛ efeɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ.
8 Kɛkɛ lɛ ŋaŋ kooloi yaa amɛbuiaŋ,
ni amɛhɔlɔ amɛshihilɛhei lɛaŋ.
9Ahum jɛɔ wuoyigbɛ ebaa,
ni fɛ̃i hu jeɔ kooyigbɛ.
10Mumɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ muɔ lɛ
hãa nu fĩɔ kpɔ,
ni fai fɛɛ fĩɔ tɔo tsɔ̃ɔ aisi.
11Ehãa atatui yiɔ kɛ nu
ni ehãa srawa kpɛlɛɔ
yɛ atatui lɛaŋ.
12Amɛbɔleɔ shi yɛ egbɛjianɔtoo
naa;
amɛyeɔ efãmɔ nɔ
yɛ je lɛ mli fɛɛ.
13Bei komɛi lɛ, ehãa
enɛɛmɛi baa koni egbala
gbɔmɛi atoi,
bei komɛi lɛ yɛ eshikpɔŋ lɛ
yibaamɔ hewɔ,
ni bei komɛi hu koni
ekɛtsɔ̃ɔ suɔmɔ ni eyɔɔ.
14Oo, bo enɛ toi, Hiob,
da gãa koni ojwɛŋ
Nyɔŋmɔ naakpɛɛ nitsumɔi lɛ ahe.
15Ani ole bɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ feɔ
efãa amɛ ehãa,
ni ehãa la kpɛɔ kɛjɛɔ
atatu mli?
16Ani ole bɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ,
mɔ ni le nii kɛwula shi lɛ
feɔ etsuɔ enaakpɛɛ nitsumɔ
ni hãa atatu sɛŋɔ shi lɛ?
17Ele bo bɔ ni otadei
amli dɔɔ la,
be ni ehã shikpɔŋ lɛ
efee shiŋŋ yɛ wuoyigbɛ kɔɔyɔɔ
lɛ hewɔ lɛ?
18Ani obaanyɛ olɛɛ ŋwɛi,
ni tamɔ dade kaŋkaŋ ni ashwie nɛɛ,
mli oha shi tamɔ Nyɔŋmɔ efee lɛ?
19Tsɔ̃ɔmɔ wɔ nɔ ni wɔkɛɛ Nyɔŋmɔ;
ejaakɛ wɔjwɛŋmɔ naa etã,
wɔbɛ nɔ ko ni wɔbaakɛɛ.
20Akakɛɛ lɛ akɛ masumɔ mawie;
mɔ ko bɛ ni baasumɔ
akɛ ekpãtã ehiɛ.
21Ni agbɛnɛ adesa nyɛɛɛ
la lɛ ekwɛ kɛ jeŋ tse tete,
ejaakɛ atatui eha hiɛ;
shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ
eloɔ atatui lɛ kɛyaa.
22La tsuru fɔɔ kpɛɔ
kɛjɛɔ kooyigbɛ kɛbaa.
Ni Nyɔŋmɔ he anunyam lɛ
hãa wɔsheɔ gbeyei.
23 Ofe lɛ, wɔnyɛŋ lɛ wɔna;
ehewalɛ da, ni eyeɔ jalɛ sane;
ekpaŋ jalɛ saneyeli.
24No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛ adesai fɛɛ,
nyɛshea lɛ gbeyei,
ejaakɛ mɛi ni buɔ amɛhe
nilelɔi lɛ, ebuuu amɛ.”

english_text:
The Lord Speaks
From Out of a Storm
1From out of a storm,
the Lord said to Job:
2Why do you talk so much
when you know so little?
3Now get ready to face me!
Can you answer
the questions I ask?
4How did I lay the foundation
for the earth?
Were you there?
5Doubtless you know who decided
its length and width.
6What supports the foundation?
Who placed the cornerstone,
7 while morning stars sang,
and angels rejoiced?
8 When the ocean was born,
I set its boundaries
9and wrapped it in blankets
of thickest fog.
10Then I built a wall around it,
locked the gates, 11and said,
“Your powerful waves stop here!
They can go no farther.”
Did You Ever Tell the Sun To Rise?
12Did you ever tell the sun to rise?
And did it obey?
13Did it take hold of the earth
and shake out the wicked
like dust from a rug?
14Early dawn outlines the hills
like stitches on clothing
or sketches on clay.
15But its light is too much
for those who are evil,
and their power is broken.
16Job, have you ever walked
on the ocean floor?
17Have you seen the gate
to the world of the dead?
18And how large is the earth?
Tell me, if you know!
19Where is the home of light,
and where does darkness live?
20Can you lead them home?
21I'm certain you must be able to,
since you were already born
when I created everything.
22Have you been to the places
where I keep snow and hail,
23until I use them to punish
and conquer nations?
24From where does lightning leap,
or the east wind blow?
25Who carves out a path
for thunderstorms?
Who sends torrents of rain
26on empty deserts
where no one lives?
27Rain that changes barren land
to meadows green with grass.
28Who is the father of the dew
and of the rain?
29Who gives birth to the sleet
and the frost
30that fall in winter,
when streams and lakes
freeze solid as a rock?
Can You Arrange Stars?
31 Can you arrange stars in groups
such as Orion
and the Pleiades?
32Do you control the stars
or set in place the Big Dipper
and the Little Dipper?
33Do you know the laws
that govern the heavens,
and can you make them rule
the earth?
34Can you order the clouds
to send a downpour,
35or will lightning flash
at your command?
36Did you teach birds to know
that rain or floods
are on their way?
37Can you count the clouds
or pour out their water
38on the dry, lumpy soil?
39When lions are hungry,
do you help them hunt?
40Do you send an animal
into their den?
41And when starving young ravens
cry out to me for food,
do you satisfy their hunger?
translation_text:
1 Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa jɛ ahum lɛ mli ehã Hiob hetoo ekɛɛ,
2 “Namɔ hu ji mɔ ni kɛ wiemɔi
ni nilee bɛ mli ehã
mijwɛŋmɔ hiɛ ehua nɛɛ?
3 Feemɔ kralo odamɔ shi
tamɔ nuu,
shi mibabi bo sane ni ohã
hetoo.
4Be ni mito je lɛ shishi lɛ,
nɛgbɛ oyɔɔ?
Kɛji ole he nɔ ko lɛ,
kɛɛmɔ mi!
5 Namɔ ji mɔ ni tsɔ̃ɔ
bɔ ni eda ehã;
aloo namɔ ji mɔ ni
mɔ kpãa mli kɛsusu edalɛ lɛ?
Bɛ ole?
6Mɛni nɔ ato je lɛ shishi ama?
Namɔ ji mɔ ni to ekoŋtɛ lɛ?
7Be ni leebi ŋulamii lɛ fɛɛ la kutuu
ni ŋwɛibii lɛ bɔ oshe
kɛ nyamɔ lɛ?
8 Aloo namɔ ŋamɔ agboi lɛ
ekɛtsi ŋshɔ lɛ naa,
be ni etue kɛjɛ je lɛ
shishitoo he lɛ.
9Be ni mihã atatui tsɔ̃ ŋshɔ hebo,
ni mihã duŋ kpii hu tsɔ̃
mama ni mikɛbala lɛ lɛ?
10 Be ni mito je lɛ husui
ni mikɛ agboi kɛ amɛsɛɛ adabaŋi
tsi enaa,
11ni mikɛɛ akɛ, ‘Biɛ nɛɛ obaawa,
ni okafo mli;
ni biɛ oshɔkei wuji lɛ baawa.’
12Hiob, ni oba jeŋ nɛɛ, ofã
ni je etsɛre dã?
Ni otsɔ̃ɔ jetsɛremɔ egbɛhe pɛŋ?
13Ani ofã jetsɛremɔ ni emɔmɔ
shikpɔŋ lɛ naagbee hei lɛ amli
koni ehwanya mɛi fɔ̃ji fɛɛ
kɛjɛ nɔ eshwie dã lo?
14Jetsɛremɔ hãa gɔji kɛ jɔi jeɔ
shi faŋŋ
tamɔ atade ni akumɔ mli
loo tamɔ naasɔomɔnɔ ni ta magbɛ hiɛ.
15Ehãa mɛi fɔɔji enãaa hei
ni amɛaatsɔ̃,
ni amɛniji ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nifɔɔjianii lɛ
kumɔɔ yɛ amɛhe.
16Aso oshɛ he ni ŋshɔ
jɛɔ lɛ pɛŋ;
ni oshara shi kɛnyiɛ ŋshɔ shishi dã?
17Ani ajie gbohiiaje agboi lɛ akpo
atsɔ̃ɔ bo,
aloo ajie duŋ kpii lɛ naa agboi
lɛ akpo atsɔ̃ɔ bo?
18Ani ole je lɛ dalɛ?
Kɛji ole nibii nɛɛ fɛɛ lɛ, wiemɔ!
19Nɛgbɛ atsɔ̃ɔ kɛyaa he ni la jɛɔ,
loo nɛgbɛ ji duŋ shihilɛhe,
20koni otsɔ̃ɔ gbɛ ni kã shi
kɛyaa eshihilɛhe lɛ mli,
koni oŋɔ lɛ oyato ehusu nɔ?
21Bɛ ole, ejaakɛ ofii fa babaoo
ni no mli lɛ afɔ bo!
22Obote tsui ni mito snoo yɛ mli,
lɛ mli pɛŋ
loo ona tsui ni mito nyɔŋmɔŋtɛi yɛ mli,
23 ni ji nii ni mito mihã
amanehulu be
loo nɔmɔ kɛ ta be lɛ?
24Nɛgbɛ gbɛ ni yaa he ni hulu
la lɛ jɛɔ egbɛɔ eshwãa,
loo he ni bokãgbɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ
jɛɔ eshwãa je lɛ mli lɛ kã?
25 Namɔ egba nujɔɔ efɔ̃ shi
koni nu ni miinɛ anyiɛ mli,
ni eje gbɛ ehã srawa,
26bɔ ni afee ni nu anɛ
ashwie shikpɔŋ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko
bɛ nɔ, kɛ shiaŋa he ni
adesa ko bɛ hu nɔ?
27Namɔ hãa shikpɔŋ olɛŋlɛ
ni kã shi efolo naa ofɔ̃,
ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ?
28Ani nu ni nɛɔ yɛ tsɛ,
loo namɔ ni fɔ bɔ́?
29 Namɔ musuŋ aisi jɛ,
ni namɔ fɔ ŋwɛi bɔ́
ni efimɔ kpɔbii.
30Nu fiɔ, ni ewaa tamɔ tɛ,
ni ŋshɔ hiɛ fɛɛ waa keketee.
31 “Ani obaanyɛ okɛ kɔsɔŋkɔsɔ
afimɔ Wuɔ kɛ ebii?
Aloo obaanyɛ kpãi ni fimɔ
Oŋwɛ ofɛne?
32Ani obaanyɛ otsɔ̃ɔ ŋulamii
ni kpɛlɛɔ lɛ he ni amɛtsɔ̃
kɛya kɛji amɛje,
aloo obaanyɛ otsɔ̃ɔ Jeŋ Kpawo
kɛ ebii lɛ gbɛ?
33Ani ole akpɔi ni hiɛ ŋwɛi,
aloo obaanyɛ ohã nakai
akpɔi lɛ aye shikpɔŋ lɛ
hu nɔ?
34Ani obaanyɛ owo ogbee nɔ
ni ofã atatui lɛ
koni amɛnɛ nu amɛshwie
onɔ?
35Ani obaanyɛ ofã srawai
akɛ amɛgbala,
ni ani amɛaaba oŋɔɔ
amɛbakɛɛ bo akɛ, ‘Naa wɔ?’
36Namɔ tsɔ̃ɔ loofɔlɔ ibis
be ni Nilo baasraŋ nɔ?
Aloo namɔ tsɔ̃ɔ wuɔ nuu
akɛ nu baanɛ?
37 Namɔ yɔɔ nilee ni ekɛbaanyɛ
atatui lɛ ekane?
Aloo ebaanyɛ ekpoo amɛnaa shi
koni amɛnɛ nu
38ni baahã su akpɔtɔ
ni efimɔ kukulibii efee tɔo?
39Ani bo omiɔ milɛloo ohãa jata,
aloo ohãa jatabii loo amɛyeɔ
shɛɔ amɛnaa
40be ni amɛbumɔ amɛbui amli,
aloo amɛhɔlɔ odɔtɔi amli
amɛwo ka lɛ?
41 Namɔ hã kwãakwãalabite niyenii,
be ni ebii bibii bolɔɔ amɛtsɛɔ
Nyɔŋmɔ,
ni amɛtsomloɔ ejaakɛ niyenii
bɛ lɛ?

english_text:
The Lord Continues
When Do Mountain Goats Give Birth?
1When do mountain goats
and deer give birth?
Have you been there
when their young are born?
* 2How long are they pregnant
3before they deliver?
4Soon their young grow strong
and then leave
to be on their own.
5Who set wild donkeys free?
6I alone help them survive
in salty desert sand.
7They stay far from crowded cities
and refuse to be tamed.
8Instead, they roam the hills,
searching for pastureland.
9Would a wild ox agree
to live in your barn
and labor for you?
10Could you force him to plow
or to drag a heavy log
to smooth out the soil?
11Can you depend on him
to use his great strength
and do your heavy work?
12Can you trust him
to harvest your grain
or take it to your barn
from the threshing place?
An Ostrich Proudly Flaps Her Wings
13An ostrich proudly
flaps her wings,
but not because
she loves her young.
14She abandons her eggs
and lets the dusty ground
keep them warm.
15And she doesn't seem to worry
that the feet of an animal
could crush them all.
16She treats her eggs as though
they were not her own,
unconcerned that her work
might be for nothing.
17I myself made her foolish
and without common sense.
18But once she starts running,
she laughs at a rider
on the fastest horse.
Did You Give Horses Their Strength?
19Did you give horses their strength
and the flowing hair
along their necks?
20Did you make them able
to jump like grasshoppers
or to frighten people
with their snorting?
21Before horses are ridden
into battle,
they paw at the ground,
proud of their strength.
22Laughing at fear, they rush
toward the fighting,
23while the weapons of their riders
rattle and flash in the sun.
24Unable to stand still,
they gallop eagerly into battle
when trumpets blast.
25Stirred by the distant smells
and sounds of war, they snort
in reply to the trumpet.
26Did you teach hawks to fly south
for the winter?
* 27Did you train eagles to build
28their nests on rocky cliffs,
29where they can look down
to spot their next meal?
30 Then their young gather to feast
wherever the victim lies.
translation_text:
1“Ani ole be mli ni afɔɔ gɔji anɔ
abotiai lo?
Ona ofrote ni eefɔ dã?
2Ole nyɔji abɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ musu?
Ole amɛfɔmɔ be lo?
3Ani ole be mli ni amɛsɔ̃ɔ shi
amɛfɔɔ amɛbii lo?
4Amɛbii lɛ naa hewalɛ,
ni amɛdaraa yɛ jwɛiiaŋ;
amɛjeɔ kpo, ni
amɛkuuu amɛsɛɛ amɛbaaa dɔŋŋ.
5Namɔ ŋmɛ̃ɛ ŋaŋ teji he
koni eye ehe?
Namɔ fɛne kpãa lɛ ehã teji?
6Ni miŋɔ ŋa kplanaa lɛ mihã lɛ
akɛ eshĩa,
ni miŋɔ mukpo shikpɔŋ lɛ mihã lɛ
akɛ eshihilɛhe lɛ.
7Esumɔɔɔ hoo ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ,
ni enuuu mɔ ko ni miikpala lɛ gbee.
8Gɔji lɛ anɔ tsɔ̃ɔ eniyelihe,
ni etaoɔ nii ni yɔɔ frɔ̃frɔ̃
yɛ jɛi eyeɔ.
9Ani koo mli tsina aaakpɛ̃lɛ
ni esɔ̃mɔ bo?
Aloo eeesumɔ ni ebawɔ
kooloi awɔɔhe?
10Ani obaanyɛ owo tsinanuu kpãa
ni etsa akofii,
aloo eninɛ ŋmɔ
yɛ jɔi amli kɛnyiɛ osɛɛ?
11Ani okɛ ohe aaafɔ̃ enɔ
yɛ ehewalɛ kpele lɛ hewɔ,
aloo oooshi nitsumɔ muu
lɛ fɛɛ oŋmɛ enɔ?
12Ani oheɔ lɛ oyeɔ akɛ
ekɛ onikpamɔnii lɛ baaku
esɛɛ; naa,
ni ebua obele lɛ naa ewo aboŋo mli?
13Duguma tswaa efijiaŋ kɛ ntɛŋ;
shi hewalɛ kome nɛkɛ bɛ mli
ni ekɛaa sumɔ bo.
14Ejaakɛ eshiɔ ewɔji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ
koni shikpɔŋ mlu mli dɔlɛ lɛ ahã
amɛhe adɔ la.
15Ni ehiɛ kpaa nɔ akɛ
mɔ ko kɛ enane aaanyɛ ajwara
amɛ;
ni ŋaŋ kooloi aaanyɛ
amɛnaanaa nɔ.
16Ewaa ebii bibii lɛ ayi,
tamɔ nɔ ni jeee ebii ni;
etɔlɛ lɛ aaanyɛ afee yaka
kɛ̃lɛ esheee no gbeyei.
17Ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ehã nilee ebɔ lɛ,
ni jwɛŋmɔ hu ehãaa lɛ eko.
18Kɛji ewo ehe nɔ, ni ebaabɔ̃i foijee lɛ,
eŋmɔɔ okpɔŋɔ kɛ mɔ ni ta nɔ lɛ fɛɛ.
19“Hiob, bo ji mɔ ni hã okpɔŋɔ
hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ?
Ekuɛ he tsɔi funyaŋŋ lɛ bo ohã lɛ?
20Ani bo ohãa okpɔŋɔ huluɔ
tamɔ baalabi tuɔ lɛ?
Etsinemɔ gbɛɛmɔ yɛ gbeyei!
21Ekɛ enane gbɛɔ shi yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli,
eshwaa efɔɔ ehewalɛ nɔ;
ejeɔ kpo ekɛ tabilɔi yakpeɔ.
22Eleee nɔ ni ji gbeyei,
no haaa ekpokpo tete;
ejooo foi yɛ klante naa.
23Gãimlibii gbɛɔ woɔ lɛ,
akplɔ kɛ damfojai kpɛlɛɔ woɔ lɛ.
24Ekɛ hiɛdɔɔ kɛ grimɔ kpitiɔ shi;
enyɛɛɛ shi edamɔ kɛji tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ gbɛɛ.
25Kɛji tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ gbɛɛ lɛ,
ekɛɔ akɛ, ‘Yiɛ, eshɛ!’
Enyiɛ shɔŋŋ ni enuɔ ta he fu,
kɛ asafoiatsɛmɛi lɛ afaamɔi kɛ blɔmɔ he.
26Ani bo onilee naa
ni laalɔɔ filikiɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi,
ni egbɛɔ efijiaŋ etsɔ̃ɔ wuoyigbɛ?
27Ani bo ofamɔ naa
ni okropɔŋ woɔ ehe nɔ
ni eyafeɔ etsu yɛ ŋwɛi shɔŋŋ lɛ?
28Tɛsaa ni kwɔ fe fɛɛ nɔ
he ni yɔɔ shɔ̃shɔ̃ɔshɔ̃ lɛ,
efeɔ eshihilɛhe yɛ.
29Jɛi ejɛɔ ni enaa kooloo ni eeemɔ;
ehiŋmɛi naa shɔŋŋ nii.
30 He ni gbohii jwere lɛ,
jɛi okropɔŋ yɔɔ;
ni ebii bibii lɛ nuɔ gbohii lɛ alá.”

english_text:
The Lord Continues
I Am the Lord All-Powerful
* 1I am the Lord All-Powerful,
2but you have argued
that I am wrong.
Now you must answer me.
3Job said to the Lord:
4Who am I to answer you?
5I did speak once or twice,
but never again.
6Then out of the storm
the Lord said to Job:
7Face me and answer
the questions I ask!
8Are you trying to prove
that you are innocent
by accusing me of injustice?
9Do you have a powerful arm
and a thundering voice
that compare with mine?
10If so, then surround yourself
with glory and majesty.
* 11Show your furious anger!
Throw down and crush
12all who are proud and evil.
13Wrap them in grave clothes
and bury them together
in the dusty soil.
14Do this, and I will agree
that you have won
this argument.
I Created You
15I created both you
and the hippopotamus.
It eats only grass like an ox,
16but look at the mighty muscles
in its body 17and legs.
Its tail is like a cedar tree,
and its thighs are thick.
18The bones in its legs
are like bronze or iron.
19I made it more powerful
than any other creature,
yet I am stronger still.
20Undisturbed, it eats grass
while the other animals
play nearby.
* 21It rests in the shade of trees
along the riverbank
22or hides among reeds
in the swamp.
23It remains calm and unafraid
with the Jordan River rushing
and splashing in its face.
24There is no way to capture
a hippopotamus—
not even by hooking its nose
or blinding its eyes.
translation_text:
1Kɛkɛ ni Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ Hiob akɛ,
2 “Aso mɔ ni miitao mɔ he tɔ̃mɔ ekɛɛ lɛ,
ebaanyɛ ekɛ Ofe lɛ ataa naa?
Mɔ ni kɛ Nyɔŋmɔ miitaa naa lɛ,
hã ehã hetoo.”
3Kɛkɛ ni Hiob here Yehowa nɔ ni ekɛɛ,
4“Naa, mijeee mɔ ko;
mɛɛ hetoo mahã?
Mikɛ minine eto minaabu.
5Miwie shi kome, ni mitoŋ nɔ dɔŋŋ.
Miwie shii enyɔ; ni miyaŋ nɔ dɔŋŋ.”
6Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa jɛ ahum lɛ mli
ekɛ Hiob wie ekoŋŋ,
7 “Miamɔ tamɔ nuu;
mibabi bo sane
koni ojie mi naa.
8Aso ooka ni otsɔ̃ɔ akɛ mitɔ̃?
Oobu mi fɔ koni oye bem?
9 Aso ohewalɛ shɛɔ Nyɔŋmɔ nɔ lɛ,
ni obaanyɛ ohã ogbee ashi
tamɔ Nyɔŋmɔ nɔ lɛ lo?
10Kɛji nakai lɛ,
no lɛ wulamɔ ohe
koni ogbojee akwɔ ni onunyam
ada kpele.
11Grimɔ kɛ mlifu ni okɛnina
hewolɔ fɛɛ hewolɔ koni
oba lɛ shi;
12hɛɛ hewolɔ fɛɛ hewolɔ lɛ oba
lɛ shi,
ni otsirɛ yiwalɔi otswia shi
yɛ hei ni amɛdamɔ.
13Tsiimɔ amɛ fɛɛ amɛnɔ owo shikpɔŋ,
ni ofimɔ amɛhiɛiaŋ yɛ gbohiiaje,
14kɛkɛ lɛ mi hu makplɛ̃ nɔ
mahã bo akɛ oyɛ hewalɛ
ni baanyɛ ehã oye kunim.
15Kwɛmɔ nuŋshwuɔ;
mi mibɔ lɛ tamɔ mibɔ bo.
Ekpeɔ jwɛi tamɔ tsina,
16shi kwɛmɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ehɛ mli,
kɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ehewojiaŋ fãi lɛ mli.
17Ehãa elei shɔ̃ɔ keketee tamɔ tsenedru,
ni atswɛ̃tswɛ̃ fãi ni yɔɔ eshuɔji amli lɛ.
18Ewui wa tamɔ akɔɔble,
ni eniji kɛ enaji
tamɔ dade adabãŋ.
19Lɛ ji Yehowa ninenaa nitsumɔi
lɛ ateŋ titri ko;
mɔ ni bɔ lɛ lɛ pɛ nyɛɔ enɔ eyeɔ,
20Ejaakɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ hãa lɛ hɔ̃ɔŋ
yɛ he ni ŋaŋ kooloi fɛɛ yashwɛɔ
yɛ lɛ.
21Ehoɔ ekãa shi yɛ ŋmei tsei ashishi,
ni eteɔ ehe yɛ glãi amli yɛ
ŋmiamɔ mli,
22ejaakɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ hãa lɛ hɔ̃ɔŋ
ni faa lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ bɔleɔ ehe kɛkpeɔ.
23Naa, kɛji faa lɛ fee hamahama tete
ewooo ehe gbeyei;
kɛji Yordan yi kɛbata esɛ̃ tete po
eyoyrooo.
24Ani mɔ ko aaanyɛ eje ehiɛgbɛ
ni emɔ lɛ,
aloo ekɛ tsɔne adu egugɔ?”

english_text:
The Lord Continues
Can You Catch a Sea Monster?
1 Can you catch a sea monster
by using a fishhook?
Can you tie its mouth shut
with a rope?
2Can it be led around
by a ring in its nose
or a hook in its jaw?
3Will it beg for mercy?
4Will it surrender
as a slave for life?
5Can it be tied by the leg
like a pet bird
for little girls?
6Is it ever chopped up
and its pieces bargained for
in the fish-market?
7Can it be killed
with harpoons or spears?
8Wrestle it just once—
that will be the end.
9Merely a glimpse of this monster
makes all courage melt.
10And if it is too fierce
for anyone to attack,
who would dare oppose me?
11I am in command of the world
and in debt to no one.
12What powerful legs,
what a stout body
this monster possesses!
13Who could strip off its armor
or bring it under control
with a harness?
14Who would try to open its jaws,
full of fearsome teeth?
* 15Its back is covered
with shield after shield,
16firmly bound and closer together
17than breath to breath.
When This Monster Sneezes
18When this monster sneezes,
lightning flashes, and its eyes
glow like the dawn.
19Sparks and fiery flames
explode from its mouth.
20And smoke spews from its nose
like steam
from a boiling pot,
21while its blazing breath
scorches everything in sight.
22Its neck is so tremendous
that everyone trembles,
23the weakest parts of its body
are harder than iron,
24and its heart is stone.
25When this noisy monster appears,
even the most powerful
turn and run in fear.
26No sword or spear can harm it,
27and weapons of bronze or iron
are as useless as straw
or rotten wood.
28Rocks thrown from a sling
cause it no more harm
than husks of grain.
This monster fears no arrows,
29it simply smiles at spears,
and striking it with a stick
is like slapping it with straw.
30As it crawls through the mud,
its sharp and spiny hide
tears the ground apart.
31And when it swims down deep,
the sea starts churning
like boiling oil,
32and it leaves behind a trail
of shining white foam.
33No other creature on earth
is so fearless.
34It is king of all proud creatures,
and it looks upon the others
as nothing.
translation_text:
1 “Obaanyɛ okɛ kpoŋ asha leviatan
aloo okɛ kpãa afi elilɛi
akpɛtɛ edaaŋ?
2Ani ooonyɛ owo egugɔŋ taŋkpee
aloo okɛ kpoŋ ala ekadaa?
3Ani eekpa bo fai babaoo?
Aloo ekɛ bo aaawie naajɔlɛ wiemɔi?
4Ani ekɛ bo aaakpãŋ akɛ
oŋɔ lɛ ofee otsulɔ kɛya naanɔ lo?
5Ani okɛ lɛ baashwɛ
tamɔ akɛ loofɔlɔ shwɛɔ,
aloo obaafi lɛ ohã oblayei lo?
6Ani wolɛi baaba amɛbaye enaa?
Ani amɛfolɔ emli amɛhã jarayelɔi lo?
7Ani ooonyɛ otsulɔ akplɔi
owo ehewojiaŋ obɔ̃,
aloo oootsulɔ eyitso kɛ wuoyaa akplɔ?
8Kɛ onine ata ehe okwɛ,
ni ofeŋ nakai ekoŋŋ;
ohiɛ kpaŋ nɔmɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ nɔ.
9Naa, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni baana leviatan lɛ
enijiaŋ jeɔ wui, ni egbeɔ shi.
10Kãkãlɔ ko kãkãlɔ ko bɛ
ni aaanyɛ awo ehiɛ la.
Belɛ namɔ ji mɔ ni aaanyɛ
mi mihiɛ adamɔ mɔ?
11Namɔ kwraa etsɔ̃ hiɛ
efee nɔ ko ehã mi,
koni mato lɛ najiaŋ?
Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ jeŋ lɛ, minɔ ni.
12Mibawie eniji kɛ enaji
kɛ ehewalɛ kpele kɛ egbɔmɔtso he daa.
13Mɔ ko bɛ ni baanyɛ ehewolo
lɛ ekpɔ;
aloo eta enyanyɔji nta lɛ ahe.
14Namɔ baanyɛ agbele edaa
kɛyanina enyanyɔji ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ.
15Ehe totoi ni ato amɛ klɛmpɛiklɛmpɛi
tsara nɔ ha ekoto sɛɛ,
ni atsara amɛ tamɔ
nɔ ni asɔo amɛnaa.
16Eko tsa eko nɔ tsikitsiki,
bɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ tete nyɛɛɛ
amɛteŋ etsɔ̃.
17Akɛ eko etsa eko nɔ,
amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe bɔ ni
ehiii amɛteŋ tsemɔ.
18Kɛji etsine lɛ ekpɛlɛɔ la,
ni ehiŋmɛiiaŋ tamɔ leebi hulu haai.
19La fãa kɛjɛɔ edaaŋ tamɔ haai;
la srɛmii fɛlɛɔ kɛjɛɔ edaaŋ.
20Egugɔŋ fãa lasu
tamɔ lamɔ fãa kɛjɛɔ kukwɛi
ni ma la nɔ mli,
loo tamɔ jwɛi ni miishã lasu.
21Egugɔŋ mumɔ tsɛ̃ɔ ŋai,
ni edaaŋ fãa la.
22Ekuɛ mli ehewalɛ yɔɔ,
hewɔ lɛ eyɛ gbeyei kɛji
oyaje ehiɛgbɛ.
23Eheloo lɛ kpɛtɛ ehe kpɛŋŋ
bɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akpɔ.
24Etsui wa tamɔ tɛ,
ewa tamɔ wiɛ.
25Kɛji ewo ehe nɔ lɛ,
kãkãlɔi sheɔ gbeyei;
ŋmiŋmi mɔmɔɔ amɛ
kɛji ekãnya ehe.
26Kɛji abã lɛ klante lɛ, efooo;
ni akplɔ loo gãi
loo loogbee akplɔ
nyɛɛɛ lɛ afo.
27Dade tamɔ jwɛi ni egbi,
ni akɔɔble tamɔ tso
ni ekpɔtɔ hã lɛ.
28Gãimlibi wooo lɛ foi;
ni aklomia mli tɛ
tsɔ̃ɔ gbetseli hãa lɛ.
29Tsokpoti tamɔ gbetseli,
ni efeɔ lɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛji
atsɛ̃rɛ lɛ akplɔ.
30Emlishi totoi lɛ tamɔ
gbɛ ko naabu sakasaka lɛ,
ni ehoɔ ekãa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli
tamɔ ŋmãagbeemɔ tso.
31Ehãa ŋshɔ lɛ tswaa
tamɔ nula;
ni afui ni etswaa lɛ
tamɔ mu ni ma la nɔ.
32Esɛɛ mo kpɛɔ
ni ehãa ŋshɔ lɛ tswaa afui
tamɔ waŋ.
33Esaso kooloo ni sheee nɔ ko nɔ ko
gbeyei bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.
34Ebuuu nɔ ko nɔ ko ni he wa,
lɛ ji kooloi hewalɔi fɛɛ atsɛ.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to the Lord
No One Can Oppose You
1Job said:
2No one can oppose you,
because you have the power
to do what you want.
3 You asked why I talk so much
when I know so little.
I have talked about things
that are far beyond
my understanding.
4 You told me to listen
and answer your questions.
5I heard about you from others;
now I have seen you
with my own eyes.
6That's why I hate myself
and sit here in dust and ashes
to show my sorrow.
The Lord Corrects Job's Friends
7The Lord said to Eliphaz:
What my servant Job has said about me is true, but I am angry with you and your two friends for not telling the truth. 8So I want you to go over to Job and offer seven bulls and seven goats on an altar as a sacrifice to please me. After this, Job will pray, and I will agree not to punish you for your foolishness.
9Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar obeyed the Lord, and he answered Job's prayer.
A Happy Ending
10 After Job had prayed for his three friends, the Lord made Job twice as rich as he had been before. 11Then Job gave a feast for his brothers and sisters and for his old friends. They expressed their sorrow for the suffering the Lord had brought on him, and they each gave Job some silver and a gold ring.
12The Lord now blessed Job more than ever; he gave him 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 pair of oxen, and 1,000 donkeys.
13In addition to seven sons, Job had three daughters, 14whose names were Jemimah, Keziah, and Keren Happuch. 15They were the most beautiful women in that part of the world, and Job gave them shares of his property, along with their brothers.
16Job lived for another 140 years—long enough to see his great-grandchildren have children of their own— 17and when he finally died, he was very old.
translation_text:
1Kɛkɛ ni Hiob here Yehowa nɔ ekɛɛ,
2“Yehowa, mile akɛ
onyɛɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ofeɔ,
ni oyiŋtoo ko bɛ ni aaanyɛ
naa aku.
3 Namɔ hu ji mɔ ni kɛ wiemɔi
ni nilee bɛ mli teɔ nilee
nɔ?
No hewɔ lɛ, miwie nibii
ni minuuu shishi,
nibii ni ahe yɔɔ naakpɛɛ tsɔ̃
hã mi bɔ ni minuuu amɛshishi.
4 Okɛɛ mi akɛ, ‘Bo toi;
ni mawie.
Mibabi bo sane koni ohã
mi hetoo!’
5Mitoi kɛkɛ mikɛnu ohe,
shi agbɛnɛ mihiŋmɛi ena bo.
6No hewɔ lɛ, eedɔ mi,
ni miishwa mihe
yɛ sũ kɛ lamlu mli.”
Sane lɛ fɛɛ naagbee
7Be ni Yehowa kɛ Hiob ewie nɛkɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Yehowa kɛɛ Elifaz, Temannyo lɛ, akɛ, “Mimli ewo bo kɛ onanemɛi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ala, ejaakɛ nyɛwieee mihe bɔ ni ja tamɔ mitsulɔ Hiob fee lɛ. 8No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ nyɛmɔmɔa tsinahii kpawo kɛ ojwɛnii hu kpawo kɛyaa mitsulɔ Hiob ŋɔɔ koni nyɛkɛyashãa shãa afɔle nyɛhãa nyɛhe. Mitsulɔ Hiob baakpa fai ehã nyɛ ni mibabo efaikpamɔ lɛ toi, ni mikɛ nyɛ yeŋ yɛ nyɛkooloofeemɔ lɛ naa, ejaakɛ nyɛwieee mihe bɔ ni ja tamɔ Hiob fee lɛ.”
9 No hewɔ lɛ, Elifaz, Temannyo lɛ, kɛ Bildad, Shuhinyo lɛ, kɛ Zofar, Naamanyo lɛ, yiŋ amɛtee ni amɛyafee bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɛ amɛ lɛ; ni Yehowa mɔ Hiob faikpamɔ lɛ mli.
10 Be ni Hiob ekpa fai ehã enanemɛi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Yehowa hã Hiob saa eshwere ekoŋŋ. Yehowa ku nii fɛɛ ni Hiob yɔɔ sa lɛ ebɔ he toi enyɔ ehã lɛ. 11Kɛkɛ ni Hiob nyɛmimɛi hii lɛ kɛ enyɛmimɛi yei lɛ fɛɛ kɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni le lɛ sa lɛ ba eŋɔɔ; ni amɛ kɛ lɛ ye nii, ni amɛye lɛ ŋkɔmɔ, ni amɛshɛje emii yɛ sane fɔŋ ni Yehowa hã ye lɛ lɛ hewɔ. Amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ke Hiob jwiɛtɛi kuku kɛ shika ga.
12Yehowa jɔɔ Hiob yɛ enaagbee wala beiaŋ fe bɔ ni ejɔɔ lɛ tsutsu lɛ. Hiob na gwantɛŋi akpei nyɔŋma kɛ ejwɛ kɛ yoomai akpei ekpaa kɛ tsinai akpei enyɔ kɛ teji yei akpe kome. 13Esaa efɔ bihii kpawo kɛ biyei etɛ̃. 14Ewo ebiyoonukpa lɛ gbɛi akɛ Yemima, ebiyoo ni ji enyɔ lɛ ewo lɛ Kezia, ni ebiyoo ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ ewo lɛ Keren-Hapak. 15Yoo ko kwraa bɛ shikpɔŋ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ ni ehe yɛ fɛo tamɔ amɛ. Amɛtsɛ Hiob hã amɛ egboshinii lɛ eko tamɔ ehã amɛnyɛmimɛi hii lɛ.
16Sane nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ Hiob saa ehi shi afii oha kɛ nyɔŋmai ejwɛ, ni ena eshwiei kɛyashi amɛyinɔ ni ji ejwɛ nɔ bii. 17 Ni Hiob gbo be ni eji nuumo kotokoto ni eye afii babaoo diɛŋtsɛ lɛ.

english_text:
BOOK I
(Psalms 1–41)
The Way to Happiness
1God blesses those people
who refuse evil advice
and won't follow sinners
or join in sneering at God.
2Instead, they find happiness
in the Teaching of the Lord,
and they think about it
day and night.
3 They are like trees
growing beside a stream,
trees that produce
fruit in season
and always have leaves.
Those people succeed
in everything they do.
4That isn't true of those
who are evil—
they are like straw
blown by the wind.
5Sinners won't have an excuse
on the day of judgment,
and they won't have a place
with the people of God.
6The Lord protects everyone
who follows him,
but the wicked follow a road
that leads to ruin.
translation_text:
KLƐŊKLƐŊ WOLO LƐ
(Lalai 1—41)
Miishɛɛ Krɔŋŋ
1 Ajɔɔ mɔ ni booo mɛi fɔ̃ji aŋaawoo toi,
ni ekɛ eshafeelɔi ebɔɔɔ,
ni etaaa hefɛoyelɔi ateŋ.
2 Shi moŋ emii shɛɔ Yehowa Mla lɛ he,
ni ejwɛŋɔ he daa shwane kɛ nyɔɔŋ.
3 Etamɔ tsei ni atɛo yɛ fai atoi,
ni woɔ yibii yɛ amɛbe mli,
ni amɛbai kpalaaa,
ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni efeɔ lɛ shwereɔ.
4 Mɛi fɔ̃ji bɛ nakai;
amɛ lɛ amɛtamɔ tutuu ni kɔɔyɔɔ loɔ kɛyaa.
5No hewɔ lɛ, eshafeelɔi nyɛŋ
kojomɔ naa amɛdamɔ;
amɛnaŋ gbɛhe yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ webii lɛ ateŋ.
6 Ejaakɛ Yehowa kudɔɔ jalɔi agbɛ lɛ,
shi mɛi fɔ̃ji agbɛ lɛ ekɛ mɛi fɔ̃ji
yaa hiɛkpãtãmɔ mli.

english_text:
The Lord's Chosen King
1 Why do the nations plot,
and why do their people
make useless plans?
2The kings of this earth
have all joined together
to turn against the Lord
and his chosen king.
3They say, “Let's cut the ropes
and set ourselves free!”
4In heaven the Lord laughs
as he sits on his throne,
making fun of the nations.
5The Lord becomes furious
and threatens them.
His anger terrifies them
as he says,
6“I've put my king on Zion,
my sacred hill.”
7 I will tell the promise
that the Lord made to me:
“You are my son, because today
I have become your father.
8Ask me for the nations,
and every nation on earth
will belong to you.
9 You will smash them
with an iron rod
and shatter them
like dishes of clay.”
10Be smart, all you rulers,
and pay close attention.
11Serve and honor the Lord;
be glad and tremble.
12Show respect to his son
because if you don't,
the Lord might become furious
and suddenly destroy you.
But he blesses and protects
everyone who runs to him.
translation_text:
Maŋtsɛ ni Yehowa efɔ lɛ mu lɛ
1 Mɛɛba majimaji lɛ toɔ atuatsemɔ he ajina?
Ni maŋbii lɛ kpãŋɔ kpãŋmɔi fɔ̃ji?
2 Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ tseɔ atua,
ni lumɛi lɛ hu feɔ ekome;
amɛkpãŋɔ Yehowa kɛ maŋtsɛ
ni efɔ lɛ mu lɛ yinɔ.
3 Amɛkɛɔ akɛ, “Nyɛhãa wɔkumɔa amɛgboklɛi lɛ;
ni wɔtserɛ amɛkpai lɛ yɛ wɔhe.”
4 Mɔ ni ta ŋwɛi lɛ miiŋmɔ
Nuŋtsɔ lɛ miiye amɛhe fɛo po;
ni eyeɔ amɛhe fɛo hu.
5Ekɛ amɛ aaawie yɛ emlifu naa,
ni ekɛ mlila aaawo amɛhe gbeyei.
6Ekɛɛ, “Miwo mimaŋtsɛ yɛ Zion,
migɔŋ krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ nɔ.”
7 “Mashiɛ akpɔ ni Yehowa ewo mi lɛ,”
Ekɛɛ, “Mibi ji bo, ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ mifɔ bo.
8 Bi mi, ni maŋɔ majimaji lɛ mahã bo akɛ ogboshinii;
ni shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ aaatsɔ̃ ogbɛfaŋnɔ.
9 Okɛ dade dɛhiɛmɔtso aaakumɔ amɛ wɔtsɔwɔtsɔ,
ni ooojwara amɛ tamɔ gbɛshɔ̃lɔ gbɛ.”
10No hewɔ lɛ, Oo, nyɛ maŋtsɛmɛi, nyɛlea nii;
Oo, nyɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔyelɔi, nyɛkwɛa jogbaŋŋ.
11 Nyɛsɔmɔa Yehowa kɛ gbeyeishemɔ;
12 nyɛkɛ hekpokpomɔ akotoa lɛ;
kɛjeee nakai lɛ emli baafu nyɛ oya, ni nyɛhiɛ aaakpãtã.
Ajɔɔ mɛi fɛɛ ni baa lɛ abo lɛ.

english_text:
(Written by David when he was running from his son Absalom.)
An Early Morning Prayer
1 I have a lot of enemies, Lord.
Many fight against 2me and say,
“God won't rescue you!”
3But you are my shield,
and you give me victory
and great honor.
4I pray to you, and you answer
from your sacred hill.
5I sleep and wake up refreshed
because you, Lord,
protect me.
6Ten thousand enemies attack
from every side,
but I am not afraid.
7Come and save me, Lord God!
Break my enemies' jaws
and shatter their teeth,
8because you protect
and bless your people.
translation_text:

1Oo Yehowa, kwɛ mɛi abɔ sɔŋŋ ni haoɔ mi!
Mɛi babaoo ni teɔ shi woɔ mi!
2Mɛi pii kɛɔ yɛ mihe akɛ,
“Mɔ nɛ lɛ, enaŋ yiwalaheremɔ ko yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ dɛŋ.”
Sela

bo ohãa mihiɛ baa nyam.

mibolɔɔ mitsɛɔ Yehowa,
ni ejɛɔ egɔŋ krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehereɔ mi nɔ.
5 Mikãa shi miwɔɔ, ni mihiɛ tsɛ̃ɔ;
ejaakɛ Yehowa buɔ mihe nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ fɛɛ.
6 Misheee mɛi akpeiakpei abɔ
ni ebɔ nsra ewo mihe lɛ gbeyei.

miNyɔŋmɔ, baahere miyiwala,

Yehowa, ojɔɔmɔ aba omaŋ lɛ nɔ.
Sela

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader. Use stringed instruments.)
An Evening Prayer
1You are my God and protector.
Please answer my prayer.
I was in terrible distress,
but you set me free.
Now have pity and listen
as I pray.
2How long will you people
refuse to respect me?
You love foolish things,
and you run after
what is worthless.
3The Lord has chosen
everyone who is faithful
