from my enemies, Lord!
I come to you for safety.
10You are my God. Show me
what you want me to do,
and let your gentle Spirit
lead me in the right path.
11Be true to your name, Lord,
and keep my life safe.
Use your saving power
to protect me from trouble.
12I am your servant.
Show how much you love me
by destroying my enemies.
translation_text:
Yelikɛbuamɔ he sɔlemɔ
David Lala ko.
1Oo Yehowa, bo misɔlemɔ toi,
feemɔ toi ohã mifaikpamɔ lɛ;
heremɔ mi nɔ yɛ onɔkwayeli kɛ ojalɛ lɛ naa.
2 Okɛ otsulɔ akakojo,
ejaakɛ hiɛkãalɔ ko hiɛkãalɔ ko yeŋ bem yɛ ohiɛ.
3Ejaakɛ henyɛlɔ lɛ etiu mi,
ekpãtã miwala hiɛ kɛmɔ shi;
ehã mita duŋ mli tamɔ mɛi ni egboi jeeŋmɔ lɛ.
4No hewɔ lɛ, mimumɔ etɔ biti yɛ mimli;
mitsui efee shikplikpii yɛ mimli.
5 Mikaiɔ blema gbii lɛ,
mijwɛŋɔ nii ni ofee lɛ fiaa he;
misusuɔ oninenaa nitsumɔi lɛ ahe.
6 Miholeɔ miniji anɔ mihãa bo yɛ sɔlemɔ mli;
ohe kumai yeɔ misusuma tamɔ shikpɔŋ gbiŋ.
7 Oo Yehowa, heremɔ mi nɔ oya;
mimumɔ miitɔ biti;
kaaŋɔ ohiɛ otee mi,
kɛjee nakai lɛ,
matamɔ mɛi ni kpelekeɔ shi kɛyaa gbohiiaje lɛ.
8Leebi lɛ hã manu osuɔmɔ ni tsakeee lɛ he,
ejaakɛ bo onɔ mihiɛ kã.
Hã male gbɛ ni sa akɛ manyiɛ nɔ,
ejaakɛ bo miŋɔɔ misusuma mihãa.
9Oo Yehowa, jiemɔ mi yɛ mihenyɛlɔi lɛ adɛŋ!
Bo oŋɔɔ mijoɔ foi kɛbaa mibatee yɛ!
10 Tsɔ̃ɔmɔ mi koni mafee osuɔmɔnaanii,
ejaakɛ bo ji miNyɔŋmɔ.
Hã omumɔ kpakpa lɛ atsɔ̃ɔ
mi gbɛ kɛnyiɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ nɔ.
11 Oo Yehowa, ogbɛi lɛ hewɔ lɛ,
hã miyi ana wala!
Ojalɛ lɛ hewɔ lɛ,
jiemɔ mi kɛje haomɔ mli.
12 Osuɔmɔ ni tsakeee hã mi lɛ hewɔ lɛ,
folɔmɔ mihenyɛlɔi lɛ oshwie;
ni okpãtã mɛi ni waa mi yi lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ;
ejaakɛ otsulɔ ji mi.

english_text:
(By David.)
A Prayer for the Nation
1I praise you, Lord!
You are my mighty rock,
and you teach me
how to fight my battles.
2You are my friend, my fortress,
where I am safe.
You are my shield,
and you made me the ruler
of our people.
3 Why do we humans mean anything
to you, our Lord?
Why do you care about us?
4We disappear like a breath;
we last no longer
than a faint shadow.
5Open the heavens like a curtain
and come down, Lord.
Touch the mountains
and make them send up smoke.
6Use your lightning as arrows
to scatter my enemies
and make them run away.
7Reach down from heaven
and set me free.
Save me from the mighty flood
8of those lying foreigners
who never tell the truth.
9In praise of you, our God,
I will sing a new song,
while playing my harp.
10By your power, kings win wars,
and your servant David is saved
from deadly swords.
11Won't you keep me safe
from those lying foreigners
who never tell the truth?
12Let's pray that our young sons
will grow like strong plants
and that our daughters
will be as lovely as columns
in the corner of a palace.
13May our barns be filled
with all kinds of crops.
May our fields be covered
with sheep by the thousands,
14and every cow have calves.
Don't let our city be captured
or any of us be taken away,
and don't let cries of sorrow
be heard in our streets.
15Our Lord and our God,
you give these blessings
to all who worship you.
translation_text:
Maŋtsɛ ko da Nyɔŋmɔ shi
David Lala.
1 Yijiemɔ ahã Yehowa, mitɛsaa lɛ,
mɔ ni tsɔ̃ɔ miniji tawuu kɛ miwaobii nɔmɔ lɛ.
2 Lɛ ji mitɛsaa kɛ mimɔ̃ɔ,
mibobaa mɔɔ ni wa,
kɛ mijielɔ, mitsɛŋ kɛ mɔ abo ni mibaa lɛ.
Lɛ ebaa mimaŋbii shi ewoɔ mishishi.
3 Oo Yehowa, mɛɛ ji gbɔmɔ adesa
ni obuɔ ehe akɔntaa,
loo gbɔmɔ bi ni ojwɛŋɔ ehe?
4Gbɔmɔ lɛ etamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ,
egbii lɛ tamɔ hɔ̃ɔŋ ni hoɔ.
5 Oo Yehowa, kpoo oŋwɛi lɛ naa shi koni oyi shi!
Taramɔ gɔji lɛ ahe koni amɛje lasu!
6Hã srawai agbala,
koni ogbɛ ohenyɛlɔi lɛ oshwã.
Tsɛ̃rɛ̃mɔ ogãimlibii lɛ
koni owo amɛ foi.
7Kpã onine mli kɛjɛ ŋwɛi;
shɔ̃ mi koni ojie mi kɛjɛ nu kwɔŋkwɔŋ lɛ mli,
kɛjɛ mɛi kpɔ̃ji adɛŋ,
8mɛi ni maleɔ, ni amɛwoɔ
amɛninejurɔ nɔ amɛkãa amale kitã lɛ.
9 Oo, Nyɔŋmɔ, mala lala hee mahã bo!
Kpãi nyɔŋma saŋku matswa kɛjie oyi.
10Bo ohãa maŋtsɛmɛi yeɔ kunim,
ni ohereɔ otsulɔ David yiwala.
11Shɔ̃ mi kɛje yiwalɔ klante naa;
kpɔ̃ mi kɛje mɛi kpɔ̃ji adɛŋ,
mɛi ni maleɔ, ni amɛwoɔ
amɛninejurɔ nɔ amɛkãa amale kitã lɛ.
12 Wɔbihii adara yɛ amɛblahiiaŋ,
tamɔ tsei ni atɛo ni amɛdara;
ni wɔbiyei lɛ hu atãmɔ koŋtɛ
ni ako ni akɛmaa maŋtsɛ we.
13Wɔboŋoi lɛ ayimɔ obɔbɔ̃,
kɛ niyenii srɔtoi fɛɛ;
wɔtoi hu afɔfɔɔ akpekpei,
kɛ akpei nyɔŋmanyɔŋmai yɛ ŋa nɔ.
14Wɔtsinai hu afɔ babaoo;
amɛkasharake, ni amɛkalaaje;
akanu haomɔ blɔmɔ ko yɛ wɔblohuiaŋ.
15 Ajɔɔ maŋ ni naa nɛkɛ jɔɔmɔ nɛɛ!
Ajɔɔ maŋ ni Yehowa ji eNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.

english_text:
(By David for praise.)
The Lord Is Kind and Merciful
1I will praise you,
my God and King,
and always honor your name.
2I will praise you each day
and always honor your name.
3You are wonderful, Lord,
and you deserve all praise,
because you are much greater
than anyone can understand.
4Each generation will announce
to the next your wonderful
and powerful deeds.
5I will keep thinking about
your marvelous glory
and your mighty miracles.
6Everyone will talk about
your fearsome deeds,
and I will tell all nations
how great you are.
7They will celebrate and sing
about your matchless mercy
and your power to save.
8You are merciful, Lord!
You are kind and patient
and always loving.
9You are good to everyone,
and you take care
of all your creation.
10All creation will thank you,
and your loyal people
will praise you.
11They will tell about
your marvelous kingdom
and your power.
12Then everyone will know about
the mighty things you do
and your glorious kingdom.
13Your kingdom will never end,
and you will rule forever.
Our Lord, you keep your word
and do everything you say.
14When someone stumbles or falls,
you give a helping hand.
15Everyone depends on you,
and when the time is right,
you provide them with food.
16By your own hand you satisfy
the desires of all who live.
17Our Lord, everything you do
is kind and thoughtful,
18and you are near to everyone
whose prayers are sincere.
19You satisfy the desires
of all your worshipers,
and you come to save them
when they ask for help.
20You take care of everyone
who loves you,
but you destroy the wicked.
21I will praise you, Lord,
and everyone will respect
your holy name forever.
translation_text:
Yijiemɔ lala
Yijiemɔ lala. David Lala.
1Makafo bo, miNyɔŋmɔ kɛ miMaŋtsɛ,
ni majie ogbɛi lɛ yi daa kɛaatee naanɔi anaanɔ.
2Daa gbi lɛ majie oyi,
ni majie ogbɛi lɛ yi daa
kɛaatee naanɔi anaanɔ.
3Yehowa je agbo;
ni esa yijiemɔ babaoo,
ni egbojee lɛ anaaa naa.
4Yinɔ kome aaakafo onitsumɔi lɛ atsɔ̃ɔ yinɔ kroko;
ni amɛaajaje ohewalɛ nifeemɔi lɛ amɛtsɔ̃ɔ.
5Majwɛŋ onunyam falɛ
kɛ ogbojee kɛ onaakpɛɛ nitsumɔi lɛ ahe.
6Mɛi aaagba ohewalɛ nitsumɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ,
ni majaje ogbojee lɛ matsɔ̃ɔ.
7Amɛaajaje omlihilɛ kpeteŋkple lɛ;
amɛaala ojalɛ lɛ he lala waa.
8 Durolɔ kɛ mɔbɔnalɔ ji Yehowa;
emli fuuu mra, ni esuɔmɔ
ni tsakeee lɛ fa babaoo.
9Yehowa hi hã mɛi fɛɛ,
ni emusuŋ tsɔ̃ɔ lɛ yɛ ebɔɔnii lɛ fɛɛ he.
10Yehowa, obɔɔnii lɛ fɛɛ aaada bo shi;
ni omɛi krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ fɛɛ aaajie oyi.
11Amɛaawie omaŋtsɛyeli lɛ anunyam lɛ he,
ni amɛaagba ohewalɛ lɛ,
12koni amɛhã gbɔmɛi adesai abii ale ohewalɛ nitsumɔi lɛ,
kɛ omaŋtsɛyeli lɛ nyam kɛ egbojee.
13Omaŋtsɛyeli lɛ, naanɔ maŋtsɛyeli ni;
ni olumɔyeli lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyaa yinɔi fɛɛ nɔ.
14 Yehowa sɔoɔ mɛi fɛɛ ni miigbee shi lɛ,
ni eholeɔ mɛi fɛɛ ni edɔrɔ kɔmɔɔ lɛ anɔ.
15 Bɔɔnii fɛɛ kwɛɔ bo gbɛ,
ni bo ohãa amɛ niyenii yɛ be ni sa mli.
16Ogbɛɔ odɛ̃ŋ, ni ohãa
nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni hiɛ kã tɔɔ kɛ nii ni etaoɔ.
17 Yehowa ja yɛ egbɛi fiaa mli,
ni emli hi yɛ enifeemɔi fiaa mli.
18Yehowa bɛŋkɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni tsɛɔ lɛ lɛ;
ebɛŋkɛɔ mɛi fɛɛ ni tsɛɔ lɛ yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ.
19 Mɛi ni sheɔ lɛ gbeyei lɛ,
efeɔ amɛnitaomɔnii ehãa amɛ;
eboɔ amɛbolɔmɔ toi ni ehereɔ amɛyiwala.
20Yehowa baa mɛi fɛɛ ni sumɔɔ lɛ lɛ ayi;
shi yiwalɔi lɛ, eeekpãtã amɛhiɛ.
21Minaabu aaajie Yehowa yi ni bɔɔnii fɛɛ aaajie
egbɛi krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ yi daa kɛaatee naanɔi anaanɔ.

english_text:
Shout Praises to the Lord
1Shout praises to the Lord!
With all that I am,
I will shout his praises.
2I will sing and praise
the Lord God
as long as I live.
3You can't depend on anyone,
not even a great leader.
4Once they die and are buried,
that will be the end
of all their plans.
5The Lord God of Jacob blesses
everyone who trusts him
and depends on him.
6 God made heaven and earth;
he created the sea
and everything else.
God always keeps his word.
7He gives justice to the poor
and food to the hungry.
The Lord sets prisoners free
8and heals blind eyes.
He gives a helping hand
to everyone who falls.
The Lord loves good people
9and looks after strangers.
He defends the rights
of orphans and widows,
but destroys the wicked.
10The Lord God of Zion
will rule forever!
Shout praises to the Lord!
translation_text:
Nyɔŋmɔ yiwalaherelɔ lɛ yijiemɔ
1Jiemɔ Yehowa yi!
Oo misusuma, jiemɔ Yehowa yi!
2Gbii abɔ ni mihiɛ kã nɛɛ,
majie Yehowa yi!
Mala majie miNyɔŋmɔ lɛ yi miwala be fɛɛ.
3 Nyɛkaŋɔa nyɛhiɛ nyɛfɔa lumɛi
loo gbɔmɔ adesa bi ko ni yelikɛbuamɔ bɛ edɛŋ lɛ nɔ.
4 Kɛji emumɔ je emli lɛ,
ekuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa esu lɛ mli ekoŋŋ;
nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ eyiŋtoo fɛɛ laajeɔ.
5Ajɔɔ gbɔmɔ ni Yakob Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ ji eyelikɛbualɔ,
mɔ ni ehiɛ kãa Yehowa, eNyɔŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ.
6 Lɛ ebɔ ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋshɔ kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ;
lɛ lɛ eyeɔ anɔkwa kɛyaa naanɔ.
7Mɛi ni ayeɔ amɛ amim lɛ,
eyeɔ amɛsane ehãa amɛ;
mɛi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ,
ehãa amɛ niyenii.
Yehowa fɛneɔ gboklɛfoi agboklɛi.
8 Yehowa gbeleɔ shwilafoi ahiŋmɛii;
Yehowa holeɔ mɛi ni edɔrɔ kɔmɔɔ lɛ anɔ;
Yehowa sumɔɔ jalɔi.
9 Yehowa baa gbɔi ayi;
efĩɔ awusa kɛ okulafo sɛɛ;
shi mɛi fɔ̃ji agbɛ lɛ, ebutuɔ.
10 Yehowa baaye maŋtsɛ kɛaatee naanɔ,
Zion, oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ aaaye maŋtsɛ kɛaatee yinɔi fɛɛ nɔ.
Nyɛjiea Yehowa yi!

english_text:
Sing and Praise the Lord
1Shout praises to the Lord!
Our God is kind,
and it is right and good
to sing praises to him.
2The Lord rebuilds Jerusalem
and brings the people of Israel
back home again.
3He renews our hopes
and heals our bodies.
4He decided how many stars
there would be in the sky
and gave each one a name.
5Our Lord is great and powerful!
He understands everything.
6The Lord helps the oppressed,
but he smears the wicked
in the dirt.
7Celebrate and sing!
Play your harps
for the Lord our God.
8He fills the sky with clouds
and sends rain to the earth,
so that the hills
will be green with grass.
9He provides food for cattle
and for the young ravens,
when they cry out.
10The Lord doesn't care about
the strength of horses
or powerful armies.
11The Lord is pleased only
with those who worship him
and trust his love.
12Everyone in Jerusalem,
come and praise
the Lord your God!
13He makes your city gates strong
and blesses your people.
14God lets you live in peace,
and he gives you
the very best wheat.
15As soon as God speaks,
the earth obeys.
16He covers the ground with snow
like a blanket of wool,
and he scatters frost
like ashes on the ground.
17God sends down hailstones
like chips of rocks.
Who can stand the cold?
18At his command the ice melts,
the wind blows,
and streams begin to flow.
19God gave his laws and teachings
to the descendants of Jacob,
the nation of Israel.
20But he has not given his laws
to any other nation.
Shout praises to the Lord!
translation_text:
Nyɔŋmɔ Ofe lɛ yijiemɔ
1 Nyɛjiea Yehowa yi!
Ehi akɛ ala ajie wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ yi;
ejaakɛ durolɔ ji lɛ,
ni yijiemɔ lala sa lɛ.
2Yehowa ji mɔ ni maa Yerusalɛm maŋ lɛ;
ebuaa Israelbii ni agbɛ amɛ ashwã lɛ anaa.
3 Lɛ etsaa mɛi ni tsuii ekumɔ lɛ,
ni efimɔɔ amɛpilamɔi lɛ anɔ.
4 Lɛ etsɔ̃ɔ ŋulamii lɛ ayibɔ,
ni ewoɔ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛi lɛ.
5WɔNuŋtsɔ lɛ je agbo;
ni ehewalɛ fa naakpa,
ni enilee lɛ anaaa naa.
6 Yehowa woɔ heshibalɔi anɔ,
shi yiwalɔi lɛ etsirɛɔ amɛ etswiaa shi.
7Nyɛlaa shidaa lala nyɛhãa Yehowa,
nyɛkɛ saŋku alaa kɛjiea wɔNyɔŋmɔ lɛ yi.
8Lɛ ekɛ atatui haa ŋwɛi,
ni ehãa nu nɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ,
ni ehãa jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gɔ̃ŋkpɔi anɔ.
9 Lɛ ehãa kooloi niyenii,
ni elɛɔ kwãakwãalabitei abii ni bolɔɔ lɛ hu.
10Emiishɛɛnamɔ bɛ okpɔŋɔ hewalɛ mli,
ni ebɛ tabilɔi ahewalɛ he miishɛɛ hu.
11Shi moŋ Yehowa naa mɛi ni sheɔ lɛ gbeyei lɛ ahe miishɛɛ,
kɛ mɛi hu ni kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔ̃ɔ esuɔmɔ ni sɛɛ efooo lɛ nɔ lɛ.
12Oo Yerusalɛm, kafomɔ Yehowa!
Oo Zion, jiemɔ oNyɔŋmɔ lɛ yi!
13Ejaakɛ lɛ ewajeɔ ogboi lɛ asɛɛ adabaŋi lɛ kpɛŋŋ;
ejɔɔ obii ni yɔɔ omli lɛ.
14 Ehãa ohusui anɔ jɔɔ;
ehãa otɔɔ kɛ ŋmãa kpakpa.
15Efãa shikpɔŋ lɛ,
ni nɔ ni ekɛɔ lɛ afeɔ lɛ oya.
16 Ehãa snoo nyɔɔ futaa tamɔ too he tsɔi yɛŋ;
egbɛɔ bɔ́ ni efĩ eshwãa tamɔ lamlu.
17Eshɛrɛɔ enutɛi lɛ eshwieɔ shi tamɔ fɔbitɛi.
Namɔ aaanyɛ efɛ̃i lɛ naa edamɔ?
18Efãa, ni ewiemɔ lɛ naa lɛ,
nutɛi lɛ sereɔ.
Ehãa ekɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa,
ni nui lɛ hoɔ.
19Ejajeɔ ewiemɔ lɛ etsɔ̃ɔ Israel,
ekɛ ekpɔi kɛ emlai lɛ hãa Israel.
20 Efeko nakai nɔ ko ehãko maŋ ko maŋ ko dã;
emlai lɛ hu, amɛleee.
Nyɛjiea Yehowa yi!

english_text:
Come Praise the Lord
1Shout praises to the Lord!
Shout the Lord's praises
in the highest heavens.
2All of you angels,
and all who serve him above,
come and offer praise.
3Sun and moon,
and all of you bright stars,
come and offer praise.
4Highest heavens, and the water
above the highest heavens,
come and offer praise.
5Let all things praise
the name of the Lord,
because they were created
at his command.
6He made them to last forever,
and nothing can change
what he has done.
7All creatures on earth,
you obey his commands,
so come praise the Lord!
8Sea monsters and the deep sea,
fire and hail, snow and frost,
and every stormy wind,
come praise the Lord!
9All mountains and hills,
fruit trees and cedars,
10every wild and tame animal,
all reptiles and birds,
come praise the Lord!
11Every king and every ruler,
all nations on earth,
12every man and every woman,
young people and old,
come praise the Lord!
13All creation, come praise
the name of the Lord.
Praise his name alone.
The glory of God is greater
than heaven and earth.
14Like a bull with mighty horns,
the Lord protects
his faithful nation Israel,
because they belong to him.
Shout praises to the Lord!
translation_text:
Jeŋ fɛɛ ajie Nyɔŋmɔ yi
1Nyɛjiea Nyɔŋmɔ yi!
Nyɛjɛa ŋwɛi nyɛjiea Yehowa yi;
nyɛjiea eyi yɛ ŋwɛi flooflo!
2 Nyɛ, ebɔfoi lɛ fɛɛ nyɛjiea eyi!
Nyɛ, etai lɛ fɛɛ nyɛjiea eyi!
3 Hulu kɛ nyɔɔŋtsere, nyɛjiea eyi!
Nyɛŋulamii ni kpɛlɛɔ fiaa, nyɛjiea eyi!
4Nyɛ ŋwɛii amli ŋwɛi,
kɛ nui ni yɔɔ ŋwɛii amli ŋwɛi lɛ,
nyɛjiea eyi!
5Hã amɛ jie Yehowa gbɛi lɛ yi,
ejaakɛ lɛ efã, ni abɔ amɛ.
6Eŋɔ amɛ emamɔ shi kɛmiiya naanɔ;
ewo amɛ akpɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ nɔ amɛku.
7Nyɛjɛa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ
nyɛjiea Yehowa yi!
Nuŋ loi wuji ni he yɔɔ gbeyei,
bui ni mli kwɔlɔ fɛɛ,
8la kɛ nyɔŋmɔŋtɛ,
snoo kɛ afua,
ahum ni yeɔ efãmɔ nɔ.
9Nyɛjiea eyi
nyɛ gɔji kɛ gɔŋkpɔi fiaa,
tsei ni woɔ yibii
kɛ tsenedrui fɛɛ!
10Ŋaŋ kooloi kɛ shĩa kooloi fɛɛ,
waamɔ nibii kɛ loofɔji.
11Shikpɔŋ nɔ majiatsɛmɛi kɛ majimaji anɔ bii fɛɛ,
lumɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kojolɔi fɛɛ,
12oblahii kɛ oblayei fɛɛ,
onukpai kɛ gbekɛbii bluublu,
13hã amɛ jie Yehowa gbɛi lɛ yi,
ejaakɛ ekoome egbɛi lɛ nɔ awo gojoo fe gbɛii fɛɛ.
Lɛ enunyam lɛ kwɔ fe shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋwɛi fɛɛ tete.
14 Ekɛ ehewalɛ kpele lɛ ewo emaŋbii anɔ.
No hewɔ lɛ, emɛi krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ ajie eyi,
Israelbii, ni ji emaŋ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ,
nyɛjiea Yehowa yi!

english_text:
A New Song of Praise
1Shout praises to the Lord!
Sing him a new song of praise
when his loyal people meet.
2People of Israel, rejoice
because of your Creator.
People of Zion, celebrate
because of your King.
3Praise his name by dancing
and playing music on harps
and tambourines.
4The Lord is pleased
with his people,
and he gives victory
to those who are humble.
5All of you faithful people,
praise our glorious Lord!
Celebrate and worship.
6 Praise God with songs
on your lips
and a sword in your hand.
7Take revenge and punish
the nations.
8Put chains of iron
on their kings and rulers.
9Punish them as they deserve;
this is the privilege
of God's faithful people.
Shout praises to the Lord!
translation_text:
Yijiemɔ lala
1 Nyɛjiea Yehowa yi!
Nyɛlaa lala hee nyɛhãa Yehowa,
nyɛjiea eyi yɛ anɔkwafoi
agwabɔɔ lɛ mli.
2 Hã Israel anya ebɔlɔ lɛ he,
ni Zion bihii lɛ amli afili amɛ
yɛ emaŋtsɛ lɛ hewɔ.
3Hã amɛkɛ joo ajie egbɛi lɛ yi,
ni amɛkɛ miji kɛ saŋku ala amɛkɛjie eyi.
4Ejaakɛ Yehowa naa emaŋbii lɛ ahe tsuijurɔ;
ehãa humii yeɔ ta mli kunim.
5Hã anɔkwafoi lɛ anya yɛ anunyam mli;
hã amɛla nyamɔ lala yɛ amɛsai anɔ.
6Hã Nyɔŋmɔ kafomɔ akã amɛlilɛi nɔ,
ni amɛhiɛ klante kɛ enaa nta yɛ amɛdɛ̃,
7koni amɛkɛtɔ owele yɛ majimaji lɛ anɔ,
koni amɛkɛgbala maŋbii lɛ atoi,
8koni amɛkɛ kɔsɔŋkɔsɔi afimɔ amɛmaŋtsɛmɛi lɛ,
ni amɛwo amɛbladei lɛ dade gboklɛi,
9koni amɛkɛ toigbalamɔ ni aŋma ato agbala amɛtoi.
Enɛ ji anunyam hã emɛi krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ fɛɛ.
Nyɛjiea Yehowa yi!

english_text:
The Lord Is Good to His People
1Shout praises to the Lord!
Praise God in his temple.
Praise him in heaven,
his mighty fortress.
2Praise our God!
His deeds are wonderful,
too marvelous to describe.
3Praise God with trumpets
and all kinds of harps.
4Praise him with tambourines
and dancing,
with stringed instruments
and woodwinds.
5Praise God with cymbals,
with clashing cymbals.
6Let every living creature
praise the Lord.
Shout praises to the Lord!
translation_text:
Kafomɔ Yehowa
1Nyɛjiea Yehowa yi!
Nyɛjiea Nyɔŋmɔ yi yɛ ehe krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ;
nyɛjiea eyi yɛ ehewalɛ atatu lɛŋ!
2Nyɛjiea eyi yɛ ehewalɛ nitsumɔi lɛ ahewɔ;
nyɛjiea eyi yɛ egbojee kpeteŋkple lɛ hewɔ!
3Nyɛjiea eyi kɛ tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ kpãmɔ;
nyɛjiea eyi kɛ obenta kɛ saŋku!
4Nyɛjiea eyi kɛ miji kɛ joo,
nyɛjiea eyi kɛ kpãa saŋku kɛ bɛji!
5Nyɛjiea eyi kɛ ŋoŋo ni naa wa;
nyɛjiea eyi kɛ ŋoŋoi ni jijeɔ!
6 Nyɛhãa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni muɔ ajiea Yehowa yi!
Nyɛjiea Yehowa yi!

english_text:
How Proverbs Can Be Used
1 These are the proverbs
of King Solomon of Israel,
the son of David.
2Proverbs will teach you
wisdom and self-control
and how to understand
sayings with deep meanings.
3You will learn what is right
and honest and fair.
4From these, an ordinary person
can learn to be smart,
and young people can gain
knowledge and good sense.
5If you are already wise,
you will become even wiser.
And if you are smart,
you will learn to understand
6proverbs and sayings,
as well as words of wisdom,
and all kinds of riddles.
7 Respect and obey the Lord!
This is the beginning
of knowledge.
Only a fool rejects wisdom
and good advice.
Warnings against Bad Friends
8My child, obey the teachings
of your parents,
9and wear their teachings
as you would a pretty hat
or a lovely necklace.
10Don't be tempted by sinners
or listen 11when they say,
“Come on! Let's gang up
and kill somebody,
just for the fun of it!
12They're well and healthy now,
but we'll finish them off
once and for all.
13We'll take their valuables
and fill our homes
with stolen goods.
14If you join our gang,
you'll get your share.”
15Don't follow anyone like that
or do what they do.
16They are in a big hurry
to commit some crime,
perhaps even murder.
17They are like a bird
that sees the bait,
but ignores the trap.
18They gang up to murder someone,
but they are the victims.
19The wealth you get from crime
robs you of your life.
Wisdom Speaks
20 Wisdom shouts in the streets
wherever crowds gather.
21She shouts in the marketplaces
and near the city gates
as she says to the people,
22“How much longer
will you enjoy
being stupid fools?
Won't you ever stop sneering
and laughing at knowledge?
23Listen as I correct you
and tell you what I think.
24You completely ignored me
and refused to listen;
25you rejected my advice
and paid no attention
when I warned you.
26“So when you are struck
by some terrible disaster,
27or when trouble and distress
surround you like a whirlwind,
I will laugh and make fun.
28You will ask for my help,
but I won't listen;
you will search,
but you won't find me.
29No, you would not learn,
and you refused
to respect the Lord.
30You rejected my advice
and paid no attention
when I warned you.
31“Now you will eat the fruit
of what you have done,
until you are stuffed full
with your own schemes.
32Sin and self-satisfaction
bring destruction and death
to stupid fools.
33But if you listen to me,
you will be safe and secure
without fear of disaster.”
translation_text:
Abɛi ahe sɛɛnamɔ
1 Israel Maŋtsɛ Solomon, David bi lɛ, abɛi nɛ.
2Abɛi nɛɛ tsɔ̃ɔ mɔ nilee, ni amɛhãa mɔ naa tsɔsemɔ. Amɛhãa mɔ nuɔ wiemɔi ni jwɛŋmɔ yɔɔ mli ashishi faŋŋ hu.
3Amɛhãa mɔ leɔ nii, eleɔ nɔ ni ja, ni eleɔ anɔkwayeli.
4Abɛi nɛɛ tsɔ̃ɔ mɛi ni nako jwɛŋmɔ lɛ hiɛtɛ̃ɛ; ni amɛtsɔ̃ɔ oblanyo hu nilee kɛ jwɛŋmɔ.
5Nilelɔ hu nuɔ, ni ekaseɔ nii efataa enilee he. Amɛhãa mɔ ni nuɔ niiashishi hu leɔ ŋaa.
6Ebaanu abɛi kɛ wiemɔi ni amɛshishinumɔ wa kɛ nilelɔi awiemɔi kɛ amɛjenui ashishi.
Ŋaawoo kɛhã oblahii
7 Nilee fɛɛ shishijee ji Yehowa gbeyeishemɔ; shi kwashiai gbeɔ nilee kɛ tsɔsemɔ he guɔ.
8 Mibi, bo otsɛ tsɔsemɔ toi, ni kaashɛ mla ni onyɛ woɔ bo lɛ ofɔ̃. 9 Ejaakɛ nomɛi ji anunyam akekre ni fi oyitso kɛ kɔsɔŋkɔsɔ ni kã okuɛ. 10Mibi, kɛji eshafeelɔi miilaka bo lɛ, kaakpɛlɛ̃. 11Kɛji amɛkɛɛ bo akɛ, “Ba wɔtee ni wɔyawo mɔ ko antɛo, ni wɔyawo mɔ ko lá ni efeko nɔ ko fɔŋ ko ka yakatswaa lɛ kaakpɛlɛ̃. 12Kɛji amɛaakɛɛ bo akɛ hã wɔmĩĩ amɛ hiɛkãalɔi tamɔ bɔ ni gbohiiaje mĩiɔ mɛi emuu, aloo tamɔ akpelekeɔ shi aboteɔ gbonyobu mli, ni akuuu sɛɛ abaaa dɔŋŋ lɛ. 13Kɛji amɛaakɛɛ akɛ no wɔbaana nibii srɔtoi wɔwo wɔshĩai amli obɔ̃bɔ̃ lɛ kaakpɛlɛ̃. 14Kɛji amɛaakɛɛ akɛ bo lɛ kɛ ohe abɔ wɔhe kɛkɛ; wɔ fɛɛ wɔbaato fotro kome, ni nɔ ni wɔbaana lɛ wɔbaaja lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ kaakpɛlɛ̃.”
15Mibi, okɛ nɛkɛ gbɔmɛi akabɔ. Tsi ohe kɛje amɛhe kwraa. 16Gbɔmɛi ni tamɔ nɛkɛ lɛ, amɛhe yɛ oya kɛ efɔŋfeemɔ; amɛhe feɔ oya kɛ láshishwiemɔ. 17Eji yaka nɔ ko feemɔ akɛ aaatsɔ̃ loofɔlɔ tsɔne be mli ni eekwɛ. 18Nɛkɛ gbɔmɛi lɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe tsɔne amɛtsɔ̃ɔ lɛ, amɛwoɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala antɛo. 19Mɛi fɛɛ ni shɔ̃ɔ nii ekãa naa yɛ mɛi adɛŋ lɛ, bɔ ni amɛnaagbee tamɔ nɛ, nɔ ni amɛkɛ hiɛkɔ̃ɔ diɔ sɛɛ lɛ, no nɔŋŋ gbeɔ amɛ.
Nilee miitsɛ kwashiai
20Bo toi! Nilee miibolɔ waa yɛ blohuiaŋ, ni eewo egbee yɛ jaji anɔ. 21 Ebolɔɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ agboi lɛ anaa kɛ he fɛɛ he ni mɛi ebua amɛhe naa kutuu yɛ.
22Oo, nyɛ mɛi ni nyɛjwɛŋmɔ naa waaa, mɛɛ beyinɔ nɔŋŋ nyɛaahiɛ nyɛkwashiafeemɔ nɛɛ mli kɛyashi? Ni mɛɛ beyinɔ nɔŋŋ kwashiai hu aaanyɛ nilee kɛyashi? 23Kɛji mikã nyɛ lɛ, nyɛboa toi. Naa, mafɔse mimumɔ mawo nyɛmli, ni mahã nyɛyoo minilee wiemɔi lɛ hu. 24 Mitsɛ nyɛ, ni nyɛbooo mi toi; mikpã miniji amli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko mɔɔɔ mli. 25Miŋaawoo lɛ hu nyɛkwa fɛɛ, ni nyɛbuuu mikãmɔ lɛ. 26 No hewɔ lɛ, mi hu nyɛmanehulu mli lɛ, maŋmɔ nyɛ; ni kɛji gbeyei nɔ ko ba lɛ, maye nyɛhe fɛo. 27Kɛji tsuifãa nɔ ko batua nyɛ tamɔ ahum, ni nyɛmanehulu te shi tamɔ lasuogbele; ni kɛji hejaramɔ kɛ tsuiyeli ba nyɛnɔ lɛ, 28 no mli lɛ nyɛaatsɛ mi, shi mihereŋ nɔ; nyɛaatao misɛɛgbɛ kpɛ̃kpɛ̃ɛkpɛ̃, shi nyɛnaŋ mi. 29Akɛni amɛsumɔɔ nilee, ni amɛsheee Yehowa gbeyei; 30asaŋ akɛni amɛsumɔ̃ɔɔ ŋaa ni miwoɔ amɛ lɛ ekoeko, ni amɛgbe mikãmɔ lɛ fɛɛ he guɔ 31 hewɔ lɛ, nɔ ni amɛdu lɛ, no yibii amɛaakpa, ni ŋaa ni amɛtotoo lɛ he sɛɛ amɛaana. 32 Mɛi ni jwɛŋmɔ naa waaa kpaleɔ kɛjeɔ nilee he kɛyaa nɔ kroko he, ni no nɔŋŋ gbeɔ amɛ; ni jwɛŋmɔ ni kwashiai jwɛŋɔ akɛ amɛyɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ, no nɔŋŋ kpãtãa amɛhiɛ. 33 Shi mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni boɔ mi toi lɛ eeehi shi shweshweeshwe, ehe aaajɔ lɛ, ni esheŋ efɔŋ ko gbeyei.

english_text:
Wisdom and Bad Friends
1My child, you must follow
and treasure my teachings
and my instructions.
2Keep in tune with wisdom
and think what it means
to have common sense.
3Beg as loud as you can
for good common sense.
4Search for wisdom
as you would search for silver
or hidden treasure.
5Then you will understand
what it means to respect
and to know the Lord God.
6 All wisdom comes from the Lord,
and so do common sense
and understanding.
7God gives helpful advice
to everyone who obeys him
and protects those
who live as they should.
8God sees that justice is done,
and he watches over everyone
who is faithful to him.
9With wisdom you will learn
what is right
and honest and fair.
10Wisdom will control your mind,
and you will be pleased
with knowledge.
11Sound judgment and good sense
will watch over you.
12Wisdom will protect you
from evil schemes
and from those liars
13who turned from doing good
to live in the darkness.
14Most of all they enjoy
being mean and deceitful.
15They are dishonest themselves,
and so are all their deeds.
Wisdom and Sexual Purity
16Wisdom will protect you
from the smooth talk
of a sinful woman,
17who breaks her wedding vows
and leaves the man she married
when she was young.
18The road to her house leads
down
to the dark world
of the dead.
19Visit her, and you will never
find the road to life again.
20Follow the example
of good people
and live an honest life.
21If you are honest and innocent,
you will keep your land;
22if you do wrong
and can never be trusted,
you will be rooted out.
translation_text:
Nilee he nyɔmɔwoo
1Mibi, mɔ miwiemɔi lɛ amli, ni okɛ mikitãi lɛ ato. 2Ba otoi shi ohã nilee, ni oto otsui shi ohã sanesɛɛkɔmɔ. 3Mibi, fo otsɛ́ niiasɛɛyoomɔ, ni odi niiashishinumɔ sɛɛ. 4Taomɔ nilee sɛɛgbɛ tamɔ ataoɔ jwiɛtɛi aloo jwetri ko ni akɛtee. 5No dani ooonu Yehowa gbeyeishemɔ shishi, ni ooona Nyɔŋmɔ he nilee; 6ejaakɛ Yehowa hãa aleɔ nii; edaaŋ nilee kɛ niiashishinumɔ jɛɔ. 7Ehãa jalɔi leɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni eji tsɛŋ hã mɛi ni yɔɔ jeŋba kpakpa lɛ. 8Ebuɔ jalɔi ajalɛ saneyeli he, ni ebaa emɛi krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ agbɛi ayi.
9No dani obaanu jalɛ kɛ jalɛ saneyeli kɛ anɔkwayeli kɛ nɔ ni ji jeŋba kpakpa shishi. 10Ni obaana jwɛŋmɔ, ni nilee baahã osusuma mii ashɛ ehe. 11Jwɛŋmɔ aaabaa oyi, ni niiashishinumɔ aaabu ohe. 12Eeejie bo kɛjɛ jeŋba fɔŋ gbɛ nɔ, kɛaajɛ mɛi ni wieɔ yaka wiemɔ adɛŋ, 13kɛ mɛi ni ekwa jalɛ gbɛi ni amɛyanyiɛɔ dujiaŋ gbɛi anɔ lɛ. 14Eeejie bo kɛjɛ mɛi ni nyaa efɔŋfeemɔ he, ni amɛmli filiɔ amɛ yɛ nɔ fɔŋ feemɔ he lɛ adɛŋ. 15Eeejie bo kɛjɛ mɛi ni amɛgbɛi ekɔ̃dɔ̃ ni amɛbaaa amɛjeŋ jogbaŋŋ lɛ adɛŋ.
16 Nilee baajie bo kɛjɛ yoo ni bɛ jeŋba dɛŋ; nilee baajie bo kɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ yoo kɛ enaa dɔkɔbii lɛ dɛŋ. 17Eeejie bo kɛjɛ yoo ni ekwa eblayeiaŋ wu, ni ehiɛ ekpa kpãŋmɔ ni ekɛ lɛ kpãŋ yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ dɛŋ. 18Nɛkɛ yoo lɛ, ewe lɛ gbele gbɛ ni; egbɛi fɛɛ anaa kã kɛmiiya gbohiiaje. 19Mɔ ko mɔ ko eyaaa eŋɔɔ, ni eku esɛɛ eba pɛŋ, walagbɛ bɔɔ mɔ lɛ. 20No hewɔ lɛ, kasemɔ mɛi kpakpai ajeŋba koni ojeŋba atamɔ jalɔi anɔ. 21 Ejaakɛ mɛi ni ja lɛ, amɛaahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni mɛi ni hi kɛwula shi lɛ ji mɛi ni aaashwere yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. 22 Shi yiwalɔi lɛ aaafolɔ amɛ kɛaajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ashwie, ni kutumpɔfoi lɛ aaafamɔ amɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi kɛje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english_text:
Trust God
1My child, remember
my teachings and instructions
and obey them completely.
2They will help you live
a long and prosperous life.
3Let love and loyalty
always show like a necklace,
and write them in your mind.
4 God and people will like you
and hold you in high esteem.
5With all your heart
you must trust the Lord
and not your own judgment.
6Always let him lead you,
and he will clear the road
for you to follow.
7 Don't ever think that you
are wise enough,
but respect the Lord
and stay away from evil.
8This will make you healthy,
and you will feel strong.
9Honor the Lord by giving him
your money and the first part
of all your crops.
10Then you will have
more grain and grapes
than you will ever need.
11 My child, don't turn away
or become bitter
when the Lord corrects you.
12 The Lord corrects
everyone he loves,
just as parents correct
a child they dearly love.
The Value of Wisdom
13God blesses everyone
who has wisdom
and common sense.
14Wisdom is worth more
than silver;
it makes you much richer
than gold.
15Wisdom is more valuable
than precious jewels;
nothing you want
compares with her.
16In her right hand
Wisdom holds a long life,
and in her left hand
are wealth and honor.
17Wisdom makes life pleasant
and leads us safely along.
18Wisdom is a life-giving tree,
the source of happiness
for all who hold on to her.
19By his wisdom and knowledge
the Lord created
heaven and earth.
20By his understanding
he let the ocean break loose
and clouds release the rain.
21My child, use common sense
and sound judgment!
Always keep them in mind.
22They will help you to live
a long and beautiful life.
23You will walk safely
and never stumble;
24you will rest without a worry
and sleep soundly.
25So don't be afraid
of sudden disasters
or storms that strike
those who are evil.
26You can be sure that the Lord
will protect you from harm.
27 Do all you can for everyone
who deserves your help.
28Don't tell your neighbor
to come back tomorrow,
if you can help today.
29Don't try to be mean
to neighbors who trust you.
30Don't argue just to be arguing,
when you haven't been hurt.
31Don't be jealous
of cruel people
or follow their example.
32The Lord doesn't like
anyone who is dishonest,
but he lets good people
be his friends.
33He places a curse on the home
of everyone who is evil,
but he blesses the home
of every good person.
34 The Lord sneers at those
who sneer at him,
but he is kind to everyone
who is humble.
35You will be praised
if you are wise,
but you will be disgraced
if you are a stubborn fool.
translation_text:
Ŋaawoo kɛhã oblahii kɛ oblayei
1Mibi, ohiɛ akakpa mimlai lɛ anɔ, shi moŋ okɛ mikitãi lɛ ato otsui mli, 2ejaakɛ mitsɔ̃ɔmɔi lɛ baahã owala sɛɛ atsɛ afii babaoo, ni obaashwere yɛ wala mli. 3Kaahã mlihilɛ kɛ anɔkwayeli miishi bo; ŋɔɔ ofi okuɛ, ŋmãa yɛ otsuiŋ tao lɛ nɔ; 4no dani ooona nyam kɛ bulɛ kpakpa yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi ahiɛ.
5Okɛ ohiɛ afɔ̃ Yehowa nɔ kɛ otsui fɛɛ, ni okɛ ohe akakpasa bo diɛŋtsɛ ojwɛŋmɔ; 6kaimɔ lɛ yɛ ogbɛi fɛɛ amli, ni lɛ eeetsɔ̃ɔ bo gbɛ ni ja ni onyiɛ nɔ. 7Kaabu ohe nilelɔ; she Yehowa gbeyei, ni owi ohe kɛje efɔŋ he. 8Enɛ aaafee tsamɔ ahã bo, ni eeewo owui amli hewalɛ. 9Okɛ onii ni oyɔɔ kɛ onibaanii fɛɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ awo Yehowa hiɛ nyam; 10no dani aaahã oboŋoi lɛ ayimɔ obɔ̃bɔ̃ kɛ ŋmãa, ni owain gbɛi lɛ hu aaayimɔ obɔ̃bɔ̃ kɛ wain.
11 Mibi, kaagbe Yehowa tsɔsemɔ lɛ he guɔ, ni kaahã ekãmɔ hu miije otsine. 12Bɔ ni tsɛ kãa ebi ni eyɔɔ ehe tsuijurɔ lɛ, nakai pɛ Yehowa kãa ebi ni esumɔɔ lɛ hu. 13Ajɔɔ gbɔmɔ ni leɔ nii, ni enaa niiashishinumɔ hu lɛ, 14ejaakɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ no mli lɛ, ehi fe sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ jwiɛtɛi kɛ shika mli. 15Nilee kɛ niiashishinumɔ jara wa aahu fe tɛ̃ŋlɛ̃o; ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ ni aaanyɛ akɛto nilee he. 16Wala sɛɛtsɛlɛ yɛ eninejurɔ kɔkɔŋ, ni ninamɔ kɛ anunyam yɛ ebɛku kɔkɔŋ. 17Miishɛɛ yɛ etɛmpɔŋi anɔ, ni toiŋjɔlɛ yɛ egbɛi anɔ. 18Nilee lɛ wala tso ni hã mɛi ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ lɛ, ni mɛi ni hiɛ emli kpɛŋŋ lɛ, ajɔɔ amɛ. 19Yehowa kɛ nilee to shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi, ni jwɛŋmɔ ni mli kwɔ ekɛhã ŋwɛi ma shi shiŋŋ. 20Enilee naa hãa fai tueɔ, ni ehãa atatui lɛ nyɔɔ bɔ shwieɔ shi.
21Mibi, kɛ nilee kɛ sanesɛɛkɔmɔ ato; kaahã ohiɛ miije nɔ kwraa, 22ni eeehã ona wala kɛ hewulamɔnii. 23No dani ooonyiɛ ogbɛ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe, ni otɛŋ onane. 24Kɛ oho okã shi lɛ, osheŋ gbeyei; shi moŋ oookã shi, ni owɔ lɛ aaaŋɔɔ. 25Kaashe kpatu nɔ ko ni baahã otsui afã, aloo bɔ ni ahum fɔŋ tswaa mɛi fɔ̃ji lɛ gbeyei, 26 ejaakɛ Yehowa ji ohiɛnɔkãmɔ, ni lɛ eeebu ohe, ni ooofee shweshweeshwe.
27Mɛi ni esa amɛ ejurɔfeemɔ lɛ, kaakãmã amɛ, kɛji eyɛ ohewalɛ mli akɛ ooonyɛ ofee lɛ. 28Kɛji nɔ ko yɛ odɛ̃ŋ ni ooonyɛ okɛfee onaanyo lɛ ejurɔ lɛ, kaafee lɛ “Yaa ni oba, yaa ni oba”. 29Kaato onaanyo ko he ŋaa fɔŋ, be mli ni lɛ lɛ ehiɛ kã onɔ akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ omasɛi. 30Okɛ mɔ ko akabe yakatswaa, kɛji efeko bo efɔŋ ko. 31Ohiɛ akakɔ̃ yiwalɔ ko nɔ, ni egbɛi fɔ̃ji lɛ hu kaakɔ amɛmli ekoeko; 32 ejaakɛ Yehowa miihi nɔfɔŋfeelɔ, shi jalɔi lɛ eheɔ amɛ eyeɔ. 33Yehowa loomɔ kã mɛi fɔ̃ji awe nɔ; shi jalɔi awe lɛ, ejɔɔ nɔ. 34 Yehowa yeɔ hefɛoyelɔi ahe fɛo, shi mɛi ni baa amɛhe shi lɛ enaa amɛ mɔbɔ. 35Nilelɔi ahiɛ baa nyam, shi kwashiai naa hiɛshishwiemɔ.

english_text:
Advice to Young People
1My child, listen closely
to my teachings
and learn common sense.
2My advice is useful,
so don't turn away.
3When I was still very young
and my mother's favorite child,
my father 4said to me:
“If you follow my teachings
and keep them in mind,
you will live.
5Be wise and learn good sense;
remember my teachings
and do what I say.
6“If you love Wisdom
and don't reject her,
she will watch over you.
7The best thing about Wisdom
is Wisdom herself;
good sense is more important
than anything else.
8If you value Wisdom
and hold tightly to her,
great honors will be yours.
9It will be like wearing
a glorious crown
of beautiful flowers.”
The Right Way and the Wrong Way
10My child, if you listen
and obey my teachings,
you will live a long time.
11I have shown you the way
that makes sense;
I have guided you
along the right path.
12Your road won't be blocked,
and you won't stumble
when you run.
13Hold firmly to my teaching
and never let go.
It will mean life for you.
14Don't follow the bad example
of cruel and evil people.
15Turn aside and keep going.
Stay away from them.
16They can't sleep or rest
until they do wrong or harm
some innocent victim.
17Their food and drink
are cruelty and wickedness.
18The lifestyle of good people
is like sunlight at dawn
that keeps getting brighter
until broad daylight.
19The lifestyle of the wicked
is like total darkness,
and they will never know
what makes them stumble.
20My child, listen carefully
to everything I say.
21Don't forget a single word,
but think about it all.
22Knowing these teachings
will mean true life
and good health for you.
23Carefully guard your thoughts
because they are the source
of true life.
24Never tell lies or be deceitful
in what you say.
25Keep looking straight ahead,
without turning aside.
26 Know where you are headed,
and you will stay
on solid ground.
27Don't make a mistake by turning
to the right or the left.
translation_text:
Nilee he sɛɛnamɔ
1Bii, nyɛboa nyɛtsɛ tsɔsemɔ lɛ toi, ni nyɛfea toi ni nyɛlea sanesɛɛkɔmɔ. 2Jeŋba kpakpa he ŋaa miwoɔ nyɛ nɛɛ; nyɛkakwaa mitsɔ̃ɔmɔ lɛ. 3Be ni mi ji gbekɛnuu yɛ mitsɛ masɛi, ni minyɛ bi koome ni eshwɛɛɛ ehe ji mi lɛ, mitsɛ tsɔ̃ɔ mi nii, ni ekɛɛ mi akɛ, 4“Hã otsui amɔ miwiemɔi amli, ye mikitãi ni miwoɔ bo lɛ anɔ, ni oyi aaana wala. 5Na nilee kɛ sanesɛɛkɔmɔ. Ohiɛ akakpa midaaŋ wiemɔi lɛ anɔ, ni kaaŋmɛɛ he hu. 6Kaakwa nilee, ni eeebaa oyi; suɔmɔ lɛ, ni eeebu ohe. 7Nilee shishijee ji ona nilee, ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ona lɛ okɛtao sanesɛɛkɔmɔ sɛɛgbɛ. 8Buu nilee akɛ nɔ ko ni jara wa, ni eeewo onɔ; kɛji oloo lɛ atuu lɛ, eeewo ohiɛ nyam. 9Nilee aaafi bo anunyam akekre, ni eeebu bo maŋtsɛ fai ni yɔɔ fɛo.”
10Mibi, bo toi, ni omɔ miwiemɔi lɛ amli koni owala sɛɛ atsɛ. 11Mitsɔ̃ɔ bo nilee gbɛ lɛ; mikɛ bo etsɔ̃ jalɛ tɛmpɔŋi anɔ. 12Kɛji onyiɛ gbɛi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ onane etɔ̃tɔ̃ŋ, ni kɛji ojo foi yɛ nɔ po, otɛŋ. 13Mɔ tsɔsemɔ mli waa, kaaŋmɛɛ he. Okɛto jogbaŋŋ, shi no ji owala. 14 Kaayi yiwalɔi agbɛ nɔ, ni mɛi fɔ̃ji agbɛ hu okanyiɛ nɔ. 15Wii ohe kɛje gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ, kaayi nɔ; tsi ohe kɛje nɔ kwraa, ni ofo mli kɛya. 16Ejaakɛ mɛi fɔ̃ji wɔɔɔ akɛ ja amɛfee efɔŋ dã. Wɔ po tseɔ yɛ amɛhiɛ ja amɛna mɔ ko awui amɛye dã. 17Ejaakɛ efɔŋfeelɔi aŋmãa ji yiwalɛ, ni amɛwain ji basabasafeemɔ.
18Shi jalɔi agbɛ lɛ etamɔ leebi la ni kpɛɔ, ni eyaa nɔ ekpɛɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ shwane. 19 Mɛi fɔ̃ji agbɛ lɛ etamɔ duŋ kabitii; amɛtɛrɛɔ, ni amɛnaaa nibii ni amɛtɛrɛɔ lɛ.
20Mibi, ka otoi ohã miwiemɔi lɛ; ba otoi shi ohã nɔ ni mikɛɔ lɛ. 21Ohiɛ akaje nɔ. Kɛto otsui mli tɔ̃ɔ. 22Ejaakɛ wala eji hã mɔ ni nine shɛɔ nɔ, ni eji tsabaa hã ehewojiaŋ fɛɛ. 23Ohiɛ akã otsui he fe nii fɛɛ; ejaakɛ no mli wala jɛɔ. 24Wiemɔ gbonyo akaje onaa; ni kaaye kutumpɔo. 25Too ohiɛ tɛ̃ɛ, ohiɛ ama he ni oyaa lɛ nɔ. 26 Le onanefãamɔ, kɛkɛ lɛ ogbɛi fɛɛ aaaja ahã bo. 27 Kaagba ejurɔ loo abɛku. Tsi ohe kɛje efɔŋ he.

english_text:
Be Faithful to Your Wife
1My son, if you listen closely
to my wisdom and good sense,
2you will have sound judgment,
and you will always know
the right thing to say.
3The words of an immoral woman
may be as sweet as honey
and as smooth as olive oil.
4But all that you really get
from being with her
is bitter poison and pain.
5If you follow her,
she will lead you down
to the world of the dead.
6She has missed the path
that leads to life
and doesn't even know it.
7My son, listen to me
and do everything I say.
8Stay away from a bad woman!
Don't even go near the door
of her house.
9You will lose your self-respect
and end up in debt
to some cruel person
for the rest of your life.
10Strangers will get your money
and everything else
you have worked for.
11When it's all over,
your body will waste away,
as you groan 12and shout,
“I hated advice and correction!
13I paid no attention
to my teachers,
14and now I am disgraced
in front of everyone.”
15You should be faithful
to your wife,
just as you take water
from your own well.
16And don't be like a stream
from which just any woman
may take a drink.
17Save yourself for your wife
and don't have sex
with other women.
18Be happy with the wife
you married
when you were young.
19She is beautiful and graceful,
just like a deer;
you should be attracted to her
and stay deeply in love.
20Don't go crazy over a woman
who is unfaithful
to her own husband!
21The Lord sees everything,
and he watches us closely.
22Sinners are trapped and caught
by their own evil deeds.
23They get lost and die
because of their foolishness
and lack of self-control.
translation_text:
Gbãlãfitemɔ he kɔkɔbɔɔ
1Mibi, bo minilee lɛ toi, ni oka otoi ohã miniiashishinumɔ; 2koni ole sanesɛɛkɔmɔ, ni odaaŋ wiemɔi aaajie onilee kpo. 3 Ejaakɛ yoo ni bɛ jeŋba lɛ, enaa ŋɔɔ tamɔ wo, ni edaaŋ shamɔɔ fe eŋmɔmi. 4Ni naagbee mli lɛ ejoɔ tamɔ taatso; enaaba tamɔ klante kɛ enaa nta. 5Enyiɛ gbele gbɛ, ni ebaakpala bo kɛya gbohiiaje. 6Enyiɛɛɛ wala gbɛ, hewɔ lɛ eduɔ gbɛ ni eleee. 7No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ, mibi, bo mi toi, ni kaashi miwiemɔi lɛ asɛɛ. 8Tsi ohe kɛje nɛkɛ yoo he kwraa. Kaabɛŋkɛ ewe lɛ shinaa lɛ naa tete. 9Kɛjeee nakai lɛ obulɛ baalaaje, ni yiwalɔi aaafo owala sɛɛ; 10asaŋ nii ni okɛ ohewalɛ tsu lɛ gbɔi baaye amɛtɔrɔ; ni nibii ni ogbo deŋme yɛ amɛhe lɛ aaaya mɔkpɔŋ ko we. 11Ni onaagbee mli lɛ, be ni ohewolo kɛ ogbɔmɔtso hiɛ ekpãtã lɛ obaakɛ̃mɔ. 12No be mli oookɛɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛ hewɔ kwraa minyɛ tsɔsemɔ, ni mikpoo kamɔ̃ kɛjɛ mitsui mli tɔ̃ɔ nɛɛ? 13Mibooo mitsɔ̃ɔlɔi atoi, ni mikaaa mitoi mihãaa mɛi ni tsɔ̃ɔ mi nii lɛ. 14Shwɛ shrao ni mihiɛ akpãtã kwraa yɛ asafo lɛ mli.”
15Ye oŋa anɔkwa, ni oŋɔ suɔmɔ ohã lɛ ekoome pɛ tamɔ bɔ ni mɔ nuɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ mli nu lɛ. 16Ejaakɛ bii ni okɛ yei krokomɛi aaafɔ lɛ, onaŋ amɛhe sɛɛ. 17Obii lɛ adara yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ owe, koni amɛye amɛbua bo diɛŋtsɛ, shi jeee mɛi kpɔ̃ji. 18No hewɔ lɛ, na oŋa he miishɛɛ koni omii ashɛ oblahiiaŋ yoo ni oyakpee lɛ he. 19Ehe fɛo tamɔ ofrote, ni ehe yɛ akɔnɔ tamɔ yɔɔ; ehe akɔnɔ lɛ ashɛje omii be fɛɛ be; hã ni esuɔmɔ aŋɔ bo nom. 20Shi mibi, mɛɛba yoo ni bɛ jeŋba he feɔ bo akɔnɔ, ni oloɔ yoo mɔkpɔŋ atuu? 21Ejaakɛ Yehowa lɛ, enaa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni afeɔ, ni eekwɛ oyaa kɛ obaa fɛɛ. 22Mɔ fɔŋ lɛ enifɔji anii lɛ nɔŋŋ duɔ lɛ tamɔ tsɔne, ni eshai ni efeɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ fimɔɔ lɛ tamɔ kpãa. 23 Egboɔ ejaakɛ ebɛ tsɔsemɔ, ni ekwashiafeemɔ babaoo hewɔ lɛ ehiɛ kpãtãa.

english_text:
Don't Be Foolish
1 My child, suppose you agree
to pay the debt of someone,
who cannot repay a loan.
2Then you are trapped
by your own words,
3and you are now in the power
of someone else.
Here is what you should do:
Go and beg for permission
to call off the agreement.
4Do this before you fall asleep
or even get sleepy.
5Save yourself, just as a deer
or a bird tries to escape
from a hunter.
6You lazy people can learn
by watching an anthill.
7Ants don't have leaders,
8but they store up food
during harvest season.
9How long will you lie there
doing nothing at all?
When are you going to get up
and stop sleeping?
10 Sleep a little. Doze a little.
Fold your hands
and twiddle your thumbs.
11Suddenly, everything is gone,
as though it had been taken
by an armed robber.
12Worthless liars go around
13 winking and giving signals
to deceive others.
14They are always thinking up
something cruel and evil,
and they stir up trouble.
15But they will be struck
by sudden disaster
and left without a hope.
16There are six or seven
kinds of people
the Lord doesn't like:
17Those who are too proud
or tell lies or murder,
18those who make evil plans
or are quick to do wrong,
19those who tell lies in court
or stir up trouble
in a family.
20Obey the teaching
of your parents—
21always keep it in mind
and never forget it.
22Their teaching will guide you
when you walk,
protect you when you sleep,
and talk to you
when you are awake.
23The Law of the Lord is a lamp,
and its teachings
shine brightly.
Correction and self-control
will lead you through life.
24They will protect you
from the flattering words
of someone else's wife.
25Don't let yourself be attracted
by the charm and lovely eyes
of someone like that.
26A woman who sells her love
can be bought for as little
as the price of a meal.
But making love
to another man's wife
will cost you everything.
27If you carry burning coals,
you burn your clothes;
28if you step on hot coals,
you burn your feet.
29And if you go to bed
with another man's wife,
you pay the price.
30We don't put up with thieves,
not even with one who steals
for something to eat.
31And thieves who get caught
must pay back
seven times what was stolen
and lose everything.
32But if you go to bed
with another man's wife,
you will destroy yourself
by your own stupidity.
33You will be beaten
and forever disgraced,
34because a jealous husband
can be furious and merciless
when he takes revenge.
35He won't let you pay him off,
no matter what you offer.
translation_text:
1 Mibi, kɛji owo onaanyo ko shi yɛ sane ko mli, aloo okɛ mɔ ko ta abasa yɛ onaanyo ko hewɔ, 2ni atsɔ̃ olilɛi nɔ adu bo, aloo atsɔ̃ odaaŋ wiemɔ nɔ amɔ bo lɛ, 3mibi, feemɔ enɛ ni okɛjie ohe; ejaakɛ onaanyo lɛ nine egbe bo. Yaa oya mramra ni oyakpa onaanyo lɛ fai. 4Kaahã ohiŋmɛii miina wɔ miiwɔ. Kaahã wɔ miiba ohiɛsɛɛ kwraa. 5Jiemɔ ohe kɛjɛ edɛŋ tamɔ soŋai jieɔ ehe yɛ gbɔbilɔ dɛŋ, aloo tamɔ loofɔlɔ jieɔ ehe yɛ loofɔlɔdulɔ dɛŋ lɛ. 6 Hejɔ̃lɔ, yaa tsatsu ŋɔɔ, jwɛŋmɔ enifeemɔi ahe ni ole nii. 7Lɛ po ni ebɛ maŋtsɛ loo nɔkwɛlɔ loo nɔyelɔ ko kwraa lɛ, 8etaoɔ eniyenii etoɔ yɛ latsaa be mli, ni ebuaa eŋmãa naa yɛ nikpamɔ be mli. 9Hejɔ̃lɔ, mɛɛbe oookã shi owɔ kɛyashi? Mɛɛbe nɔŋŋ ooote shi kɛaajɛ owɔ mli? 10 Hejɔ̃lɔ kɛɔ akɛ, “Mawɔ fioo; majie mihiɛsɛɛ fioo; makota miniji majɔɔ mihe fioo.” 11Be ni ooohɛle shi lɛ, ohia ebatua bo tamɔ ojotswalɔ; ni fimɔ aaatua bo tamɔ tabilɔ ni hiɛ tsɛŋ.
12 Yakagbɔmɔ, nɔfɔŋfeelɔ yɔɔ nɛɛ, enyiɛɔ eyeɔ kutumpɔo. 13Ebɛɔ mɔ hiŋmɛi, ekɛ enaji tete wieɔ, ni ekɛ ewaobii toɔ okadi. 14Etoɔ nibii fɔ̃ji yɛ etsui mli, eshwieɔ eyiŋ ŋaa fɔŋ daa, bei sɔŋŋ ewoɔ. 15No hewɔ lɛ, ehiɛ aaakpãtã trukaa, ni aaakumɔ lɛ trukaa ashwie shi bɔ ni ebɛ tsabaa.
16Yehowa miihi nibii kpawo: 17hewoo; amale lilɛi kɛ niji ni shwieɔ lá ni efeko efɔŋ ko shi. 18Tsui ni shwieɔ yiŋ fɔŋ, naji ni he yɔɔ oya kɛ efɔŋfeemɔ. 19Mɔ ni yeɔ amale odase, ni efoɔ sane ni bɛ mli etãa; mɔ ni woɔ nanemɛi ateŋ bei.
Gbãlãfitemɔ he kɔkɔbɔɔ
20 Mibi, ye otsɛ kitãi lɛ anɔ, ni nii ni onyɛ tsɔ̃ɔ bo lɛ kaakwa ekoeko. 21 Ŋɔɔ kitãi lɛ amli wiemɔi lɛ oto otsui mli daa nɛɛ; ŋɔɔ ofi okuɛ. 22 Kɛji onyiɛ lɛ eeetsɔ̃ɔ bo gbɛ; kɛji okã shi owɔ lɛ, eeebu ohe, ni kɛji ohiɛ tsɛ̃ lɛ, ekɛ bo aaagba sane. 23Ejaakɛ kitã lɛ, kane ni, ni mla lɛ, la ni, ni tsɔsemɔkãmɔ lɛ, wala gbɛ ni. 24Tsɔ̃ɔmɔ nɛɛ aaabaa oyi kɛje yoo fɔŋ dɛŋ, eeekpɔ̃ bo kɛje yoo ni bɛ jeŋba lilɛi dɔkɔbii lɛ dɛŋ. 25Kaadi ehe fɛo sɛɛ yɛ otsui mli, ni kaahã ekɛ ehiɛsɛɛ miimɔ bo. 26Abaanyɛ akɛ aboloo akwaabɔ abɔ yoo ajwamãŋ apaa, shi yoo gbãlãfitelɔ aaahã nuu wala tete abɔ lɛ.
27Aso mɔ ko aaaje la ashwie emiinaa, ni etadei eshãŋ? 28Aloo mɔ ko aaanyiɛ ŋai kɛ la nɔ, ni enaji eshaŋ? 29 Nakai eji hã nuu ni nyiɛɔ mɔ kroko ŋa sɛɛ; mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ ni aaata ehe ni eeeye ehe kɔkɔɔkɔ. 30Kɛji hɔmɔ naa kɛkɛ ni julɔ yaju lɛ, agbeee ehe guɔ. 31Shi kɛji amɔ lɛ lɛ, ani ahaŋ eto najiaŋ toi kpawo lo? Ekɛ ewe nii fɛɛ tswɛm hãa. 32 Shi nuu ni fiteɔ gbãlã lɛ ebɛ yitsoŋ; mɔ ni feɔ nakai lɛ, lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe efiteɔ. 33Pilamɔ kɛ heguɔgbee eeena, ni ehiɛshishwiemɔ lɛ, anyɛŋ atsumɔ kɔkɔɔkɔ. 34Ejaakɛ awuŋayeli hãa nuu mlifu naa waa, ni kɛji eetɔ owele lɛ, ekɔ̃ɔɔ efiliii. 35Eheŋ kpãtãmɔ nii ko, ni nyɔɔŋnii pii po ebaakwa.

english_text:
The Foolishness of Unfaithfulness
1My son, pay close attention
and don't forget
what I tell you to do.
2Obey me, and you will live!
Let my instructions be
your greatest treasure.
3Keep them at your fingertips
and write them
in your mind.
4Let wisdom be your sister
and make common sense
your closest friend.
5They will protect you
from the flattering words
of someone else's wife.
6From the window of my house,
I once happened to see
7some foolish young men.
8It was late in the evening,
sometime after dark.
9One of these young men
turned the corner
and was walking by the house
of an unfaithful wife.
10She was dressed fancy
like a woman of the street
with only one thing in mind.
11She was one of those women
who are loud and restless
and never stay at home,
12who walk street after street,
waiting to trap a man.
13She grabbed him and kissed him,
and with no sense of shame,
she said:
14“I had to offer a sacrifice,
and there is enough meat
left over for a feast.
15So I came looking for you,
and here you are!
16The sheets on my bed
are bright-colored cloth
from Egypt.
17And I have covered it
with perfume made of myrrh,
aloes, and cinnamon.
18“Let's go there
and make love all night.
19My husband is traveling,
and he's far away.
20He took a lot of money along,
and he won't be back home
before the middle
of the month.”
21And so, she tricked him
with all of her sweet talk
and her flattery.
22At once he followed her
like an ox on the way
to be slaughtered,
or like a fool on the way
to be punished
23and killed with arrows.
He was no more than a bird
rushing into a trap,
without knowing
it would cost him his life.
24My son, pay close attention
to what I have said.
25Don't even think about
that kind of woman
or let yourself be misled
by someone like her.
26Such a woman has caused
the downfall and destruction
of a lot of men.
27Her house is a one-way street
leading straight down
to the world of the dead.
translation_text:
1Mibi, ye miwiemɔi lɛ anɔ, ni okɛ mikitãi lɛ ato. 2Ye mikitãi lɛ anɔ ní oyi ana wala; ni obu mitsɔ̃ɔmɔi lɛ tamɔ ohiŋmɛi mli ajaŋmalaatɛ. 3Hã ehi owaobii anaa. Ŋmãa yɛ otsuiŋ tao lɛ nɔ. 4Tsɛ nilee akɛ, “Minyɛmi yoo,” koni otsɛ sanesɛɛkɔmɔ akɛ oshieŋnyɛ. 5Amɛ amɛaabaa oyi kɛjɛ yoo ni bɛ jeŋba dɛŋ, amɛaakpɔ̃ bo kɛjɛ yoo ni naa yɔɔ dɔkɔbii lɛ dɛŋ.
Yoo ni bɛ jeŋba lɛ
6Ejaakɛ mitsɔ̃ miwe lɛ samflɛ lɛ mli mikwɛ, 7ni mina oblanyo ko ni bɛ yitsoŋ, yɛ oblahii komɛi ni ajwɛŋmɔ esako komɛi ateŋ. 8Oblanyo lɛ nyiɛ gbɛjegbɛ ko ni tsɔ̃ɔ yoo nɛɛ shĩa lɛ koŋ lɛ nɔ; ni eyi yoo lɛ we lɛ gbɛ. 9Gbɛkɛ ni, ni hiɛ efee tuutuu, ni duŋ kpii miihe awo. 10Ni naa, yoo ko kɛ oblanyo lɛ bakpe. Yoo lɛ wo ajwamãŋ atade, ni etsui esa. 11Enaa wa, ni etoi egbo, ni etaaa shĩa. 12Bianɛbianɛ etee agbo lɛ naa; bianɛbianɛ etee jara lɛ nɔ, ni ewoɔ ka yɛ tsu koŋ fɛɛ tsu koŋ. 13Yoo nɛɛ mɔ oblanyo lɛ ni eshwɔ enaa, ni yoo lɛ mia ehiɛ ni ekɛɛ lɛ akɛ, 14 “Kulɛ esa akɛ mashã afɔle, shi ŋmɛnɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ miyawo mishiwoonii lɛ. 15No hã mije kpo koni mabɔ mɔdɛŋ matao bo ni mikɛ bo akpe, ni trukaa mibana bo nɛɛ. 16Mikɛ saanɔboi ni akɛ kpãi sui srɔtoi ni akɛjɛ Ijipt loo eha misaa lɛ nɔ. 17Mikɛ mire kɛ aloe kɛ sinamon ewo misaa lɛ mli ŋma. 18Ba ni wɔkɛ suɔmɔ ajie wɔkɔnɔ kɛyashi leebi. Wɔkɛ suɔmɔ anya kɛ miishɛɛ. 19Ejaakɛ miwu bɛ, efã gbɛ kɛtee shɔŋŋ. 20Ehiɛ shika pii kɛ kotoku kɛtee. Nyɔɔŋtsere lɛ baaye emuu dani ebaaba.” 21Yoo lɛ kɛ ewiemɔ kɛ ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ kɔne oblanyo lɛ yiŋ, ni eyitsoŋ tsɔ̃. Ekɛ enaa dɔkɔbii lɛ kpala lɛ kɛtee ewe. 22Oblanyo lɛ nyiɛ yoo lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛtee ewe lɛ tamɔ tsina ni ayaagbe lɛ, aloo ofrote ni tsɔne edu lɛ kpɛŋŋ 23kɛyashi beyinɔ ni gãimlibi tsuɔ emusuŋ nii amli. Etamɔ loofɔlɔ ni shaa foi kɛyaduɔ tsɔne ni eleee akɛ lɛ ewala hewɔ atsɔ̃ tsɔne lɛ.
24Oo, mibii, nyɛboa mi toi agbɛnɛ. Nyɛfea toi nyɛhãa midaaŋ wiemɔi lɛ. 25Kaahã otsui mɔ nɛkɛ yoo. Kaadu gbɛ kɛyaje egbɛ nɔ; 26ejaakɛ yoo ni tamɔ nɛkɛ lɛ ekpãtã mɛi pii ahiɛ, mɛi ni egbe lɛ ayi fa naakpa. 27 Ewe lɛ, gbohiiaje gbɛ ni, ekã kɛmiiya gbele piai amli tɔ̃ɔ.

english_text:
In Praise of Wisdom
1 With great understanding,
Wisdom is calling out
2as she stands at the crossroads
and on every hill.
3She stands by the city gate
where everyone enters the city,
and she shouts:
4“I am calling out
to each one of you!
5Good sense and sound judgment
can be yours.
6Listen, because what I say
is worthwhile and right.
7I always speak the truth
and refuse to tell a lie.
8Every word I speak is honest,
not one is misleading
or deceptive.
9“If you have understanding,
you will see that my words
are just what you need.
10Let instruction and knowledge
mean more to you than silver
or the finest gold.
11 Wisdom is worth much more
than precious jewels
or anything else you desire.”
Wisdom Speaks
12I am Wisdom—Common Sense
is my closest friend;
I possess knowledge
and sound judgment.
13If you respect the Lord,
you will hate evil.
I hate pride and conceit
and deceitful lies.
14I am strong, and I offer
sensible advice
and sound judgment.
15By my power kings govern,
and rulers make laws
that are fair.
16Every honest leader rules
with help from me.
17I love everyone who loves me,
and I will be found by all
who honestly search.
18I can make you rich and famous,
important and successful.
19What you receive from me
is more valuable
than even the finest gold
or the purest silver.
20I always do what is right,
21and I give great riches
to everyone who loves me.
22 From the beginning,
I was with the Lord.
I was there before he began
23to create the earth.
At the very first,
the Lord gave life to me.
24When I was born,
there were no oceans
or springs of water.
25My birth was before
mountains were formed
or hills were put in place.
26It happened long before God
had made the earth
or any of its fields
or even the dust.
27 I was there when the Lord
put the heavens in place
and stretched the sky
over the surface of the sea.
28I was with him when he placed
the clouds in the sky
and created the springs
that fill the ocean.
29I was there when he set
boundaries for the sea
to make it obey him,
and when he laid foundations
to support the earth.
30I was right beside the Lord,
helping him plan and build.
I made him happy each day,
and I was happy at his side.
31I was pleased with his world
and pleased with its people.
32 Pay attention, my children!
Follow my advice,
and you will be happy.
33Listen carefully
to my instructions,
and you will be wise.
34Come to my home each day
and listen to me.
You will find happiness.
35By finding me, you find life,
and the Lord will be pleased
with you.
36But if you don't find me,
you hurt only yourself,
and if you hate me,
you are in love with death.
translation_text:
Nilee yijiemɔ
1Ani jeee blɔmɔ nilee bolɔɔ kɛtsɛɔ lɛ;
ni jeee niiashishinumɔ hu woɔ egbee lɛ?
2Edamɔ hei grɔŋŋi lɛ yɛ gbɛ lɛ he yɛ ŋmaŋmashai lɛ.
3 Ebolɔɔ gegeege yɛ maŋ lɛ agboi lɛ anaa yɛ maŋ lɛ klotia yɛ shinaa lɛ shi akɛ,
4“Oo, nyɛ hii, nyɛ mibolɔɔ mitsɛɔ,
ni nyɛ gbɔmɛi abii,
nyɛ miwoɔ migbee nɔ mihãa.
5Oo, nyɛ mɛi ni nyɛnako jwɛŋmɔ, nyɛkasea hiɛtɛ̃ɛ.
Oo, nyɛ hii kwashiai hu, nyɛboa toi jogbaŋŋ.
6Nyɛboa toi, ejaakɛ mibawie wiemɔi wuji ni he jaraa;
ni minaa ni magbele nɛɛ,
wiemɔi ni ja sɔŋŋ aaajɛ mli.
7Ejaakɛ anɔkwale wiemɔ aaajɛ midaaŋ;
minaabu miihi nɔ fɔŋ.
8Midaaŋ wiemɔi fɛɛ lɛ, jalɛ ni,
ekoeko bɛ mli ni ji amale loo kutumpɔo.
9Fɛɛ kã shi faŋŋ hã mɔ ni kɔɔ sane sɛɛ
lɛ, ni amɛja yɛ nilelɔ hiɛ.
10 Nyɛmɔa mitsɔsemɔ lɛ moŋ mli fe jwiɛtɛi,
kɛ nilee hu mli fe shika ŋmiiŋmi.
11Ejaakɛ nilee hi fe tɛ̃ŋlɛ̃o,
ni nɔ ko bɛ ni obaatao ni kɛ lɛ ye hegbɔ.
12Mi, nilee, mihiɛ tɛ̃;
mile nii, ni mibuɔ atɛŋ kpakpa.
13 Yehowa gbeyeishemɔ ji ohi nɔ fɔŋ.
Hewoo kɛ hetsɔ̃ɔmɔ kɛ jeŋba fɔŋ kɛ kutumpɔo wiemɔ lɛ miihi.
14Minɔ ji ŋaawoo kɛ nilee kpakpa,
miyɛ sanesɛɛkɔmɔ;
miyɛ hewalɛ hu.
15 Minɔ maŋtsɛmɛi tsɔ̃ɔ yeɔ maŋtsɛ,
ni nɔyelɔi hu woɔ jalɛ mla.
16Minɔ lumɛi tsɔ̃ɔ yeɔ lumɔ,
ni abladei yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.
17Misumɔɔ mɛi ni sumɔɔ mi;
ni mɛi ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ taoɔ mi lɛ, naa mi.
18Ninamɔ kɛ anunyam fɛɛ yɛ midɛŋ;
ninamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ shweremɔ fɛɛ yɛ midɛŋ.
19Miyibii hi fe shika, efe shika ŋmiiŋmi;
ni minibaanii lɛ hu hi fe jwiɛtɛi krɔŋŋ.
20Minyiɛɔ jalɛ gbɛ nɔ,
ni mikojoɔ jalɛ naa.
21Ni mɛi ni sumɔɔ mi lɛ, mifeɔ amɛ niiatsɛmɛi,
ni miwoɔ amɛfotroi lɛ obɔ̃bɔ̃.
22Mi Yehowa bɔ kɛje enitsumɔ shishi;
mi ji klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ yɛ eblema nitsumɔi lɛ ateŋ.
23Kɛjɛ naanɔ beebe abɔ mi klɛŋklɛŋ dani aje jeŋbɔɔ shishi.
24Be ni ŋshɔ tete po bɛ lɛ, afɔ mi momo,
be ni nuhiŋmɛi bɛ lɛ, miyɛ momo.
25Dani ashɔ̃ gɔji lɛ kɛ gɔ̃ŋkpɔi lɛ, afɔ mi momo.
26Be ni Nyɔŋmɔ nako ebɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ enɔ jwɛii kɛ je lɛ mli mlu tete lɛ,
mi lɛ, abɔ mi momo.
27 Be ni ebɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, miyɛ jɛi; be ni efo ŋshɔ he akrabatsa lɛ, miyɛ.
28Be ni eŋɔ atatui lɛ esɛŋ shi shiŋŋ yɛ ŋwɛi,
ní etsi ŋshɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ naa lɛ, miyɛ.
29 Be ni efo husu ewo ŋshɔ lɛ he,
ni nu akaku ekitã lɛ nɔ,
be ni eto shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ,
30miyɛ emasɛi akɛ ŋaawolɔ.
Ni mi ji emiishɛjelɔ daa.
Ni mimii shɛɔ mihe yɛ ehiɛ.
31 Minaa je lɛ he miishɛɛ,
minaa gbɔmɛiabii ahe tsuijurɔ.
32No hewɔ lɛ, mibii nyɛboa mi toi!
Ajɔɔ mɛi ni yeɔ mimlai anɔ lɛ!
33Nyɛboa tsɔsemɔ toi koni nyɛle nii;
ni nyɛkakwaa lɛ kwraa.
34Ajɔɔ gbɔmɔ ni boɔ mi toi ni ebuɔ migboi lɛ anaa daa
ní emɛɔ daa yɛ mishinai lɛ anaa lɛ.
35Ejaakɛ mɔ ni aaaná mi lɛ,
ena wala ni ehiɛ aaaba nyam yɛ Yehowa hiɛ.
36Shi mɔ ni nine shɛɛɛ minɔ lɛ,
eeye lɛ diɛŋtsɛ esusuma awui.
Mɛi fɛɛ ni nyɛɔ mi lɛ, amɛmiisumɔ gbele.”

english_text:
Wisdom Gives a Feast
1Wisdom has built her house
with its seven columns.
2She has prepared the meat
and set out the wine.
Her feast is ready.
3She has sent her servant women
to announce her invitation
from the highest hills:
4“Everyone who is ignorant
or foolish is invited!
5All of you are welcome
to my meat and wine.
6If you want to live,
give up your foolishness
and let understanding
guide your steps.”
True Wisdom
7Correct a worthless bragger,
and all you will get
are insults and injuries.
8Any bragger you correct
will only hate you.
But if you correct someone
who has common sense,
you will be loved.
9If you have good sense,
instruction will help you
to have even better sense.
And if you live right,
education will help you
to know even more.
10 Respect and obey the Lord!
This is the beginning
of wisdom.
To have understanding,
you must know the Holy God.
11I am Wisdom. If you follow me,
you will live a long time.
12Good sense is good for you,
but if you brag,
you hurt yourself.
A Foolish Invitation
13Stupidity is reckless,
senseless, and foolish.
14She sits in front of her house
and on the highest hills
in the town.
15She shouts to everyone
who passes by,
16“If you are stupid,
come on inside!”
And to every fool she says,
17“Stolen water tastes best,
and the food you eat in secret
tastes best of all.”
18None who listen to Stupidity
understand that her guests
are as good as dead.
translation_text:
Nilee kɛ kwashiafeemɔ
1Nilee ema etsu kɛ ehe akulashiŋi kpawo. 2 Egbe elɛɛ kooloi; efutu ewain lɛ, ni eŋmɛ ekpɔlɔ̃ lɛ hu. 3Etsu etsuji yei lɛ kɛtee maŋ lɛ mli hei grɔŋŋi fe fɛɛ lɛ, ni amɛyatsɛ mɛi akɛ, 4“Mɔ ni jwɛŋmɔ esako lɛ, ebatsɔ̃ biɛ,” ni mɔ ni bɛ jwɛŋmɔ lɛ, ekɛɔ lɛ akɛ, 5“Ba ni obaye miniyenii lɛ eko ni obanu wain ni mifutu lɛ eko. 6Kaaŋɔ ohe obɔ kwashia he, koni oyi ana wala; ni dii sanesɛɛkɔmɔ sɛɛ.”
7Mɔ ni jajeɔ hefɛoyelɔ jeŋba lɛ, enaa jɛmɔ; ni mɔ ni kãa yiwalɔ lɛ, enaa pilamɔ. 8Hɛfɛoyelɔ lɛ kɛ okã ehiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ bo; shi nilelɔ lɛ kɛji okã ehiɛ lɛ, ebaasumɔ bo. 9Tsɔ̃ɔmɔ nilelɔ nii, ni eeele nii efata nɔ ni ele momo lɛ he; tsɔ̃ɔmɔ jalɔ nii, ni enilee aaafa.
10 Yehowa gbeyeishemɔ ji nilee shishijee; ni Mɔ Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ lee ji sanesɛɛkɔmɔ.
11Ejaakɛ minɔ baatsɔ̃ ni ogbii baafa; ni owala afii lɛ asɛɛ baatsɛ. 12Kɛ ole nii lɛ, ole ohã ohe; shi kɛ hefɛoyelɔ ji bo lɛ, bo okome obaatere.
13Yoo kwashia lɛ, naawalɔ ni, ebɛ jwɛŋmɔ, ni ehiɛgbele tɔ ejwa. 14Etaa shi yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshinaa shi; etaa hei grɔŋŋi lɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli; 15ni etsɛɔ mɛi ni hoɔ ni amɛnyiɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛgbɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ. 16Ekɛɔ akɛ, “Mɔ ni jwɛŋmɔ esako lɛ, eba biɛ,” ni mɔ ni bɛ jwɛŋmɔ lɛ ekɛɔ lɛ akɛ, 17 “Nu ni ayaju lɛ, enumɔ ŋɔɔ. Ni aboloo ni ateɔ ayeɔ lɛ eyɛ akɔnɔ.” 18Mɛi ni ekpeɔ kɛyaa ewe lɛ leee akɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni yaa jɛi lɛ gboiɔ; amɛleee akɛ mɛi ni akpee kɛtee jɛi momo lɛ gbohiiaje tɔ̃ɔ amɛyɔɔ lɛ.

english_text:
Solomon's Wise Sayings
1Here are some proverbs
of Solomon:
Children with good sense
make their parents happy,
but foolish children
make them sad.
2What you gain by doing evil
won't help you at all.
Obeying God is the only way
to be saved from death.
3If you obey the Lord,
you won't go hungry;
if you are wicked,
God won't let you have
what you want.
4Laziness leads to poverty;
hard work makes you rich.
5At harvest season
it's smart to work hard,
but stupid to sleep.
6Everyone praises good people,
but evil hides behind
the words of the wicked.
7Good people are remembered
long after they are gone,
but the wicked
are soon forgotten.
8If you have good sense,
you will listen and obey;
if all you do is talk foolishly,
you will destroy yourself.
9You will be safe,
if you always do right,
but you will get caught,
if you are dishonest.
10Deceit causes trouble,
and foolish talk
will bring you to ruin.
11The words of good people
are a source of life,
but evil hides behind
the words of the wicked.
12 Hatred stirs up trouble;
love overlooks the wrongs
that others do.
13If you have good sense,
it will show when you speak.
But if you are stupid,
you will be beaten
with a stick.
14If you have good sense,
you will learn all you can,
but foolish talk
will soon destroy you.
15Great wealth can be a fortress,
but poverty
is no protection at all.
16If you live right,
the reward is a good life;
if you are evil,
all you have is sin.
17Accept correction,
and you will find life;
reject correction,
and you will miss the road.
18You can hide your hatred
by telling lies,
but you are a fool
to spread lies.
19You will say the wrong thing
if you talk too much—
so be sensible and watch
what you say.
20The words of a good person
are like pure silver,
but the thoughts
of an evil person
are almost worthless.
21Many are helped
by useful instruction,
but fools are killed
by their own stupidity.
22When the Lord blesses you
with riches,
you have nothing to regret.
23Fools enjoy doing wrong,
but anyone with good sense
enjoys acting wisely.
24What evil people dread most
will happen to them,
but good people will get
what they want most.
25Those crooks will disappear
when a storm strikes,
but God will keep safe
all who obey him.
26Having a lazy person on the job
is like a mouth full of vinegar
or smoke in your eyes.
27If you respect the Lord,
you will live longer;
if you keep doing wrong,
your life will be cut short.
28If you obey the Lord,
you will be happy,
but there is no future
for the wicked.
29The Lord protects everyone
who lives right,
but he destroys anyone
who does wrong.
30Good people will stand firm,
but the wicked will disappear
from the land.
31Honest people speak sensibly,
but deceitful liars
will be silenced.
32If you obey the Lord,
you will always know
the right thing to say.
But no one will trust you
if you tell lies.
translation_text:
Solomon Abɛi
1 Bi nilelɔ hãa etsɛ naa miishɛɛ; shi bi kwashia lɛ, ehãa enyɛ tsui yeɔ.
2Efɔŋfeemɔ mli ninamɔ lɛ ehe bɛ sɛɛnamɔ; shi jalɛ hereɔ mɔ yiwala yɛ gbele dɛŋ.
3 Yehowa hãaa hɔmɔ aye jalɔi; shi nɔ ni efɔŋfeelɔi shweɔ akɛ amɛna lɛ, etswaa yɛ amɛdɛŋ. 4 Mɔ ni nijiaŋ ŋɔɔ lɛ lɛ, ohia hiaa lɛ, shi mɔ ni nine kãaa shi lɛ etsɔ̃ɔ niiatsɛ.
5Bi ni buaa ŋmãa naa yɛ nikpamɔ be mli lɛ, bi nilelɔ ni; shi bi ni wɔɔ yɛ nikpamɔ be mli lɛ, bi ni woɔ mɔ hiɛgbele ni.
6Ajɔɔ mɛi ni feɔ jalɛ nii, shi efɔŋfeelɔi kɛ amɛdaaŋ wiemɔ haa amɛyitsoŋwalɛ nɔ.
7 Kɛ akai jalɔ lɛ, ajɔɔ lɛ; shi efɔŋfeelɔ lɛ atsiŋ egbɛi tã ajɔŋ lɛ.
8Nilelɔ kpɛlɛ̃ɔ kãmɔ; shi kwashia naafuutsɛ hiɛ kpãtãa.
9Anɔkwayelɔ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe, shi mɔ ni bɛ jeŋba lɛ, aaayoo lɛ.
10Mɔ ni bɛɔ mɔ hiŋmɛi lɛ ewoɔ bei; shi mɔ ni kɛ ekãa kãa mɔ lɛ hãa toiŋjɔlɛ baa.
11Jalɔ daaŋ wiemɔ lɛ, wala nubu ni; shi efɔŋfeelɔ daaŋ wiemɔ haa yitsoŋwalɛ nɔ.
12 Nyɛɛ teɔ bei shi; shi suɔmɔ haa tɔ̃mɔi fɛɛ anɔ.
13Niiashishinulɔ daaŋ anaa nilee yɛ; shi mɔ ni bɛ jwɛŋmɔ lɛ kpãa kã ekotosɛɛ.
14Nilelɔ tiaa nilee, shi kwashia daaŋ wiemɔ lɛ ekɛ hiɛkpãtãmɔ baa.
15Niiatsɛ nii ji emɔ̃ɔ ni wa lɛ, shi ohia kpãtãa ohiafo hiɛ.
16 Jalɛ nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo lɛ wala ni, efɔŋfeemɔ he sɛɛnamɔ ji esha.
17Mɔ ni boɔ tsɔsemɔ toi lɛ, enyiɛɔ gbɛ ni kɛ mɔ yaa wala mli nɔ; shi mɔ ni kwaa kãmɔ lɛ, eduɔ gbɛ.
18Mɔ ni kɛ nyɛɛ teɔ lɛ, amalelɔ ni; mɔ ni yeɔ mɔ he osheku lɛ, kwashia ji lɛ.
19Wiemɔ babaoo yɔɔ nɛɛ tɔ̃mɔ kpaaa yɛ mli; shi mɔ ni le enaabu mli mɔmɔ lɛ, nilelɔ ni.
20Jalɔ lilɛi lɛ, etamɔ jwiɛtɛi krɔŋŋ; shi mɔ fɔŋ jwɛŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he.
21Jalɔ naabu lɛɔ mɛi babaoo, shi kwashia lɛ, jwɛŋmɔ ni ebɛ hewɔ lɛ egboɔ.
22 Yehowa jɔɔmɔ lɛ, no feɔ mɔ niiatsɛ; shi odeŋmegbomɔ nyɛŋ ekɛ nɔ ko afata he.
23Kwashia lɛ efɔŋfeemɔ feɔ lɛ miishɛɛ, shi mɔ ni yɔɔ jwɛŋmɔ lɛ, nilee feɔ lɛ miishɛɛ.
24 Nɔ ni mɔ fɔŋ sheɔ lɛ, no nɔŋŋ baaba enɔ; shi jalɔ lɛ enine aaashɛ etaomɔnii anɔ.
25Kɛ ahum tswa pɛ, mɔ fɔŋ yi etã, shi jalɔ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛyaa naanɔ tɔ̃ɔ.
26Bɔ ni ashiŋ feɔ nyanyɔji ni lasu feɔ hiŋmɛi lɛ, nakai anihaolɔ feɔ mɛi ni tsu lɛ lɛ.
27 Yehowa gbeyeishemɔ hãa wala sɛɛ tsɛɔ; shi mɛi fɔ̃ji afii lɛ, aaafo nɔ.
28 Jalɔi ahiɛnɔkãmɔ lɛ baafee miishɛɛ; shi mɛi fɔ̃ji agbɛkwɛmɔ lɛ baafee yaka.
29Yehowa ji mɔɔ ni wa hã mɔ ni baa ejeŋ jogbaŋŋ, shi eji hiɛkpãtãmɔ hã efɔŋfeelɔ.
30 Jalɔ lɛ eeehi shi shweshweeshwe; shi mɔ fɔŋ lɛ ehiŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.
31 Jalɔi alilɛi wieɔ nilee wiemɔi; shi kutumpɔo lilɛi lɛ, aaafo ashɛ afɔ̃.
32Jalɔi anaabu le nɔ ni sa wiemɔ; shi mɔ fɔŋ wieɔ kutumpɔo wiemɔ.

english_text:
Watch What You Say and Do
1The Lord hates anyone
who cheats,
but he likes everyone
who is honest.
2Too much pride
can put you to shame.
It's wiser to be humble.
3If you do the right thing,
honesty will be your guide.
But if you are crooked,
you will be trapped
by your own dishonesty.
4When God is angry,
money won't help you.
Obeying God is the only way
to be saved from death.
5If you are truly good,
you will do right;
if you are wicked,
you will be destroyed
by your own sin.
6Honesty can keep you safe,
but if you can't be trusted,
you trap yourself.
7When the wicked die,
their hopes die with them.
8Trouble goes right past
the Lord's people
and strikes the wicked.
9Dishonest people use gossip
to destroy their neighbors;
good people are protected
by their own good sense.
10When honest people prosper
and the wicked disappear,
the whole city celebrates.
11Good people bring prosperity
to their city,
but deceitful liars
can destroy a city.
12It's stupid to say bad things
about your neighbors.
If you are sensible,
you will keep quiet.
13A gossip tells everything,
but a true friend
will keep a secret.
14 A city without wise leaders
will end up in ruin;
a city with many wise leaders
will be kept safe.
15It's a dangerous thing
to guarantee payment
for someone's debts.
Don't do it!
16A gracious woman
will be respected,
but a ruthless man
will only get rich.
17Kindness is rewarded—
but if you are cruel,
you hurt yourself.
18Meanness gets you nowhere,
but goodness is rewarded.
19Always do the right thing,
and you will live;
keep on doing wrong,
and you will die.
20The Lord hates sneaky people,
but he likes everyone
who lives right.
21You can be sure of this:
All crooks will be punished,
but God's people won't.
22A beautiful woman
who acts foolishly
is like a gold ring
on the snout of a pig.
23Good people want what is best,
but troublemakers
hope to stir up trouble.
24Sometimes you can become rich
by being generous
or poor by being greedy.
25Generosity will be rewarded:
Give a cup of water,
and you will receive
a cup of water in return.
26Charge too much for grain,
and you will be cursed;
sell it at a fair price,
and you will be praised.
27Try hard to do right,
and you will win friends;
go looking for trouble,
and you will find it.
28Trust in your wealth,
and you will be a failure,
but God's people will prosper
like healthy plants.
29Fools who cause trouble
in the family
won't inherit a thing.
They will end up as slaves
of someone with good sense.
30Live right, and you will eat
from the life-giving tree.
And if you act wisely,
others will follow.
31 If good people are rewarded
here on this earth,
all who are cruel and mean
will surely be punished.
translation_text:
1 Yehowa miihi shishiumɔ nsɛni, shi nsɛnitɛ shishiishi lɛ enaa he miishɛɛ.
2 Kɛ hewoo ba pɛ, hiɛgbele nyiɛɔ esɛɛ, shi heshibalɔ lɛ nilelɔ ni.
3 Jalɔ lɛ enɔkwayeli tsɔ̃ɔ lɛ gbɛ; shi kutumpɔfo lɛ eshishiumɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ kpãtãa ehiɛ.
4Mlifu gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ninamɔ he bɛ sɛɛnamɔ ko; shi jalɛ jieɔ mɔ kɛjɛɔ gbele dɛŋ.
5Jalɔ lɛ enɔkwayeli hãa egbɛ jaa ehãa lɛ; shi mɔ fɔŋ lɛ, enifɔjianii lɛ gbeɔ lɛ shi.
6Mɛi ni ja lɛ amɛjalɛ lɛ aajie amɛ, shi kutumpɔfoi lɛ, amɛkɔnɔ ŋɔɔ amɛ nom.
7Kɛ mɔ fɔŋ gbo lɛ; ehiɛnɔkãmɔ laajeɔ; ni mɔ ni leee Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛnɔkãmɔ lɛ efeɔ yaka.
8Ajieɔ jalɔi kɛjɛɔ haomɔ mli; shi mɛi fɔ̃ji yanyɔɔ haomɔ mli.
9Mɛi ni leee Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛdaaŋ wiemɔi fiteɔ amɛnanemɛi; shi atsɔ̃ɔ nilee nɔ, ni ajieɔ jalɔi.
10Kɛji nɔ fɛɛ nɔ tee nɔ jogbaŋŋ hã jalɔ lɛ maŋ fɛɛ nyaa; ni kɛji mɛi fɔ̃ji ahiɛ kpãtã lɛ, maŋ fɛɛ bɔɔ oshe kɛ miishɛɛ.
11 Jalɔi adɛŋ jɔɔmɔ woɔ maŋ nɔ; shi mɛi fɔ̃ji anaabu butuɔ maŋ.
12Mɔ ni gbeɔ enaanyo he guɔ lɛ, ebɛ yitsoŋ; shi mɔ ni yɔɔ jwɛŋmɔ lɛ efeɔ diŋŋ.
13Mɔ ni tãa sane kɛfoɔ shi lɛ, ejieɔ teemɔŋ saji akpo; shi mɔ ni yɔɔ anɔkwale mumɔ lɛ etsimɔɔ sane nɔ.
14He ni maŋ kudɔmɔ bɛ lɛ, maŋ gbeɔ shi; shi he ni ŋaawolɔi pii yɔɔ lɛ, maŋ feɔ shweshweeshwe.
15Mɔ ni damɔɔ gbɔ sɛɛ lɛ, eeeshwa ehe; shi mɔ ni kɛ ehe wooo mli lɛ ehi hã lɛ.
16Yoo ni hiɛ yɔɔ nyam tiuɔ woo sɛɛ, ni nuu yiwalɔ tiuɔ ninamɔ sɛɛ.
17Mɔ ni naa mɔbɔ lɛ, lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe ejurɔ efeɔ; shi mɔ ni yitsoŋ wa lɛ, lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe efɔŋ efeɔ.
18Mɔ fɔŋ naa shishiumɔ mli nyɔmɔwoo; shi mɔ ni feɔ jalɛ nii lɛ enaa anɔkwale mli nyɔmɔwoo.
19Mɔ ni fiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ jalɛ mli lɛ, eyi aaana wala; shi mɔ ni nyiɛɔ efɔŋfeemɔ sɛɛ lɛ egboɔ.
20Yehowa miihi mɛi ni hiɛ yitso fɔŋ; shi Yehowa sumɔɔ mɛi ni shwamɔ bɛ amɛjeŋba he.
21Na ole akɛ bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ efɔŋfeelɔ yeŋ ehe; shi jalɔ lɛ aaahere eyiwala.
22Yoo ni he yɔɔ fɛo ni ebɛ jeŋba kpakpa lɛ etamɔ kplotoo ni awo egugɔ mli shika ga.
23Jalɔi shweɔ nibii kpakpai sɔŋŋ; shi mɛi fɔ̃ji agbɛkwɛmɔnii lɛ mlifu ni.
24Mɔ ko yɛ ni edɛŋ kpɔɔ, shi eyaa nɔ eshwereɔ kɛtekeɔ nɔ kɛ̃, mɔ ko hu feɔ kpɛkpɛɛ, shi eyeɔ ohia moŋ.
25Mɔ ni edɛŋ kpɔɔ lɛ, enaa nii, ni mɔ ni hãa mɛi tɔrɔɔ lɛ, lɛ hu etɔɔ.
26Mɔ ni tiaa abele etoɔ lɛ, maŋ lomɔɔ lɛ; shi mɔ ni hɔ̃ɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ maŋ jɔɔ lɛ. 27Mɔ ni tiuɔ nɔ kpakpa sɛɛ kɛ hiɛdɔɔ naa nɔ kpakpa; shi mɔ ni diɔ efɔŋ sɛɛ lɛ efɔŋ blaa lɛ.
28 Mɔ ni kɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ɔ eninamɔ nɔ lɛ, etamɔ baa gbiŋ ni kpalaa; shi jalɔ aaafrɔke tamɔ baa ŋmɔŋ. 29Mɔ ni gbaa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshĩaŋbii anaa lɛ, eyeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ abɔ; ni buulu tsɔ̃ɔ tsulɔ hãa nilelɔ be fɛɛ be.
30 Jalɛ yibii lɛ wala ni; shi mla kwamɔ lɛ wala hiɛkpãtãmɔ ni. 31 Kɛji jalɔ lɛ enaa enyɔmɔwoo yɛ je nɛɛ mli lɛ, mɔ fɔŋ kɛ eshafeelɔ lɛ te amɛnyɔmɔwoo aaatamɔ tɛŋŋ?

english_text:
You Can't Hide behind Evil
1 To accept correction is wise,
to reject it is stupid.
2The Lord likes everyone
who lives right,
but he punishes everyone
who makes evil plans.
3Sin cannot offer security!
But if you live right,
you will be as secure
as a tree with deep roots.
4A helpful wife is a jewel
for her husband,
but a shameless wife
will make his bones rot.
5Good people have kind thoughts,
but you should never trust
the advice of someone evil.
6Bad advice is a deadly trap,
but good advice
is like a shield.
7Once the wicked are defeated,
they are gone forever,
but no one who obeys God
will ever be thrown down.
8Good sense is worthy of praise,
but stupidity is a curse.
9It's better to be ordinary
and have only one servant
than to think you are somebody
and starve to death.
10Good people are kind
to their animals,
but a mean person is cruel.
11Hard working farmers have more
than enough food;
daydreamers are nothing more
than stupid fools.
12An evil person tries to hide
behind evil;
good people are like trees
with deep roots.
13We trap ourselves
by telling lies,
but we stay out of trouble
by living right.
14We are rewarded or punished
for what we say and do.
15Fools think they know
what is best,
but a sensible person
listens to advice.
16Losing your temper is foolish;
ignoring an insult is smart.
17An honest person
tells the truth in court,
but a dishonest person
tells nothing but lies.
18Sharp words cut like a sword,
but words of wisdom heal.
19Truth will last forever;
lies are soon found out.
20An evil mind is deceitful,
but gentle thoughts
bring happiness.
21Good people never have trouble,
but troublemakers
have more than enough.
22The Lord hates every liar,
but he is the friend of all
who can be trusted.
23Be sensible and don't tell
everything you know—
only fools spread
foolishness everywhere.
24Work hard, and you
will be a leader;
be lazy, and you
will end up a slave.
25Worry is a heavy burden,
but a kind word
always brings cheer.
26You are better off to do right,
than to lose your way
by doing wrong.
27Anyone too lazy to cook
will starve,
but a hard worker
is a valuable treasure.
28Living right is a pathway
that leads to life
and away from death.
translation_text:
1 Mɔ ni sumɔɔ tsɔsemɔ lɛ, esumɔɔ nilee; shi mɔ ni ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ kãmɔ lɛ, kwashia ni.
2Gbɔmɔ kpakpa hiɛ baa nyam yɛ Yehowa hiɛ, shi mɔ ni toɔ yiŋ fɔŋ lɛ, ebuɔ lɛ fɔ.
3Efɔŋfeemɔ hãaa mɔ afi shi; shi jalɔi ashishi fã lɛ, anyɛŋ afã kɔkɔɔkɔ.
4 Yoo kpakpa lɛ ewu akekre ji lɛ; shi yoo ni shwieɔ ewu hiɛ shi lɛ, etamɔ wuiaŋ sasabro.
5 Jalɔ jwɛŋmɔ ja; shi mɔ fɔŋ ŋaawoo lɛ, kutumpɔo ni.
6Mɛi fɔ̃ji woɔ lá antɛo, shi jalɔi awiemɔ hereɔ mɔ yiwala.
7Abutuɔ mɛi fɔ̃ji kɛ amɛshishi fɛɛ; shi jalɔi awe maa shi shiŋŋ.
8Gbɔmɔ nilee akɛjieɔ eyi, shi mɔ ni hiɛ jwɛŋmɔ fɔŋ lɛ, abuuu lɛ.
9Ohiafo humi ni sɔ̃mɔɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe lɛ, ehi fe mɔ ni feɔ ehe niiatsɛ, tsɛbelɛ ebɛ nɔ ko.
10 Jalɔ nuɔ he ehãa eshĩa kooloo tete; shi mɔ fɔŋ musuŋtsɔlɛ tete lɛ, yiwaa ni.
11 Mɔ ni huɔ eŋmɔ lɛ eeetɔ kɛ ŋmãa pii; shi mɔ ni nyiɛɔ yakanii asɛɛ lɛ ebɛ jwɛŋmɔ.
12Mɔ fɔŋ mɔɔ ni wa lɛ hiɛ kpãtãa; shi jalɔ shishifã maa shi shiŋŋ.
13Mɔ fɔŋ diɛŋtsɛ daaŋ wiemɔ nɔŋŋ ni duɔ lɛ; shi jalɔ lɛ, ejeɔ haomɔ mli.
14 Gbɔmɔ daaŋ wiemɔ aaahã etɔ kɛ nii kpakpai, ni nɔ ni gbɔmɔ tsuɔ lɛ no he nyɔmɔ awoɔ lɛ.
15Kwashia yɔɔ nɛɛ, egbɛ ja yɛ ehiɛ; shi nilelɔ lɛ, eboɔ ŋaawoo toi.
16Kwashia yɔɔ nɛɛ anaa emlifu oya; shi nilelɔ lɛ ebuuu jɛmɔ tete.
17Mɔ ni wieɔ anɔkwale lɛ, eyeɔ anɔkwa odase; shi amale odasefonyo lɛ mɔ elakaa.
18 Mɔ ko yɛ ni ewiemɔ bambam dumɔɔ mɔ tamɔ kakla; shi nilelɔ daaŋ wiemɔ lɛ etsaa mɔ.
19Anɔkwale wiemɔ hiɔ shi kɛyaa naanɔ; shi amale lɛ, ehiɔ shi hiŋmɛitswaa kɛkɛ.
20Mɛi ni toɔ ŋaa fɔŋ lɛ amɛtsuiiaŋ eyi kɛ mɔshishiumɔ; shi mɛi ni toɔ ŋaa kpakpa lɛ amɛmii shɛɔ amɛhe.
21Haomɔ baaa jalɔ nɔ; shi mɔ fɔŋ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ haomɔi jwere enɔ.
22 Yehowa miihi amalelɔ; shi mɔ ni yeɔ anɔkwa lɛ enaa ehe miishɛɛ.
23 Nilelɔ kɛ enilee teɔ; shi kwashia jieɔ ekwashiafeemɔ kpo.
24Mɔdɛŋbɔlɔ yeɔ onukpa; shi hejɔ̃lɔ lɛ ayeɔ lɛ nyɔŋ.
25 Mligbigblimɔ dɔɔ mɔ kɔmɔɔ; shi wiemɔ kpakpa yɔɔ nɛɛ ehãa mɔ mii shɛɔ ehe.
26Jalɔ tsɔ̃ɔ enaanyo gbɛ; shi mɔ fɔŋ hãa mɛi duɔ gbɛ moŋ.
27Hejɔ̃lɔ lɛ, enine shɛɛɛ nɔ ni etaoɔ nɔ; shi mɔdɛŋbɔlɔ lɛ enaa nii ni jara wa.
28Jalɛ lɛ wala gbɛ ni; shi gbɛ gbonyo lɛ, gbele gbɛ ni.

english_text:
Wise Friends Make You Wise
1Children with good sense
accept correction
from their parents,
but stubborn children
ignore it completely.
2You will be well rewarded
for saying something kind,
but all some people think about
is how to be cruel and mean.
3 Keep what you know to yourself,
and you will be safe;
talk too much,
and you are done for.
4No matter how much you want,
laziness won't help a bit,
but hard work will reward you
with more than enough.
5A good person hates deceit,
but those who are evil
cause shame and disgrace.
6Live right, and you are safe!
But sin will destroy you.
7Some who have nothing
may pretend to be rich,
and some who have everything
may pretend to be poor.
8The rich may have
to pay a ransom,
but the poor don't have
that problem.
9The lamp of a good person
keeps on shining;
the lamp of an evil person
soon goes out.
10Too much pride causes trouble.
Be sensible and take advice.
11Money wrongly gained
will disappear bit by bit;
money earned little by little
will grow and grow.
12Not getting what you want
can break your heart,
but a wish that comes true
is a life-giving tree.
13If you reject God's teaching,
you will pay the price;
if you obey his commands,
you will be rewarded.
14Sensible instruction
is a life-giving fountain
that helps you escape
all deadly traps.
15Sound judgment is praised,
but people without good sense
are on the way to disaster.
16If you have good sense,
you will act sensibly,
but fools act like fools.
17Whoever delivers your message
can make things better
or worse for you.
18All who refuse correction
will be poor and disgraced;
all who accept correction
will be praised.
19It's a good feeling
to get what you want,
but only a stupid fool
hates to turn from evil.
20 Wise friends make you wise,
but you hurt yourself
by going around with fools.
21You are in for trouble
if you sin,
but you will be rewarded
if you live right.
22If you obey God,
you will have something
to leave your grandchildren.
If you don't obey God,
those who live right
will get what you leave.
23Even when the land of the poor
produces good crops,
they get cheated
out of what they grow.
24If you love your children,
you will correct them;
if you don't love them,
you won't correct them.
25If you live right,
you will have plenty to eat;
if you don't live right,
you will go away empty.
translation_text:
1 Bi nilelɔ boɔ etsɛ tsɔsemɔ toi; hefɛoyelɔ lɛ ebooo kãmɔ toi.
2 Gbɔmɔ kpakpa daaŋ wiemɔ aaahã etɔ kɛ nii kpakpai; shi nɔ ni kutumpɔfoi taoɔ ji basabasafeemɔ.
3 Mɔ ni mɔɔ enaabu mli lɛ, eebaa ewala yi; shi mɔ ni mɔɔɔ enaabu mli lɛ, eekpãtã lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe hiɛ.
4Hejɔ̃lɔ shweɔ nɔ ko, ni enaaa; shi mɔdɛŋbɔlɔ naa nii kɛtekeɔ nɔ.
5Jalɔ miihi amale, shi mɔ fɔŋ feɔ hiɛgbejianii, ni ebɔɔ ehe ahora.
6Jalɛ buɔ mɔ ni baa ejeŋ jogbaŋŋ he; shi eshafeemɔ butuɔ mɔ fɔŋ. 7 Mɔ ko yɛ ni feɔ ehe niiatsɛ, tsɛbelɛ ebɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko; mɔ ko hu yɛ ni feɔ ehe ohiafo, tsɛbelɛ eyɛ nii babaoo.
8Gbɔmɔ kpɔ̃mɔ nii ji enii ni eyɔɔ; shi ohiafo bɛ nɔ ko ni ekɛkpɔ̃ɔ ehe.
9 Jalɔi akane tsoɔ hɛŋŋ; shi mɛi fɔ̃ji akane lɛ aaagbo.
10 Hewoo lɛ bei kɛkɛ ekɛbaa; shi mɛi ni boɔ ŋaawoo toi lɛ, amɛleɔ nii.
11Nii ni anaa oya lɛ, ehiɛ kpãtãa; shi nii ni akpɛteɔ shi anaa lɛ eshwereɔ.
12Hiɛnɔkãmɔ ni baaa mli mra lɛ, ewoɔ mɔ tsui hela; shi kɛji nɔ ni ashweɔ lɛ na ba mli lɛ, ehãa wala.
13Mɔ ni gbeɔ wiemɔ lɛ he guɔ lɛ, ekpãtãa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe hiɛ; shi mɔ ni buɔ kitã lɛ, ebaana he sɛɛ.
14Nilelɔ nitsɔɔmɔ lɛ, wala nubu ni; ejieɔ mɔ kɛjɛɔ gbele akpa mli.
15Nilee kpakpa hãa mɔ hiɛ baa nyam; shi kutumpɔfoi agbɛ lɛ ekpãtãa amɛ nɔŋŋ amɛhiɛ.
16 Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ mli lɛ hiɛtɛ̃lɔ feɔ enii kɛ nilee; shi kwashia gbɛɔ ebuulufeemɔ eshwãa.
17Tsulɔ fɔŋ lɛ ekɛ mɛi woɔ haomɔ mli; shi bɔfo anɔkwafo lɛ ekɛ toiŋjɔlɛ baa. 18Mɔ ni ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ tsɔsemɔ lɛ ohia kɛ hiɛgbele ji enɔ; shi mɔ ni buɔ kãmɔ lɛ awoɔ ehiɛ nyam.
19Kɛji susuma na nɔ ni etaoɔ lɛ, enaa miishɛɛ; shi kwashiai sumɔɔɔ akɛ amɛjeɔ efɔŋ he.
20Mɔ ni kɛ nilelɔ nyiɛɔ lɛ, etsɔ̃ɔ nilelɔ; shi mɔ ni kɛ kwashiai bɔɔ lɛ eeena jaramɔ.
21Eshafeelɔi lɛ efɔŋ nyiɛɔ amɛsɛɛ; shi jalɔi lɛ amɛshwereɔ.
22 Gbɔmɔ kpakpa shiɔ gboshinii ehãa ebii abii; shi eshafeelɔ nii lɛ jalɔ atiaa ahãa.
23Ohiafoi ashikpɔŋ ni kã shi efolo baa niyenii pii; shi jalɛ sane ni ayeee hewɔ lɛ, nii lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛ.
24Mɔ ni emiii ni etsɔseɔ ebi kɛ kpãa lɛ, eenyɛ ebi lɛ; shi mɔ ni sumɔɔ ebi lɛ, ejeɔ mra etsɔseɔ lɛ.
25 Jalɔ yɛ nii pii ni eyeɔ etɔɔ; shi mɔ fɔŋ lɛ musuŋ hɔmɔ po yeɔ lɛ.

english_text:
Wisdom Makes Good Sense
1A woman's family
is held together
by her wisdom,
but it can be destroyed
by her foolishness.
2By living right, you show
that you respect the Lord;
by being deceitful, you show
that you despise him.
3Proud fools are punished
for their stupid talk,
but sensible talk
can save your life.
4Without the help of an ox
there can be no crop,
but with a strong ox
a big crop is possible.
5An honest witness
tells the truth;
a dishonest witness
tells nothing but lies.
6Make fun of wisdom,
and you will never find it.
But if you have understanding,
knowledge comes easily.
7Stay away from fools,
or you won't learn a thing.
8Wise people have enough sense
to find their way,
but stupid fools get lost.
9Fools don't care
if they are wrong,
but God is pleased
when people do right.
10No one else can really know
how sad or happy you are.
11The tent of a good person
stands longer than the house
of someone evil.
12 You may think you are
on the right road
and still end up dead.
13Sorrow may hide
behind laughter,
and happiness may end
in sorrow.
14You harvest what you plant,
whether good or bad.
15Don't be stupid
and believe all you hear;
be smart and know
where you are headed.
16Only a stupid fool
is never cautious—
so be extra careful
and stay out of trouble.
17Fools have quick tempers,
and no one likes you
if you can't be trusted.
18Stupidity leads to foolishness;
be smart and learn.
19The wicked will come crawling
to those who obey God.
20You have no friends
if you are poor,
but you have lots of friends
if you are rich.
21It's wrong to hate others,
but God blesses everyone
who is kind to the poor.
22It's a mistake
to make evil plans,
but you will have loyal friends
if you want to do right.
23Hard work is worthwhile,
but empty talk
will make you poor.
24Wisdom can make you rich,
but foolishness leads
to more foolishness.
25An honest witness
can save your life,
but liars can't be trusted.
26If you respect the Lord,
you and your children
have a strong fortress
27and a life-giving fountain
that keeps you safe
from deadly traps.
28Rulers of powerful nations
are held in honor;
rulers of weak nations
are nothing at all.
29It's smart to be patient,
but it's stupid
to lose your temper.
30It's healthy to be content,
but envy can eat you up.
31If you mistreat the poor,
you insult your Creator;
if you are kind to them,
you show him respect.
32In times of trouble
the wicked are destroyed,
but even at death
the innocent have faith.
33Wisdom is found in the minds
of people with good sense,
but fools don't know it.
34Doing right brings honor
to a nation,
but sin brings disgrace.
35Kings reward servants
who act wisely,
but they punish those
who act foolishly.
translation_text:
1Yoo nilelɔ kpɛɔ eshĩa; shi yoo kwashia jwaa eshĩa.
2Mɔ ni sheɔ Yehowa gbeyei lɛ efeɔ jalɛnii; shi mɔ ni gbeɔ Yehowa he guɔ lɛ efeee jalɛ nii.
3Buulu daaŋ wiemɔ gwaoɔ lɛ; shi nilelɔ daaŋ wiemɔ baa eyi.
4He ni tsina hii bɛ lɛ, niyenii bɛ jɛi; shi he ni tsinanuu hewalɔ yɔɔ lɛ jɛi ŋmãa babaoo yɔɔ.
5Odasefonyo anɔkwafo maleee; shi apasa odasefonyo maleɔ pam.
6Hefɛoyelɔ taoɔ nilee, shi enaaa; shi nilee taomɔ waaa hãaa niiashishinulɔ.
7Jee kwashia hiɛ; ejaakɛ onaŋ nilee wiemɔ yɛ edaaŋ.
8Mɔ ni yɔɔ jwɛŋmɔ ni ehiɛ tɛ̃ lɛ, ele he ni eyaa; shi kwashiai abuulufeemɔ hãa amɛduɔ gbɛ.
9Kwashia ebuuu eshafeemɔ akɛ eji nɔ fɔŋ; shi jalɔi tiuɔ eshaifaa sɛɛ.
10Tsui pɛ ni le enidɔɔnii; ni nɔ ni ji emiishɛɛ lɛ ekɛ mɔ ko mɔ ko ejaaa.
11 Mɔ fɔŋ we hiɛ aaakpãtã; shi jalɔ we aaashwere.
12 Gbɛ ko yɛ ni ja yɛ gbɔmɔ hiɛ; shi enaagbee lɛ gbele gbɛ ni.
13Ŋmɔlɔ mli tete lɛ, tsui werɛ hoɔ ehe; ni miishɛɛ naagbee lɛ ŋkɔmɔyeli baa.
14Mɔ fɔŋ lɛ eeena ejeŋba he nyɔmɔwoo; ni mɔ kpakpa lɛ, eeena enifeemɔnii kpakpa he nyɔmɔwoo.
15Mɔ ni jwɛŋmɔ mli kwɔɔɔ heɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ eyeɔ; shi hiɛtɛ̃lɔ leɔ enanenaa kwɛmɔ.
16Nilelɔ sheɔ ehe gbeyei, ni ewiɔ ehe kɛjeɔ efɔŋ he; shi kwashia feɔ kakampu ni efeɔ anyagbã.
17Mɔ ni mli etsɛɛɛ fumɔ lɛ, efeɔ kwashiaianii, ni yitsofɔŋtsɛ lɛ anyɛɔ lɛ.
18 Mɔ ni jwɛŋmɔ mli kwɔɔɔ lɛ, abuɔ lɛ buulu fai; shi nilelɔ lɛ afiɔ lɛ nilee akekre.
19Mɛi fɔ̃ji kotoɔ mɛi kpakpai, ni efɔŋfeelɔi kotoɔ jalɔi yɛ agboi anaa.
20 Ohiafo lɛ, enaanyo tete sumɔɔɔ lɛ, shi niiatsɛ lɛ, esuɔlɔi faa babaoo.
21Mɔ ni nyaŋeɔ enaanyo lɛ, eshafeelɔ ni; shi mɔ ni feɔ ohiafo ekpakpa lɛ ajɔɔ lɛ. 22Mɔ ni tsɔ̃ɔ ŋaa fɔŋ lɛ ani jeee tɔ̃ etɔ̃ɔ lɛ lo? Shi mɔ ni toɔ ŋaa kpakpa lɛ, afiɔ esɛɛ, ni ayeɔ lɛ anɔkwa.
23Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ deŋmegbomɔ mli; shi ohia kɛkɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ naabu folo wiemɔ mli.
24Nilelɔi akekre ji amɛnilee. Shi kwashiai akekre ji amɛbuulufeemɔ.
25 Anɔkwa odasefonyo lɛ ehereɔ gbɔmɛi ayiwala; shi amalelɔ lɛ mɔsɛɛgbɛtsɔ̃ɔlɔ ni.
26 Yehowa gbeyeishemɔ mli hiɛnɔkãmɔ ni mli wa yɔɔ; ni mɔ ni yɔɔ no lɛ ebii naa abobaahe.
27 Yehowa gbeyeishemɔ lɛ nuhiŋmɛi ni hãa wala ni, ejieɔ mɔ kɛjeɔ gbele tsɔnei amli.
28Maŋbii ayifalɛ ji maŋtsɛ anunyam; shi kɛji maŋbii bɛ lɛ, lumɔ hiɛkpãtãmɔ ni.
29 Mɔ ni mli fuuu mra lɛ, eyɛ niiashishinumɔ kpele; shi mɔ ni mli fuɔ mramra lɛ ejieɔ ebuulufeemɔ kpo.
30Toiŋjɔlɛ hãa gbɔmɔtso naa hewalɛ; shi awuŋayeli woɔ wuiaŋ hela.
