17Emiaa, ni etsuɔ nii kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ.
18Ekwɛɔ jogbaŋŋ dani eheɔ jarayeli nii ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he; ekane tete gbooo nyɔɔŋ.
19Ekɛ enine mɔɔ odonti mlijiemɔ tso mli, ni ekɛ enine nɔŋŋ hiɛɔ akeke lɛ ni ekɛloɔ mama.
20Egbeleɔ edɛŋ ehãa nɔnalɔ, ni ekpãa enine mli ehãa ohiafo.
21Esheee snoo gbeyei yɛ eshĩaŋbii lɛ ahewɔ, ejaakɛ shĩaŋbii lɛ fɛɛ bumɔɔ mama tsuji fɛɛfɛji.
22Eloɔ saanɔboi ehãa ehe; klala fɛɛfɛo kɛ afaseo mama ji ehe bo.
23Ayoɔ ewu yɛ koi shi, kɛji ekɛ maŋ onukpai tara shi lɛ.
24 Ekpɛɔ klala atadei kɛ hɛfiinɔ, ni ehɔ̃ɔ ehãa guɔyelɔ.
25 Ehewulamɔ mli ehewalɛ kɛ ehiɛnyam yɔɔ; ni eŋmɔɔ be ni baaba lɛ.
26Ewieɔ nilee wiemɔ, ni etsɔseɔ mɔ kɛ mlihilɛ wiemɔ.
27Ekwɛɔ eshĩaŋbii lɛ ayaa kɛ baa jogbaŋŋ, ni efeee hejɔ̃ kwraa.
28Ebii teɔ shi ni amɛjɔɔ lɛ daa; ni ewu hu kafoɔ lɛ.
29Ewu kɛɔ lɛ akɛ, “Yei pii ebɔ mɔdɛŋ moŋ, shi bo lɛ ota amɛ fɛɛ amɛnɔ!”
30 Hiɛnyam lɛ lakamɔ ni; ni hefɛo hu, yakayakanɔ ni; shi yoo ni sheɔ Yehowa gbeyei lɛ, aaakafo lɛ.
31Nyɛŋɔa eninenaa nitsumɔi lɛ eko nyɛhãa lɛ, ni hã enitsumɔi lɛ ajie eyi yɛ koii lɛ ashi.

english_text:
Nothing Makes Sense
1When the son of David was king in Jerusalem, he was known to be very wise, and he said:
2Nothing makes sense!
Everything is nonsense.
I have seen it all—
nothing makes sense!
3What is there to show
for all of our hard work
here on this earth?
4 People come, and people go,
but still the world
never changes.
5The sun comes up,
the sun goes down;
it hurries right back
to where it started from.
6The wind blows south,
the wind blows north;
round and round it blows
over and over again.
7All rivers empty into the sea,
but it never spills over;
one by one the rivers return
to their source.
8All of life is far more boring
than words could ever say.
Our eyes and our ears
are never satisfied
with what we see and hear.
9Everything that happens
has happened before;
nothing is new,
nothing under the sun.
10Someone might say,
“Here is something new!”
But it happened before,
long before we were born.
11No one who lived in the past
is remembered anymore,
and everyone yet to be born
will be forgotten too.
It Is Senseless To Be Wise
12I said these things when I lived in Jerusalem as king of Israel. 13With all my wisdom I tried to understand everything that happens here on earth. And God has made this so hard for us humans to do. 14I have seen it all, and everything is just as senseless as chasing the wind.
15If something is crooked,
it can't be made straight;
if something isn't there,
it can't be counted.
16 I said to myself, “You are by far the wisest person who has ever lived in Jerusalem. You are eager to learn, and you have learned a lot.” 17Then I decided to find out all I could about wisdom and foolishness. Soon I realized that this too was as senseless as chasing the wind.
18The more you know,
the more you hurt;
the more you understand,
the more you suffer.
translation_text:
Wala he bɛ sɛɛnamɔ
1Nilelɔ lɛ, ni ji David binuu lɛ, ni ye maŋtsɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ wiemɔi nɛ,
2“Yakanii amli yakanɔ!” Tsɔɔlɔ lɛ kɛɛ, “Yakanii amli yakanɔ! Fɛɛ lɛ yakanii ni.” 3Mɛni gbɔmɔ naa yɛ deŋme fɛɛ ni egboɔ yɛ jeŋ he? 4Yinɔ hoɔ eyaa, ni yinɔ baa; shi je lɛ yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛmiiya naanɔ. 5Hulu lɛ teɔ shi, ni hulu lɛ saa eyanyɔɔ shi, ni eyeɔ oyai kɛyaa he ni eteɔ shi yɛ lɛ. 6Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa kɛyaa wuoyigbɛ; ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa kɛbaa kooyigbɛ; kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ bɔleɔ shi kɛyaa kɛbaa. 7Faa fɛɛ faa naa yaboteɔ ŋshɔ mli, kɛ̃lɛ ŋshɔ yiii. Hei ni fai lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ, jɛi nɔŋŋ amɛhoɔ kɛyaa be fɛɛ be. 8Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ, henaagbamɔ sɔŋŋ ni; shi adesa nyɛɛɛ ekɛɛ. Etɔɔɔ hiŋmɛi kɛ nikwɛmɔ, ni etɔɔɔ toi hu kɛ ninumɔ. 9Nɔ ni eba dã lɛ, no nɔŋŋ baaba ekoŋŋ; ni nɔ ni afee dã lɛ, no nɔŋŋ abaafee ekoŋŋ; nɔ hee ko nɔ hee ko bɛ jeŋ. 10Ani nɔ ko yɛ jeŋ ni aaanyɛ akɛɛ yɛ he akɛ, “Kwɛmɔ, enɛ lɛ nɔ hee ni?” Eba jeeŋmɔ yɛ yinɔi ni etsɔ̃ wɔhiɛ lɛ amli. 11Akaiii blema nibii, ni akaiŋ nii ni baaba, ni yinɔi ni baaba lɛ kaiŋ ŋmɛnɛ kɛ wɔ mli sane.
Jajelɔ lɛ niiashikpamɔ
12Mi, Tsɔɔlɔ lɛ, miye Israel maŋtsɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm. 13Mikɛma mihiɛ akɛ mikɛ nilee baagbugbuu shi, kɛtao nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni afeɔ yɛ jeŋ; ni naa, eko fɛɛ eko lɛ yakanii ni. 14Etamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ abɔyeli. 15Nii ni ekɔ̃dɔ̃ lɛ ehiii jajemɔ trɔmɔɔ dɔŋŋ; ni nii ni eko bɛ lɛ anyɛɛɛ akane efalɛ. 16Mikɛɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mihe akɛ, “Mile nii jogbaŋŋ fe mɛi fɛɛ ni etsɔ̃ mihiɛ eye maŋtsɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm dã lɛ, ni nibii ashi ni mikpa egbele mijwɛŋmɔ kɛ nilee mli pam.” 17Mikɛma mihiɛ akɛ mibatao male nɔ ni ji nilee kɛ nɔ ni ji sɛkɛyeli kɛ nɔ ni ji kwashiafeemɔ fɛɛ. 18Ejaakɛ nilee tuutu lɛ, ekɛ naagba nyiɛ, ni mɔ ni hãa nilee faa lɛ, ehaomɔi hu faa.

english_text:
It Is Senseless To Be Selfish
1I said to myself, “Have fun and enjoy yourself!” But this didn't make sense. 2Laughing and having fun is crazy. What good does it do? 3I wanted to find out what was best for us during the short time we have on this earth. So I decided to make myself happy with wine and find out what it means to be foolish, without really being foolish myself.
4 I did some great things. I built houses and planted vineyards. 5I had flower gardens and orchards full of fruit trees. 6And I had pools where I could get water for the trees. 7 I owned slaves, and their sons and daughters became my slaves. I had more sheep and goats than anyone who had ever lived in Jerusalem. 8 Foreign rulers brought me silver, gold, and precious treasures. Men and women sang for me, and I had many wives who gave me great pleasure.
9 I was the most famous person who had ever lived in Jerusalem, and I was very wise. 10I got whatever I wanted and did whatever made me happy. But most of all, I enjoyed my work. 11Then I thought about everything I had done, including the hard work, and it was simply chasing the wind. Nothing on earth is worth the trouble.
Wisdom Comes from God
12I asked myself, “What can the next king do that I haven't done?” Then I decided to compare wisdom with foolishness and stupidity. 13And I discovered that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness. 14Wisdom is like having two good eyes; foolishness leaves you in the dark. But wise or foolish, we all end up the same.
15Finally, I said to myself, “Being wise got me nowhere! The same thing will happen to me that happens to fools. Nothing makes sense. 16Wise or foolish, we all die and are soon forgotten.” 17This made me hate life. Everything we do is painful; it's just as senseless as chasing the wind.
18Suddenly I realized that others would someday get everything I had worked for so hard, then I started hating it all. 19Who knows if those people will be sensible or stupid? Either way, they will own everything I have earned by hard work and wisdom. It doesn't make sense.
20I thought about all my hard work, and I felt depressed. 21When we use our wisdom, knowledge, and skill to get what we own, why do we have to leave it to someone who didn't work for it? This is senseless and wrong. 22What do we really gain from all of our hard work? 23 Our bodies ache during the day, and work is torture. Then at night our thoughts are troubled. It just doesn't make sense.
24 The best thing we can do is to enjoy eating, drinking, and working. I believe these are God's gifts to us, 25and no one enjoys eating and living more than I do. 26 If we please God, he will make us wise, understanding, and happy. But if we sin, God will make us struggle for a living, then he will give all we own to someone who pleases him. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_text:
1Mikɛɛ mihe akɛ, “Agbɛnɛ maka nɔ ni ji mliflimɔ makwɛ; shwɛ oyinɔ!” Shi naa, enɛ hu lɛ yakanii ni. 2Mikɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ he akɛ, “Sɛkɛyeli ni”; ni mikɛɛ yɛ miishɛɛ hu he akɛ, “Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he?” 3Mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ tao mli mikwɛ akɛ wain baahã mana miishɛɛ lo? Asaŋ mikɛ jwɛŋmɔ kɛ nilee tao mli bɔ ni mafee mamɔ buulufeemɔ koŋ mli kɛdamɔ shi kɛyashi beyinɔ ni mana nɔ ni hi hã gbɔmɛi abii akɛ amɛfee yɛ jeŋ, yɛ amɛwala be kukuoo lɛ mli.
4Mitsu nitsumɔi wuji: mimamɔ shĩai mihã mi diɛŋtsɛ mihe, ni mifee waintromi hu mihã mihe; 5mifee abɔi kɛ tromi mihã mi diɛŋtsɛ mihe, ni mitɛo aduawa tsei srɔtoi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ mli; 6mije bukoi ni akɛ amɛmli nu shwieɔ tsei ni atɛo lɛ anɔ; 7mihe hii nyɔji kɛ yei nyɔji fɛɛ, ni afɔfɔɔ nyɔji hu ahã mi yɛ miwe lɛ mli; mina toi kɛ tsinai fe mɛi fɛɛ ni etsɔ̃ mihiɛ amɛhi Yerusalɛm. 8Mibua shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi kɛ mishishi maŋtsɛmɛi kɛ shikpɔji anɔ bii adɛŋ jwetri naa mihã mihe. Mina hii lalɔi kɛ yei lalɔi fɛɛ ni laa kɛjieɔ mihiɛtserɛ; ni miyɛ nuu tsuinaa nii ni ji shieŋnyɛmɛi babaoo hu.
9Mibatsɔ̃ gbɔmɔ wulu, ni migbojee bakwɔ fe mɛi fɛɛ ni etsɔ̃ mihiɛ amɛhi Yerusalɛm dã lɛ, ni nilee hu ebɔɔɔ mi. 10Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni fee mi akɔnɔ lɛ, mikamaaa mihe. Mitsiii mihe naa yɛ miishɛɛ ko miishɛɛ ko gbɛfaŋ, ejaakɛ mina nibii fɛɛ ni migbo amɛhe deŋme lɛ ahe miishɛɛ. Deŋme ni migbo lɛ he sɛɛnamɔ ji no. 11Shi be ni misusu nibii fɛɛ ni mikɛ minine etsu, kɛ tɔlɛ ni etɔ mi kɛtsu nii lɛ hu fɛɛ he lɛ, nɔ ni mina ji akɛ fɛɛ lɛ yakanii ni, ni etamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ abɔyeli. Anɔkwa, nɔ ko kwraa bɛ ni adesa naa he sɛɛ yɛ jeŋ.
12Ejaakɛ mɛni po maŋtsɛ ni ebaye maŋtsɛ kroko sɛɛ baanyɛ efee? Nɔ ni mɛi ni etsɔ̃ ehiɛ lɛ fee lɛ, no nɔŋŋ pɛ lɛ hu ebaafee.
No hewɔ lɛ, agbɛnɛ, miku sɛɛ misusu nilee kɛ sɛkɛyeli kɛ kwashiafeemɔ he. 13Mina akɛ nilee hi fe kwashiafeemɔ, tamɔ bɔ ni la hi fe duŋ lɛ, 14ni nilelɔ lɛ enyiɛɔ kɛ hiɛshikãmɔ; shi kwashia lɛ, enyiɛɔ duŋduŋ tamɔ mɔ ni nyiɛ duŋ mli; shi kɛ̃lɛ amɛ fɛɛ amɛshɛɛ mli ekome. 15Kɛkɛ ni mikɛɛ mihe akɛ, “Sane koome ni baa kwashia nɔ lɛ, no nɔŋŋ ni baaba minɔ. Nɛgbɛ mɔ mikɛ nilee pii nɛɛ yaa?” Mikɛɛ mihe akɛ, “Enɛ hu lɛ yakanii ni.” 16Ejaakɛ bɔ ni akaiii kwashia kɛyaa naanɔ lɛ, nakai akaiii nilelɔ bei fɛɛ, ejaakɛ be ni wɔsɛɛ ko baashɛ lɛ hiɛ ekpa amɛ fɛɛ amɛnɔ jeeŋmɔ. Bɔ ni nilelɔ gboɔ lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ kwashia hu gboɔ. 17No hewɔ lɛ, jeŋshihilɛ je mitsine, ejaakɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni afeɔ yɛ jeŋ hao mi, ejaakɛ fɛɛ lɛ yakanii ni, ni etamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ abɔyeli.
18Deŋme fɛɛ ni migbo yɛ jeŋ je mitsine, ejaakɛ mina akɛ mibashi fɛɛ kwa mibahã mɔ ni baaba ebaye misɛɛ. 19Gbɔmɔ nɛɛ baafee nilelɔ jio, kwashia ni jio, namɔ le? Ni kɛ̃lɛ nii fɛɛ ni migbo he deŋme ni mina yɛ nilee naa, yɛ je nɛɛ mli lɛ, lɛ ebaaye. Enɛ hu yakanii ni. 20No hewɔ lɛ, minijiaŋ je wui akɛ migbo deŋme kɛtsu nii nɛkɛ yɛ je nɛɛ mli; 21ejaakɛ bei komɛi lɛ mɔ ko ni egbo deŋme kɛ nilee kɛ jwɛŋmɔ kɛ ŋaa shiɔ egboshinii lɛ ehãa mɔ ni gboko nii lɛ he deŋme ko, ni ebayeɔ. Enɛ hu lɛ yakanii kɛ nɔ fɔŋ kpele ni. 22Mɛni ji nɔ ni gbɔmɔ naa yɛ deŋme ni egboɔ kɛ etɔlɛ he yɛ je nɛɛ mli? 23Ejaakɛ ewala gbii fɛɛ lɛ piŋmɔ ni, ni enitsumɔ fɛɛ lɛ mlifu sɔŋŋ tɔ, ni nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ fɛɛ tete ewɔɔɔ kɛ jwɛŋmɔ sɔŋŋ. Enɛ hu yakanii ni. 24Nɔ ko bɛ hã gbɔmɔ adesa fe akɛ nii ni egbo he deŋme ni ena lɛ, eye eko, ni enu eko, ni ena ehe miishɛɛ. Enɛ hu mina akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ dɛŋ ejɛ, 25ejaakɛ namɔ ji mɔ ni baanyɛ eye nii aloo ena miishɛɛ ko kɛji Nyɔŋmɔ nine bɛ mli? 26Ejaakɛ gbɔmɔ ni feɔ nɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ sumɔɔ lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ duroɔ lɛ nilee kɛ jwɛŋmɔ kɛ miishɛɛ fɛɛ; shi eshafeelɔ lɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hãa ebuaa, ni etĩaa nii anaa emaa shi, shi Nyɔŋmɔ kɛhãa mɔ ni feɔ esuɔmɔnaanii lɛ. Enɛ hu lɛ yakanii ni, ni etamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ abɔyeli.

english_text:
Everything Has Its Time
1Everything on earth
has its own time
and its own season.
2There is a time
for birth and death,
planting and reaping,
3for killing and healing,
destroying and building,
4for crying and laughing,
weeping and dancing,
5for throwing stones
and gathering stones,
embracing and parting.
6There is a time
for finding and losing,
keeping and giving,
7for tearing and sewing,
listening and speaking.
8There is also a time
for love and hate,
for war and peace.
What God Has Given Us To Do
9What do we gain by all our hard work? 10I have seen what difficult things God demands of us. 11God makes everything happen at the right time. Yet none of us can ever fully understand all he has done, and he puts questions in our minds about the past and the future. 12I know the best thing we can do is to always enjoy life, 13because God's gift to us is the happiness we get from our food and drink and from the work we do. 14Everything God has done will last forever; nothing he does can ever be changed. God has done all this, so that we will worship him.
15Everything that happens
has happened before,
and all that will be
has already been—
God does everything
over and over again.
The Future Is Known Only to God
16Everywhere on earth I saw violence and injustice instead of fairness and justice. 17So I told myself that God has set a time and a place for everything. He will judge everyone, both the wicked and the good. 18I know God is testing us to show us that we are merely animals. 19Like animals we breathe and die, and we are no better off than they are. It just doesn't make sense. 20All living creatures go to the same place. We are made from earth, and we return to earth. 21Who really knows if our spirits go up and the spirits of animals go down into the earth? 22We were meant to enjoy our work, and that's the best thing we can do. We can never know the future.

1I looked again and saw people being mistreated everywhere on earth. They were crying, but no one was there to offer comfort, and those who mistreated them were powerful. 2I said to myself, “The dead are better off than the living. 3But those who have never been born are better off than anyone else, because they have never seen the terrible things that happen on this earth.”
4Then I realized that we work and do wonderful things just because we are jealous of others. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
5Fools will fold their hands
and starve to death.
6Yet a very little food
eaten in peace
is better than twice as much
earned from overwork
and chasing the wind.
7Once again I saw that nothing on earth makes sense. 8For example, some people don't have friends or family. But they are never satisfied with what they own, and they never stop working to get more. They should ask themselves, “Why am I always working to have more? Who will get what I leave behind?” What a senseless and miserable life!
It Is Better To Have a Friend
9You are better having a friend than to be all alone, because then you will get more enjoyment out of what you earn. 10If you fall, your friend can help you up. But if you fall without having a friend nearby, you are really in trouble. 11If you sleep alone, you won't have anyone to keep you warm on a cold night. 12Someone might be able to beat up one of you, but not both of you. As the saying goes, “A rope made from three strands of cord is hard to break.”
13You may be poor and young, but if you are wise, you are better off than a foolish old king who won't listen to advice. 14Even if you were not born into the royal family and have been a prisoner and poor, you can still be king. 15I once saw everyone in the world follow a young leader who came to power after the king was gone. 16His followers could not even be counted. But years from now, no one will praise him—this makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_text:
1Asaŋ mikwɛ yiwalɛ nibii ni afeɔ yɛ je lɛ mli lɛ. Naa yaafonui jwere mɛi ni awaa amɛ yi lɛ ahiɛ, shi amɛbɛ mɔ ko ni shɛjeɔ amɛmii. Mɛi ni waa amɛ yi lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ko yɛ amɛsɛɛ, ni mɔ ko bɛ ni shɛjeɔ amɛmii. 2No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni misusu ji akɛ mɛi ni egboi momo lɛ anɔ hi fe mɛi ni yɔɔ wala mli lolo nɛɛ. 3Shi mɔ ni nɔ hi fe mɛi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ anɔ lɛ ji mɔ ni anako afɔ lɛ, ni ebanako nibii fɔ̃ji ni afeɔ yɛ jeŋ lɛ.
4Agbɛnɛ miyoo akɛ deŋme ni gbɔmɔ gboɔ fɛɛ, kɛ tɔlɛ ni etɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, fɛɛ jɛɔ ehiɛ ni kɔ̃ɔ enaanyo nɔ. Enɛ hu yakanii ni, ni etamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ abɔyeli. 5Kwashia kotaa eniji ekɛtaa shi, ni hɔmɔ gbeɔ lɛ. 6Dɛ̃kɔkɔ kome mli nii ni toiŋjɔlɛ yɛ mli lɛ, ehi fe niji enyɔ ni akɛmiigbo yaka deŋme tamɔ ayeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ abɔ.
7Asaŋ mina yakanii ko yɛ jeŋ. 8No ji mɔ ko ni ebɛ mɔ ko mɔ ko, ebɛ bi lɛ, ebɛ nyɛminuu hu, kɛ̃lɛ ekpaaa deŋmegbomɔ, ni nii ni ena hu esaaa ehiɛ. Gbɔmɔ nɛɛ biko ehe dã akɛ, “Kwɛ, namɔ kwraa hewɔ ni migboɔ deŋme, ni mikamaa mihe jeŋ ŋɔɔmɔ nɛɛ?” Enɛ hu yakanii ni, kɛ awerɛho sane fɛɛ.
9Mɛi enyɔ hi fe mɔ kome, ejaakɛ mɛi enyɔ naa deŋme ni amɛgboɔ lɛ he sɛɛ. 10Ejaakɛ kɛji shi amɛgbee lɛ, amɛteŋ mɔ kome kɛ̃ aaawo enaanyo nɔ. Shi mɔ ni ekoome lɛ, kpoo hã lɛ ejaakɛ kɛji egbee shi lɛ, mɔ ko bɛ ni aaawo enɔ. 11Asaŋ kɛji mɛi enyɔ kamɔ shi lɛ, amɛhe dɔɔ la; shi te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni mɔ ni ekome lɛ ehe aaadɔ la hu? 12Kɛji mɔ ko tua mɔ ni ekome lɛ, mɔ lɛ nine nyɛɔ etsɔ̃ɔ enɔ; shi kɛji mɛi enyɔ ni lɛ, amɛbaaye mɔ ni tua amɛ lɛ nɔ. Kpãa ni akɛ kpãa blawai etɛ̃ elo lɛ emlitsemɔ wa.
13Oblanyo ohiafo nilelɔ hi fe maŋtsɛ nuumo kwashia ni ekpɛlɛ̃ɛɛ ŋaawoo dɔŋŋ, 14tsɛbelɛ gboklɛfoiatsuŋ ejɛ ni ebaye maŋtsɛ lɛ, aloo afɔ lɛ ohiafo yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ emaŋtsɛyeli lɛ mli. 15Misusu gbɔmɛi hiɛkãalɔi fɛɛ ni yaa baa yɛ jeŋ kɛ oblanyo hu, mɔ ni baaba ebaye maŋtsɛ sɛɛ lɛ he. 16Gbɔmɛi nɛɛ ayi fa bɔ ni anyɛŋ amɛ akane, shi maŋtsɛ ta amɛ fɛɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ̃lɛ yinɔ ni baaba lɛ nyaŋ maŋtsɛ lɛ he. Anɔkwa, enɛ hu lɛ yakanii ni, ni etamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ abɔyeli.

english_text:
Be Careful How You Worship
1Be careful what you do when you enter the house of God. Fools go there to offer sacrifices, because all they do is sin. But it's best just to listen when you go to worship. 2Don't talk before you think or make promises to God without thinking them through. God is in heaven, and you are on earth, so don't talk too much. 3If you keep thinking about something, you will dream about it. If you talk too much, you will say the wrong thing.
4 God doesn't like fools. So don't be slow to keep your promises to God. 5It's better not to make a promise at all than to make one and not keep it. 6Don't let your mouth get you in trouble! And don't say to the worship leader, “I didn't mean what I said.” God can destroy everything you have worked for, so don't say something that makes God angry.
7Respect and obey God! Daydreaming leads to a lot of senseless talk.
8Don't be surprised if the poor of your country are abused, and injustice takes the place of justice. After all, the lower officials must do what the higher ones order them to do. 9And since the king is the highest official, he benefits most from the taxes paid on the land.
10If you love money and wealth, you will never be satisfied with what you have. This doesn't make a bit of sense. 11The more you have, the more everyone expects from you. Your money won't do you any good—others will just spend it for you. 12If you have to work hard for a living, you can rest well at night, even if you don't have much to eat. But if you are rich, you can't even sleep.
13I have seen something terribly unfair. People get rich, but it does them no good. 14Suddenly they lose everything in a bad business deal, then have nothing to leave for their children. 15 They came into this world naked, and when they die, they will be just as naked. They can't take anything with them, and they won't have anything to show for all their work. 16That's terribly unfair. They leave the world just as they came. They gained nothing from running after the wind. 17Besides all this, they are always gloomy at mealtime, and they are troubled, sick, and bitter.
18What is the best thing to do in the short life God has given us? I think we should enjoy eating, drinking, and working hard. This is what God intends for us to do. 19Suppose you are very rich and able to enjoy everything you own. Then go ahead and enjoy working hard—this is God's gift to you. 20God will keep you so happy that you won't have time to worry about each day.
translation_text:
Kaawo shi oya
1Kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji ooya Nyɔŋmɔ We lɛ. Kɛji ooya jɛi oyabo wiemɔ toi lɛ, ehi fe oooya jɛi oyashã afɔle ni kwashiai yaa amɛyashãa lɛ; ejaakɛ amɛleee akɛ amɛmiifee nɔ fɔŋ. 2Kaahã onaa miifee blɛblɛ, ni kaahã otsui miihã osha ohe owie yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛ. Ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ ŋwɛi eyɔɔ, ni bo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oyɔɔ; no hewɔ lɛ, kaahã owiemɔ miifa. 3Ejaakɛ kɛji odi lamɔ sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ nitsumɔ pii shwieɔ onɔ; wiemɔ pii akɛyoɔ kwashia. 4Kɛ owo Nyɔŋmɔ shi lɛ, kaahã shiwoo lɛ nɔyeli sɛɛ miitsɛ, ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ bɛ kwashiai ahe tsui; shi ni owo lɛ ye nɔ. 5Faŋ nɔ ni owooo shi kwraa, fe nɔ ni owo shi ni oyeee nɔ. 6Kaaŋmɛ onaabu gbɛ ni ehã ofee esha; ni kaakɛɛ yɛ bɔfo lɛ hiɛ akɛ onaa ni etɛ shi. Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ mli afu yɛ owiemɔ hewɔ ni efite oninenaa nitsumɔ lɛ? 7Kɛji lamɔi fa pɛ, wiemɔi hu efa; shi bo lɛ oshe Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei.
Wala lɛ yaka nɔ ko ni
8Kɛji ona akɛ aawa ohiafo ko yi, asaŋ aatsɔ̃ jalɛ saneyeli hiɛ aaabu shi, ni afeee nɔ ni ja yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ, kaahã enɛ miifee bo naakpɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsulɔnukpa lɛ, tsulɔnukpa ko ni fe lɛ yɛ ni kwɛɔ enɔ, ni tsulɔi krokomɛi hu yɛ lolo ni amɛgbɛnaa kwɔlɔ fe klɛŋklɛŋ tsulɔi lɛ.
9Shi enɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ maŋtsɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔji yɔɔ nɔ nɔ.
10Mɔ ni sumɔɔ shika lɛ, etɔɔɔ shika; ni mɔ ni sumɔɔ ninamɔ etɔɔɔ ninamɔ. Enɛ hu lɛ yakanii ni. 11Kɛ ninamɔ fa lɛ, naabui ni yeɔ nii lɛ hu faa. Mɛɛ sɛɛ nɔtsɛ lɛ naa? Sɛɛ ni enaa ji akɛ kɛji ekɛ ehiŋmɛi kwɛ enii lɛ, enaa miishɛɛ. 12Apaafonyo na nii babaoo eye jio, fioo ena eye jio, ewɔɔ kɛ miishɛɛ; shi niiatsɛ nii ni ena lɛ he jwɛŋmɔ hãaa ena wɔ ewɔ.
13Awerɛho sane ko ni mina yɛ jeŋ nɛ: gbɔmɔ adesa tiaa nii naa ehãa ehe, shi no nɔŋŋ moŋ ni yeɔ lɛ awui. 14Nii nɛɛ fɛɛ hiɛ kpãtãa kɛji akɛtee jarayeli. Gbɔmɔ nɛɛ yɛ bi nɛ, shi nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ edɛŋ ni ebaashi ehã ebi lɛ. 15Bɔ ni ejɛ enyɛ musuŋ eba kɛ ehe yayai lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ eeeku esɛɛ kɛaatee bɔ ni eba lɛ, ni ekɔŋ edeŋmegbomɔ lɛ mli nɔ ko nɔ ko kɛyaŋ. 16Awerɛho sane nɛ: bɔ pɛ ni eba lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ eeetee. Mɛɛ sɛɛ ena fe akɛ egbo deŋme folo; 17ni ewala gbii fɛɛ amli lɛ, ehi duŋ kɛ awerɛho kɛ mlila kpele kɛ hela mli, ni jeŋshihilɛ je etsine?
18Naa, nɔ ni mikpa shi mina akɛ ehi, ni esa hã gbɔmɔ adesa feemɔ ji akɛ eye, ni enu; ni deŋme fɛɛ ni egboɔ yɛ ewala kukuoo ni Nyɔŋmɔ ehã lɛ yɛ je nɛɛ mli lɛ, eye emli ŋɔɔmɔ koni ena miishɛɛ, ejaakɛ no ji egbɛfaŋ nɔ. 19Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ hu ni Nyɔŋmɔ ehã ena shika kɛ nii kɛ hewalɛ koni eye eninamɔ lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ, emɔ egbɛfaŋ nɔ lɛ mli, ni emii ashɛ edeŋmegbomɔ he. Nyɔŋmɔ dromɔ nikeenii ni. 20Ejaakɛ esusuŋ ewala gbii lɛ ahe tsɔ̃, ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ehã etsui eyi obɔ kɛ miishɛɛ.

english_text:
Don't Depend on Wealth
1There is something else terribly unfair, and it troubles everyone on earth. 2God may give you everything you want—money, property, and wealth. Then God doesn't let you enjoy it, and someone you don't even know gets it all. That's senseless and terribly unfair!
3You may live a long time and have a hundred children. But a child born dead is better off than you, unless you enjoy life and have a decent burial. 4-5That child will never live to see the sun or to have a name, and it will go straight to the world of darkness. But it will still find more rest than you, 6even if you live two thousand years and don't enjoy life. As you know, we all end up in the same place.
7We struggle just to have enough to eat, but we are never satisfied. 8We may be sensible, yet we are no better off than a fool. And if we are poor, it still doesn't do us any good to try to live right. 9It's better to enjoy what we have than to always want something else, because that makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
10Everything that happens was decided long ago. We humans know what we are like, and we can't argue with God, because he is too strong for us. 11The more we talk, the less sense we make, so what good does it do to talk? 12Life is short and meaningless, and it fades away like a shadow. Who knows what is best for us? Who knows what will happen after we are gone?
translation_text:
1Nɔ fɔŋ ko yɛ ni mina yɛ jeŋ ni ebu yɛ gbɔmɛi ateŋ. 2Mɔ ko hiɔ shi, ni Nyɔŋmɔ hãa enaa shika kɛ nii kɛ anunyam bɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ ni eshweɔ ni enaaa; shi kɛ̃lɛ edurooo lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛye eninamɔ lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ; shi moŋ mɔkpɔŋ ji mɔ ni bayeɔ eninamɔ lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ. Enɛ lɛ yakanii ni, ni eji hejaramɔ sane kpele. 3Kɛji mɔ ko fɔ bii oha, ni ewala sɛɛ tsɛ, ni eye afii babaoo, shi eyeee jeŋ nibii kpakpai amli ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ eko, ni enaaa fuu kpakpa hu lɛ, miikɛɛ akɛ abifao ni ashrake tete nɔ hi fe lɛ. 4Sharakemɔ bi lɛ yaka eba jeŋ lɛ; enyiɛ duŋ mli kɛba, ni duŋ lɛ mli nɔŋŋ etsɔ̃ɔ kɛyaa, ni hiɛ jeɔ enɔ. 5Enaaa hulu lɛ, eleee nɔ ko nɔ ko hu; kɛ̃lɛ lɛ moŋ enaa hejɔlɛ fe mɔ ni 6aaaye afii akpei enyɔ tete, shi eyeee jeŋ nibii kpakpai lɛ amli ŋɔɔmɔ ko. Ani jeee he koome mɛi enyɔ nɛɛ fɛɛ yaa lo?
7Gbɔmɔ tɔlɛ kɛ deŋme fɛɛ lɛ, emusu kɛkɛ hewɔ; kɛ̃lɛ gbɔmɔ leee mitɔ. 8Mɛni ji nɔ ni nilelɔ kɛfe kwashia? Ni mɛni ohiafo naa kɛji ele bɔ ni ahiɛɔ he ahãa yɛ mɛi ahiɛ? 9Nɔ ni onaa kɛ ohiŋmɛii lɛ, ehi fe nɔ ni oshweɔ. Enɛ hu lɛ yakanii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abɔyeli ni.
10Nɔ ni eba dã lɛ, awo lɛ gbɛi momo; ni ale nɔ ni ji gbɔmɔ, asaŋ akɛ gbɔmɔ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe lɛ afu daa. 11Wiemɔ pii lɛ ekɛ yakanii pii nyiɛ; ni mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ mli hã gbɔmɔ? 12Namɔ le nɔ ni hi hã gbɔmɔ adesa ni eyɔɔ yaka wala be kukuoo nɛɛ ni hoɔ tamɔ lamɔ nɛɛ mli? Ni namɔ baanyɛ egba gbɔmɔ nɔ ni baaba jeŋ yɛ egbele sɛɛ?

english_text:
The Best in Life
1 A good reputation
at the time of death
is better than loving care
at the time of birth.
2It's better to go to a funeral
than to attend a feast;
funerals remind us
that we all must die.
3Choose sorrow over laughter
because a sad face
may hide a happy heart.
4A sensible person mourns,
but fools always laugh.
5Correction from someone wise
is better by far
than praise from fools.
6Foolish laughter is stupid.
It sounds like thorns
crackling in a fire.
7Corruption makes fools
of sensible people,
and bribes can ruin you.
8Something completed is better
than something just begun;
patience is better
than too much pride.
9 Only fools get angry quickly
and hold a grudge.
10It isn't wise to ask,
“Why is everything worse
than it used to be?”
11Having wisdom is better
than an inheritance.
12Wisdom will protect you
just like money;
knowledge with good sense
will lead you to life.
13Think of what God has done!
If God makes something crooked,
can you make it straight?
14When times are good,
you should be cheerful;
when times are bad,
think about what it means.
God makes them both
to keep us from knowing
what will happen next.
Some of Life's Questions
15I have seen everything during this senseless life of mine. I have seen good citizens die for doing the right thing, while criminals live and prosper. 16So don't destroy yourself by being too good or acting too smart! 17Don't die before your time by being too evil or acting like a fool. 18Keep to the middle of the road. You can do this if you truly respect God.
19Wisdom will make you stronger than the ten most powerful leaders in your city.
20No one in this world always does right.
21Don't listen to everything that everyone says, or you might hear your servant cursing you. 22Haven't you cursed many others?
23I told myself that I would be smart and try to understand all this, but it was too much for me. 24The truth is beyond us. It's far too deep. 25So I decided to learn everything I could and become wise enough to discover what life is all about. At the same time, I wanted to understand why it's stupid and senseless to be an evil fool.
26Here is what I discovered: A bad woman is worse than death. She is a trap, reaching out with body and soul to catch you. But if you obey God, you can escape. If you don't obey, you are done for. 27With all my wisdom I have tried to find out how everything fits together, 28but so far I have not been able to. I do know there is one good man in a thousand, but never have I found a good woman. 29I did learn one thing: We were completely honest when God created us, but now we have twisted minds.
translation_text:
Wala he susumɔi
1Gbɛi kpakpa hi fe mu ni jara wa, ni gbele gbi hi fe fɔmɔ gbi.
2Kɛji otee shĩa ni aafee yara yɛ mli lɛ, ehi fe nɔ ni otee shĩa ni aŋmɛ okplɔ̃ yɛ jɛi, ejaakɛ esa akɛ gbɔmɔ hiɛ ahi nɔ akɛ gbɔmɛi fɛɛ anaagbee ji gbele.
3Awerɛho hi fe ŋmɔlɔ; ejaakɛ awerɛho baahã ohiɛ afee mɔbɔmɔbɔ moŋ nɛ, shi ehãa jwɛŋmɔ mli gbeleɔ.
4He ni nilelɔ tsui kãa ji shĩa ni yara yɔɔ mli; shi he ni kwashia tsui kãa ji shĩa ni mliflimɔ yɔɔ mli.
5Ehi akɛ ooonu ni nilelɔi miikã bo, fe nɔ ni ooonu ni kwashiai miila kɛmiikafo bo.
6Ejaakɛ kwashiai aŋmɔlɔ lɛ, etamɔ ŋmei fɛlɛmɔ yɛ kukwɛi shishi la mli. No hu yakanii ni.
7Niseniianii hãa nilelɔ tsɔ̃ɔ kwashia, ni nyɔɔŋnihamɔ fiteɔ gbɔmɔ jwɛŋmɔ.
8Nɔ ko naagbee hi fe eshishijee; ni tsuishitoo mumɔ hi fe hewoo mumɔ.
9Kaahã omli fu oya, ejaakɛ kwashiai amiinaa ji he ni mlifu yɔɔ.
10Kaakɛɛ akɛ, “Mɛɛba nyɛsɛɛ ŋɔɔ fe ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ?” Ejaakɛ jeee nilee mli obaajɛ obi nɛkɛ sane.
11Nilee ni gboshinii fata he he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ hã hiɛkãalɔi; 12ejaakɛ nilee baa mɔ yi tamɔ shika baa mɔ yi lɛ, shi nɔ ni nilee kɛfe shika ji akɛ nilee baa mɔ ni yɔɔ eko yi.
13Susumɔ Nyɔŋmɔ nitsumɔ he. Namɔ baanyɛ ejaje nɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ diɛŋtsɛ ekɔ̃dɔ̃ lɛ. 14Be ni nibii eshwere lɛ, nya; ni kɛji joomɔ be ba lɛ susumɔ he; ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ dɛŋ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ jɛ, bɔ ni afee ni gbɔmɔ adesa akanyɛ ele nɔ ni baaba wɔsɛɛ.
15Mina mihiɛ nii yɛ yaka je nɛɛ mli. Jalɔ gboɔ yɛ ejalɛ nifeemɔ mli, ni gbɔmɔ fɔŋ lɛ moŋ wala sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ efɔŋ ni efeɔ mli. 16Kaafee ohe jalɔ tuutu; asaŋ kaafee ohe nilelɔ tuutu. Mɛɛba oookpãtã bo diɛŋtsɛ ohiɛ? 17Kaafee ohe yiwalɔ tuutu, ni asaŋ kaafee kwashia. Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ogbo be ni ogbele be shɛko. 18Ehi akɛ omɔɔ enɛ mli, ni kaajie onine yɛ he; ejaakɛ mɔ ni sheɔ Nyɔŋmɔ lɛ ebaaje fɛɛ mli shweshweeshwe.
19Nilee hãa nilelɔ kome naa hewalɛ ni fe nɔyelɔi nyɔŋma ahewalɛ yɛ maŋ.
20Anɔkwa, adesa ko bɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ ni ekpakpa sɔŋŋ kɛkɛ efeɔ, ni efeee esha.
21Kaadi gbɔmɛi anaa wiemɔi fɛɛ asɛɛ, kɛjeee nakai lɛ ooonu ni otsulɔ miilomɔ bo; 22ole yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oyitsoŋ akɛ bo hu olomɔ mɛi komɛi shii abɔ pɛŋ.
23Mikɛ nilee eka enɛɛmɛi fɛɛ mikwɛ. Mitswa fai shi akɛ male nii; shi miyanyɛɛɛ. 24Namɔ baanyɛ ena? Esɛɛ jɛkɛ, ni emli kwɔ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ. 25Mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ fɔ̃ nɔ akɛ mibagbɛlɛ shi matao nilee kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ mli. Mitao akɛ male yitsoŋwalɛ ni yɔɔ buulufeemɔ mli, kɛ bɔ ni buulufeemɔ lɛ sɛkɛyeli ni.
26Mina nɔ ko ni joɔ fe gbele tete; no ji yoo. Etsui mli eyi kɛ tsɔnei kɛ yai ni akɛduɔ mɔ, ni eniji lɛ kɔsɔŋkɔsɔ ni fimɔɔ mɔ ni. Mɔ ni sheɔ Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei jeɔ yoo akpa mli; shi eshafeelɔ lɛ yoo duɔ lɛ. 27Tsɔɔlɔ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, “Naa, mihiɛ taomɔ mli ekomekome lɛ, nɔ ni mina nɛ. 28Nibii ni mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ etao aahu lɛ, minako. Mɛi akpe mli lɛ, mina nuu kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hiɛsɔɔ; shi minaaa yoo kome nɛkɛ yɛ amɛteŋ. 29Naa, nɔ ni kɛkɛ ni mina ji akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ bɔ gbɔmɔ adesa koni ehi shi krɔŋŋ; shi gbɔmɔ adesa ni eto ŋai srɔtoi.

english_text:
1Who is smart enough
to explain everything?
Wisdom makes you cheerful
and gives you a smile.
Obey the King
2If you promised God that you would be loyal to the king, I advise you to keep that promise. 3Don't quickly oppose the king or argue when he has already made up his mind. 4The king's word is law. No one can ask him, “Why are you doing this?” 5If you obey the king, you will stay out of trouble. So be wise and learn what to do and when to do it. 6Life is hard, but there is a time and a place for everything, 7though no one can tell the future. 8We cannot control the wind or determine the day of our death. There is no escape in time of war, and no one can hide behind evil. 9I noticed all this and thought seriously about what goes on in the world. Why does one person have the power to hurt another?
Who Can Understand the Ways of God?
10I saw the wicked buried with honor, but God's people had to leave the holy city and were forgotten. None of this makes sense. 11When we see criminals commit crime after crime without being punished, it makes us want to start a life of crime. 12They commit hundreds of crimes and live a long time, in spite of the saying:
Everyone who lives right
and respects God
will prosper,
13but no one who sins
and rejects God
will prosper or live very long.
14There is something else that doesn't make sense to me. Good citizens are treated as criminals, while criminals are honored as though they were good citizens. 15So I think we should get as much out of life as we possibly can. There is nothing better than to enjoy our food and drink and have a good time. Then we can make it through this troublesome life that God has given us here on earth.
16Day and night I went without sleep, trying to understand what goes on in this world. 17I saw everything God does, and I realized no one can really understand what happens. We may be very wise, but no matter how much we try or how much we claim to know, we cannot understand it all.
translation_text:
1Namɔ kɛ nilelɔ ye egbɔ; ni namɔ nuɔ nibii ashishi? Nilee hãa gbɔmɔ saa ehiɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ, ni ehiɛtumɔ laajeɔ.
Ye Maŋtsɛ gbee nɔ
2Ye maŋtsɛ lɛ fãmɔ nɔ; yɛ okitã krɔŋŋ ni okã lɛ hewɔ lɛ kaahã enɔyeli hao bo. 3Kɛji sane lɛ eŋɔɔɔ enaa lɛ kaashashao shi; oshi ehiɛ oya, ejaakɛ maŋtsɛ feɔ nɔ ni lɛ esumɔɔ. 4Kɛji maŋtsɛ kɛɛ lɛ, akɛɛɛ dɔŋŋ; ni namɔ po baanyɛ lɛ ebi akɛ, “Mɛni po ofeɔ nɛɛ?” 5Mɔ ni yeɔ famɔ nɔ lɛ, enaaa amane. Nilelɔ le beyinɔ kɛ gbɛ nɔ ni eeetsɔ̃ efee nɔ ni yɔɔ feemɔ; 6ejaakɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ be kɛ gbɛ nɔ ni atsɔ̃ɔ atsuɔ ehenii; kɛ̃lɛ naagba kpaaa yɛ gbɔmɔ adesa nɔ. 7Gbɔmɔ ko leee nɔ ni baaba; ni namɔ hu aaanyɛ atsɔ̃ɔ lɛ bɔ ni ebaaba lɛ ehã? 8Mɔ ko kwraa bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛaatsĩ gbɔmɔ wala mumɔ naa koni ekafã yɛ emli; ni gbi ni gbɔmɔ gboɔ lɛ, mɔ ko kwraa bɛ hewalɛ yɛ nɔ. Ta ko ni wɔnyɛŋ naa foi wɔje ni; ni nɔ ko hu nyɛŋ ehã mɛi ni ahe yɔɔ mli aje mli.
Mɔ ni efeee nɔ ni ja kɛ Mɔ ni feɔ nɔ ni ja
9Be ni mitao nii fɛɛ ni afeɔ yɛ jeŋ ni gbɔmɔ adesa kpɔfuɔ enyɛmi gbɔmɔ yɛ mli nɛɛ mli fitsofitso lɛ, nɔ ni mina nɛ: 10Mina mɛi fɔ̃ji ni egboi ni afu amɛ. Gbɔmɛi nɛɛ awalabeiaŋ lɛ, anaa amɛ amɛyaa amɛbaa yɛ Sɔlemɔ we lɛ; shi amɛgbele mli lɛ, ajie amɛyi yɛ maŋ lɛ mli, he nɔŋŋ ni amɛfee nakai efɔ̃ji lɛ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ hu shishinumɔ bɛ he.
11Akɛ ni awooo esha he nyɔmɔ oya hewɔ lɛ, gbɔmɛi ahe ehomɔ kɛ efɔŋfeemɔ. 12Yɛ mli akɛ eshafeelɔ feɔ esha shii oha, ni ewala sɛɛ tsɛɔ moŋ nɛ, kɛ̃lɛ mile akɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni sheɔ Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei lɛ ebaahi ehã amɛ, ejaakɛ amɛsheɔ Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei; 13shi yiwalɔ lɛ ehiŋ ehaŋ lɛ, ni ewala sɛɛ etsɛŋ tamɔ hɔ̃ɔŋ, ejaakɛ esheee Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei.
14Nɔ ko hu ni yaa nɔ yɛ je nɛɛŋ ni shishinumɔ bɛ he nɛ: gbɔmɛi kpakpai komɛi naa amanehului ni sa gbɔmɛi fɔ̃ji moŋ; ni yiwalɔi komɛi yɛ ni amɛna dromɔ ni sa gbɔmɛi kpakpai moŋ. Nɔ ni mikɛɛ ji akɛ enɛ hu lɛ shishinumɔ bɛ he. 15Kɛkɛ ni mikafo miishɛɛ ejaakɛ nɔ kpakpa ko bɛ hã gbɔmɔ yɛ hulu shishi nɛɛ, fe akɛ eye nii ni enu nɔ ko, ni ena miishɛɛ. Eeenyɛ ekã he efee enɛ be mli ni eyɔɔ wala ni Nyɔŋmɔ ehã lɛ yɛ je nɛɛŋ.
16Be ni mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ fɔ̃ nɔ akɛ matao male nii koni manu nii ni yaa nɔ, yɛ je nɛɛŋ shishi, hewɔ ni nyɔɔŋnyɔɔŋ kɛ shwaneshwane fɛɛ lɛ gbɔmɔ naaa wɔ ewɔ lɛ, 17mina mile Nyɔŋmɔ dɛŋ nitsumɔi fɛɛ; shi mina akɛ bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni gbɔmɔ baagba ehe naa ehã lɛ, enuŋ nii ni yaa nɔ yɛ je nɛɛ mli lɛ shishi kɔkɔɔkɔ. Tsɛbelɛ nilelɔ aaakɛɛ akɛ ena ele nii fɛɛ nɛ, shi anɔkwale ji akɛ enyɛŋ ele nɔ fɛɛ nɔ.

english_text:
One Day at a Time
1I thought about these things. Then I understood that God has power over everyone, even those who are wise and live right. Anything can happen to any one of us, and so we never know if life will be good or bad. 2But exactly the same thing will finally happen to all of us, whether we live right and respect God or sin and don't respect God. Yes, the same thing will happen if we offer sacrifices to God or if we don't, if we keep our promises or are afraid to make them.
3It's terribly unfair for the same thing to happen to each of us. We are mean and foolish while we live, and then we die. 4As long as we are alive, we still have hope, just as a live dog is better off than a dead lion. 5We know we will die, but the dead don't know a thing. Nothing good will happen to them—they are gone and forgotten. 6Their loves, their hates, and their jealous feelings have all disappeared with them. They will never again take part in anything that happens on this earth.
7So be happy and enjoy eating and drinking! God decided long ago that this is what you should do. 8Dress up, comb your hair, and look your best. 9Life is short, and you love your wife, so enjoy being with her. This is what you are supposed to do as you struggle through life on this earth. 10Work hard at whatever you do. You will soon go to the world of the dead, where no one works or thinks or reasons or even knows anything.
11Here is something else I have learned:
The fastest runners
and the greatest heroes
don't always win races
and battles.
Wisdom, intelligence, and skill
don't always make you healthy,
rich, or popular.
We each have our own share
of misfortune.
12None of us know when we might fall victim to a sudden disaster and find ourselves like fish in a net or birds in a trap.
Better To Be Wise than Foolish
13Once I saw what people really think of wisdom, and it made an impression on me. 14It happened when a powerful ruler surrounded and attacked a small city where only a few people lived. The enemy army was getting ready to break through the city walls. 15But the city was saved by the wisdom of a poor person who was soon forgotten. 16So I decided that wisdom is better than strength. Yet if you are poor, no one pays any attention to you, no matter how smart you are.
17Words of wisdom spoken softly
make much more sense
than the shouts of a ruler
to a crowd of fools.
18Wisdom is more powerful
than weapons,
yet one mistake can destroy
all the good you have done.
translation_text:
1Mikɛ mitsui fɔ̃ nibii nɛɛ anɔ, ni mitao fɛɛ mli. Nɔ ni mina ji akɛ jalɔi kɛ nilelɔi kɛ amɛnifeemɔi lɛ, Nyɔŋmɔ dɛŋ fɛɛ yɔɔ; suɔmɔ ni jio, nyɛɛ ni jio, gbɔmɔ ko leee. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni kã gbɔmɛi ahiɛ lɛ yakanii ni, 2ejaakɛ jalɔ kɛ mɔ ni ejaaa, kɛ gbɔmɔ kpakpa kɛ gbɔmɔ fɔŋ, kɛ mɔ ni he tse kɛ mɔ ni he tseee, kɛ mɔ ni shãa afɔle kɛ mɔ ni eshãaa afɔle fɛɛ lɛ, amɛ fɛɛ lɛ amɛnaagbee kome. Nɔ ni baa gbɔmɔ kpakpa nɔ lɛ, no nɔŋŋ baa efɔŋfeelɔ nɔ, ni nakai nɔŋŋ baa mɔ ni kãa kitã kɛ mɔ ni kãaa kitã fɛɛ nɔ. 3Nɔ ko ni ejaaa yɛ nii fɛɛ ni afeɔ yɛ je nɛɛŋ ji akɛ mɛi fɛɛ anaagbee afee ekome. Gbɔmɛi atsuiiaŋ eyimɔ obɔ̃bɔ̃ kɛ efɔŋ kɛ sɛkɛyeli nifeemɔi, beiaŋ ni amɛyɔɔ walaŋ, shi no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgboiɔ, ni amɛyaa gbohiiaje. 4Shi mɔ ni hiɛ kã lɛ, eyɛ hiɛnɔkãmɔ ko kɛ̃ ejaakɛ gbee hiɛkãalɔ lɛ, ehi fe jata ni egbo. 5Ejaakɛ hiɛkãalɔi lɛ amɛle akɛ amɛbaagboi, shi gbohii lɛ amɛleee nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni amɛbɛ nɔ ko hu ni amɛbaana dɔŋŋ, ni hiɛ kpaa amɛnɔ kwraa. 6Amɛsuɔmɔ kɛ amɛnyɛɛ kɛ amɛwuŋayeli fɛɛ eho etee momo; ni kɛyaashi naanɔ lɛ, nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ je nɛɛŋ lɛ amɛhe bɛ mli dɔŋŋ.
7Yaa nɔ oye oboloo kɛ miishɛɛ, ni onu owain hu kɛ mliflimɔ, ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ ejɔɔ nɔ ni ofeɔ lɛ nɔ momo. 8Hã otadei ahiɛ ayɛ be fɛɛ be; wo oyiteŋ mu be fɛɛ be hu. 9Okɛ oŋa ni osumɔɔ lɛ ahi shi yɛ miishɛɛ mli, bei abɔ ni oyɔɔ yaka wala ni Nyɔŋmɔ eduro bo yɛ je nɛɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ejaakɛ deŋme ni ogbo yɛ je nɛɛŋ lɛ, ogbɛfaŋ nɔ ni ona yɛ jeŋ ji no. 10Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ tsumɔ ni ooomɔ mli lɛ, tsu kɛ onyɛmɔ fɛɛ, ejaakɛ gbohiiaje he ni oyaa lɛ, nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitsumɔ loo yiŋshwiemɔ loo nilee loo jwɛŋmɔ lɛ eko bɛ jɛi.
11Asaŋ mina akɛ jeŋ ni ayɔɔ mli nɛɛ lɛ, jeee be fɛɛ be mɔ ni najiaŋ wa yeɔ foidamɔ mli kunim, aloo kãkãlɔ yeɔ ta mli kunim; aloo nilelɔ naa edaaŋŋmaa, aloo hiɛshikãlɔ tsɔ̃ɔ niiatsɛ, aloo mɔ ni he esa yɛ nitsumɔ ko mli hiɛ baa nyam; shi amɛ fɛɛ lɛ dromɔ naa kɛkɛ ni. 12Ejaakɛ gbɔmɔ adesa leee ebe. Kɛji be lɛ banina lɛ trukaa lɛ, etsɔ̃ɔ tamɔ faaŋ loo ni ahiɛ, loo loofɔji ni akɛ tsɔne edu amɛ.
Nilee kɛ Kwashiafeemɔ he susumɔ
13Nilee sane ko hu ni mina yɛ jeŋ ni enɔ bɛ hã mi nɛ: 14Be ko lɛ maŋtsɛ wulu ko tee akɛ eyaatua maŋ bibioo kɛ emli bii fioo ko. Maŋtsɛ nɛɛ sa maŋ bibioo lɛ yi, ni etswa kawoo gbogboi ekɛbɔle maŋ lɛ. 15Nuu ohiafo ko yɛ maŋ bibioo lɛ mli, ni lɛ etsɔ̃ enilee nɔ ehere maŋ lɛ yiwala. Shi mɔ ko mɔ ko kaiii nuu ohiafo nɛɛ. 16Shi nɔ ni mikɛɔ ji akɛ nilee hi fe hewalɛ, tsɛbelɛ abuuu ohiafo nilee, ni akɛ ewiemɔ efeee nɔ ko. 17Nilelɔ wiemɔ ni ewieɔ lɛ ablɛbi lɛ, anuɔ, ni ehi fe bolɔmɔ ni nɔyelɔ bolɔɔ yɛ kwashiai ateŋ. 18Nilee he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ fe tawuu nii; shi eshafeelɔ kome kpãtãa nii kpakpai babaoo hiɛ.

english_text:
1A few dead flies in perfume
make all of it stink,
and a little foolishness
outweighs a lot of wisdom.
2Sensible thoughts lead you
to do right;
foolish thoughts lead you
to do wrong.
3Fools show their stupidity
by the way they live;
it's easy to see
they have no sense.
4Don't give up your job
when your boss gets angry.
If you stay calm,
you'll be forgiven.
5Rulers do some things that are terribly unfair: 6They honor fools, but dishonor the rich; 7they let slaves ride on horses, but force slave owners to walk.
8 If you dig a pit,
you might fall in;
if you break down a wall,
a snake might bite you.
9You could even get hurt
by chiseling a stone
or chopping a log.
10If you don't sharpen your ax,
it will be harder to use;
if you are wise,
you'll know what to do.
11The power to charm a snake
does you no good
if it bites you anyway.
12If you talk sensibly,
you will have friends;
if you talk foolishly,
you will destroy yourself.
13Fools begin with nonsense,
and their stupid chatter
ends with disaster.
14They never tire of talking,
but none of us really know
what the future will bring.
15Fools wear themselves out—
they don't know enough
to find their way home.
16A country is in for trouble
when its ruler is childish,
and its leaders
party all day long.
17But a nation will prosper
when its ruler is mature,
and its leaders
don't party too much.
18Some people are too lazy
to fix a leaky roof—
then the house collapses.
19Eating and drinking
make you feel happy,
and money can buy
everything you need.
20Don't let yourself think about
cursing the king;
don't curse the rich,
not even in secret.
A little bird might hear
and tell everything.
translation_text:
1Adɔdɔji ni egboi hãa ojeŋma feelɔ ojeŋma tete shaa, ni ejeɔ fu; no hewɔ lɛ, buulufeemɔ fioo lɛ efiteɔ nilee kɛ nyam nitsumɔ fɛɛ. 2Nilelɔ tsui kpalaa lɛ kɛyaa nɔ ni ja he; shi kwashia tsui kpalaa lɛ kɛyaa nɔ ni ejaaa he. 3Kɛji kwashia nyiɛ tɛmpɔŋ nɔ tete po lɛ, enaaa jwɛŋmɔ, ni ehãa mɔ fɛɛ mɔ naa akɛ kwashia ji lɛ.
4Kɛji onɔyelɔ mli fu bo lɛ, no akahã oshi ogbɛnaa ni ohiɛ yɛ eshishi lɛ, ejaakɛ saneheŋmɛɛmɔ lɛ ejɔɔ tɔ̃mɔi wuji tete ahe. 5Mina nɔ ko ni ejaaa gbɛ yɛ je nɛɛ mli ni nɔyelɔi feɔ. 6Aholeɔ kwashiai anɔ ataraa hei grɔŋgrɔŋŋ; ni akɛ niiatsɛmɛi taraa hei ni bɛ nyam. 7Ni mina nyɔji tara okpɔŋɔi anɔ be ni lumɛi nyiɛ amɛnane nɔ tamɔ nyɔji.
8Mɔ ni tsaa bu lɛ, lɛ nɔŋŋ eeegbee mli, ni mɔ ni gbuɔ gbogbo ewoɔ mli lɛ, lɛ onufu aaakɔ̃. 9Mɔ ni tsaa tɛ lɛ, lɛ tɛ pilaa, ni mɔ hu ni gbaa lai lɛ, lɛ awui lai yeɔ. 10Kɛji mɔ ko lema naa egbo, ni ejɔɔɔ naa lɛ, no lɛ ja emia ekpɔiaŋ waa. Nilee akɛtoɔ nifeemɔ he dani ayeɔ kunim. 11Akamɛ ni onufu kɔ̃ mɔ dani akɛ ŋkunyaayeli kũ enaa; no lɛ sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he. 12Nilelɔ daaŋ wiemɔ hãa ehiɛ baa nyam, shi kwashia naabu kpãtãa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehiɛ. 13Ejeɔ ewiemɔ shishi kɛ kwashiai awiemɔi, ni egbeɔ naa kɛ sɛkɛyelɔi awiemɔ. 14Kwashia wieɔ babaoo. Gbɔmɔ ko leee nɔ ni baaba; ni mɔ ko hu nyɛŋ egba lɛ nɔ ni baaba yɛ esɛɛ.
15Kwashia deŋmegbomɔ hãa etɔɔ lɛ bɔ sɔŋŋ ni maŋ gbɛ tete laajeɔ lɛ.
16Kpoo hã bo, maŋ ni omaŋtsɛ lɛ gbekɛ ni, ni olumɛi tsɛɔ yelikɛnumɔ leebi. 17Shi ajɔɔ bo, bo maŋ ni omaŋtsɛ lɛ abladei abi ni, ni olumɛi lɛ tsɛɔ okplɔ̃ yɛ be ni sa mli koni amɛye nii ni amɛna gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ, shi jeee koni amɛtɔrɔ dãa.
18Hejɔ̃ hãa tsu duɔ, ni anihao hãa tsu wuleɔ ewoɔ mli.
19Ŋmaa hãa mɔ miishɛɛ, ni wain hãa mɔ mli filiɔ lɛ, shi eko fɛɛ eko lɛ shika akɛfeɔ.
20Kaalomɔ maŋtsɛ yɛ oyitsoŋ tete, ni kaalomɔ niiatsɛ hu yɛ osɛɛtsu mli, ejaakɛ gbogbo he yɛ folɔ.

english_text:
It Pays To Work Hard
1Be generous, and someday
you will be rewarded.
2Share what you have
with seven or eight others,
because you never know
when disaster may strike.
3Rain clouds always bring rain;
trees always stay
wherever they fall.
4If you worry about the weather
and don't plant seeds,
you won't harvest a crop.
5No one can explain how a baby breathes before it is born. So how can anyone explain what God does? After all, God created everything.
6Plant your seeds early in the morning and keep working in the field until dark. Who knows? Your work might pay off, and your seeds might produce.
Youth and Old Age
7Nothing on earth is more beautiful than the morning sun. 8Even if you have a very long life, you should try to enjoy each day, because darkness will come and will last a long time. Nothing makes sense.
9Be cheerful and enjoy life while you are young! Do what you want and find pleasure in what you see. But don't forget that God will judge you for everything you do.
10Rid yourself of all worry and pain, because the wonderful moments of youth quickly disappear.
translation_text:
Nilelɔ nifeemɔ
1Feemɔ ejurɔ oto, ni wɔsɛɛ ko lɛ aaafee bo ejurɔ. 2Feemɔ mɛi kpawo loo kpaanyɔ ejurɔ, ejaakɛ oleee sane gbonyo ni nyiɛ gbɛ baa yɛ jeŋ.
3Kɛji atatuiaŋ yi tɔ kɛ nu lɛ, amɛnɛɔ nu amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; ni kɛji tso yaagbee shi, ni eyagbee wuoyigbɛ loo kooyigbɛ lɛ, eshigbeemɔhe lɛ nɔŋŋ ekãa. 4Mɔ ni saraa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ, eduŋ nii, ni mɔ hu ni kwɛɔ atatui lɛ, ekpaŋ nii. 5Bɔ ni onyɛŋ ole bɔ ni feɔ ni mumɔ baa bi ni yɔɔ yoohɔlɔ musuŋ lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ onyɛŋ ole bɔ ni Nyɔŋmɔ tsɔ̃ɔ tsuɔ enii fɛɛ. 6Du odumɔwui leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ fɛɛ, ejaakɛ onyɛŋ ole wui lɛ ateŋ nɔ ni baahi, enɛ loo enɛ, loo kɛji fɛɛ aaahi.
7La ŋɔɔ, ni kɛji hiŋmɛi miina hulu lɛ, gbɔmɔ naa miishɛɛ. 8Kɛji gbɔmɔ ye afii babaoo lɛ, ena miishɛɛ yɛ fɛɛ mli; shi moŋ ekai akɛ gbele duŋ be fa. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni baa lɛ yakanii ni.
Ŋaa kɛhã Oblahii kɛ Oblayei
9Oblanyo, nya yɛ oblahiiaŋ; hã omii ashɛ ohe yɛ oblahiiaŋ fɛɛ; ye otsui naa sane; feemɔ nɔ ni hi yɛ ohiɛ; shi moŋ kaimɔ akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ bo baakojo yɛ nibii fɛɛ ni ofee lɛ ahewɔ.
10Jiemɔ mlifu kɛje oyiŋ, ni kaapiŋ ohe yɛ nɔ ko hewɔ, ejaakɛ ogbekɛbiiashi kɛ oblahiiaŋ lɛ yakanii be ni.

english_text:
1Keep your Creator in mind while you are young! In years to come, you will be burdened down with troubles and say, “I don't enjoy life anymore.”
2Someday the light of the sun
and the moon and the stars
will all seem dim to you.
Rain clouds will remain
over your head.
3Your body will grow feeble,
your teeth will decay,
and your eyesight fail.
4The noisy grinding of grain
and the voices of singers
will be shut out
by your deaf ears,
but even the song of a bird
will keep you awake.
5You will be afraid
to climb up a hill
or walk down a road.
Your hair will turn as white
as almond blossoms.
You will feel lifeless
and drag along
like an old grasshopper.
We each go to our eternal home,
and the streets here are filled
with those who mourn.
6The silver cord snaps,
the golden bowl breaks;
the water pitcher is smashed,
and the pulley at the well
is shattered.
7So our bodies return
to the earth,
and the life-giving breath
returns to God.
8Nothing makes sense.
I have seen it all—
nothing makes sense.
Respect and Obey God
9I was a wise teacher with much understanding, and I collected a number of proverbs that I had carefully studied. 10Then I tried to explain these things in the best and most accurate way.
11Words of wisdom are like the stick a farmer uses to make animals move. These sayings come from a shepherd, and they are like nails that fasten things together. 12My child, I warn you to stay away from any teachings except these.
There is no end to books,
and too much study
will wear you out.
13Everything you were taught can be put into a few words:
Respect and obey God!
This is what life
is all about.
14God will judge
everything we do,
even what is done in secret,
whether good or bad.
translation_text:
1Kaimɔ obɔlɔ lɛ yɛ oblahiiaŋ, be ni gbii fɔ̃ji lɛ kɛ afii fɔ̃ji lɛ nako ashɛ, be mli ni obaakɛɛ akɛ, “Jeŋshihilɛ eŋɔɔɔ” lɛ. 2Nakai be lɛ hulu la lɛ kɛ nyɔɔŋtsere lɛ kɛ ŋulamii lɛ baafee sulii, ni atatui baabua amɛhe naa ekoŋŋ yɛ nunɛmɔ sɛɛ. 3Nakai be lɛ ogbɔmɔtso shĩa lɛ he bulɔi, ni ji oniji lɛ baakpokpo, ni onaji kpiŋtiŋkpliŋŋ lɛ egbɔjɔ, ni onyanyɔji, nigbɛlɛlɔi lɛ, nyɛɛɛ nii amɛgbɛlɛ dɔŋŋ, ejaakɛ eshwɛ amɛyi fioo ko kɛkɛ, ni hiŋmɛii lɛ ni kwɛɔ samfɛji lɛ amli nii lɛ anɔ eha. 4Toii lɛ ni anaa kamɔ ni boɔ blohuiaŋ toi lɛ nuŋ nɔ ko nɔ ko dɔŋŋ; amɛnuŋ nigbɛlɛmɔ tsɔne lɛ gbɛɛmɔ ni naa eba shi lɛ he ekpakpa ko. Loofɔlɔ gbee aaatsĩɛ bo yɛ wɔ mli moŋ, shi ooonu yei lalɔi agbei, ejaakɛ osharãi sɔŋŋ yɔɔ gbɛteŋ. 5Oooshe hei ni kwɔlɔ gbeyei, ni onyiɛmɔ tete baatsɔ̃ osharã ahã bo. Oyiteŋ baayɛ tamɔ odonti ni egba, ni ohetsimɔ baawa ahã bo, ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efeŋ bo akɔnɔ dɔŋŋ.
Akɛni gbɔmɔ adesa miiya enaanɔ shĩa lɛ, no hewɔ ni yarafeelɔi foɔ shi yɛ blohuiaŋ lɛ. 6Jwiɛtɛi kɔsɔŋkɔsɔ lɛ baatse, ni shika kane lɛ baatswa shi ni ejwa, ni faaŋyaa gbɛ lɛ baajwa yɛ nubu lɛ naa. 7Wɔsũ gbɔmɔtsei lɛ baaku sɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ sũ mli ekoŋŋ, he ni amɛjɛ lɛ, ni mumɔ lɛ hu baaku esɛɛ eya Nyɔŋmɔ mɔ ŋɔɔ ni ejɛ eba lɛ ŋɔɔ ekoŋŋ.
8Yakanii mli yakanii, Tsɔɔlɔ lɛ kɛɛ; fɛɛ lɛ yakanii ni.
Wiemɔi lɛ anaamuu
9Tsɔɔlɔ lɛ le nii, ni etsɔ̃ɔ emaŋbii lɛ nii ni ele lɛ eko. Ekase abɛi ahe nii, ejwɛŋ amɛhe ni ekɛ amɛ to shihilɛ he ekwɛ kɛ hiɛshikãmɔ. 10Tsɔɔlɔ lɛ bɔ mɔdɛŋ etao wiemɔi ni ŋɔɔ, asaŋ ni ja, ni eŋmala anɔkwale wiemɔi. 11Nilelɔ daaŋ wiemɔi lɛ etamɔ kplamɔ tso. Tookwɛlɔ koome ni yɔɔ lɛ, ewiemɔi ni abua naa lɛ yɛ kpɛŋŋ tamɔ plɛkoo ni aka awo tso mli.
12Mibi, kwɛmɔ ni ahi yɛ enɛɛmɛi asɛɛ. Woloŋmaa bɛ naagbee, ni nikasemɔ tuutu lɛ gbɔmɔtso tɔlɛ ni.
13Sane tso muu lɛ ni onu lɛ fɛɛ naagbee nɛ. She Nyɔŋmɔ gbeyei, ni oye ekitãi lɛ anɔ, ejaakɛ enɛ ji nitsumɔ kwraa ni gbɔmɔ yɔɔ tsumɔ. 14Ejaakɛ Nyɔŋmɔ baakojo wɔ yɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni wɔfee gbɛfaŋ, ehi jio, ehiii jio, teemɔŋ nibii fɛɛ fata he.

english_text:
Love Is Better than Wine
1 This is Solomon's
most beautiful song.
She Speaks:
2Kiss me tenderly!
Your love is better than wine,
3and you smell so sweet.
All the young women adore you;
the very mention of your name
is like spreading perfume.
* 4Hurry, my king! Let's hurry.
Take me to your home.
The Young Women Speak:
We are happy for you!
And we praise your love
even more than wine.
She Speaks:
Young women of Jerusalem,
it is only right
that you should adore him.
5My skin is dark and beautiful,
like a tent in the desert
or like Solomon's curtains.
6Don't stare at me
just because the sun
has darkened my skin.
My brothers were angry with me;
they made me work in the vineyard,
and so I neglected
my complexion.
7My darling, I love you!
Where do you feed your sheep
and let them rest at noon?
Don't let the other shepherds
think badly of me.
I'm not one of those women
who shamelessly follow
after shepherds.
He Speaks:
8My dearest, if you don't know,
just follow the path
of the sheep.
Then feed your young goats
near the shepherds' tents.
9You move as gracefully
as the pony that leads
the chariot of the king.
10Earrings add to your beauty,
and you wear a necklace
of precious stones.
11Let's make you some jewelry
of gold, woven with silver.
She Speaks:
12My king, while you
were on your couch,
my aroma was a magic charm.
13My darling, you are perfume
between my breasts;
14you are flower blossoms
from the gardens of En-Gedi.
He Speaks:
15My darling, you are lovely,
so very lovely—
your eyes are those of a dove.
She Speaks:
16My love, you are handsome,
truly handsome—
the fresh green grass
will be our wedding bed
17in the shade of cedar
and cypress trees.
translation_text:
1 Solomon lalai amli lala nɛ.
Klɛŋklɛŋ lala
Yoo lɛ
2Ao, mina ni kulɛ ooobashwɔ minaa;
ejaakɛ osuɔmɔ fe wain.
3Omui ni okpaa jeɔ ŋma naakpa,
ogbɛi jeɔ ŋma tamɔ muŋma
ni afɔse ashwie shi.
No hewɔ ni oblayei lɛ sumɔɔ bo lɛ.
4MiMaŋtsɛ, hã manyiɛ osɛɛ;
hã wɔye wɔhe oyai
kɛya opiai lɛ amli.
Wɔɔnya, ni wɔmii aaashɛ.
Wɔɔkafo osuɔmɔ lɛ fe wain;
ŋwanejee ko bɛ he akɛ,
no hewɔ yei sumɔɔ bo lɛ.
5Nyɛ Yerusalɛm biyei,
midiɔ nɛ,
shi mihe yɛ fɛo;
midiɔ tamɔ Kedar bui lɛ,
mitamɔ muhɔi ni yɔɔ Solomon we lɛ.
6Kaakwɛ mi gãa yɛ dimɔ ni midiɔ,
kɛ hulu ni eshã mi hewɔ.
Minyɛ bihii lɛ amli fu mi,
ni amɛfee mi waintromi anɔkwɛlɔ.
Tsɛbelɛ, mi diɛŋtsɛ minɔ lɛ, mikwɛɛɛ.
7Bo mɔ ni mitsui sumɔɔ,
tsɔ̃ɔmɔ mi otoi alɛɛhe lɛ,
kɛ he ni ohãa amɛbumɔɔ shwane.
Mɛni hewɔ matamɔ mɔ ni tsomloɔ
kɛtaoɔ bo yɛ onanemɛi atookui ahe?
Nuu lɛ
8Bo yoo ni ohe yɔɔ fɛo fe yei fɛɛ,
kɛ oleee jɛi lɛ,
bo lɛ jaa tooku lɛ asɛɛ mo kɛya,
ni oyalɛ abotiai abii lɛ
yɛ tookwɛlɔi abuui lɛ amasɛi.
9Mishieŋnyɛ, mikɛ bo toɔ okpɔŋɔi
ni yɔɔ Farao shwiilii lɛ ateŋ
eko he.
10Odabii yɛ fɛo kɛ wulamɔnii;
okuɛ hu yɛ fɛo kɛ jwinei ni
atsɛ̃rɛ.
11Wɔbaafee shika hewulamɔnii
ni akɛ jwiɛtɛi eholɔ mli wɔhã bo.
Yoo Lɛ
12Be ni maŋtsɛ kã ekpasa mli lɛ,
belɛ minuatrɛ lɛ miije ŋma.
13Misuɔlɔ lɛ he jeɔ ŋma krɔbɔo
kɛji ekã mifufɔi ateŋ lɛ.
14Misuɔlɔ lɛ tamɔ ŋaŋ fɔfɔi
yɛ En-Gedi waintromii lɛ amli hã mi.
Nuu Lɛ
15Naa, ohe yɛ fɛo, mishieŋnyɛ!
Naa, ohe yɛ fɛo.
Ohiŋmɛi tamɔ okpo hiŋmɛi.
Yoo lɛ
16Naa, ohe yɛ fɛo, misuɔlɔ,
ohe yɛ akɔnɔ hu;
jwɛifɔ ji wɔsaa ni wɔkãa nɔ.
17Wɔtsu mplaŋi lɛ tsenedru ni.
Ni wɔŋmɔŋmloi lɛ sɛsɛo ni.

english_text:
Love Makes Everything Beautiful
She Speaks:
1I am merely a rose
from the land of Sharon,
a lily from the valley.
He Speaks:
2My darling, when compared
with other young women,
you are a lily among thorns.
She Speaks:
3And you, my love,
are an apple tree
among trees of the forest.
Your shade brought me pleasure;
your fruit was sweet.
4You led me to your banquet room
and showered me with love.
5Refresh and strengthen me
with raisins and apples.
I am hungry for love!
6Put your left hand under my head
and embrace me
with your right arm.
7Young women of Jerusalem,
promise me by the power
of deer and gazelles
never to awaken love
before it is ready.
Winter Is Past
She Speaks:
8I hear the voice
of the one I love,
as he comes leaping
over mountains and hills
9like a deer or a gazelle.
Now he stands outside our wall,
looking through the window
10and speaking to me.
He Speaks:
My darling, I love you!
Let's go away together.
11Winter is past,
the rain has stopped;
12flowers cover the earth,
it's time to sing.
The cooing of doves
is heard in our land.
13Fig trees are bearing fruit,
while blossoms on grapevines
fill the air with perfume.
My darling, I love you!
Let's go away together.
14You are my dove
hiding among the rocks
on the side of a cliff.
Let me see how lovely you are!
Let me hear the sound
of your melodious voice.
15Our vineyards are in blossom;
we must catch the little foxes
that destroy the vineyards.
She Speaks:
16My darling, I am yours,
and you are mine,
as you feed your sheep
among the lilies.
17Pretend to be a young deer
dancing on mountain slopes
until daylight comes
and shadows fade away.
translation_text:
1Mi lɛ, Sharon fɔfɔi ji mi,
mi ji jɔi amli oflɔ fɔfɔi.
Nuu lɛ
2Bɔ ni oflɔ fɔfɔi yɔɔ
yɛ ŋmei ateŋ lɛ,
nakai mishieŋnyɛ yɔɔ
yɛ oblayei ateŋ.
Yoo lɛ
3Bɔ ni akututso yɔɔ yɛ kooŋtsei ateŋ lɛ,
nakai misuɔlɔ yɔɔ
yɛ oblahii ateŋ.
Miishɛɛ mikɛtaa ehɔ̃ɔŋ,
ni eyibii lɛ ŋɔɔ minaa.
4Ekɛ mi ba shĩa ni aŋmɛ okplɔ̃ yɛŋ
ni ekɛ suɔmɔɔ aflaŋaa ha minɔ.
5Kɛ wainyibii ni aka lɛ fã kɛ fã awaje mi;
kɛ aduawai ajɔɔ mitsui he;
ejaakɛ suɔmɔ ewo mi hela.
6Mina ni kulɛ, enine abɛku
hɔ miyitso shishi,
ni ekɛ eninejurɔ efua mi atuu.
7Nyɛ Yerusalɛm biyei,
mina soŋai kɛ ŋa nɔ ofrote yei akɛ,
nyɛkagbaa wɔsuɔmɔ lɛ naa;
ni nyɛkatsĩɛa ehiɛ kɛjɛ ewɔ mli,
kɛyaashi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsui aaatɔ.
Lala ni ji enyɔ
Yoo lɛ
8Minu misuɔlɔ lɛ gbee!
Naa, eeba,
eehuru yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ,
ehiɛ foi waa yɛ gɔŋkpɔi lɛ anɔ.
9Misuɔlɔ lɛ tamɔ soŋai,
loo ofrote oblanyo.
Naa, edamɔ wɔgbogbo lɛ sɛɛ;
eekwɛ samfɛji lɛ amli gãa,
eefili kɛ miitsɔ̃ samfɛji fɔji lɛ amli.
10Misuɔlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ,
Nuu lɛ
“Mishieŋnyɛ, mimɔ ni he yɔɔ fɛo!
Tee shi, ni oba wɔtee.
11Shi, naa, fɛ̃i be lɛ eho etee;
nunɛmɔ be lɛ sɛɛ efo kwraa.
12Fɔfɔii egba yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ;
lala be lɛ eshɛ,
ni aanu kosɛɛ okpo gbee yɛ
wɔshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.
13Agbãmitso miiwo yibii,
ni waintsei lɛ hu egba afofroi
kɛ ŋma.
No hewɔ lɛ, misuɔlɔ, tee shi ni oba wɔtee,
bo ji mimɔ ni he yɔɔ fɛo.
14Mikosɛɛ okpo ni hiɔ tɛsaa fɔjiaŋ,
yɛ gɔŋ grɔŋŋ hɔ̃ɔŋ,
hã mana ohiɛ,
ni manu ogbee;
ejaakɛ ogbee ŋɔɔ,
ni ohiɛ hu yɛ fɛo.
15Nyɛmɔmɔa osɔi lɛ,
osɔi bibii ni fiteɔ waintromii lɛ,
ejaakɛ wɔwaintsei lɛ
egba afofro.”
Yoo lɛ
16Minɔ ji misuɔlɔ lɛ, ni lɛ hu enɔ ji mi.
Elɛɔ etoi lɛ
yɛ oflɔ fɔfɔii ateŋ.
17Kuu osɛɛ, misuɔlɔ,
tamɔ soŋai loo ofrote oblanyo,
yɛ Beta gɔji lɛ anɔ,
ni oba dani je atsɛre,
ni duŋ alaaje.

english_text:
Beautiful Dreams
She Speaks:
1While in bed at night,
I reached for the one I love
with heart and soul.
I looked for him,
but he wasn't there.
2So I searched through the town
for the one I love.
I looked on every street,
but he wasn't there.
3I even asked the guards
patrolling the town,
“Have you seen the one
I love so much?”
4Right after that, I found him.
I held him and would not let go
until I had taken him
to the home of my mother.
5Young women of Jerusalem,
promise me by the power
of deer and gazelles,
never to awaken love
before it is ready.
The Groom and the Wedding Party
Their Friends Speak:
6What do we see approaching
from the desert
like a cloud of smoke?
With it comes the sweet smell
of spices, including myrrh
and frankincense.
7It is King Solomon
carried on a throne,
surrounded by sixty
of Israel's best soldiers.
8Each of them wears a sword.
They are experts at fighting,
even in the dark.
9The throne is made of trees
from Lebanon.
10Its posts are silver,
the back is gold,
and the seat is covered
with purple cloth.
You women of Jerusalem
have taken great care
to furnish the inside.
11Now come and see the crown
given to Solomon by his mother
on his happy wedding day.
translation_text:
1Be ni mikã misaa nɔ nyɔɔŋ lɛ,
mitao mɔ ni mitsui sumɔɔ lɛ;
mitao lɛ, shi minaaa lɛ.
Mitsɛ lɛ, shi ehereee mi nɔ.
2Agbɛnɛ mate shi
mayakpa maŋ lɛ mli
gbɛjegbɛi kɛ blohuiaŋ.
Mayatao mɔ ni mitsui sumɔɔ lɛ lɛ.
Mitao lɛ, shi minaaa lɛ.
3Bulɔi ni buɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ,
na mi.
Mibi amɛ akɛ, “Ani nyɛna
mɔ ni mitsui sumɔɔ lɛ lo?”
4Miho amɛhe fioo pɛ,
kɛkɛ ni mina mɔ ni mitsui sumɔɔ lɛ.
Mimɔ emli; ni miŋmɛɛɛ ehe kwraa
kɛyashi mikɛ lɛ ba minyɛwe lɛ,
kɛtee minyɛ, mɔ ni fɔ mi lɛ sɛɛtsuŋ.
5Nyɛ Yerusalɛm biyei,
mina soŋai kɛ ŋa nɔ ofrote
akɛ nyɛkagbaa wɔsuɔmɔ lɛ naa,
ni nyɛkatsĩɛa ehiɛ kɛjɛ ewɔ mli
kɛyaashi be ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsui aaatɔ.
Lala ni ji etɛ̃
Yoo lɛ
6Mɛni ji nɔ ni jɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ baa
tamɔ lasu kusuu ni teɔ shi nɛɛ?
Namɔ nɛ ni mire kɛ krɔbɔo kɛ
jarayelɔi atsofãi srɔtoi fɛɛ jeɔ ŋma
yɛ ehe nɛɛ?
7Naa, Solomon ji mɔ ni
atere yɛ akpãkãi lɛ mli lɛ.
Asraafoi kakabãŋi nyɔŋmai ekpaa
ni jɛ Israel kãkãalɔi
ateŋ lɛ ebɔle ehe.
8Amɛ fɛɛ kwa amɛmia kɛ tawuu klantei,
ni amɛhe esa kɛ tawuu.
Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ klante ŋmɔ ehɛ,
yɛ nyɔɔŋ tuamɔ hewɔ.
9Maŋtsɛ Solomon kɛ Lebanon tsei
fee akpakãi hã ehe.
10Ehe tsei lɛ
akɛ jwiɛtɛi fee.
Emli kpasamɔnɔ lɛ akɛ
shika fee.
Emli sɛi lɛ akɛ mama
afaseo ha he.
Yerusalɛm biyei lɛ kɛ
suɔmɔ wula emligbɛ lɛ.
11Nyɛ Zion biyei, nyɛjea kpo
nyɛbakwɛa Maŋtsɛ Solomon,
kɛ akekre ni enyɛ kɛfi lɛ
yɛ eyookpeemɔ gbi
kɛ emliflimɔ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english_text:
What a Beautiful Bride
He Speaks:
1My darling, you are lovely,
so very lovely—
as you look through your veil,
your eyes are those of a dove.
Your hair tosses about
as gracefully as goats
coming down from Gilead.
2Your teeth are whiter
than sheep freshly washed;
they match perfectly,
not one is missing.
3Your lips are crimson cords,
your mouth is shapely;
behind your veil are hidden
beautiful rosy cheeks.
4Your neck is more graceful
than the tower of David,
decorated with thousands
of warriors' shields.
5Your breasts are perfect;
they are twin deer
feeding among lilies.
6I will hasten to those hills
sprinkled with sweet perfume
and stay there till sunrise.
7My darling, you are lovely
in every way.
8My bride, together
we will leave Lebanon!
We will say goodbye
to the peaks of Mount Amana,
Senir, and Hermon,
where lions and leopards
live in the caves.
9My bride, my very own,
you have stolen my heart!
With one glance from your eyes
and the glow of your necklace,
you have stolen my heart.
10Your love is sweeter than wine;
the smell of your perfume
is more fragrant than spices.
11Your lips are a honeycomb;
milk and honey
flow from your tongue.
Your dress has the aroma
of cedar trees from Lebanon.
12My bride, my very own,
you are a garden, a fountain
closed off to all others.
13Your arms are vines,
covered with delicious fruits
and all sorts of spices—
henna, nard, 14saffron,
calamus, cinnamon,
frankincense, myrrh, and aloes
—all the finest spices.
15You are a spring in the garden,
a fountain of pure water,
and a refreshing stream
from Mount Lebanon.
She Speaks:
16Let the north wind blow,
the south wind too!
Let them spread the aroma
of my garden,
so the one I love
may enter and taste
its delicious fruits.
translation_text:
Nuu lɛ
1Naa, ohe yɛ fɛo, misuɔlɔ,
naa, ohe yɛ fɛo.
Ohiŋmɛiŋ kpɛlɛɔ kɛ suɔmɔ
tamɔ okpo hiŋmɛii,
kɛtsɔ̃ɔ ohiɛhaanɔ lɛ mli.
Oyitsɔi bua onɔ tamɔ abotiai aku
ni bua shi yɛ Gilead gɔji lɛ ahe.
2Onyanyɔji yɛɔ futafuta
tamɔ gwantɛŋi ni aku amɛhetsɔi
ni aju amɛhe.
Amɛ fɛɛ kwa amɛfɔfɔɔ enyɔnyɔɔnyɔ
ni eko eko gboko.
3Onaabu tamɔ kpãa tsuru,
ni onaabu yɛ fɛo kɛ wiemɔ.
Odabii yɛ ohiɛhaanɔ lɛ mli
tamɔ maŋo tsuru.
4Okuɛ tamɔ David mɔɔ ni kwɔ,
ni ato tawuunii yɛ mli lɛ, ni
tawulɔi atsɛŋi bibii kɛ ewuji
tsotsoro shi yɛ mli fɛɛ
tamɔ kuɛnii.
5Ofufɔi tamɔ soŋai bii enyɔ.
Tamɔ ofrotebii hãaji ni
yeɔ nii yɛ oflɔ fɔfɔii ateŋ.
6Mayatee mihe yɛ mire gɔŋ lɛ nɔ,
ni mayashera shi yɛ
krɔbɔo gɔŋkpɔ lɛ nɔ,
kɛyashi beyinɔ ni je aaana
ni hiɛ aaabu.
7 Mishieŋnyɛ, ohe yɛ fɛo kɛmɔ shi;
kpa ko kpa ko bɛ ohe.
8Miyɛmfro, okɛ mi ajɛ Lebanon;
okɛ mi ajɛ Lebanon ni wɔya.
Jɛɛ Amana gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ oba;
Jɛɛ Senir kɛ Hermon gɔji lɛ anɔ,
jatai kɛ mlaŋtswii ashihilɛhe lɛ,
oba ni wɔtee.
9Minyɛmi yoo, miyɛmfro, oŋɔ mitsui;
okɛ okwɛmɔ ni okwɛ mi shi kome
kɛ ojarawatɛ kome ni yɔɔ okuɛnii lɛ mli lɛ
eŋɔ mitsui kwraa.
10Minyɛmi yoo, miyɛmfro,
osuɔmɔ yɛ akɔnɔ.
Osuɔmɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ aahu fe wain.
Omui lɛ jeɔ ŋma aahu fe tsofakɛŋmai srɔtoi fɛɛ.
11Miyɛmfro, onaabu tsereɔ wo shwieɔ shi;
wo kɛ fufɔ yɛ olilɛi shishi.
Ohebo mli ŋma tamɔ
Lebanon ŋma.
12Minyɛmi yoo, miyɛmfro lɛ,
etamɔ trom ni aŋmɛ naa;
etamɔ abɔɔ ni aŋmɛ naa;
etamɔ nuhiŋmɛi ni tueɔ ni asɔo naa.
13Otsei fɔbii lɛ tamɔ trom
ni maŋo tsei yɔɔ mli,
ni amɛwoɔ yibii srɔtoi
ni yɔɔ fɛo naakpa tamɔ kofer fɔfɔi kɛ nardo fiaa.
14Trom ni nardo kɛ safron kɛ
kalamo kɛ sinamon
kɛ krɔbɔo tsei fɛɛ kɛ
mire kɛ aloe kɛ tsofaikɛŋmai
titrii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ omli.
15Bo oji abɔɔ ni
nuhiŋmɛi kɛ wala nubu yɔɔ omli,
fai ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ Lebanon ji bo.
Yoo lɛ
16Bo, kooyigbɛ kɔɔyɔɔ, ohiɛ atsɛ̃,
ni bo wuoyigbɛ kɔɔyɔɔ, ba
ni obatswa yɛ mitrom lɛ mli,
koni anu emli ŋma
gbalaŋŋ lɛ yɛ hei fɛɛ.
Hã misuɔlɔ lɛ aba ebɔɔ lɛ mli
ni ebaye etsei ayibii
ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english_text:
He Speaks:
1My bride, my very own,
I come to my garden
and enjoy its spices.
I eat my honeycomb and honey;
I drink my wine and milk.
Their Friends Speak:
Eat and drink until
you are drunk with love.
Another Dream
She Speaks:
2I was asleep, but dreaming:
The one I love was at the door,
knocking and saying,
“My darling, my very own,
my flawless dove,
open the door for me!
My head is drenched
with evening dew.”
3But I had already undressed
and bathed my feet.
Should I dress again
and get my feet dirty?
4Then my darling's hand
reached to open the latch,
and my heart stood still.
5When I rose to open the door,
my hands and my fingers
dripped with perfume.
6And I yearned for him
while he spoke to me,
but when I opened the door,
my darling had disappeared.
I searched and shouted,
but I could not find him—
there was no answer.
7Then I was found by the guards
patrolling the town
and guarding the wall.
They beat me up
and stripped off my robe.
8Young women of Jerusalem,
if you find the one I love,
please say to him,
“She is weak with desire.”
Their Friends Speak:
9Most beautiful of women,
why is the one you love
more special than others?
Why do you ask us
to tell him how you feel?
She Speaks:
10He is handsome and healthy,
the most outstanding
among ten thousand.
11His head is purest gold;
his hair is wavy,
black as a raven.
12His eyes are a pair of doves
bathing in a stream
flowing with milk.
13His face is a garden
of sweet-smelling spices;
his lips are lilies
dripping with perfume.
14His arms are branches of gold
covered with jewels;
his body is ivory
decorated with sapphires.
15His legs are columns of marble
on feet of gold.
He stands there majestic
like Mount Lebanon
and its choice cedar trees.
16His kisses are sweet.
I desire him so much!
Young women of Jerusalem,
he is my lover and friend.
translation_text:
Nuu lɛ
1Minyɛmi yoo, miyɛmfro,
miba mitrom lɛ mli,
miibua mimire kɛ tsofaikɛŋmai anaa.
Miiye miwo agbaku kɛ emli wo lɛ.
Miinu miwain kɛ mifufɔ lɛ.
Yoo lɛ
Minanemɛi, nyɛyea ni nyɛnua,
ni nyɛ, suɔlɔi, nyɛnua ni nyɛtɔrɔa!
Lala ni ji ejwɛ
Yoo lɛ
2Be ni miwɔ lɛ, mitsui hiɛ kã.
Naa! Mishieŋtsɛ miishi shinaa lɛ.
Nuu lɛ
Minyɛmi yoo, misuɔlɔ!
Mikosɛɛ okpo, misuɔlɔ ni fe fɛɛ,
bɔ efɔ miyitsei ahe fɛɛ;
miyitsɔi akuklui lɛ
eyi obɔ̃ kɛ nyɔɔŋ bɔ.
Yoo lɛ
3Mijie mitade lɛ;
mɛni hewɔ mawo ekoŋŋ?
Mifɔ minaji ahe,
mɛni hewɔ mawo amɛhe muji ekoŋŋ?
4Misuɔlɔ lɛ kpã enine mli
ekɛmɔ klɔklɔ lɛ mli,
kɛkɛ ni mitsui tswa kɛ miishɛɛ.
5Mite shi ni mayagbele misuɔlɔ lɛ,
mire tsere yɛ miniji ahe,
mire ŋleŋle tsere
yɛ miwaobii ahe shwie
shinaa klɔklɔ lɛ nɔ.
6Shi be ni migbele misuɔlɔ lɛ,
etsɔ̃ ehe etee momo.
Mishwe akɛ manu egbee.
Mitao lɛ, shi minaaa lɛ.
Mitsɛ lɛ, shi ehereee mi nɔ hu.
7Bulɔi lɛ na mi
be ni amɛnyiɛ amɛbuɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ.
Amɛtswia mi nii, ni amɛpila mi.
Gbogbo nɔ bulɔi lɛ shɔ̃ mihiɛhaanɔ lɛ.
8Nyɛ Yerusalɛm biyei,
nyɛwoa mi shi veveeve akɛ
kɛji nyɛna misuɔlɔ lɛ,
nyɛkɛa lɛ akɛ,
suɔmɔ ewo mi hela.
Yei lɛ
9Bo yoo ni ohe yɔɔ fɛo
fe yei fɛɛ,
Mɛni osuɔlɔ lɛ kɛfe suɔlɔ
kroko,
hewɔ ni obiɔ akɛ wɔwo bo shi veveeve nɛɛ?
Yoo lɛ
10Misuɔlɔ lɛ he yɛ fɛo,
ni ehewolo kã.
Esoro lɛ yɛ mɛi akpei
nyɔŋma he.
11Ehiɛ tsuɔ oo,
eyitsɔi edɔrɔdrɔi;
ni ediɔ tamɔ kwãakwãalabite.
12Ehiŋmɛii tamɔ fai ahe okpoi ahiŋmɛii;
okpoi ni amɛju amɛhe kɛ fufɔ
ni amɛdamɔ fai atoi.
13Edabii tamɔ tsofakɛŋma akofii
ni miije ŋma.
Enaabu yɛ fɛo tamɔ Oflɔ fɔfɔi
ni efɔ kɛ krɔbɔo ŋleŋle.
14Eniji yɛ fɛo,
ni ewo gai ni ojarawatɛi tara mli.
Egbɔmɔtso tamɔ nɔ ko ni akɛ shuɔ wu fee,
ni akɛ safiro etara he.
15Eshuɔji tamɔ alabastro akulashiŋi,
ni mamɔ shika nibii anɔ.
Eje agbo tamɔ Lebanon gɔŋ lɛ,
ni eje oblaŋ tamɔ Lebanon tsenedrutso lɛ.
16Edaaŋ wiemɔ ŋɔɔ naakpa,
ni enɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ akɔnɔ.
Naa, nyɛ Yerusalɛm biyei,
bɔ ni misuɔlɔ,
mishieŋtsɛ lɛ yɔɔ nɛ.

english_text:

I come to my garden
and enjoy its spices.
I eat my honeycomb and honey;
I drink my wine and milk.
Their Friends Speak:

you are drunk with love.
Another Dream
She Speaks:
2I was asleep, but dreaming:
The one I love was at the door,
knocking and saying,
“My darling, my very own,
my flawless dove,
open the door for me!
My head is drenched
with evening dew.”
3But I had already undressed
and bathed my feet.
Should I dress again
and get my feet dirty?
4Then my darling's hand
reached to open the latch,
and my heart stood still.
5When I rose to open the door,
my hands and my fingers
dripped with perfume.
6And I yearned for him
while he spoke to me,
but when I opened the door,
my darling had disappeared.
I searched and shouted,
but I could not find him—
there was no answer.
7Then I was found by the guards
patrolling the town
and guarding the wall.
They beat me up
and stripped off my robe.
8Young women of Jerusalem,
if you find the one I love,
please say to him,
“She is weak with desire.”
Their Friends Speak:
9Most beautiful of women,
why is the one you love
more special than others?
Why do you ask us
to tell him how you feel?
She Speaks:
10He is handsome and healthy,
the most outstanding
among ten thousand.
11His head is purest gold;
his hair is wavy,
black as a raven.
12His eyes are a pair of doves
bathing in a stream
flowing with milk.
13His face is a garden
of sweet-smelling spices;
his lips are lilies
dripping with perfume.
14His arms are branches of gold
covered with jewels;
his body is ivory
decorated with sapphires.
15His legs are columns of marble
on feet of gold.
He stands there majestic
like Mount Lebanon
and its choice cedar trees.
16His kisses are sweet.
I desire him so much!
Young women of Jerusalem,
he is my lover and friend.

dripped with perfume.

patrolling the town
and guarding the wall.

and stripped off my robe.

more special than others?

dripping with perfume.

covered with jewels;

decorated with sapphires.

on feet of gold.

like Mount Lebanon
and its choice cedar trees.

I desire him so much!

Their Friends Speak:
1Most beautiful of women,
tell us where he has gone.
Let us help you find him.
She Speaks:
2My darling has gone down
to his garden of spices,
where he will feed his sheep
and gather lilies.
3I am his, and he is mine,
as he feeds his sheep
among the lilies.
He Speaks:
4My dearest, the cities of Tirzah
and Jerusalem
are not as lovely as you.
Your charms are more powerful
than all of the stars
in the heavens.
5Turn away your eyes—
they make me melt.
Your hair tosses about
as gracefully as goats
coming down from Gilead.
6Your teeth are whiter
than sheep freshly washed;
they match perfectly,
not one is missing.
7Behind your veil are hidden
beautiful rosy cheeks.
8What if I could have
sixty queens, eighty wives,
and thousands of others!
9You would be my only choice,
my flawless dove,
the favorite child
of your mother.
The young women, the queens,
and all the others
tell how excited you are
as they sing your praises:
10“You are as majestic
as the morning sky—
glorious as the moon—
blinding as the sun!
Your charms are more powerful
than all the stars above.”
She Speaks:
11I went down to see if blossoms
were on the walnut trees,
grapevines, and fruit trees.
12But in my imagination
I was suddenly riding
on a glorious chariot.
Their Friends Speak:
13Dance! Dance!
Beautiful woman from Shulam,
let us see you dance!
She Speaks:
Why do you want to see
this woman from Shulam
dancing with the others?
translation_text:
Yei lɛ
1Bo mɔ ni ohe yɔɔ fɛo fe fɛɛ
yɛ yei ateŋ,
nɛgbɛ osuɔlɔ lɛ etee?
Nɛgbɛ osuɔlɔ lɛ etsɔ̃,
koni wɔ kɛ bo fɛɛ ayatao lɛ?
Yoo lɛ
2Misuɔlɔ lɛ etee etrom lɛ mli,
yɛ tsofakɛŋma akofii lɛ ahe,
koni eyalɛ etooku lɛ yɛ jɛi,
koni etserɛ oflɔ fɔfɔii hu.
3Misuɔlɔ lɛ nɔ ji mi,
ni mi hu minɔ ji lɛ.
Lɛ mɔ ni elɛɔ etooku lɛ
yɛ oflɔ fɔfɔii ateŋ lɛ.
Nuu lɛ
4Mishieŋnyɛ, ohe yɛ fɛo tamɔ Tirza maŋ,
ni ohe yɛ akɔnɔ tamɔ Yerusalɛm.
Ohe yɛ gbeyei tamɔ tabilɔi
ni hiɛ aflaŋai.
5Tsɔ̃ ohiɛ oto afã
ejaakɛ ohiŋmɛii gbaa minaa.
Oyitsɔi tamɔ abotiai aku
ni miikpeleke
Gilead gɔji lɛ ahetsɔi.
6Onyanyɔji yɛɔ futaa tamɔ gwantɛŋi
ni aju amɛhe
ni amɛ fɛɛ kwa amɛfɔfɔɔ enyɔnyɔɔnyɔ
ni amɛteŋ ekome folo gboko.
7Odabii yɛ fɛo tamɔ maŋo ni etsu
yɛ ohiɛhaanɔ lɛ mli.
8 Maŋtsɛ aaahi maŋnyɛmɛi nyɔŋmai ekpaa,
kɛ hemɛi nyɔŋmai kpaanyɔ,
kɛ oblayei ni aleee amɛyibɔ moŋ nɛ;
9shi mɔ koome pɛ ji misuɔlɔ,
ni ehe yɛ fɛo tamɔ okpo.
Enyɛ suɔmɔ bi koome ji lɛ.
Enyɛ enaaa kpa ko yɛ ehe.
Oblayei lɛ na lɛ, ni amɛna ehe miishɛɛ.
Maŋnyɛmɛi kɛ lumɛi jie eyi.
10Namɔ pueɔ tamɔ leebi hulu nɛɛ,
ni ehe yɔɔ fɛo tamɔ nyɔɔŋtsere,
ni ehe tse tamɔ hulu,
ni ehe yɔɔ gbeyei tamɔ
tabilɔi ni hiɛ aflaŋai nɛɛ?
11Mikpeleke shi kɛtee tsoyibii atrom lɛ mli
koni mayakwɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli jwɛi frɔ̃frɔ̃ lɛ.
Mitee koni mayakwɛ akɛ waintsei lɛ
kɛ maŋotsei lɛ hu egba afofro lo?
12Be ni mihɛleɔ shi lɛ,
naa mi, ni mita shwiili mli,
ni mi yɛ misuɔlɔ lɛ masɛi.
Yei lɛ
13Kuu osɛɛ, kuu osɛɛ
bo Shulamyoo!
Kuu osɛɛ, kuu osɛɛ,
koni wɔkwɛ bo.
Yoo lɛ
Mɛni hewɔ nyɛbaakwɛ Shulamyoo?
Te aaafee tɛŋŋ majo joo enyɔ hu?

english_text:
Their Friends Speak:
1Most beautiful of women,
tell us where he has gone.
Let us help you find him.
She Speaks:
2My darling has gone down
to his garden of spices,
where he will feed his sheep
and gather lilies.
3I am his, and he is mine,
as he feeds his sheep
among the lilies.
He Speaks:
4My dearest, the cities of Tirzah
and Jerusalem
are not as lovely as you.
Your charms are more powerful
than all of the stars
in the heavens.
5Turn away your eyes—
they make me melt.
Your hair tosses about
as gracefully as goats
coming down from Gilead.
6Your teeth are whiter
than sheep freshly washed;
they match perfectly,
not one is missing.
7Behind your veil are hidden
beautiful rosy cheeks.
8What if I could have
sixty queens, eighty wives,
and thousands of others!
9You would be my only choice,
my flawless dove,
the favorite child
of your mother.
The young women, the queens,
and all the others
tell how excited you are
as they sing your praises:
10“You are as majestic
as the morning sky—
glorious as the moon—
blinding as the sun!
Your charms are more powerful
than all the stars above.”
She Speaks:
11I went down to see if blossoms
were on the walnut trees,
grapevines, and fruit trees.
12But in my imagination
I was suddenly riding
on a glorious chariot.
Their Friends Speak:
13Dance! Dance!
Beautiful woman from Shulam,
let us see you dance!
She Speaks:
Why do you want to see
this woman from Shulam
dancing with the others?

english_text:
The Wedding Dance
He Speaks:
1You are a princess,
and your feet are graceful
in their sandals.
Your thighs are works of art,
each one a jewel;
2your navel is a wine glass
filled to overflowing.
Your body is full and slender
like a bundle of wheat
bound together by lilies.
3Your breasts are like twins
of a deer.
4Your neck is like ivory,
and your eyes sparkle
like the pools of Heshbon
by the gate of Bath-Rabbim.
Your nose is beautiful
like Mount Lebanon
above the city of Damascus.
5Your head is held high
like Mount Carmel;
your hair is so lovely
it holds a king prisoner.
6You are very beautiful,
so desirable!
7You are tall and slender
like a palm tree,
and your breasts are full.
8I will climb that tree
and cling to its branches.
I will discover that your breasts
are clusters of grapes,
and that your breath
is the aroma of apples.
9Kissing you is more delicious
than drinking the finest wine.
How wonderful and tasty!
She Speaks:
10My darling, I am yours,
and you desire me.
11Let's stroll through the fields
and sleep in the villages.
12At dawn let's slip out and see
if grapevines and fruit trees
are covered with blossoms.
When we are there,
I will give you my love.
13Perfume from the magic flower
fills the air, my darling.
Right at our doorstep
I have stored up for you
all kinds of tasty fruits.
translation_text:
Nuu lɛ
1Bo lumɔ biyoo,
Onajifãamɔi yɛ otokotai amli
yɛ fɛo naakpa!
Oshuɔji yɛ fɛo
tamɔ jwinei ni ŋaalɔ nukpa kɛ eniji fee.
2Olaŋmɔ tamɔ likɔlikɔ kokroo
ni wain ni ŋɔɔ etãko yɛ mli dã.
Omusu tamɔ ŋmãa ku,
ni akɛ oflɔ fɔfɔii etserɛ he.
3Ofufɔi tamɔ ofrote bii enyɔ,
loo tamɔ soŋaibii hãaji.
4Okuɛ kɛ tamɔ shuɔwu mɔɔ.
Ohiŋmɛii tamɔ Heshbon kpaakpoi
ni yɔɔ Bat-Rabbim maŋ lɛ agbo
lɛ he lɛ.
Ogugɔ yɛ fɛo tamɔ Lebanon mɔɔ
ni kwɔ ni hiɛ kwɛɔ Damasko gbɛ lɛ.
5Oyitso ni ma onɔ tamɔ Karmel Gɔŋ;
Oyitsɔi akuklui tamɔ mama afaseo.
Oyitsɔi fɛo lɛ ŋɔɔ maŋtsɛ nom.
6Mishieŋnyɛ, ohe yɛ fɛo,
ni ohe yɛ akɔnɔ akɛ nɔ ko.
7Oje oblaŋ tamɔ tɛŋ,
ni ofufɔi tamɔ ŋmedurui.
8Mikɛɛ, “Makwɔ tɛŋ lɛ,
ni mamɔmɔ eniji lɛ amli.
Ao, mina ofufɔi tamɔ
waintso yibii ŋmedurui,
ni mumɔ ni jɛɔ ogugɔ mli jeɔ
ŋma tamɔ aadɔŋ.”
Yoo lɛ
9Mina ni onaashwɔmɔ ŋɔɔmɔ
tamɔ wain kpakpa fe fɛɛ
ni tsɔ̃ɔ naabu kɛ nyanyɔŋ teŋ,
kɛyaa omusuŋ tɔ̃ɔ.
10Mi lɛ, misuɔlɔ lɛ nɔ ji mi.
Ni mi ji mɔ ni eshweɔ.
11Misuɔlɔ, ba ni wɔtee ŋa lɛ nɔ,
ni wɔyato gbɔ
yɛ akrowai lɛ amli.
12Hã wɔte shi maŋkɛ mra,
ni wɔya waintromii lɛ amli,
ni wɔyakwɛ akɛ waintso lɛ miifrɔke
ni eegba afofro,
ni maŋotsei lɛ hu
egba afofro lo?
Jɛi mikɛ misuɔmɔ baahã bo yɛ.
13Ao! Misuɔlɔ suɔmɔ yibii lɛ miije ŋma,
ni tso yibii ni jara wa srɔtoi fɛɛ yɛ wɔshinaa lɛ shi.
Mikɛ ememeji kɛ ehei fɛɛ eto ehã bo.

english_text:
If Only You and I …
She Speaks:
1If you were my brother,
I could kiss you
whenever we happen to meet,
and no one would say
I did wrong.
2I could take you to the home
of my mother,
who taught me all I know.
I would give you delicious wine
and fruit juice as well.
3Put your left hand under my head
and embrace me
with your right arm.
4Young women of Jerusalem,
promise me never to awaken love
before it is ready.
Their Friends Speak:
5Who is this young woman
coming in from the desert
and leaning on the shoulder
of the one she loves?
She Speaks:
I stirred up your passions
under the apple tree
where you were born.
6Always keep me in your heart
and wear this bracelet
to remember me by.
The passion of love
bursting into flame
is more powerful than death,
stronger than the grave.
7Love cannot be drowned
by oceans or floods.
It cannot be bought—
any offer would be scorned
no matter how great.
Their Friends Speak:
8We have a little sister
whose breasts
are not yet formed.
If someone asks to marry her,
what should we do?
9She isn't a wall
that we can defend
behind a silver shield.
Neither is she a room
that we can protect
behind a wooden door.
She Speaks:
10I am a wall around a city,
my breasts are towers,
and just looking at me
brings him great pleasure.
11Solomon has a vineyard
at Baal-Hamon,
which he rents to others
for a thousand pieces
of silver each.
12My vineyard is mine alone!
Solomon can keep his silver
and the others can keep
their share of the profits.
He Speaks:
13You are in the garden
with friends all around.
Let me hear your voice!
She Speaks:
14Hurry to me, my darling!
Run faster than a deer
to mountains of spices.
translation_text:
1Ao, mina ni kulɛ
minyɛmi nuu ni ye minyɛ fufɔ ji bo.
Kulɛ kɛ mina bo yɛ agbo naa
ni mishwɔ onaa lɛ,
mɔ ko shwaŋ mi po.
2Kulɛ manyiɛ ohiɛ kɛya minyɛ we lɛ,
manyiɛ ohiɛ kɛya minyɛ awo ni fɔ mi sɛɛtsuŋ.
Ni mahã bo wain ni jeɔ ŋma onu;
ni tamɔ migranata dãa.
3Mina ni kulɛ miyitso tsɔle enine abɛku
ni ekɛ eninejurɔ efua mi atuu.
4Nyɛ Yerusalɛm biyei,
nyɛwoa mi shi veveeve akɛ,
nyɛhosoŋ misuɔlɔ lɛ,
ni nyɛkatsiɛ̃a ehiɛ hu,
kɛyaashi be ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ esumɔɔ.
Lala ni ji ekpaa
Yei lɛ
5Namɔ ji yoo nɛɛ
ni jɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ baa
ni ekɛ esuɔlɔ ela kɛ baa nɛɛ?
Mi mitsiɛ̃ ohiɛ yɛ akututso lɛ shishi,
jɛi ji he ni onyɛ kɔ̃mɔ bo yɛ,
jɛi onyɛ ni fɔ bo lɛ kɔ̃mɔ bo yɛ.
Yoo lɛ
6Sɔomɔ minaa owo otsui mli
tamɔ adikiɔ nine he lɛ.
Okɛ yoo ko yoo ko akala,
ja mi pɛ.
Ejaakɛ suɔmɔ he wa tamɔ gbele;
ni awuŋayeli hu yi wa tamɔ gbele.
Ehereɔ tamɔ la,
ni etsoɔ grigri.
7Nu babaoo po nyɛɛɛ suɔmɔ agbe,
ni nu afua tete nyɛɛɛ lɛ ashiu.
Kɛji mɔ ko ŋɔ eshĩaŋ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ehã
ekɛmiihe suɔmɔ lɛ,
ŋmɔ abaaŋmɔ lɛ.
Yoo lɛ nyɛmimɛihii lɛ
8Wɔyɛ nyɛmi yoo fioo ko
ni ejeko fufɔ.
Mɛni wɔɔfee wɔhã wɔnyɛmi yoo nɛɛ,
gbi ni aaaba akɛ abaatsɛ ehebaa lɛ?
9Eji gbogbo ji lɛ kulɛ
wɔɔma jwiɛtɛi mɔɔ ni kwɔ
wɔma enɔ.
Eji shinaa ji lɛ kulɛ
wɔkɛ tsenedrutsei ŋmoŋmolo aaaha ehe.
Yoo lɛ
10Mi lɛ, gbogbo ji mi,
ni mifufɔi mamɔ shi tamɔ mɔji.
Ni yɛ misuɔlɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ,
mitsui nyɔɔ mimli,
ni minaa hejɔlɛ.
Nuu lɛ
11Solomon yɛ waintrom ko ni atsɛɔ jɛi Baal-Hammon.
Ekɛ waintrom lɛ hã mɛi ni amɛhu mli.
Amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ woɔ jwiɛtɛi kukuji akpe
akɛ adɔde.
12Miwaintrom, ni ji mi diɛŋtsɛ minɔ lɛ,
mikoome minɔ ni.
Bo Solomon, ooona akpe lɛ,
ni mɛi ni ji apaafoi lɛ aaana ohai enyɔ.
13Ao, bo mɔ ni oyɔɔ abɔi lɛ amli,
minanemɛi lɛ miibo ogbee toi.
Hã mi hu manu ogbee lɛ.
Yoo lɛ
14Ohe afee oya, misuɔlɔ,
ofoi awa tamɔ soŋai,
tamɔ ofrote oblanyo
yɛ tsofakɛŋma gɔji lɛ anɔ.

english_text:
1 I am Isaiah, the son of Amoz.
And this is the message that I was given about Judah and Jerusalem when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah:
A Guilty Nation
2The Lord has said,
“Listen, heaven and earth!
The children I raised
have turned against me.
3Oxen and donkeys know
who owns and feeds them,
but my people won't ever learn.”
4Israel, you are a sinful nation
loaded down with guilt.
You are wicked and corrupt
and have turned from the Lord,
the holy God of Israel.
5Why be punished more?
Why not give up your sin?
Your head is badly bruised,
and you are weak all over.
6From your head to your toes
there isn't a healthy spot.
Bruises, cuts, and open sores
go without care
or oil to ease the pain.
A Country in Ruins
7Your country lies in ruins;
your towns are in ashes.
Foreigners and strangers
take and destroy your land
while you watch.
8Enemies surround Jerusalem,
alone like a hut
in a vineyard
or in a cucumber field.
9 Zion would have disappeared
like Sodom and Gomorrah,
if the Lord All-Powerful
had not let a few
of its people survive.
Justice, Not Sacrifices
10You are no better
than the leaders and people
of Sodom and Gomorrah!
So listen to the Lord God:
11 “Your sacrifices
mean nothing to me.
I am sick of your offerings
of rams and choice cattle;
I don't like the blood
of bulls or lambs or goats.
12“Who asked you to bring all this
when you come to worship me?
Stay out of my temple!
13Your sacrifices are worthless,
and your incense disgusting.
I can't stand the evil you do
on your New Moon Festivals
or on your Sabbaths
and other times of worship.
