He doesn't have sex with someone else's wife or with a woman having her monthly period. 7He never cheats or robs anyone and always returns anything taken as security for a loan; he gives food and clothes to the poor 8and doesn't charge interest when lending money. He refuses to do anything evil; he is fair to everyone 9 and faithfully obeys my laws and teachings. This man is good, and I promise he will live.
10But suppose this good man has an evil son who is violent and commits sins 11his father never did. He eats meat at local shrines, has sex with someone else's wife, 12cheats the poor, and robs people. He keeps what is given to him as security for a loan. He worships idols, does disgusting things, 13and charges high interest when lending money. An evil man like that will certainly not live. He is the one who has done these horrible sins, so it's his own fault that he will be put to death.
14But suppose this evil man has a son who sees his father do these things and refuses to act like him. 15He doesn't eat meat at local shrines or worship Israel's idols, and he doesn't have sex with someone else's wife. 16He never cheats or robs anyone and doesn't even demand security for a loan. He gives food and clothes to the poor 17and refuses to do anything evil or to charge interest. And he obeys all my laws and teachings. Such a man will live. His own father sinned, but this good man will not be put to death for the sins of his father. 18It is his father who will die for cheating and robbing and doing evil.
19You may wonder why a son isn't punished for the sins of his father. It is because the son does what is right and obeys my laws. 20 Only those who sin will be put to death. Children won't suffer for the sins of their parents, and parents won't suffer for the sins of their children. Good people will be rewarded for what they do, and evil people will be punished for what they do.
21Suppose wicked people stop sinning and start obeying my laws and doing right. They won't be put to death. 22All their sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they did right. 23I, the Lord God, don't like to see wicked people die. I had much rather see them turn back from their sins and live.
24But when good people start sinning and doing disgusting things, will they live? No! All their good deeds will be forgotten, and they will be put to death because of their sins.
25You people of Israel accuse me of being unfair! But listen—I'm not unfair; you are! 26If good people start doing evil, they must be put to death, because they have sinned. 27And if wicked people start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment. 28They will think about what they've done and stop sinning, and so they won't be put to death. 29But you still say that I am unfair. You are the ones who have done wrong and are unfair!
30I will judge each of you for what you've done. So stop sinning, or else you will certainly be punished. 31Give up your evil ways and start thinking pure thoughts. And be faithful to me! Do you really want to be put to death for your sins? 32 I, the Lord God, don't want to see that happen to anyone. So stop sinning and live!
translation_text:
Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ gbɛnaa nitsumɔ
1Yehowa kɛ mi wie ekoŋŋ ni ekɛɛ, 2 “Mɛni ji shishinumɔ ni nyɛkɛbuɔ abɛ nɛɛ yɛ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ he akɛ, ‘Tsɛmɛi lɛ eye wainyibii ŋmilikitii, ni bii lɛ moŋ anyanyɔji eshwã’ lɛ?
3“Gbii abɔ ni mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ lɛ nɛɛ, nyɛbuŋ nɛkɛ abɛ nɛɛ dɔŋŋ yɛ Israel.” Yehowa kɛɛ. 4“Naa, gbɔmɛi fɛɛ awala lɛ, minɔ ni. Bɔ ni tsɛ wala ji minɔ lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ bi hu nɔ ji minɔ. Gbɔmɔ ni feɔ esha lɛ, lɛ nɔŋŋ eeegbo.
5“Ŋɔɔ lɛ akɛ mɔ ko yɛ ni ji jalɔ, ni eyeɔ jalɛ sane, ni efeɔ nɔ ni ja. 6 Eyeee nii ni akɛshã afɔle ahã wɔji yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ. Ni ewooo ehiɛ nɔ ekwɛɛɛ Israel we lɛ wɔji lɛ tete, ni enyiɛɛɛ enaanyo ŋa sɛɛ, ni ebɛŋkɛɛɛ yoo ni etee tsuiasɛɛ. 7 Ewaaa mɔ yi; shi ekpaleɔ nyɔmɔtsɛ awabatoonii ehãa lɛ; ni etswaaa ojo; ehaaa mɔ ko nɔ ko, shi moŋ ehãa mɔ ni hɔmɔ miiye lɛ nii eyeɔ; asaŋ mɔ ni nyiɛ yayai lɛ ebuɔ lɛ mama.
8 “Ekɛ shika efaaa ni ehe hekpa fe nine. Ewiɔ ehe yɛ eshafeemɔ he, ni ekojoɔ mɔ kɛ mɔ teŋ yɛ jalɛ naa. 9 Ebaa ejeŋ yɛ mikpɔi lɛ anaa, ni eyeɔ mimlai lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nɛkɛ gbɔmɔ lɛ jalɔ ji lɛ, eyi aaana wala kɛ̃, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.
10“Agbɛnɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ akɛ nɛkɛ gbɔmɔ nɛɛ fɔ binuu yiwalɔ kɛ gbɔmɔgbelɔ. 11Bi nɛɛ efeee nii ni sa feemɔ nɛɛ ateŋ ekoeko; shi moŋ eyeɔ nii ni akɛshãa afɔle ahãa wɔji yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ; ni enyiɛɔ enaanyo ŋa sɛɛ. 12Ewaa ohiafo kɛ mɔ ni efi lɛ yi. Etswaa ojo, ni ekpaleee nyɔmɔtsɛ awabatoonii ehãaa lɛ. Ejaa amãgã, ni efeɔ musubɔɔnii. 13Efaa shika ni eheɔ hekpa fe nine. Aso nɛkɛ gbɔmɔ yi aaana wala? Eyi naŋ wala. Akɛni efee nɛkɛ musubɔɔnii nɛɛ fɛɛ eko hewɔ lɛ gbo kɛ̃ eeegbo; ela aaabua lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eyiteŋ.
14“Shi agbɛnɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ akɛ nɛkɛ gbɔmɔ nɛɛ fɔ binuu ko, ni ebinuu nɛɛ na eshai fɛɛ ni etsɛ lɛ efee lɛ, ni eshe gbeyei, ni efeee nakai eshai lɛ eko. 15Ni eyeee nii ni akɛshã afɔle ahã wɔji yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ, ni ejaaa Israel we lɛ amãgãi lɛ ekoeko. Ni enyiɛɛɛ enaanyo ŋa sɛɛ. 16Ni efeee mɔ ko efɔŋ, eheee mɔ ko awabatoonii; etswaaa mɔ ko ojo. Shi moŋ ehãa mɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ aboloo, asaŋ mɔ ni nyiɛ yayai lɛ, ebuɔ lɛ mama. 17Ewiɔ ehe yɛ eshafeemɔ he, ni ekɛ shika efaaa ni ehe hekpa ni fe nine. Ni eyeɔ mimlai lɛ anɔ, ni ebaa ejeŋ yɛ mikpɔi lɛ anaa. Nɛkɛ gbɔmɔ lɛ egboŋ yɛ eshai ni etsɛ efee lɛ ahewɔ, shi moŋ eyi aaana wala kɛ̃. 18Shi etsɛ lɛ, akɛni etswaa ojo, ni ejuɔ enyɛmi, ni efeɔ nɔ ni ehiii yɛ emaŋbii ateŋ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, lɛ lɛ, gbo eeegbo yɛ ehe eshai lɛ ahewɔ.
19“Kɛ̃lɛ nyɛbiɔ akɛ, ‘Mɛɛ hewɔ esaaa akɛ bi naa amanehului yɛ esha ni etsɛ efee hewɔ?’ Kɛji bi lɛ yeɔ jalɛ sane, ni efeɔ nɔ ni ja, ni eyeɔ mikpɔi lɛ fɛɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, no lɛ esa akɛ eyi ana wala kɛ̃. 20 Gbɔmɔ ni feɔ esha lɛ gbo eeegbo. Bi enaŋ amanehulu yɛ eshai ni etsɛ efee ahewɔ, ni tsɛ hu enaŋ amanehulu yɛ eshai ni ebii efee ahewɔ. Jalɔ aaana ejalɛnii ni efee lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo, ni mɔ fɔŋ hu aaana efɔŋ ni efee lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo.
21“Shi kɛji eshafeelɔ fɔ̃ɔ eshai fɛɛ ni efeɔ, ni eye mikpɔi lɛ fɛɛ anɔ, ni eye jalɛ sane, ni efee nɔ ni ja lɛ, eyi aaana wala kɛ̃, egboŋ. 22 Tɔ̃mɔi ni etɔ̃ lɛ akaiŋ ekoeko dɔŋŋ, akɛaafa lɛ. Ejalɛnii ni efee lɛ hewɔ lɛ eyi aaana wala. 23Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa miibi akɛ, “Aso minyaa efɔŋfeelɔ gbele he lo? Dabida, nɔ ni mitaoɔ moŋ ji akɛ etsake ejeŋba koni eyi ana wala.”
24 “Shi kɛji jalɔ fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni ja feemɔ ni efee esha, ni efee musubɔɔ nii ni mɔfɔŋ feɔ lɛ, aso eyi aaana wala lo? Jalɛnii ni efee lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, akaiŋ ekoeko. Etɔmɔi ni etɔ̃ lɛ kɛ eshai ni efee lɛ, eeegbo yɛ nomɛi ahewɔ.
25“Kɛ̃lɛ nyɛkɛɔ akɛ Nuŋtsɔ lɛ yeee jalɛ sane. Ao, nyɛ Israelbii, nyɛboa toi ko! Ani mi, miyeee jalɛ sane? Ani jeee nyɛ moŋ ni nyɛyeee jalɛ sane? 26Kɛji jalɔ fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni ja feemɔ, ni efee efɔŋ lɛ, gbo eeegbo yɛ no hewɔ. Ebaagbo yɛ efɔŋ ni efee lɛ hewɔ. 27Asaŋ kɛji mɔ fɔŋ fɔ̃ɔ eshai ni efeɔ lɛ fɛɛ, ni eye mikpɔi lɛ anɔ, ni efee nɔ ni ja ni ehi lɛ, eeehere eyiwala. 28Ejaakɛ ekɔ eyiŋ, ni efɔ̃ɔ enifɔɔji anii lɛ fɛɛ ni efee lɛ, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ, eyi aaana wala kɛ̃, egboŋ. 29Kɛ̃lɛ, Israelbii lɛ kɛɔ akɛ, ‘Nuŋtsɔ lɛ yeee jalɛ sane.’ Ao, nyɛ Israelbii, ani mi ni miyeee jalɛ sane lo? Ani jeee nyɛ moŋ ni nyɛyeee jalɛ sane?
30 “No hewɔ lɛ, Ao, nyɛ Israelbii, makojo nyɛ, makojo nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ yɛ enifeemɔ nii anaa. Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ. Nyɛtsakea nyɛtsuiiaŋ, ni nyɛfɔ̃a nyɛnifɔɔjianii lɛ fɛɛ; koni nyɛnifɔɔjianii lɛ akakpãtã nyɛhiɛ. 31Nyɛkpaa efɔŋ fɛɛ efɔŋ ni nyɛfee nyɛshi mi lɛ feemɔ, ni nyɛtsakea nyɛtsuiiaŋ ni nyɛnaa mumɔ hee. Ao, Israelbii, shi mɛɛba ni nyɛaagboi? 32Minyaaa mɔ ko mɔ ko gbele he. Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛtsakea nyɛtsuiiaŋ koni nyɛyi anaa wala.”

english_text:
A Funeral Song for Israel's Leaders
The Lord said:
1Ezekiel, sing a funeral song for two of Israel's leaders:
2Your mother was a brave lioness
who raised her cubs
among lions.
3She taught one of them to hunt,
and he learned to eat people.
4When the nations heard of him,
they trapped him in a pit,
then they used hooks
to drag him to Egypt.
5His mother waited
for him to return.
But soon she lost all hope
and raised another cub,
who also became fierce.
6He hunted with other lions
and learned to eat people.
7He destroyed fortresses
and ruined towns;
his mighty roar
terrified everyone.
8Nations plotted to kill him,
and people came from all over
to spread out a net
and catch him in a trap.
9They put him in a cage
and took him to Babylonia.
The lion was locked away,
so that his mighty roar
would never again be heard
on Israel's hills.
10Your mother was a vine like you,
growing near a stream.
There was plenty of water,
so she was filled with branches
and with lots of fruit.
11Her strong branches
became symbols of authority,
and she was taller
than all other trees—
everyone could see how strong
and healthy she was.
12But in anger, I pulled her up
by the roots
and threw her to the ground,
where the scorching desert wind
dried out her fruit.
Her strong branches wilted
and burned up.
13Then she was planted
in a hot, dry desert,
14where her stem caught fire,
and flames burned
her branches and fruit.
Not one strong branch is left;
she is stripped bare.
This funeral song must be sung with sorrow.
translation_text:
Awerɛho lalawiemɔ
1Wo yaafo lala nɔ
okɛfo Israel lumɛi lɛ, ni okɛɛ akɛ,
2“Ani onyɛ lɛ jeee jatayoo ni?
Ni ebu jata oblahii ateŋ
ni elɛ ebii lɛ yɛ amɛteŋ?
3Ni etsɔse ebii lɛ ateŋ ekome
ni etsɔ̃ jata oblanyo;
ekase loomɔmɔ,
ni eyeɔ gbɔmɔ tete?
4 Jeŋmaji lɛ bɔ ehe oshe;
ni adu lɛ yɛ amɛbu lɛ mli;
ni amɛkɛ kpoji gbala lɛ
kɛtee Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.
5Be ni enyɛ mɛ aahu lɛ,
ehiɛnɔkãmɔ tã.
Esaa eŋɔ ebii lɛ ateŋ ekroko
efee jata oblanyo.
6 Be ni eda etsɔ̃ jata oblanyo lɛ
ekɛ jatai lɛ nyiɛ aahu.
Ekase gbɔbimɔ
ni eyeɔ gbɔmɔ tete.
7Ejwra amɛ mɔji, ni efite maji hu;
ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii lɛ she gbeyei
yɛ ehuumɔ lɛ gbɛɛmɔ hewɔ.
8Kɛkɛ ni jeŋmaji lɛ gba wo lɛ kɛkpe,
ni amɛfɔ̃ enɔ yaa,
ni adu lɛ yɛ amɛbu lɛ mli.
9 Ni amɛkɛ kpoji gbala lɛ
amɛwo kooloi adeka mli;
ni amɛkɛ lɛ yahã Babilon Maŋtsɛ lɛ,
ni akɛ lɛ to mɔɔ lɛ mli;
bɔ ni afee ni akanu egbee
yɛ Israel gɔji lɛ anɔ dɔŋŋ.
10 Onyɛ tamɔ waintso
ni atɛo yɛ faa toi;
egbala niji, ni ewo yibii babaoo,
ejaakɛ enaa nu pii.
11Eniji lɛ na hewalɛ
tamɔ maŋtsɛ tsi.
Ni ewo ekwɔlɛ nɔ yɛ
niji kusukusuu lɛ ateŋ.
Ni ana ekwɔlɛ kɛ eniji kusukusuu lɛ.
12Shi akɛ mlila fã lɛ kɛ eshishi fɛɛ
ni ashɛ lɛ afɔ̃ shikpɔŋ,
ni bokã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbi lɛ,
ni eyibii lɛ kpala,
ni etso ni wa lɛ gbi,
ni eshã wɛɛ.
13Agbɛnɛ afã lɛ ayatɛo
yɛ ŋa nɔ,
yɛ shikpɔŋ gbiŋ ni nu bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.
14Ni la jɛ tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mli
ni eshã eniji lɛ
kɛ eyibii lɛ fɛɛ;
ni tso bɛ emli dɔŋŋ
ni aaanyɛ akɛfee maŋtsɛ tsi dɔŋŋ.
Awerɛho lala nɛɛ alaa akɛyeɔ ŋkɔmɔ daa.

english_text:
Israel Keeps On Rebelling
1Seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, some of Israel's leaders came to me on the tenth day of the fifth month. They sat down and asked for a message from the Lord. 2Just then, the Lord God said:
3Ezekiel, son of man, these leaders have come to find out what I want them to do. As surely as I live, I will not give them an answer of any kind.
4Are you willing to warn them, Ezekiel? Then remind them of the disgusting sins of their ancestors.
5 Tell them that long ago I, the Lord God, chose Israel to be my own. I appeared to their ancestors in Egypt and made a solemn promise that I would be their God and the God of their descendants. 6I swore that I would rescue them from Egypt and lead them to a land I had already chosen. This land was rich with milk and honey and was the most splendid land of all. 7I told them to get rid of their disgusting idols and not to sin by worshiping the gods of Egypt. I reminded them that I was the Lord their God, 8but they still rebelled against me. They refused to listen and kept on worshiping their idols and foreign gods.
In my anger, I decided to punish the Israelites in Egypt. 9But that would have made me look like a liar, because I had already promised in front of everyone that I would lead them out of Egypt. 10So I brought them out and led them into the desert. 11 I gave them my laws and teachings, so they would know how to live right. 12 And I commanded them to respect the Sabbath as a way of showing that they were holy and belonged to me. 13But the Israelites rebelled against me in the desert. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath like any other day.
Then in my anger, I decided to destroy the Israelites in the desert once and for all. 14But that would have disgraced me, because many other nations had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt. 15 Instead, I told them in the desert that I would not lead them into the beautiful, fertile land I had promised. 16I said this because they had not only ignored my laws and teachings, but had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped idols.
17Yet, I felt sorry for them and could not let them die in the desert. 18So I warned the children not to act like their parents or follow their evil ways or worship their idols. 19I reminded them that I was the Lord their God and that they should obey my laws and teachings. 20I told them to respect my Sabbath to show that they were my people and that I was the Lord their God. 21But the children also rebelled against me. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath as any other day.
I became angry and decided to punish them in the desert. 22But I did not. That would have disgraced me in front of the nations that had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt. 23 So I solemnly swore that I would scatter the people of Israel across the nations, 24because they had disobeyed my laws and ignored my teachings; they had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped the idols their ancestors had made. 25I gave them laws that bring punishment instead of life, 26and I let them offer me unacceptable sacrifices, including their first-born sons. I did this to horrify them and to let them know that I, the Lord, was punishing them.
27Ezekiel, tell the people of Israel that their ancestors also rejected and insulted me 28by offering sacrifices, incense, and wine to gods on every hill and under every large tree. I was very angry, because they did these things in the land I had given them! 29I asked them where they went to worship those gods, and they answered, “At the local shrines.” And those places of worship are still called shrines.
30Then ask the Israelites why they are following the example of their wicked ancestors 31by worshiping idols and by sacrificing their own children as offerings. They commit these sins and still think they can ask me for a message. As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will give them no answer. 32They may think they can be like other nations and get away with worshiping idols made of wood and stone. But that will never happen!
The Lord Promises To Restore Israel
The Lord said to the people of Israel:
33As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will rule over you with my powerful arm. You will feel my fierce anger 34and my power, when I gather you from the places where you are scattered 35and lead you into a desert surrounded by nations. I will meet you there face to face. Then I will pass judgment on you 36and punish you, just as I punished your ancestors in the desert near Egypt. 37I will force each of you to obey the regulations of our solemn agreement. 38I will separate the sinful rebels from the rest of you, and even though I will bring them from the nations where they live in exile, they won't be allowed to return to Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
39Go ahead and worship your idols for now, you Israelites, because soon I will no longer let you dishonor me by offering gifts to them. You will have no choice but to obey me! 40When that day comes, everyone in Israel will worship me on Mount Zion, my holy mountain in Jerusalem. I will once again call you my own, and I will accept your sacred offerings and sacrifices. 41When I bring you home from the places where you are now scattered, I will be pleased with you, just as I am pleased with the smell of the smoke from your sacrifices. Every nation on earth will see that I am holy, 42and you will know that I, the Lord, am the one who brought you back to Israel, the land I promised your ancestors. 43Then you will remember your wicked sins, and you will hate yourselves for doing such horrible things. They have made you unacceptable to me, 44so you deserve to be punished. But I will treat you in a way that will bring honor to my name, and you will know that I am the Lord God.
Fire from the South
45The Lord said, 46“Ezekiel, son of man, turn toward the south and warn the forests 47that I, the Lord God, will start a fire that will burn up every tree, whether green or dry. Nothing will be able to put out the blaze of that fire as it spreads to the north and burns everything in its path. 48Everyone will know that I started it, and that it cannot be stopped.”
49But I complained, “Lord God, I don't want to do that! People already say I confuse them with my messages.”
translation_text:
Nyɔŋmɔ suɔmɔnaanii kɛ gbɔmɔ atuatsemɔ
1Yɛ wɔnomŋɔɔ afi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ, nyɔŋ ni ji enumɔ lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma lɛ nɔ lɛ, Israel onukpai lɛ ateŋ mɛi komɛi ba miŋɔɔ koni amɛbabi Yehowa nii. Amɛbatara shi yɛ mihiɛ. 2Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ, 3 “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, okɛ Israel maŋ onukpai nɛɛ awie ni okɛɛ amɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, ani mi nibimɔ nyɛbaa nɛɛ? Gbii abɔ ni mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ lɛ nɛɛ, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ, Mihaŋ nyɛbi mi nii. 4Ani oookojo amɛ, Gbɔmɔ Adesa? Ani oookojo amɛ? Belɛ hã amɛle musubɔɔnii ni amɛtsɛmɛi lɛ fee lɛ, ni okɛɛ amɛ akɛ, 5Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, gbi ni miŋɔ Israel lɛ mikã Yakob shwiei lɛ akitã ni mihã amɛle mi yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mikã amɛ kitã akɛ, ‘Mi ji Yehowa, nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.’ 6 Nakai gbi lɛ mikã amɛ kitã akɛ majie amɛ kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ ko ni mito miha amɛ lɛ nɔ; shikpɔŋ ni hi ni ebaa nii, ni eji shikpɔji lɛ ateŋ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ. 7 Mikɛɛ amɛ akɛ, nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ashɛrɛ musubɔɔnii ni ehiŋmɛii nyaa he lɛ eshwie; ni nyɛkɛ Ijipt wɔji lɛ akabulea nyɛhe! Mi ji Yehowa nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ! 8Shi amɛtse mihiɛ atua, ni amɛbooo mi toi. Amɛteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko shɛrɛɛɛ musubɔɔnii ni ehiŋmɛii nyaa he lɛ eshwieee, ni Ijipt wɔji lɛ hu ahewɔ lɛ, mito miyiŋ akɛ mikɛ mlila kɛ mlifu aaafee amɛ efɔŋ yɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. 9 Shi kɛ̃lɛ, mifeee; mitsake miyiŋtoo lɛ yɛ migbɛi hewɔ, bɔ ni afee ni mikagbe migbɛi lɛ he guɔ yɛ jeŋmaji ni amɛyɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ ahiɛ, mɛi ahiɛ ni mihã amɛle mi yɛ, be ni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.
10“No hewɔ lɛ, mijie amɛ kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni mikɛ amɛ ba ŋa lɛ nɔ. 11 Miwo amɛ mlai kɛ akpɔi lɛ, ni kɛ gbɔmɔ ye nɔ ni eyi aaana wala lɛ. 12 Asaŋ miŋɔ mihejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ mihã amɛ, koni nomɛi atsɔ̃ okadi yɛ mi kɛ amɛteŋ, koni amɛkɛle akɛ mi Yehowa, mi ji mɔ ni tsuɔ amɛhe.
13“Shi Israel we lɛ tse mihiɛ atua yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ; amɛbaaa amɛjeŋ yɛ mimlai lɛ anaa, shi moŋ amɛkwa mikpɔi ni kɛ gbɔmɔ ye nɔ ni eyi aaana wala lɛ; ni amɛbule mihejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ hu naakpa. No hewɔ lɛ, mito miyiŋ akɛ mikɛ mimlila aaaplene amɛ yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ kwrakwra. 14Shi kɛ̃lɛ, mitsake miyiŋtoo lɛ, bɔ ni afee ni akagbe migbɛi lɛ he guɔ yɛ jeŋmaji ni amɛyɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ ahiɛ; mɛi ahiɛ ni mi mijie Israel kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. 15 Asaŋ mikã amɛ kitã yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ akɛ mikɛ amɛ baŋ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛhã amɛ lɛ nɔ; shikpɔŋ ni hi ni ebaa nii, ni eji shikpɔji lɛ ateŋ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ.
16“Ejaakɛ amɛkwa mimlai lɛ, ni amɛbaaa amɛjeŋ yɛ mikpɔi lɛ anaa. Ni amɛbule mihejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ; ejaakɛ amɛkɛ amɛtsui fɛɛ hã amɛwɔji lɛ. 17Kɛ̃lɛ mina amɛ mɔbɔ, ni mikpãtãaa amɛhiɛ ni mipleneee amɛ kwrakwra yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ.
18“Mikɛɛ amɛbii yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ akɛ, ‘Nyɛkabaa nyɛjeŋ yɛ nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ amlai lɛ anaa, ni nyɛkayea amɛkpɔi lɛ anɔ, ni nyɛkɛ amɛwɔji lɛ akabulea nyɛhe. 19Yehowa, mi ji nyɛNyɔŋmɔ; nyɛbaa nyɛjeŋ yɛ mimlai lɛ moŋ anaa; ni nyɛyea mimlai lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. 20Ni nyɛfea mihejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ koni nomɛi atsɔ̃ okadi yɛ mi kɛ nyɛ teŋ; koni nyɛkɛle akɛ mi, Yehowa, mi ji nyɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ.’
21“Shi nyɛbii lɛ hu tse mihiɛ atua; amɛbaaa amɛjeŋ yɛ mlai lɛ anaa, ni amɛyeee mikpɔi lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ; mlai ni kɛji gbɔmɔ ye nɔ ni eyi aaana wala lɛ; amɛbule mihejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ hu. Kɛkɛ ni mito miyiŋ akɛ mafee amɛ efɔŋ yɛ mimlifu kɛ mimlila naa yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ, 22Shi kɛ̃lɛ, mitsake miyiŋtoo lɛ, bɔ ni afee ni akagbe migbɛi lɛ he guɔ yɛ jeŋmaji ni amɛyɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ ahiɛ; mɛi ahiɛ ni mi, mijie Israelbii lɛ yɛ, kɛje Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. 23Kɛ̃lɛ, mikã amɛ kitã yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ akɛ magbɛ amɛ mashwã jeŋmaji lɛ ateŋ, ni magbɛ amɛ mashwã shikpɔji lɛ anɔ; 24ejaakɛ amɛyeee mikpɔi lɛ anɔ, shi moŋ amɛkwa mimlai lɛ, ni amɛbule mihejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ, ni amɛhiɛ yakɔ̃ amɛtsɛmɛi lɛ awɔji lɛ anɔ.
25“No hewɔ lɛ, mi hu miwo amɛ mlai ni ehiii, kɛ akpɔi ni haŋ amɛna wala. 26 Mibule amɛ kɛtsɔ̃ amɛnikeenii anɔ, no ji amɛkromɔbii ni amɛgbe kɛshã afɔle lɛ, koni mahã amɛhe ajɔ̃ amɛhe. Mifee enɛ, koni amɛkɛna amɛle akɛ, mi ji Yehowa.
27“No hewɔ lɛ, Gbɔmɔ Adesa, kɛɛmɔ Israel we lɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, enɛ mli hu nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ bɔ musu amɛshi mi yɛ, ejaakɛ amɛyeee mi anɔkwa. 28Ejaakɛ be ni mihã amɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikã kitã akɛ mikɛaahã amɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, gɔŋkpɔ fɛɛ gɔŋkpɔ ni kwɔ, loo tso kusuu fɛɛ tso kusuu ni amɛaana lɛ, amɛyashãa amɛ afɔlei lɛ yɛ jɛi, ni amɛkɛ afɔleshãa nɛɛ wo mimli la; jɛi nɔŋŋ amɛshãa amɛtsofakɛŋmai lɛ yɛ, ni jɛi nɔŋŋ amɛfɔse amɛdãa afɔle lɛ amɛshwie shi yɛ. 29Mibi amɛ akɛ, mɛni ji nakai he grɔŋŋ lɛ ni nyɛyaa lɛ? No hewɔ atsɛɔ jɛi akɛ ‘He Grɔŋŋ’ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ. 30No hewɔ lɛ, kɛɛmɔ Israel we lɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, ani nyɛaabule nyɛhe tamɔ nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ fee lɛ; ani nyɛaanyiɛ amɛmusubɔɔnii lɛ asɛɛ ni nyɛdu gbɛ? 31 Gbii abɔ ni nyɛkɛ nyɛnikeenii yahãa wɔji, ni nyɛgbeɔ nyɛbihii nyɛkɛshãa afɔlei nyɛhãa amɛ lɛ, nyɛmiibule nyɛhe kɛ nɛkɛ nyɛwɔji nɛɛ ajamɔ kɛbashi ŋmɛnɛ. Ao, Israel we, nyɛmiiba ni nyɛbabi mi nii? Gbii abɔ ni mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ lɛ nɛɛ, mihaŋ nyɛbi mi nii! Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ. 32Nɔ ni nyɛsusuɔ ni nyɛkɛɔ akɛ, wɔɔtamɔ jeŋmaji kɛ shikpɔji anɔ wekui lɛ, ni wɔsɔmɔ tso kɛ tɛ lɛ, ebaŋ mli kɔkɔɔkɔ.”
Nyɔŋmɔ gbalaa toi, ni ekɛfaa
33Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Gbii abɔ ni mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ hiɛkãalɔ lɛ nɛɛ lɛ, mikɛ nineshiwalɛ kɛ hewalɛ kɛ mlila ni naa wa baaye nyɛnɔ maŋtsɛ. 34Mikɛ nineshiwalɛ kɛ hewalɛ kɛ mlila baajie nyɛ kɛaajɛ shikpɔji ni agbɛ nyɛ ashwã amɛnɔ lɛ anɔ. 35 Ni mikɛ nyɛaaba majimaji lɛ ateŋ ni mabua nyɛnaa kɛaajɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ, ni jɛi magbala nyɛtoi yɛ hiɛ kɛ hiɛ.”
36 Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Bɔ ni migbala nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ atoi yɛ Ijipt ŋa lɛ nɔ lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ magbala nyɛ hu nyɛtoi.
37“Maha nyɛtsɔ̃ kplamɔtso lɛ shishi, ni makane nyɛ ekomekome mawo kpãŋmɔ mli. 38Ni majie atuatselɔi lɛ kɛ mɛi ni etɔ̃ minɔ lɛ kɛaaje nyɛteŋ. Majie amɛ kɛaajɛ he ni amɛyato gbɔ yɛ lɛ moŋ nɛ, shi amɛnane yiŋ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No dani nyɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.”
39Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ, “Ao, nyɛ Israel we, (nyɛ lɛ kɛji nyɛboŋ mi toi lɛ, kɛjɛ kɛyaa nɛɛ lɛ) nyɛyaa ni nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ayasɔmɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewɔji lɛ; shi kɛfee sɛɛ lɛ nyɛabo mi toi kɛ̃, ni migbɛi krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ nyɛkɛ nyɛnikeenii lɛ kɛ nyɛwɔŋjamɔ lɛ babuleŋ lɛ dɔŋŋ.” 40Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ, “Shi migɔŋ krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ, ni ji Israel Gɔŋ ni kwɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, jɛi Israel we lɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aaasɔmɔ mi yɛ; mana amɛhe tsui yɛ jɛi, ni mabi nyɛfɔlei lɛ kɛ nyɛnikeenii kpakpai lɛ kɛ nyɛkeenii krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ fɛɛ shi. 41Kɛji mijie nyɛ kɛjɛ majimaji lɛ amli, ni mibua nyɛnaa kɛjɛ shikpɔji ni agbɛ nyɛ ashwã nɔ lɛ anɔ kɛba lɛ, mana nyɛhe tsui tamɔ nɔ ko ni jeɔ ŋma, ni majie mikrɔŋkrɔŋ ni mi ji lɛ kpo matsɔ̃ɔ yɛ nyɛteŋ ni majimaji aaana. 42Kɛji mikɛ nyɛ bashɛ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shikpɔŋ ni mikã he kitã akɛ maŋɔ hã nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ, no nyɛkɛaale akɛ mi ji Yehowa. 43Ni jɛi nyɛaakai nyɛjeŋba kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni nyɛfee ni nyɛkɛbule nyɛhe lɛ yɛ, ni nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛhe aaafee nyɛ nyaŋemɔ yɛ nifɔɔjianii fɛɛ ni nyɛfee lɛ hewɔ. 44Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, nyɛ Israel we, kɛji mikɛnyɛ ye yɛ migbɛi lɛ hewɔ, shi jeee yɛ nyɛjeŋba gbohii lɛ ahewɔ, loo nyɛnifeemɔnii gbohii lɛ ahewɔ lɛ, no nyɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.”
Wuoyigbɛ la lɛ
45Yehowa kɛmi wie ni ekɛɛ, 46“Gbɔmɔ Adesa, tsɔ̃ ohiɛ ohã wuoyigbɛ; wiemɔ oshi Yuda wuoyigbɛ lɛ; gbaa oshi wuoyigbɛ koo lɛ. 47Kɛɛmɔ Yuda wuoyigbɛ koo lɛ akɛ, bo Yehowa wiemɔ toi. Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ: naa, mawo la yɛ omli, ni eeeshã omli tso ŋmɔŋ fɛɛ tso ŋmɔŋ, kɛ tso gbiŋ fɛɛ tso gbiŋ. La ni tsoɔ grigri lɛ agbeŋ, ni eeeshã he fɛɛ he kɛaajɛ wuoyigbɛ aahu kɛyashi kooyigbɛ tɔ̃ɔ. 48Gbɔmɛi fɛɛ baana akɛ mi, Yehowa, mi miwo la lɛ, ni anyɛŋ agbe.” 49Kɛkɛ ni mikɛɛ akɛ, “Ao, Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ, amɛkɛɔ yɛ mihe akɛ, ‘Ani jeee abɛbuaŋ sɔŋŋ ewieɔ yɛ?’ ”

english_text:
The Lord Will Punish Jerusalem
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the places in Jerusalem where people worship. Warn everyone in Israel 3that I am about to punish them. I will pull out my sword and have it ready to kill everyone, whether good or evil. 4From south to north, people will die, 5knowing that my sword will never be put away.
6Ezekiel, groan in sorrow and despair so that everyone can hear you. 7When they ask why you are groaning, tell them you have terrifying news that will make them faint and tremble in fear and lose all courage. These things will happen soon. I, the Lord God, make this promise!
A Sword Is Ready To Attack Israel
8The Lord said:
9-10Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Jerusalem:
I have sharpened my sword
to slaughter you;
it is shiny and will flash
like lightning!
Don't celebrate—
punishment is coming,
because everyone has ignored
my warnings.
11My sword has been polished;
it's sharp and ready to kill.
12Groan in sorrow, Ezekiel;
the sword is drawn against
my people and their leaders.
They will die!
So give up all hope.
13I am testing my people,
and they can do nothing
to stop me.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
14Ezekiel, warn my people,
then celebrate my victory
by clapping your hands.
My vicious sword will attack
again and again,
killing my people
with every stroke.
15They will lose all courage
and stumble with fear.
My slaughtering sword
is waiting at every gate,
flashing and ready to kill.
16It will slash right and left,
wherever the blade is pointed.
17Then I will stop being angry,
and I will clap my hands
in victory.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The King of Babylonia and His Sword
18The Lord said:
19Ezekiel, son of man, mark two roads for the king of Babylonia to follow when he comes with his sword. The roads will begin at the same place, but be sure to put up a signpost where the two roads separate and go in different directions. 20Clearly mark where the two roads lead. One goes to Rabbah, the capital of Ammon, and the other goes to Jerusalem, the fortified capital of Judah. 21When the Babylonian king stands at that signpost, he will decide which way to go by shaking his arrows, by asking his idols, and by carefully looking at the liver of a sacrificed animal. 22His right hand will pull out the arrow marked “Jerusalem.” Then he will immediately give the signal to shout the battle cry, to build dirt ramps up to the top of the city walls, to break down its walls and gates with large wooden poles, and to kill the people. 23Everyone in Jerusalem had promised to be loyal to Babylonia, and so none of them will believe that this could happen to them. But Babylonia's king will remind them of their sinful ways and warn them of their coming captivity.
24Ezekiel, tell the people of Jerusalem and their ruler that I, the Lord God, am saying:
Everything you do is wicked and shows how sinful you are. You are guilty and will be taken away as prisoners.
25And now, you evil and wicked ruler of Israel, your day of final punishment is almost here. 26I, the Lord God, command you to take off your royal turban and your crown, because everything will be different. Those who had no power will be put in charge, and those who now rule will become nobodies. 27I will leave Jerusalem in complete ruins like no one has ever seen until my chosen one comes to punish this city.
Judgment against Ammon
28 The Lord God said:
Ezekiel, son of man, the Ammonites have insulted Israel, so condemn them and tell them I am saying:
A sword is drawn,
ready to slaughter;
it is polished and prepared
to kill as fast as lightning.
29You wicked Ammonites see false visions and believe untrue messages. But your day of punishment is coming soon, and my sword will slaughter you!
30Your days to punish others are over, so put your swords away. You will be punished in the land of your birth. 31My furious anger will scorch you like fire, and I will hand you over to cruel men who are experts in killing. 32You will be burned and will die in your own land. Then you will be forgotten forever. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Yehowa klante lɛ
1Yehowa kɛ miwie ni ekɛɛ, 2“Gbɔmɔ Adesa, tsɔ̃ ohiɛ oha Yerusalɛm ni oshiɛ oshi hei krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ, he ni ajaa yɛ lɛ; gbaa oshi Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ, 3ni okɛɛ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, naa, mikɛ bo ena, ni magbala miklante lɛ kɛaaje ehebo lɛ mli, ni mikɛaagbe jalɔ kɛ mɔfɔŋ fɛɛ yɛ nyɛteŋ. 4Akɛni makpãtã jalɔ kɛ mɔfɔŋ fɛɛ hiɛ kɛaaje nyɛteŋ hewɔ lɛ mafã miklante lɛ kɛjɛ ehebo lɛ mli mawo gbɔmɛi kɛjɛ wuoyigbɛ aahu kɛyashi kooyigbɛ tɔ̃ɔ. 5No gbɔmɛi fɛɛ kɛaana ale akɛ, mi Yehowa mifã miklante kɛjɛ ehebo lɛ mli; ni akɛwoŋ ehebo lɛ mli dɔŋŋ.
6“No hewɔ lɛ, bo, Gbɔmɔ Adesa, hũumɔ kɛ tsui ni ekumɔ, hũumɔ kɛ awerɛho kpele yɛ amɛhiɛ. 7Ni kɛji amɛbi bo akɛ, ‘Mɛni hewɔ ohũɔ lɛ?’ Okɛɛ akɛ, ‘Saji ni minu lɛ hewɔ ni. Kɛji eba mli lɛ, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ baashe gbeyei, ni kɔ̃ɔji fɛɛ baakplɔke, ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ baatsɔ̃ feetɔ, ni nakutsei fɛɛ tswɛm baakpokpo tamɔ ayawaŋ nu. Naa, be lɛ eshɛ, ni ebaaba mli kɛ̃;’ ” Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.
8Yehowa kɛ mi wie ekoŋŋ akɛ, 9 “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, gbaa ni okɛɛ akɛ, nɔ ni mi, Nuŋtsɔ, mikɛɔ nɛ,
Klante! Klante! Ajɔ klante naa,
ni asha he kaŋkaŋ.
10Ajɔ naa koni akɛgbe mɔ;
asha he ni ekpɛ kaŋkaŋ
tamɔ srawa.
Aso wɔmli afili wɔ?
Mibi, ogbe kpãa kɛ tsɔsemɔ fɛɛ tsɔsemɔ he guɔ.
11Hewɔ lɛ akɛ klante lɛ ehã
ni asha he,
koni afee lɛ kralo kɛhã nitsumɔ.
Ajɔ naa, ni asha he kaŋkaŋ
koni akɛwo mɔgbelɔ lɛ dɛŋ.
12Gbɔmɔ Adesa, wo yara ni ofo,
ejaakɛ afã klante awo miwebii lɛ.
Afã klante awo Israel lumɛi fɛɛ.
Ajɔɔ amɛ kɛ miwebii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ
ahã klante;
hewɔ lɛ, nyɛyia nyɛhe ma.
13Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa miibi, akɛ,
‘Nyɛjwɛŋa he jogbaŋŋ,
ani nyɛsusuɔ akɛ
kɛ nyɛkwa tsɔsemɔ lɛ
toigbalamɔ lɛ baŋ lo?’ ”
14“Gbɔmɔ Adesa, no hewɔ lɛ, gbaa. Tswaa odɛ̃ koni klante lɛ ni baagbe mɛi lɛ abamɔ amɛ nɔtonɔto. No ji klante ni baakpãtã mɛi babaoo ahiɛ lɛ; ni no hewɔ lɛ, gbele ebɔle amɛhe kɛkpe; 15koni amɛshe gbeyei, ni mɛi babaoo agbeegbee shi hewɔ mitsɔ̃ klante lɛ naa mihã maŋ lɛ agboi lɛ anaa. Mikɛ klante ni kpɛlɛɔ tamɔ srawa lɛ ehã. Ehe miikpɛ tamɔ srawa. Asha he kɛha mɔgbee. 16Klante, bãa kɛya ninejurɔ ni obã kɛya abɛku, tsɔ̃ ohe ni ofo kɛya he fɛɛ he. Hã enyɔ loo mli. 17Mi hu matswa midɛ̃, ni mimlifu lɛ naa aba shi. Mi, Yehowa, miwie.”
Babilon Maŋtsɛ lɛ klante lɛ
18Yehowa kɛ mi wie ekoŋŋ ni ekɛɛ, 19“Gbɔmɔ Adesa, kadimɔ gbɛjegbɛi enyɔ nɔ ni Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ eklante lɛ aaanyɛ atsɔ̃ nɔ kɛba lɛ. Gbɛi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ aaanyɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛba. Too gbɛtsɔ̃ɔmɔ okadi oma maŋ lɛ ŋmaŋmasha lɛ. 20Okadi lɛ ekome atsɔ̃ɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ gbɛ ni ekɛ eklante lɛ atsɔ̃ nɔ kɛba Raba, ni ji Amonbii lɛ amaŋ lɛ mli; okadi kroko lɛ atsɔ̃ɔ gbɛ kɛya Yuda shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛbote Yerusalɛm ni atswa gbogbo awo ehe lɛ mli tɔ̃ɔ. 21Ejaakɛ Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ damɔ gbɛnta lɛ naa, yɛ he ni gbɛi enyɔ lɛ gbaa akloŋta yɛ lɛ. Ebaahoso gãimlibii kɛkla ni eeebi emãgãi lɛ anii, ni eeekwɛ afɔle kooloo ni agbe lɛ mlɛbo mli fitsofitso. 22Eklamɔ lɛ tsɔ̃ɔ lɛ akɛ etsɔ̃ ninejurɔgbɛ kɛya Yerusalɛm, koni ebɔ ta oshe, ni awo naa nɔ abolɔ, ni aŋɔ gbogbokuumɔnii apiŋ agboi lɛ ahe, ni atswa kpokui ni amãmɔ mɔji ni wa. 23Eeefee Yerusalɛmbii lɛ akɛ klamɔ ni bɛ mli ni, ejaakɛ amɛkɛ maji ekpãŋ, shi moŋ esa akɛ amɛkai amɛnɔsha lɛ akɛ abaamɔmɔ amɛ.” 24No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, “Akɛni nyɛha ana eshai ni nyɛfee lɛ, ni nyɛnifɔɔjianii eje kpo yɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni nyɛfeɔ mli, ni mikai nyɛ hewɔ lɛ abaamɔmɔ nyɛ kɛya nomŋɔɔ mli. 25Bo Israel lumɔ, yiwalɔ ni he tseee, bo ni obe eshɛ kɛhã onaagbee toigbalamɔ, 26bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ bo nɛ, Jiemɔ oyifiinɔ lɛ, ni jiemɔ okekre lɛ yɛ oyitso. Nibii ehiŋ shi tamɔ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ nɛɛ dɔŋŋ; nɔ ni eba shi lɛ, awo nɔ; ni nɔ ni awo nɔ lɛ, aba lɛ shi. 27 Butumɔ! Butumɔ! Butumɔ mabutu maŋ lɛ. Anaŋ he okadi ko kwraa kɛyaashi mɔ gbɛnaa ni ji lɛ aaaba, ni lɛ maŋɔ hã.”
Klante lɛ kɛ Amonbii lɛ
28 “Ni bo Gbɔmɔ Adesa, gbaa ni okɛɛ Amonbii lɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nyɛ yɛ ahora ni amɛbɔɔ Israel lɛ he nɛ; kɛɛmɔ akɛ: ‘Klante, agbala klante kɛhã gbɔmɔgbee; asha he kaŋkaŋ, ni ekpɛ tamɔ srawa.’ ”
29“Nii ni nyɛnaa lɛ amale ninaa ni, ni nyɛgbalɛi hu amale gbalɛi ni, koni nyɛkɛ sɔ̃ lɛ afɔ̃ lumɛi kɛ mɛi fɔ̃ji ni egboi lɛ anɔ. Amɛ lɛ, amɛnaagbee hiɛkpãtãmɔ be lɛ eshɛ. 30Kɛ klante awo ehebo lɛ mli, Makojo bo yɛ he ni abɔ bo yɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ojɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. 31Mimli baawo bo la, ni mimlifu ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tamɔ la lɛ aaaba onɔ; ni majie bo mawo hii dikalɔi yitsoŋwalɔi ni le nifitemɔ he ŋaa lɛ adɛŋ. 32Nyɛbaatsɔ̃ latɛ naa lai; aaashwie nyɛlá shi akpa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; ni akaiŋ nyɛ dɔŋŋ; ejaakɛ mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.”

english_text:
Jerusalem Is Condemned
1Some time later, the Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, are you ready to condemn Jerusalem? That city is filled with murderers, so remind the people of their sins 3and tell them I am saying:
Jerusalem, you have murdered many of your own people and have worshiped idols. You will soon be punished! 4Those crimes have made you guilty, and the idols have made you unacceptable to me. So your final punishment is near. Other nations will laugh at you and make insulting remarks, 5and people far and near will make fun of your misery.
6Your own leaders use their power to murder. 7 None of you honor your parents, and you cheat foreigners, orphans, and widows. 8 You show no respect for my sacred places and treat the Sabbath just like any other day. 9Some of your own people tell lies, so that others will be put to death. Some of you eat meat sacrificed to idols at local shrines, and others never stop doing vulgar things. 10 Men have sex with their father's wife or with women who are having their monthly period 11or with someone else's wife. Some men even sleep with their own daughter-in-law or half sister. 12 Others of you accept money to murder someone. Your own people charge high interest when making a loan to other Israelites, and they get rich by cheating. Worst of all, you have forgotten me, the Lord God.
13I will shake my fist in anger at your violent crimes. 14When I'm finished with you, your courage will disappear, and you will be so weak that you won't be able to lift your hands. I, the Lord, have spoken and will not change my mind. 15I will scatter you throughout every nation on earth and put a stop to your sinful ways. 16You will be humiliated in the eyes of other nations. Then you will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things.
Jerusalem Must Be Purified
17The Lord said:
18Ezekiel, son of man, I consider the people of Israel as worthless as the leftover metal in a furnace after silver has been purified. 19So I am going to bring them together in Jerusalem. 20-21I will be like a metalworker who collects that metal from the furnace and melts it down. I will collect the Israelites and blow on them with my fiery anger. They will melt inside the city of Jerusalem 22like silver in a furnace. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them in my anger.
Everyone in Jerusalem Is Guilty
23The Lord said:
24Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel that their country is full of sin, and that I, the Lord, am furious! 25Their leaders are like roaring lions, tearing apart their victims. They put people to death, then steal everything of value. Husbands are killed, and many women are left as widows.
26 The priests of Israel ignore my Law! Not only do they refuse to respect any of my sacred things, but they don't even teach the difference between what is sacred and what is ordinary or between what is clean and what is unclean. They treat my Sabbath like any other day, and so my own people no longer honor me.
27Israel's officials are like ferocious wolves, ripping their victims apart. They make a dishonest living by injuring and killing people.
28And then the prophets in Israel cover up these sins by giving false visions. I have never spoken to them, but they lie and say they have a message from me. 29The people themselves cheat and rob; they abuse the poor and take advantage of foreigners.
30I looked for someone to defend the city and to protect it from my anger, as well as to stop me from destroying it. But I found no one. 31So in my fierce anger, I will punish the Israelites for what they have done, and they will know that I am furious. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Nifɔɔjianii ni Yerusalɛm fee lɛ
1Yehowa kɛ mi wie ekoŋŋ akɛ, 2“Bo Gbɔmɔ Adesa, ani oookojo, ani oookojo maŋ ni ashwieɔ lá shi yɛ mli lɛ? Belɛ hã ele emusubɔɔnii ni efee lɛ fɛɛ. 3Kɛɛmɔ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, maŋ ni ashwieɔ lá shi yɛ emli, asaŋ ni efeɔ amãgãi ni ekɛbuleɔ ehe lɛ; ebe aaashɛ, 4lá shi ni oshwie kɛ amãgãi ni ofee okɛbule ohe lɛ hewɔ lɛ oye fɔ; ehã ogbii lɛ ebɛŋkɛ; afii ni ato ahã bo lɛ eshɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, miha jeŋmaji lɛ miibɔ bo ahora, ni shikpɔji lɛ fɛɛ miiye ohe fɛo. 5Mɛi ni bɛŋkɛ bo kɛ mɛi ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ aaaye ohe fɛo, bo mɔ ni ohe guɔ egbo, ni basabasafeemɔ eyi omli obɔ̃. 6Naa, Israel lumɛi ni yɔɔ omli lɛ, amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ tswaa efai shi akɛ ebaashwie lá shi yɛ omli, bɔ ni eeenyɛ. 7 Abuuu tsɛ kɛ nyɛ yɛ omli, ayeɔ gbɔ amim yɛ omli; awaa awusa kɛ okulafo yi yɛ omli. 8 Obuuu minii krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ, ni obuleɔ mihejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ. 9Mɛi yɛ nyɛteŋ ni yeɔ osheku, bɔ ni afee ni ashwie mɛi alá shi; mɛi komɛi yɛ nyɛteŋ ni amɛyeɔ afɔlei ni ashã ahã amãgãi lɛ, ni mɛi komɛi hu yɛ nyɛteŋ ni bɔɔ nyɛnyɛŋtswi. 10 Mɛi komɛi kɛ amɛtsɛmɛi aŋamɛi naa bɔlɛ yɛ omli, ni mɛi komɛi tuaa yei ni etee tsuiasɛɛ, ni amɛhe tseee lɛ yɛ omli. 11Mɔ kɛ enaanyo ŋa naa bɔlɛ; mɔ ko hu kɛ ebinuu ŋa naa bɔlɛ; mɔ ko hu kɛ enyɛmiyoo ni ji etsɛbi naa bɔlɛ yɛ omli. 12 Mɛi heɔ nyɔɔŋnii, koni ashwie lá shi yɛ omli; aheɔ hekpa ni fe nine, ni atswaa nanemɛi ojo. Nyɛhiɛ ekpa minɔ.” Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.
13“No hewɔ lɛ, mitswa midɛ̃ mishwie onɔ yɛ shishiumɔnii ni ona kɛ lá shi ni oshwie yɛ omli lɛ hewɔ. 14Gbi ni mikɛ bo aaaye lɛ, aso ooonyɛ naa odamɔ? Aloo ooonyɛ onine nɔ po owo? Mi, Yehowa, miwie, ni mafee. 15Magbɛ omlibii lɛ mashwã jeŋmaji kɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ, ni mikɛaatsuu ohe muji lɛ mashwie. 16Ni ohe guɔ baagbo yɛ jeŋmaji lɛ ahiɛ, ni ooona ole akɛ mi ji Yehowa lɛ.”
Nyɔŋmɔ niiahetsuumɔ flɔnɔɔ lɛ
17Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ, 18 “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, Israel we lɛ etsɔ̃ tamɔ shika shishi ehã mi. Amɛ fɛɛ kwa lɛ, jwiɛtɛi kɛ akɔɔble kɛ sanyaa kɛ dade kɛ sumui ni asere yɛ flɔnɔɔ mli lɛ shishi muji ji amɛ. 19No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ nɛ, ‘Akɛni nyɛ blublu nyɛtsɔmɔ shika shishi hewɔ lɛ, naa, mabua nyɛnaa mawo Yerusalɛm, 20taakɛ bɔ ni mɛi buaa jwiɛtɛi kɛ akɔɔble kɛ dade kɛ sumui kɛ tsɛnsi naa amɛwoɔ flɔnɔɔ mli ni ahuɔ la awoɔ he, ni asereɔ lɛ, nakai mikɛ mlifu kɛ mlila aaabua nyɛnaa, ni mikɛ nyɛ aaawo la mli ni masere nyɛ. 21Mabua nyɛnaa ni mahuu mimlifu mlila lɛ mashwie nyɛnɔ, ni nyɛbaasere. 22Bɔ ni jwiɛtɛi sereɔ yɛ flɔnɔɔ mli lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ aaasere nyɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm; ni nyɛaana nyɛle akɛ mi, Yehowa, mi mihuu mimlila lɛ mishwie nyɛnɔ.’ ”
Israel Hiɛnyiɛlɔi lɛ ahe eshai lɛ
23Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa kɛ mi wie ekɛɛ, 24“Gbɔmɔ Adesa, kɛɛmɔ Israel akɛ, bo ji shikpɔŋ ko ni ohe tseee, ni nu hu enɛŋ onɔ yɛ mimlifu be lɛ mli. 25 Emli lumɛi lɛ tamɔ jatai ni huuɔ ni amɛmiitserɛ amɛmilɛ loo mli; amɛkpãtã gbɔmɛi awala ahiɛ; amɛshɔ̃ mɛi ajwetri kɛ nii ni jara wa yɛ amɛdɛŋ; amɛhã yei pii etsɔmɔ okulafoi yɛ Yerusalɛm. 26 Omli osɔfoi lɛ ku mimlai lɛ amli, ni amɛbule minii krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ; amɛhãaa ana srɔto ni yɔɔ nɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni abule teŋ; asaŋ amɛtsɔ̃ɔɔ srɔto ni yɔɔ nɔ ni he tse kɛ nɔ ni he tseee teŋ, ni amɛbuuu mihejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ, ni no hewɔ lɛ, abule mi yɛ amɛteŋ.
27“Emli lumɛi lɛ tamɔ klãji ni tserɛɔ milɛloo mli, amɛshwieɔ lá shi, amɛkpãtãa mɛi ahiɛ, bɔ ni afee ni amɛwo shishiumɔ ninamɔ. 28Emli gbalɔ lɛ maleɔ ekɛhaa eshai nɛɛ anɔ tamɔ akɛ kaaloo shaa gbogbo he lɛ. Amɛnaa amale ninaa, ni amɛgbaa amale gbalɛi akɛ, ‘Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ.’ Be mli ni mi, Yehowa miwieko tete. 29Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niiatsɛmɛi lɛ tswaa ojo, ni amɛjuɔ; amɛwaa ohiafoi kɛ mɛi ni efi amɛ lɛ ayi, ni amɛyeɔ gbɔ amim, ni atooo lɛ najiaŋ. 30Hewɔ lɛ, mitao akɛ mana mɔ ko kɛjɛ amɛteŋ ni eeetswa gbogbo ni ewule lɛ, ni eeebu folɔ lɛ naa yɛ mihiɛ ehã shikpɔŋ lɛ, koni mikafite lɛ; shi minaaa mɔ ko mɔ ko. 31No hewɔ lɛ, mimli wo amɛ la, ni mikɛ mlifu plenee amɛ, ni miha amɛmusu ebua amɛyiteŋ.” Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_text:
Two Sinful Sisters
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, listen to this story about two sisters. 3While they were young and living in Egypt, they became prostitutes. 4The older one was named Oholah, which stands for Samaria; the younger one was Oholibah, which stands for Jerusalem. They became my wives and gave birth to my children.
5Even though Oholah was my wife, she continued to be a prostitute and chased after Assyrian lovers. 6She offered herself to soldiers in purple uniforms: handsome, high-ranking officers and cavalry troops. 7She had sex with all the important Assyrian officials and even worshiped their disgusting idols. 8Once she started doing these things in Egypt, she never stopped. Men slept with her, and she was always ready for sex.
9So I gave Oholah to the Assyrian lovers she wanted so badly. 10They ripped off her clothes, then captured her children and killed her. Women everywhere talked about what had happened to Oholah.
11Oholibah saw all this, but she was more sinful and wanted sex more than her sister Oholah ever did. 12Oholibah also chased after good-looking Assyrian officers, uniformed soldiers, and cavalry troops. 13Just like her sister, she did vulgar things.
14But Oholibah behaved worse than her sister. Oholibah saw images of Babylonian men carved into walls and painted red. 15They had belts around their waists and large turbans on their heads, and they reminded her of Babylonian cavalry officers. 16As soon as she looked at them, she wanted to have sex with them. And so, she sent messengers to bring them to her. 17Men from Babylonia came and had sex with her so many times that she got disgusted with them. 18She let everyone see her naked body and didn't care if they knew she was a prostitute. That's why I turned my back on her, just as I had done with her older sister.
19Oholibah didn't stop there, but became even more immoral and acted as she had back in Egypt. 20She eagerly wanted to go to bed with Egyptian men, who were famous for their sexual powers. 21And she longed for the days when she was a young prostitute, when men enjoyed caressing her body.
The Lord Will Punish Oholibah
22The Lord God said:
Oholibah, though you no longer want to be around your lovers, they will surround you like enemies, when I turn them against you. 23I will gather all the handsome young officials and the high-ranking cavalry officers from Babylonia and Assyria, as well as from the Chaldean tribes of Pekod, Shoa, and Koa. 24Their large armies will come from the north with chariots and wagons carrying weapons. They will wear shields and helmets and will surround you, and I will let them judge and sentence you according to their own laws. 25I am angry with you, so I will let them be very cruel. They will cut off your nose and ears; they will kill your children and burn alive anyone in your family who survives. 26Your clothes and jewelry will be torn off. 27I will stop your wickedness and the prostitution you started back in Egypt. You will never want to think about those days again.
28I, the Lord God, am ready to hand you over to those hateful enemies that you find so disgusting. 29They will cruelly take away everything you have worked for and strip you naked. Then everyone will see you for the prostitute you really are. Your own vulgar sins 30have led to this. You were the one determined to have sex with men from other nations and to worship their idols. 31You have turned out no better than your older sister, and now you must drink from the cup filled with my anger.
32I, the Lord God, gave your sister a large, deep cup filled with my anger. And when you drink from that cup, you will be mocked and insulted. 33You will end up drunk and devastated, because that cup is filled with horror and ruin. 34But you must drink every drop! Then smash the cup and chew on its broken pieces. Use them to cut your breasts in sorrow. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
35You have completely rejected me, and so I promise that you will be punished for the disgusting things you did as a prostitute.
The Two Sisters Are Condemned
36The Lord said:
Ezekiel, son of man, it's time for you to tell Oholah and Oholibah that they are guilty. Remind them of their evil ways! 37They have been unfaithful by worshiping idols, and they have committed murder by sacrificing my own children as offerings to idols. 38-39They came into my temple that same day, and that made it unfit as a place to worship me. They have even stopped respecting the Sabbath.
40They sent messengers to attract men from far away. When those men arrived, the two sisters bathed themselves and put on eye shadow and jewelry. 41They sat on a fancy couch, and in front of them was a table for the olive oil and incense that had belonged to me. 42Their room was always filled with a noisy crowd of drunkards brought in from the desert. These men gave the women bracelets and beautiful crowns, 43and I noticed that the men were eager to have sex with these women, though they were exhausted from being prostitutes. 44In fact, the men had sex over and over with Oholah and Oholibah, the two sinful sisters. 45But honest judges will someday accuse those two of murder and of being unfaithful, because they are certainly guilty.
46So I, the Lord God, now say to these sisters:
I will call together an angry mob that will abuse and rob you. 47They will stone you to death and cut you to pieces; they will kill your children and burn down your houses. 48I will get rid of sinful prostitution in this country, so that women everywhere will be warned not to act as you have. 49You will be punished for becoming prostitutes and for worshiping idols. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_text:
Nyɛmimɛiyei eshafeelɔi lɛ
1Yehowa kɛ mi wie akɛ, 2“Gbɔmɔ Adesa, yei enyɔ komɛi, ni ji yoo kome musuŋbii hi shi. 3Be ni amɛ ji oblayei yɛ Ijipt lɛ amɛbɔ ajwamãŋ yɛ jɛi, ni jɛi atara amɛfufɔi ahe yɛ, ni jɛi hu afite amɛ yɛ. 4Onukpa lɛ gbɛi ji Ohola, ni fioo lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ Oholiba. Mikɛ amɛ hi shi, ni mikɛ amɛ fɔfɔɔ bihii kɛ biyei. Ohola damɔ shi kɛha Samaria, ni Oholiba damɔ shi kɛhã Yerusalɛm. 5Ohola je misɛɛ ni eyabɔ ajwamãŋ, ni ehiɛ yakɔ̃ esuɔlɔi lɛ ni ji Asiriabii lɛ anɔ. 6Tabilɔi ni woɔ afaseo atadei ji amɛ; amraloi kɛ lumɛi kɛ oblahii ni he yɔɔ akɔnɔ kɛ okpɔŋɔnɔtalɔi sɔŋŋ ji amɛ. 7Asiria hii ni ajegbɛ ahala lɛ fɛɛ lɛ ekɛ amɛ bɔ ajwamãŋ; ni mɛi fɛɛ ni ehiɛ kɔ̃ amɛnɔ lɛ, eja amɛwɔji lɛ, ni ekɛbule ehe. 8Efɔ̃ko ajwamãŋbɔɔ ni ebɔi kɛjɛ Ijipt lɛ, ejaakɛ hii kɛ lɛ wɔ eblayeiaŋ ni amɛmiamia eblayeiaŋ kpokpoai lɛ, ni amɛhiɛ lɛ basabasa tamɔ ajwamãŋ ko. 9No hewɔ lɛ, mitu lɛ miwo esuɔlɔi lɛ ni ji Asiriabii ni ehiɛ kɔ̃ amɛnɔ lɛ adɛŋ. 10Amɛ jie eyayaiaŋ kpo amɛmɔmɔ ebihii kɛ ebiyei lɛ; ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ amɛkɛ klante gbe lɛ; ni etsɔ wiemɔ ni yei kɛyeɔ fɛo akɛ akojo lɛ.
11“Oholiba na nɔ ni ba enyɛmi yoo Ohola nɔ lɛ nɛ; shi kɛ̃lɛ ehiɛkɔ̃ɔ lɛ naa wa fe Ohola nɔ lɛ, ni ejwamaŋbɔɔ lɛ hu fe enyɛmi yoo lɛ nɔ lɛ. 12Oholiba hiɛ kɔ̃ Asiriabii ni ji amralofoi kɛ lumɛi kɛ tabilɔi ni ewula kɛ tayaa atadei kɛ okpɔŋɔnɔtalɔi, ni ji oblahii ni he yɔɔ akɔnɔ lɛ anɔ. 13Kɛkɛ ni mina akɛ ebule ehe, ni amɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ amɛnyiɛ gbɛ kome nɔ.
14“Shi Oholiba tee nɔ lolo kɛ ejwamaŋbɔɔ lɛ; ena Babilon hii mfonirii ni akɛ atiifɔ tsuru etɛŋ yɛ gbogbo he. 15Ena akɛ amɛkɛ hɛfiinii efimɔ amɛhɛi, ni amɛkɛ yitsofiinii kakadaji efimɔ amɛyitsei; mfoniri nɛɛ mli bii lɛ tamɔ Babilon lumɛi ni afɔ yɛ Kaldea shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. 16Be ni ena amɛfonirii lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ ehiɛ kɔ̃ amɛnɔ, ni etsu bɔfoi kɛtee lumɛi nɛɛ aŋɔɔ yɛ Babilon. 17Kɛkɛ ni Babilon hii lɛ ba eŋɔɔ, ni amɛkɛ lɛ bawɔ, ni amɛkɛ ajwamãŋbɔɔ lɛ bule lɛ. Agbɛnɛ be ni ekɛ amɛ ewo ehe muji egbe naa lɛ amɛje etsine. 18Bɔ ni ebɔ ajwamãŋ faŋŋ lɛ, ni ejie eyayaiaŋ kpo lɛ hã esane je mitsine tamɔ bɔ ni enyɛmi yoo lɛ sane je mitsine lɛ nɔŋŋ. 19Shi kɛ̃lɛ etee nɔ ebɔ ejwamaŋ lɛ fe nine, ni ekai eblayeiaŋ bei amli ni eyɔɔ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebɔɔ ajwamãŋ lɛ. 20Ehemɛi ni ehiɛ kɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ nɛɛ anuutso tamɔ teji nɔ, ni amɛhenu hu tamɔ okpɔŋɔ he nu. 21Bo, Oholiba, nɛkɛ oshwe oblayeiaŋ basabasa nyiɛmɔi ni onyiɛ, be ni Ijiptbii lɛ miamia ofufɔi, ni amɛfite bo lɛ.”
Nyɔŋmɔ kojo Oholiba
22“No hewɔ lɛ, bo Oholiba, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, naa mibatee osuɔlɔi ni amɛje otsine lɛ shi mawo bo, ni maha amɛte shi amɛwo bo kɛjɛ he fɛɛ he. 23Maha hii ni he yɔɔ akɔnɔ ajɛ Babilon kɛ Kaldea kɛ Pekod kɛ Shoa kɛ Koa kɛ Asiria fɛɛ aba. Mɛnɛɛmɛi fɛɛ lɛ oblahii kɛ amraloi kɛ asafoiatsɛmɛi kɛ lumɛi kɛ gbɛnaahiɛlɔi kɛ tabilɔi ni tara okpɔŋɔi anɔ ji amɛ. 24 Ni mɛi pii kɛ ta shwiilii kɛ tsɔnei ni gbalaa nii aaajɛ kooyigbɛ aba; ni amɛaagba amɛwo ohe kɛ tsɛŋi bibii kɛ dade fai, ni maha amɛ hegbɛ ni amɛkojo bo yɛ amɛmlai anaa. 25Mimli aaafu bo koni amɛkɛ bo aye yɛ mlila naa. Amɛaafolɔ ogugɔ kɛ otoii, ni amɛkɛ klante aaagbegbee omɛi ni baashwɛ lɛ. Amɛaaloo obihii kɛ obiyei lɛ kɛaaya, ni omɛi ni aaashwɛ lɛ la aaakpãtã amɛhiɛ. 26Amɛaakpɔlɔ otadei lɛ yɛ ohe, ni amɛaajie ojwinei fɛɛfɛji lɛ. 27Bɔ ni mafee ni mikɛku ohiɛkɔ̃ɔ kɛ ojwamaŋbɔɔ ni obɔi kɛjɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa nɛ; no aaahã owoŋ ohiɛ nɔ okwɛ Ijiptbii lɛ, ni okaiŋ amɛ hu dɔŋŋ.”
28Ejaakɛ bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Naa, mibatu bo mawo ohenyɛlɔi kɛ mɛi ni eje otsine lɛ adɛŋ. 29Amɛkɛ bo aaaye yɛ yiwalɛ naa. Amɛaaloo nii ni ogbo deŋme yɛ he lɛ fɛɛ, ni amɛaashi bo yayai kɛ ohe pasaa: ni amɛaajie ojwamaŋbɔɔ yayaiaŋ kpo. Ohiɛkɔ̃ɔ kɛ ojwamaŋbɔɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ ba onɔ. 30Aaafee bo enɛɛmɛi ejaakɛ okɛ jeŋmaji lɛ yabɔbɔɔ ajwamãŋ, ni oyanyiɛ amɛwɔji lɛ asɛɛ ni okɛwo ohe muji, 31Onyiɛ onyɛmi yoo lɛ nanefaamɔi lɛ asɛɛ, no hewɔ lɛ, magbala otoi tamɔ migbala etoi lɛ nɔŋŋ.” 32Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ,
“Ooonu nii kɛaajɛ onyɛmi yoo lɛ kpulu lɛ mli;
emli kwɔ, ni eda.
Abaaŋmɔ bo, ni abaaye ohe fɛo.
Ejaakɛ emli nii lɛ fa.
33 Dãa aaatɔ bo, ni owerɛ aaaho ohe.
Onyɛmi yoo Samaria toigbalamɔ lɛ
gbeyei kɛ fitemɔ kpulu ni.
34Obaanu nii yɛ mli, ni ooolɛmɔ mli.
Ooofamɔ oyitsɔi tete,
ni oootserɛ ofufɔi ahe;
ejaakɛ mi, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa, mikɛɛ.
35No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ nɛ, “Akɛni ohiɛ ekpa minɔ, ni oshɛ mi ofɔ osɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, obaana ohiɛkɔ̃ɔ kɛ ojwamaŋbɔɔ lɛ he nɔ.”
Nyɔŋmɔ kojo yei enyɔ lɛ
36Yehowa bi mi akɛ, “Gbɔmɔ Adesa ani obaakojo Ohola kɛ Oholiba? Belɛ jajemɔ musubɔɔnii ni amɛfee lɛ otsɔ̃ɔ amɛ. 37 Ejaakɛ amɛfite gbãlã, ni amɛshwie lá shi; amɛkɛ amɛwɔji lɛ bɔ ajwamãŋ, ni bii ni mikɛ amɛfɔ lɛ, tete amɛkɛ amɛ fee niyenii amɛkɛhã amɛwɔji. 38Asaŋ nɔ hu ni amɛfee mi nɛ: amɛwo mihe krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ he muji, ni amɛbule mihejɔɔmɔ gbii lɛ. 39Ejaakɛ gbi ni amɛgbe amɛbii lɛ amɛhã amɛwɔji lɛ, nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ amɛbabule mihe krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ; ni nakai nɔŋŋ amɛbafee miwe lɛ.
40“Asaŋ, amɛtsu bɔfoi kɛtee majiasɛɛ shɔŋŋ tete po ayaŋɔ hii abaha amɛ; ni kɛ amɛba lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ yei enyɔ nɛɛ juɔ amɛhe, ni amɛdikiɔ amɛhiŋmɛii asɛɛ kɛ adibri, ni amɛwulaa amɛhe kɛ jwinei. 41Amɛtaa saa fɛɛfɛo nɔ, ni aŋmɛɔ okplɔ̃, ni amɛkɛ mitsofakɛŋma kɛ mimu lɛ mamɔɔ nɔ. 42Anu mɛi babaoo anyamɔ gbee yɛ jɛi, ni ayaŋɔ dãatɔlɔi kɛjɛ ŋa nɔ kɛba ni amɛkɛ nineshigai bawo yei lɛ aniji, ni amɛkɛ akekrei fɛɛfɛji fimɔ amɛyitsei. 43Kɛkɛ ni mikɛɛ akɛ, hii ni kɛ yoo nɛɛ wɔɔ lɛ, ani jeee ajwamãŋ amɛbɔɔ lɛ? 44Ejaakɛ amɛkɛ lɛ yawɔɔ tamɔ akɛ yoo ajwamãŋ wɔɔ. Nakai nɔŋŋ amɛkɛ hiɛkɔ̃ɔ kɛ Ohola kɛ Oholiba ni ji yei nyɛnyɛŋtswii lɛ yawɔ. 45 Shi kojolɔi jalɔi baabu amɛ fɔ akɛ gbãlãfitelɔi kɛ yei láshishwielɔi, ejaakɛ gbãlãfitelɔi kɛ láshishwielɔi ji amɛ.”
46Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, “Mahã asafo yuu abatua amɛ ni awo amɛhe gbeyei ní aha amɛ. 47Asafo lɛ atswia amɛ tɛi, ni amɛkɛ amɛklantei lɛ ashwie amɛ; ni amɛaagbegbee amɛbihii kɛ biyei lɛ, ni amɛaashãshãa amɛshĩai lɛ. 48Nɛkɛ mafee ni mikɛku ahoshwibɔɔ naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa koni akɛbɔ yei fɛɛ kwa kɔkɔ ni amɛkabɔ ajwamãŋ nɛɛ eko dɔŋŋ tamɔ nyɛfee lɛ. 49Ni mawo nyɛ yei enyɔ nɛɛ, nyɛjwamãŋbɔɔ lɛ kɛ nyɛhe ni nyɛkɛ nyɛwɔji lɛ bule lɛ he nyɔmɔ, ni nyɛna nyɛle akɛ mi, mi ji Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa.”

english_text:
A Cooking Pot
1Nine years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the tenth day of the tenth month. He said:
2 Ezekiel, son of man, write down today's date, because the king of Babylonia has just begun attacking the city of Jerusalem. 3Then tell my rebellious people:
“Pour water in a cooking pot
and set it over a fire.
* 4Throw in the legs and shoulders
of your finest sheep
and put in the juicy bones.
5Pile wood underneath the pot,
and let the meat and bones
boil until they are done.”
6These words mean that Jerusalem is doomed! The city is filled with murderers and is like an old, rusty pot. The meat is taken out piece by piece, and no one cares what happens to it. 7The people of Jerusalem murdered innocent people in the city and didn't even try to cover up the blood that flowed out on the hard ground. 8But I have seen that blood, and it cries out for me to take revenge.
9I, the Lord God, will punish that city of violence! I will make a huge pile of firewood, 10so bring more wood and light it. Cook the meat and boil away the broth to let the bones scorch. 11Then set the empty pot over the hot coals until it is red-hot. That will clean the pot and burn off the rust. 12I've tried everything else. Now the rust must be burned away.
13Jerusalem is so full of sin and evil that I can't get it clean, even though I have tried. It will stay filthy until I let loose my fierce anger against it. 14That time will certainly come! And when it does, I won't show the people of Jerusalem any pity or change my mind. They must be punished for the evil they have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
Ezekiel's Wife Dies
15The Lord said, 16“Ezekiel, son of man, I will suddenly take the life of the person you love most. But I don't want you to complain or cry. 17Mourn in silence and don't show that you are grieving. Don't remove your turban or take off your sandals; don't cover your face to show your sorrow, or eat the food that mourners eat.”
18One morning, I was talking with the people as usual, and by sunset my wife was dead. The next day I did what the Lord had told me, 19and when people saw me, they asked, “Why aren't you mourning for your wife?”
20I answered:
The Lord God says 21he is ready to destroy the temple in which you take such pride and which makes you feel so safe. Your children who now live in Jerusalem will be killed. 22Then you will do the same things I have done. You will leave your face uncovered and refuse to eat the food that mourners usually eat. 23You won't take off your turbans and your sandals. You won't cry or mourn, but all day long you will go around groaning because of your sins.
24I am a warning sign—everything I have done, you will also do. And then you will know the Lord God has made these things happen.
25The Lord said, “Ezekiel, I will soon destroy the temple that makes everyone feel proud and safe, and I will take away their children as well. 26On that same day, someone will escape from the city and come to tell you what has happened. 27Then you will be able to speak again, and the two of you will talk. You will be a warning sign to the people, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_text:
Dadesɛŋ ni edɔ ŋkanale lɛ
1Nomŋɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ afi ni ji nɛɛhu lɛ nɔ nyɔŋ ni ji nyɔŋma lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma lɛ nɔ lɛ Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ, 2 “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, ŋmãa ŋmɛnɛ gbi nɛɛ ofɔ̃ shi, ejaakɛ ŋmɛnɛ ji gbi krɛdɛɛ nɔ ni Babilon Maŋtsɛ lɛ sa Yerusalɛm yi lɛ. 3Buu weku ni toi egbo lɛ abɛ nɛɛ, ni okɛɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ,
Okɛ dadesɛŋ ama la nɔ,
ni okɛ nu awo mli.
4Okɛ loo ni afolɔ lɛ kukulii awo mli:
hei ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ
eshuɔ lɛ kɛ ekɔŋ lɛ
akɛ wui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ
afata he ni eyi obɔ̃.
5Ŋɔɔ too ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ ateŋ ekome,
too lai owo latɛŋ yɛ dadesɛŋ lɛ shishi.
Ha ni nu lɛ atswa,
hoomɔ, ni wui lɛ tete abe.”
6No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, “Kpoo hã maŋ ni ashwieɔ lá shi yɛ emli; nakai maŋ lɛ, etamɔ dadesɛŋ ni mli edɔ ŋkanale, ni ŋkanale lɛ yɛ mli lolo. Kɔlɔmɔ loi lɛ yɛ dadesɛŋ lɛ mli ekomekome, kaahala mli. 7Ejaakɛ mɛi ni agbe yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ alá yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lolo. Lá nɛɛ jwere tɛsaa kpataa nɔ, jeee shikpɔŋ nɔ eshwie bɔ ni akɛ su aaanyɛ aha nɔ. 8Mihã mɛi ahiɛ ni akpãtã lɛ alá lɛ shwie tɛsaa kplanaa lɛ nɔ, koni akanyɛ nɔ su aha, bɔ ni afee ni etee mimlifu shi ni ehã matɔ he owele. 9 No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, kpoo ha maŋ ni ashwie lá shi yɛ emli lɛ. Mi diɛŋtsɛ hu mato laii pii mawo eshishi. 10Ha lai lɛ afa, shɛremɔ la lɛ, hoomɔ loo lɛ ni ebe jogbaŋŋ, ni otsɔ̃ wonu lɛ yɛ dadesɛŋ lɛ mli; ha wui lɛ tete aŋala. 11Agbɛnɛ kɛ dadesɛŋ folo lɛ ama ŋai la lɛ nɔ koni edɔ klakla, ni akɔɔble dadesɛŋ lɛ atsu hɛŋŋ, bɔ ni afee ni emli muji lɛ asere, ni ŋkanale lɛ aje kwraa. 12Migbo he yaka deŋme, shi kɛ̃lɛ, emli ŋkanale titrii lɛ, lá tete nyɛɛɛ ajie. 13Ohiɛkɔ̃ɔ kɛ mujinii lɛ no ji ŋkanale lɛ. Akɛni kulɛ mitsuu ohe ni ohe atse shi ohe tseee hewɔ lɛ, hii shi yɛ ohe muji lɛ mli kɛyaashi beyinɔ ni matɔ mihe owele, ni mimii aaashɛ mihe. 14Mi, Yehowa, miwie, ni ebaaba mli, ni mafee hu, mifɔŋ, ni minaŋ mɔbɔ, ni mishwaŋ mihe hu; bɔ ni ojeŋba yɔɔ lɛ, kɛ bɔ ni onifeemɔnii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nakai naa makojo bo yɛ; Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.”
Gbalɔ lɛ ŋa gbo
15Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ, 16“Gbɔmɔ Adesa, naa, mibaŋɔ mɔ ni ji ohiŋmɛi mli ajaŋmalaatɛ lɛ trukaa kɛje ohe kɛya. Kɛji eba lɛ nakai lɛ kaawo yara, ni okafo hu, ni ohiŋmɛiŋ akakpala nu tete. 17Fo yɛ osɛŋ, kaahã oyaafo je kpo ni anu yɛ onaabu. Kaafee yara ko. Okɛ obɔnduku lɛ afi oyitso, ni owo otokotai lɛ; okɛ mama ko akabala onaabu, ni kaaye yara nɔ niyenii hu.”
18Mikɛ maŋ lɛ wie leebi mli, ni gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, miŋa lɛ gbo. Hewɔ lɛ enɔ jetsɛremɔ leebi lɛ, mifee bɔ ni afã mi lɛ. 19Kɛkɛ ni maŋbii lɛ bi mi akɛ, “Mɛni ofeɔ nɛɛ? Ani oootsɔ̃ɔ wɔ nɔ ni ofeɔ nɛɛ shishi?”
20Mihã amɛ hetoo akɛ, 21“Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ, Kɛɛmɔ Israel we lɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, Naa, mibabule mihekrɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ, ni ji nyɛhewalɛ ni nyɛkɛwoɔ nyɛhe nɔ lɛ; he krɔŋkrɔŋ ni ji nyɛhiŋmɛiŋ ajaŋmalaatɛ lɛ kɛ nyɛsusumai ashwee lɛ. Nyɛbihii kɛ nyɛbiyei ni nyɛshi yɛ Yerusalɛm lɛ, akɛ klante baagbe amɛ. 22Kɛkɛ lɛ nyɛbaafee tamɔ bɔ ni mifee mitsɔ̃ɔ nyɛ nɛɛ: nyɛkɛ mama eblaŋ nyɛnaabui, ni nyɛyeŋ yara nɔ niyenii hu. 23Nyɛbaafimɔ nyɛbɔnduku lɛ, ni nyɛtokotai lɛ aahi nyɛnaji, nyɛwoŋ yara, asaŋ nyɛfoŋ, shi moŋ yɛ nyɛnishaianii ahewɔ lɛ, nyɛaatãrã loo, ni nyɛaakɛ̃mɔ nyɛtsɔ̃ɔ nyɛhe. 24Enɛ baaha Ezekiel atsɔ̃ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ahã nyɛ, ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni eeefee lɛ, nakai nyɛaafee. Kɛji enɛ ba mli lɛ, no dani nyɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa lɛ.
25“Agbɛnɛ lɛ, bo Gbɔmɔ Adesa, gbi nɔ ni mafite amɛSɔlemɔ we lɛ, ni ji amɛmiishɛɛ kɛ amɛhiɛnyam, amɛhiŋmɛiŋ ajaŋmalaatɛ kɛ amɛtsuiŋ nitaomɔnii lɛ, ni makpãtã amɛbihii kɛ amɛbiyei lɛ hu ahiɛ lɛ 26nakai gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, mɔ ko ni lɛ lɛ ehe eje hiɛkpãtãmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aaaba oŋɔɔ abatswa bo adafi. 27Nakai gbi lɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ aaagbele onaabu, ni okɛ mɔ ni he eje mli lɛ aaawie, ni otɔŋ mu dɔŋŋ; no hewɔ lɛ, oootsɔ̃ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ oha amɛ, ni amɛaana amɛle akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.”

english_text:
Judgment on Ammon
1 The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Ammon 3and tell them:
You celebrated when my temple was destroyed, when Israel was defeated, and when my people were taken away as prisoners. 4Now I am going to let you be conquered by tribes from the eastern desert. They will set up their camps in your land and eat your fruit and drink your milk. 5Your capital city of Rabbah will be nothing but pastureland for camels, and the rest of the country will be pastures for sheep. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
6You hated Israel so much that you clapped and shouted and celebrated. 7And so I will hand you over to enemies who will rob you. I will completely destroy you. There won't be enough of your people left to be a nation ever again, and you will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
Judgment on Moab
8 The Lord God said, “The people of Moab thought Judah was no different from any other nation. 9So I will let Moab's fortress towns along its border be attacked, including Beth-Jeshimoth, Baal-Meon, and Kiriathaim. 10The same eastern desert tribes that invade Ammon will invade Moab, and just as Ammon will be forgotten forever, 11Moab will be punished. Then the people there will know that I am the Lord.”
Judgment on Edom
12 The Lord God then said, “The people of Edom are guilty of taking revenge on Judah. 13So I will punish Edom by killing all its people and livestock. It will be an empty wasteland all the way from Teman to Dedan. 14I will send my own people to take revenge on the Edomites by making them feel my fierce anger. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord God.”
Judgment on Philistia
15 The Lord God said, “The cruel Philistines have taken revenge on their enemies over and over and have tried to destroy them. 16Now it's my turn to treat the Philistines as my enemies and to kill everyone living in their towns along the seacoast. 17In my fierce anger, I will take revenge on them. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_text:
Amon he Gbalɛ
1 Yehowa kɛɛ mi ekoŋŋ akɛ,
2“Gbɔmɔ Adesa, tsɔ̃ ohiɛ ohã Amonbii lɛ, ni ogba oshi amɛ. 3Kɛɛmɔ Amonbii lɛ akɛ, nyɛboa Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa wiemɔ toi, bɔ ni mi, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa, mikɛɔ nɛ, akɛni nyɛnya, ejaakɛ abule miHe Krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ, ni afee Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ amaŋfɔ̃, ni aŋɔ Yuda we lɛ nom lɛ 4hewɔ lɛ, maŋɔ bo maha mɛi ni yɔɔ bokãgbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛye onɔ. Amɛbaafee tabilɔi ashitoohei yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, amɛbaato maji amɛhi mli yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; amɛbaaye otsei ayibii lɛ, ni amɛaanu otsina fufɔ lɛ. 5Maha Rama atsɔ̃ yoomai aniyelihe, ni maha Amonbii amaji wuji lɛ baatsɔ toi atsu. No nyɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.
6“Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, akɛni otswa odɛ̃, ni otumɔ kɛ miishɛɛ, ni okɛ yiŋsha ni yɔɔ omli fɛɛ nya, ni oye Israel yɔɔ waa 7hewɔ lɛ, naa, mite shi miwo bo, ni maŋɔ bo mahã jeŋmaji lɛ ni amɛha onibii. Makpãtã ohiɛ yɛ majimaji fɛɛ ateŋ; ni mafite bo yɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ; makpãtã ohiɛ, ni ooona ole akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.”
Moab he gbalɛ
8 Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɔ nɛ, “Akɛni Moab kɛɛ akɛ, naa, Yuda tamɔ shikpɔji krokomɛi lɛ nɔŋŋ 9hewɔ lɛ, mifite Moab anunyam maji wuji ni buɔ ehusu nɔ lɛ. Maji nɛɛ ji Bet-Yeshimot kɛ Baal-Meon kɛ Kiriataim. No baahã Moab he akã aha henyɛlɔi. 10Mikɛ Moab baafata Amonbii lɛ ahe maha bokãgbɛbii lɛ ni amɛŋɔ, ni akaiŋ lɛ dɔŋŋ yɛ majimaji lɛ ateŋ. 11Mibagbala Moabbii atoi, ni amɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.”
Edom he Gbalɛ
12 “Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɔ nɛ, akɛni Edom tɔ ehe owele yɛ Yuda we lɛ nɔ, ni yɛ oweletɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ etɔ̃ babaoo lɛ, 13hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, mate shi mawo Edom, ni makpãtã emli gbɔmɔ kɛ kooloo fɛɛ hiɛ; ni mafee lɛ amaŋfɔ̃; ni kɛjɛ Teman aahu kɛyashi Dedan lɛ amɛbaanyɔnyɔɔ yɛ klante naa. 14Mibatsɔ̃ mimaŋ Israelbii anɔ matɔ mihe owele yɛ Edom nɔ. Israelbii kɛ Edom baaye yɛ mimlifu kɛ mimlila naa. Ni amɛaale bɔ ni mitɔɔ owele mihãa.” Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.
Filistia he Gbalɛ
15 “Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, akɛni Filistibii lɛ to yiŋsha yɛ amɛtsuiŋ ni amɛkɛtɔ mɛi ni ji amɛhenyɛlɔi kɛjɛ teteete lɛ anɔ owele, ni amɛkpãtã amɛhiɛ kwraa kɛmɔ shi 16hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, naa mate shi mawo Filistibii lɛ, ni maplene Keretibii lɛ, ni makpãtã mɛi ni baashwɛ yɛ ŋshɔnaagbɛ lɛ ahiɛ. 17Mikɛ mlifu kpele baakã amɛ, ni matɔ mihe owele jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛnɔ, ni no amɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa, kɛji mitɔ mihe owele yɛ amɛnɔ lɛ.”

english_text:
Judgment on the City of Tyre
1 Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, the people of the city of Tyre have celebrated Jerusalem's defeat by singing,
“Jerusalem has fallen!
It used to be powerful,
a center of trade.
Now the city is shattered,
and we will take its place.”
3Because the people of Tyre have sung that song, I have the following warning for them: I am the Lord God, and I am now your enemy! I will send nations to attack you, like waves crashing against the shore. 4They will tear down your city walls and defense towers. I will sweep away the ruins until all that's left of you is a bare rock, 5where fishermen can dry their nets along the coast. I promise that you will be robbed 6and that the people who live in your towns along the coast will be killed. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
7King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia is the world's most powerful king, and I will send him to attack you. He will march from the north with a powerful army, including horses and chariots and cavalry troops. 8First, he will attack your towns along the coast and kill the people who live there. Then he will build dirt ramps up to the top of your city walls and set up rows of shields around you. 9He will command some of his troops to use large wooden poles to beat down your walls, while others use iron rods to knock down your watchtowers. 10He will have so many horses that the dust they stir up will seem like a thick fog. And as his chariots and cavalry approach, even the walls will shake, especially when he proudly enters your ruined city. 11His troops will ride through your streets, killing people left and right, and your strong columns will crumble to the ground. 12The troops will steal your valuable possessions; they will break down your walls, and crush your expensive houses. Then the stones and wood and all the remains will be dumped into the sea. 13 You will have no reason to sing or play music on harps, 14because I will turn you into a bare rock where fishermen can dry their nets. And you will never rebuild your city. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
15The people of the nations up and down the coast will shudder when they hear your screams and moans of death. 16 The kings will step down from their thrones, then take off their royal robes and fancy clothes, and sit on the ground, trembling. They will be so shocked at the news of your defeat that they will shake in fear 17and sing this funeral song:
“The great city beside the sea
is destroyed!
Its people once ruled the coast
and terrified everyone there.
18But now Tyre is in ruins,
and the people on the coast
stare at it in horror
and tremble in fear.”
19I, the Lord God, will turn you into a ghost-town. The ocean depths will rise over you 20and carry you down to the world of the dead, where you will join people of ancient times and towns ruined long ago. You will stay there and never again be a city filled with people. 21 You will die a horrible death! People will come looking for your city, but it will never be found. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Tiro he Gbalɛ
1 Be ni wɔyɔɔ wɔnomŋɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ ekome lɛ nɔ, nyɔŋ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ,
2“Gbɔmɔ Adesa, akɛni Tiro kɛɛ yɛ Yerusalɛm he akɛ, ‘Yiɛ, akumɔ maŋbii agbo lɛ, enaa kã hã mi. Ni akɛni etsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃ nɛɛ lɛ, mibashwere!’ Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ,
3“Bo Tiro, naa, mikɛ bo ena, ni mahã majimaji babaoo ate shi awo bo tamɔ ŋshɔkei kumɔɔ lɛ. 4Amɛbaafite Tiro gbogboi lɛ, ni amɛbaakumɔ emɔji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ amɛshwie shi. Kɛkɛ lɛ mabɛɛ enɔ su tete, ni mafee lɛ tɛsaa kpataa. 5Eeetsɔ̃ mɔ ni jeŋmaji aaaha enii. 6Ni eshikpɔji lɛ diɛŋtsɛ nɔ hu akɛ klante baagbe maŋbii lɛ fɛɛ; kɛkɛ lɛ Tirobii aaana ale akɛ, mi, mi ji Yehowa.”
7Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Naa, maha Babilon maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar, ni ji maŋtsɛmɛi amaŋtsɛ lɛ, kɛ okpɔŋɔi kɛ shwiilii kɛ okpɔŋɔnɔtalɔi kɛ asraafoi babaoo ajɛ kooyigbɛ abatua Tiro. 8Ekɛ klante baakpãtã mɛi ni yɔɔ ohewɔ maji ni jwere ŋa lɛ nɔ lɛ ahiɛ, eeetswa ka gbogbo ewo ohe, ni eeetswa kpoku ewo ohe; ni ekɛ tsɛŋi babaoo baaba abatua bo. 9Maŋtsɛ nɛɛ baahã akɛ gbogbokuumɔnii lɛ ashimɔ ogbogboi lɛ, ni akɛ lemai aaakumɔ omɔji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ. 10Ekpɔŋɔi ayifalɛ sɔŋŋ naa lɛ, amɛnaneshi mlu kpɔŋŋ lɛ aaatsi onɔ. Kɛji eetsɔ̃ ogboi lɛ amli kɛbote omaŋ lɛ mli tamɔ aboteɔ maŋ ni ajwa egbogbo awo mli lɛ, ekpɔŋɔnɔtalɔi lɛ abolɔmɔ kɛ enigbalamɔ shwiilii kɛ eta shwiilii agbɛɛmɔ naawalɛ sɔŋŋ naa lɛ ogbogboi lɛ aaahoso. 11Maŋtsɛ nɛɛ kɛ ekpɔŋɔi lɛ akoklotoi lɛ aaanaanaa oblohuŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ fɛɛ anɔ; ekɛ klante aaakpãtã omaŋbii lɛ ahiɛ, ni okulashiŋi ni wa lɛ aaagbeegbee shi. 12Ohenyɛlɔi lɛ baaha ojwetrii kɛ oguɔ nii ni oyɔɔ lɛ, amɛbaakumɔ ogbogboi lɛ, ni amɛbaafite oshĩai fɛɛfɛji lɛ; ni tɛi lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ kɛ sũ lɛ tete amɛbaaloo amɛyawo ŋshɔ mli. 13 Mahã olalai lɛ agbɛɛmɔ sɛɛ afo, ni anuŋ okpãa saŋkui lɛ agbɛɛmɔ dɔŋŋ.
14“Mahã otsɔ̃ tɛsaa kpataa, he ni akaa yaa yɛ. Asaŋ bo amaŋ dɔŋŋ, ejaakɛ mi, Yehowa, miwie.
15“Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ Tiro nɛ, ani ŋshɔnaa shikpɔji lɛ ahe kpokpoŋ yɛ oshigbeemɔ lɛ gbɛɛmɔ naa, be ni pilafoi miikɛ̃mɔ, ni aakpãtã omɛi lɛ ahiɛ yɛ omli lɛ? 16Kɛkɛ lɛ ŋshɔhiɛ lumɛi fɛɛ aaajɛ amɛsɛ̃ii anɔ akpeleke shi, amɛaajie amɛtadei lɛ, amɛaakpɔlɔ amɛheboi wuji ni alo nii awo mli lɛ, amɛaabu hekpokpomɔ tamɔ abuɔ mama, amɛaashwata shikpɔŋ ni amɛhe baakpokpo blibli; be fɛɛ be lɛ amɛhe baajɔ̃ amɛhe yɛ ohewɔ. 17Amɛaawo yara yɛ ohewɔ amɛaakɛɛ bo akɛ,
‘Bo maŋ ni ogbɛi ehehe,
ni okɛ omlibii fɛɛ
hiɛ ŋshɔ hiɛ hewalɛ;
bo, ni ohe ŋmiŋmi mɔmɔ
mɛi fɛɛ ni bɔle bo
yɛ shikpɔŋ,
te aye tɛŋŋ ni osha shi
yɛ ŋshɔ hiɛ nɛɛ?
18 Agbɛnɛ, ŋshɔkpɔi lɛ ahe miikpokpo
gbi nɔ ni ogbee shi lɛ.
Hɛɛ, ŋshɔkpɔi ni yɔɔ ŋshɔŋ
anaa ekpɛ amɛhe
yɛ ohiɛkpãtãmɔ lɛ hewɔ.’
19“Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, kɛji mifee omaŋ lɛ amaŋfɔ̃, tamɔ maji ni gbɔmɛi bɛ mli lɛ eko, kɛji mihã ŋshɔŋ bu kwɔŋkwɔŋ lɛ baha onɔ, ni nu babaoo tsimɔ onɔ lɛ, 20no ni manyɛ onɔ koni okɛ mɛi ni kpelekeɔ shi kɛyaa gbohiiaje lɛ ayafata blemabii ni yɔɔ jɛi momo lɛ ahe. Maha bo kɛ mɛi ni kpelekeɔ shi kɛyaa gbohiiaje lɛ ahi shi yɛ gbohiiaje yɛ naanɔ amaŋfɔ̃i lɛ amli, bɔ ni afee ni mɔ ko akahi omli dɔŋŋ, aloo ona gbɛhe ko yɛ hiɛkãalɔi ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu. 21 Maha onaagbee afee gbeyei, ni ohiŋ shi dɔŋŋ; tsɛbelɛ mɛi aaatao bo nɛ, shi kɛ̃lɛ, anaŋ bo dɔŋŋ kɛaatee naanɔ.” Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.

english_text:
A Funeral Song for Tyre
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for Tyre, 3the city that is built along the sea and that trades with nations along the coast. Tell the people of Tyre that the following message is from me:
Tyre, you brag about
your perfect beauty,
4and your control of the sea.
You are a ship
built to perfection.
5Builders used cypress trees
from Mount Hermon
to make your planks
and a cedar tree from Lebanon
for your tall mast.
6Oak trees from Bashan
were shaped into oars;
pine trees from Cyprus
were cut for your deck,
which was then decorated
with strips of ivory.
7The builders used fancy linen
from Egypt for your sails,
so everyone could see you.
Blue and purple cloth
from Cyprus was used
to shade your deck.
8Men from Sidon and Arvad
did the rowing,
and your own skilled workers
were the captains.
9Experienced men from Byblos
repaired any damages.
Sailors from all over
shopped at the stores
in your port.
10Brave soldiers from Persia,
Lydia, and Libya
served in your navy,
protecting you with shields
and helmets,
and making you famous.
11Your guards came from
Arvad and Cilicia,
and men from Gamad
stood watch in your towers.
With their weapons
hung on your walls,
your beauty was complete.
12Merchants from southern Spain traded silver, iron, tin, and lead for your products. 13The people of Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded slaves and things made of bronze, 14and those from Beth-Togarmah traded work horses, war horses, and mules. 15You also did business with people from Rhodes, and people from nations along the coast gave you ivory and ebony in exchange for your goods. 16Edom traded emeralds, purple cloth, embroidery, fine linen, coral, and rubies. 17Judah and Israel gave you their finest wheat, fancy figs, honey, olive oil, and spices in exchange for your merchandise. 18The people of Damascus saw what you had to offer and brought you wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar. 19Vedan and Javan near Uzal traded you iron and spices. 20The people of Dedan supplied you with saddle blankets, 21while people from Arabia and the rulers of Kedar traded lambs, sheep, and goats. 22Merchants from Sheba and Raamah gave you excellent spices, precious stones, and gold in exchange for your products. 23You also did business with merchants from the cities of Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad, 24and they gave you expensive clothing, purple and embroidered cloth, brightly colored rugs, and strong rope. 25 Large, seagoing ships carried your goods wherever they needed to go.
You were like a ship
loaded with heavy cargo
26and sailing across the sea,
but you were wrecked
by strong eastern winds.
27Everything on board was lost—
your valuable cargo,
your sailors and carpenters,
merchants and soldiers.
28The shouts of your drowning crew
were heard on the shore.
29Every ship is deserted;
rowers and sailors and captains
all stand on shore,
30mourning for you.
They show their sorrow
by putting dust on their heads
and rolling in ashes;
31they shave their heads
and dress in sackcloth
as they cry in despair.
32In their grief they sing
a funeral song for you:
“Tyre, you were greater
than all other cities.
But now you lie in silence
at the bottom of the sea.
33“Nations that received
your merchandise
were always pleased;
kings everywhere got rich
from your costly goods.
34But now you are wrecked
in the deep sea,
with your cargo and crew
scattered everywhere.
35People living along the coast
are shocked at the news.
Their rulers are horrified,
and terror is written
across their faces.
36The merchants of the world
can't believe what happened.
Your death was gruesome,
and you are gone forever.”
translation_text:
Tiro yarafeemɔ lala
1Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ, 2“Agbɛnɛ, bo Gbɔmɔ Adesa, ye Tiro ŋkɔmɔ, 3 ni okɛɛ Tiro, maŋ ni kã ŋshɔnaa, ni ekɛ ŋshɔnaa majimaji yeɔ guɔ lɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ,
“Ao Tiro, okɛɛ akɛ,
‘Mihe yɛ fɛo kɛwula shi.’
4Ohusu yɛ ŋshɔ teŋ.
Mɛi ni kpɛ bo akɛ lɛlɛ lɛ
kpɛ bo fɛɛfɛo kɛwula shi.
5 Amɛkɛ Hermon Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ
sɛsɛotsei sɔŋŋ hɛhɛ bo,
ni Lebanon tsenedru
akɛfee oshimaatso lɛ.
6Bashan tsei wuji
akɛgbɔ tablɔi lɛ.
Kipro tsei akɛfee odɛke,
ni akɛ shuɔ wu ka mli.
7 Obalaa lɛ Ijipt klala fɛɛfɛo
ni alo nii awo mli akɛfee;
no nɔŋŋ ji oflaŋaa
Onɔhaa buu lɛ, mama bluu
kɛ afaseo ni akɛjɛ
Kipro ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ akɛfee.
8Sidonbii kɛ Arvadbii ji owirilɔi.
Bo diɛŋtsɛ omli ŋaalɔi
ji okudɔɔtsɛmɛi.
9 Gebal onukpai kɛ ŋaalɔi
ni yɔɔ omli lɛ ji srɛŋkifoi
ni tsimɔɔ omli fɔ̃ji lɛ.
Ŋshɔ hiɛ lɛji kɛ amɛsraafoi fɛɛ
baa omli amɛbayeɔ bo jara.
10“Persiabii kɛ Ludbii kɛ Libiabii yɛ otabilɔi lɛ ateŋ; amɛkɛ tsɛŋ kɛ dade fai tsotsoroɔ shi yɛ otabilɔi ashihilɛhei lɛ amli; amɛ amɛhãa ohiɛ baa nyam. 11Arvadhii kɛ Helekhii buɔ yɛ ogbogboi lɛ anɔ kɛkpeɔ, ni Gamad hii buɔ yɛ omɔji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Amɛkɛ amɛtsɛŋi lɛ tsotsoroɔ ogbogboi lɛ ahe kɛkpeɔ. Amɛ amɛhãa ohe feɔ fɛo kɛwulaa shi.
12“Tarshishbii kɛ bo ye jara, ejaakɛ oyɛ guɔ nibii babaoo; amɛkɛ jwiɛtɛi kɛ dade kɛ tsɛnsi kɛ sumui baa ni amɛkɛbatsakeɔ oguɔ nibii lɛ. 13Helabii kɛ Tubalbii kɛ Meshekbii kɛ bo ye jara. Amɛkɛ gbɔmɛi kɛ akɔɔble nibii baa ni amɛkɛbatsakeɔ oguɔyeli nibii lɛ. 14Togarmabii kɛ okpɔŋɔi kɛ tawuu okpɔŋɔi kɛ tejiokpɔŋɔi baa ni amɛkɛbatsakeɔ oguɔ nibii lɛ. 15Rodobii kɛ bo ye jara. Ŋshɔnaa maji babaoo kɛ bo ye jara krɛdɛɛ ko; amɛ lɛ amɛkɛ shuɔ wu kɛ ebɔnetsei bawoɔ oguɔ nibii ni amɛbaheɔ lɛ nyɔmɔ. 16Siria hu kɛ bo ye jara ejaakɛ oyɛ nii babaoo. Amɛkɛ kafuŋklei, mama afaseo tsuru ni alo nii awo mli, kɛ klala kpakpa, kɛ tɛ̃ŋlɛo kɛ rubitɛi baa, ni amɛkɛbatsakeɔ oguɔ nibii lɛ. 17Yuda kɛ Israel kɛ bo ye jara, amɛkɛ ŋmãa kɛ mu kɛ agbãmi kɛ wo kɛ mu kɛ tsofakɛŋma baa, ni amɛkɛbatsakeɔ oguɔ nibii lɛ. 18Damasko kɛ bo ye oguɔ nibii babaoo lɛ he jara. Ekɛ bo ye jara yɛ guɔ nibii srɔtoisrɔtoi babaoo ni oyɔɔ lɛ ahewɔ. Ekɛ wain jɛɔ Helbon, ni akɛ toi ahetsɔi yɛŋ futaa jɛɔ Shar baa. 19Amɛkɛ wain jɛɔ Uzal batsakeɔ oguɔ nibii lɛ. Akɛ dade nibii kɛ kashia kɛ sinamon batsakeɔ oguɔ nibii lɛ. 20Dedan kɛ bo ye okpɔŋɔtamɔ sɛi nɔ mama jara. 21 Arabiabii kɛ Kedar lumɛi lɛ fɛɛ ji mɛi ni osumɔ amɛ kɛ gwantɛŋbii kɛ ojwɛnii kɛ abotiai ajarayeli jogbaŋŋ. 22Sheba kɛ Rama jarayelɔi kɛ bo ye jara. Amɛkɛ tsofakɛŋmai fɛɛ mli ekpakpai kɛ tɛi ni jara wa fɛɛ kɛ shika baa batsakeɔ oguɔ nibii lɛ. 23Haran kɛ Kane kɛ Eden kɛ Sheba kɛ Ashur kɛ Kilmad kɛ bo ye jara. 24Maji nɛɛ kɛ bo ye atadei kpakpai kɛ mama bluu ni alo nii awo mli atadei, kɛ tsu mli kapɛtii ni hiɛ sui srɔtoi ni akɛ taŋkpee kpãa efimɔ mli kpɛŋŋ jara. 25 Tarshish lɛji lɛ woɔ oguɔ nibii lɛ.
No hewɔ lɛ, otamɔ lɛlɛ
ni awo lɛ nii obɔ̃ yɛ ŋshɔ teŋ.
26Mɛi ni wiriɔ bo lɛ
kɛ bo etee ŋshɔ teŋ tɔ̃ɔ;
shi bokã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ
ejwra bo yɛ ŋshɔ teŋ.
27Oshika kɛ oguɔnii
kɛ ojarayelinii kɛ osrafoi
kɛ okudɔɔtsɛmɛi kɛ mɛi ni
tsimɔɔ ofɔji lɛ, kɛ oguɔyelɔi
kɛ otabilɔi fɛɛ kɛ osafo muu fɛɛ
ni yɔɔ omli lɛ shiu yɛ ŋshɔ teŋ,
yɛ ohiɛkpãtãmɔ gbi lɛ nɔ.
28Be ni okudɔɔtsɛmɛi lɛ
bolɔ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ hoso
29ni wirilɔi lɛ fɛɛ kpeleke shi
kɛjɛ lɛlɛ lɛ mli.
Asrɛfoi lɛ kɛ kudɔɔtsɛmɛi lɛ
badamɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa.
30Amɛwo ohe yara
ni amɛfo bo waa.
Amɛloo mlu amɛwo amɛyiteŋ
ni amɛkoklo lamlu mli.
31Amɛshɛ amɛyi yɛ ohewɔ,
ni amɛbu kpekpe.
Amɛwo yara, ni amɛfo bo waa
kɛ dɔlɛ naakpa.
32Yɛ amɛlelewomɔ lɛ mli lɛ
amɛwo yaafo lala amɛkɛfo bo akɛ,
‘Namɔ akpãtã ehiɛ pɛŋ
yɛ ŋshɔ teŋ tamɔ Tiro?
33Be ni akɛ oguɔ nibii
jɛ ŋshɔŋ kɛba lɛ
oha mɛi pii tɔrɔ;
onii ni ona babaoo
kɛ ojarayeli nibii lɛ,
oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ maŋtsɛmɛi na nii.
34Agbɛnɛ, ŋshɔ ejwra bo,
ni oshiu kɛtee ŋshɔ shishi;
oguɔ nibii kɛ osrafoi lɛ fɛɛ
kɛ bo eshiu.’
35“Ŋshɔnaa majiaŋbii fɛɛ ahe ejɔ̃ amɛhe yɛ ohewɔ,
ni gbeyei ni naa wa emɔmɔ amɛmaŋtsɛmɛi lɛ,
ni amɛhiɛ hu efee amɛ yaa.
36Majimaji anɔ jarayelɔi miibo bo ‘tsiaa’,
ejaakɛ onaagbee lɛ efee gbeyei,
ni olaaje kɛmiiya naanɔ.”

english_text:
Judgment on the King of Tyre
1The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Tyre that I am saying:
You are so arrogant that you think you're a god and that the city of Tyre is your throne. You may claim to be a god, though you're nothing but a mere human. 3You think you're wiser than Daniel and know everything.
4Your wisdom has certainly made you rich, because you have storehouses filled with gold and silver. 5You're a clever businessman and are extremely wealthy, but your wealth has led to arrogance!
6You compared yourself to a god, so now I, the Lord God, 7will make you the victim of cruel enemies. They will destroy all the possessions you've worked so hard to get. 8Your enemies will brutally kill you, and the sea will be your only grave.
9When you face your enemies, will you still claim to be a god? They will attack, and you will suffer like any other human. 10Foreigners will kill you, and you will die the death of those who don't worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken.
A Funeral Song for the King of Tyre
11The Lord said:
12Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for the king of Tyre and tell him I am saying:
At one time, you were perfect, intelligent, and good-looking. 13You lived in the garden of Eden and wore jewelry made of brightly colored gems and precious stones. They were all set in gold and were ready for you on the day you were born. 14I appointed a winged creature to guard your home on my holy mountain, where you walked among gems that dazzled like fire.
15You were truly good from the time of your birth, but later you started doing wicked things. 16You traded with other nations and became more and more cruel and evil. So I forced you to leave my mountain, and the creature that had been your protector now chased you away from the jewels.
17It was your good looks that made you arrogant, and you were so famous that you started acting like a fool. That's why I threw you to the ground and let other kings sneer at you. 18You have cheated so many other merchants that your places of worship are corrupt.
