So I set your city on fire and burned it down. Now everyone sees only ashes where your city once stood, 19and the people of other nations are shocked. Your punishment was horrible, and you are gone forever.
Judgment on Sidon and Peace for Israel
20 The Lord said:
21Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the city of Sidon 22and tell its people:
I, the Lord God, am your enemy! People will praise me when I punish you, and they will see that I am holy. 23I will send deadly diseases to wipe you out, and I will send enemies to invade and surround you. Your people will be killed, and you will know that I am the Lord.
24When that happens, the people of Israel will no longer have cruel neighbors that abuse them and make them feel as though they are in a field of thorns and briers. And the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things.
A Blessing for Israel
25The Lord God said:
Someday I will gather the people of Israel from the nations where they are now scattered, and every nation will see that I am holy. The Israelites will once again live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob. 26They will be safe and will build houses and plant vineyards. They will no longer be in danger, because I will punish their hateful neighbors. Israel will know that I am the Lord their God.
translation_text:
Gbalɛ ni shiɔ Tiro Maŋtsɛ lɛ
1Yehowa kɛ mi wie ni ekɛɛ, 2 “Gbɔmɔ Adesa kɛɛmɔ Tiro lumɔ lɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɔ nɛ, ‘Owoɔ ohe nɔ ni otsɛɔ ohe nyɔŋmɔ,’ Okɛɔ akɛ, ‘Nyɔŋmɔ ji mi, ni mita nyɔŋmɔi lɛ alumɔ sɛi lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋshɔteŋ;’ tsɛbelɛ gbɔmɔ adesa kɛkɛ ji bo, shi jeee nyɔŋmɔ ko. Tsɛbelɛ obuɔ ohe akɛ ole nii tamɔ nɔ ni nyɔŋmɔ ji bo. 3 Efeɔ bo akɛ ole nii fe Daniel, ni teemɔŋ sane ko bɛ ni oleee. 4Onilee kɛ oniiashishinumɔ eha ona nii; ona shika kɛ jwiɛtɛi owo ofotroi amli. 5Jarayeli he nilee kpele ni oyɔɔ eha onii ni oyɔɔ efa babaoo; ni oninamɔ lɛ eha oowo ohe nɔ.
6“No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɔ nɛ: akɛni efeɔ bo akɛ ole nii tamɔ nyɔŋmɔ ko 7hewɔ lɛ, naa, mahã gbɔi amaji lɛ ateŋ maŋ ni he yɔɔ gbeyei fe fɛɛ, abatua bo; amɛkɛ klante aaabakpãtã nibii fɛɛfɛji ni okɛ onilee na lɛ ahiɛ, amɛaahã onunyam aaaba shi. 8 Amɛbaanyɛ onɔ amɛwo gbohiiaje bu kwɔŋkwɔŋ lɛ mli, ni obaagbo; obaagbo mɛi ni gboiɔ yɛ ŋshɔ teŋ lɛ agbele lɛ eko. 9Be ni oyɔɔ mɛi ni gbeɔ bo lɛ adɛŋ lɛ, ani ooonyɛ okɛɛ akɛ ‘Nyɔŋmɔ ko ji mi?’ Be mli ni gbɔmɔ kɛkɛ ji bo, shi ojeee nyɔŋmɔ ko lɛ? 10Obaatsɔ gbɔi anine nɔ ni ogbo foolɔi agbele, ejaakɛ mi, miwie. Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.”
Tiro Maŋtsɛ lɛ butumɔ
11Yehowa kɛ mi wie ekoŋŋ ni ekɛɛ akɛ, 12 “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, ye Tiro maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋkɔmɔ, koni okɛɛ lɛ akɛ bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ: bo lɛ, osɛɛ lɛ mɔ ko bɛ, ole nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ohe yɛ fɛo kɛwula shi. 13Ohi Eden, Nyɔŋmɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli. Okɛ tɛ fɛɛ tɛ ni jara wa wula ohe: ojarawatɛi ni ji, rubi kɛ daiamɔnd kɛ topasiɔn kɛ beril kɛ sardio kɛ yaspi kɛ safiro kɛ smaragdo kɛ gaanɛt. Oyɛ fabii kɛ bɛji ni ashwie amɛhe shika. Gbi nɔ ni abɔ bo lɛ, nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ afee amɛ ahã bo. 14 Miha mibɔfo ni mifɔ lɛ mu bu ohe; ohi shi yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ gɔŋ krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni onyiɛ tɛi ni tsoɔ tamɔ la ateŋ. 15Kɛjɛ be ni abɔ bo lɛ shwamɔ ko bɛ ojeŋba he kɛyashi obɔi efɔŋfeemɔ. 16Ojarayeli shweremɔ hewɔ lɛ awuiyeli yi bo obɔ̃, ni ofee esha; ni no hewɔ ni mishwie bo kɛje Nyɔŋmɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ; ni bɔfo ni buɔ ohe lɛ shwie bo kɛje tɛi ni tsoɔ tamɔ la lɛ ateŋ. 17Owo ohe ejaakɛ ohe yɛ fɛo. Onilee ha ofee onii tamɔ buulu. Miŋɔ bo mitswa shi; miŋmɛ bo yayai yɛ maŋtsɛmɛi ahiɛ koni amɛkwɛ bo. 18Onishaianii lɛ afalɛ yɛ ojarayeli mli anɔkwa ni oyeee lɛ, okɛbule ohei krɔŋkrɔŋi lɛ. Mihã la je yɛ omli ni eshã bo wɛɛ, ni mihã otsɔ̃ lamlu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ mɛi fɛɛ ni na bo lɛ ahiɛ. 19 Ni Maji ni le bo fɛɛ she gbeyei, ejaakɛ onaagbee yɛ gbeyei, ni olaaje kɛmiiya naanɔ.”
Gbalɛ ni shiɔ Sidon
20 Yehowa kɛ mi wie ni ekɛɛ mi akɛ,
21“Gbɔmɔ Adesa, tsɔ̃ ohiɛ oha Sidon koni ogba oshi lɛ akɛ, 22bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, bo Sidon, naa mikɛ bo ena, ni mawo mihiɛ nyam yɛ ohewɔ, ni omaŋbii kɛaale akɛ mi ji Yehowa, kɛji migbala mɛi ni yɔɔ omli lɛ atoi ni mikɛtsɔ̃ɔ bɔ ni miyɔɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ miha lɛ. 23Ejaakɛ mibaha gbele hela abote omli, ni maha ashwie lá shi yɛ oblohui lɛ amli. Gbohii aaajwere shi yɛ oblohui lɛ amli; mɛi aaanyɔnyɔɔ yɛ klante ni akɛjɛ okoji anɔ fɛɛ naa. Kɛkɛ lɛ amɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.”
Aaajɔɔ Israel
24“Maji ni bɔle Israel we lɛ, ni amɛbɔ lɛ ahora lɛ ateŋ eko eteŋ shi epilaŋ lɛ dɔŋŋ, tamɔ ŋmei loo aklati. No amɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa.”
25Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Kɛji mibua Israel we lɛ naa kɛjɛ majimaji ni agbɛ amɛ ashwã nɔ lɛ amli, ni miwo mihiɛ nyam kɛtsɔ̃ amɛnɔ yɛ majimaji lɛ ahiɛ lɛ, no lɛ, amɛaahi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshikpɔŋ nɔ, shikpɔŋ ni mikɛhã mitsulɔ Yakob lɛ. 26 Amɛbaahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe, amɛbaamamɔ tsui, ni amɛbaafee waintromi. Amɛbaahi shi shweshweeshwe be ni magbala majimaji ni bɔle amɛ, mɛi ni bɔ amɛ ahora lɛ atoi lɛ; kɛkɛ lɛ amɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.”

english_text:
Judgment on the King of Egypt
1 Ten years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the twelfth day of the tenth month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt. Tell him and his people 3that I am saying:
King of Egypt, you were like a giant crocodile lying in a river. You acted as though you owned the Nile and made it for yourself. But now I, the Lord God, am your enemy! 4I will put a hook in your jaw and pull you out of the water, and all the fish in your river will stick to your scaly body. 5I'll throw you and the fish into the desert, and your body will fall on the hard ground. You will be left unburied, and wild animals and birds will eat your flesh. 6 Then everyone in Egypt will know that I am the Lord.
You and your nation refused to help the people of Israel and were nothing more than a broken stick. 7When they reached out to you for support, you broke in half, cutting their arms and making them fall.
8So I, the Lord God, will send troops to attack you, king of Egypt. They will kill your people and livestock, 9until your land is a barren desert. Then you will know that I have done these things.
You claimed that you made the Nile River and control it. 10Now I am turning against you and your river. Your nation will be nothing but an empty wasteland all the way from the town of Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south, and as far as the border of Ethiopia. 11No human or animal will even dare travel through Egypt, because no sign of life will be found there for 40 years. 12It will be the most barren place on earth. Every city in Egypt will lie in ruins during those 40 years, and I will scatter your people throughout the nations of the world.
13Then after those 40 years have passed, I will bring your people back from the places where I scattered them. 14They will once again live in their homeland in southern Egypt. But they will be a weak kingdom 15and won't ever be strong enough to rule nations, as they did in the past. 16My own people Israel will never again depend on your nation. In fact, when the Israelites remember what happened to you Egyptians, they will realize how wrong they were to turn to you for help. Then the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, did these things.
King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia Will Conquer Egypt
17Twenty-seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the first month. He said:
18King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked the city of Tyre. He forced his soldiers to carry so many heavy loads that their heads were rubbed bald, and their shoulders were red and sore. Nebuchadnezzar and his army still could not capture the city. 19So now I will hand over the nation of Egypt to him. He will take Egypt's valuable treasures and give them to his own troops. 20Egypt will be his reward, because he and his army have been following my orders. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
21Ezekiel, when Egypt is defeated, I will make the people of Israel strong, and I will give you the power to speak to them. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_text:
Ijipt he gbalɛ
1 Wɔnomŋɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ afii nyɔŋma lɛ mli nyɔŋ ni ji nyɔŋma lɛ nɔ, gbi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Yehowa kɛ mi wie akɛ, 2“Gbɔmɔ Adesa, tsɔ̃ ohiɛ owo Farao, Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ, ni ogba oshi lɛ kɛ Ijipt muu lɛ fɛɛ akɛ, 3bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɔ nɛ, naa, mi kɛ bo ena, bo Farao ni ji, Ijipt Maŋtsɛ, bo baa wulu kpele ni yɔɔ efai lɛ amli ni oshwãa okɛɔ akɛ, ‘Nilo Faa lɛ, minɔ ni, ni mi mibɔ mihã mihe.’ 4 Mikɛ kpoŋ baala okadaa, ni mahã ofaa lɛ mli loi lɛ akpɛtɛ ohetotoi lɛ ahe; ni magbala bo kɛjɛ ofaa lɛ mli kɛ faa lɛ mli loi lɛ fɛɛ ni kpɛtɛ ohetotoi lɛ ahe lɛ kɛba. 5Mibashɛ bo mafɔ ŋa lɛ nɔ, bo okɛ oloi ni jɛ ofaa lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Obaaya oyagbee ŋa kplanaa nɔ, ni awoŋ bo, ni afuŋ bo hu. Mikɛ bo eha shikpɔŋ kooloi kɛ ŋwɛi loofɔji ni amɛye bo. 6 Enɛ baaha Ijiptbii fɛɛ ana ale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa; ejaakɛ amɛtsɔmɔ glã amɛhã Israel we lɛ.”
7“Be ni amɛkɛ amɛnine mɔ omli lɛ, omli kumɔ, ni okpɔlɔ amɛkoji fɛɛ; be ni amɛkpasa bo lɛ, oku, ni amɛhɛ lɔŋe. 8No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, naa, mafã klante mawo bo, ni maplene omli gbɔmɛi kɛ kooloi fɛɛ. 9Ni maha Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ atsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃ kɛ olɛŋlɛ. No Ijiptbii kɛaale akɛ, mi, mi ji Yehowa. Akɛni okɛɛ akɛ, ‘Nilo Faa lɛ minɔ ni, ni mi mibɔ lɛ,’ 10no hewɔ lɛ, naa, mi kɛ bo ena, ni mikɛ ofaa Nilo lɛ hu ena; ni mafee Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ olɛŋlɛ kɛ amaŋfɔ̃ kwraa, kɛjɛ Migdol ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ kɛyashi Aswan ni yɔɔ wuoyigbɛ lɛ aahu kɛyashi Kush husui anɔ tɔ̃ɔ. 11Gbɔmɔ adesa ko tsɔŋ jɛi kɛhoŋ ni kooloo ko hu tsɔŋ jɛi kɛhoŋ. Ahiŋ nɔ afii nyɔŋmai ejwɛ sɔŋŋ. 12Mafee Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ shikpɔji amaŋfɔ̃i amli amaŋfɔ̃; ni emaji wuji lɛ hu aaatsɔmɔ amaŋfɔ̃i afii nyɔŋmai ejwɛ yɛ maji ni akpãtã amɛhiɛ lɛ ateŋ. Mashwie Ijiptbii lɛ mawo majimaji lɛ anɔ ni magbɛ amɛ mashwã shikpɔji lɛ anɔ.”
13Hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɔ nɛ, “Afii nyɔŋmai ejwɛ sɛɛ lɛ, mabua Ijiptbii lɛ anaa kɛaajɛ mɛi ateŋ ni agbɛ amɛ ashwã lɛ. 14Makpale Ijiptbii lɛ, ni mikɛ amɛ aaaba Patros ni ji Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni aŋɔ amɛ nom kɛjɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ; ni amɛaahi jɛi akɛ mɛi ni aba amɛlumɔyeli shi. 15Ebaatsɔ̃ maŋtsɛyelii lɛ ateŋ nɔ ni aba lɛ shi fe fɛɛ, ni ewoŋ ehe nɔ yɛ majimaji lɛ anɔ dɔŋŋ. Ni maha ehewalɛ nɔ agbɔ bɔ ni eyeŋ maŋ ko maŋ ko nɔ lumɔ dɔŋŋ. 16Ijipt efeŋ maŋ bɔ ni Israel we lɛ kɛ ehe baafɔ̃ enɔ dɔŋŋ, bɔ ni aaafee Ijipt ahã lɛ, eeehã Israel we lɛ akai akɛ etɔ̃ akɛ eyabi Ijipt dɛŋ yelikɛbuamɔ. No Israel kɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa.”
Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar baaye Ijipt nɔ kunim
17Wɔnomŋɔɔ lɛ mli afi ni ji nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ kpawo lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, Yehowa kɛ mi wie akɛ, 18“Gbɔmɔ Adesa, Babilon maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar hã etabilɔi lɛ gbo deŋme ni naa wa yɛ Tiro tuamɔ hewɔ. Ewebii lɛ tsu nii waa ni yiteŋ fɛɛ yiteŋ kpa, ni kɔŋ fɛɛ kɔŋ nɔ kpɔlɔ; shi kɛ̃lɛ, lɛ kɛ etabilɔi lɛ nãaa nɔ ko kɛjɛɛɛ Tiro akɛ amɛnyɔmɔwoo yɛ amɛdeŋme ni amɛgbo yɛ Tiro tuamɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ mli. 19Agbɛnɛ, bɔ ni mi, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa mikɛɔ nɛ, naa, mikɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ baawo Babilon Maŋtsɛ Nebukadnezar dɛŋ; ni ebaaha emli nii, ni ebaakpãtã maŋ lɛ hiɛ, ni emli jwetri lɛ ekɛbaaya; ni no baatsɔ̃ etabilɔi lɛ anyɔmɔwoo. 20 Mikɛ Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ eha lɛ akɛ edeŋmegbomɔ lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo, ejaakɛ mi etsu nii lɛ eha.” Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.
21“Nakai gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ maha hewalɛtsɛ ko ate shi yɛ Israel we lɛ ni magbele bo Ezekiel onaa ni owie yɛ amɛteŋ. No amɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.”

english_text:
Egypt Will Be a Barren Desert
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Egypt that I am saying:
Cry out in despair,
3because you will soon
be punished!
That will be a time
of darkness and doom
for all nations.
4Your own nation of Egypt
will be attacked,
and Ethiopia will suffer.
You will be killed in battle,
and your land will be robbed
and left in ruins.
5Soldiers hired from Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, Arabia, Kub, as well as from Israel, will die in that battle. 6All of your allies will be killed, and your proud strength will crumble. People will die from Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south. I, the Lord, have spoken.
7Your nation of Egypt will be the most deserted place on earth, and its cities will lie in complete ruin. 8I will set fire to your land, and anyone who defended your nation will die. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
9On the same day I destroy Egypt, I will send messengers to the Ethiopians to announce their coming destruction. They think they are safe, but they will be terrified.
10Your Egyptian army is very strong, but I will send King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to completely defeat that army. 11He and his cruel troops will invade and destroy your land and leave your dead bodies piled everywhere.
12I will dry up the Nile River, then sell the land to evil buyers. I will send foreigners to turn your entire nation into a barren desert. I, the Lord, have spoken.
Egypt's Proud Cities Will Lie in Ruins
The Lord said to the people of Egypt:
13All the idols and images you Egyptians worship in the city of Memphis will be smashed. No one will be left to rule your nation, and terror will fill the land. 14The city of Pathros will be left in ruins, and Zoan will be burned to the ground. Thebes, your capital city, will also be destroyed! 15The fortress city of Pelusium will feel my fierce anger, and all the troops stationed at Thebes will be slaughtered.
16I will set fire to your nation of Egypt! The city of Pelusium will be in anguish. Thebes will fall, and the people of Memphis will live in constant fear. 17The young soldiers in the cities of Heliopolis and Bubastis will die in battle, and the rest of the people will be taken prisoner. 18You were so proud of your nation's power, but when I crush that power and kill that pride, darkness will fall over the city of Tahpanhes. A dark, gloomy cloud will cover the land as you are being led away into captivity. 19When I'm through punishing Egypt, you will know that I am the Lord.
Egypt's King Is Powerless
20Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the seventh day of the first month. He said:
21Ezekiel, son of man, I, the Lord, have defeated the king of Egypt! I broke his arm, and no one has wrapped it or put it in a sling, so that it could heal and get strong enough to hold a sword. 22So tell him that I am now his worst enemy. I will break both his arms—the good one and the broken one! His sword will drop from his hand forever, 23and I will scatter the Egyptians all over the world.
24-25I will strengthen the power of Babylonia's king and give him my sword to use against Egypt. I will also make the wounded king of Egypt powerless, and he will moan in pain and die in front of the Babylonian king. Then everyone on earth will know that I am the Lord. 26I will force the Egyptians to live as prisoners in foreign nations, and they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them.
translation_text:
Yehowa baagbala Ijipt toi
1Yehowa kɛ mi wie ni ekɛɛ mi akɛ, 2“Gbɔmɔ Adesa, gbaa ni okɛɛ akɛ bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, nyɛwoa lele! Kpoo hã nakai gbi lɛ.
3 Gbi lɛ ebɛŋkɛ,
Yehowa gbi lɛ ebɛŋkɛ.
Gbi lɛ aaafee oblɔtu gbi.
Eeefee majimaji lɛ ahiɛkpãtãmɔ be.
4Aaafã klante awo Ijipt
ni ŋmiŋmi baamɔmɔ mɛi
yɛ Kush.
Mɛi baanyɔnyɔɔ yɛ Ijipt,
ni abaaloo enii babaoo ni eyɔɔ
lɛ kɛya;
ni abaafee lɛ amaŋfɔ̃.
5“Akɛ klante baaplene Etiopiabii kɛ Ludbii kɛ Libiabii kɛ Arabbii kɛ Kubbii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii fɛɛ hu ni kɛ Ijipt efee ekome lɛ.
6“Bɔ ni Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, mɛi fɛɛ ni fi Ijipt sɛɛ lɛ aaaplene, ni ehewalɛ ni ekɛshwãa lɛ baaba shi kɛjɛ Migdol ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ lɛ kɛyashi Aswan yɛ wuoyigbɛ lɛ; amɛaanyɔnyɔi yɛ klante naa. Mi, Yehowa miwie. 7Eshikpɔŋ lɛ aaatsɔ̃ shikpɔji ni ji amaŋfɔ̃i lɛ amli amaŋfɔ̃, ni emaji wuji lɛ hu baafata maji wuji ni abutu amɛ lɛ ahe. 8Kɛji mima Ijipt naa la mishã, ni mikpãtã mɛi ni ye bua lɛ lɛ ahiɛ lɛ, no amɛkɛaale akɛ, mi, mi ji Yehowa.
9 “Gbi nɔ ni mafite Ijipt lɛ, matsu tsuji kɛtsɔ̃ lɛlɛ mli ni amɛyawo Etiopiabii ni kpaaa ta ko gbɛ lɛ ahe gbeyei. Ijipt butumɔ lɛ baahã ŋmiŋmi amɔmɔ amɛ, ejaakɛ, naa, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ, nakai gbi lɛ baana aba. 10Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, matsɔ̃ Nebukadnezar, Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ, nine nɔ mafo Ijipt ninamɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. 11Lɛ kɛ emɛi lɛ ji maŋ ni he yɔɔ gbeyei fe maji fɛɛ. Amɛbaaba amɛbakpãtã shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ; amɛbaafã klante amɛwo Ijipt, ni amɛbaahã gbohii ayi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ̃ tɔ. 12Ni mahã Nilo Faa lɛ amii; ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baawo mɛi fɔ̃ji adɛŋ. Matsɔ̃ mɛi kpɔ̃ji anine nɔ, ni mahã shikpɔŋ lɛ atsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃, ni mafite nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ nɔ. Mi, Yehowa, mikɛɛ.” 13Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Mafite amɛmɔji lɛ; ni mahã akumɔ amɛmãgãi ni yɔɔ Memfis lɛ. Ayeŋ lumɔ ko dɔŋŋ yɛ Ijipt, ni mahã Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aba gbeyei. 14Mahã Patros, ni yɔɔ Ijipt wuoyigbɛ lɛ atsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃; ni mawo la mashã Zoan ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ lɛ; ni magbala Tebes maŋ wulu lɛ toi. 15Mimli baawo la waa awo Pelusium ni ji Ijipt mɔɔ ni wa lɛ, ni maplene asafo yuu ni yɔɔ Tebis lɛ. 16Mawo la mashã Ijipt, ni Pelusium baakɛ̃mɔ. Abaawule ni akumɔ Tebes gbogboi lɛ ashwie shi. 17Oblahii ni yɔɔ Awen kɛ Pi-Beset baanyɔnyɔɔ yɛ klante naa, ni aaaŋɔ amɛyei lɛ nom. 18Duŋ baawo shwane yɛ Tehafnehes, gbi nɔ ni mafite Ijipt nɔyeli hewalɛ lɛ, ni ehewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ehe lɛ sɛɛ baafo. Atatu ko baaha Ijipt nɔ, ni abaaŋɔ emaŋbii lɛ fɛɛ nom. 19Bɔ ni magbala Ijipt toi maha nɛ, ni no ekɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.”
Ijipt Maŋtsɛ hewalɛ fitemɔ
20Wɔnomŋɔɔ lɛ mli afi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ ekome lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji kpawo lɛ nɔ lɛ, Yehowa kɛ mi wie ni ekɛɛ, 21“Gbɔmɔ Adesa, miku Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ nine; ni naa, akɛ flanɔfii mama efiko nɔ, koni etsa ni emli awa bɔ ni eeenyɛ klante mli emɔ. 22No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, naa, mikɛ Farao ni ji, Ijipt Maŋtsɛ lɛ, ena, ni makumɔ eniji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛ nɔ ni akumɔ momo lɛ fɛɛ, ni maha klante lɛ aje edɛŋ agbee shi. 23Mashwie Ijiptbii lɛ mawo majimaji lɛ anɔ, ni magbɛ amɛ mashwã shikpɔji lɛ anɔ. 24 Ni mawo Babilon Maŋtsɛ lɛ hewalɛ, ni mikɛ miklante lɛ baawo edɛŋ; shi Farao lɛ, lɛ lɛ maku enine, ni eeekɛ̃mɔ yɛ Babilon Maŋtsɛ lɛ hiɛ tamɔ mɔ ni apila lɛ gbele nɔ. 25Mawaje Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ, shi Farao niji aaakpɔlɔ; ni amɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji, Yehowa. Kɛji mikɛ miklante lɛ wo Babilon maŋtsɛ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ, eeefã ewo Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ. 26Mashwie Ijiptbii lɛ mawo majimaji lɛ anɔ ni magbɛ amɛ mashwã shikpɔji lɛ anɔ; ni amɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.”

english_text:
Egypt's King Will Be Chopped Down like a Cedar Tree
1Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the third month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Egypt and his people that I am saying:
You are more powerful
than anyone on earth.
Now listen to this.
3There was once a cedar tree
in Lebanon
with large, strong branches
reaching to the sky.
4This tree had plenty of water
to help it grow tall,
and nearby streams watered
the other trees
in the forest.
5But this tree towered over
those other trees,
and its branches
grew long and thick.
6Birds built nests
in its branches,
and animals were born
beneath it.
People from all nations
lived in the shade
of this strong tree.
7It had beautiful,
long branches,
and its roots found water
deep in the soil.
8 None of the cedar trees
in my garden of Eden
were as beautiful
as this tree;
no tree of any kind
had such long branches.
9I, the Lord, gave this tree
its beauty,
and I helped the branches
grow strong.
All other trees in Eden
wanted to be just like it.
10King of Egypt, now listen to what I, the Lord God, am saying about that tree:
The tree grew so tall that it reached the sky and became very proud and arrogant. 11So I, the Lord God, will reject the tree and hand it over to a foreign ruler, who will punish it for its wickedness. 12Cruel foreigners will chop it down and leave it wherever it falls. Branches and broken limbs will be scattered over the mountains and in the valleys. The people living in the shade of those branches will go somewhere else. 13Birds will then nest on the stump of the fallen tree, and wild animals will trample its branches.
14Never again will any tree dare to grow as tall as this tree, no matter how much water it has. Every tree must die, just as humans die and go down to the world of the dead.
15On the day this tree dies and goes to the world below, I, the Lord God, will command rivers and streams to mourn its death. Every underground spring of water and every river will stop flowing. The mountains in Lebanon will be covered with darkness as a sign of their sorrow, and all the trees in the forest will wither. 16This tree will crash to the ground, and I will send it to the world below. Then the nations of the earth will tremble.
The trees from Eden and the choice trees from Lebanon are now in the world of the dead, and they will be comforted when this tree falls. 17Those people who found protection in its shade will also be sent to the world below, where they will join the dead.
18King of Egypt, all these things will happen to you and your people! You were like this tree at one time—taller and stronger than anyone on earth. But now you will be chopped down, just as every tree in the garden of Eden must die. You will be sent down to the world of the dead, where you will join the godless and the other victims of violent death. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Akɛ Ijipt to Seda tso he
1Wɔnomŋɔɔ lɛ mli afi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ ekome lɛ nɔ nyɔŋ ni ji etɛ̃ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, Yehowa kɛ mi wie akɛ, 2“Gbɔmɔ Adesa, bi Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ etabilɔi lɛ fɛɛ akɛ,
Namɔ nyɛtamɔ yɛ agbojee mli?
3 Naa, nyɛtamɔ Asiria, ni mikɛ miito
Lebanon tsenedru kɛ
eniji fɛɛfɛji kɛ
eshishi hɔɔŋ,
tso grɔŋŋ ni
eyiteŋ shɛɔ atatuiaŋ he.
4Ena nu,
shikpɔŋ ofɔ̃ ehã eda,
ni ekwɔ grɔŋŋ
Fai lɛ hã he ni atɛo
tso lɛ yɛ lɛ nu,
ni nu lɛ gbala niji
kɛtee kooŋ tsei lɛ
fɛɛ ashishi.
5Akɛni ena nu hewɔ lɛ
ekwɔ fe kooŋ tsei lɛ fɛɛ.
Eniji wuji lɛ dara,
ni eniji bibii lɛ kɛlɛ;
ejaakɛ eshishi fãi lɛ
na nu babaoo.
6Ŋwɛi loofɔji fɛɛ
fee amɛtsui
yɛ eniji wuji lɛ ateŋ,
ni ŋaŋ kooloi fɛɛ fɔ amɛbii
yɛ eniji bibii ashishi;
ni eshishi hɔɔŋ lɛ mli
jeŋmaji wuji fɛɛ hi.
7Edalɛ lɛ yɛ fɛo naakpa.
Eniji bibii akɛlɛmɔ hu yɛ akɔnɔ,
ejaakɛ eshishi fãi lɛ
tee shikpɔŋ tɔ̃ɔ
kɛyanina nu pii.
8 Tsenedrui ni yɔɔ Nyɔŋmɔ trom lɛ mli
lɛ, eko eko kɛ lɛ yeee hegbɔ;
sɛsɛo lɛ kɛ eniji wuji lɛ yeee hegbɔ,
ni papaoi lɛ jeee fɛifɛi kɛ okɛ amɛto
bibii lɛ ahe.
Tso ko tso ko bɛ
Nyɔŋmɔ trom lɛ mli
ni kɛ lɛ ye egbɔ kɛ he fɛo.
9Mi mifee, ni mihã eniji bibii lɛ
abumɔ hã ehe fee fɛo lɛ,
ni Eden tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ
Nyɔŋmɔ trom lɛ mli lɛ
ahiɛ kɔ̃ enɔ.
10 “No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, akɛni ekwɔ grɔŋŋ, ni eyiteŋ shɛ atatuiaŋ hewɔ lɛ, efee ntɛŋ; 11hewɔ lɛ, mikɛ lɛ ewo jeŋmaji lɛ ateŋ eko ni he wa lɛ dɛŋ; ekɛ lɛ aye waa; bɔ ni sa eyitsoŋwalɛ lɛ. Ejaakɛ mishwie lɛ. 12Gbɔi ni ji jeŋmajimaji lɛ ateŋ yiwalɔi ni fe fɛɛ lɛ too lɛ fɔ̃ shi, ni amɛshi lɛ. Eniji bibii lɛ shwie gɔji lɛ anɔ kɛ jɔi lɛ amli, ni eniji wuji lɛ kumɔ shwie nujɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mɛi fɛɛ bashi ehɔɔŋ lɛ mli amɛtee. 13Ŋwɛi loofɔji basɔ̃mɔ etsokuku ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ; ni ŋaŋ kooloi fɛɛ banyiɛ eniji bibii lɛ anɔ. 14Afee enɛ bɔ ni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso ni ma shi yɛ faa toi akakwɔ kakadaŋŋ, ni ebai yashɛ atatuiaŋ nɛkɛ dɔŋŋ; bɔ ni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso ni shishifã naa nu lɛ akakwɔ kɛtee ŋwɛi kɛyanina amɛ. Ejaakɛ aŋɔ amɛ fɛɛ ahã gbele; akɛ amɛ eshi gbɔmɛi adesai kɛ mɛi hu ni yaa gbohiiaje lɛ anɔ.
15“Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, kɛ ekpeleke shi kɛtee gbohiiaje lɛ, mahã bu kwɔŋkwɔŋ lɛ awo yara yɛ ehewɔ ni matsi efai lɛ anaa, ni nu ko nu ko hoŋ. Mahã Lebanon gɔji lɛ anɔ awo duŋ, ni ŋa nɔ tsei lɛ fɛɛ baatɔ biti yɛ ehewɔ. 16Kɛ mitsi lɛ kɛ mɛi krokomɛi lɛ ayisɛɛ miwo gbohiiaje bu kwɔŋkwɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Mahã majimaji lɛ ahoso yɛ eshigbeemɔ gbɛɛmɔ lɛ naa. Eden tsei fɛɛ kɛ Lebanon tsei kpakpai ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ ni naa nu kpakpa lɛ amii baashɛ amɛhe yɛ gbohiiaje. 17Amɛ hu amɛkɛ lɛ baaya gbohiiaje kɛyanina mɛi ni nyɔnyɔi yɛ klante naa lɛ. Hɛɛ! Nakai nɔŋŋ mɛi fɛɛ ni hi tso lɛ hɔɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ majimaji lɛ ateŋ lɛ hiɛ baakpãtã.
18“Belɛ yɛ anunyam kɛ agbojee gbɛfaŋ lɛ, namɔ po otamɔ yɛ Eden tsei lɛ ateŋ? Aaatoo bo kɛ Eden tsei krokomɛi lɛ, ni akɛ nyɛ baawo gbohiiaje; ni oookã foolɔi kɛ mɛi ni enyɔnyɔɔ yɛ klante naa lɛ ateŋ. Bɔ ni Farao kɛ emaŋbii lɛ fɛɛ anaagbee baatamɔ nɛ.” Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ.

english_text:
A Funeral Song for the King of Egypt
1Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the twelfth month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt and tell him I am saying:
You act like a lion
roaming the earth;
but you are nothing more than
a crocodile in a river,
churning up muddy water
with your feet.
3King of Egypt, listen to me. I, the Lord God, will catch you in my net and let a crowd of foreigners drag you to shore. 4I will throw you into an open field, where birds and animals will come to feed on your flesh. 5I will spread your rotting flesh over the mountains and in the valleys, 6and your blood will flow throughout the land and fill up the streams. 7 I will cover the whole sky and every star with thick clouds, so that the sun and moon will stop shining. 8The heavens will become black, leaving your country in total darkness. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
9Foreign nations you have never heard of will be shocked when I tell them how I destroyed you. 10They will be horrified, and when I flash my sword in victory on the day of your death, their kings will tremble in the fear of what could happen to them.
11The king of Babylonia is coming to attack you, king of Egypt! 12Your soldiers will be killed by the cruelest army in the world, and everything you take pride in will be crushed. 13I will slaughter your cattle that graze by the river, and no people or livestock will be left to muddy its water. 14The water will be clear, and streams will be calm. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
15Egypt will become a barren wasteland, and no living thing will ever survive there. Then you and your people will know that I am the Lord.
16This is your warning, and it will be used as a funeral song by foreign women to mourn the death of your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
A Sad Ending for Egypt
17On the fifteenth day of that same month, the Lord said:
18Ezekiel, son of man, mourn for the Egyptians and condemn them to the world of the dead, where they will be buried alongside the people of other powerful nations. 19Say to them:
You may be more beautiful
than the people
of other nations,
but you will also die
and join the godless
in the world below.
20You cannot escape! The enemy's sword is ready to slaughter every one of you. 21Brave military leaders killed in battle will gladly welcome you and your allies into the world of the dead.
22-23The graves of soldiers from Assyria are there. They once terrified people, but they were killed in battle and now lie deep in the world of the dead.
24-25The graves of soldiers from Elam are there. The very sight of those godless soldiers once terrified their enemies and made them panic. But now they are disgraced and ashamed as they lie in the world of the dead, alongside others who were killed in battle.
26The graves of soldiers from Meshech and Tubal are there. These godless soldiers who terrified people were all killed in battle. 27They were not given a proper burial like the heroes of long ago, who were buried with their swords under their heads and with their shields over their bodies. These were the heroes who made their enemies panic.
28You Egyptians will be cruelly defeated, and you will be buried alongside these other godless soldiers who died in battle.
29The graves of kings and leaders from Edom are there. They were powerful at one time. Now they are buried in the world of the dead with other godless soldiers killed in battle.
30The graves of the rulers of the north are there, as well as those of the Sidonians. Their powerful armies once terrified enemies. Now they lie buried in the world of the dead, where they are disgraced like other soldiers killed in battle.
31The Lord God says:
When your king of Egypt sees all of these graves, he and his soldiers will be glad they are not the only ones suffering. 32I sent him to terrify people all over the earth. But he and his army will be killed and buried alongside other godless soldiers in the world of the dead. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Akɛ Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ to baa he
1Yɛ afi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ lɛ nɔ nyɔŋ ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, Yehowa kɛ mi wie akɛ, 2“Gbɔmɔ Adesa, ye Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋkɔmɔ ni okɛɛ lɛ akɛ Obuɔ ohe akɛ jata ko yɛ majimaji lɛ ateŋ, shi moŋ, otamɔ báa yɛ faa mli, otswaa aŋmɔ yɛ onui lɛ amli, okɛ onaji taa nu mli ni okpɔtɔɔ fai lɛ. 3Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, maŋmɛ onɔ adrã yaa yɛ majimaji ateŋ, ni aaagbala bo kɛba shia nɔ. 4Mashɛ bo mafɔ̃ shikpɔŋ; ni mafɔ̃ bo mashɛ mafɔ shikpɔŋ kplanaa nɔ, ni mahã ŋwɛi loofɔji abasɔmɔ onɔ, ni mahã shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ kooloi aye bo amɛtɔrɔ. 5Mikɛ oheloo baashwã gɔji lɛ anɔ, ni mikɛ ogbohii lɛ aaawo jɔi lɛ obɔ̃bɔ̃. 6Mikɛ olá ni hoɔ lɛ baafɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔtsɔɔtsɔ kɛyashi gɔji lɛ anɔ tete, ni olá lɛ aayi nujɔi lɛ obɔ̃bɔ̃. 7 Kɛji mikpãtã ohiɛ lɛ, mahã ŋwɛi hiɛ aha, ni eŋulamii lɛ awo duŋ. Mikɛ atatu aaaha hulu lɛ hiɛ, ni nyɔɔŋtsere hu kpɛŋ. 8Magbe ŋwɛi kanei ala ni kpɛɔ lɛ yɛ onɔ; ni mahã duŋ awo yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.” Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.
9“Kɛji mikpãtã ohiɛ yɛ majimaji lɛ ateŋ, ni mikpala bo kɛtee shikpɔji ni oleee anɔ lɛ, no baahã mɛi pii atsuii aye. 10Kɛji mifɔ̃fɔ̃ɔ miklante lɛ yɛ amɛhiɛ lɛ, mahã majimaji pii ahe ajɔ̃ amɛhe ni ŋmiŋmi aaamɔmɔ amɛmaŋtsɛmɛi lɛ hu yɛ ohewɔ. Gbi nɔ ni ooogbee shi lɛ amɛteŋ amɛhe, amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ he aaakpokpo hiŋmɛitswaa fɛɛ hiŋmɛitswaa, amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ he aaakpokpo yɛ ewala hewɔ.
11“Ejaakɛ bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ Ijipt nɛ, Babilon maŋtsɛ kɛ eklante aaabatua bo. 12Mahã asraafoi kãkãlɔi kɛ klante abakpãtã omaŋbii babaoo lɛ ahiɛ; asraafoi nɛɛ fɛɛ lɛ, yiwalɔi fe fɛɛ ni jɛ majimaji lɛ ateŋ ji amɛ. Amɛbaafite nibii ahewɔ ni Ijipt wo ehe lɛ, ni abaakpãtã maŋbii kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ hiɛ. 13Maplene emli shĩa kooloi fɛɛ kɛaajɛ fai lɛ anaa. Ni gbɔmɔ nane ko etaŋ mli dɔŋŋ; asaŋ shĩa kooloi akoklotoi etaŋ mli dɔŋŋ. 14Kɛkɛ lɛ mahã amɛnu fɛɛ nu hiɛ atɛ̃, ni mahã amɛfai lɛ aho nyaa tamɔ mu. Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ. 15Kɛji mifee Ijipt shikpɔŋ lɛ amaŋfɔ̃, ni mikpãtã emli nii fɛɛ hiɛ, ni miplenee emli gbɔmɛi fɛɛ lɛ, no dani amɛaana amɛle akɛ, mi, mi ji Yehowa. 16Nɛkɛ kɔkɔbɔɔ nɛɛ baatsɔ̃ yarafeemɔ lala, ni majimaji lɛ amli biyei lɛ baala amɛkɛfo Ijipt kɛ emlibii babaoo lɛ. Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.”
17Yɛ afi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ enumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Yehowa kɛ mi wie akɛ, 18 “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, fo Ijipt kɛ emaŋbii babaoo lɛ, mɛi ni abaatsirɛ amɛ kɛ maji wuji abiyei lɛ hu awo gbohiiaje kɛyafata mɛi ni etee gbohiiaje momo lɛ ahe lɛ. 19 Bi akɛ ‘Ohe yɛ fɛo fe namɔ?’ Kpelekemɔ shi kɛya gbohiiaje ni akɛ bo ayaŋmɛ foolɔi lɛ amasɛi! 20 Ijiptbii lɛ baafata mɛi ni baanyɔnyɔi yɛ klante naa lɛ ahe, ni aaafu emɛi babaoo lɛ afata ehe. 21 Ijipt kãkãlɔi lɛ kɛ mɛi ni wa amɛ yɛ ta mli lɛ baakɛɛ yɛ amɛhe yɛ gbohiiaje akɛ, ‘Foolɔi lɛ ni nyɔ yɛ klante naa lɛ ekpeleke shi kɛba gbohiiaje, ni amɛkamɔ shi diŋŋ!’
22“Asiria yɛ jɛi ni esafo yuu lɛ fɛɛ asaŋi ebɔle lɛ. Amɛ fɛɛ lɛ klante naa amɛnyɔnyɔɔ yɛ. 23 Amɛsaŋi lɛ yɛ gbohiiaje teŋteŋ tɔ̃ɔ, asafo lɛ asaŋi lɛ ebɔle lɛ diɛŋtsɛ esaŋ lɛ he kɛkpe; amɛ mɛi ni amɛhã ŋmiŋmi mɔmɔ mɛi yɛ hiɛkãalɔi ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amɛ fɛɛ lɛ, klante naa amɛnyɔnyɔɔ yɛ.
24“Elam yɛ jɛi ni esafo yuu lɛ fɛɛ asaŋi ebɔle lɛ. Amɛ fɛɛ lɛ klante naa amɛnyɔnyɔɔ yɛ. Foolɔi ni kpeleke shi kɛtee gbohiiaje ni. Amɛhã ŋmiŋmi mɔmɔ hiɛkãalɔi yɛ hiɛkãalɔi ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, agbɛnɛ amɛ kɛ mɛi ni kpelekeɔ shi kɛyaa gbohiiaje lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ eshwie shi. 25Elam kã mɛi ni nyɔnyɔi yɛ klante naa lɛ ateŋ. Esafo yuu lɛ asaŋi lɛ ebɔle lɛ kɛkpe. Amɛ fɛɛ lɛ foolɔi ni, ni amɛnyɔnyɔɔ yɛ klante naa. Amɛhã ŋmiŋmi mɔmɔ mɛi yɛ hiɛkãalɔi ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; agbɛnɛ amɛ kɛ mɛi ni kpelekeɔ shi kɛyaa gbohiiaje lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ eshwie shi. Amɛkamɔ mɛi ni enyɔnyɔɔ lɛ ateŋ.
26 “Meshek kɛ Tubal yɛ jɛi, kɛ amɛsafo yuu lɛ fɛɛ, ni amɛsaŋi lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛkpe. Amɛ fɛɛ lɛ foolɔi ni, ni amɛnyɔnyɔɔ yɛ klante naa; ejaakɛ amɛhã ŋmiŋmi mɔmɔ mɛi yɛ hiɛkãalɔi ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.
27“Amɛ lɛ, afuuu amɛ tamɔ afu blema kãkãlɔi lɛ, mɛi ni kpeleke shi kɛtee gbohiiaje kɛ amɛtawuunii lɛ; mɛi ni ahã amɛtsɔle amɛtawuu klantei, ni akɛ amɛtsɛŋi eshwie amɛnɔ lɛ. Ejaakɛ kãkãlɔi nɛɛ ehã ŋmiŋmi emɔmɔ mɛi yɛ hiɛkãalɔi ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛŋ. 28Nɛkɛ nɔŋŋ, bo Ijipt, abaakumɔ bo, ni oooyakã foolɔi ni nyɔnyɔɔ yɛ klante naa lɛ ateŋ.
29“Edom yɛ jɛi; emaŋtsɛmɛi kɛ elumɛi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ jɛi. Mɛi ni yɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ amɛkamɔ mɛi ni nyɔnyɔɔ yɛ klante naa lɛ ateŋ. Amɛ hu amɛkamɔ foolɔi ni kpelekeɔ shi kɛyaa gbohiiaje lɛ ateŋ.
30“Kooyigbɛ lumɛi lɛ kɛ Sidonbii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ jɛi. Amɛmɛi ni amɛhe wa lɛ hã ŋmiŋmi mɔmɔ mɛi lɛ, amɛ hu amɛkɛ mɛi ni nyɔnyɔɔ yɛ klante naa lɛ hu fɛɛ etee gbohiiaje kɛ hiɛgbele. Foolɔi ni kɛ mɛi ni enyɔnyɔɔ yɛ klante naa lɛ kamɔ shi, ni amɛkɛ mɛi ni kpelekeɔ shi kɛyaa gbohiiaje lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ eshwie shi.
31 “Kɛji Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ na amɛ lɛ emii aaashɛ ehe yɛ esafo yuu lɛ hewɔ, ejaakɛ Ijipt maŋtsɛ lɛ kɛ esafo yuu lɛ hu nyɔŋyɔɔ yɛ klante naa. Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.
32“Akɛni ehã ŋmiŋmi mɔmɔ mɛi yɛ hiɛkãalɔi ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewɔ lɛ, abaafu lɛ kɛ esafo yuu lɛ ashi foolɔi kɛ mɛi ni akɛ klante gbegbee amɛ yɛ ta mli lɛ anɔ. Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.”

english_text:
The Lord Appoints Ezekiel To Stand Watch
(Ezekiel 3.16-21)
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, warn your people by saying:
Someday, I, the Lord, may send an enemy to invade a country. And suppose its people choose someone to stand watch 3and to sound a warning signal when the enemy is seen coming. 4-5If any of these people hear the signal and ignore it, they will be killed in battle. But it will be their own fault, because they could have escaped if they had paid attention.
6But suppose the person watching fails to sound the warning signal. The enemy will attack and kill some of the sinful people in that country, and I, the Lord, will hold that person responsible for their death.
7Ezekiel, I have appointed you to stand watch for the people of Israel. So listen to what I say, then warn them for me. 8When I tell wicked people they will die because of their sins, you must warn them to turn from their sinful ways. But if you refuse to warn them, you are responsible for their death. 9If you do warn them, and they keep sinning, they will die because of their sins, and you will be innocent.
The Lord Is Always Fair
(Ezekiel 18.21-30)
10The Lord said:
Ezekiel, son of man, the people of Israel are complaining that the punishment for their sins is more than they can stand. They have lost all hope for survival, and they blame me. 11Tell them that as surely as I am the living Lord God, I don't like to see wicked people die. I enjoy seeing them turn from their sins and live. So if the Israelites want to live, they must stop sinning and turn back to me.
12Tell them that when good people start sinning, all the good they did in the past cannot save them from being punished. And remind them that when wicked people stop sinning, their past sins will be completely forgiven, and they won't be punished.
13Suppose I promise good people that they will live, then later they start sinning and believe they will be saved by the good they did in the past. These people will certainly be put to death because of their sins. Their good deeds will be forgotten.
14Suppose I warn wicked people that they will die because of their sins, and they stop sinning and start doing right. 15For example, they need to return anything they have taken as security for a loan and anything they have stolen. Then if they stop doing evil and start obeying my Law, they will live. 16Their past sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they have done right.
17Ezekiel, your people accuse me of being unfair. But they are the ones who are unfair. 18If good people start doing evil, they will be put to death, because they have sinned. 19And if wicked people stop sinning and start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment. 20But the Israelites still think I am unfair. So warn them that they will be punished for what they have done.
The News of Jerusalem's Fall
21 Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, a refugee who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me on the fifth day of the tenth month. He told me that the city had fallen.
22The evening before this man arrived at my house, the Lord had taken control of me. So when the man came to me the next morning, I could once again speak.
What Will Happen to Those Left in Israel?
23Then the Lord said:
24Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in the ruined cities of Israel are saying, “Abraham was just one man, and the Lord gave him this whole land of Israel. There are many of us, and so this land must be ours.”
25So, Ezekiel, tell them I am saying:
How can you think the land is still yours? You eat meat with blood in it and worship idols. You commit murder 26and spread violence throughout the land. Everything you do is wicked; you are even unfaithful in marriage. And you claim the land is yours!
27As surely as I am the living Lord God, you people in the ruined cities will be killed in battle. Those of you living in the countryside will be eaten by wild animals, and those hiding in caves and on rocky cliffs will die from deadly diseases. 28I will make the whole country an empty wasteland and crush the power in which you take such pride. Even the mountains will be bare, and no one will try to cross them. 29I will punish you because of your sins, and I will turn your nation into a barren desert. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
The People Listen, but Don't Change
The Lord said:
30Ezekiel, son of man, the people with you in Babylonia talk about you when they meet by the city walls or in the doorways of their houses. They say, “Let's ask Ezekiel what the Lord has said today.” 31So they all come and listen to you, but they refuse to do what you tell them. They claim to be faithful, but they are forever trying to cheat others out of their money. 32They treat you as though you were merely singing love songs or playing music. They listen, but don't do anything you say.
33Soon they will be punished, just as you warned, and they will know that a prophet has been among them.
translation_text:
Nyɔŋmɔ to Ezekiel bulɔ
1Yehowa kɛ mi wie akɛ, 2“Gbɔmɔ Adesa, kɛ omaŋbii lɛ awie ni okɛɛ amɛ akɛ, kɛji mihã ta ba shikpɔŋ ko nɔ, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bii lɛ fã amɛteŋ mɔ kome akɛ bulɔ, 3ni ena akɛ ta miiba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ekpã tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ kɛtswa maŋ lɛ adafi lɛ, 4no lɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni aaanu tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ lɛ gbɛɛmɔ ni ebooo adafitswaa lɛ toi lɛ, kɛji ta lɛ banina lɛ, ni etsɔ̃ mli egbo lɛ, elá abua lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eyiteŋ. 5Ejaakɛ enu tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ lɛ gbɛɛmɔ, shi ebooo adafitswaa lɛ toi; elá abua lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eyiteŋ. Eji ebo adafitswaa lɛ toi kulɛ eeehere eyiwala. 6Shi kɛji bulɔ lɛ na ta lɛ miiba, ni ekpãaa tɛtɛrɛmantɛrɛ lɛ, ni etswaaa maŋ lɛ adafi, ni ta lɛ ba ni mɔ ko tsɔ̃ mli egbo lɛ, no lɛ, mɔ ni gbo lɛ, egbo yɛ enishaianii ahewɔ moŋ nɛ, shi mabi elá shi yɛ bulɔ lɛ dɛŋ.
7 “No hewɔ lɛ, bo Gbɔmɔ Adesa, mito bo bulɔ mihã Israel we lɛ. Be fɛɛ be ni ooonu wiemɔ ko kɛaajɛ minaa lɛ, bɔɔ amɛ kɔkɔ oha mi. 8Kɛji mikɛɛ efɔŋfeelɔ akɛ, ‘Bo efɔŋfeelɔ, gbo ooogbo!’ Ni owieee obɔɔɔ efɔŋfeelɔ lɛ kɔkɔ koni ekpale kɛje egbɛ fɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ; nakai efɔŋfeelɔ lɛ, eeegbo yɛ enishaianii lɛ ahewɔ moŋ nɛ, shi mabi elá shi yɛ odɛ̃ŋ. 9Shi kɛji obɔ efɔŋfeelɔ lɛ kɔkɔ koni ekpale kɛje egbɛ fɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni kɛ̃lɛ ekpaleee lɛ, eeegbo yɛ enishaianii lɛ ahewɔ, shi bo lɛ ooohere oyiwala.”
Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ nifeemɔnii kɛ ehe nyɔmɔwoo
10“Agbɛnɛ, bo Gbɔmɔ Adesa, kɛɛmɔ Israel we lɛ akɛ nɔ ni nyɛkɛɛ pɛŋ ji akɛ, ‘Wɔtɔ̃mɔi lɛ kɛ wɔhe eshai lɛ miisu wɔtsui, ni ehã wɔtãra loo. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ mɔ, ni wɔyi ana wala hu?’ 11 Kɛɛmɔ amɛ akɛ gbii abɔ ni mi, mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ Hiɛkãalɔ lɛ nɛɛ, minaaa efɔŋfeelɔ gbele he miishɛɛ; shi moŋ minaa miishɛɛ kɛji efɔŋfeelɔ tsake ejeŋba, ni eyi na wala. Ao Israel we, nyɛkpalea, nyɛkpalea kɛjea nyɛgbɛi fɔ̃ji lɛ anɔ koni nyɛyi ana wala. Mɛni hewɔ nyɛaagboi?
12“No hewɔ lɛ, bo Gbɔmɔ Adesa, kɛɛmɔ omaŋbii lɛ akɛ jalɔ lɛ ejalɛ nyɛŋ lɛ ajie kɛji etɔ̃; ni kɛji efɔŋfeelɔ hu kpa efɔŋfeemɔ lɛ, adamɔŋ efɔŋ ni efee momo lɛ nɔ ni abu lɛ fɔ. Ni jalɔ hu etsutsu jalɛ haŋ eyi ana wala kɛji efee esha. 13Kɛ mikɛɛ jalɔ akɛ eyi aaana wala, ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ ejalɛ lɛ nɔ, ni efee esha lɛ, ejalɛnii fɛɛ ni efee kɛho lɛ, akaiŋ ekoeko; shi moŋ ebaagbo yɛ esha ni efee lɛ hewɔ. 14Asaŋ, kɛji mikɛɛ efɔŋfeelɔ akɛ ‘Gbo kɛ̃ ooogbo,’ ni ekpa eshafeemɔ, ni efee nɔ ni ja ni ehi lɛ, 15kɛ efɔŋfeelɔ kpale nɔ ni akɛbato lɛ awaba eha nɔtsɛ, ni ekpale nɔ ni ekɛ ojotswaa shɔ̃ lɛ ehã; kɛji eye mlai ni hãa wala lɛ anɔ, ni efeee efɔŋ lɛ, eyi aaana wala kɛ̃, egboŋ. 16Esha fɛɛ esha ni efee kɛho lɛ akɛ ekoeko ebuŋ lɛ fɔ, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ eyi aaana wala, egboŋ.
17“Shi, omaŋbii lɛ kɛɔ akɛ, ‘Nɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ lɛ feɔ lɛ ejaaa;’ tsɛbelɛ amɛ moŋ, nɔ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ ni ejaaa. 18Kɛji jalɔ fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni ja feemɔ ni efee efɔŋ lɛ, ebaagbo yɛ no hewɔ. 19Ni kɛji efɔŋfeelɔ fɔ̃ɔ efɔŋfeemɔ, ni efee nɔ ni ja ni ehi lɛ, eyi baana wala. 20Kɛ̃lɛ, nyɛkɛɔ akɛ, ‘Nɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ lɛ feɔ lɛ ejaaa.’ Bo Israel we, makojo nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ yɛ enifeemɔnii anaa.”
Yerusalɛm fitemɔ he adafitswaa
21 Wɔnomŋɔɔ lɛ mli afi ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ lɛ nɔ, nyɔŋ ni ji nyɔŋma lɛ nɔ gbi ni ji enumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nuu ko ni ejo foi kɛjɛ Yerusalɛm ba miŋɔɔ ni ebakɛɛ mi akɛ abutu maŋ lɛ.
22Yehowa hewalɛ lɛ ba minɔ gbɛkɛ, ni mitɔ mu dani foijelɔ lɛ ba, shi leebi mli be ni foijelɔ lɛ ba miŋɔɔ lɛ, agbele minaa ni mitɔko mu dɔŋŋ.
Esha ni maŋbii feɔ
23Yehowa kɛ mi wie ni ekɛɛ akɛ, 24 “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, maŋbii ni yɔɔ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amaŋfɔ̃i lɛ amli lɛ kɛɔ akɛ, ‘Abraham lɛ, gbɔmɔ kome too ni, kɛ̃lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔ̃ enɔ, shi wɔ lɛ, wɔyi fa; akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eha wɔ akɛ wɔŋɔ.’
25“No hewɔ lɛ, kɛɛmɔ amɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, nyɛyeɔ loo ni emli lá tsereko; ni amãgã jamɔ kɔ̃ɔ nyɛhiɛ, ni nyɛshwieɔ lá shi; aso shikpɔŋ lɛ aaatsɔ̃ nyɛnɔ kɛ̃? 26Nyɛfãa klante nyɛwoɔ nyɛhe, nyɛfeɔ musubɔɔnii; nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ kɛ enaanyo ŋa bɔɔ ajwamãŋ; Aso shikpɔŋ lɛ aaatsɔ̃ nyɛnɔ kɛ̃?
27“Kɛɛmɔ amɛ akɛ bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, gbii abɔ ni mi, mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ Hiɛkãalɔ lɛ nɛɛ lɛ, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ akɛ klante baakpãtã mɛi ni yɔɔ amaŋfɔ̃i lɛ amli lɛ ahiɛ, ni mɔ ni yɔɔ ŋa kplanaa nɔ lɛ, maŋɔ lɛ maha ŋaŋ kooloi ni amɛye. Mɛi ni yɔɔ mɔji kɛ tɛkpoji amli lɛ, gbele hela aaagbe amɛ. 28Makpãtã shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni ebaatsõ amaŋfɔ̃; ni ehewalɛ ni ekɛshwãa lɛ sɛɛ baafo; ni Israel gɔji lɛ anɔ baatsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃, bɔ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko tsɔŋ jɛi kɛhoŋ. 29Amɛaana amɛle akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa, kɛji mikpãtã shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni etsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃ yɛ musubɔɔnii fɛɛ ni amɛfee lɛ ahewɔ.”
Gbalɔ lɛ wiemɔ lɛ sɛɛ sane
30“Shi bo Gbɔmɔ Adesa, omaŋbii lɛ wieɔ ohe yɛ gbogboi ahe kɛ shĩai ashinai ashi, ni amɛkɛɛkɛɔ amɛhe akɛ, ‘Nyɛbaa nyɛbaboa nɔ wiemɔ ni jɛ Yehowa ŋɔɔ toi.’ 31 Ni amɛbuaa amɛhenaa kɛbaa oŋɔɔ akɛ maŋ, ni amɛbataraa ohiɛ akɛ mimaŋbii, ni amɛboɔ owiemɔ lɛ toi, shi amɛyeee nɔ. Ejaakɛ amɛsumɔɔ gbɔmɔ kɛ amɛnaabu, shi amɛkɛ amɛtsui fɔɔ amɛsɛɛnamɔ nɔ. 32Shi, naa, bo lɛ otamɔ mɔ ko kɛkɛ ni kɛ gbee ni ŋɔɔ laa suɔmɔ lalai, ni etswaa saŋku jogbaŋŋ ohã amɛ. Ejaakɛ amɛnuɔ owiemɔ lɛ nɛ, shi amɛyeŋ nɔ. 33Kɛ enɛ ba mli lɛ, naa, ebaana eba mli kɛ̃, no dani amɛkɛaale akɛ gbalɔ ko ehi amɛteŋ pɛŋ.”

english_text:
Israel's Leaders Are Worthless Shepherds
1 The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, Israel's leaders are like shepherds taking care of my sheep, the people of Israel. But I want you to condemn these leaders and tell them:
I, the Lord God, say you shepherds of Israel are doomed! You take care of yourselves while ignoring my sheep. 3You drink their milk and use their wool to make your clothes. Then you butcher the best ones for food. But you don't take care of the flock! 4You have never protected the weak ones or healed the sick ones or bandaged those that get hurt. You let them wander off and never look for those that get lost. You are cruel and mean to my sheep. 5 They strayed in every direction, and because there was no shepherd to watch them, they were attacked and eaten by wild animals. 6So my sheep were scattered across the earth. They roamed on hills and mountains, without anyone even bothering to look for them.
7-8Now listen to what I, the living Lord God, am saying to you shepherds. My sheep have been attacked and eaten by wild animals, because you refused to watch them. You never went looking for the lost ones, and you fed yourselves without feeding my sheep. 9-10So I, the Lord, will punish you! I will rescue my sheep from you and never let you be their shepherd again or butcher them for food. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Is the Good Shepherd
11The Lord God then said:
I will look for my sheep and take care of them myself, 12just as a shepherd looks for lost sheep. My sheep have been lost since that dark and miserable day when they were scattered throughout the nations. But I will rescue them 13and bring them back from the foreign nations where they now live. I will be their shepherd and will let them graze on Israel's mountains and in the valleys and fertile fields. 14They will be safe as they feed on grassy meadows and green hills. 15I promise to take care of them and keep them safe, 16to look for those that are lost and bring back the ones that wander off, to bandage those that are hurt and protect the ones that are weak. I will also slaughter those that are fat and strong, because I always do right.
Judgment on the Strong Sheep
17The Lord God said to his sheep, the people of Israel:
I will carefully watch each one of you to decide which ones are the strong sheep and which ones are weak. 18Some of you eat the greenest grass, then trample down what's left when you finish. Others drink clean water, then step in the water to make the rest of it muddy. 19That means my other sheep have nothing fit to eat or drink.
20So I, the Lord God, will separate you strong sheep from the weak. 21You strong ones have used your powerful horns to chase off those that are weak, 22but I will rescue them and no longer let them be mistreated. I will separate the good from the bad.
23 After that, I will give you a shepherd from the family of my servant King David. All of you, both strong and weak, will have the same shepherd, and he will take good care of you. 24 He will be your leader, and I will be your God. I, the Lord, have spoken.
A Bright Future for the Lord's Sheep
The Lord God said:
25The people of Israel are my sheep, and I solemnly promise that they will live in peace. I will chase away every wild animal from the desert and the forest, so my sheep will not be afraid. 26They will live around my holy mountain, and I will bless them by sending more than enough rain 27to make their trees produce fruit and their crops to grow. I will set them free from slavery and let them live safely in their own land. Then they will know that I am the Lord. 28Foreign nations will never again rob them, and wild animals will no longer kill and eat them. They will have nothing to fear. 29I will make their fields produce large amounts of crops, so they will never again go hungry or be laughed at by foreigners. 30Then everyone will know that I protect my people Israel. I, the Lord, make this promise. 31They are my sheep; I am their God, and I take care of them.
translation_text:
Israel maŋhiɛnyiɛlɔi lɛ
1Yehowa kɛ mi wie ni ekɛɛ akɛ, 2 “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, gbaa oshi Israel tookwɛlɔi lɛ. Gbaa ni okɛɛ amɛ, amɛ mɛi ni ji maŋhiɛnyiɛlɔi lɛ, ni amɛ ji tookwɛlɔi lɛ. Kɛɛmɔ amɛ akɛ bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, Ao, nyɛ Israel tookwɛlɔi ni nyɛlɛɔ nyɛ kɛkɛ nyɛhe. Ani esaaa akɛ tookwɛlɔi lɛ alɛ toi lɛ?
3“Nyɛyeɔ amɛfɔ, ni nyɛkɛ amɛhetsɔi feɔ mama nyɛbuɔ, ni nyɛgbeɔ nii ni eshwishwii lɛ nyɛyeɔ; shi nyɛlɛɛɛ toi lɛ. 4 Toi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ, nyɛwajeee amɛ; nii ni he yeɔ lɛ, nyɛtsaaa amɛ; nii ni epila lɛ nyɛfimɔɔɔ amɛpilamɔi lɛ anɔ; nii ni edu gbɛ lɛ, nyɛyakpalaaa amɛ kɛbaaa shĩa; ni nii ni elaaje lɛ nyɛyataooo amɛ; shi moŋ nyɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ kɛ yiwalɛ yeɔ amɛnɔ. 5 No hewɔ lɛ, amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ejaakɛ amɛbɛ kwɛlɔ; ni amɛtsɔ̃ niyenii amɛha ŋaŋ kooloi awuiyelɔi fɛɛ. 6Mitoi lɛ gbɛ shwã, ni amɛtsomlo kɛnyiɛ gɔji kɛ gɔŋkpɔi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ fɛɛ anɔ. Mitoi lɛ egbɛ eshwã shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ, ni mɔ ko bɛ ni diɔ amɛsɛɛ aloo etaoɔ amɛ.
7“No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛ tookwɛlɔi, nyɛboa Yehowa wiemɔ toi. 8Mitoi lɛ etsɔ̃ milɛloo; amɛtsɔmɔ ŋaŋ kooloi fɛɛ aniyenii; amɛbɛ kwɛlɔ ejaakɛ mitookwɛlɔi lɛ eyataooo amɛ; shi moŋ amɛyeɔ nii amɛtɔɔ, shi amɛlɛɛɛ mitoi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, gbii abɔ ni mi, mi ji Yehowa Hiɛkãalɔ lɛ nɛɛ lɛ, 9nyɛ tookwɛlɔi lɛ, nyɛboa Yehowa wiemɔ toi. 10Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, naa, mikɛ tookwɛlɔi lɛ ena, ni mabi mitoi lɛ ashi kɛjɛ amɛdɛŋ. Magu amɛ toi lɛ akwɛmɔ, ni tookwɛlɔi lɛ elɛŋ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe dɔŋŋ. Mahe mitoi lɛ yɛ amɛdɛŋ koni amɛkana amɛ amɛye dɔŋŋ.”
Tookwɛlɔ kpakpa lɛ
11Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Naa, mi, mi diɛŋtsɛ madi mitoi lɛ asɛɛ ni matao amɛsɛɛgbɛ. 12 Bɔ ni tookwɛlɔ taoɔ etooku ni egbɛ eshwã lɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ matao mitoi lɛ asɛɛgbɛ. Mabua amɛnaa kɛjɛ he fɛɛ he ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛtee, yɛ gbi ni atatu kɛ duŋ kpii ewo nɔ tete. 13Maŋɔ amɛ kɛaajɛ majimaji anɔ bii ateŋ, ni mabua amɛnaa kɛjɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ; ni maŋɔ amɛ kɛba amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Malɛ amɛ yɛ Israel gɔji lɛ anɔ, kɛ gɔji ateaŋ jɔi lɛ amli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛhei fɛɛ. 14 Mikɛ jwɛfɔ kpakpa aaalɛ amɛ; Israel gɔji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ aaafee amɛniyelihe. Amɛaabumɔ shi yɛ niyelihe kpakpa shikpɔŋ nɔ; ni Israel gɔji lɛ anɔ hei ni jwɛfɔ frɔ̃frɔ̃ yɔɔ lɛ amɛaaye nii yɛ. 15Mi diɛŋtsɛ mafee mitoi lɛ akwɛlɔ, ni mahã amɛbumɔ shi yɛ hejɔlɛ mli. Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.
16“Too fɛɛ too ni elaaje lɛ, matao lɛ, ni nɔ ni edu gbɛ lɛ, makpala lɛ kɛba shĩa; ni nɔ ni epila lɛ, mafi epilamɔ lɛ nɔ; ni nɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ mawaje lɛ. Nɔ ni ewo fɔ, kɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ makpãtã ehiɛ. Mikɛ amɛ baaye yɛ jalɛ naa.
17 “Nyɛ mitoi, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, naa, mikojoɔ gwantɛŋ kɛ gwantɛŋ teŋ; mikojoɔ ojwɛni kɛ too kpakpo teŋ. 18Ani jwɛi kpakpa ni nyɛnaa nyɛyeɔ yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ lɛ, nyɛtsui etɔ̃ɔɔ hewɔ ni nyɛkɛ nyɛnaji naanaa nyɛjwɛi kpakpa ni shwɛɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ani nu hu ni hiɛ tɛ̃ kɔtekɔte ni nyɛnuɔ lɛ, nyɛtsui etɔ̃ɔɔ hewɔ ni nyɛkɛ nyɛnaji kpɔtɔɔ nɔ ni shwɛɔ lɛ! 19Ani esa akɛ mitoi lɛ aye niyenii ni nyɛkɛ nyɛnaji enaanaa nɔ lɛ, ni amɛnu nu ni nyɛkɛ nyɛnaji ekpɔtɔ lɛ?
20“No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ amɛ nɛ, naa, Mi, mi diɛŋtsɛ mibakojo too ni ewo fɔ kɛ too ni etã loo lɛ teŋ. 21Akɛni nyɛkɛ nyɛkɔ̃ji tsirɛɔ toi lɛ; ni nyɛkɛ nyɛkoji hɛlɛɔ amɛmli helatsɛmɛi lɛ kɛyashiɔ nyɛgbɛɔ kui enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ nyɛshwãa majiasɛɛ 22hewɔ lɛ, mibahere mitoi lɛ ayiwala, ni amɛtsɔŋ kooloi anaa loo dɔŋŋ. Mibakojo gwantɛŋ kɛ gwantɛŋ teŋ. 23 Mibato tookwɛlɔ kome maha amɛ, ni ji mitsulɔ David, ni lɛ eeelɛ amɛ; ebaalɛ amɛ ni eeetsɔ̃ amɛkwɛlɔ.”
24 “Ni mi, Yehowa, matsɔ amɛNyɔŋmɔ; ni mitsulɔ David baatsɔ lumɔ aha amɛ. Mi, Yehowa mikɛɛ.
25Mikɛ amɛ baakpãŋ kpãŋmɔ ni baahã amɛhe ajɔ amɛ, ni mashwie kooloi awuiyelɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe yɛ ŋa nɔ; amɛaawɔ yɛ koo mli.
26“Ni mibajɔɔ amɛ kɛ hei ni bɔle migɔŋkpɔ lɛ he lɛ, ni maha nu anɛ yɛ ebe mli, ni nu lɛ aaatsɔ jɔɔmɔ aha amɛ. 27Kɛkɛ lɛ ŋa nɔ tsei baawo amɛyibii ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baaba nii babaoo, ni amɛaahi shi shweshweeshwe yɛ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji mikumɔ amɛkɔŋtsei ni akɛbɔ amɛ apã lɛ, ni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ mɛi ni yeɔ amɛ nyɔŋ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ, no amɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa. 28Amɛtsɔŋ tamɔ kooloo naa loo amɛhaŋ jeŋmaji lɛ dɔŋŋ; ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kooloi lɛ yeŋ amɛloo. Amɛaabahi shi shweshweeshwe, ni mɔ ko mɔ ko woŋ amɛhe gbeyei. 29Maha niyenii babaoo aba amɛŋmɔji ashi bɔ ni afee ni hɔmɔ akaplene amɛ dɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ; ni maji krokomɛi lɛ hu egbeŋ amɛhe guɔ dɔŋŋ. 30Amɛaana amɛle akɛ, mi, Yehowa amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ, mikɛ amɛ yɛ, ni amɛ Israel we lɛ amɛ ji mimaŋ. Mi, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa mikɛɛ! 31 Ni nyɛ lɛ, mitoi ji nyɛ, milɛɛhe toi ji nyɛ. Mi ji nyɛNyɔŋmɔ! Mi, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa, mi kɛɛ!”

english_text:
Edom Will Be a Wasteland
1 The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Edom 3and say to them:
I, the Lord God,
am now your enemy!
And I will turn your nation
into an empty wasteland,
4leaving your towns in ruins.
Your land will be a desert,
and then you will know
that I am the Lord.
5People of Edom, not only have you been Israel's longtime enemy, you simply watched when disaster wiped out its people as punishment for their sins. 6And so, as surely as I am the living Lord God, you are guilty of murder and must be put to death. 7I will destroy your nation and kill anyone who travels through it. 8Dead bodies will cover your mountains and fill up your valleys, 9and your land will lie in ruins forever. No one will live in your towns ever again. You will know that I am the Lord.
10You thought the nations of Judah and Israel belonged to you, and that you could take over their territory. But I am their God, 11and as surely as I live, I will punish you for treating my people with anger and hatred. Then they will know that I, the Lord, am punishing you! 12And you will finally realize that I heard you laugh at their destruction and say their land was yours to take. 13You even insulted me, but I heard it all.
14Everyone on earth will celebrate when I destroy you, 15just as you celebrated when Israel was destroyed. Your nation of Edom will be nothing but a wasteland. Then everyone will know that I am the Lord.
translation_text:
Nyɔŋmɔ gbala Edom toi
1 Yehowa kɛɛ mi akɛ,
2“Gbɔmɔ Adesa, tsɔ̃ ohiɛ owo Edom shikpɔŋ lɛ,
ni ogba oshi lɛ akɛ,
3bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ,
naa, Edom shikpɔŋ, mikɛ bo ena,
ni makpãtã ohiɛ,
mafee bo amaŋfɔ̃ butubutu.
4Makpãtã omaji wuji lɛ ahiɛ, ni
obaatsɔ shikpɔŋ amaŋfɔ̃,
ni ooona ole akɛ, mi, mi ji Yehowa.
5“Akɛni onyɛ Israel hiɛ kɛjɛ blema beebe, ni yɛ Israel amanehulu be mli lɛ, oŋɔ amɛ oha ni akɛ klante kpãtã amɛhiɛ, be mli ni agbalaa amɛtoi nɔ ni ji naagbee nɔ lɛ, yɛ amɛhe eshai ahewɔ; 6 no hewɔ lɛ, gbii abɔ ni mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ Hiɛkãalɔ lɛ nɛɛ lɛ, masaa bo maha láshishwiemɔ, ni láshishwiemɔ baanyiɛ osɛɛ. Oshwie lá shi, no hewɔ lɛ, láshishwiemɔ baanyiɛ osɛɛ. 7Maha Edom shikpɔŋ lɛ atsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃ butubutu, ni mɔ ko mɔ ko tsɔŋ jɛi kɛhoŋ. 8Maha ogɔji lɛ anɔ ayimɔ obɔ̃bɔ̃ kɛ gbohii, ni mɛi ni enyɔnyɔɔ yɛ klante naa lɛ agbohii aaayimɔ ogɔŋkpɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ ojɔi kɛ onujɔi lɛ amli. 9Maha otsɔ amaŋfɔ̃ kɛya naanɔ; ni mɔ ko mɔ ko ehiŋ omaŋ wuji lɛ ekoeko mli. Enɛ okɛaana ole akɛ mi, mi ji, Yehowa.
10“Nɔ ni okɛɛ ji akɛ, ‘Yuda kɛ Israel maji enyɔ lɛ minii ni, ni amɛshikpɔji enyɔ lɛ hu minii ni hewɔ lɛ maŋɔ amɛ;’ tsɛbelɛ, mi, Yehowa, miyɛ jɛi. 11No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, gbii abɔ ni mi ji Nyɔŋmɔ Hiɛkãalɔ lɛ nɛɛ, mi hu mikɛ nyɛ baaye tamɔ bɔ pɛ ni nyɛkɛ mimaŋbii lɛ ye kɛ mlifu kɛ hiɛkɔ̃ɔ lɛ. Ni maha amɛle akɛ nɔ ni nyɛfee amɛ lɛ he toigbalamɔ nyɛnaa lɛ. 12Maha nyɛle akɛ mi, Yehowa, minu musubɔɔ wiemɔi fɛɛ ni nyɛwieɔ nyɛshiɔ Israel gɔji lɛ akɛ ‘amɛtsɔmɔ amaŋfɔ̃i, ni ajɔɔ nɔ ahã wɔ ni wɔkpãtã hiɛ lɛ.’ 13Mi diɛŋtsɛ minu bɔ ni ejɛ nyɛnaa ni nyɛkɛ henɔwomɔ wie wiemɔi babaoo nyɛshi mi lɛ.
14“Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, maha otsɔ amaŋfɔ̃ koni je lɛ mli fɛɛ anya! 15 Bɔ ni onya yɛ Israel we lɛ gboshinii lɛ ahewɔ ejaakɛ etsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃ lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ mafee bo. Obaatsɔ amaŋfɔ̃; ni Seir gɔŋ lɛ kɛ Edom shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tswɛm hu baatsɔ̃ amaŋfɔ̃, kɛkɛ lɛ amɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.”

english_text:
A Message for Israel's Mountains
1The Lord said:
Ezekiel, son of man, tell the mountains of Israel 2that I, the Lord God, am saying:
Your enemies sneered and said that you mountains belonged to them. 3They ruined and crushed you from every side, and foreign nations captured and made fun of you. 4So all you mountains and hills, streams and valleys, listen to what I will do. Your towns may now lie in ruins, and nations may laugh and insult you. 5But in my fierce anger, I will turn against those nations, and especially the Edomites, because they laughed at you the loudest and took over your pasturelands. 6You have suffered long enough, and, I, the Lord God, am very angry! Nations have insulted you, 7so I will now insult and disgrace them. That is my solemn promise.
8Trees will grow on you mountains of Israel and produce fruit for my people, because they will soon come home. 9I will take care of you by plowing your soil and planting crops on your fertile slopes. 10The people of Israel will return and rebuild your ruined towns and live in them. 11Children will be born, and animals will give birth to their young. You will no longer be deserted as you are now, but you will be covered with people and treated better than ever. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
12I will bring my people Israel home, and they will live on you mountains, because you belong to them, and your fertile slopes will never again let them starve. 13It's true that you have been accused of not producing enough food and of letting your people starve. 14-15But I, the Lord, promise that you won't hear other nations laugh and sneer at you ever again. From now on, you will always produce plenty of food for your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
The Lord Will Be Honored
16The Lord said:
17Ezekiel, son of man, when the people of Israel were living in their own country, they made the land unclean by the way they behaved, just as a woman's monthly period makes her unclean. 18They committed murders and worshiped idols, which made the land even worse. So in my anger, I punished my people 19and scattered them throughout the nations, just as they deserved. 20Wherever they went, my name was disgraced, because foreigners insulted my people by saying I had forced them out of their own land.
21I care what those foreigners think of me, 22so tell the Israelites that I am saying:
You have disgraced my holy name among the nations where you now live. So you don't deserve what I'm going to do for you. I will lead you home to bring honor to my name 23and to show foreign nations that I am holy. Then they will know that I am the Lord God. I have spoken.
24I will gather you from the foreign nations and bring you home. 25I will sprinkle you with clean water, and you will be clean and acceptable to me. I will wash away everything that makes you unclean, and I will remove your disgusting idols. 26 I will take away your stubborn heart and give you a new heart and a desire to be faithful. You will have only pure thoughts, 27because I will put my Spirit in you and make you eager to obey my laws and teachings. 28You will once again live in the land I gave your ancestors; you will be my people, and I will be your God.
29I will protect you from anything that makes you unclean. Your fields will overflow with grain, and no one will starve. 30Your trees will be filled with fruit, and crops will grow in your fields, so that you will never again feel ashamed for not having enough food. 31You will remember your evil ways and hate yourselves for what you've done. 32People of Israel, I'm not doing these things for your sake. You sinned against me, and you must suffer shame and disgrace for what you have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
33After I have made you clean, I will let you rebuild your ruined towns and let you live in them. 34Your land will be plowed again, and nobody will be able to see that it was once barren. 35Instead, they will say that it looks as beautiful as the garden of Eden. They won't see towns lying in ruins, but they will see your strong cities filled with people. 36Then the nearby nations that survive will know that I am the one who rebuilt the ruined places and replanted the barren fields. I, the Lord, make this promise.
37I will once again answer your prayers, and I will let your nation grow until you are like a large flock of sheep. 38The towns that now lie in ruins will be filled with people, just as Jerusalem was once filled with sheep to be offered as sacrifices during a festival. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_text:
Nyɔŋmɔ jɔɔ Israelbii
1Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Bo Gbɔmɔ Adesa, gbaa otsɔ̃ɔ Israel gɔji lɛ, ni nɔ ni okɛɛ amɛ nɛ, nyɛ Israel gɔji, nyɛboa, Yehowa wiemɔ toi. 2Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, akɛni Israel henyɛlɔ lɛ nya ni ekɛɛ akɛ, ‘Yiɛ, agbɛnɛ blema gɔji lɛ etsɔmɔ wɔgbɛfaŋnɔ,’ 3hewɔ lɛ, gbaa ni okɛɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ! Majimaji ni bɔle nyɛ lɛ fee nyɛ maŋ lɛ amaŋfɔ̃, ni amɛwiɛ nyɛ mɔnyɔmɔnyɔ, ni eha nyɛtsɔmɔ majimaji krokomɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ. Amɛsopa nyɛ ni amɛye nyɛhe osheku hu. 4No hewɔ lɛ, nyɛ Israel gɔji, nyɛboa Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa wiemɔ toi. Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ gɔji lɛ kɛ gɔŋkpɔi lɛ kɛ nujɔi lɛ kɛ jɔi lɛ kɛ amaŋfɔ̃i lɛ, kɛ maji wuji ni ashi ashwie shi efolo lɛ, ni amɛtsɔmɔ kooloo naa loo kɛ hefɛoyeli nii amɛha majimaji ni eshwɛ ni bɔle amɛ kɛkpe lɛ nɛ.
5“No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni mi, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa, mikɛɔ nɛ, miiwie kɛ awuŋayeli ni naa wa miishi maji ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ Edom fɛɛ, mɛi ni kɛ miishɛɛ ŋɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛfee amɛnɔ, ni amɛbuuu akɛ minɔ ni. Amɛŋɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ amɛhã amɛhe akɛ haanii ni amɛhi nɔ. 6No hewɔ lɛ, gbaa yɛ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni okɛɛ gɔji lɛ kɛ gɔŋkpɔi lɛ kɛ nujɔi lɛ kɛ gɔji ateŋ jɔi lɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, naa, nyɛkɛɛ awuŋã ni miyeɔ hewɔ lɛ, miiwie kɛ mlifu akɛ, nyɛhã jeŋmaji lɛ eshwie mimaŋ lɛ hiɛ shi. 7No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni mi, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa mikɛɔ nɛ, Miikã midiɛŋtsɛ mihe kitã akɛ, majimaji ni bɔle nyɛ lɛ hu hiɛ baashwie shi nakai nɔŋŋ. 8Shi nyɛ, Israel gɔji lɛ nyɛnɔ tsei lɛ baagbala niji, ni amɛbaawo yibii nyɛha mimaŋ Israel lɛ; ejaakɛ etsɛŋ ni Israelbii aaku amɛsɛɛ kɛba amɛmaŋ ekoŋŋ. 9Shi naa, miyɛ mihã nyɛ, ni matsɔ mihiɛ mahã nyɛ, gɔji lɛ, ni abaahu nyɛnɔ, ni abadu nii yɛ nyɛnɔ. 10Maha Israel we lɛ fɛɛ tswɛm yi afa toi abɔ. Abaahi maji wuji lɛ amli ekoŋŋ, ni amɛaatswa tsu koi lɛ. 11Maha gbɔmɛi kɛ kooloi ayi afa yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ; amɛaafɔfɔi, ni amɛyi aaafa. Ni mahã gbɔmɛi ahi nyɛnɔ tamɔ tsutsu lɛ; ni mafee nyɛ ejurɔ pii fe tsutsu lɛ. No nyɛkɛaale akɛ, mi, mi ji Yehowa. 12Naa, mahã gbɔmɛi anyiɛ yɛ nyɛnɔ, ni mimaŋ Israelbii lɛ tete anyiɛ yɛ onɔ. Amɛaaŋɔ bo akɛ amɛnɔ ni oootsɔ̃ amɛgboshinii kwraa, ni ogbeŋ amɛbii lɛ hɔmɔ dɔŋŋ.
13“Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ mɛi kɛɔ nyɛ akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ kpãtãa gbɔmɔ hiɛ ni gbekɛbii tɛooo yɛ nɔ moŋ, 14shi agbɛnɛ kɛjɛ kɛyaa nɛɛ, nyɛkpãtãŋ gbɔmɔ hiɛ dɔŋŋ ni gbekɛbii hu gboiŋ yɛ nyɛnɔ dɔŋŋ. Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.” 15Majimaji ni yeɔ ohe fɛo lɛ, mihaŋ onu oheguɔ ni amɛgbeɔ lɛ dɔŋŋ, ni onaŋ amɛ maŋbii ahorabɔɔ lɛ, ni mihaŋ omaŋ lɛ nane atɔ̃tɔ̃. Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ.
Israel wala hee lɛ
16Yehowa kɛ mi wie ni ekɛɛ akɛ, 17 “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, be ni Israelbii lɛ yɔɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛjeŋba kɛ amɛnifeemɔnii bule shikpɔŋ lɛ. Amɛjeŋba yɛ mihiɛ lɛ tamɔ yoo ni etee tsuiasɛɛ ni ehe tseee. 18No hewɔ lɛ, mimli wo amɛ la naakpa yɛ lá shi ni amɛshwie yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amɛhã amãgãi ni amɛkɛbule shikpɔŋ lɛ hewɔ. 19Migbɛ amɛ mishwã majimaji lɛ ateŋ kɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ. Amɛjeŋba kɛ amɛnifeemɔnii ahewɔ lɛ migbala amɛtoi. 20 Be ni amɛtee majimaji lɛ amli lɛ, he fɛɛ he ni amɛshɛ lɛ amɛgbe migbɛi krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ he guɔ; ejaakɛ nɔ ni mɛi kɛɛ yɛ amɛhe ji akɛ, ‘Yehowa webii nɛ, shi kɛ̃lɛ naa amɛ ni amɛje amɛNyɔŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.’ 21 Shi migbɛi krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ ni Israel we lɛ hã agbe he guɔ yɛ majimaji lɛ ateŋ he ni amɛtee lɛ dɔ mi.
22 “No hewɔ lɛ, kɛɛmɔ Israel we lɛ akɛ bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, nyɛ Israel we, jeee nyɛhewɔ mafee nɔ ko, shi moŋ, migbɛi krɔŋkrɔŋ ni nyɛgbe he guɔ yɛ majimaji lɛ ateŋ, hei ni nyɛyahi lɛ, hewɔ.
23“Masaa mafee minunyam gbɛi kpeteŋkple lɛ ni abule lɛ yɛ jeŋmaji lɛ ateŋ, ni nyɛ hu nyɛgbe he guɔ yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ. Kɛji kɛtsɔ̃ nyɛnɔ lɛ, misaa mifee minunyam gbɛi kpeteŋkple lɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ yɛ amɛhiɛ lɛ, no amɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa, Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɛ. 24Ejaakɛ maŋɔ nyɛ kɛaajɛ maji lɛ amli, ni mabua nyɛnaa kɛaajɛ shikpɔji lɛ fɛɛ anɔ, ni mikɛ nyɛ aaaba nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. 25 Mikɛ nu ni mli tse baashwã nyɛnɔ, ni nyɛhe baatse. Ni matsuu nyɛwɔji ahe muji ni yɔɔ nyɛhe lɛ hu.
26“Mahã nyɛ tsui hee ni mikɛ mumɔ hee baawo nyɛmli, ni majie nyɛtsui ni wa tamɔ tɛ lɛ kɛje nyɛmli ni mahã nyɛ heloo tsui ni he jɔ. 27 Mikɛ miMumɔ lɛ baawo nyɛmli, ni mahã nyɛba nyɛjeŋ yɛ mikpɔi lɛ anaa, ni nyɛbaaye mimlai lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ. 28 Nyɛbaahi shikpɔŋ ni mikɛhã nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ anɔ; ni nyɛaatsɔ̃ mimaŋ, ni mi hu matsɔ̃ nyɛNyɔŋmɔ. 29Majie nyɛ kɛjɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni woɔ nyɛhe muji lɛ mli; mafã, ni ŋmãa aaaba babaoo, ni mihaŋ nyɛye hɔmɔ ko dɔŋŋ. 30 Mahã tseiayibii kɛ ŋmɔshinii afa pii koni hɔmɔ akaha nyɛhiɛ shwie shi yɛ jeŋmaji lɛ ahiɛ kɔkɔɔkɔ. 31Enɛ baahã nyɛkai nyɛjeŋba fɔŋ ni nyɛba kɛ nii gbohii ni nyɛfee lɛ; ni nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛhe aaafe nyɛ nyaŋemɔ yɛ eshai ni nyɛfee lɛ kɛ musubɔɔ nii ni nyɛfeefee lɛ ahewɔ. 32Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, bo Israel we, nyɛnaa nyɛlea akɛ jeee nyɛhewɔ mafee enɛ nɛɛ; nyɛhiɛ agboia ni nyɛhiɛ ashwiea shi yɛ nyɛjeŋba hewɔ.
33“Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ nɛ, gbi nɔ ni matsuu nyɛhe kɛjɛ nyɛhe eshai lɛ amli lɛ, mahã mɛi ahi maji wuji lɛ amli, ni abaasaa tsu koi lɛ amãmɔ. 34Shikpɔŋ ni kulɛ yɛ mɛi ahiɛ lɛ ekã efolo lɛ, abaahu nɔ, bɔ ni ekaŋ shi efolo dɔŋŋ. 35Mɛi baana, ni amɛaakɛɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ ni kulɛ ekã shi efolo lɛ, no nɔŋŋ etsɔ̃ tamɔ Eden trom nɛɛ; ni maji ni tsɔmɔ amaŋfɔ̃i ni mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ amɛmli lɛ, nomɛi amli gbɔmɛi ebahi ni atswa gbogboi awo amɛhe nɛɛ. 36 Kɛkɛ lɛ jeŋmaji ni eshwɛ ni bɔle nyɛ kɛkpe lɛ aaana ale akɛ mi, Yehowa, mi ni misaa tsu koi lɛ mitswa, ni he ni ka shi efolo lɛ, mitɛo nii yɛ jɛi. Mi, Yehowa miwie ni bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni ji lɛ, mafee.
37 “Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, mahã Israel we lɛ abi mi enɛ hu ni mafee mahã amɛ; no ji akɛ mahã amɛyi afa tamɔ toiku. 38Mahã maji wuji ni etsɔmɔ amaŋfɔ̃i lɛ amli aaayimɔ obɔ̃bɔ̃ kɛ gbɔmɛi babaoo tamɔ toi kui ni akɛyaashã afɔle yɛ Yerusalɛm yɛ egbii juji lɛ anɔ lɛ. Enɛ amɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa.”

english_text:
Dry Bones Live Again
1Some time later, I felt the Lord's power take control of me, and his Spirit carried me to a valley full of bones. 2The Lord showed me all around, and everywhere I looked I saw bones that were dried out. 3He said, “Ezekiel, son of man, can these bones come back to life?”
I replied, “Lord God, only you can answer that.”
4He then told me to say:
Dry bones, listen to what the Lord is saying to you, 5“I, the Lord God, will put breath in you, and once again you will live. 6I will wrap you with muscles and skin and breathe life into you. Then you will know that I am the Lord.”
7I did what the Lord said, but before I finished speaking, I heard a rattling noise. The bones were coming together! 8I saw muscles and skin cover the bones, but they had no life in them.
9The Lord said:
Ezekiel, now say to the wind, “The Lord God commands you to blow from every direction and to breathe life into these dead bodies, so they can live again.”
10 As soon as I said this, the wind blew among the bodies, and they came back to life! They all stood up, and there were enough to make a large army.
11The Lord said:
Ezekiel, the people of Israel are like dead bones. They complain that they are dried up and that they have no hope for the future. 12So tell them, “I, the Lord God, promise to open your graves and set you free. I will bring you back to Israel, 13and when that happens, you will realize that I am the Lord. 14My Spirit will give you breath, and you will live again. I will bring you home, and you will know that I have kept my promise. I, the Lord, have spoken.”
Judah and Israel Together Again
15The Lord said:
16Ezekiel, son of man, get a stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Judah.” Then get another stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Israel.” 17Hold these two sticks end to end, so they look like one stick. 18And when your people ask you what this means, 19tell them that I, the Lord, will join together the stick of Israel and the stick of Judah. I will hold them in my hand, and they will become one.
20Hold these two sticks where they can be seen by everyone 21and then say:
I, the Lord God, will gather the people of Israel and bring them home from the foreign nations where they now live. 22I will make them into one nation and let them once again live in the land of Israel. Only one king will rule them, and they will never again be divided into two nations. 23They will no longer worship idols and do things that make them unacceptable to me. I will wash away their sin and make them clean, and I will protect them from everything that makes them unclean. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
24-25 Their king will always come from the family of my servant King David and will care for them like a shepherd. The people of Israel will faithfully obey my laws. They and their descendants will live in the land I gave my servant Jacob, just as their ancestors did. 26I solemnly promise to bless the people of Israel with unending peace. I will protect them and let them become a powerful nation. My temple will stand in Israel for all time, 27 and I will live among my people and be their God. 28Every nation on earth will know that my temple is in Israel and that I have chosen the Israelites to be my people.
translation_text:
Wui ni ekwakwao lɛ
1Yehowa hewalɛ lɛ bayi minɔ, ni Yehowa Mumɔ lɛ ŋɔ mi kɛje kpo, ni eyayi mi shi yɛ jɔɔ ko mli. Wui eyi jɔɔ lɛ mli obɔ̃ tɔ. 2Enyiɛ mihiɛ kɛbɔle wui lɛ kɛkpe; ni naa, amɛfa naakpa; asaŋ amɛhe ekwakwao hu naakpa. 3Ebi mi akɛ, “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, aso wala aaanyɛ wui nɛɛ amli aba ekoŋŋ.” Mihã hetoo akɛ, “Ao, Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa, bo pɛ ole.”
4Ekɛ mi wie ekoŋŋ akɛ, “Gbaa ni okɛɛ wui nɛɛ akɛ, nyɛ wui ni nyɛhe ekwakwao, nyɛboa Yehowa wiemɔ toi. 5 Nɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ wui nɛɛ nɛ, naa maha mumɔ abote nyɛmli ni wala baaba nyɛmli. 6 Maha nyɛna fãi, ni mahã loo aba nyɛhe ni mahã hewolo aha nyɛhe. Mikɛ mumɔ baawo nyɛmli ni wala baaba nyɛmli, ni nyɛaana nyɛle akɛ, mi, mi ji Yehowa.”
7No hewɔ lɛ, migba, taakɛ afã mi lɛ. Be ni migbaa lɛ, minu gbɛɛmɔ kɛ hetsirɛmɔi ahe. Kɛkɛ ni wui lɛ bua amɛhe naa, ni wu kɛ ewu tsa. 8Be ni mikwɛ lɛ amɛna fãi kɛ hewolo; shi mumɔ bɛ amɛmli.
9Agbɛnɛ Mumɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ, “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, gbaa ni okɛ mumɔ lɛ awie ni okɛɛ mumɔ lɛ akɛ nɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, bo mumɔ, jɛɛ jeŋ koji ejwɛ lɛ mli ni obamu oshwie nɛkɛ mɛi ni agbegbee nɛɛ anɔ koni amɛna wala.”
10 No hewɔ lɛ, migba taakɛ afã mi lɛ, ni mumɔ ba amɛmli, ni wala ba amɛmli, ni amɛte shi amɛdamɔ amɛnaji anɔ, amɛyi fa babaoo diɛŋtsɛ.
11Kɛkɛ ni Yehowa Mumɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ, “Gbɔmɔ Adesa nɛkɛ wui nɛɛ Israel we muu lɛ fɛɛ ni. Naa, amɛwieɔ akɛ ‘wɔwui ahe ekwakwao, ni wɔhiɛnɔkãmɔ etã, ni abɛɛ wɔ kwraa ashwie.’ 12No hewɔ lɛ, gbaa ni okɛɛ amɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, Ao, mimaŋbii, naa, mibagbele nyɛgbonyobui lɛ anaa, ni matee nyɛ shi kɛaajɛ nyɛgbonyobui lɛ amli, ni mikɛ nyɛ aaaba nyɛmaŋ, ni ji Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. 13Ao, mimaŋbii, kɛji migbele nyɛgbonyobui lɛ anaa ni mitee nyɛ shi kɛjɛ nyɛgbonyobui lɛ amli lɛ, no nyɛkɛaale akɛ mi, mi ji Yehowa. 14Mikɛ miMumɔ lɛ baawo nyɛmli, ni wala baaba nyɛmli, ni maŋɔ nyɛ kɛya nyɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛkɛ lɛ nyɛbaale akɛ mi, Yehowa, mi, mikɛɛ, ni mifee hu.” Yehowa kɛɛ.
Yuda kɛ Israel yɛ Maŋtsɛyeli kome shishi
15Yehowa kɛ mi wie, ni ekɛɛ akɛ, 16 “Gbɔmɔ Adesa, kɔ tso kome koni oŋma yɛ nɔ akɛ, ‘Yuda kɛ Israelbii ni fata ehe lɛ anɔ nɛ.’ Agbɛnɛ kɔ tso kroko hu koni oŋma yɛ nɔ akɛ ‘Yosef tso,’ ni ji Efraim kɛ Israel we lɛ fɛɛ ni fata ehe lɛ nɔ nɛ.
17“Agbɛnɛ lɛ okɛ tso kome atsa tso kome nɔ, koni amɛtsɔ tso kome yɛ odɛ̃ŋ. 18Ni kɛji omaŋbii lɛ bi bo akɛ, ‘Otsɔ̃ɔɔ wɔ enɛ shishi lo?’ lɛ.”
19Kɛɛmɔ amɛ akɛ, “Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, ‘Naa mibakɔ Yosef tso ni yɔɔ Efraim kɛ Israel akutsei ni fata ehe lɛ adɛŋ lɛ, ni mikɛ no kɛ Yuda tso lɛ baatsa. Mafee amɛ tso kome koni amɛfee tso kome yɛ midɛŋ.’
20“Hiɛmɔ tsei ni oŋma nii yɛ amɛnɔ lɛ yɛ odɛ̃ŋ ni amɛna, 21koni okɛɛ amɛ akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, naa, majie Israelbii lɛ kɛaajɛ majimaji lɛ anɔ hei ni amɛtee lɛ, ni mabua amɛnaa kɛaajɛ hei fɛɛ; ni mikɛ amɛ aaaba amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. 22 Kɛkɛ lɛ mafee amɛ maŋ kome yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ Israel gɔji lɛ anɔ. Amɛaahi maŋtsɛ kome shishi ni amɛfeŋ maji enyɔ dɔŋŋ. Mligbalamɔ hu baŋ amɛmaŋtsɛyeli mli dɔŋŋ.
23“Amɛkɛ amɛmãgãi kɛ amɛmusubɔɔnii lɛ kɛ eshai ni amɛfeɔ lɛ ekoeko buleŋ amɛhe dɔŋŋ; shi moŋ mahere amɛyiwala kɛaajɛ eshai ni amɛfee ni etse amɛ kɛje mihe lɛ amli, ni matsuu amɛhe; kɛkɛ lɛ amɛaatsɔ mimaŋ, ni matsɔ amɛNyɔŋmɔ. 24 Mitsulɔ David baaye amɛ nɔ maŋtsɛ, ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛaana lumɔ kome. Amɛbaakwɛ koni amɛye mimlai lɛ kɛ mikpɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ. 25Amɛaahi shikpɔŋ ni nyɛtsɛmɛi lɛ hi nɔ lɛ nɔ, shikpɔŋ ni mikɛhã mitsulɔ Yakob lɛ. Amɛ kɛ amɛbii kɛ amɛbii abii baahi nɔ kɛya naanɔ; ni mitsulɔ David baaye amɛnɔ lumɔ kɛya naanɔ. 26 Mikɛ amɛaakpãŋ toiŋjɔlɛ kpãŋmɔ; ni ebaafee naanɔ kpãŋmɔ yɛ mi kɛ amɛ teŋ. Majɔɔ amɛ ni mahã amɛshwere, ni mikɛ mihe krɔŋkrɔŋ lɛ, ni ji Sɔlemɔ we lɛ, baama amɛteŋ, ni ebaahi jɛi kɛya naanɔ tɔ̃ɔ. 27 Mi kɛ amɛ baahi jɛi, ni matsɔ̃ amɛNyɔŋmɔ ni amɛaatsɔ̃ mimaŋ. 28Kɛji mihe krɔŋkrɔŋ, ni ji Sɔlemɔ we lɛ yɛ amɛteŋ kɛmiiya naanɔ lɛ, no majimaji kɛaale akɛ mi, Yehowa, mi mitsuɔ Israel he, mifeɔ lɛ krɔŋkrɔŋ.”

english_text:
Gog Invades Israel
1The Lord said:
2 Ezekiel, son of man, condemn Gog, that wicked ruler of the kingdoms of Meshech and Tubal in the land of Magog. Tell him:
3I, the Lord God, am your enemy, 4and I will make you powerless! I will put a hook in your jaw and drag away both you and your large army. You command cavalry troops that wear heavy armor and carry shields and swords. 5Your army includes soldiers from Persia, Ethiopia, and Libya, 6as well as from Gomer and Beth-Togarmah in the north. Your army is enormous!
7So keep your troops prepared to fight, 8because in a few years, I will command you to invade Israel, a country that was ruined by war. It was deserted for a long time, but its people have returned from the foreign nations where they once lived. The Israelites now live in peace in the mountains of their own land. 9But you and your army will attack them like a fierce thunderstorm and surround them like a cloud.
10When that day comes, I know that you will have an evil plan 11to take advantage of Israel, that weak and peaceful country where people live safely inside towns that have no walls or gates or locks. 12You will rob the people in towns that were once a pile of rubble. These people lived as prisoners in foreign nations, but they have returned to Israel, the most important place in the world, and they own livestock and property. 13The people of Sheba and Dedan, along with merchants from villages in southern Spain, will be your allies. They will want some of the silver and gold, as well as the livestock and property that your army takes from Israel.
14I, the Lord God, know that when you see my people Israel living in peace, 15you will lead your powerful cavalry from your kingdom in the north. 16You will attack my people like a storm-cloud that covers their land. I will let you invade my country Israel, so that every nation on earth will know that I, the Lord, am holy.
Judgment on Gog
17The Lord said to Gog:
Long ago, I ordered my prophets to warn the people of Israel that someday I would send an enemy to attack them. You, Gog, are that enemy, and that day is coming. 18When you invade Israel, I will become furious, 19and in my anger I will send a terrible earthquake to shake Israel. 20Every living thing on earth will tremble in fear of me—every fish and bird, every wild animal and reptile, and every human. Mountains will crumble, cliffs will fall, and cities will collapse. 21I, the Lord, will make the mountains of Israel turn against you. Your troops will be so terrified that they will attack each other. 22I will strike you with diseases and punish you with death. You and your army will be pounded with rainstorms, hailstones, and burning sulfur. 23I will do these things to show the world that I, the Lord, am holy.
translation_text:
Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ Gog tsu nii
1Yehowa kɛ mi wie ni ekɛɛ mi akɛ, 2 “Gbɔmɔ Adesa tsɔ̃ ohiɛ owo Gog, ni ji Meshek kɛ Tubal lumɔnukpa ni yɔɔ Magog shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Gbaa oshi lɛ ni okɛɛ akɛ, 3bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, bo Gog, ni oji Meshek kɛ Tubal lumɔnukpa, naa, mikɛ bo ena, 4ni madɔ oyi, ni mawo okadaaŋ kpoŋ, ni magbala bo kɛ ota lɛ fɛɛ kɛje kpo. Magbala okpɔŋɔi lɛ kɛ amɛnɔtalɔi ni wo amɛdamai fɛɛ; asafo kpele ni hiɛ amɛtsɛŋi wuji kɛ tsɛŋi bibii kɛ klante. 5Magbala Persiabii kɛ Etiopiabii kɛ Libiabii fɛɛ ni amɛhiɛhiɛ tsɛŋi ni amɛbu dadefai lɛ hu mafata amɛhe. 6Tabilɔi ni jɛ Gomer kɛ Bet-Togarma ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ lɛ fɛɛ aaashi onɔ; asafo kpele diɛŋtsɛ. 7Saamɔ ohe ni ofee kralo, bo kɛ ta ni bua shi kɛbɔle ohe lɛ fɛɛ, koni obu amɛhe. 8Afii komɛi asɛɛ lɛ abaabua omɛi lɛ anaa. No sɛɛ lɛ, obaate shi oshi shikpɔŋ ni akpɔ̃ amɛ kɛjɛ ta mli kɛba lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Israel gɔji lɛ anɔ ni kã shi efolo daa, he ni abua mɛi pii anaa kɛjɛ majimaji anɔ kɛba lɛ. Ajie emaŋbii lɛ kɛjɛ majimaji lɛ amli, ni agbɛnɛ amɛ fɛɛ tswɛm amɛfee shweshweeshwe. 9Bo okɛ ota lɛ fɛɛ aaafã kɛaaba tamɔ ahum, ni majimaji pii aaafata ohe ni ooofee tamɔ atatu ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.”
10Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, “Nakai gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ susumɔi pii baaba oyiŋ, ni obajwɛŋ efɔŋfeemɔ he. 11 Obaakɛɛ akɛ, ‘Mafa kɛyatua akrowai ni atswako gbogbo awoko amɛhe lɛ, ni mayatua mɛi ni yɔɔ kpoo ni amɛyɛ shweshweeshwe, maji ni atswako gbogbo awoko amɛhe, ni amɛbɛ agbosɛɛ adabaŋi kɛ agboi hu lɛ. 12Oooyaha nii, ni oooyatswa ojo. Ooote shi oyatua amaŋfɔ̃i ni agbɛnɛ mɛi yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ, kɛ mɛi ni abua amɛnaa kɛjɛ majimaji lɛ anɔ ni amɛyɔɔ tsinai kɛ nibii pii yɛ majimaji ni bɔle amɛ lɛ ateŋ lɛ.’ 13Shebabii kɛ Dedanbii kɛ jarayelɔi ni jɛ Tarshish kɛ ehe akrowai lɛ baabi bo akɛ, ‘Nihaa obaa nɛɛ? Ani oba ni obaha nii lo? Ani obua ota asafo lɛ naa kɛkpe kɛbatswa ojo ni nyɛkɛha nii koni nyɛkɛloo jwiɛtɛi kɛ shika kɛ tsinai kɛ nibii pii kɛya?’
14“No hewɔ lɛ, Gbɔmɔ Adesa, gbaa ni okɛɛ Gog akɛ, bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛɔ nɛ, gbi nɔ ni mimaŋ Israel aaahi shi shweshweeshwe lɛ, no ooote shi owo amɛ. 15Bo okɛ mɛi babaoo ni tara okpɔŋɔi anɔ ni fata ohe lɛ kɛaajɛ ojɛɛhe ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ tɔ̃ɔ lɛ aaaba, ta asafo kpele diɛŋtsɛ. 16Ooote shi owo mimaŋ Israel; nyɛyifalɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji gbi lɛ shɛ lɛ mahã otua mishikpɔŋ lɛ, ni bɔ ni mafee bo yɛ majimaji lɛ ahiɛ lɛ, baahã amɛle mi akɛ mɔ krɔŋkrɔŋ ji mi.
17 “Bɔ ni Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɔ nɛ, ani bo ohe miwie yɛ blema gbii lɛ amli kɛtsɔ̃ mitsuji, ni ji Israel gbalɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ, mɛi ni gba afii babaoo yɛ nakai beiaŋ akɛ mahã obatua amɛ lɛ?”
Nyɔŋmɔ gbala Gog toi
18Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, “Gbi nɔ ni Gog baate shi abatua Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ, mimli baawo la waa diɛŋtsɛ. 19Ejaakɛ mikɛ awuŋayeli kɛ mlila miigba mli kpoo makɛɛ akɛ, nakai gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ kukrudu ni naa wa baashi yɛ Israel shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. 20Nakai gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ ŋshɔŋloi kɛ ŋwɛi loofɔji kɛ ŋaŋ kooloi kɛ waamɔnii fɛɛ ni wamɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ gbɔmɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he baakpokpo yɛ mihegbeyei naa. Abaatsirɛ gɔji atswia shi, ni tɛsai ni kwɔlɔ lɛ baagbeegbee shi, ni aaawule gbogbo fɛɛ gbogbo ashwie shi. 21Nuŋtsɔ Yehowa kɛɛ akɛ, mikɛ hejaramɔ aaaba Gog nɔ, ni nuu fɛɛ nuu baawo klante nɔ yɛ enaanyo nɔ. 22 Mikɛ gbele hela kɛ láshishwiemɔ baagbala etoi; ni mahã nu ni naa wa kɛ nyɔŋmɔŋtɛi kɛ la kɛ swɔɔ anɛ ashwie lɛ kɛ etai lɛ kɛ mɛi babaoo ni fata ehe lɛ anɔ. 23 Ni enɛ mikɛaahã maji fɛɛ ale akɛ mida ni mihe tse; ni amɛaana amɛle hu akɛ mi ji Yehowa.”

english_text:
Gog Is Defeated
The Lord said:
1Ezekiel, son of man, condemn Gog and tell him:
You are the ruler of Meshech and Tubal, but I, the Lord, am your enemy! 2I will turn you around and drag you from the north until you reach the mountains of Israel. 3I will knock the bow out of your left hand and the arrows out of your right hand, 4 and you and your army will die on those mountains. Then birds and wild animals will eat the flesh 5of your dead bodies left lying in open fields. I, the Lord, have spoken.
6I will set fire to the land of Magog and to those nations along the seacoast that think they are so secure, and they will know that I am the Lord.
7My people Israel will know me, and they will no longer disgrace my holy name. Everyone on earth will know that I am the holy Lord God of Israel. 8The day is coming when these things will happen, just as I have promised.
